summary: Sensient Technologies reported quarterly EPS of $0.80, exceeding the $0.78 consensus estimate. The company announced a quarterly dividend of $0.30 per share, payable March 1, with an annualized yield of 1.53%. KeyCorp raised its price target from $80 to $84, maintaining an “overweight” rating, while Zacks upgraded the stock from “sell” to “hold.” Sensient manufactures and markets colors, flavors and fragrances.

The Weather Channel’s Android app uses IBM mesh networking to relay information between phones when mobile networks fail. Designed for emerging markets in Asia, Latin America and Africa, it transmits data over Bluetooth and Wi-Fi across 200–500 feet without extra battery burden or network reconfiguration. Its effectiveness depends on enough people running the app. Digital signatures verify trusted sources and detect modifications. The 3.2MB app also supports older 2G networks.
This technical report discusses bioimpedance phase angle clusters as an alternative to body mass index and has not been peer-reviewed.

XYZprinting’s MfgPro220 xPF 3D printer, priced at $19,950 with a 16-liter build volume, will be demonstrated at the Fort Worth Convention Center April 24–28, 2018. Designed for prototyping, tooling and end-use parts, it uses Nexa3D’s photo-curing technology, machine learning, sensors, and onboard and cloud controls to support high-speed production. XYZprinting also announced a partnership under which BEGO will exclusively market a dental printer manufactured by XYZprinting, with Nexa3D developing the technology and products. An earlier agreement covers XYZprinting’s investment in Nexa3D and manufacturing and sales of its printers.

Collagen provides structural support, strength and elasticity to skin, tendons and bones, but natural production decreases with age. Most collagen supplements come from animals. Research suggests hydrolysed collagen, which is broken down for easier digestion and absorption, may be the most effective form.

Studies indicate supplements may support skin firmness, brittle nails, bone density, joint health and muscle repair. Evidence for thicker hair is limited to studies in mice, and research into benefits remains ongoing.

Dosage depends on the intended benefit and product. Manufacturers commonly recommend at least 12 weeks for noticeable results, and third-party-tested products are recommended to verify their contents.

A balanced diet containing protein and essential nutrients, including vitamin C, zinc and copper, is described as the most reliable way to support the body’s natural collagen production.

Bethesda will release Wolfenstein II: The New Colossus on Nintendo Switch on June 29, digitally and physically. The cartridge version also requires a download, potentially needing microSD storage. The port follows Bethesda’s Switch releases of Doom and Skyrim in November.

Bell Academy received a November 2016 grant from Blue Cross Blue Shield of Mississippi to build a physical education facility. Parent and community volunteers constructed the building, which provides equipment and dedicated indoor space for more activities without disrupting other classes. Teacher Joyce Aycock plans to add a horizontal rock-climbing wall before the building’s official ribbon cutting Friday at 9:30 a.m.

The council says it is coordinating roadworks and utility maintenance to reduce congestion around Southway, Tamerton Foliot and the Derriford Transport Scheme. Measures include restricting temporary signal hours, requesting off-peak working, suspending Tavistock Road bus lane restrictions and adjusting George Junction signal timings. Proposed lane-marking changes at Budshead Roundabout require safety approval. Further changes to road markings and possible additional signs are intended to improve traffic flow. Planned roadworks information is available online, through email alerts and via public notices.

The article argues ADT is undervalued relative to newly listed Verisure, citing revenue growth, improving profitability, and recurring revenue. Partnerships with Google and State Farm, debt reduction, and share buybacks support an 11% shareholder yield. Customer churn and stagnant subscriber numbers remain challenges, while investments in AI, remote assistance, and smart home solutions aim to improve retention. Applying a 12–14x price-to-earnings multiple suggests at least 33% upside. The author discloses a long position in ADT.

The Department of Higher Education and Training is working to integrate NSFAS with institutional systems after delayed student payments sparked protests. Minister Naledi Pandor ordered urgent action on outstanding funding cases and a review of NSFAS processes. Integration problems have affected registration data needed to release funding. Government allocated nearly R7.2bn in additional bursary funding for 2018 and R105m over the medium term to strengthen NSFAS administration. The DA said it would seek an urgent parliamentary committee meeting, criticising the lack of clear answers on how many students were affected, why payments were delayed and when funding would arrive.

The Drive concept pairs a 10–12-yard basic in-cut route with a 3–4-yard shallow crossing route from the same side of the formation. It creates a triangle read for the quarterback, stresses linebackers in coverage, and can serve as a primary or secondary read.

Drive works well against man coverage, with receivers staying on the move, and against Cover 4, where complementary routes can create deep opportunities or a numbers advantage underneath. Cover 2 and Cover 3 present difficulties because additional underneath defenders outnumber receiving options. Against zone coverage, the basic and shallow routes settle into open spaces.

The quarterback checks the post route before the snap, then progresses through the go route, shallow cross, basic route, and running back check-down. Variations include bunch formations that create natural picks and rubs, and backside combinations that provide quick options against blitzes or outlets when downfield throws are unavailable.

The lecture introduces discrete stochastic processes and distinguishes mathematical probability from modeling real-world uncertainty. Solving a specified model is different from selecting an appropriate model: mathematically correct analysis can produce unreliable conclusions when its assumptions poorly represent the situation. Useful models balance simplicity with sufficient detail and require understanding of the application.

Stochastic processes describe outcomes evolving over time, often through sequences of random variables. The course covers counting and Poisson processes, Markov chains, renewal processes, random walks, martingales, and combinations of these. Applications include communications, networks, computer systems, queues, risk management, system failures, biology, medicine, and control.

A probability model consists of a sample space, a collection of events, and a probability measure. Events are subsets of the sample space, with closure requirements including complements and countable unions. For uncountable sample spaces, not every subset can necessarily be treated as an event. The probability axioms require:
- The sample space has probability one.
- Event probabilities are nonnegative.
- The probability of a countable union of disjoint events equals the sum of their probabilities.

Consequences include zero probability for the empty set, the complement rule, monotonicity, and the union bound. Events and their probabilities are foundational; random variables and expectations are derived concepts.

Two events are independent when their intersection probability equals the product of their probabilities. Independent experiments can be combined through Cartesian-product sample spaces. Dice examples illustrate how distinguishability affects model construction and why assumptions must be explicit.

A random variable maps sample points to finite real values and must satisfy the condition that each set of outcomes mapped to values at or below a real threshold is an event. Its cumulative distribution function therefore exists. Distribution functions accommodate discrete, continuous, and other distributions, including cases not described solely by probability mass functions or densities.

The lecture emphasizes combining intuition with proof. Constructing arguments, identifying gaps, and checking for counterexamples are important for analyzing complicated systems where intuition alone is insufficient.

Allen reported that Korean refugee Kim Ok-kiun was assassinated in Shanghai by Hong Chong-oo. Chinese authorities subsequently delivered Hong and Kim’s body to Korea, where the body was mutilated despite Japanese diplomatic objections. Other foreign representatives favored limiting their response to unofficial explanations of foreign attitudes. In Tokyo, Japanese police arrested suspects in a plot against refugee Pak Yung-ho, forcibly removing one from the Korean legation after Korean officials refused to surrender him.

Sill reported uprisings against oppressive officials in three southern Korean provinces, with officials killed, beaten, or dispossessed. Government troops appeared ineffective, and unrest threatened to spread. At the government’s request, he recalled American missionaries from the interior and forwarded the King’s request for an American warship at Chemulpo. He also advocated more frequent American naval visits.

The author returns a bill to the House of Representatives with objections, calling it inexpedient and unconstitutional. The bill would grant States 20,000 acres of public land for each Senator and Representative, with additional grants following the 1860 census, to support colleges emphasizing agriculture and the mechanic arts. Initial grants would total 6,060,000 acres, valued at $7,575,000 at the minimum government price. States without qualifying public lands would receive saleable land scrip. Each State would have to provide at least one college within five years and replace any losses to its endowment.

The author presents six principal objections:
- Land scrip would depress land prices, reduce federal revenue during financial difficulty, and diminish the value of soldiers’ land warrants.
- Federal support for State education would blur governmental responsibilities, encourage State dependence and excessive spending, and deplete public lands valuable as security for wartime borrowing.
- Speculators could acquire desirable lands cheaply and resell them at higher prices, harming settlers and new States.
- The Federal Government could not compel States to apply the proceeds as intended.
- New federally endowed colleges would compete with existing institutions, while disputes over local allocations could undermine educational goals. Supporting agricultural and mechanical professorships at existing colleges would be preferable if grants were made.
- Congress lacks constitutional authority to fund State education through either taxation or public-land donations. The author argues that the constitutional power to “dispose of” federal property permits sales, not unrestricted gifts, and that converting tax revenue into land cannot expand congressional authority.

The author distinguishes earlier educational land grants in new States, defending them as prudent measures that encouraged settlement and increased the value and saleability of remaining federal lands. Grants for colleges throughout the States, the author argues, do not serve that purpose.

UPMSP will announce the 2018 UP Board Class 10 and Class 12 results on April 29 at 12:30 pm. Results will be available at upresults.nic.in and upmspresults.up.nic.in. Students can access results using their roll numbers or send “UP10 ROLLNUMBER” or “UP12 ROLLNUMBER” by SMS to 56263.

Tight checking and Hasek’s puck handling have hindered forechecking and possession. Detroit’s system adjustments have added frustration, while defensive breakdowns have proved costly in otherwise close games. The team plans to review mistakes, tighten defensive play and refocus, supporting lineup changes made by the coaching staff.

Tesla Motors’ unaudited first-quarter 2016 report describes increased revenue, wider losses, and plans to accelerate vehicle production and infrastructure investment.

- **Financial results:** Revenue rose to $1.147 billion from $939.9 million a year earlier. Automotive revenue was $1.026 billion, while services and other revenue reached $121.0 million. Gross profit declined to $252.5 million, and gross margin fell to 22.0% from 27.7%, primarily reflecting product mix. Operating expenses increased to $500.7 million. Net loss widened to $282.3 million, or $2.13 per share, from $154.2 million, or $1.22 per share.
- **Financial position and cash flows:** At March 31, cash and cash equivalents totaled $1.442 billion, assets were $9.192 billion, liabilities were $8.179 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $970.4 million. Operating activities used $249.6 million in cash, investing activities used $233.8 million, and financing activities provided $715.4 million. Customer deposits increased to $391.4 million from $283.4 million at year-end.
- **Production and demand:** Tesla produced 15,510 vehicles during the quarter, including approximately 2,650 Model X vehicles, despite supplier shortages affecting the Model X production ramp. Model 3 received more than 325,000 reservations within one week of its unveiling. Tesla expected Model 3 volume production and deliveries in late 2017 and targeted 80,000–90,000 Model S and Model X deliveries in 2016.
- **Expansion plans:** Tesla advanced its annual production target of 500,000 vehicles to 2018, acknowledging execution challenges and likely additional capital requirements. It expected 2016 capital spending approximately 50% above its previous $1.5 billion estimate and operating-expense growth of 20–25%. Plans included more than 70 additional retail and service locations and approximately 250 new Supercharger locations. Gigafactory battery-cell production was expected to begin in the fourth quarter of 2016.
- **Financing and risks:** Tesla expanded its revolving credit commitments to $1 billion, had $565 million outstanding at quarter-end, and repaid $350 million in April. Leasing and resale-value guarantees required revenue deferrals and exposed Tesla to residual-value and liquidity risks. Other risks included supplier dependence, manufacturing inefficiencies, expansion delays, and potential Gigafactory cost overruns. Tesla cautioned that forward-looking results could differ materially from expectations.

Christian Pulisic and Weston McKennie headline Mauricio Pochettino’s 26-player U.S. roster for two October friendlies in Austin, Texas, and Commerce City, Colorado. Following September’s experimentation, the squad largely features expected first-team players.

Antonee Robinson returns after recovering from knee surgery, while McKennie receives his first call-up since March. Tanner Tessmann and Aidan Morris were rewarded for strong club performances. Pulisic enters camp with six goals and two assists for AC Milan this season. Injuries and selection decisions kept several players out of the squad. Training camp begins Oct. 4.

Russia’s central bank cut its key interest rate from 9.75 to 9.25 percent, exceeding analysts’ expectations, and signaled further gradual cuts. It forecast inflation would reach 4 percent before year-end and remain within target in 2018–2019, while reiterating concerns about inflation and global market volatility.

Jennifer Thompson’s mistaken identification led to Ronald Cotton’s conviction for raping her. Eleven years later, DNA testing identified Bobby Poole as the perpetrator; Thompson says he raped six more women while Cotton was imprisoned. After Cotton’s exoneration, Thompson apologized, and they became close friends. She discusses how questioning can alter witnesses’ memories and established Healing Justice, which brings harmed parties together to share their stories. Cotton regularly attends its retreats.

An Oct. 15 payday for 1.3 million active-duty military members could pressure Congress and the White House to end the government shutdown or pass temporary funding. Goldman economists expect a resolution by mid-October, although prediction markets indicate a 71% chance the shutdown will extend beyond Oct. 14. Alternative arrangements to pay troops could reduce pressure for a broader agreement. Disruptions to government services, potential airport delays and expiring benefits may also encourage compromise. Analysts warn the shutdown could persist into November.

The document describes Versioned Chip Endorsement Key (VCEK) certificates and AMD’s Key Distribution System (KDS) interface for developers supporting SEV-SNP virtualized environments.

- A VCEK is an ECDSA private key unique to an AMD chip running a specific Trusted Compute Base (TCB) version. Its certificate chain uses the product-specific AMD Root Key (ARK) and AMD SEV Key (ASK).
- VCEK certificates follow X.509v3 and are generated on request rather than stored in KDS. Their validity starts one day before issuance to accommodate clock differences and ends seven years afterward. ARK and ASK certificates remain valid for 25 years.
- Certificate extensions identify product stepping, hardware ID, and TCB components. Hardware IDs are 64 bytes for Family 19h processors and eight bytes for Family 1Ah processors.
- KDS provides an HTTP interface using TLS 1.2 at `https://kdsintf.amd.com` to retrieve VCEK certificates, PEM-formatted certificate chains, and DER-formatted certificate revocation lists.
- VCEK requests specify a product, hardware ID, and security patch levels (SPLs). Omitted SPLs default to zero. Microcode SPL values range from 0–255; other SPL parameters range from 0–127.
- Requests may encounter rate limits; clients should honor `Retry-After`. Unsupported URLs and nonexistent device IDs generally return HTTP 404, while malformed parameters can return HTTP 400.
- The service supports pre-fetching and locally caching certificates for future firmware SPL values to ease security upgrades.

Joe Bryant’s Week 10 fantasy football newsletter evaluates passing and rushing matchups using recent performance, defensive yardage allowed, fantasy points allowed and injury updates. He emphasizes that matchup strength is only one factor in lineup decisions and introduces “On Target,” a feature tracking intended passes to receivers.

**Passing matchups**
- **Strongest offensive advantages:** New Orleans against San Francisco, San Diego against Seattle, Oakland against Kansas City, Green Bay against Minnesota, Indianapolis against Chicago, and Kansas City against Oakland.
- **Other favorable matchups:** Carolina, Buffalo, Miami, Chicago, New England, Seattle and Minnesota.
- **Strongest defensive advantages:** Pittsburgh against Tennessee, Baltimore against Cincinnati, the Giants against Cleveland, Washington against Arizona, and Tennessee against Pittsburgh.
- Despite difficult matchups, Bryant remains supportive of productive San Francisco players, including Jeff Garcia, Terrell Owens and Jerry Rice.

**Rushing matchups**
- **Strongest offensive advantages:** Stephen Davis against Arizona; Ron Dayne and Tiki Barber against Cleveland; Curtis Martin against Denver; Edgerrin James against Chicago; Ricky Williams against San Francisco; and Warrick Dunn and Mike Alstott against Atlanta.
- **Other favorable situations:** Terrell Davis returning against the Jets and Marshall Faulk facing Carolina. San Diego and Philadelphia have favorable opponents, but uncertain backfield workloads complicate player selection.
- **Strongest defensive advantages:** The Giants against Travis Prentice, New Orleans against Charlie Garner, Buffalo against New England’s backs, Pittsburgh against Eddie George, and Tennessee against Jerome Bettis. Bryant still considers Garner and a healthy George starters despite the opposition.

**Personnel developments**
- Jeff George replaces Brad Johnson as Washington’s starter after Johnson suffered a knee-ligament sprain.
- Jim Miller takes over at quarterback for Chicago; Jon Kitna starts for Seattle while Brock Huard recovers from a concussion; Randall Cunningham starts for Dallas with Troy Aikman out.
- Wesley Walls’ absence affects Carolina’s receiving options.
- Injuries could increase workloads for Napoleon Kaufman, Ahman Green, Shaun Alexander and Thomas Jones.
- Terrell Davis is expected to return and receive most of Denver’s rushing work, with Mike Anderson providing relief.

The invention describes a vehicle radar sensing system that uses a two-dimensional array of transmitting and receiving antennas with two-dimensional multiple input multiple output (MIMO) processing. This creates an enhanced virtual antenna aperture to improve horizontal and vertical angular accuracy and resolution simultaneously, without time-multiplexed scans.

One embodiment includes 12 transmitting antennas arranged in three rows and 16 receiving antennas arranged in four columns, functioning as 192 virtual receivers. Other two-dimensional arrangements are possible. Each transmitter independently emits a distinct waveform, allowing received echoes to be associated with the respective transmitter.

A control processes radar data to detect objects outside the vehicle. Applications include autonomous and semi-autonomous driving, automated parking, blind spot detection, cross-traffic alerts, lane-change assistance, emergency braking, pedestrian detection, and collision mitigation.

The system may combine radar data with exterior camera images to enhance object detection. When an object of interest is detected, it may generate visual, audible, or haptic alerts; control vehicle steering or braking; or highlight the object on a display showing camera images.

On Day 1 of the 2025 World Grand Prix of Darts, Rob Cross beat Nijman in a deciding leg of the third set. Ratajski won 2-0 with a 95.94 average, while Menzies eliminated the eighth seed. Joe Cullen defeated James Wade 2-0 after recovering from a 2-0 deficit in the second set.

Ghana’s major gold miners welcome government tests certifying export values to strengthen oversight and taxation, the Chamber of Mines said. Precious Minerals Marketing Company officials now access gold rooms, collect samples and participate in pre-shipment procedures. Ghana earned $5.78 billion from gold exports last year, up 17.6 percent from 2016. President Nana Akufo-Addo said about $5 billion in gold export revenues to the United Arab Emirates remain unaccounted for.

A report says Minnesota’s Edina School District introduces “white privilege” concepts as early as kindergarten. At Highlands Elementary, K–2 students create skin-tone hand cutouts for a poster promoting equality. Separately, Michigan State University professor Shreena Gandhi and co-author Lillie Wolff argue that U.S. yoga practices are linked to white supremacy, colonialism, cultural appropriation, and economic exploitation.

Workforce diversity supports understanding of global markets, but subconscious biases can lead employers to overlook qualified candidates. Studies cited found hiring disparities based on gender and applicants’ names. To reduce bias, employers should describe desired behaviors rather than personality types in job postings, remove names from resumes where possible, reconsider reasons for rejecting applicants, and assess relevant skills through challenges before collecting other information. Rigorous comparisons of qualifications and setting aside irrelevant information can produce a more diverse interview pool. Employers should also examine negative interview impressions to ensure prejudice is not influencing their judgment.

China’s foreign exchange regulator said capital outflow pressure eased somewhat in 2016 and yuan exchange-rate flexibility would increase in 2017. Authorities planned measures to attract capital inflows. The yuan weakened 6.5 percent against the dollar in 2016 but gained nearly 1 percent in early 2017. Final data showed a 2016 current account surplus of $196.4 billion, equivalent to 1.8 percent of GDP.

The author argues that well-designed tutoring can improve student learning while preparing future teachers. Teach For America’s Ignite Fellowship has trained more than 5,500 virtual tutors and reached over 40 communities. Reported academic gains include middle school math scores growing up to 2.5 times the expected rate and elementary reading progress up to three times faster than average.

The passage emphasizes structured tutor training, ongoing coaching and technology that supports human relationships. It cites research finding that participation as an Ignite tutor nearly triples the likelihood of applying to TFA’s teacher program, with the largest effects among men, people of color and non-education majors. Since Ignite launched, 550 fellows have joined TFA’s teaching corps. The author calls for treating tutoring as a long-term strategy for student growth and teacher recruitment rather than solely an emergency response to learning loss.

The study describes fabrication and characterization of NbN coplanar waveguide resonators on n-doped Si/Si₀.₇Ge₀.₃ quantum-well wafers for CMOS-compatible hybrid quantum circuits. Fabrication used a 100 nm sputtered NbN film, electron-beam lithography, and dry etching. An additional 1 μm-deep substrate etch in resonator gaps moved interfaces and quantum-well charge-noise sources away from high-electric-field regions, potentially reducing microwave losses. Microscopy showed crystalline SiGe layers but oxygenation and loss of crystallinity in the silicon cap.

Two nominally identical samples underwent four cooldowns over two years. At 50 mK, their studied resonances ranged from approximately 5.04 to 5.60 GHz. Internal quality factors increased with input power, from about 860 to 1064 for one sample and 500 to 600 for the other. Measurements showed no measurable degradation over two years, while coupling quality factors remained largely independent of power and temperature.

Loss modeling indicated that scattering-related losses dominated over two-level-system (TLS) losses at low temperature; quasiparticle losses were negligible at 50 mK. Increasing power produced resonance-frequency increases of up to 700 kHz, attributed to TLS saturation. Temperature-dependent measurements showed behavior consistent with thermal TLS saturation at lower temperatures and increasing quasiparticle effects at higher temperatures.

An RLC model characterized resonator inductance, capacitance, and resistance. Despite stable operation, the estimated maximum gatemon relaxation time for the wafer and design was approximately 14 ns, indicating substantial improvements are needed for scalable qubits. Proposed priorities include optimizing wafer growth, doping, interface roughness, buffer-layer thickness, and resonator coupling to reduce microwave loss while maintaining carrier mobility.

The departing President thanks his administration and the American people, expresses confidence in the nation’s strength and ideals, and pledges support for his successor. He describes the presidency as powerful but constrained by law, custom, and public consent, emphasizing democratic participation, public scrutiny, and preserving presidential authority against fragmented special-interest pressures.

He identifies three major global challenges: nuclear destruction, environmental stewardship, and human rights. While affirming the need for military strength, he urges international efforts to control and reduce nuclear arsenals. He warns that pollution, resource depletion, population growth, and environmental damage threaten the planet’s ability to sustain life, but maintains that foresight and determined action can address these problems.

He calls for continued defense of human rights at home and abroad, including education, medical care, employment, and freedom from discrimination, injustice, and religious intolerance. He argues that democratic values must remain central despite future tensions and competition for scarce resources, and that each generation must renew democracy.

He promises to facilitate the presidential transition, continue working for the American hostages held in Iran, and pursue the nation’s founding values as a private citizen.

Mary Brunkow, Fred Ramsdell and Shimon Sakaguchi won the 2025 Nobel Prize in physiology or medicine for discovering regulatory T cells and their role in preventing the immune system from attacking the body. These cells calm immune responses after infection or injury and help prevent fetal rejection during pregnancy. Their failure can cause autoimmune disorders or damaging inflammation. Brunkow and Ramsdell identified a mutation causing fatal autoimmune disease in male mouse pups. Scientists are exploring ways to harness regulatory T cells to treat cancer and other immune-related conditions.

The Yankees will start Paul Goldschmidt at first base, batting sixth, instead of Ben Rice in ALDS Game 4 against Toronto with their season on the line. Rice, who started the first three games and went 2-for-11, moves to the bench, providing options as a pinch-hitter or catching replacement. Toronto will use Louis Varland as an opener in a bullpen game.
Geary County deputies arrested Isaac Torgerson on suspicion of aggravated assault Saturday after witnesses reported a truck passenger waving a gun toward another vehicle near Fort Riley.

Donnell Gibson, a behavior intervention specialist and junior varsity basketball coach at Como Park Senior High in St. Paul, helps students navigate life challenges. After saving a family of 10 from a house fire in 2015, he received the Fire Department’s highest honor and reconsidered plans for a recreation center. Instead, he established the Gibson Foundation to mentor young African-American inner-city men through speakers, college tours and basketball. His work draws on his childhood experiences of homelessness and encouragement from his high school principal.

Amazon, founded by Jeff Bezos, launched its website in 1995 as an online bookstore. By the twentieth anniversary of its 1997 IPO, it had become the fourth-largest U.S. public company, with a market capitalization of $458 billion and shareholder returns of nearly 64,000%. Its cumulative net income from 1997 through 2016 totaled $4.9 billion, reflecting a strategy that prioritized expansion, research and development, and long-term cash flow growth over short-term profitability.

Amazon expanded into additional product categories and acquired businesses including Audible, Zappos, and Quidsi. Its customer-focused approach emphasized discounts, reviews, convenient ordering, broader selection, and faster delivery. Prime, introduced in 2005, expanded from a shipping membership into a package of digital services and shopping benefits. Following Prime Day 2017, membership reached nearly half of U.S. households.

The company developed devices including Kindle, Fire tablets, and Echo speakers. Amazon Web Services began in 2006 by renting excess computing capacity and subsequently attracted both startups and established companies. Despite failures such as the Fire Phone, Bezos maintained that experimentation and tolerance for failure supported innovation.

Financial performance improved between 2014 and 2016:
- Revenue increased from $89.0 billion to $136.0 billion.
- Net results improved from a $241 million loss to a $2.37 billion profit.
- Operating cash flow rose from $6.84 billion to $16.44 billion.
- In 2016, AWS generated $12.22 billion in sales and $3.11 billion in operating income, compared with retail’s $123.77 billion and $1.08 billion, respectively.

Amazon reported 2016 free cash flow of $9.71 billion. Alternative measures were lower after accounting for lease repayments or assets acquired under capital leases. Its stated financial objective remained sustainable long-term free cash flow growth through improved customer experience, operating performance, and capital management.

Enron replaced Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow with former treasurer Jeff McMahon on October 24, 2001, amid an informal Securities and Exchange Commission inquiry into partnerships Fastow managed while serving as CFO. Chief Executive Kenneth Lay said the change was needed to restore investor confidence, reversing his public support for Fastow the previous day. Fastow was placed on leave.

The partnerships raised conflict-of-interest concerns and were associated with a $35 million third-quarter loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. Reports said McMahon had previously objected to Fastow’s dual roles. Enron denied wrongdoing and maintained that its finances and operations remained sound.

Enron shares fell 17% to $16.41 on October 24, having lost roughly half their value since its October 16 earnings announcement. Other energy-trading stocks also declined. Analysts downgraded Enron and criticized its complex financing arrangements and inadequate disclosures. Investors worried about additional losses, off-balance-sheet obligations, potential credit-rating downgrades and dilution from new share issuance.

Several analysts welcomed the leadership change but said it would not resolve uncertainty without fuller financial disclosure. Shareholder lawsuits alleged misleading statements, overvalued assets, undisclosed obligations and insider trading; Enron declined to comment on pending litigation.

Temu resumed direct shipping from China after pausing over the summer amid changes to US tariffs. The de minimis exemption had allowed overseas packages worth under $800 to enter the US duty-free. When new rules took effect in May, Temu and Shein restricted US customers to products shipped from local warehouses to avoid unexpected fees.

After direct shipping resumed, the author ordered toys from Temu. The package arrived within two weeks, and no additional tariff fees appeared after a month, though product quality varied. Prices also increased after tariffs took effect; a summer research report found average price increases of around 30% on Shein.

An upbeat team meeting addressed game-plan adjustments. The team needs to improve its speed and skating while maintaining physical play. One player has kept them competitive despite subpar performances in the last two games. Success requires mental preparation, individual responsibility, intensity and emotion, supported by the home crowd.

Ethereum’s proposed enshrined Proposer–Builder Separation (ePBS) removes reliance on trusted relays and supports scaling through separate execution-payload and blob-delivery deadlines. However, it creates a “free option”: after committing to a block, builders can withhold blobs if late-arriving market information makes its trades unfavorable. The payload then fails to become canonical, leaving an empty slot. Builders still pay their bids but face no additional protocol penalty.

The study models this incentive and evaluates it using historical Ethereum data covering January 1, 2024, through March 8, 2025, including approximately 6.9 million CEX–DEX searcher transactions across 1.88 million blocks. Its theoretical analysis links option value and exercise incentives to liquidity, volatility, the option window’s length, and dependence on externally informed trading. Exploitation can distort DEX prices and cause liquidity-provider losses. PeerDAS could extend the effective option window by reducing last-minute data-propagation requirements.

With an assumed eight-second window, exercising the option would be profitable in 0.82% of observed blocks on average, with substantially higher rates during volatile periods. Builders whose revenue depends more heavily on CEX–DEX arbitrage show higher exercise probabilities. Under an assumption that non-CEX–DEX value carries into the next slot, accumulated MEV reduces incentives to exercise the option in consecutive slots.

The study evaluates two mitigation approaches:

- **Shorter windows:** Reducing the window from eight to four seconds cuts average exercise probability by over 50%; reducing it to two seconds cuts it by over 77%. Earlier deadlines, however, reduce ePBS’s scaling benefits.
- **Builder penalties:** A static penalty of 0.075 ETH reduces average exercise probability by roughly 75%. A dynamic mechanism that raises penalties after exercise and lowers them otherwise achieves a 0.096% average exercise probability with an average penalty of 0.104 ETH, compared with the 0.82% baseline. Penalties can increase builder entry barriers and discourage blob inclusion.

The empirical estimates have limitations: historical builders could not exploit this option and might change their trading behavior under ePBS; pricing assumptions introduce potentially opposing biases; and the dataset excludes some searchers, tokens, and cross-domain signals. The problem could also affect prediction markets and other applications where valuable information arrives between commitment and delivery deadlines.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2020 describes its business, strategy, operations, and principal risks. The company develops software, cloud services, devices, business solutions, and gaming products, and provides advertising, consulting, and support services.

Microsoft reports through three operating segments:
- **Productivity and Business Processes:** Office, Microsoft 365, LinkedIn, and Dynamics.
- **Intelligent Cloud:** Azure, server products, developer tools, GitHub, and enterprise services.
- **More Personal Computing:** Windows, Surface and PC accessories, Xbox gaming products and services, and search advertising.

Its strategic priorities are reinventing productivity and business processes, building intelligent cloud and edge platforms, and creating more personal computing experiences. Investments emphasize cloud infrastructure, artificial intelligence, collaboration, security, devices, and gaming. LinkedIn had over 700 million members, while Xbox Game Pass had over 10 million members across 41 countries.

COVID-19 prompted office closures, remote work, travel restrictions, and cancellation or conversion of marketing events to virtual formats through fiscal 2021. Microsoft reported substantial uncertainty about the pandemic’s continuing operational and economic effects.

The company announced a $1 billion investment over four years in climate technologies and solutions, targeting carbon negativity by 2030 and removal by 2050 of its historical direct and electricity-related carbon emissions. It also committed to expanding digital skills access and doubling specified categories of Black and African American managers and senior employees in the United States by 2025.

Microsoft distributes products through manufacturers, direct sales, distributors, and resellers. In June 2020, it announced plans to close its physical Microsoft Store locations. At June 30, 2020, it employed approximately 163,000 full-time workers, including 96,000 in the United States.

Principal risks include intense competition, uncertain returns on cloud infrastructure and product investments, acquisition integration difficulties, asset impairments, cyberattacks, security vulnerabilities, and personal-data disclosure or misuse. These risks could adversely affect revenue, margins, operations, and reputation.

Common stock held by non-affiliates had an aggregate market value of $1.2 trillion at December 31, 2019. Approximately 7.57 billion common shares were outstanding at July 27, 2020.

Donchian Channels, invented by Richard Donchian, use upper and lower bands representing the highest and lowest prices over a specified number of bars. Traditionally, traders use them to identify breakouts and follow trends.

The article finds them better suited to trend-following in commodities and currencies than in stocks, where reversing the approach into a mean-reversion strategy produced stronger results.

A long-only S&P 500 trend-following backtest from 1960 to October 2021 returned 4.57% annually versus 7.15% for buy-and-hold, excluding reinvested dividends, but had substantially lower maximum drawdown. A mean-reversion backtest on SPY from 1993 to October 2021 achieved its highest annual return, 9.16%, with a five-day lookback, approximately matching buy-and-hold while showing small drawdowns and a high win rate.

The article notes that faster, technology-driven markets have changed the indicator’s effectiveness. Donchian Channels and Bollinger Bands can look similar but may produce different backtest results.

Canadian lumber stocks fell after BMO downgraded West Fraser, Interfor and Canfor, citing U.S. duties, a stronger Canadian dollar and ongoing litigation. BMO said a near-term resolution to the lumber dispute was unlikely, while its analysts viewed stock prospects more positively over three to five years.

An October 23, 2001 compilation of news reports details Enron’s financial difficulties, investor concerns, management practices and disputes in India.

- A securities class action accused Enron and certain executives of misleading investors about broadband demand, investment losses and impaired assets. It covered stock purchases from January 18, 2000, through October 17, 2001.
- Enron reported a $638 million third-quarter loss after $1.01 billion in charges. Unwinding arrangements involving partnerships managed by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow also reduced shareholder equity by $1.2 billion.
- The Securities and Exchange Commission requested information about related-party transactions. Enron described the request as an informal inquiry and pledged cooperation.
- Shares closed at $19.79 on October 23, down 76 percent for the year. Many brokerage analysts retained favorable ratings despite investors’ concerns about disclosure and management credibility.
- Bloomberg reported that Enron sought a $750 million loan arranged by Citigroup. Moody’s placed $13 billion in long-term debt under review for a possible downgrade, while Enron executives said available bank credit was sufficient for normal operations.
- An investor conference call left questions about off-balance-sheet financing, asset values and repayment obligations unresolved.
- A Texas Monthly profile traced Enron’s transformation into an energy-trading company under Kenneth Lay and Jeffrey Skilling. It described aggressive recruitment, performance rankings, incentives for short-term profits, extensive mark-to-market accounting and setbacks in broadband, water and overseas power investments. Skilling resigned after six months as CEO; Lay returned and promised greater transparency and a renewed focus on core businesses.
- AES sought Indian Prime Minister Atal Bihari Vajpayee’s intervention over alleged government interference and contract violations in Orissa. Enron separately threatened legal action involving claims of up to $5 billion over its Dabhol power-project dispute and was withdrawing from the project.

Other business briefs covered the WTO’s planned Qatar conference, declining 3M profits and copper prices, and corporate restructuring.

Hungary’s education system is shaped by its demographics, government, economy, and teacher preparation practices. Schooling includes pre-primary, primary, secondary, and post-secondary education. Families can choose schools, but admissions are selective, and secondary education involves entrance examinations, community service, and school-leaving examinations that influence higher education opportunities.

Hungary established its special education system in 1802 and a special education teacher-training college in 1906. Legislation provides educational rights and financial support for individuals with disabilities. Professional committees assess disabilities and recommend placements and services, while parents make final placement decisions. Available supports include early intervention, counseling, speech therapy, and specialized instruction.

In 2019, Hungary had more than 88,000 students with special educational needs, with 60% educated in inclusive environments. The country seeks greater inclusion, but specialized schools remain important, particularly for students requiring accessible facilities and specialized instruction. General education teachers typically receive little preparation for teaching students with disabilities, although the passage describes an inclusive school using trained staff, collaboration, and classroom-based special education support.

Special education teachers complete a four-year university program and specialize in one or two of eight disability-related areas. Their initial two-year traineeship includes evaluation and a written portfolio. Continuing professional training remains part of their careers.

Major challenges include difficulties diagnosing autism and distinguishing learning disabilities from learning difficulties, inaccessible school buildings, limited inclusion, insufficient teacher preparation, low salaries, and teacher attrition. The authors recommend school referral systems, more diagnostic training, improved physical accessibility, stronger preparation in inclusive teaching and collaboration, higher wages, and retention incentives. They also suggest examining church-run teacher education institutions, which show comparatively higher teacher retention.

Nvidia and Micron rallied after recent market declines, but their technical outlooks differ. Nvidia exceeded earnings expectations and rebounded from its rising 50-day trendline, which the passage views as supportive of further gains. Micron remains below its 50-day moving average, now showing a bearish pattern. Its rebound follows an oversold RSI reading, but the passage warns that resistance at $84 could reverse the rally.

President Donald Trump suggested some furloughed federal workers might not receive back pay during the government shutdown, saying it “depends on who we’re talking about.” A draft White House memo argued that retroactive pay is not guaranteed, despite recent administration guidance and a 2019 law stating furloughed employees shall be paid. A White House official said Congress must specifically appropriate the funds.

The administration’s position has been widely viewed as pressure on Senate Democrats to support Republicans’ temporary funding proposal. Trump also warned of substantial permanent layoffs if the shutdown continues.

Democrats want a funding agreement to extend enhanced Affordable Care Act premium tax credits. Republicans need at least seven additional Senate votes to overcome a filibuster.

The American Federation of Government Employees condemned the back-pay argument as a misinterpretation of the law and urged Congress to end the shutdown.

An Enron-forwarded collection of February 23, 2001 news reports covers California’s electricity crisis, utility rescue negotiations, rising public costs and political disputes.

- Gov. Gray Davis announced a tentative agreement to buy Southern California Edison’s transmission lines for approximately $2.7 billion. The framework included low-cost electricity commitments, payments from Edison’s parent company and withdrawal of a lawsuit challenging rate caps. Davis said the transaction would not require higher consumer rates. Negotiations with PG&E and Sempra continued, with significant differences remaining with PG&E.
- The state sought to purchase 26,000 miles of transmission lines to help utilities address nearly $13 billion in reported losses. Some utility executives considered bankruptcy an alternative, while critics questioned the purchase price and growing state control.
- California’s electricity purchases could exceed $3 billion by mid-March, raising concerns about funding other state programs. Disputes persisted over utility reimbursements, customer revenues and responsibility for costs exceeding those revenues.
- Long-term power contracts progressed slowly because suppliers wanted assurance that utilities would repay existing debts. Williams signed a 10-year supply agreement.
- Small electricity producers supported legislation expected to reduce average contract prices from approximately 17 cents to 8–8.5 cents per kilowatt-hour, potentially saving billions while providing five-year price stability.
- California lifted all power alerts on February 22 for the first time since January 13. Improved supplies, milder weather and more advance purchasing helped, but officials urged continued conservation and warned of summer shortages.
- Republicans sought to challenge Davis over the crisis but faced difficulties developing alternatives and addressing their support for deregulation. Other reports examined Davis’ missed deadlines, returned utility campaign donations and proposed discounts for residents near power plants.
- La Cresta residents opposed transmission lines associated with Enron’s proposed $450 million Lake Elsinore hydroelectric project. Routing, financing and construction arrangements remained unsettled.

Select Security acquired Charlotte-based Intelligent Technology Inc. and Carolina Security Group, adding nearly 1,000 customers, account executives and technicians. The acquisition also provides a downtown Charlotte branch location where the company will consolidate its western North Carolina operations.

Newcastle University scientists have 3D printed human corneas using a bio-ink combining donor corneal stem cells, alginate and collagen. A low-cost printer produced the corneal shape in under 10 minutes, and the stem cells subsequently grew. Researchers also demonstrated that eye scans could guide printing to match a patient’s corneal size and shape. The technique could help address the worldwide shortage of transplant corneas, but further testing is required, and use in transplants remains several years away.

A water advisory near Galveston Beach’s 57th Street was lifted Friday after samples tested clear. Health officials say rain runoff can carry feces-associated bacteria into coastal waters, potentially causing illness. Galveston County regularly tests 52 locations. Beachgoers should avoid water under advisory and check conditions at TexasBeachWatch.com or GCHD.org.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examines microtubule (MT) regulation and treatment resistance in prostate cancer, proposing computational imaging of patient-derived cells to help select therapies. Treatment options for metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer remain limited, and reliable markers predicting taxane efficacy are lacking.

The computational approach tracks fluorescent EB1 or EB3 markers at growing MT tips in live-cell microscopy images. Tracking and clustering algorithms measure polymerization and infer periods of pausing and shortening. In M12 prostate cancer cells, average MT growth speeds were 17.3 µm/min without androgen receptor (AR), 16.2 µm/min with wild-type AR, and 24.6 µm/min with the taxane-resistance-associated ARv7 variant. ARv7-expressing cells also lacked the slowdown in MT growth observed near cell edges in wild-type AR cells.

Organoids were derived from primary and metastatic tissues from 16 prostate cancer patients. Establishing tumor cultures was complicated by normal epithelial cells overgrowing tumor cells. Reducing the ROCK inhibitor Y-27632 concentration fourfold temporarily favored high-grade tumor cells. The passage also reports small, PSMA-positive circulating tumor cells in advanced disease that could be missed by detection methods emphasizing large cells, while acknowledging that these observations were not statistically representative.

Experiments implicate pVHL and GSK3β in MT regulation. Restoring pVHL reduced MT growth rates, while GSK3β-mediated phosphorylation impaired its MT-stabilizing functions during serum starvation. GSK3 inhibition reduced MT turnover in quiescent cells. The passage associates both unusually fast and unusually slow MT turnover with drug resistance and discusses contributions from Op18, ERG, and MT modifications.

Drug-response imaging provided additional resistance measures. Paclitaxel reduced MT growth rates in breast cancer cells. In A549 cells, circular MT bundles formed in 83% of parental cells but only 27% of BRCA1-knockdown cells after treatment; bundles were also brighter in parental cells. Circular Hough-transform analysis quantified these differences.

Proposed next steps include correlating organoid MT dynamics with gene expression and clinical outcomes, testing candidate regulators in xenografts, and evaluating drug effects in tissue cultures. Potential strategies discussed include GSK3 inhibition, GPX4 inhibition to target drug-tolerant persister cells, endogenous compounds such as NAD+, and tumor–immune-cell screening. These approaches are presented as avenues for investigation rather than established clinical solutions. The passage emphasizes that dose-dependent effects on MT dynamics are nonlinear and that quantitative imaging may support drug development, resistance assessment, and individualized regimen selection.

Japan’s economy grew at an annualised rate of 4% in April–June, exceeding expectations of 2.5%. Consumer spending and capital investment supported growth, with strong domestic demand offsetting falling exports. The country is experiencing its longest economic expansion in a decade.

A 70-mile-wide radar mass over Colorado was identified as migrating Painted Lady butterflies after National Weather Service scientists initially mistook it for birds. Public responses helped identify the insects, which have appeared in clouds around Denver. Forecasters say radar detection of flying insects is uncommon.

The passage identifies archival, published, and online sources documenting foreign policy. The Library of Congress holds Alexander Haig’s papers on his worldview and Donald Regan’s papers on administration planning and Executive-Legislative relations. Other repositories include the Department of State, Reagan Presidential Library, National Security Council, and Washington National Records Center. The Office of the Historian maintains an online resource list.

Source notes document Reagan’s 1980 campaign statements and speeches in Florence, Worcester, Chicago, Los Angeles, and Arlington, alongside George Bush’s September address in San Francisco. They provide archival locations, event details, and related press coverage concerning military strength, China and Taiwan, peace, and arms control.

Speaking at the University of Virginia, President Ronald Reagan honors Thomas Jefferson’s contributions to education, religious freedom, and self-government. He connects Jefferson’s emphasis on reason, tolerance, and balanced government to contemporary democratic movements and argues that political and economic freedom are inseparable.

Reagan describes advances in U.S.-Soviet relations, including the INF treaty’s elimination of an entire class of nuclear missiles, negotiations over strategic weapons reductions, increased exchanges, and improvements in Soviet human rights. He also cites progress toward resolving conflicts in Afghanistan, Cambodia, and Angola, and the PLO’s acceptance of conditions for dialogue with the United States. He attributes these developments partly to democratic nations’ renewed confidence, military strength, and resolve.

He offers three cautions for sustaining progress:
- Improved Soviet-American relations remain uncertain and require verification, strong defenses, and candor about fundamental differences.
- Soviet reforms were not inevitable; Gorbachev’s decisions and Western actions helped bring them about.
- Effective foreign policy requires cooperation between Congress and the President while respecting their separate constitutional responsibilities.

Reagan criticizes congressional restrictions that he believes undermine executive flexibility. He concludes by presenting Jefferson and John Adams’s reconciliation as a lesson in tolerance and common purpose.

During questions, Reagan says assistance to Soviet democratization should depend on whether actions match promises. He emphasizes that Middle East peace requires negotiations among the parties, defends his administration’s resistance to terrorism, and urges young people to register and vote.

Discussing his administration’s achievements, he highlights restored military strength, renewed national pride, and economic recovery, which he credits to tax cuts and deregulation. He cites nearly 19 million new jobs and increased tax revenues, while arguing that spending growth remains a problem. After leaving office, he plans to advocate a balanced budget amendment, a line-item veto, and strong defenses, and may write a book.

The ICRC launched “Pehlay Zindagi: Give Way to Ambulances—Give Way to Life,” a nationwide campaign in Pakistan encouraging motorists to give ambulances priority. Supported by over 30 partner organizations, it will run until December 2017, using media outreach, awareness activities and public pledges. Part of the global Health Care in Danger project, it also highlights challenges faced by ambulance staff. Observational studies will assess changes in motorists’ behaviour. The initiative follows the 2016 “Rasta Dein” campaign.

Rain delayed Mariners–Tigers ALDS Game 3 in Detroit, with the series tied 1-1. Originally scheduled for 4:08 p.m. ET, first pitch is now expected at 7 p.m. ET, according to the Tigers. The game moved to FS2 because of overlap with Blue Jays–Yankees Game 3 and will also air on MLB Network and the Fox One App.

A study across seven acute care trusts in Greater Manchester developed a reproducible method for selecting AI-detected chest X-ray abnormalities for urgent reporting to support lung cancer diagnosis. It compared 1,282 X-rays from patients with confirmed lung cancer against 13,802 primary care X-rays. The Annalise AI system assessed 124 findings, operating in shadow mode during prospective data collection without influencing patient care.

Researchers combined findings’ relative prevalence with clinical judgement to evaluate three prioritisation strategies:
- Selecting 19 findings with the highest prevalence ratios achieved 92.82% sensitivity and 87.21% specificity.
- Selecting 41 high-priority findings increased sensitivity to 97.27% but reduced specificity to 62.68%.
- A clinically reviewed selection of 32 findings achieved 95.87% sensitivity, 79.11% specificity, 99.95% negative predictive value and 4.43% positive predictive value.

The clinically reviewed strategy identified 1,229 of 1,282 cancer cases, balancing sensitivity and specificity. An Excel-based tool supported comparison and refinement of finding combinations.

Performance estimates were indicative rather than definitive: the referral cohort used an assumed 1% detectable cancer prevalence rather than individual diagnostic verification, and development and testing used populations from the same region. External validation and prospective implementation studies are needed to assess generalisability, reporting workflows and effects on patients whose X-rays are not prioritised.

Bridgeton National Bank sued Hepner to recover on a $1,400 renewal promissory note. Hepner alleged that Kil-Tone Company obtained the original note through fraudulent stock representations and promised not to negotiate it unless the stock was resold profitably for him. He sought to attribute knowledge of the alleged fraud to the bank through its cashier, who also served as Kil-Tone’s treasurer and allegedly participated in the fraud. The trial court excluded this evidence and directed a verdict for the bank. Applying New Jersey precedent limiting when an agent’s knowledge is chargeable to a principal, the reviewing court upheld the exclusion and discharged the rule seeking a new trial.

The Non-Farm Payrolls (NFP) report, published by the US Bureau of Labor Statistics, measures monthly changes in employment across non-agricultural businesses. Usually released on the first Friday of each month at 8:30 a.m. Eastern time, it is an indicator of US economic health and influences expectations for Federal Reserve interest-rate decisions.

NFP releases can trigger substantial volatility across bonds, stocks, currencies, and commodities. Traders compare reported figures with the previous month and market expectations, while also considering unemployment, hourly earnings, hours worked, and revisions.

Stronger-than-expected employment generally supports the US dollar and stock-market sentiment but can depress bond prices by increasing expectations of higher interest rates and inflation. Weaker results generally have the opposite effects. The report also affects gold prices and demand for energy.

The passage presents backtests of SPY, which tracks the S&P 500, and TLT. On NFP release days, SPY averaged a 0.09% gain from market open to close, while TLT averaged a 0.02% loss. Subsequent-day tests showed weak performance for both, with SPY averaging a 0.04% loss when exiting five trading days later.

The authors conclude that these backtests do not establish a clear NFP trading strategy and report finding no trading edge from macroeconomic releases.

Rite-Hite’s Uni-Dox Inflatable Shelter accommodates varied truck and trailer configurations. It inflates around docked trailers and manually deflates before departure, using counterweight retraction and non-inflatable draft pads to reduce damage risks. Optional controls provide feedback, while the PitMaster Under-leveler Seal helps block debris and pests.

Lower global and US interest rates could support a housing-sector rebound over the next one to four years. Homebuilding and home improvement stocks historically outperformed SPY during falling-rate periods, except during the subprime crisis. Lumber and wooden-goods tariffs favor domestic manufacturers, though trade deals could alter this advantage. Loose lending poses risks, but leverage appears lower than in 2007. The author favors a diversified approach to housing-related stocks while noting technology’s extended valuations.

The lecture explores how adjacency-matrix eigenvalues measure graph pseudorandomness. An \((n,d,\lambda)\)-graph is a \(d\)-regular graph on \(n\) vertices whose eigenvalues other than the top eigenvalue \(d\) have absolute value at most \(\lambda\). The expander mixing lemma bounds edge-count discrepancies using \(\lambda\), so smaller values indicate stronger pseudorandomness.

Cayley graphs provide deterministic constructions from groups and symmetric subsets. Paley graphs are examples built on integers modulo a prime \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), using nonzero quadratic residues. Their eigenvectors are explicitly described using roots of unity, and Gauss-sum calculations show that their nontrivial eigenvalues are small compared with their degree. For Abelian Cayley graphs, this spectral description corresponds to Fourier coefficients; representation theory provides the broader connection for non-Abelian groups.

A theorem of Conlon and Zhao establishes that discrepancy and eigenvalue conditions are equivalent up to a constant factor for all Cayley graphs, including sparse and non-Abelian examples. Specifically, \(\mathrm{EIG}(\epsilon)\) implies \(\mathrm{DISC}(\epsilon)\), while \(\mathrm{DISC}(\epsilon)\) implies \(\mathrm{EIG}(8\epsilon)\). The reverse implication fails for general regular graphs: adding a small disjoint complete graph can preserve discrepancy while producing a second eigenvalue equal to \(d\).

The Cayley-graph proof combines group symmetries with Grothendieck’s inequality. This inequality bounds a vector-valued relaxation of a sign-valued bilinear optimization problem by a universal constant factor. Its semidefinite formulation also permits efficient constant-factor approximation.

The lecture then addresses the limits of pseudorandomness. For fixed degree \(d\), the Alon–Boppana bound states that the second-largest eigenvalue is at least
\[
2\sqrt{d-1}-o(1)
\]
as the number of vertices grows. One proof constructs weighted vectors around two distant vertices and combines them into a vector orthogonal to the all-ones vector. A second, slightly weaker proof bounds the second-largest absolute eigenvalue through traces of even matrix powers, closed-walk counts, and Catalan numbers. The threshold \(2\sqrt{d-1}\) is the spectral radius of the infinite \(d\)-regular tree.

The speaker ranks Bird’s Celtics and Magic’s Lakers above Jordan’s Bulls, recalls discovering hockey in Birmingham and attending Flyers games, and names Ron Hextall as his favorite hockey player because of his determination to win. He praises the excitement of the NHL playoffs, especially overtime, while criticizing the NBA playoffs’ lack of close games. Using Kevin Durant and his own experience in Phoenix as examples, he argues that strong teammates ease great players’ responsibilities. He particularly admires teams that win multiple championships, emphasizing how difficult sustained winning is.

The Appellate Division reversed Solomon Montlake’s first-degree grand larceny conviction and granted a new trial because the jury received erroneous instructions on his alibi defense.

The court rejected Montlake’s former-jeopardy claim arising from an earlier trial’s termination. Before a case is submitted to the jury, a judge may discharge it for a substantial reason in the interests of justice. Here, the prosecutor’s repeated accusations that defense counsel was a criminal justified discharge. The court also regarded the discharge as effectively granting defense counsel’s earlier request.

The court criticized cross-examination of an alibi witness about unpaid rent, finding that an unrelated unpaid debt did not tend to show moral turpitude. It did not regard that ruling alone as warranting reversal.

The decisive error was instructing jurors that the alibi evidence had to establish that the defendants could not have been at the crime scene. This improperly required exclusion of even the possibility of their presence. The defendant bore no burden to prove an alibi; acquittal was required if the alibi evidence, considered with all other evidence, raised a reasonable doubt about his presence. General instructions on the prosecution’s burden of proof did not cure the specific error.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal first quarter ended December 31, 2022, reported net sales of $117.2 billion, down 5% from $123.9 billion a year earlier. Apple attributed the decline to weakness in foreign currencies relative to the U.S. dollar. The quarter included an additional week compared with the prior-year period.

- **Profitability:** Net income declined to $30.0 billion from $34.6 billion, and diluted earnings per share fell to $1.88 from $2.10. Operating income decreased to $36.0 billion from $41.5 billion. Gross margin was 43.0%, compared with 43.8%.
- **Products and services:** iPhone sales fell 8% to $65.8 billion; Mac sales fell 29% to $7.7 billion; and Wearables, Home and Accessories sales fell 8% to $13.5 billion. iPad sales increased 30% to $9.4 billion, while Services sales increased 6% to $20.8 billion.
- **Geographic performance:** Sales declined across all reportable segments: Americas, Europe, Greater China, Japan and Rest of Asia Pacific.
- **Operating conditions:** COVID-related disruptions significantly reduced capacity at the primary iPhone 14 Pro and Pro Max assembly facility in Zhengzhou, China, affecting shipments. Apple also cited impacts from inflation, rising interest rates and currency fluctuations.
- **Expenses:** Operating expenses increased to $14.3 billion from $12.8 billion. Research and development expenses reached $7.7 billion, with growth driven primarily by headcount-related expenses.
- **Financial position:** Total assets were $346.7 billion, liabilities were $290.0 billion and shareholders’ equity was $56.7 billion. Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $165.5 billion. Outstanding term debt had a carrying amount of $109.4 billion, and commercial paper totaled $1.7 billion.
- **Cash flow and shareholder returns:** Operating cash flow was $34.0 billion, compared with $47.0 billion a year earlier. Apple repurchased 133 million shares for $19.0 billion and paid $3.8 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents.
- **Commitments and disclosures:** Manufacturing purchase obligations totaled $55.1 billion, including $54.8 billion payable within 12 months. Apple considered its liquidity sufficient for cash requirements and capital returns. Disclosure controls were deemed effective, and no material changes in risk factors were reported. Appeals remained pending in the Epic Games litigation, with the injunction stayed pending appeal.

VentureWire’s May 16, 2001 newsletter reports venture financing, acquisitions, layoffs, business closures, product launches, and leadership changes.

- **Top stories:** Buzzsaw.com laid off 70 employees, or 30% of its workforce, and expected to close a $20 million financing round at a lower valuation. UGO Networks acquired rival Bla-Bla.com for an undisclosed amount. EYP Mission Critical Facilities raised $57.5 million, partly to finance its separation from Einhorn Yaffee Prescott. Flatiron Partners planned to move into J.P. Morgan Chase’s offices to reduce rental costs.
- **Financing:** DigiPlex secured $48 million in equity and drew $35 million in debt. STSN raised $66.5 million in debt and equity. Creditek received $30 million from General Atlantic Partners. Other funding included $12.4 million for VDSL Systems, $12.2 million for LifeClips, $11.2 million for Opsys, and $5.8 million for KeepSmart. Viator expected to close a $5 million–$10 million round.
- **Financial difficulties:** WorkingWoman.com cut approximately 63% of its staff and sought buyers or additional funding. Metiom filed for Chapter 11 after investors declined to provide the remaining funding from an announced round. Mybiz.com shut down after failing to secure financing or an acquisition. OnSite Access laid off roughly two-thirds of its staff, while Eyecast cut about half. eLedger planned to discontinue its hosted accounting service on May 31.
- **Acquisitions:** Motient agreed to acquire Rare Medium in a cash-and-stock transaction. Parthus acquired Chicory Systems for $41.4 million. XCare.net agreed to acquire Confer Software, Escalate acquired Managize’s core technology and assets, and Qiva expected to acquire Capstan Systems. BrainHeart purchased bankrupt Linq’s mobile Internet division, and EMS Technologies acquired CI Wireless.
- **Launches and management:** KPE launched a television division; Model N introduced private business network software; DataPower launched its XML networking business; and Christianity.com changed its name to Starwire. Guru, Cognitive Arts, Mimeo, and Callbutton announced new chief executives.
- **Venture funds:** Invesco closed its $150 million EuroMedia fund as part of a $530 million capital pool. Schneider Electric launched a $44 million venture fund. Axiomlab raised $17.1 million, Friends Ivory & Sime closed a $61 million investment trust, and CalPERS committed $10 million to Silicon Valley Community Ventures’ second fund. According to a source, PSINet Ventures stopped making new investments and focused on managing and liquidating its portfolio after staffing fell to three employees.

One police officer and two gunmen were killed, and eight officers wounded, when Barrio 18 gang members attacked police searching for illegal weapons in San Salvador. One slain gunman was identified as a gang leader suspected of involvement in more than a dozen murders. The wounded officers suffered superficial bullet wounds; four were released, and four were expected to leave hospital within a week.

Japan’s government upgraded its assessment of business sentiment in April for the first time in four months, following improved corporate confidence in the Bank of Japan’s tankan survey. Its overall assessment remained unchanged: the economy is recovering gradually despite pockets of weakness. Stronger global demand supported exports and factory output, while overseas uncertainty and financial-market fluctuations remained concerns.

The October 12, 2000 Haas alumni jobs bulletin lists 20 recruitment postings covering executive leadership, product management, finance, business development, strategy, fundraising, compliance, and supply-chain planning. Locations include California, New York/New Jersey, Denver, South Florida, Reno, and Las Vegas. Many positions require or prefer an MBA.

Featured opportunities include:
- President/CEO of a Berkeley wireless/broadband video startup.
- Product management positions at Vividence.
- Business development and partnership roles at CommerceRoute, BeVocal, Nuance Communications, and a cable network.
- Director of the Haas School Fund and Reunion Giving.
- Banking, equity research, venture lending, financial planning, and portfolio management positions.
- Strategy and market intelligence leadership at a healthcare company.
- Supply-chain analysis and planning roles at Office Depot.
- Financial consultant positions at Merrill Lynch.

Gap Inc. announces an October 18 career fair at San Francisco’s Hotel Nikko, from 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. The bulletin also promotes Haas Homecoming and Reunion Weekend on October 14.

Expanded postings provide responsibilities, qualifications, and application contacts. Employers may submit openings to recruitalumni@haas.berkeley.edu; alumni seeking career assistance may contact morel@haas.berkeley.edu. The bulletin is restricted to Haas alumni and supported partly by the Haas School Annual Fund. Haas states that it has not researched the listed employers or search firms and advises readers to check them independently.

Comcast abandoned its pursuit of most Twenty-First Century Fox assets, citing insufficient engagement to make a definitive offer. Disney remains the sole suitor for the $40 billion-plus deal. Sources said negotiations continued and an agreement could come this month. Comcast and Disney shares rose after hours; Fox shares fell.
A 26-year-old Aroland man was charged with assault with a weapon after an injured 30-year-old man found on Aroland First Nation died in hospital. Police continue investigating.

A study of U.S. death certificate data from 1999–2020 compared mortality among non-Hispanic Black and White people younger than 85. It estimated 658,356 excess deaths among Black females and 1,154,108 among Black males, alongside approximately 35 million and 47 million excess years of potential life lost (YPLL), respectively.

Mortality disparities initially declined, then plateaued before increasing sharply in 2020, coinciding with the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic. Among Black males, age-adjusted excess mortality fell from 404 deaths per 100,000 people in 1999 to 211 in 2011, then reached 395 in 2020. Among Black females, it declined from 224 in 1999 to 87 in 2015 before rising to 192 in 2020. Excess YPLL followed similar patterns.

Heart disease accounted for the highest excess mortality rates, while perinatal deaths contributed the highest cause-specific YPLL rates. Infants had the greatest Black–White differences in YPLL, with mortality and YPLL rate ratios exceeding 2.3. Disparities generally increased again after childhood.

The authors propose publicly reporting excess deaths and YPLL as measures of health equity and national accountability. They identify social determinants, access to care, structural barriers, and bias as potential contributors requiring further investigation. Limitations include possible inaccuracies in death certificate race, ethnicity, and cause-of-death information. The findings indicate persistent disparities and the need for new strategies to address them.

U.S. colleges are preparing for demonstrations marking the second anniversary of Hamas’s Oct. 7, 2023, attacks. Columbia required advance protest plans, while the University of Maryland restricted campus access. Maryland’s Students for Justice in Palestine planned solidarity events, including a teach-in and sit-in. Demonstrations are planned at other institutions nationwide.

Thirty-seven Cadwalader lawyers, including 10 incoming partners, are joining Orrick, bringing expertise in collateralized loan obligations and asset-backed lending. They will work in Charlotte, London, Washington, D.C., and New York. Bloomberg Law reported that Cadwalader has lost nearly a fifth of its partnership this year despite new hires. Its revenue ranking fell from No. 39 in 2007 to No. 85 in 2024, though profits per equity partner averaged $3.7 million in 2024. The firm has added a second managing partner and is hiring to strengthen core practices.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 28, 2018 reported:

- **Quarterly results:** Revenue increased 21% year over year to $3.181 billion. Operating income rose 18% to $1.058 billion, net income increased 47% to $1.230 billion, and diluted earnings per share rose to $1.97 from $1.33.
- **Business performance:** GPU revenue increased 25% to $2.774 billion, while Tegra Processor revenue declined 3% to $407 million. Gaming revenue reached $1.764 billion, datacenter $792 million, professional visualization $305 million, and automotive $172 million. OEM and IP revenue declined 23% to $148 million due to the absence of cryptocurrency mining revenue.
- **Margins and expenses:** Gross margin increased to 60.4% from 59.5% a year earlier, despite $57 million in charges related to prior-generation components and chips following reduced cryptocurrency mining demand. Operating expenses increased 28% to $863 million, primarily reflecting increased headcount and related costs.
- **Taxes:** NVIDIA recognized a quarterly income tax benefit of $149 million. The lower effective tax rate primarily reflected U.S. tax reform and a $138 million reduction in its provisional transition tax amount.
- **Nine-month results:** Revenue totaled $9.511 billion, compared with $6.803 billion a year earlier. Net income was $3.575 billion, compared with $1.928 billion. Operating cash flow increased to $2.845 billion from $2.144 billion.
- **Financial position:** Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $7.591 billion. Inventories increased to $1.417 billion from $796 million at January 28, 2018. Total assets were $13.657 billion, liabilities $4.182 billion, and shareholders’ equity $9.475 billion.
- **Shareholder returns:** During the first nine months, NVIDIA repurchased $855 million of shares and paid $273 million in dividends. In November, it authorized an additional $7 billion in share repurchases and increased its quarterly dividend to $0.16 per share.
