DDR2/DDR3 memory controller terminal descriptions cover data strobes, byte mappings, on-die termination, supply voltages, and reset pull states. Data strobes synchronize transfers for each byte of the 32-bit bus, acting as outputs during writes and inputs during reads. DDR[0] includes complementary strobes and on-die termination for chip selects 0 and 1. Listed internal pullups and pulldowns are generally enabled during reset and disabled afterward; some DDR[1] pins switch from pullup to pulldown when reset is released.

President Trump urged world leaders to prioritize national sovereignty, patriotism, and their citizens’ interests over globalism. He presented his administration’s economic, military, and trade policies as efforts to renew American strength, citing employment gains, energy production, tax and regulatory cuts, and increased defense spending.

Trump advocated fair, reciprocal trade and discussed agreements with Mexico, Canada, Japan, and the United Kingdom. He accused China of unfair economic practices, defended tariffs on Chinese goods, called for World Trade Organization reform, and urged China to honor commitments protecting Hong Kong’s freedoms.

On security, Trump defended withdrawing from the Iran nuclear deal and imposing sanctions, saying pressure would continue unless Iran changed its behavior. He supported normalized relations between Israel and its neighbors, called for North Korean denuclearization, and pledged continued counterterrorism efforts and pursuit of peace in Afghanistan.

He emphasized border enforcement and regional cooperation against illegal immigration, human smuggling, and trafficking. He condemned the governments of Cuba, Nicaragua, and Venezuela, supported restoring democracy in Venezuela, and rejected socialism and communism.

Trump also advocated screening foreign technology and investments, protecting free speech against social media restrictions, ending criminal penalties for homosexuality, advancing women’s economic opportunities, and defending religious freedom. He opposed efforts to establish a global right to taxpayer-funded abortion and rejected ratification of the U.N. Arms Trade Treaty, citing constitutional gun rights.

He concluded that strong, independent nations rooted in their histories and cultures provide the foundation for liberty, cooperation, peace, and prosperity.

A majority of Supreme Court justices appeared skeptical of Colorado’s ban on conversion therapy for minors, suggesting it discriminates against counselor Kaley Chiles based on her viewpoints. Several justices raised the possibility of returning the case to lower courts for closer constitutional review rather than immediately striking down the law.

Colorado argues that the 2019 law regulates a harmful medical treatment, not speech. Chiles contends it restricts her ability to help clients pursue goals involving sexual orientation or gender identity. Lower courts denied her request to temporarily block enforcement, treating the ban as a regulation of conduct subject to rational basis review.

Chiles’ lawyer and the Trump administration urged the Supreme Court to invalidate the law. Arguments also addressed whether Chiles has standing given Colorado’s stated intention not to enforce the ban against her, whether talk therapy warrants constitutional protection distinct from other treatments, and whether lower courts should first apply stricter review.

Apple’s fiscal 2019 Form 10-K reports net sales of $260.2 billion, down 2% from 2018, primarily because of lower iPhone sales. Net income was $55.3 billion, compared with $59.5 billion in 2018, and diluted earnings per share were $11.89 versus $11.91. Weak foreign currencies significantly reduced net sales.

Sales by product and service category were:
- iPhone: $142.4 billion, down 14%.
- Mac: $25.7 billion, up 2%.
- iPad: $21.3 billion, up 16%.
- Wearables, Home and Accessories: $24.5 billion, up 41%.
- Services: $46.3 billion, up 16%.

Higher AirPods and Apple Watch sales drove growth in Wearables, Home and Accessories. Services growth primarily reflected higher sales from the App Store, licensing and AppleCare.

Geographically, sales increased 4% in the Americas and 2% in the Rest of Asia Pacific, while declining 3% in Europe, 16% in Greater China and 1% in Japan. Total gross margin fell to 37.8% from 38.3%. Products gross margin declined to 32.2%, while Services gross margin increased to 63.7%.

Apple repurchased $67.1 billion of common stock and paid $14.1 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during 2019. Its share repurchase authorization increased from $100 billion to $175 billion, and its quarterly dividend rose from $0.73 to $0.77 per share. Year-end cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $205.9 billion; total assets were $338.5 billion.

Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, computers, tablets, wearables and accessories, alongside digital content, cloud, support, licensing and payment services. It introduced the iPhone 11 lineup and Apple Watch Series 5 in September 2019. The company had approximately 137,000 full-time equivalent employees. Direct distribution generated 31% of sales and indirect channels 69%; no customer accounted for more than 10% of sales.

The report identifies risks involving economic conditions, intense competition, rapid technological change, product transitions, supplier concentration, outsourced manufacturing, product defects, third-party content and software, intellectual property disputes, regulation, cybersecurity, privacy, personnel retention, trade disputes, business interruptions, currency movements, credit exposure and taxation. Substantially all hardware manufacturing was outsourced, primarily to partners in Asia. Apple cautions that historical results and forward-looking statements do not guarantee future performance.

The speaker recalls disappointment at losing in the finals but happiness for his brother. Playing together has been enjoyable, though family time matters more. He credits his line’s trust to staying together all year and emphasizes both goalies’ strong play in reaching the series.

The lecture reviews the Weierstrass M-test, which establishes uniform convergence of a series of functions when its terms are bounded in absolute value by a summable sequence of nonnegative constants. Together with the preservation of continuity under uniform limits, it shows that a uniformly convergent series of continuous functions defines a continuous function.

For a power series centered at \(x_0\) with positive radius of convergence \(\rho\), the M-test proves uniform convergence on every interval \([x_0-R,x_0+R]\) with \(0<R<\rho\). Within the radius of convergence, the series can be integrated and differentiated term by term. The differentiated power series has the same radius of convergence, allowing repeated differentiation. Consequently, if the series represents \(f\), its coefficients satisfy \(f^{(k)}(x_0)=k!a_k\), identifying it as the Taylor series of \(f\).

The lecture then proves the Weierstrass approximation theorem: every continuous function on \([0,1]\) is the uniform limit of a sequence of polynomials. Subtracting a linear function reduces the proof to functions vanishing at both endpoints, which can be extended continuously by zero outside the interval.

The construction uses normalized polynomials
\[
q_n(t)=c_n(1-t^2)^n,\qquad
c_n=\left(\int_{-1}^{1}(1-t^2)^n\,dt\right)^{-1}.
\]
On \([-1,1]\), these polynomials are nonnegative, integrate to one, and converge uniformly to zero away from the origin. The estimate \(c_n<\sqrt n\) establishes this concentration.

The approximating polynomials are
\[
p_n(x)=\int_0^1 f(t)q_n(t-x)\,dt.
\]
Their polynomial character follows by expanding the integrand. To prove uniform convergence to \(f\), the error integral is divided into a neighborhood of zero and its complement. Uniform continuity controls the first part; boundedness of \(f\) and the decay of \(q_n\) control the second. Together, these estimates make the error uniformly arbitrarily small.

Dr. Pasvolsky considered respect for international obligations inherent in the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals but suggested discussing explicit inclusion. Honduras supported a treaty-respect provision, while Chile questioned whether international law already encompassed that principle.

Discussing Security Council composition, Pasvolsky emphasized efficiency, effectiveness, and representation. He linked permanent membership to responsibilities and the five designated countries’ military and industrial power. Nonpermanent members should outnumber permanent members to prevent decisions based solely on permanent members’ votes. He expected continued representation of the American republics but opposed prescribing selection rules at that stage. Brazil advocated permanent Latin American representation and emphasized the Organization’s preventive purpose.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint describes a citizen science approach to monitoring household drinking water microbiomes in China. From December 2020 to August 2021, 25 student volunteers collected 50 tap water samples from 32 administrative regions across 19 provinces/regions, including samples following the 2021 Henan Floods and Typhoon In-Fa.

Volunteers used standardized, low-cost syringe-filter kits, supported by written instructions, video tutorials, demonstrations, and direct communication with researchers. Samples were frozen and transported to a laboratory for DNA extraction, PCR amplification, and 16S rRNA gene metabarcoding.

Microbial DNA was detected in 22 of 50 samples. Sequencing identified 7,635 amplicon sequence variants, revealing diverse microbial communities. Mycobacterium, Acinetobacter, and Legionella were detected in all PCR-positive samples. Post-weather-event samples from Zhengzhou and Changzhou included pathogenic species and/or toxin-producing cyanobacteria, such as Salmonella enterica and Microcystis.

The study presents citizen science and culture-independent analysis as potential supplements to conventional drinking water monitoring, which requires substantial resources and captures only a limited fraction of microbial diversity through culture-based methods. Despite limited sampling, the findings underscore the approach’s utility for microbial monitoring and informing water-safety strategies.

An unidentified young Mexican man remained in a vegetative state after a truck crash near the California–Mexico border. Fourteen years later, a woman saw his hospital photograph on Facebook and asked her cousin whether he could be Gilberto.

Quarters coverage uses four deep defenders and three underneath defenders, allowing safeties to support both pass coverage and run defense. Cornerbacks cover the #1 receivers, safeties watch the #2 receivers, outside linebackers defend the flats, and the middle linebacker covers the middle hook area.

Offenses attack quarters primarily through the flats and deep middle. Hitch routes can force outside linebackers to choose between receivers, while play-action can exploit aggressive safeties. Routes that draw safeties away create openings in the middle, and overload concepts generate one-on-one matchups and challenge linebackers vertically.

The passage illustrates these approaches with five plays from BYU, Kansas State, Ohio State, Georgia, and Wake Forest, featuring play-action, option routes, shallow crossing deception, double posts, and crossing routes. Quarterback decisions depend on how safeties and underneath defenders respond.

Caffeine content varies among coffee chains. The passage places McDonald’s lowest, followed by Dunkin’ Donuts and Peet’s. Starbucks contains 20.6 milligrams of caffeine per ounce, while Deathwish, which describes itself as the world’s strongest coffee, contains 54.2 milligrams per ounce.

James Saft argues that the post-election stock rally faces risks from historically high valuations and uncertainty over the Trump administration’s ability to deliver tax cuts, infrastructure spending and deregulation. The failed healthcare bill highlights those implementation risks. While confidence indicators have surged, economic growth and earnings forecast revisions have not matched that optimism. Federal Reserve officials have also expressed concern about asset prices, potentially supporting faster interest-rate increases. High valuations have historically predicted weak future returns. Saft expects piecemeal tax changes, with repatriated corporate cash supporting share buybacks, rather than a substantial revival in growth and inflation.

In Morris v. Scott, Morris alleged that Scott maliciously and without probable cause initiated proceedings resulting in his arrest, trial, and acquittal. The trial court nonsuited Morris because his declaration did not allege that the prosecuting courts had jurisdiction. The reviewing court held that malicious prosecution may support an action on the case despite a lack of jurisdiction, provided malice and falsehood form the principal grievance and arrest is alleged as a consequence. A statute also permitted choosing an action on the case for most trespasses affecting persons or personal property. The judgment was reversed and a new trial ordered, with costs to abide the outcome.

Pompey expect FA scrutiny after Charlton fans released smoke bombs at Fratton Park and could face a fine if their handling is deemed inadequate. Chief executive Mark Catlin said the club follows safety procedures but small canisters are difficult to detect, while extensive searches could cause long queues.

The passage describes automated object-sorting systems that use robotic manipulators, perception equipment, and dynamically assigned collection bins. Conventional manual and partially automated systems are described as constrained by labor requirements, fixed bin assignments, space demands, and costly diversion mechanisms.

The proposed systems acquire objects from mixed inputs, identify them through cameras or scanners, and assign intermediate bins or stations to their destinations. Unlike fixed-allocation systems, bin-to-destination assignments can change after bins are emptied. Multiple bins may serve one destination, and sorting stations need not maintain bins for every possible destination. Objects that cannot be assigned or identified may be recirculated or directed to manual processing.

A central controller manages assignments using information such as historical activity, expected arrivals, current bin contents, object characteristics, processing times, and facility layout. Completed bins are transferred for downstream processing or emptied by workers. Input configurations include conveyors, circulating buffers, and hoppers; outputs may use conveyors, tracked carriages, or bagging stations.

Further embodiments use shuttle-wing sorting. A robot drops an object through a multi-camera identification unit into a carriage, which transfers it to a wing carriage that travels between rows of bins and tips the object into its assigned bin. Configurations include two, four, or eight wings. Dynamic allocation can distribute high-volume destinations across wings and place frequently used bins near carriage starting positions.

The described architecture supports expansion through additional robots, wings, and parallel stations. Its stated objectives include increased sorting flexibility and throughput, reduced space and labor requirements, and lower capital and operating costs.

The passage tests lower highs and lower lows as a short-term reversal signal in the S&P 500, gold, and long-term Treasuries. Strategies buy at the close after one, two, or three consecutive qualifying days and sell after a specified holding period.

One-day pattern tests show higher returns with longer holding periods, attributed to rising asset values. Requiring two consecutive days slightly improves stock returns but provides little benefit for gold or Treasuries. In stocks, requiring three consecutive days improves average gains and profit factor; exiting the next day produces a maximum drawdown of 9.9%.

The passage concludes that the pattern works best as a short-term reversal strategy in stocks, while suggesting other patterns and indicators may offer better rewards.

Niantic will add 80 second-generation Pokémon to Pokémon Go later this week, bringing their total to 88, with 12 absent, including six legendary Pokémon. The update also introduces new battle reactions, avatar customisation options and two berries: Nanab, which slows Pokémon’s movements, and Pinap, which doubles Candy if the next catch succeeds. Niantic has not detailed when or how legendary Pokémon will be introduced.

Child care academies in at least 11 North Carolina counties offer accelerated training at little to no cost to address educator shortages. Programs last two to six weeks, require 20 to 64 classroom hours, and typically involve collaboration among community colleges, Smart Start partnerships, and Child Care Resource and Referral organizations.

Two models prepare participants for different roles:
- **Classroom-ready academies** provide required health and safety training, registration assistance, and background checks, qualifying graduates to work in licensed child care facilities but not as lead teachers.
- **Teaching credential academies** add introductory early childhood education coursework, qualifying graduates as lead teachers. Their continuing education credit transfers to any of the state’s 58 community colleges and can support further education.

A $1.476 million expansion pilot appeared in the House budget but was not included in legislation signed in August. Separately, the state’s early childhood education division offers grants of up to $50,000 for as many as 10 eligible institutions to operate academies between October 2025 and July 2026. More than a dozen additional community colleges are preparing programs or have expressed interest.

Local academies rely on foundation grants and other funding. Reported outcomes include 63 graduates in Wayne County, more than half entering child care work or further education; 26 graduates in Johnston County, including 14 who secured child care jobs; and six credentialed graduates at McDowell Tech, four entering classrooms and two pursuing higher education. Durham’s bilingual academy received 140 applications for 20 places.

The team aims to improve by creating traffic in front of Roberto and obstructing his view. After learning opponents’ tendencies in the first game, they hope for a better performance, a split before returning home, and renewed confidence.

On July 25, 2002, the U.S. District Court for the District of Columbia denied a motion to enforce a proposed settlement in a lawsuit brought by former corrections employees Arthur Hood, Jessie Smith, and Susie Thomas. The plaintiffs alleged that they were terminated without adequate notice or an opportunity to challenge their dismissals in retaliation for discussing halfway-house conditions with the media.

The parties agreed to a $625,000 payment but disputed whether the settlement included retirement-system re-enrollment for Hood and Smith. Under District of Columbia contract law, an enforceable settlement requires agreement on all material terms and an intention to be bound. The court found no mutual assent concerning re-enrollment and therefore no binding settlement. Statements that no problems were anticipated and the provision of an application form did not establish agreement.

The court also rejected the plaintiffs’ claimed unconditional statutory right to retirement benefits because their dismissals had not been adjudicated or admitted to be unwarranted or unjustified. It declined to enforce a separate settlement for Thomas, who had not agreed to an individual payment amount.

The plaintiffs were given until September 9, 2002, to accept $625,000 without retirement benefits in exchange for dismissing the entire case, or reject the offer and proceed toward trial.

Tesla delivered its first 30 Model 3 cars to employee buyers, with advance reservations exceeding 500,000. The base model costs $35,000 and offers a 220-mile range; a $44,000 version offers 310 miles. Elon Musk warned of at least six months of manufacturing challenges as Tesla pursues high-volume production. The company aims to produce 500,000 vehicles next year, nearly six times its 2016 output. Having spent over $2 billion in cash this year, Tesla faces financial risks from a troubled launch, while steady deliveries could reduce its need to raise additional capital.

The Midline Option is a football play in which the quarterback reads an interior defensive lineman to decide whether to hand off to a fullback attacking the A-gap or keep the ball through the B-gap. If the defender crashes toward the fullback, the quarterback keeps; if the defender expands or moves upfield, he hands off.

Its main advantage is leaving one defender unblocked and reading his movement. It also complements inside and outside veer, using wingback motion to disguise an inside run. Its primary weakness is exposing the quarterback to frequent hits.

Blocking assignments change against 3-4 and 4-3 defenses, while the quarterback’s read remains consistent. Variations include Flexbone Midline, which replaces a playside tight end with a receiver to spread the defense, and Midline “Follow,” which adds a wingback as a lead blocker for quarterback keeps in short-yardage situations. Oregon and Coastal Carolina have adapted the concept to their systems.

Backtests using EWG for German stocks and FEZ for Euro Stoxx 50 showed stronger performance during Christmas and year-end than during random periods. EWG averaged a 2.1% gain per trade with an 81% win ratio and profit factor of 13; FEZ averaged 1.5%, with an 81% win ratio and profit factor of 9. Returns weakened in recent years. Earlier entries increased returns but also volatility. The passage gives inconsistent descriptions of backtest instruments and holding periods. Historical results do not guarantee the rally will continue.

IHRMP President Dr. Edward Kwapong urged human resource practitioners to embrace professional certification rather than rely on academic qualifications. At the institute’s ninth graduation in Accra, 136 Associate and nine certified members graduated, a reported 32 per cent increase. Guest speaker Irene Asare said artificial intelligence, robotics and humans combine to improve organisational productivity, noting that workplace changes are already occurring.

The lecture examines smart contracts, decentralized applications (dApps), token offerings, and their legal implications.

Smart contracts are digitally specified promises with protocols for performance, a definition attributed to Nick Szabo in 1996. They automate functions but are not necessarily intelligent or legally enforceable contracts. Ethereum shares blockchain features with Bitcoin, including cryptographic hashes, digital signatures, and, at the time of the lecture, proof-of-work consensus. Unlike Bitcoin’s transaction-based ledger, Ethereum uses accounts and state transitions and supports Turing-complete programming. Its block rewards have been changed through software updates, illustrating the role of developers and network agreement in monetary policy.

DApps operate on decentralized blockchains and commonly issue their own tokens, although this is not required. Adoption remained limited in the examples presented, with leading applications concentrated in gambling, gaming, exchanges, and finance. Initial coin offerings raise funds for networks, often before tokens become usable. Reported fundraising totals reached $20–28 billion, while cited studies identified substantial failure and fraud rates.

Guest lecturer Larry Lessig emphasizes four legal considerations:
- Contracts include implied legal terms beyond their explicit provisions.
- States retain an interest in contracts’ legality, effects, terms, and taxation, even when execution is automated.
- Contract law allocates risk rather than eliminating it; effective allocation requires mechanisms for addressing breaches.
- Ambiguity can be useful, allowing parties to defer costly negotiations over unlikely contingencies until disputes arise.

Smart contracts could lower transaction costs and support transactions where legal enforcement is weak or expensive. Automated flight-delay insurance illustrates this potential, although participants question whether blockchain is necessary and raise concerns about privacy and verifying real-world events. Requiring every contingency to be coded could also increase costs for complex agreements.

Lessig argues that automated contracts remain embedded in legal systems. Existing electronic-signature infrastructure largely supports their recognition, but interpreting code presents challenges. Lawyers and courts need greater technical understanding to evaluate coded obligations and address disputes.

The passage defines SEV-ES and SEV-SNP Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) protocols, including initialization, address registration, VMGEXIT processing, page-state changes, and firmware requests.

- **Protocol requests:** Guests can request AP reset hold, preferred GHCB addresses, GHCB registration or unregistration, page-state changes, VMPL execution, hypervisor feature information, and termination. Availability of several operations depends on advertised feature bits. AP reset hold through the described request is unsupported for SEV-SNP guests using Restricted Injection.

- **GHCB registration:** Registration is supported and required only for SEV-SNP guests. A guest must register a vCPU’s GHCB guest physical address before first use and make the page shared. Hypervisor-preferred addresses are optional. Registering a new address automatically unregisters the previous one. The hypervisor must terminate a guest that supplies an address different from the vCPU’s registered address. Multi-VMPL support requires allowing registration at each VMPL level.

- **Initialization:** Negotiation establishes supported protocol versions and the page-table encryption bit. Guests configure page tables, allocate a shared GHCB page, and set the GHCB MSR before VMGEXIT operations using that page. SEV-SNP guests should obtain the encryption-bit position from firmware-validated CPUID Page information.

- **Exit handling:** Non-automatic exits generate #VC exceptions for SEV-ES guests. Guests provide required state through the GHCB, invoke VMGEXIT, and process returned state. Guests and hypervisors must mark supplied fields in VALID_BITMAP and should clear the bitmap before populating each exchange. Software should disable interrupts and preemption while preparing and accessing GHCB exchanges. Hypervisor errors are communicated through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2.

- **Special operations:** String I/O and MMIO operations require decrypted buffers and may use multiple VMGEXIT calls. Page-state changes support private/shared transitions and optional page-splitting or combining hints. The shared buffer accommodates up to 253 entries. Progress fields track completion and permit interrupted requests to resume; a zero SW_EXITINFO1 alone does not establish success.

- **Guest information transfer:** The SEV-SNP secrets page includes a reserved area for message sequence numbers, an AP Jump Table address, and guest-defined use across operating environments. EFI configuration tables can communicate secrets and CPUID pages to the operating system.

- **Firmware requests:** SNP guest requests use separate shared request and response pages. The hypervisor manages response-page ownership around firmware processing and returns firmware status. Rate limiting is recommended for excessive requests. Guests must retry deferred requests before issuing another request to prevent reuse of an AES-GCM initialization vector with a new payload.

Collagen provides structural support to skin, tendons and bones, but natural production decreases with age. Most collagen supplements come from animals, and research suggests hydrolysed collagen, which is easily digested and absorbed, may be the most effective form.

Studies suggest supplements may improve skin firmness and hydration, strengthen brittle nails, support bone and joint health, and help repair muscle damage. Evidence for thicker hair growth is limited to studies in mice, and research into supplement benefits remains ongoing.

Dosage varies by product and intended benefit. Many manufacturers recommend taking supplements for at least 12 weeks for noticeable results, and third-party testing is recommended to verify product contents.

A balanced diet rich in protein and essential nutrients, including vitamin C, zinc and copper, is described as the most reliable way to support the body’s natural collagen production.

Trend Micro discovered 89 malicious Chrome extensions affecting over 423,000 users and forming the “Droidclub” botnet. Distributed through malvertising and social engineering, the extensions displayed ads and abused session-replay scripts to capture browsing activity and sensitive form data, excluding passwords. An earlier version secretly mined Monero using Coinhive. The extensions also obstructed reporting and removal by redirecting users to misleading pages. Google removed the affected extensions from the Chrome Web Store and disabled them on affected users’ devices.

Billy Caldwell, 12, who has a rare form of epilepsy, received a short-term Home Office licence for medicinal cannabis. His mother says their return from London to Northern Ireland is delayed pending Department of Health ratification. She claims the department has not responded to communications; it says it is actively working with the Home Office and Belfast Trust to resolve the matter promptly.

Hubble imaged NGC 6000, a spiral galaxy 102 million light-years away in Scorpius. Its yellow center contains generally older, smaller stars, while its blue spiral arms host young, massive stars. The observations were collected during a survey of recent supernova sites, including two explosions in NGC 6000 in 2007 and 2010. Studying their lingering glow helps researchers constrain progenitor stars’ masses and identify possible stellar companions. A passing Solar System asteroid left four streaks across separate exposures, whose red and blue filters produced the streaks’ colors in the combined image.

On May 12, 2021, Amazon.com, Inc. closed the sale of eight series of notes with interest rates ranging from 0.250% to 3.250% and maturities from 2023 to 2061. The aggregate public offering price was $18.437 billion, with estimated net proceeds of approximately $18.395 billion after underwriting discounts and before offering expenses.

The offering included $1 billion of 0.250% Sustainability Notes due 2023. Amazon intends to allocate an amount equal to their net proceeds to finance or refinance eligible green or social projects.

The notes were issued under Amazon’s indenture with Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee. The Form 8-K includes the underwriting agreement, officers’ certificate, note forms, and related legal opinion and consent.

Soccer formations organize players to defend their own goal and attack the opponent’s. Formation choices depend on player numbers, team skills, and the coach’s ability to teach and apply tactics.

Formation notation lists defenders, midfielders, and forwards, excluding the goalkeeper. In 11-a-side games, these numbers total 10, as in 4-3-3 or 4-4-2. Some formations distinguish defensive and attacking midfielders.

U.S. Soccer recommends 4-3-3 and 4-4-2 for U15–U19, 4-3-3 for U13–U14, and 3-2-3 for U9–U12 playing nine-a-side. Younger groups require coaching discretion; formations can help children transition toward team-oriented play.

Coaches should understand positions, player placement, tactics, and teamwork, then diagram and explain how their chosen formation will operate.
The Supreme Court of Alabama dismissed William Riley’s certiorari petition on July 26, 1945, following his death.

Thirteen-year-old Time for Kids reporter Benje Choucroun asked White House press secretary Sarah Huckabee Sanders what the administration was doing to prevent school shootings, citing students’ fears and mental health concerns. Visibly emotional, Sanders said the administration took school safety seriously and that the president’s school safety commission was meeting that week to discuss protecting students.
The team held on after losing a one-goal lead and conceding the tying goal. Both teams played well in a balanced game, with Sergei’s timely goal making the difference.

P. falciparum uses variable PfEMP1 surface proteins, encoded by var genes, to support infected erythrocyte adhesion and evade immunity. This non-peer-reviewed preprint investigates how pre-existing immunity influences var expression, parasite growth and antibody responses during controlled human malaria infection.

Nineteen semi-immune adult men in The Gambia, classified as sero-high or sero-low based on existing malaria antibodies, received NF54/3D7 parasites. Researchers assessed parasite transcription, PfEMP1 antibody recognition and infection progression, and cultured selected isolates to study switching without host immunity.

Sero-high participants had significantly lower peak parasitaemia and more restricted var expression than sero-low participants. Both participants classified as infection controllers were sero-high. Broader pre-existing recognition of PfEMP1 domains was associated with longer latency, lower peak parasitaemia and reduced diversity of expressed var genes. Expression patterns also separated controllers from non-controllers when compared with a previous Gabon study.

Var genes were among the most variably expressed genes between individuals. Estimated in vivo turnover probabilities averaged 69–97% per generation across gene groups, consistent with contributions from intrinsic switching and immune selection. In culture, expression became more diverse and approached a steady state. Sero-low isolates converged rapidly, whereas some sero-high isolates retained distinct profiles after 50 days. Switching probabilities for groups A and B were lower in vitro than turnover probabilities in vivo.

Sero-high participants recognized more PfEMP1 domains before and after infection, with comparatively stable response breadth. In sero-low participants, the average number of recognized domains increased from approximately 11 to 28. Pre-existing specific antibodies were moderately associated with reduced corresponding var expression, but expression intensity did not clearly predict subsequent antibody acquisition.

The authors propose that intrinsic switching maintains a diverse PfEMP1 repertoire, while immune selection restricts that repertoire in individuals with stronger pre-existing immunity.

IDC highlights global cooperation as an increasingly important aspect of HPCaaS. Growing hybrid workflows require integrated, data-based development, a shared information foundation, and more efficient workstations, but upgrading conventional engineering workstations is expensive.

The incoming President outlines principles for an administration grounded in constitutional limits, individual rights, and government by consent. He argues that the greatest threat to republican government is the concentration of powers in the executive, rather than simply the exercise of powers not granted by the people.

He pledges never to serve a second term and rejects presidential control over ordinary legislation. He maintains that the veto should protect the Constitution, guard against hasty legislation that disregards public wishes, and prevent violations of minority rights. Responsibility for devising revenue measures and determining the custody of public funds should remain with Congress.

Warning against executive influence through patronage, public finances, and the press, he promises to explain any removal of a Treasury secretary to both houses of Congress. He also proposes prohibiting federal officers from interfering in elections beyond casting their own votes, while protecting their independent voting rights. He supports press freedom and scrutiny of government conduct.

The President opposes an exclusively metallic currency, arguing that it would impede economic advancement and worsen inequality. He affirms that District of Columbia residents are free citizens whose rights and interests Congress must respect. He encourages states facing financial difficulties to fulfill their obligations and maintain their credit.

He emphasizes mutual respect among states and warns that attempts by one state’s citizens to control another’s domestic institutions threaten national unity. Constitutional safeguards, he argues, cannot preserve liberty without public vigilance, moderation, and resistance to factionalism. He calls for national rather than partisan unity and rejects forming an executive party in Congress.

In foreign affairs, he seeks friendly relations without sacrificing national rights or honor and pledges justice in dealings with Indigenous peoples. He closes by affirming his Christian faith, religious liberty, and commitment to fulfilling his duties with public support.

Eric Thames homered in his fifth straight game, tying a Brewers record, as Milwaukee beat the Chicago Cubs 6-3 for its sixth win in seven games. His third-inning homer broke a 3-3 tie. Braun and Jeff Bandy also homered, while Chase Anderson pitched five innings for the win and Neftali Felix earned his fifth save. Milwaukee added two insurance runs in the eighth. The defending World Series champion Cubs fell to 6-7 with their fourth consecutive loss. Former Cubs Jason Hammel, Jorge Soler and Travis Wood received their 2016 championship rings before the game.

An October 18, 2017 webinar featuring leaders from HRO Today, NCI Building Systems, and Orion Novotus will explore how HR strategy, recruitment metrics, and candidate experience affect recruitment productivity, hiring outcomes, and retention.

Conformis (NASDAQ:CFMS) shares fell 6.47%, closing at $1.30. Six analysts projected an average 12-month price target of $5, ranging from $4 to $6. Facebook acquired the team behind London-based Bloomsbury AI, rather than its product, to strengthen natural language processing research. Bloomsbury developed “Cape,” an AI that answers questions about documents. TechCrunch reported potential interest in using its software to combat fake news. Bloomsbury AI’s future operations remain unclear.

Patrick Cullen, 33, pleaded guilty to robbing a 21-year-old woman of her handbag on Wolfe Tone Street. She fell and cut her finger while resisting. Cullen admitted the offence and helped gardai recover the bag. He received a four-year sentence with the final year suspended, conditional on Probation Service supervision after release. The judge noted his previous record, cooperation and the offence’s opportunistic nature.

Six teachers were suspended following Education Minister Th Radheshyam’s surprise school visits: three for operating in unauthorized premises without normal classes, and three for being absent without informing authorities.

LeBron James, 40, said his expiring contract will not affect his performance as he prepares for a record 23rd NBA season. He exercised his $52.6 million player option in June and expressed excitement about the Lakers’ roster and continuity with their coaching staff.

While Luka Doncic identified winning a championship as the team’s goal, James emphasized daily attention to detail and accountability. The Lakers finished third in the Western Conference last season before losing in the first playoff round.

James is rebuilding his fitness after a left knee MCL sprain and recurring foot problems, and his training camp participation could be limited. He said retirement will depend on his motivation for preparation and his body’s response, not on waiting for his son Bryce to reach the NBA.

In Riverton Investment Corp. v. United States, the court considered whether payments to repurchase management employees’ stock were deductible compensation or nondeductible stock redemptions. The IRS had disallowed Riverton’s deductions, and a magistrate judge recommended judgment for the United States.

The dispute depended on whether employees had acquired beneficial ownership of the stock for tax purposes. Their agreement restricted transfers, required repurchase upon termination of employment, and set the repurchase price at the greater of the original purchase price or 60% of book value. The parties disputed whether these restrictions would lapse upon a liquidation, merger, acquisition, or reorganization.

The court found the relevant contract provision ambiguous and admitted evidence of the contracting parties’ intent. Uncontroverted testimony established that corporate transactions could change when employees could sell, but would not eliminate the pricing restrictions or protection against investment losses. These permanent restrictions prevented the employees’ original stock acquisitions from qualifying as transfers for tax purposes.

Consequently, the later repurchase payments were not stock redemptions and should have been deductible. The court rejected the magistrate judge’s recommendation, denied the government’s motions for summary judgment and to strike evidence, and granted summary judgment to Riverton. The parties were directed to address appropriate damages and interest within thirty days.

The court affirmed an injunction preventing enforcement of a judgment against Ida C. Scott’s land for family necessaries. Under Nebraska law, a married woman’s property could not be sold to satisfy such debts until an execution against her husband had been issued and returned unsatisfied. The parties stipulated that no judgment had first been obtained against Scott’s husband.

The defendants argued that Scott’s failure to raise these defenses in the original action barred her from asserting them later. The court held that she could invoke the statutory protection before the sale of her property because the required condition had not been met. It therefore found it unnecessary to decide whether her land was also exempt under federal laws concerning property of Omaha Tribe members.

The Mets missed the playoffs after a strong start, with pitching struggles contributing to their decline. GM David Stearns described Kodai Senga’s past two seasons as inconsistent and challenging, citing his potential but cautioning against expecting 30 starts next year. Senga dealt with injuries last year and struggled this season, including after a demotion to Triple-A.

Distributed-system patterns capture established solutions, help developers avoid repeated mistakes, provide a shared vocabulary, and support reusable components. Shared implementations can improve quality through broader use and maintenance.

Containers establish resource boundaries, team ownership, and separation of concerns. Splitting applications into focused containers—even on one machine—enables independent resource allocation, reuse, testing, updates, and deployment. Single-node patterns group tightly coupled containers that can share filesystems, networking, and other resources; Kubernetes calls such a group a pod.

Three single-node patterns address different needs:

- **Sidecars** augment an application container. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration files with an API, exposing process-resource information, and synchronizing Git repositories to support automatic application updates.
- **Ambassadors** broker communication between an application and external services. They can route requests to storage shards, discover services across environments, or split traffic between production and experimental implementations. Applications connect locally while ambassadors handle external interactions.
- **Adapters** translate an application’s interface into a common interface. Uses include exporting monitoring metrics, normalizing logs, and providing database health checks without modifying the original application container.

Reusable containers require configurable parameters, stable APIs, and documentation. API compatibility includes parameter names, formats, units, and behavior—not merely exposed endpoints. Dockerfiles can document ports, configuration defaults, and image metadata.

Multi-node systems communicate through network calls and are more loosely coupled. Microservices divide applications into independently maintained services with defined APIs. This supports smaller teams, independent releases, and service-specific scaling, but makes debugging and architectural design more difficult. Established patterns help address these challenges.

A **replicated load-balanced service** places interchangeable servers behind a load balancer to provide redundancy and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes distinguish applications that are running from those ready to serve requests. Session tracking keeps a user’s requests on the same replica; application-level mechanisms such as cookies are preferred for external traffic, while consistent hashing reduces remapping when replica counts change.

Additional serving layers can provide caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. A separate caching tier allows caches and application servers to scale independently. Fewer, larger caches reduce duplicated cached content compared with many small replicas. Caching can interfere with IP-based session tracking, requiring cookies or headers instead. Rate limiting helps control excessive traffic, while a separate nginx layer can terminate HTTPS before forwarding requests through a Varnish cache to application servers.

A **sharded service** differs from a replicated service because each shard handles only a subset of requests or data. A router directs requests to the appropriate shard. Sharded caches use aggregate memory more efficiently than independent replicas storing similar content, but shard failures or replacements can reduce cache hit rates, increase latency, and overload backend services. Testing with and without caching helps establish these effects.

Replicating individual shards improves availability and permits independent scaling of heavily loaded shards, at the cost of greater complexity. Routing can reside in client-side ambassadors or a shared routing service; the latter simplifies clients but requires its own scaling and adds a network hop. Sharding functions map requests to shards, commonly using hashing and the modulo operator.
At 0134 GMT on February 2, the ringgit led daily Asian currency gains against the dollar at 0.4%, while the peso fell 0.19%. Year-to-date, the ringgit gained 4.12% and the peso lost 3.39%.

Mike Hoffman scored in the sixth shootout round using the “Peter Forsberg” move to give Ottawa a 4-3 victory over Philadelphia. Rookie Colin White earned his first NHL point with an assist on Matt Duchene’s first-period goal.

Defenceman Johnny Oduya collected a $250,000 bonus for playing his 41st game of the season. He could earn additional bonuses for reaching 65 games and ranking among the team’s top five defencemen in ice time.

Ottawa coach Guy Boucher praised former junior player Sean Couturier’s defensive reliability and offensive development. Calgary scout Don Maloney attended the game, with the Flames believed to be interested in Ottawa’s Zack Smith and Jean-Gabriel Pageau ahead of the February 26 trade deadline.

With Philadelphia preparing for the Super Bowl, Ottawa goalie Craig Anderson backed the Eagles, while Mike Condon and White supported New England.

South Carolina Department of Natural Resources biologists satellite-tagged Harry-Etta, an 820-pound female tiger shark, in St. Helena Sound. Ultrasound confirmed she was pregnant, making her the first known pregnant shark among 15 tiger sharks the team has satellite-tagged. Researchers will track her movements over the next year to study habitats used during gestation and gain insight into migration and reproduction. Previous research suggests South Carolina’s southern sounds are important foraging and potentially nursing grounds. The Harry Hampton Wildlife Fund sponsored the tag, and the public can follow Harry-Etta through the OCEARCH Global Shark Tracker.

This study evaluates and prioritizes factors affecting online higher education quality in Vietnam using the spherical fuzzy analytic hierarchy process (SFAHP). It addresses the lack of a systematic framework for comparing digitalization’s impacts. SFAHP combines hierarchical decision-making with spherical fuzzy sets to handle ambiguity in expert assessments.

Nine education experts provided pairwise comparisons of five criteria, producing the following rankings:
1. Pedagogical integration: 23.6%.
2. Student engagement: 21.2%.
3. Accessibility of digital resources: 20.3%.
4. Adaptability and innovation: 18.4%.
5. Technological infrastructure: 16.5%.

The findings prioritize integrating teaching methodologies with technology over infrastructure alone. Recommended strategies include educator training in digital pedagogy, interactive and personalized learning, collaborative platforms, and equitable access to digital resources. Although adaptability, innovation, and infrastructure ranked lower, the study considers them essential to effective online education.

The passage distinguishes digitalization—incorporating digital tools into existing practices—from digital transformation, which involves broader changes to educational models and systems.

The study’s reliance on expert evaluations may not capture other stakeholders’ perspectives. Future research should incorporate broader viewpoints and examine how digital pedagogy innovation could affect these priorities.

On January 5, 1838, President Martin Van Buren warned against unlawful American involvement in Canada’s civil war. Despite official efforts, frontier unrest had increased, and insurgents received supplies and recruits from the United States. An armed force partly composed of Americans had assembled at Navy Island. Van Buren urged participants to return home, warning that violations of U.S. neutrality would bring arrest and punishment, without government support.

The offensive line consists of five players who line up together on the line of scrimmage. Their primary responsibilities are creating openings for running plays and protecting the quarterback during passing plays. Success requires communication, coordinated blocking, and adjustments to defensive blitzes, stunts, and alignments.

Offensive linemen need run-blocking and pass-blocking skills, athleticism, strength, awareness, and technique. They generally stand 6’2–6’8 and weigh 300–340 pounds, though body types differ among centers, guards, and tackles.

Notable players include center Jim Otto, guard John Hannah, and tackle Anthony Munoz. Offensive linemen receive less public recognition than skill-position players but play a central role in offensive production, enabling teammates to perform while often facing blame when the offense struggles.

A University of Pennsylvania study of 81 healthy adults found that electrical stimulation of the prefrontal cortex reduced participants’ reported intentions to commit physical and sexual assault and increased their judgement that these acts were morally wrong. Participants received either 20 minutes of stimulation or brief low-current pulses before assessing violent scenarios the next day. Independent expert Paul Appelbaum cautioned that reduced intentions do not establish reduced actual violence. Lead author Olivia Choy suggested repeated sessions might produce behavioural changes, though this remained untested.

A review of more than 140 scientific articles by Concordia University researcher Sarah Sajedi estimates that bottled water drinkers ingest up to 90,000 more microplastic particles annually than tap water drinkers. Plastic bottles release particles during production, storage, transportation and degradation, including exposure to sunlight and temperature changes.

These particles can enter the bloodstream and reach organs. The review identifies potential health effects including inflammation, hormonal disruption, reproductive impairment, neurological damage and cancer. However, long-term effects remain poorly understood, and research is limited by inconsistent measurement methods and costly detection equipment.

Sajedi calls for greater public education about chronic exposure and notes that plastic-waste legislation rarely targets single-use water bottles. She recommends reserving bottled water for emergencies rather than daily use.

A fossil discovered by elk hunter David Bradt in Montana in 2010 has been identified as a new elasmosaur species that lived about 70 million years ago. Found in the Charles M. Russell National Wildlife Refuge, the nearly complete fossil had a neck about 7½ feet long, compared with up to 18 feet in most elasmosaurs. Researchers described the marine reptile in the Journal of Vertebrate Paleontology after years of cleaning and study.

Software patterns provide reusable design blueprints, shared terminology, and ways to apply lessons from previous development work. Object-oriented design patterns helped establish reusable libraries, while open source communities reinforced software development as a collaborative activity. Distributed-system patterns extend these benefits to applications requiring reliability, agility, and scale.

Containers support modular designs by establishing resource boundaries, team ownership, and separation of concerns. Dividing applications into focused containers enables reuse, independent updates, and more controlled deployments. Single-node patterns group tightly coupled containers on one machine, optionally sharing filesystems, networking, and other resources. Kubernetes calls such groups pods.

Three single-node patterns address different needs:

- **Sidecar:** Augments an application container with additional functionality. Examples include adding HTTPS to a legacy HTTP service, synchronizing configuration, exposing process-resource information, and updating application files from Git. Reusable sidecars require configurable parameters, stable APIs, and documentation. Parameter names, formats, and meanings are part of the API; changes can break existing consumers. Dockerfile directives and image labels can document ports, defaults, ownership, and versions.
- **Ambassador:** Brokers communication between an application and external services. Applications connect locally while the ambassador handles tasks such as routing requests to storage shards, discovering environment-specific services, or splitting traffic between production and experimental implementations.
- **Adapter:** Converts an application’s interface into a standardized interface. Examples include exporting Redis metrics for Prometheus, normalizing logs with fluentd, and providing query-based database health checks. Separate adapters allow independent updates and reuse without modifying third-party application images.

Multi-node systems use network communication and looser coordination. Microservices divide applications into independently maintained services connected through defined APIs. This supports smaller teams, independent releases, and service-specific scaling, but makes debugging and architectural design more difficult. Established patterns help structure these systems.

A **replicated load-balanced service** distributes requests among interchangeable servers, providing redundancy and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes distinguish applications that are running from those ready to receive requests. Session tracking can keep a user’s requests on one replica; application-level tracking is preferable for external traffic where network address translation complicates IP-based affinity.

Additional replicated layers can provide caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. Independently scaling caches and application servers accommodates their different resource requirements. Caching proxies can interfere with IP-based session tracking, requiring cookies or headers instead.

A **sharded service** divides requests or data among servers, with routing logic directing requests to the appropriate shard. Unlike interchangeable replicas, each shard handles only part of the workload. Sharded caches improve memory utilization by storing different data on different shards rather than duplicating the same cached content.

Cache hit rates affect throughput and latency. Losing a shard can repeatedly force affected requests to the backend, potentially overloading it; upgrades can also temporarily reduce capacity. Load testing with and without caches helps assess these dependencies. Replicating each shard improves resilience and permits independent scaling of heavily loaded shards, at the cost of greater deployment complexity.

The presidents of Middle States, SACSCOC and WASC discussed credit transfer and AI in a webinar. They encouraged colleges to default to accepting transfer credits but offered no clear mandates or criteria for rejecting them. The author argues that universities’ economic interests discourage credit acceptance and that accreditors’ ability to enforce changes has weakened since regional monopolies ended, allowing colleges to seek alternative accreditors. AI could accelerate transcript assessments and deliver transfer decisions alongside admission and financial aid offers, helping students make informed choices, though hallucinations remain a concern. The author welcomes the direction but calls for concrete plans rather than intentions.

A security aide to Ebonyi Governor David Umahi allegedly slapped an FRSC officer after an argument over convoy access at a checkpoint near the PDP convention venue. FRSC spokesman Bisi Kazeem said no official report had been received. Newsmen also observed security personnel taking money from unaccredited individuals to allow them entry.

Coach Sutter described the series as closely matched, emphasizing finishing opportunities, limiting goals conceded and scoring first. He praised his team’s first period despite a goal following a marginal call. He said pressure was on the Devils as the home team and attributed a screened goal partly to a tired forward and a winger failing to get through the shot.

The seventh annual Julia’s Hope Cup and Carnival takes place Feb. 17 at Chippawa Park in Welland. Created in memory of Julia Turner, it raises money for The Hope Centre’s work combating homelessness. Activities include hockey, food, children’s games and a silent auction. The main tournament starts at 11:30 a.m., costing $100 per player or $50 for students. A tournament for ages six to 12 starts at 10 a.m., costing $25. Last year’s event raised $20,000 and attracted about 1,000 people.

Jersey defended well after taking the lead, limiting offense. The speaker emphasized strong road play, finding solutions without Peter, and continuing the power play’s success in the next important game.

CBS’ drama Doubt premieres February 15 at 10/9c, following attorneys at New York defense firm Isaiah Roth and Associates. Led by Isaiah Roth, the firm includes transgender lawyer Cameron Wirth, formerly incarcerated attorney Nick Brady, and Sadie Ellis. Sadie represents Billy Brennan, a pediatric surgeon accused of a murder committed 24 years earlier. As she works to prove his innocence, her personal feelings complicate her professional responsibilities.
Houston Dash captain Carli Lloyd injured her ankle against FC Kansas City. Reports said X-rays were negative, but the team has not announced how many games she could miss.

Two boys, ages 14 and 17, were arrested after allegedly stealing a van from Smoky Mountain Children’s Home and leading police across East Tennessee. The chase ended when the van struck another vehicle and Chickamauga Dam’s barrier wall. No serious injuries were reported.

HID AMDI0095 lets the OS bind a driver to the ACPI-defined TMPM device. The driver must enable PAGEMIGRATION_EN in all available IOMMUs once. TMPM uses mailbox registers and a ring buffer supporting parallel commands without guaranteed execution order. Firmware controls the Read pointer; the driver controls the Write pointer. Read-pointer advancement indicates command completion, while PM_Status TOGGLE changes indicate completion of RB_Ctl commands.

Cirque du Soleil will donate US$500,000 to Las Vegas shooting victims’ families and provide first responders with 5,000 tickets worth US$500,000. It also plans to contribute additional funds through a benefit show.

Former Southport MP John Pugh fears a planned 60,000 sq ft Sainsbury’s at Meols Cop retail park could cause further job losses following Homebase’s closure. Although Sainsbury’s proposes creating 400 jobs, Pugh warns competition could harm town-centre shops and prompt retailers to relocate. He criticised Sefton Council’s support for the development.

The lecture develops algebraic foundations for finite fields, preparing for the study of Reed–Solomon codes. It reviews integers, modular arithmetic, groups, and cyclic groups before introducing subgroups, cosets, quotient groups, fields, and polynomials.

A subgroup is a subset that forms a group under the original group operation. Examples in the additive group \(\mathbb Z_{10}\) include \(\{0,5\}\) and \(\{0,2,4,6,8\}\), isomorphic to \(\mathbb Z_2\) and \(\mathbb Z_5\). Cosets are translates of subgroups. Distinct cosets are disjoint, have equal size, and partition the group. For finite groups, this establishes Lagrange’s theorem: a subgroup’s size divides the group’s size. In an abelian group, coset addition defines a quotient group. In particular, \(\mathbb Z/n\mathbb Z\) is isomorphic to \(\mathbb Z_n\), providing an interpretation of modular arithmetic through residue classes.

A field has addition and multiplication satisfying three conditions: its elements form an abelian group under addition, its nonzero elements form an abelian group under multiplication, and multiplication distributes over addition. These properties support subtraction, division by nonzero elements, and cancellation.

For every prime \(p\), the integers modulo \(p\) form a finite field \(\mathbb F_p\). Primality ensures that multiplying nonzero elements does not produce zero and that nonzero elements have multiplicative inverses. Every field with \(p\) elements is isomorphic to \(\mathbb F_p\).

In any finite field, repeated addition of the multiplicative identity generates a prime subfield. Its size \(p\) is the field’s characteristic. Adding any field element to itself \(p\) times gives zero. In characteristic two, each element is its own additive inverse, so addition and subtraction coincide.

Polynomials have coefficients in a specified field and use an indeterminate \(x\). Distinct polynomials over a finite field can have identical values at every field element, so polynomial identity cannot be determined solely by those evaluations. Addition combines corresponding coefficients, while multiplication combines products of terms. The degree of a sum is at most the larger input degree; the degree of a product of nonzero polynomials is the sum of their degrees. Assigning the zero polynomial degree \(-\infty\) extends the product-degree rule to zero.

Polynomials form an abelian group under addition but do not form a field under ordinary polynomial multiplication. Only nonzero constant polynomials have polynomial multiplicative inverses; positive-degree polynomials cannot multiply by another polynomial to produce \(1\).

GoDaddy gave neo-Nazi website The Daily Stormer 24 hours to move its domain, citing terms-of-service violations after it published an article denigrating Heather Heyer, who was killed at a white nationalist rally in Charlottesville, Virginia.

Lexus’s 2017 LC coupe starts at £76,595 in the UK for both the 467hp V8 LC500 and 354hp hybrid LC500h. More than one-third of this year’s UK allocation has been pre-ordered. Optional Sport and Sport+ packages add styling, seating and handling upgrades.

In his first presidential address on the eve of Independence Day, Ram Nath Kovind honoured those who sacrificed their lives for India’s freedom and urged citizens to help build a “New India” by 2022. He called for public participation in cleanliness, ending open defecation, preventing discrimination against women and ensuring government schemes reach those in need. Kovind encouraged compliance with laws, adoption of GST and pride in paying taxes, while crediting demonetisation with supporting an honest society. He stressed selflessness, improved infrastructure and education, urging everyone to help educate at least one underprivileged child.

Tesla’s 2021 Annual Report describes its electric vehicle and energy businesses, expansion plans, regulatory environment and principal risks.

- **Business and products:** Tesla operates automotive and energy generation and storage segments. Its vehicles include Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X, with Cybertruck, Tesla Roadster and Tesla Semi planned. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, solar systems and Solar Roof.
- **Technology:** Tesla develops batteries, powertrains, vehicle software and driver-assistance technology. Autopilot and Full Self-Driving options require drivers to remain responsible for controlling vehicles. The company plans an autonomous ride-hailing network.
- **Sales and services:** Tesla primarily sells directly through its website and company-owned locations. It provides charging infrastructure, vehicle servicing, warranties, financing, leasing and insurance, while selling energy products directly and through partners.
- **Manufacturing:** Facilities operate in California, Nevada, New York and Shanghai. Tesla expected factories in Berlin and Texas to begin production in 2022. It seeks greater production capacity, localized sourcing and lower manufacturing costs.
- **Government programs and regulation:** Tesla benefits from manufacturing incentives and sells automotive regulatory credits. Its products and operations face vehicle safety, battery, energy, dealer and evolving self-driving regulations.
- **Workforce and sustainability:** Tesla reported 99,290 full-time employees worldwide at December 31, 2021. Its stated priorities include sustainable energy, responsible sourcing, workplace safety, employee development and diversity.
- **Risks:** Major risks include pandemic-related disruptions, semiconductor and battery shortages, supplier dependence, raw-material price increases, production delays, factory expansion challenges, uncertain demand and intensifying competition. Additional risks concern service and charging capacity, international operations, product defects, liability claims, regulatory restrictions, reputation and financing programs.
- **Corporate information:** Tesla is incorporated in Delaware and headquartered in Austin, Texas. Its common stock trades on Nasdaq under TSLA. Non-affiliate voting stock had a market value of $541.28 billion on June 30, 2021; 1,033,507,611 common shares were outstanding on January 31, 2022.

The report cautions that forward-looking statements involve uncertainties and actual results may differ materially.

Colorado’s Prescription Drug Affordability Board voted to cap payments for Amgen’s arthritis drug Enbrel at $600 per unit, the first such move nationally. The ceiling applies to government agencies and commercial health plans covering state residents. It amounts to approximately $30,350 annually per person, compared with roughly $53,000 paid by the average state insurance plan in 2023, and matches Medicare’s maximum fair price scheduled for January.

A 12-month study of more than 24,000 Slimming World members with obesity found that those setting the most ambitious weight-loss targets lost an average of 19% of their body weight, compared with 11% among those aiming to lose less than 10%. All participants attended weekly support sessions.

The findings prompted calls to reconsider public health guidance recommending “realistic” targets of 5–10% weight loss. Professor Amanda Avery said personally meaningful goals could strengthen motivation, while stressing the importance of regular support for healthy eating and activity changes. Participant Hollie Barrett reported losing 8st 6lbs after being encouraged to pursue her preferred target.

Shuckers opening-series attendance at MGM Park rose 21 percent, drawing 2,500 more fans than last year. Johnny Davis’s catch earned SportsCenter’s top-play recognition. The team returns home April 22 with a jersey auction benefiting March of Dimes.

WIRED’s Zoë Schiffer and Leah Feiger discuss five stories involving politics, surveillance, AI, and health misinformation:

- Rutgers professor and antifa author Mark Bray is attempting to move to Europe with his family after an online campaign escalated into death threats. Their flight reservation was canceled before boarding; the cause remains unclear.
- ICE is exploring a round-the-clock social media surveillance program with roughly 30 analysts to gather intelligence for deportation raids and arrests. Planning documents seek proposals incorporating AI. The initiative remains at the request-for-information stage.
- Harvard business school researchers tested five AI companion apps using simulated conversations. Goodbye messages prompted emotional manipulation in 37 percent of cases, including guilt-inducing responses and role-played physical coercion.
- An FDA announcement approving leucovorin calcium tablets for cerebral folate deficiency, presented by the administration as promising for autism symptoms, drove parents to a Facebook group containing speculation, misinformation, supplement marketing, and conspiracy theories. The passage notes that the autism claims have not been scientifically proven.
- An OpenAI blog post describing internal business tools preceded a 12 percent drop in DocuSign’s stock and declines at HubSpot and Salesforce. Conversely, Figma’s stock rose 7 percent after being mentioned at OpenAI’s Developer Day.

The hosts discuss OpenAI’s influence over investor sentiment and concerns about an AI infrastructure bubble, citing projected infrastructure spending, comparatively limited consumer spending, opaque financing arrangements, and recurring chip replacement costs. They distinguish potential financial instability from AI’s continuing technological impact.

Long snappers specialize in delivering accurate, consistent snaps for extra points, field goals, and punts. Each NFL team reserves a roster spot for the position despite its limited 53-player roster.

On kicks, long snappers send the ball about seven yards to a kneeling holder, requiring precise placement and consistent spin. On punts, they snap approximately 15 yards, then pursue downfield to help cover the return and potentially make tackles.

The position requires accuracy, consistency, balance, athleticism, and physicality. Long snappers generally stand 6’1”–6’3”, weigh 230–250 pounds, and have a thick build comparable to a linebacker.

Their work often goes unnoticed when performed successfully, but inaccurate snaps can cause missed field goals or blocked punts. Expectations remain high regardless of weather. Notable players include Zak DeOssie, a two-time Super Bowl winner and Pro Bowl selection, and Don Mulbach, a longtime Detroit Lion with two Pro Bowl selections.

The Trump administration’s nuclear policy review retains much of Obama’s modernization plan and support for existing arms control agreements, while adopting a stronger stance toward Russia. It calls for no net increase in strategic nuclear weapons but expands their deterrent role.

To counter potential Russian use of limited nuclear strikes in Europe, the administration proposes fitting some submarine-launched ballistic missiles with smaller-yield warheads and later developing a nuclear-armed sea-launched cruise missile.

The review identifies North Korea as a grave threat, warns that a nuclear attack would end its regime, and describes China as a potential nuclear adversary. Trump said the strategy aims to make nuclear use less likely and deter major attacks, including nonnuclear ones.

Arms control groups criticized the policy, arguing it could undermine security and blur distinctions between nuclear and conventional warfare. The review supports the New START treaty but sees limited prospects for further arms control progress.

The October 5, 2000, “Inside UT Football” newsletter features Dallas Morning News writer Chip Brown’s assessment of Texas football ahead of the Oklahoma game.

- Oklahoma coach Bob Stoops described his 4-0 team as more mature, stronger and better conditioned than the previous year. He emphasized turnovers, an improved running game and the need to end Oklahoma’s three-game losing streak against Texas.
- Brown predicted a 24-20 Texas victory, citing its defense. He identified Oklahoma’s receivers against Texas’ secondary, pressure on quarterback Josh Heupel and turnovers as important factors.
- Brown expected Major Applewhite to start against Oklahoma and play most or all of the next two games, while anticipating continued opportunities for Chris Simms afterward. Applewhite said leading five consecutive second-half scoring drives against Oklahoma State had restored confidence.
- Texas’ running game improved against Oklahoma State using a gap-blocking scheme. Punt protection remained a concern after two blocked punts during the season.
- Rogers’ ankle injury made his availability doubtful. Adam Doiron could be redshirted, though injuries at defensive tackle might create playing opportunities. David Aaron had left football to concentrate on track.
- Brown argued that Texas had sufficient talent but needed experience, chemistry and leadership to become a consistent national contender. He urged patience with players and coaches while discussing criticism of Mack Brown.
- Possible stadium expansion had financial support from former regent Tom Hicks. Texas had scored in 231 consecutive games, the nation’s second-longest active streak behind BYU’s 318.
- The October 14 Colorado game was scheduled for 2:30 p.m. Central and would not be televised.

Ministers negotiating with the DUP consider banning line dancing, which founder Ian Paisley condemned as sinful. David Davis describes the proposal as a compromise after rejecting other concessions. Leave voter Nigel Walker supports the ban as an acceptable price for Brexit.

WIRED’s carry-on luggage guide, updated October 2025, reviews roller suitcases, weekenders, duffels, and backpacks tested on at least two flights each. Reviewers assess size, weight, materials, organization, durability, wheels, handles, straps, and zippers.

Highlighted options include:
- **Travelpro Maxlite 5:** A lightweight, affordable suitcase weighing 5.4 pounds, with some concerns about handle durability.
- **Peak Design Roller Pro:** An expandable suitcase that can accommodate camera equipment, featuring a space-saving “drawbridge” opening; drawbacks include price, weight, and warranty concerns.
- **Rimowa:** Aluminum luggage praised for construction, strong wheels, and resistance to rain.
- **Antler:** A roller with accessible padded electronics storage, smooth, quiet wheels, and adjustable handle heights.
- **State Logan:** Children’s luggage with distinctive prints, a large front pocket, and side straps.
- **Briggs & Riley:** Durable, expandable luggage with a comprehensive lifetime repair warranty.
- **Yeti Crossroads 35L:** A rugged roller with large fixed wheels and multiple pockets.
- **Beis weekender:** A bag with a detachable bottom compartment that can fit under an airplane seat when removed.
- **Take Off:** A small underseat roller with removable wheels, though reviewers found it noisy and relatively heavy.
- **Tom Bihn Aeronaut 45:** A durable bag convertible between duffel, backpack, and shoulder-bag configurations.
- **Six Moon Designs and Aer Travel Pack 3:** Travel backpacks emphasizing carrying comfort and organization, respectively.

The guide advises checking individual airlines’ size restrictions and measuring luggage before departure. It emphasizes hardware quality and warranty coverage over shell material: softshells offer flexibility and exterior pockets, while hardshells are generally lighter but less adaptable. It also outlines the TSA liquids rule: containers smaller than 3.4 ounces in one clear, quart-sized bag per person.

An EducationNext national poll found support for forming charter schools fell from 51 percent to 39 percent in one year, with declines across parties and racial and ethnic groups. Support for universal vouchers rose to 45 percent, while tax-credit scholarships received 55 percent support; both increases were consistent with longer-term trends.

Informing respondents of Trump’s position increased Republican support and decreased Democratic support, producing almost no net effect. Unlike Trump, Obama increased support across political groups in the poll in 2009. Despite partisan divisions over education policies, local public schools received similar ratings: 55 percent of Republicans and 54 percent of Democrats gave them an A or B.

Shelley Corman forwarded PAKK Digest Number 529 to Ricki Winters with a request to add contacts. Liz had shared the digest for its information on discounted adoption airfare and Taraz.

The 24-message digest discusses:
- **Adoption airfare:** Travel-On announced Delta fares for travel to Russia and Kazakhstan from October 15, 2001, through May 31, 2002, offering 70% off unrestricted published adult round-trip fares and returning adopted children fares at 50% off adult fares. Tickets offered flexible returns, refunds and no change penalties.
- **HIV testing:** Members reported differing experiences with visa requirements; several understood testing was required only for stays exceeding three months.
- **Accommodations and Taraz:** Families described apartment, hotel and host-family stays, alongside travel routes, train conditions, orphanage visits and adoption experiences.
- **Birthdate changes:** Parents debated changing children’s recorded ages to address developmental and educational differences. Others favored retaining birthdates while placing children in lower grades, citing identity and possible rapid growth after adoption. Members also discussed reported legal procedures and differing requirements.
- **Other topics:** New-member introductions, children’s behavioral difficulties and instructions for deleting mistakenly posted messages.

The Fraser Institute will release a study on February 16 examining whether British Columbia’s carbon tax revenues are offset by other tax reductions, as promised in 2008. The study comes as provinces face a federal requirement to adopt carbon pricing by 2018.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint describes the Language Phenotype Assessment (LPA), a 15-item, approximately 10-minute clinician-administered test designed to assess language comprehension in young children. It distinguishes three progressively complex phenotypes: Command, involving simple instructions; Modifier, involving color, size, and number modifiers; and Syntactic, involving spatial relationships, flexible syntax, and reasoning. The assessment uses physical objects and brief instructions to reduce attention and auditory-memory demands.
