Researchers assessed 116 neurotypical children aged 1.5–7 years and 79 children diagnosed with autism spectrum disorder (ASD) aged 2–8 years. Parents also completed the 15-item Language Phenotype Evaluation Checklist (LPEC).

Among neurotypical participants, median acquisition ages measured by the LPA were 1.6 years for Command, 3.0 years for Modifier, and 3.7 years for Syntactic comprehension. All attained these phenotypes by ages 3, 4, and 5, respectively. Parent-reported median acquisition ages were 1.6, 2.7, and 3.0 years. Both assessments showed increasing scores through approximately age 5, followed by ceiling effects.

The LPA demonstrated high internal consistency (Cronbach’s alpha = 0.92), test-retest correlation (r = 0.96), and inter-observer agreement (98.7%). LPEC internal consistency was 0.91, and its test-retest correlation was 0.85. Clinician and parent scores correlated strongly (r = 0.78).

Among children with ASD aged 5 years or older, 39% attained the Syntactic Phenotype on the LPA, compared with all neurotypical peers. Autistic participants also showed greater difficulty following noncanonical rather than canonical word order.

The authors propose that these assessments could support early identification of comprehension deficits, monitoring of language development, and tailoring of therapy beyond vocabulary acquisition. They note that foundational vocabulary must be established before testing and that physical manipulatives create logistical challenges. The preprint states that its findings should not guide clinical practice.

The De’Longhi Rivelia automatic latte maker is discounted by $200 to $1,300. It prepares milk-based coffee drinks through touchscreen controls and features swappable bean hoppers, adjustable “bean adapt” settings, and a milk frother that produces silky microfoam. It simplifies preparation but does not match the potential coffee quality of a classic portafilter machine, and its frother produces less heat than a traditional steam wand.

Total solar eclipses have historically inspired fear and religious interpretations, including divine anger and apocalypse. In “American Eclipse,” David Baron describes how the 1878 eclipse terrified some Americans despite scientific understanding of the event. Some Christians also feared the approaching Aug. 21 eclipse, but Sister Mary Elizabeth of a Missouri monastery reassured callers that it was neither a bad omen nor a sign of Christ’s return. In Islamic tradition, Muhammad explained that an eclipse was a sign of God, not connected to a person’s death. Baron says eclipses can inspire profound awe even among nonreligious observers, emphasizing humanity’s smallness compared with the universe.

A funnel-web spider was found inside a home in Springwood, in the Blue Mountains near Sydney. Common but rarely seen along Australia’s east coast, funnel-webs favour cool, damp environments.

Taronga Zoo invertebrate keeper Paul Hare urged anyone bitten to seek immediate hospital treatment, as symptoms can develop quickly. The Australian Museum has recorded 13 deaths, but no fatalities have occurred since antivenene was introduced in 1981.

Hare described funnel-webs as defensive rather than aggressive. He advised leaving them alone, wearing gloves while gardening and avoiding placing bare hands where spiders may hide. They help control cockroaches, flies and mosquitoes.

Imran Mohammad, a Rohingya man recognized as a refugee by UNHCR, describes spending four birthdays in detention on Manus after arriving in Papua New Guinea in October 2013, aged 19. He recounts overcrowded shipping-container accommodation, extreme heat, inadequate toilets and laundry facilities, lengthy queues, shortages of basic supplies, and restrictions on food and family phone calls.

Mohammad describes severe emotional distress, isolation, hunger and thoughts of suicide. He found strength through prayer, hope, studying with teachers and developing his writing. To avoid conflict and queues, he altered his sleeping and eating routines and limited interactions with others. Although detainees were later allowed phones, slow internet continued to hinder communication. He reflects on the suffering of indefinite detention, separation from family, and the contrast between seeking safety in Australia and experiencing pain and anguish.

KGI analyst Ming-Chi Kuo predicts this year’s Apple Watch will retain its existing design for a third generation, contrary to an earlier report. He expects LTE and non-LTE versions in 38mm and 42mm sizes. The passage discusses potential changes, including reduced thickness or improved battery life, while noting that a major redesign could require substantial changes to the interface and apps.

The Triangle (1-3-1) offense attacks a Diamond & One defense by positioning the star player at the high post, isolating them against a defender primarily focused on pass denial. Drives create drop-pass opportunities for layups as teammates adjust their positions. If inside action produces no good shot, kick-out passes offer outside shots or dribble penetration, while post flashes provide additional options. When the defender overplays the high-post entry, the star cuts toward the basket for a lob.

Successful execution requires coordinated movement, interior passing, spot-up shooting, defensive recognition, communication and timing. Preparation includes isolation drills and scrimmaging. Teams should scout defensive tendencies and matchups, monitor adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders. The Diamond & One uses four zone defenders and one defender denying the opposing scoring ace.

The passage describes robotic systems that selectively grip and transport objects using multi-gripper assemblies with independently controlled vacuum regions. These regions can hold one or multiple objects, including irregularly shaped items and objects adjacent to others, and support simultaneous or sequential pickup and release.

The systems combine robotic arms, vacuum sources, manifold assemblies, controllers, imaging devices, and force or pressure sensors. Controllers analyze images to identify target objects, select gripping regions, and develop transport plans based on object arrangements, carrying capacity, available destination space, and transport paths. Stored object records can include dimensions, weight, appearance, and center-of-mass information, and can be updated during operation.

End-effector-mounted vision sensors monitor objects beneath the gripper, including areas obscured from external sensors. Their output supports positioning, pickup verification, object counting, and collision avoidance. Force and torque measurements can help determine package weight, position, and grip condition. Vacuum levels and airflow can be adjusted to maintain grip while limiting packaging damage.

Gripper configurations can vary in number, arrangement, and shape. Manifolds distribute suction to selected regions or suction elements. Compressible suction elements and sealing materials accommodate different object surfaces.

The operating process includes scanning pickup and destination areas, identifying objects, selecting vacuum regions, executing a motion plan, and checking grip quality. If an initial grip is insufficient, the system can release, reposition, and regrip within a defined attempt limit. Continued failure can stop the plan and prompt operator input. During transport, sensor feedback can trigger deviations from the plan if grip weakens or incorrect packages are held.

Applications described include warehouse unloading, palletizing, transport, loading, sorting, packaging, manufacturing, assembly, and healthcare automation.

The lecture distinguishes pointwise from uniform convergence of sequences of functions. Pointwise convergence requires convergence at each fixed point; uniform convergence requires a single index threshold that works across the entire domain. Uniform convergence implies pointwise convergence, but not conversely.

Examples illustrate the distinction:
- On \([0,1]\), \(f_n(x)=x^n\) converges pointwise to a function equal to zero for \(x<1\) and one at \(x=1\). Convergence is uniform on every \([0,b]\) with \(b<1\), but not on \([0,1]\).
- Triangular “tent” functions with base \([0,1/n]\) and height \(2n\) converge pointwise to zero, but not uniformly. Their integrals remain one, whereas the integral of the limit is zero.
- The functions \(x^n/n\) converge to zero, but their derivatives converge pointwise to a function that differs from the derivative of the limit.

The lecture frames continuity, differentiation, and integration of limits as questions about interchanging limiting processes. Pointwise convergence alone does not generally justify these interchanges.

Three results are proved:
1. A uniform limit of continuous functions is continuous, using an epsilon-over-three argument.
2. For continuous functions on \([a,b]\) converging uniformly, the integrals converge to the integral of the limit.
3. If continuously differentiable functions converge pointwise to \(f\), and their derivatives converge uniformly to \(g\), then \(f\) is continuously differentiable and \(f'=g\). The proof uses the fundamental theorem of calculus.

Finally, the Weierstrass M-test provides a sufficient condition for uniform convergence of a function series. If \(|f_j(x)|\le M_j\) throughout the domain and \(\sum_j M_j\) converges, then \(\sum_j f_j(x)\) converges absolutely at every point, and its partial sums converge uniformly. The proof bounds the remainder uniformly by a tail of the convergent numerical series. Together with preservation of continuity, this yields continuous functions defined by uniformly convergent series of continuous functions.

The team suffered a frustrating playoff loss after surrendering two-goal leads and allowing too many third-period chances. The speaker praised the team’s tenacity, credited Detroit’s hard play, and expressed determination to rebound.

In a September 1, 1814 proclamation, President James Madison condemns enemy destruction of public buildings in the nation’s capital, plundering of Alexandria, and British plans to devastate coastal communities. He rejects the British justification of retaliation for American destruction in Upper Canada and criticizes these actions amid peace negotiations. Madison urges national unity against the invasion, directs civil and military officers to fulfill their duties, and authorizes military district commanders to summon nearby militia to defend threatened areas, regardless of federal service quotas.

At least 30 children died at Gorakhpur’s BRD Hospital, where a central team found patient numbers at 10 times admission capacity and multiple infants sharing warmers. Reports highlighted overcrowding, oxygen supply problems and non-existent or non-functional newborn care units in nearby districts. Union health officials announced an Rs 85 crore regional medical centre in Gorakhpur for research on children’s diseases.

The incoming president pledges to uphold the Constitution and preserve its benefits for future generations. He credits constitutional government with advancing liberty, prosperity, territorial expansion, and national security, while acknowledging disease, foreign conflict, and internal divisions.

He urges citizens to abandon lingering partisan hostility and judge public servants by talent and virtue. Warning that geographical divisions may be more enduring and dangerous than policy disagreements, he emphasizes mutual respect between state and federal governments and protection of their respective powers. He affirms popular elections, fiscal accountability, civilian control of the military, freedom of the press and religious opinion, peace, and national union.

Praising his predecessor’s administration, he highlights debt reduction, repeal of internal taxes, military reforms, acquisition of the Floridas, recognition of independence among southern nations of the hemisphere, and progress in defense and internal improvements. He promises to continue these policies, particularly public works, while seeking resolution of constitutional disagreements over federal authority.

Acknowledging that he enters office with less public confidence than his predecessors, he pledges devoted service and seeks cooperation from Congress, executive departments, state governments, and citizens, alongside divine guidance.

The speaker attributed the tight hockey game’s outcome to missed scoring opportunities, mistakes and favorable bounces for the opposition. They described a goal following blocked shots and a rebound off the boards, and an unusual puck resting on Osgood’s back that someone covered with a hand. The speaker also acknowledged striking an opponent’s foot in response to taunting. Despite conceding at a key moment, the team continued generating chances. The speaker expected a difficult series, maintained confidence in the team’s play and looked ahead to preparing for the next game.

A recent music education graduate living at home describes financial strain and conflict with their mother. With no savings and a three-month minimum-wage job about to begin, they owe $1,700 in tuition, need about $600 for certification exams, and want to save for a car and apartment. Their mother demands $480 monthly for rent and phone costs. The graduate says she imposed rent after mistaking their hearing difficulty for ignoring her and previously withheld a $5,000 school refund while charging $3,000 in rent.

The columnist recommends budgeting carefully, considering additional jobs, and exploring different work experiences rather than rushing into an expected post-college life. They also encourage honesty about the family conflict, saying the mother’s reported behavior warrants professional help if accurately described, while urging the graduate to acknowledge any role they may have played and consider their mother’s perspective.

The global aluminum foil packaging market is expected to grow at approximately 4.5% CAGR during the forecast period, driven by packaging innovation, pharmaceutical and cosmetic demand, changing lifestyles, and rising spending power. Aluminum packaging protects products from contamination and helps reduce waste. Limited recycling processes in some countries may constrain growth. Manufacturers are researching production locations and shorter supply distances to reduce costs. Asia Pacific is expected to be the fastest-growing regional market, supported by rising per capita income and consumer purchasing power.

MyWorld is a gaming platform where players create games, control rules and multiplayer options, and save creations locally or share them with the community. Design mode allows object placement, while constructor mode provides a model editor for creating objects, including functional devices. Players unlock pre-built materials through progression and can customize avatars. Demonstrated on livestream but not yet ready for release, MyWorld has launched a Kickstarter campaign to fund further development, offering exclusive materials to early backers.

Apple announced on February 5, 2019, that Angela Ahrendts, Senior Vice President of Retail, would depart effective April 15, 2019. Deirdre O’Brien succeeded her, assuming the role of Senior Vice President, Retail + People, effective February 5, 2019.

Successful Forex trading requires skills rather than exceptional talent or expectations of quick profits. Traders should wait for suitable opportunities, make independent decisions, and develop their own trading styles rather than copy experts. Mental stability helps traders accept losses without taking excessive risks. The passage emphasizes mastering technical, fundamental, and sentiment analysis, improving judgment, and starting small to develop gradually. Expert advice can provide knowledge, but inexperienced traders should consider it carefully before acting.

The passage proposes a new semantics for deontic argumentation, which concerns whether actions or states of affairs are obligatory or permitted. It focuses on weak permission: an action is weakly permitted when the obligation prohibiting it cannot be justified.

Grounded and stable argumentation semantics fail to justify weak permissions in the presence of unresolved conflicts between obligations. This also prevents those permissions from supporting subsequent reasoning.

The proposed wp-semantics builds on argumentation semantics for Defeasible Logic. It distinguishes natural arguments, derived from facts and rules, from imaginary arguments representing potential weak permissions. An iterative construction identifies accepted and rejected arguments. Weak-permission arguments are accepted when all arguments supporting the contrary obligation are rejected.

The paper presents results establishing that the wp-extension is unique, conflict-free, and never classifies an argument as both justified and rejected. It also states that wp-semantics preserves arguments justified under grounded semantics. When conflicting obligations have justified premises, the approach supports weak permissions for both an action and its opposite, allowing further conclusions that depend on those permissions.

The discussion argues that withholding justification from unresolved conflicting obligations avoids unavoidable sanctions and ad hoc legal resolutions. Future work includes integrating competing approaches to ambiguity and developing a semantic account of deontic operators.

The National Technology Security Coalition (NTSC) and Cloud Security Alliance (CSA) are partnering to improve cloud vendor security evaluations by promoting CSA’s Security, Trust & Assurance Registry (STAR) and related tools. They will develop a STAR-based questionnaire mapped to commonly used compliance frameworks and a whitepaper explaining implementation for CISOs and vendors. The partnership aims to streamline security reviews, encourage best practices, and improve vendor transparency. The organizations will also participate in each other’s events, discuss industry issues in working groups, and collaborate on cloud security research.

The May 9, 2001 news compilation covers Enron-related developments in India, Japan and other markets:

- **Dabhol dispute:** Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) had defaulted on payments, citing high electricity costs, while Dabhol Power Company pursued arbitration and possible termination of its power purchase agreement. Lenders indicated they might support termination unless governments resolved the crisis; a three-week reprieve expired May 15. MSEB appointed former Bombay High Court judge M. L. Pendse as arbitrator. Enron agreed to meet a government panel but said attendance did not imply willingness to renegotiate.
- **Personnel and political developments:** Reports said expatriate executives’ families were relocating from Mumbai to Singapore and security had increased amid uncertainty over Dabhol. It was unclear whether relocation reflected corporate or personal decisions. The Swadeshi Jagran Manch demanded a judicial investigation and cancellation of the deal. MSEB denied federal pressure to retain the agreement.
- **Power supply:** MSEB rejected allegations that it underused its own generating capacity to justify Dabhol purchases. It cited gas shortages, costly alternative fuel and the need to maintain grid frequency.
- **Japan:** Enron said regulatory barriers and transmission charges hindered competition and called for an independent power regulator. New entrants held only 0.2% of the market.
- **Other energy business:** Williams planned a London-based European trading and risk-management operation. Prize Petroleum sought Enron’s 30% stake in the Panna, Mukta and Tapti fields, valuing it at approximately Rs 600 crore.
- **Corporate and market news:** Questia, backed by investors including Enron Chairman Ken Lay, cut 139 jobs and slowed book digitization because additional financing was difficult to obtain. Enron shares fell $1.93 to $56.11 during a mixed stock-market session.

This optimization study tested a mobile health platform combining behavioral sleep promotion and financial incentives for children with insufficient sleep. Ninety-seven children aged 9–12 from southeastern Pennsylvania and southern New Jersey participated. Average baseline weeknight sleep duration was 7.7 hours.

After a two-week run-in, participants underwent a seven-week intervention and two-week follow-up. All received Fitbit sleep tracking and weekly performance feedback. A factorial design tested five components: guideline-based versus personalized sleep goals, child-directed and caregiver-directed loss-framed financial incentives, screen-time reduction messaging, and daily-routine messaging. Active incentives provided a $70 endowment, with $2 deducted for each weeknight the sleep goal was missed.

Overall, weeknight sleep increased by an average of 24 minutes during intervention and 21 minutes during follow-up. No individual component setting achieved the predefined target of a 30-minute increase. Two component combinations met that target during intervention:

- Sleep tracking, feedback, a sleep goal, caregiver-directed incentives, and both messaging components increased sleep by 39.6 minutes during intervention and 33.2 minutes during follow-up.
- The same combination without screen-time messaging increased sleep by 32.0 minutes during intervention and 26.6 minutes during follow-up.

Both sleep-goal settings were equally effective in these combinations. Child-directed incentives did not improve effectiveness.

Limitations included a single geographic setting, a predominantly non-Hispanic White sample, fewer recorded nights among Black participants, short follow-up, and reliance on a single-sensor commercial tracker with a proprietary algorithm. The researchers plan a randomized controlled trial to evaluate the optimized intervention; its long-term effects remain undetermined.

Tesla’s Form 8-K reported results from its October 7, 2021 annual stockholder meeting:

- James Murdoch and Kimbal Musk were elected as Class II directors for three-year terms.
- Management proposals to shorten director terms to two years and eliminate applicable supermajority voting requirements failed to obtain approval from at least 66⅔% of outstanding common shares.
- Stockholders ratified PricewaterhouseCoopers LLP as independent auditor for fiscal 2021.
- Non-binding advisory stockholder proposals supporting one-year director terms and additional diversity and inclusion reporting were approved.
- Non-binding advisory proposals concerning employee arbitration reporting, independent board-committee oversight of human capital management, and additional human rights reporting were not approved.

Consumer Electricals Ltd submitted a bid for Kenstar’s business and brand on September 20, 2017. The price was undisclosed, results were pending, and no negotiations or binding agreements had occurred. Kenstar’s parent, Videocon, was considering asset sales to reduce debt exceeding Rs 40,000 crore.

Police arrested Zette Madden, 52, after she allegedly threatened Oklahoma City Taco Bell employees with a tire iron, demanded money and caused thousands of dollars in damage. An officer tased her after repeated commands to drop the weapon. She received treatment for cuts and remains jailed on property destruction and robbery charges.

Riley Oil Company in Paoli, Indiana, is one of the area’s last full-service gas stations, pumping gas, washing windshields and checking oil at no extra charge. Founded by Glendon Riley in 1971, the business employs six Riley family members. Owners Jo Ann and Jeff Riley value conversations with customers and expect the station to remain family-run for generations.

Daniella Teutsch and Sara Wolf founded HydroChic in 2007 to offer attractive, modest swimwear. Customer feedback revealed demand from women who had undergone mastectomies or bariatric surgery, or had skin conditions. They expanded into garments offering support, concealment, compression and skin protection. Serving women with health needs became a business cornerstone, bringing financial rewards and positive feedback from customers who felt more comfortable being active.

On June 2, 2022, Microsoft updated its guidance for the quarter ending June 30, 2022, citing unfavorable foreign exchange rate movements through May. The revised guidance was furnished in a slide deck as Exhibit 99.1 to its Form 8-K. Microsoft cautioned that forward-looking statements are subject to risks and uncertainties and that it undertakes no duty to update them. The report and exhibit are not deemed filed for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act.

Falkland Islands fisheries scientist Alexander Arkhipkin warned that largely unregulated high-seas catches constrain assessments of shared fish stocks and increase overfishing risks. More than 250 vessels fish annually in the Southwest Atlantic, while almost 300 foreign jiggers target jumbo squid in the Eastern Pacific. In September 2017, Arkhipkin joined an international workshop hosted by Peru’s IMARPE. Participants developed recommendations on surveys, stock analysis and assessment methods to improve squid research, international collaboration and understanding of high-seas fishing impacts.

Nintendo confirmed that Labo will include Toy Con Garage, a kit for creating custom cardboard accessories using basic inputs, actions, and if-then statements. Demonstrations included a cardboard electric guitar and electronic tennis. Whether access requires purchasing a Labo set remains unclear.

Darren Till defeated Stephen Thompson by a controversial unanimous decision at UFC Fight Night 130 in Liverpool on May 27, 2018. Amid criticism of the scoring and location, Till offered a rematch in America as soon as possible, provided Thompson was uninjured. The close fight featured little action beyond Till’s final-round knockdown.

Legal experts expect higher education to feature prominently in the Supreme Court’s new term, particularly through its emergency, or shadow, docket. Unlike regular proceedings, emergency rulings can arrive within days or weeks, often without explanations, leaving universities little time to prepare.

Two college-related cases on the main docket, West Virginia v. B.P.J. and Little v. Hecox, concern transgender athletes barred by state laws from participating in women’s sports. Hecox has requested dismissal because she no longer intends to participate. Experts say rulings could affect matters beyond athletics, including bathrooms, locker rooms and other protections against discrimination.

Potential emergency-docket issues include immigration policies, federal funding, academic freedom and First Amendment challenges. Trump v. Orr concerns whether transgender and nonbinary people can obtain passports matching their gender identity; experts warn that broader application could complicate university operations.

The court has allowed administration policies affecting higher education to proceed while litigation continues. Experts caution that resulting changes could cause irreversible harm before final rulings are issued.

British banks should expect few further regulatory changes following Basel III implementation, BoE regulator Vicky Saporta said. The central bank will focus on emerging risks and unintended regulatory consequences, including cybersecurity and leverage rules discouraging central clearing.

Aaron Judge is unsure whether his injured elbow will require surgery this offseason. The late-July injury sidelined him for 10 days and limited him to designated hitter duties for nearly a month. His arm strength remained diminished after returning to the outfield, but his hitting was unaffected. Judge said he plans to address the injury.

The Department of Justice asked the Education Department to investigate the University of Nevada at Reno’s UndocuPack program, questioning whether taxpayer funds support illegal immigration. University president Brian Sandoval defended the program, saying it serves all students regardless of citizenship, receives no federal funding and complies with federal and state law. The university plans to respond through legal channels.

Advocates describe the move as an escalation of federal efforts targeting undocumented students’ access to higher education, following challenges to in-state tuition policies and scholarships. They fear universities could reduce or eliminate lawful support programs to avoid scrutiny. Diego Sánchez of the Presidents’ Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration said no court has interpreted the cited federal benefits law as prohibiting such campus support services. TheDream.US leader Gaby Pacheco warned that scaling back programs could make undocumented students feel unwelcome without preventing federal attention.

The study combines molecular dynamics nanoindentation simulations with orientation-resolved Schmid factor mapping to examine temperature-dependent plasticity in single-crystalline α-titanium. Simulations investigated the [0001], [10̅10], and [2̅110] orientations at 10, 300, and 600 K, analyzing load–displacement behavior, dislocation networks, strain distributions, and surface morphology.

Temperature and crystallographic orientation strongly influenced deformation. The [0001] orientation showed pronounced pop-in events marking plasticity onset and the greatest residual indentation depth, while the other orientations exhibited smoother dislocation nucleation. Contact pressure stabilized beyond approximately 3 nm indentation depth and decreased with increasing temperature.

Basal and prismatic slip accommodated much of the deformation, with pyramidal ⟨c+a⟩ slip becoming more active at elevated temperatures. Stress-driven HCP-to-BCC transformations were favored at low temperatures, where dislocation mobility was limited. Higher temperatures generally produced broader plastic zones, more diffuse slip traces, and enhanced recovery. Regions with high Schmid factors coincided with plastic deformation beneath the indenter.

Surface patterns differed by orientation: [0001] produced circular or quasi-hexagonal pile-up, [10̅10] developed symmetric dual lobes, and [2̅110] exhibited asymmetric curved features. Prismatic loops formed through a lasso mechanism particularly evident in [10̅10] at 300 K, whereas loops in [2̅110] nucleated beneath the indenter and expanded through glide and interactions.

The [0001] orientation retained the highest dislocation density, increasing from 0.86 to 1.52 × 10¹⁶ m⁻² between 10 and 600 K. Over the same range, densities decreased from 0.45 to 0.38 × 10¹⁶ m⁻² for [10̅10] and from 0.41 to 0.12 × 10¹⁶ m⁻² for [2̅110], reflecting enhanced recovery and annihilation. The simulated surface features agreed closely with reported AFM observations.

The disclosure describes physical-layer preamble and signaling designs for wireless communications, including IEEE 802.11be and future protocols. The designs address bandwidths up to and potentially beyond 320 MHz, flexible resource allocation, subchannel puncturing, and signaling across multiple content channels while limiting preamble length.

A universal signal field (U-SIG), placed after legacy signaling, identifies the protocol version, packet format, and frequency occupation. Receiving devices use this information to determine the packet format, locate subchannels carrying version-specific signaling, and decode those fields. U-SIG may contain version-independent information, such as uplink/downlink indication, BSS color, and transmission opportunity duration, alongside version-dependent fields.

An Extremely High Throughput signal field (EHT-SIG) may follow U-SIG and carry resource-unit allocations, spatial-stream configurations, user-specific scheduling information, and overflow information from U-SIG. Its structure varies by packet format: trigger-based packets may omit EHT-SIG, while single-user and multi-user packets may use separate or unified formats. Compression options can omit unnecessary allocation information.

Bandwidth and puncturing information may be represented through combined indicators, separate subfields, lookup tables, or bitmaps. Signaling may describe the entire channel or individual 80 MHz portions, including puncturing at 20 MHz granularity. EHT-SIG content may be duplicated or distributed across subchannels, with signaling omitted from punctured subchannels.

Additional design options support OFDMA, multi-user MIMO, full-bandwidth, partial-bandwidth, and aggregated resource allocations, and up to or potentially more than 16 spatial streams. The disclosure also describes receiver methods, processor-based apparatuses, computer-readable instructions, wireless-device architectures, and possible modifications to spatial-reuse signaling.

The passage describes a method, system, and computer program product for mobile payments when user devices and merchant payment systems cannot connect to payment servers.

An e-wallet’s offline payment mode is enabled on only one associated device at a time to prevent multiple devices from exceeding reserved funds. Users select an amount to reserve for offline purchases, which the payment server checks against available funds and pre-authorizes. Devices with offline mode enabled can still make online payments when connectivity is available.

During an offline transaction, the merchant sends a payment request through local communications, such as Bluetooth, NFC, a local network, USB, or QR-code scanning. The user device checks its remaining offline balance, rejects requests with insufficient funds, and otherwise seeks user approval. After approval, it reduces the stored balance and sends a payment approval message to the merchant.

Both the user device and merchant retain transaction information and submit it to the payment server when connectivity returns. The server checks transaction identifiers to prevent duplicate processing, debits the payer’s account, updates the pre-authorized offline amount, and credits the merchant’s account.

Offline payment mode can also be transferred between devices without server connectivity. The devices exchange wallet and balance information through local communications, temporarily suspend offline payments, and confirm that the original device’s offline mode is disabled before enabling the receiving device. When a transfer is requested through the server, the server refuses to enable another device if it cannot contact the currently enabled device to disable its offline mode.

Implementation may use cloud computing or other computing environments.

The High Post Split Offense uses a 2-3 high alignment, quick splits, down screens and back cuts to create scoring opportunities for all five players. Its spacing opens the baseline for cuts, limits defensive help and supports offensive rebounding. Entries can be adapted to individual players’ strengths.

The offense has four main phases:
- **High post split:** A guard passes to the high post and cuts first, followed closely by the other guard. Counters to defensive anticipation include fake splits, direct basket cuts and both guards cutting to the same side.
- **Down screens:** If neither guard receives a pass, the wings screen for them. Options include curls, fades, back cuts, screen-and-roll actions and slipping screens, depending on the defense.
- **High post isolation:** The high post faces the basket in a triple-threat position to shoot, drive or pass. Overplayed entries can be countered with lob passes, wing feeds or player exchanges. The position should be occupied by the best triple-threat player, not necessarily a post player.
- **Strong post-ups:** Players exploit smaller defenders inside when the defense focuses on stopping shooters.

Entry variations include wing back cuts, wing passes, weakside double screens and single/double-screen actions. Offensive rebounding requires anticipation, determination, hustle and repeated efforts; players should expect missed shots and box out defenders.

Successful execution depends on spacing, timing, coordination, defensive recognition and individual skill development. Ballhandlers, screeners and receivers must function together, while coaches remain alert to defensive adjustments.

The disclosure describes a folding tonneau cover for pickup truck beds, with a fixed base panel and movable, hinged panel sections. Its features include interconnected pinch latches, vertical supports, sealing components, adjustable side rails, and a buckle securement system.

Each movable panel can have spring-loaded latch assemblies on opposite sides, joined by a connector. Pinching either handle retracts both latches, allowing the panel to be released from one side of the truck. Releasing the handles returns the latches to their latched positions. The assemblies fit substantially flush within the panel frames and may incorporate removable lights that illuminate the bed and help locate the handles.

Rail-mounted gussets support folded panels upright by engaging the panel latches. These supports can slide along the rails, pivot beneath the panels for storage, and be removed. Hinges incorporate resilient seals, spacers, and seal rods to maintain separation, improve sealing, and reduce slipping or misalignment.

Side rails attach to the truck bed walls through adjustable clamps and carry movable latch clips. Rail seals, panel edges, and tailgate gaskets help limit water entry.

A channel bracket on the base panel receives folded panels and keeps them off its surface. Buckle straps secure the panels upright against movement or hold them folded horizontally to prevent unfolding while the truck is moving.

Martin Colin Hodder, 45, was jailed for 18 weeks after admitting two assaults on his ex-partner and her daughter. He injured both women with a butter knife during a sustained attack after drinking one and a half bottles of vodka. The sentence included a year-long restraining order. His ex-partner condemned the sentence as inadequate. Hodder had previous violence convictions, though his defence said he had not been in trouble for six years.

Ben Bishop said he felt better after a couple of days, making it easier to play. He credited Doug Armstrong and Bryan Murray with providing opportunities and said several years in the minors helped prepare him for his chance in Tampa. Bishop emphasized maintaining the same preparation regardless of a game’s stakes and credited team consistency for playoff success. He expected the team to bounce back after a loss and described enjoying the experience with his teammates.

The passage describes semiconductor packaging methods for forming large multi-die integrated fan-out (InFO) packages for high-performance computing, advanced networking, servers, and artificial intelligence applications. It identifies thermal expansion differences among packaging materials as a source of stress, delamination, and electrical failures.

In one manufacturing approach, tested, known-good interconnect structures are attached to a temporary carrier, encapsulated, and planarized to expose electrical contacts. These structures may contain through-substrate vias, metallization layers, redistribution layers, and protective layers. Tested semiconductor packages containing processors, memory cubes, or other components are then bonded to the interconnect structures using direct copper-to-copper bonding or solder bonding. Underfill protects the connections, and a second encapsulant surrounds the semiconductor packages. After thinning and carrier removal, external contacts are formed for connection to other devices.

Alternative configurations allow semiconductor packages to bridge adjacent interconnect structures or share a single universal interconnect structure. Another approach forms multiple universal redistribution layers over encapsulated interconnect structures, then bonds semiconductor components to those layers before underfilling, encapsulating, thinning, and removing the carrier.

The disclosed methods support package sizes greater than 70 mm by 70 mm and allow completed packages to connect to printed circuit boards without further singulation. The passage attributes improved component and board reliability to using known-good components, lower-temperature bonding, protective underfill, and package thermal expansion characteristics close to those of connected components and circuit boards. Wafer-form integration also simplifies the manufacturing process.

Coach Julien said an injured player was being evaluated and he had no further update. He praised a replacement’s performance in Bergy’s spot despite limited league experience and unfamiliarity with the line. Julien said his team improved in the third period after sitting back too much earlier and needed greater awareness around the net, where Kane had found scoring opportunities.

Facing a must-win home game, Julien described the group as committed and determined to bounce back. He emphasized that every player must contribute and that playoff success requires depth and secondary scoring rather than reliance on top players.

Julien defended Zdeno against criticism, praising his defensive ability, offensive contributions, conditioning and leadership. He explained that lineup and defensive-pair changes reflected matchups and available options. Gregory Campbell’s injury had prompted consideration of Daugavins, Soderberg and Pandolfo, with the choice depending on the team’s needs.

He said the team needed better starts and described momentum shifts caused by penalties, poor shifts and sustained offensive pressure. Both coaches were adjusting lines and matchups to gain an advantage. Julien expected another competitive game but said scoring, penalties and goaltending made its course difficult to predict. In overtime, he sought an early goal, used the bench to help players recover, then shortened it, prioritizing scoring opportunities over line matching.

Enron’s shares closed at $4.01 on November 26, 2001, down about 15%, amid growing doubts that Dynegy’s proposed acquisition would proceed under its original terms. Enron’s bonds also fell sharply. Investors questioned its financial disclosures following a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity, a $586 million earnings restatement and revelations of additional financial obligations.

Dynegy continued due diligence and maintained its previously stated commitment to the merger, while board members declined comment. Analysts warned that declining trading volumes reduced Enron’s value and that cancellation of the acquisition could threaten its survival. Dynegy’s bonds also weakened over concerns that acquiring Enron would damage its credit rating.

Enron sought additional financing and finalized an extension of a $690 million loan deadline to December 14. A downgrade below investment grade could trigger another $3.9 billion in debt repayments. Citigroup had entered transactions potentially transferring approximately $2.38 billion of Enron credit exposure to institutional investors.

A third employee retirement-plan lawsuit sought $850 million, alleging Enron encouraged purchases of artificially inflated shares and sold stock without a required prospectus. Employees had been prevented from selling shares during an administrative lockdown. The litigation prompted calls to limit employer-stock holdings in 401(k) plans.

Other reports said Petrobras and Petros were nearing regulatory approval to purchase Enron’s stakes in Brazilian gas distributors. India’s AV Birla group denied interest in Enron’s Dabhol stake. Broader energy-sector coverage highlighted weak stock valuations and increased scrutiny of accounting practices and financial disclosure.

The speaker describes the team’s latest win as essential to remaining competitive in the Stanley Cup finals against New Jersey. Improved skating helped generate offense, increase physical play and make the game more even after two games with little speed, flow or attacking pressure. However, the team still needs better puck management and stronger second periods.

The speaker emphasizes winning faceoffs to gain possession, creating chances through proper positioning, involving players in the rush and maintaining familiar strategies under pressure. Players are praised for professionalism, contributions and leadership, particularly Carney, whose poise helps settle the team.

New Jersey’s success is credited to strong team play rather than individual players alone, although Brodeur’s important saves are acknowledged. The speaker stresses resilience, preparation and emotional control, urging the team to focus on its own performance rather than media coverage. The win allowed players to absorb technical feedback more effectively, but further improvement is necessary. The speaker believes hard work earns opportunities and that the best team will win the Stanley Cup.

University of Michigan researchers developed a clear, durable “omniphobic” coating that repels nearly every known liquid and prevents grime buildup on surfaces. Inspired by making cleanup after children easier, the coating combines fluorinated polyurethane and F-POSS. Researchers envision applications in homes, daycares and industry and are studying whether the material is toxic.

Microsoft’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended June 30, 2021 describes its businesses, strategy, workforce, operations, and competitive risks. Common stock held by non-affiliates had a market value of $1.7 trillion on December 31, 2020; approximately 7.515 billion shares were outstanding on July 26, 2021.

Microsoft develops and supports software, cloud services, devices, gaming products, and advertising solutions. Its three operating segments are:
- **Productivity and Business Processes:** Office, Microsoft 365, LinkedIn, and Dynamics.
- **Intelligent Cloud:** Azure, server products, developer tools, GitHub, and enterprise support and consulting.
- **More Personal Computing:** Windows, Surface and accessories, Xbox hardware and services, and search advertising.

Its strategy emphasizes productivity and collaboration, cloud and edge computing, artificial intelligence, security, and personal computing. Microsoft continues investing in datacenters, hybrid infrastructure, developer tools, mixed reality, and gaming content and distribution. It acquired ZeniMax Media in March 2021, agreed to acquire Nuance Communications in April 2021, and announced Windows 11 in June 2021.

As of June 30, 2021, Microsoft employed approximately 181,000 full-time workers, including 103,000 in the United States and 78,000 internationally. Workforce initiatives address inclusion, pay equity, employee development, wellness, and flexible working. Pandemic responses included remote work, expanded leave, testing, vaccinations, and additional health benefits.

Microsoft’s sustainability commitments include becoming carbon negative, water positive, and zero waste by 2030, and removing its historical carbon emissions by 2050. It committed $1 billion over four years to climate technologies and solutions. Its racial-equity initiatives include increasing Black and African American representation in specified U.S. leadership and professional roles, supporting businesses and communities, and expanding access to technology and education. Identified risks include intense competition, competing platform ecosystems, free and open-source offerings, and uncertainty in executing cloud strategies. Competitive pressures and infrastructure investment could reduce revenue or margins. Cloud success depends on customer adoption, developer participation, compatibility, reliability, security, and compliance. COVID-19’s future business effects remain uncertain, and forward-looking statements are subject to risks and assumptions.

Queen Elizabeth visited young victims of the Manchester bombing and met medical staff and emergency responders. The attack killed 22 and injured more than 100. She described it as “wicked” and noted local unity.

The Triangle Post Offense, developed and refined by Tex Winter, relies on reading the defense rather than running set plays. Its three components are entries, a sideline triangle, and a weakside two-player game. Every player must understand each position’s options and execute basketball fundamentals and footwork.

Players maintain spacing of 15–20 feet to discourage defensive help and double-teaming while creating passing lanes, post opportunities, drives, and cuts. Multiple pass and dribble entries allow the triangle to form on either side of the court, with entry choices dictated by defensive positioning.

Sideline triangle options include post isolations, post splits, give-and-go cuts, and screen-and-roll actions. The weakside two-player game uses passes, handoffs, and screens to generate drives, jump shots, rolls, and mismatches. Players counter defensive overplay through back cuts, lob passes, ball reversals, penetration, and passes to open teammates.

Successful implementation requires coordinated execution, defensive recognition, and individual skill development. Teaching progresses through two-player and three-player drills, combined actions, and full scrimmages. Game preparation emphasizes scouting expected defensive responses, explaining counters, monitoring adjustments, and varying entries.

On February 26, 2003, the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of Alabama granted summary judgment to Waste Away Group, Inc., on Paula Norrell’s Title VII claims of sex discrimination and disparate impact.

Norrell, an employee since 1996 who had received promotions and positive evaluations, applied to manage the company’s combined Montgomery and Opelika sales districts in 2001. Waste Away selected Terry White, a male employee who had previously managed the combined district. The company offered Norrell another sales position at a slightly lower salary. She declined after maternity leave and left the company.

The court found that Norrell established a prima facie failure-to-promote case because she was qualified, applied, was rejected, and the position went to a man. Waste Away nevertheless articulated a legitimate, nondiscriminatory explanation: it considered White the most qualified candidate based on his relevant experience, market knowledge, and leadership and organizational skills.

The court concluded that Norrell failed to establish a genuine factual dispute over whether that explanation was a pretext for discrimination. Her alleged instruction to train White, supervisors’ remarks concerning women and pregnancy, and comparisons of qualifications were insufficient. The court found that the decisionmakers independently interviewed and evaluated the candidates and that the challenged remarks did not establish discriminatory motivation in the promotion decision.

Norrell acknowledged after discovery that she was not pursuing a disparate-impact claim. The court entered judgment for Waste Away on all claims and assessed costs against Norrell.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, measure asset volatility and potential trend changes. They consist of a moving average with upper and lower bands calculated by adding and subtracting multiples of standard deviation.

TradingView allows users to adjust the default 20-period moving average, standard deviation multiplier, and price source, or construct the indicator using Pine Script. Breakout strategies seek to capitalize on prices breaching the bands.

Limitations include false signals, reduced effectiveness in range-bound markets, delayed signals, and sensitivity to settings. Bollinger Bands alone do not ensure profitability; trading rules, parameter testing, backtesting, and risk definition are necessary. An example using the H4 time frame and all capital per trade produced considerable returns but potentially uncomfortable drawdowns. TradingView supports developing breakout, mean-reversion, and squeeze strategies using the indicator.

The passage describes peripherals, implementation guidance, development support, and packaging information for Texas Instruments MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers.

- **Low-frequency subsystem:** LFSS_B contains the RTC_B real-time clock and an independent watchdog timer. Its typical 32kHz clock supports long-term timekeeping and low-power operation.
- **RTC_B:** Provides calendar counters, alarms, periodic interrupts, binary or BCD formatting, leap-year correction for 1901–2099, crystal calibration, temperature-drift compensation, and clock output for calibration.
- **Watchdogs:** IWDT uses an independent clock and generates a power-on reset if software fails to service it within the programmed interval, with eight selectable periods from 2ms to 2 hours. WWDT supports reset or interrupt generation, eight periods, automatic stopping during sleep, and interval-timer operation.
- **Timers:** General-purpose TIMG and advanced TIMA timers support programmable prescalers, synchronization, cross-triggering, and interrupt/DMA generation. Advanced timers additionally provide complementary PWM, programmable dead bands, repeat counters, and fault handling.
- **Connections and interfaces:** Enabling DAC_OUT connects it to PA15, where external signals are not recommended during DAC_OUT use. IOMUX controls peripheral selection, digital input/output paths, and shutdown wake-up logic; available features vary by pin. Debug access uses a two-wire SWD interface.
- **Bootloader and factory data:** The boot strap loader supports UART or I2C programming and configuration, protected by a user-defined 256-bit password. It is enabled by default but can be disabled. Invocation can occur through a hardware condition, unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or software command. A read-only FACTORY region contains device capabilities, identification, revision, and trim information.
- **Application guidance:** TI recommends nearby 10µF and 0.1µF supply-decoupling capacitors and a 47kΩ pullup with a 10nF pulldown capacitor on NRST. SYSOSC frequency correction requires an external 100kΩ precision resistor. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47µF capacitor and must not connect to other circuits. Open-drain outputs require pullup resistors to output high.
- **Development and documentation:** Resources include development hardware, SDKs, SysConfig, training, graphical tools, IDEs, compiler toolchains, technical manuals, and support forums. “X” identifies experimental devices; “MSP” identifies qualified production devices. TI recommends production use only of qualified devices and appropriate ESD precautions.
- **Revisions and packaging:** The April 2025 revision updates device features, electrical specifications, peripheral descriptions, and package options. Packaging sections provide assembly guidance and identify automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions.
- **Responsibilities:** Application guidance is outside the component specification. TI provides technical resources “as is”; customers are responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

Jane Goodall, who died October 1 at 91, left a scientific legacy that includes a collection of chimpanzee skeletons from Tanzania’s Gombe National Park. Because the chimps’ ages, sexes, weights and life histories were known, researchers could examine how individual development and experiences influenced skeletal features.

Recalling a 1990 interview, the author describes Goodall’s caution about interpreting the collection and her principle that field researchers should waste nothing. The skeleton of Flo, a chimp Goodall knew closely, illustrated the difficulty of estimating body weight from bone size and revealed bone loss unlike that seen in human females with osteoporosis. Goodall’s preservation work continued contributing to research after she shifted from fieldwork to environmental activism and writing.

The author describes the second week of motherhood as particularly difficult, marked by sleep deprivation, painful breastfeeding, babies’ weight-gain problems, loneliness, and difficulty soothing crying newborns. As family support and visits diminished, exhaustion and emotional distress undermined her confidence and strained her relationship with her husband. Frequent nighttime feeding and holding left her feeling more like a pacifier than a mother. Although this period was overwhelming, her experience eventually improved, and she came to enjoy the fourth trimester.

A follow-through day, developed by William J. O’Neil, is a market-timing signal intended to identify a new uptrend after a correction or downtrend. It occurs on Day 4 or later of a rally attempt when a major stock index closes significantly higher than the previous day on increased volume.

A rally attempt generally begins with a higher close. During Days 2 and 3, the index must not fall below Day 1’s low. Follow-through signals typically work best between Days 4 and 7, though later signals can succeed. A new low below the level where the rally attempt began indicates complete failure.

The signal is imperfect and does not justify becoming fully invested immediately. The passage recommends considering leading stocks, sentiment, trading style, and risk tolerance.

A backtest using SPY as a proxy for the S&P 500 produced poor short-term results, attributed to the market’s tendency toward mean reversion rather than continued strength. Adding a filter requiring the 25-day RSI to be below 55 slightly improved results. The passage concludes that follow-through days have limited short-term usefulness for index trading, while results for individual stocks could differ.

A northeastern U.S. heat wave is expected to move west after July Fourth, reaching Southern California by Friday. The double top is a bearish reversal chart pattern featuring two swing highs near the same level with a swing low between them. The highs form resistance, while a neckline serves as support. A break below the neckline signals a potential downward reversal.

Suggested trading rules include identifying an existing uptrend, ensuring the highs are within 3% of each other, and waiting for a break below the neckline with significant volume. Traders may close long positions or enter short positions on the break or a subsequent neckline retest. Profit targets are estimated by projecting the pattern’s height downward from the neckline; stop losses may be placed midway through or above the pattern.

Thomas Bulkowski’s research manually examined patterns across 500 stocks over five years without adjusting for survivorship bias. Only 39% of double top formations reached their targets, compared with 68% for double bottoms. The passage cautions that manual identification involves judgment and concludes that double tops are difficult to trade, particularly given the stock market’s upward tailwind.

The companies announced the agreement jointly on June 16, 2017. Amazon cautioned that shareholder approval, regulatory clearance, financing availability, delays, and operational risks could affect completion and anticipated benefits.

Enron faced declining investor confidence and tightening credit conditions on October 29, 2001, following investment losses and disclosures about off-balance-sheet partnerships associated with former CFO Andrew Fastow. The SEC was examining the transactions, and Fastow had been removed.

Moody’s downgraded Enron’s senior unsecured debt from Baa1 to Baa2, two levels above junk, and warned of further reductions. Enron’s shares closed down 10 percent at $13.81, near seven-year lows. Chikungunya, a mosquito-borne viral disease first documented in Ethiopia in June 2016, has spread across multiple districts and remains a public health concern. This systematic review and meta-analysis examined its seroprevalence and associated factors to inform prevention and control.

The review followed PRISMA guidelines and was registered with PROSPERO. Searches identified 40 publications, of which five English-language studies published between 2016 and November 2023 met eligibility criteria. Four were cross-sectional and one was case-control; diagnostic methods included ELISA and RT-qPCR.

The reported pooled seroprevalence was 12.35%. District-level prevalence ranged from 6.25% in Lare to 51.58% in Debub Ari. Results varied by geographical location, occupation, education, age, and sex. Several studies reported higher prevalence among farmers and adults, while sex-related findings were inconsistent.

Substantial heterogeneity was observed across districts (I² = 97.72%). Studies using ELISA showed significant variability, whereas those using RT-qPCR showed none. Begg’s and Egger’s tests found no significant evidence of publication bias or small-study effects.

Limitations included the small number of eligible studies, predominantly cross-sectional designs, and insufficient molecular research to characterize circulating strains. The authors cautioned that pooled prevalence might not accurately reflect current rates and recommended stronger outbreak preparedness, collaboration, public awareness, and consideration of geographical, demographic, and diagnostic differences when planning interventions. The report was posted as a non-peer-reviewed preprint in January 2024.

The Piotroski F-Score, developed by Joseph Piotroski, is a stock-selection method that evaluates financial strength using nine criteria covering profitability, liquidity, and efficiency. Each criterion receives 0 or 1 point; scores of 8–9 indicate strong financials, while scores of 0–4 indicate poor financials. Investors use it to identify undervalued stocks and assess growth stocks.

The strategy should complement other research rather than serve as a guarantee of investment success. Portfolio implementation involves setting goals, calculating scores, researching high-scoring stocks, diversifying, monitoring investments, and rebalancing.

Alpha Architect backtested the strategy on NYSE stocks from 1974 through December 2014, restricting the sample to the largest 40% by market value. For companies scoring at least 6, annual returns were 13.3% for its modified F-Score, 12.6% for the original score, and 11.2% for the S&P 500, with broadly similar standard deviations. Restricting portfolios to the cheapest 20% of stocks with Piotroski scores above 6 produced annual returns of 15.9% for the modified method and 15.2% for the original.

Backtesting can help evaluate historical performance and refine the strategy to suit investment goals.

Several Supreme Court justices appeared receptive to allowing trial judges to restrict discussions between defense lawyers and clients during overnight recesses while clients are testifying. David Villarreal, convicted of murdering his boyfriend, challenged an order allowing discussions of trial strategy but prohibiting discussion of his testimony. Texas courts upheld his conviction.

Villarreal’s lawyer argued that the distinction was unclear and would chill advice protected by the Sixth Amendment. Several justices suggested courts could distinguish direct preparation of testimony from strategic discussions that incidentally involve testimony, though questions exposed disagreement over permissible advice.

Texas proposed prohibiting management of testimony, including its content and delivery, while allowing discussion of strategic consequences. The United States advocated barring discussion of testimony altogether while permitting advice on matters such as pursuing a plea bargain.

The TPS7H500x-SP series comprises radiation-hardness-assured, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. Devices operate from a 4–14 V supply, provide a 0.613 V reference with +0.7%/−1% accuracy, and support switching frequencies from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. External gate drivers are recommended.

**Device variants**
- **TPS7H5001-SP:** Dual-output controller optimized for silicon- and GaN-based converters, with synchronous rectifier outputs, programmable dead times, and selectable 50%, 75%, or 100% maximum duty cycles.
- **TPS7H5002-SP:** Single-output controller supporting buck and single-ended isolated applications, with synchronous rectification, programmable dead time and leading-edge blanking, and 75% or 100% duty-cycle limits.
- **TPS7H5003-SP:** Single-output controller with synchronous rectification, fixed 50 ns dead time and leading-edge blanking, and 75% or 100% duty-cycle limits.
- **TPS7H5004-SP:** Dual-output controller for nonsynchronous push-pull and full-bridge topologies, with programmable leading-edge blanking and a fixed 50% duty-cycle limit.

**Control and operation**

Output voltage is programmed through a resistor divider connected to VSENSE. A capacitor sets soft-start duration; synchronous rectifier outputs become active after the SS voltage exceeds 1 V. Startup requires adequate internal regulator voltage, an available reference, an asserted enable signal, no active fault, and junction temperature below the thermal shutdown threshold.

Frequency can be established by an RT resistor, an external clock, or primary-secondary synchronization between two controllers. External synchronization requires RT to float and a 200 kHz–4 MHz clock at twice the desired switching frequency. Primary-secondary operation supports independent synchronized converters or parallel interleaved phases.

Programmable timing permits optimization of switching transitions and current-sense noise rejection. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations. Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, while Type 2A or Type 2B networks provide frequency compensation.

**Protection**

A nominal 1.05 V current-sense threshold initiates cycle-by-cycle current limiting. Persistent overcurrent causes hiccup shutdown and subsequent soft-start retries, with timing controlled by the HICC capacitor. The FAULT input supports externally implemented protection and restarts the controller after fault clearance and a delay. Thermal shutdown stops switching at approximately 175°C; startup resumes below approximately 160°C.

**Application and layout guidance**

A synchronous GaN push-pull design example uses the TPS7H5001-SP at 500 kHz with a 5 V output, approximately 25 ns dead time, 50 ns leading-edge blanking, and 7.5 ms soft start. Selected components include a transformer turns ratio of 2.5, 40 µH primary inductance, a 0.47 µH output inductor, and approximately 2.3 mF output capacitance. Additional capacitance addresses radiation-induced single-event transients.

Supply bypassing, short switching loops, separation of analog and power grounds with a single-point connection, and isolation of sensitive control traces from switching signals are emphasized. Bypass capacitors and compensation components should be placed close to the controller. Customers remain responsible for component suitability and application validation and testing.

The March 2024 paper examines how states are advancing education policy across political divides despite polarization, pandemic-related learning loss, declining institutional trust, and heightened scrutiny of schools. It uses “cross-partisan” to describe support spanning political perspectives, even when participants have different motivations or avoid publicly presenting their work as bipartisan.

Drawing on state policy initiatives and discussions with education leaders, the paper identifies five recurring factors associated with successful cross-partisan efforts:
- **Clear communication:** Proposals gain broader appeal when problems and solutions are understandable and connected to shared values.
- **Local responsiveness:** Policies benefit from addressing community needs and having credible, visible local supporters.
- **Political cover:** Constituencies, leaders, evidence, or legal requirements can help policymakers pursue controversial changes.
- **Wins for all sides:** Collaboration becomes more feasible when participants can claim distinct achievements.
- **Strategic media use:** Reporting can increase public awareness and accelerate policy action, although coverage can also distort or disrupt debate.

Examples include reading instruction reforms following the *Sold a Story* podcast, teacher apprenticeships supported by federal funding, and an interstate teacher licensing compact addressing employment barriers for relocating military spouses. Locally responsive career and technical education initiatives in Idaho and workforce credential programs in North Carolina also illustrate collaboration.

Virginia’s revised history standards demonstrate how a mandated deadline and sustained deliberation helped a politically diverse board reach unanimous agreement. Teacher pay increases paired with school choice policies, along with civics education initiatives, illustrate opportunities for different political groups to claim victories.

The paper advises advocates to understand political conditions, establish realistic expectations, identify shared problem definitions, assess urgency, and consider effects on frontline school employees. It recommends framing policies as expanding opportunities, maintaining organizational priorities, avoiding mission creep, and listening to political opponents. Rudy Gestede urged Middlesbrough to stay positive ahead of Monday’s match against Arsenal. Winless in the league since mid-December, Middlesbrough sit 19th, six points from safety with seven games remaining. Gestede warned of Arsenal’s quality despite their recent poor form.

The report covers events through Hawaii’s January 17, 1893 revolution, with subsequent developments addressed in a report accompanying the President’s February 15 message transmitting a treaty with Hawaii’s Provisional Government. Indonesia’s sovereign wealth fund Danantara plans to launch at least eight waste-to-power projects by the end of October, beginning in Jakarta and eventually covering 33 municipalities. Each plant is designed to process 1,000 tonnes of waste daily and generate about 15 megawatts of electricity, with projected capital costs of 2–3 trillion rupiah per facility.

Danantara will finance and oversee the projects, while state utility PLN will purchase the electricity. Local governments will provide land, and the government has removed municipal tipping fees. The initiative supports Indonesia’s 2025–2034 target of 453 MW of waste-to-energy capacity. MTN and four banks plan to raise GH¢4.67 billion on the Ghana Stock Exchange within six months, testing its capacity to accommodate simultaneous large transactions. This non-peer-reviewed study examined immune responses to two doses of Pfizer or Moderna COVID-19 vaccines in 40 participants: 13 healthy controls and 27 people with rheumatoid arthritis treated with methotrexate, abatacept, or rituximab. Researchers measured spike-specific antibodies, serum neutralization activity, and vaccine-specific B and T cell responses.

Rituximab-treated participants had almost no detectable spike-specific antibodies and reduced spike-specific CD4+ T cell responses. Abatacept-treated participants had significantly lower spike-specific antibody levels and neutralization activity than healthy controls. Although their numbers of receptor-binding-domain-specific B cells were similar to controls, these cells showed reduced activation, impaired switching to IgG, and altered memory differentiation. Abatacept also reduced production of the T cell cytokines IL-2, IFNγ, and IL-21.

Methotrexate-treated participants had significantly fewer spike-specific activated CD4+ T cells, but no significant reductions in antibody levels, neutralization activity, or B cell class switching. The proportion of T cells simultaneously producing IL-21, IL-2, and IFNγ was reduced in both methotrexate and abatacept groups.

Age and blood-sampling timing did not explain the diminished antibody responses associated with abatacept. The findings link impaired vaccine responses, particularly during abatacept treatment, to disrupted T cell–B cell collaboration. The authors suggest temporary abatacept cessation around vaccination when clinically manageable. Small participant numbers, particularly in the rituximab group, limited some analyses.

The Supreme Court will consider whether restitution under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act constitutes criminal punishment subject to the Constitution’s ex post facto clause. The decision will determine whether later statutory changes can increase Holsey Ellingburg’s restitution obligations for bank robbery. Ellingburg cites restitution’s inclusion in criminal sentences, criminal procedures, incarceration for nonpayment, and punitive purposes. The government agrees restitution is criminal for this purpose. A court-appointed lawyer defending the lower court’s decision argues that evidence of Congress’s intent is insufficiently conclusive to warrant reversal.
Delta intends to acquire up to an additional 32% of Grupo Aeroméxico at MXP$43.59 per share through a tender offer, pending Mexican and U.S. regulatory approvals.

This study translated and evaluated an Arabic version of the Orthognathic Quality of Life Questionnaire (OQLQ) for patients undergoing combined orthodontic and surgical treatment for dentofacial deformities. Previously used Arabic versions had not undergone formal psychometric evaluation.

The 22-item questionnaire measures social aspects, facial esthetics, oral function, and awareness of dentofacial aesthetics; higher scores indicate poorer quality of life. Translation involved independent forward and backward translation, expert review, and pilot testing with five volunteers.

The main sample comprised 74 adults seeking orthognathic treatment in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, during 2021–2022. Twelve completed questionnaires both before and after surgery. A separate group of 15 patients completed the questionnaire twice, two weeks apart, to assess test-retest reliability.

Internal consistency was excellent (Cronbach’s α = 0.92). Overall test-retest correlation was 0.859, with domain correlations ranging from 0.601 to 0.879. Associations with surgical satisfaction and perceived improvement in appearance supported construct validity.

Across the main sample, median overall scores were lower after surgery than before surgery, at 10 versus 34 (p < 0.0001). In the paired subgroup, median scores decreased from 22 to 11.5 (reported p = 0.09), while facial-esthetics scores improved significantly (p = 0.03).

Limitations included small test-retest and paired samples, lack of comparison with other validated instruments, no direct assessment of questionnaire comprehension, and recruitment of the main sample from one private practice. The authors concluded that the Arabic OQLQ was reliable, valid, and responsive, and recommended its standardized use in future studies.

Erik Demaine presents lower bounds for the predecessor problem, showing that the upper bounds achieved by van Emde Boas structures and fusion tries are nearly optimal. The lecture surveys earlier results and later tight trade-offs among problem size, word size, and space, then develops a communication-complexity argument using round elimination.

The proof considers colored predecessor, where each stored element is red or blue and a query reports only its predecessor’s color. A lower bound for this easier problem also applies to ordinary predecessor search.

In the cell-probe model, Alice holds the query and Bob holds the data structure. For a structure occupying \(s\) words of \(w\) bits, Alice sends an address using \(a=\log s\) bits, and Bob returns a word using \(b=w\) bits. Each communication round represents one memory read, so a lower bound on rounds gives a lower bound on query time.

Round elimination removes a protocol’s first message while reducing the problem and slightly increasing its error probability. In the underlying construction, one participant has \(k\) inputs but does not know which input matters. A short first message conveys little information about the relevant input. The lemma bounds the additional error by \(O(\sqrt{a/k})\), or the corresponding expression involving \(b\) when Bob speaks first.

The proof alternates two reductions:
- Eliminating an Alice-to-Bob message partitions the query into chunks, reducing the effective word size by a factor of \(\Theta(at^2)\).
- Eliminating a Bob-to-Alice message partitions the stored elements into subproblems, reducing their number by a factor of \(\Theta(bt^2)\).

These constructions resemble van Emde Boas search and fusion-tree search, respectively. Choosing the partition sizes appropriately keeps the total accumulated error below one-half. Eliminating every message would then produce a zero-communication protocol that outperforms guessing, yielding a contradiction.

The resulting lower bound is
\[
\Omega\!\left(\min\{\log_a w,\log_b n\}\right).
\]
For polynomial space, this becomes
\[
\Omega\!\left(\min\left\{\frac{\log w}{\log\log n},\log_w n\right\}\right).
\]
It applies even to static, randomized data structures and nearly matches the known upper bounds. The lecture explains the reductions but does not fully prove the information-theoretic round-elimination lemma.

NVIDIA’s Ampere GA10x GPU family, including GA102 and GA104, builds on Turing with improvements to graphics, ray tracing, AI acceleration, memory, and connectivity. The passage reports performance gains of up to 1.7× for traditional raster graphics and 2× for ray tracing, with up to 1.9× greater power efficiency at equivalent performance.

GA102 powers the GeForce RTX 3090, RTX 3080, RTX A6000, and NVIDIA A40; GA104 powers the RTX 3070. Manufactured using Samsung’s 8nm process, the full GA102 contains 28.3 billion transistors, 84 streaming multiprocessors (SMs), 10,752 CUDA cores, 84 second-generation RT cores, and 336 third-generation Tensor cores.

Key architectural changes include:
- **FP32 processing:** Both primary SM datapaths support FP32 operations, doubling peak throughput relative to Turing. Actual gains depend on workload instruction mixes.
- **Ray tracing:** Second-generation RT cores double ray/triangle intersection testing throughput, accelerate motion blur, and support concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute workloads.
- **AI acceleration:** Third-generation Tensor cores support additional data types and structured sparsity, which doubles Tensor operation throughput over Turing. Applications include DLSS, denoising, video and voice enhancement, and AI-powered painting.
- **Cache and raster operations:** Each SM has 128 KB of combined L1 cache/shared memory, with twice Turing’s shared-memory bandwidth. Moving raster operators into graphics processing clusters increases the full GA102’s total to 112 ROPs.

The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X memory and supports many games at 8K and 60 fps with DLSS 8K enabled. The RTX 3080 uses GDDR6X and delivers 1.5× the memory bandwidth of the RTX 2080 Super. RTX A6000 and A40 each provide 48 GB of GDDR6, expandable to 96 GB across two identical NVLink-connected GPUs.

GA10x also supports PCIe 4.0, which doubles PCIe 3.0 bandwidth, alongside HDMI 2.1 and AV1 decoding for 8K HDR content. These capabilities target gaming, professional rendering, simulation, AI, data science, and virtual workstations.
