Some developers cited political and financial risks, while critics questioned whether ownership concentrated among existing suppliers would lower prices.

AMD’s SEV-ES Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) specification standardizes communication between protected guests and hypervisors, including required exit handling, shared state, booting, and interrupt behavior.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP encrypt guest register state during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access or modification. Automatic Exits do not require exposing guest register state. For Non-Automatic Exits, guests selectively share required information through the GHCB.

The GHCB occupies a 4 KB, page-aligned, decrypted or shared page. Its address is communicated through MSR 0xc001_0130, which hypervisors must not intercept. The GHCB MSR protocol supports communication before a shared GHCB page is available, including version negotiation, CPUID requests, feature discovery, page-state changes, and termination requests. SEV-SNP guests must register each GHCB guest physical address before use.

Version 2 introduces SEV-SNP support and hypervisor advertisement of optional features through a 52-bit bitmap. Subsequent revisions add or document 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, expanded error reporting, VLEK certificates, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, trusted I/O, Secure AVIC, and GHCB unregistration.

For supported Non-Automatic Exits, guests prepare required GHCB fields and invoke VMGEXIT. Guests and hypervisors mark supplied fields in VALID_BITMAP and clear previous validity information before preparing new requests or responses. Software should disable interrupts and preemption while accessing the GHCB around VMGEXIT; NMI handling should use a separate GHCB or preserve the active one.

The protocol covers:
- I/O, MSR access, hypercalls, and MMIO operations.
- Page-state changes, including private/shared transitions and resumable processing.
- SEV-SNP firmware requests using separate shared request and response pages.
- Extended requests returning certificates alongside attestation information.
- AP creation, APIC ID discovery, VMPL switching, restricted-injection doorbells, IPIs, and timers.
- Trusted-device requests returning measurements, certificates, and attestation reports.
- Secure AVIC backing-page registration and guest termination.

The SEV-SNP secrets page communicates information between operating environments, including request sequence numbers and the AP jump-table address. An EFI configuration table can communicate secrets and CPUID pages to the operating system.

Traditional AP booting requires special handling because hypervisors cannot modify encrypted register state. SEV-SNP AP Creation lets guests supply VMSA pages and supports vCPU hotplug. NMI handling uses a guest “NMI Complete” notification. Debug-register handling depends on hardware virtualization support. SMM is unsupported in this specification version; nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

The accompanying agreement restricts specification use to interface planning/design and feedback, prohibits duplication and redistribution, and grants no intellectual-property rights. AMD provides the information “AS IS,” disclaims warranties and liability, and may change it without notice. Voluntary feedback may be used without restriction, fee, or confidentiality obligations. Export restrictions apply; California law governs the agreement.

The study proposes a DNN–Transformer–Autoencoder framework for corporate tax-risk assessment, addressing limitations of manual inspections and rule-based supervision. A DNN models static enterprise attributes, a Transformer captures temporal financial patterns, and an autoencoder detects anomalies through reconstruction errors. Their outputs are combined to classify enterprises as high, medium, or low risk.

The framework was evaluated using tax declarations and financial records from approximately 12,000 enterprises across multiple industries. Data were divided into training, validation, and test sets in proportions of 70%, 15%, and 15%. The model achieved 0.91 accuracy, 0.86 recall, and 0.88 macro F1, outperforming logistic regression, random forest, XGBoost, and DNN-LSTM baselines. Training and validation losses converged after approximately 40 epochs.

The approach supports risk identification and supervisory resource allocation. Limitations include the exclusion of macroeconomic conditions and inter-firm relationships, alongside computational demands that may hinder deployment in resource-constrained tax offices. Suggested future work includes incorporating macroeconomic and policy data and developing more interpretable, lightweight models.

Value area trading uses volume profiles to identify the price range where 70% of trading volume occurred during a specified period. Traders use these areas as potential support and resistance levels and look for breakouts, reversals, or pullbacks to generate trading signals.

The strategy is commonly used in futures markets but also applies to stocks and forex. It can be used on intraday, daily, weekly, or monthly charts. Candlestick patterns and momentum indicators may help interpret price action around value areas. These levels can also guide stop-loss placement, profit targets, and adjustments to other trading signals.

Risks include false signals, changing value areas, and reliance on outdated information. The passage recommends stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, and considering additional factors rather than relying solely on value areas.

Although the passage initially promises a backtest, none is provided; it notes that backtesting requires defined trading rules and settings.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement arrested the superintendent of Iowa’s largest school district. The passage also lists education news and features covering school integration, college access, student achievement, education policy, pandemic recovery, youth activities and community initiatives, alongside requests to support The 74.

Scientists will study an upcoming total solar eclipse crossing the U.S. from Oregon to South Carolina using ground instruments, satellites, aircraft and high-altitude balloons. NASA and the National Science Foundation are spending about $7.7 million on eclipse research.

Researchers will focus on the sun’s corona, including why its temperature exceeds the surface temperature by more than 1 million degrees. They will also examine effects on Earth’s weather, space weather, animals and plants.

Public participation includes Citizen CATE, which will combine images from volunteers at 68 locations into a movie, alongside projects collecting wildlife observations, photographs and video.

Eclipses have enabled major scientific discoveries, including the detection of helium’s chemical spectrum in 1868 and observations in 1919 supporting Einstein’s general theory of relativity.

The passage presents a theoretical framework for orbital degrees of freedom in coupled magnon–phonon systems, or magnon-polarons. It distinguishes contributions from global lattice rotation and quantum geometry, showing that wavepacket self-rotation can produce a finite orbital angular moment (OAM) even when the lattice remains fixed. The framework treats magnons and phonons on equal footing and is described as applicable to both bosonic and fermionic systems.

Using a two-dimensional honeycomb antiferromagnet with Néel order and parameters for MnPS₃, the study demonstrates two mechanisms for orbital transfer: magnetoelastic coupling breaks symmetries to enable intra-band OAM and creates inter-band transitions that support inter-band OAM. Consequently, linearly polarized out-of-plane phonons can acquire out-of-plane OAM and a magnetic moment through hybridization with magnons.

The authors propose detecting these effects through electric polarization and a transverse voltage generated under a temperature or strain gradient. Calculations predict voltages of several microvolts at low magnetic fields, with the orbital contribution dominating the spin Berry curvature contribution. Compared with a previously reported case involving only Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, polarization is enhanced by five to six orders of magnitude. The voltage increases with temperature and coupling strength and can persist without an external magnetic field.

The findings establish a theoretical connection between phonon and magnon orbitronics and suggest opportunities for electrical detection and control of hybrid excitations.

A Danish study found that children born to mothers with rheumatoid arthritis had nearly three times the risk of rheumatoid arthritis, 2.2 times the risk of thyroid disease and 1.6 times the risk of epilepsy. Researchers urged increased awareness among doctors.

The IMF urged Saudi Arabia to pace economic reforms and price increases to avoid harming growth while praising efforts to boost non-oil revenue and reduce spending. It recommended balancing the budget by 2022 rather than 2019. Saudi Arabia posted $200 billion in deficits over three years following the 2014 oil-price crash. Its reforms include higher taxes, energy prices and expatriate labour fees, plus a planned five-percent VAT. The IMF forecast 0.1 percent economic growth this year, with lower oil production offsetting expected non-oil growth.

The study develops a first-principles statistical-mechanics framework for calculating equilibrium vacancy concentrations in nine-component refractory alloys containing group 4, 5, and 6 elements. It combines a density-functional-theory-trained embedded cluster expansion model with canonical Monte Carlo simulations and a coarse-graining method for dilute vacancies. The selected model achieves a test error of 7.72 meV/site. For HfNbTaTiZr, the coarse-graining method matches semi-grand canonical simulations while requiring only a few hundred samples rather than approximately 100 million.

Vacancy concentrations depend strongly on alloy composition, short-range order, and chemical bonding. Alloys containing only group 5 and 6 elements exhibit low vacancy concentrations, approximately 10⁻⁷ at 2000 K, whereas the group-4-containing HfNbTaTiZr alloy approaches 10⁻⁴ at 1700 K. Increasing group 4 content lowers vacancy formation free energies; the investigated ternary and nonary systems require approximately 50–60% group 4 elements to attain vacancy concentrations of 10⁻⁴–10⁻⁵ at 1500°C.

Binary-alloy comparisons show that nearly ideal Mo–W mixing produces nearly ideal vacancy concentrations, unfavorable Cr–W bonding increases concentrations, and favorable Nb–W bonding reduces them. Related bonding trends persist in concentrated alloys. In HfMoNbTiZr, vacancies preferentially have Zr and Hf first neighbors and Mo second neighbors.

Single special quasi-random structure calculations underestimate vacancy concentrations by factors of three and seven for Cr–Ti and HfNbTaTiZr, respectively, compared with the study’s finite-temperature approach. Differences involve chemical potentials, sampling, and local ordering. Some investigated compositions may undergo phase transitions, requiring caution when interpreting their calculated concentrations.

The framework supports composition-based control of vacancy thermodynamics but neglects vibrational free-energy contributions, divacancies, and larger vacancy clusters.

The Scottish Accountancy & Finance Awards annually recognise accountants’ contributions to private and public sector organisations across seven categories. Sarah Heaney will present the 2018 awards, with entertainment by DNA. Tickets include a reception, dinner, wine and entertainment, costing £132 individually or £1,200 for ten, plus VAT.

A study of 1,099 participants linked energy drink consumption among young adults to increased risk of cocaine and non-medical prescription stimulant use. Occasional consumers also faced increased risk. Researchers said the unexplained association warrants further investigation.

In Waterhouse v. Gibson & al., the plaintiff sued for removal of a barn and blacksmith’s shop from land acquired through an execution levy and subsequent deed. The defendants offered evidence that the buildings had been excluded from appraisal by agreement and reserved for the debtor, although the execution returns contained no reservation.

The court held that a conveyance by execution levy follows the same construction rules as a deed. Buildings owned by the landowner pass with the land unless expressly excepted, regardless of whether their foundations extend below ground. Exceptions allowing tenants to remove certain buildings did not apply. Parol evidence could not establish a reservation contradicting the written returns. The court upheld exclusion of the evidence and entered judgment on the plaintiff’s verdict for the buildings’ value.

The player fondly recalls Detroit, his first team, including two consecutive semifinal appearances and positive treatment by the city. His trade to Washington was initially difficult, and the team struggled before improving after summer changes. He remains confident in Washington’s players and road performance and considers returning to Detroit special.

Azerbaijan aims to increase honey and beekeeping product exports. Agriculture Minister Heydar Asadov cited anticipated growth in global demand and opportunities for organic honey in premium markets. The ministry plans to submit proposals for increased state support for beekeeping.

Marc Ó Sé believes James O'Donoghue could hugely boost Kerry if he stays injury-free. O'Donoghue scored nine points against Clare on his return. Ó Sé expects regular games to build his confidence and believes pairing him with Paul Geaney would challenge opposing defences.

- **Sampling-point tuning:** CMD19 supplies a fixed tuning block to optimize host–card timing and compensate for static delays. Tuning is mandatory for HOST-SDR-VD and optional for HOST-SDR-FD. CMD19 is valid only for an unlocked card in Transfer State using 1.8 V signaling. Forty consecutive executions must complete within 150 ms, excluding host processing time.

- **Card selection and transfer states:** Hosts remain at identification frequency until Card Identification Mode ends. CMD9 retrieves card-specific data, and CMD7 selects one card for Transfer State. Data communication is point-to-point with the selected card. CMD12 can abort reads and writes; writes must stop before deselection. Deselection does not terminate programming or erase operations, but resetting a card can terminate programming and destroy data.

- **Reads and writes:** CMD17 reads one block, while CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12 stops transmission. CRC protects transferred blocks, and data failing write CRC checks is discarded. Write buffering may allow another block to arrive during programming; DAT0 indicates busy conditions. CMD13 reports card status. Multiple-block writes and ACMD23 pre-erasure can improve performance, while ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks.

- **Addressing and bus width:** SDSC cards use byte addresses and block lengths set through CMD16. SDHC and SDXC cards use block addresses and fixed 512-byte memory-access blocks, without partial or misaligned access. ACMD6 selects bus width; the default is one bit after power-up or CMD0. Locked cards reject bus-width changes.

- **Erase, discard and logical erase:** Erasure uses CMD32, CMD33 and CMD38 in sequence, leaving write-protected sectors intact. DISCARD permits partial or complete deallocation, and hosts must treat discarded contents as unspecified. Full User Area Logical Erase logically erases the entire user area. DISCARD and FULE require support checks, apply only to SDHC and SDXC, and are unavailable through SPI. Their busy timeouts are 250 ms and one second, respectively.

- **Protection and passwords:** Protection includes a host-enforced mechanical switch, optional internal write protection and password locking. Passwords persist across power cycles; cards with a password automatically lock after power-on. Locked cards permit specified initialization and status commands but prevent data access. CMD42 manages passwords and locking, with passwords up to 16 bytes.

- **Card Ownership Protection:** COP adds a Force Erase Password. Setting FEP disables ordinary Force Erase and password clearing. COP Unlock enables COP-specific operations and is required after reset when FEP is set. FEP Force Erase requires the correct FEP, erases user data and the card-lock password, but preserves FEP. Ordinary Force Erase can erase a locked card and its password when FEP is not set.

- **Command extensions and function switching:** CMD55 marks the next command as application-specific. CMD6 queries or switches functions involving access mode, command system, driver strength and power limit. Hosts must verify supported functions and available power. Busy functions cannot be switched, and invalid selections cancel switching. Optional High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires one-to-one host–card connections.

- **Initialization, clocks and errors:** CMD8 checks host-voltage compatibility before ACMD41 during initialization. Hosts may reduce or stop the clock subject to specified restrictions and must provide eight clocks after transactions. CRC7 protects commands and most responses; CRC16 protects data blocks. Failed command CRC checks and illegal commands leave card state unchanged and set error indicators. SDHC and SDXC reads require at least a 100 ms timeout; SDHC write busy periods have a 250 ms maximum.

The disclosure describes methods, apparatuses, and computer-readable instructions for video encoding and decoding using intra prediction and non-separable transforms.

For a block coded with a directional prediction mode, coding information identifies a nominal mode and an angular offset. Together, these determine the prediction direction. A non-separable transform set is selected based on the nominal mode, regardless of the angular offset. A signaled transform index can select a particular transform within that set, and the block is reconstructed using the prediction mode and selected transform.

Non-directional prediction modes—including DC, PAETH, SMOOTH variants, recursive filtering, and chroma-from-luma—can also be associated with transform sets. Multiple non-directional modes, or a non-directional mode and a nominal directional mode, may share a set.

The non-separable transform may serve as a primary or secondary transform. Secondary transforms can be restricted to selected coefficients, such as the first coefficients in an entropy-coding scan or coefficients whose coordinate sums fall below a threshold. Coefficients processed with and without a secondary transform may be entropy-decoded separately. Some embodiments exclude PAETH or recursive filtering modes from secondary transformation, or omit non-separable transforms for transform-skip blocks.

The passage also describes reduced low-frequency non-separable transforms that map coefficient vectors into smaller dimensions to reduce computation and storage, along with transform-selection signaling, line graph transforms, and encoder–decoder architectures. These techniques are discussed for video formats and standards including AV1, subsequent AOMedia formats, HEVC, and VVC.

Microsoft’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended March 31, 2020 reported:

- **Quarterly results:** Revenue was $35.021 billion, compared with $30.571 billion a year earlier. Operating income increased to $12.975 billion from $10.341 billion, and net income rose to $10.752 billion from $8.809 billion. Diluted earnings per share were $1.40, versus $1.14.
- **Nine-month results:** Revenue totaled $104.982 billion, operating income $39.552 billion, and net income $33.079 billion, compared with $92.126 billion, $30.554 billion, and $26.053 billion, respectively, a year earlier.
- **Segment performance:** Quarterly revenue reached $11.743 billion in Productivity and Business Processes, $12.281 billion in Intelligent Cloud, and $10.997 billion in More Personal Computing.
- **Cloud and product growth:** Commercial cloud revenue increased 39% to $13.3 billion. Azure revenue grew 59%, Office 365 Commercial revenue 25%, Dynamics 365 revenue 47%, and LinkedIn revenue 21%. Office 365 Consumer subscribers reached 39.6 million.
- **Financial position:** At March 31, cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments totaled $137.626 billion. Total assets were $285.449 billion, liabilities $170.948 billion, and stockholders’ equity $114.501 billion. Total debt, including its current portion, was $66.610 billion.
- **Cash flow and shareholder returns:** Quarterly operating cash flow was $17.504 billion, compared with $13.520 billion a year earlier. Microsoft repurchased $6 billion of shares under its repurchase programs and paid $3.876 billion in dividends during the quarter. Its latest repurchase authorization had $36.8 billion remaining.
- **Future revenue commitments:** Remaining performance obligations totaled $93 billion, including $89 billion related to commercial revenue. Microsoft expected to recognize approximately half within 12 months.
- **COVID-19:** The pandemic had minimal net impact on quarterly revenue. Remote working and learning increased cloud usage and demand for Windows OEM and Surface, while gaming engagement rose. Advertising spending and some transactional licensing weakened. Microsoft warned that future effects remained uncertain and might not yet be fully reflected in results.
- **Contingencies:** Accrued legal liabilities were $304 million, with approximately $800 million in additional adverse outcomes considered reasonably possible. Unresolved IRS transfer-pricing matters could materially affect financial statements when resolved.

Deloitte’s review identified no material modifications needed for the interim financial information to conform with U.S. GAAP.

Microsoft announced on July 1, 2020, that Frank H. Brod will retire as Chief Accounting Officer, stepping down July 31 and remaining through September 30 to assist the transition. Alice L. Jolla, 54, will become Corporate Vice President and Chief Accounting Officer effective July 31. Jolla has served as Microsoft’s Corporate Controller since 2014 and previously held senior accounting and financial planning roles. She will receive a $1.5 million stock award under Microsoft’s 2017 Stock Plan, vesting 6.25% quarterly, contingent on continuous employment. The share count will be based on Microsoft’s closing stock price on the grant date.

The Texas Education Agency is investigating hundreds of teachers’ social media posts about Charlie Kirk’s killing. Education Commissioner Mike Morath called the comments “reprehensible and inappropriate” and recommended license suspensions. Gov. Greg Abbott supported the investigations, accusing teachers of calling for or inciting violence.

Legal experts and education advocates argue that the investigations threaten teachers’ First Amendment rights. They say public school employees retain free speech protections when speaking personally on matters of public concern, and disciplinary action requires considering whether comments significantly disrupted work or teachers’ ability to perform their jobs. Public outrage alone, experts say, likely does not justify punishment.

Critics also warn that political pressure could intimidate educators into silence. The agency did not answer questions about how it would account for constitutional protections. Texas American Federation of Teachers President Zeph Capo characterized the response as a politically driven “witch hunt” and opposed firing teachers over such comments.

Bitcoin fell below US$8,000 before recovering to US$8,715, remaining down 21 per cent for the week and more than half from its December peak. Cryptocurrencies faced regulatory threats, the US$500 million Coincheck theft, price-manipulation fears and Facebook’s cryptocurrency advertising ban. Ripple, Ether and Litecoin also fell at least 18 per cent.

President Trump criticized ABC for not apologizing for statements about him after it canceled “Roseanne” over Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet targeting Valerie Jarrett. Disney CEO Bob Iger called Jarrett to apologize and explain the cancellation. Some Democratic lawmakers criticized Trump’s response. Jarrett called for the incident to become a teaching moment, saying both the president and individual citizens bear responsibility for confronting racism.

The study examines Hungarian higher education lecturers’ employment, demographics, qualifications and earnings using national and international statistics and legislative analysis.

Higher education expanded after 1990, but subsequent demographic changes, funding reductions and restrictive admissions policies contributed to declining enrollment. The study reports increased inequalities in access and stagnation in the proportion of young graduates below the EU’s 2020 target. Admissions requirements were relaxed from 2021 following enrollment declines.

Lecturer numbers have not tracked student numbers closely since 2005. The student–teacher ratio rose from 5.9 in 1990 to 17.9 in 2006 before falling to 10.4 in 2022. Hungarian academic staff are somewhat older than the developed-country average but occupy a middle position internationally. Women represented 41.5% of lecturers in 2020.

Legislation restored universities’ authority to award doctorates in 1993 while preserving some qualification functions of the Hungarian Academy of Sciences. Later reforms tightened academic appointment requirements and reduced institutional autonomy through government-appointed chancellors and foundation governing boards. The transfer of most public universities to foundations replaced civil-service employment with labor-market contracts. Staff at these institutions received substantial salary increases linked to performance evaluations.

Academic staffing shifted away from senior positions: university and college professors numbered 3,224 in 2005 and 2,100 in 2020. The study identifies retirement, funding constraints, stricter qualification requirements and low salaries as possible contributors.

Earnings analysis shows that doctoral graduates pursuing academic careers in public institutions face low starting pay and delayed earnings growth. Their estimated lifetime earnings fall below the national average for university graduates and substantially below those of business-sector graduates. These findings do not necessarily apply to institutions offering higher salaries after restructuring.

Hungary also ranks relatively low internationally in doctoral student numbers, raising concerns about the future supply of lecturers and researchers. The study calls for policymakers to address employment conditions, earnings and other barriers affecting academic careers.

Bond trading strategies aim to preserve capital, generate income, or achieve capital appreciation. The passage focuses on Treasury bonds and backtests involving TLT, an ETF tracking 20-year Treasury bonds.

Strategies vary by investment goals, time horizon, risk tolerance, and market conditions. Examples include yield curve, duration, credit spread, seasonal, and tactical asset allocation strategies. Bond prices generally fall when interest rates rise and increase when rates decline.

The passage emphasizes bonds’ diversification benefits because their returns often have limited correlation with stocks. It describes seasonal and swing-trading backtests in TLT and reports that combining selected bond strategies with an S&P 500 strategy bundle increased returns and reduced drawdowns. Historical performance does not guarantee future results.

Common trading mistakes include inadequate market understanding, excessive reliance on historical data, poor risk management, chasing yields without assessing risks, insufficient diversification, and emotional decision-making.

Day trading bonds requires understanding pricing, liquidity, and interest-rate influences; traders typically focus on liquid government securities. Strategies can be automated using predefined criteria, but human oversight remains important. For beginners, the passage suggests dollar-cost averaging—investing a fixed amount regularly regardless of market conditions.

Best Hope Services plans to launch what it calls Nigeria’s first online trade exhibition on May 1, promoting innovations by local inventors, scholars and entrepreneurs. Exhibitors will showcase products globally without hiring physical venues, while visitors can participate remotely. The expo will cover multiple industries, and Nigerians are encouraged to register before May.

- Northwest Natural confirmed discussions to acquire Enron’s Portland General Electric utility. Reports valued the potential transaction at approximately $1.8 billion in cash and stock plus assumed debt, generally estimated at $1 billion. Financing, final terms and board approval remained uncertain. Enron’s earlier proposed sale to Sierra Pacific Resources had collapsed partly because of the California energy crisis.
- Enron planned to reduce its European workforce by 5–10 percent, or up to approximately 500 jobs, preferably through voluntary severance. The company cited cost control and maintaining earnings growth; slow European market liberalization had constrained its energy-trading businesses.
- BG Group’s proposed $388 million purchase of Enron’s Indian offshore oil and gas interests faced uncertainty over operatorship. Existing partners ONGC and Reliance also sought operating rights, while BG made full operatorship a condition of the acquisition.
- Tata Power was expected to finalize an offer for Enron’s 65 percent stake in Dabhol Power within three weeks. The project was stalled following a payment dispute with its sole electricity buyer. Indian lenders sought equity discounts, financing and tax concessions, and resolution of stakeholder disputes. BSES ruled out buying the stake because of the project’s economics.
- Moody’s said it would assess any Tata Power acquisition’s financial implications but saw no immediate need for action on its bonds.
- Northwest Natural increased its quarterly common dividend from 31 cents to 31.5 cents per share.

Microsoft is reportedly developing Polaris, a modular Windows 10 version built on Windows Core OS for desktops, laptops and 2-in-1 devices. It would use the new CShell interface and support Microsoft Store UWP apps rather than traditional desktop applications, aiming to improve security, efficiency and battery life. Unlike Windows 10 S, Polaris would not allow upgrades to Windows 10 Pro. Microsoft is reportedly exploring remote virtualization to support legacy applications. Windows Central suggests Polaris could arrive in 2019.

The passage outlines a proposed Reagan-Bush administration’s approach to China and Taiwan, emphasizing shared U.S.-Chinese interests in peace, trade, modernization and concern over Soviet military expansion. It advocates expanding ties with China, cooperating with regional partners for Western Pacific stability and opposing aggression or hegemony. While criticizing Carter’s concessions in normalizing relations with China, it pledges to conduct Taiwan relations under the Taiwan Relations Act. The Act supports peaceful resolution of Taiwan’s future, defensive arms sales and U.S. capacity to resist coercion threatening Taiwan. It also establishes arrangements for administering relations through the American Institute in Taiwan, with congressional funding and oversight.

Researchers studied how polypropylene’s molecular regularity, or isotacticity, and cooling conditions affect its mechanical properties. Their findings, published in Polymer, could help produce materials with predetermined elasticity or hardness.

The team tested films with isotacticity ranging from 25 to over 95 percent, prepared by either rapid quenching or slow cooling. Stretching tests showed that mechanical behavior depended on both isotacticity and thermal history. Higher isotacticity promotes crosslinks and crystalline regions, strengthening the material. The researchers also linked elastic modulus to crystallinity and found that cooling methods produced differently shaped crystallites.

The study concludes that controlling molecular structure during synthesis and preparation conditions determines the polymer network and the resulting material’s properties.

Wal-Mart’s bid for Bonobos is part of its effort to compete with Amazon in online fashion and attract younger, affluent shoppers. A successful deal would be its fourth acquisition of a small online clothing-and-accessories brand in 2017, following ShoeBuy, Moosejaw and ModCloth. The strategy is led by e-commerce chief Marc Lore, who joined after Wal-Mart bought Jet.com for $3.3 billion. Online sales account for about 3 percent of Wal-Mart’s total sales. Analysts said the acquisitions offer growth opportunities but remain too small for a material impact, while one consultant questioned the strategy’s past results.

The JACL Kakehashi Program will select up to 200 Japanese American or Asian American college students and young professionals, ages 18–25, for nine-day trips to Japan featuring cultural activities and homestays. The program aims to strengthen U.S.-Japan relations. Application deadlines are October 9 and January 2, 2018.

This week’s making tips include adding rare earth magnets to tester wires for quick hookups, repurposing an old motor as a filming turntable, and fitting a hobby knife into a compatible compass. Other recommendations include consistently marking untrue material edges with squiggly lines on both sides, converting a drill press into a makeshift drum sander, and using a $10 Ikea flexible-neck LED lamp for workbench lighting.

Kent Howerton won the 1976 AMA 500cc motocross opener, ahead of Bob Hannah and Tony DiStefano, with six brands represented in the top six. In 1982, Ricky Johnson won High Point’s 250 National, Darrell Shultz won the 500 Class, and Mark Barnett won Toronto Supercross. Yamaha cut budgets and discontinued coach Gary Bailey’s services, while riders questioned Trans-USA’s financial appeal. Ross Pederson won the 1987 Montreal Supercross.

Modeling disordered materials requires scalable, accurate methods that reproduce experimental structures. Standard Monte Carlo and molecular dynamics simulations do not guarantee experimental agreement. Reverse and hybrid reverse Monte Carlo methods improve agreement but can generate unphysical structures or require costly sampling. Previous experimentally constrained molecular dynamics approaches faced scaling, accuracy, and thermal-broadening limitations.

The article presents molecular augmented dynamics (MAD), a linearly scaling modified molecular dynamics method designed to obtain low-energy, ab-initio accurate structures consistent with experimental data. Its Hamiltonian combines kinetic energy, an interatomic potential, and an experimental potential measuring disagreement between predicted and measured observables. This enables simultaneous optimization of physical plausibility and experimental agreement.

The authors derive smooth, analytic experimental forces for X-ray diffraction, neutron diffraction, pair distribution functions, and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy, accounting for thermal broadening. The approach also accommodates observables based on local, position-differentiable descriptors. CPU and GPU implementations are provided in TurboGAP. A rigorous interpretation as a biased-sampling protocol is deferred to future work.

Intel released Coffee Lake desktop processors and Z370 chipsets, with additional desktop, notebook and enterprise products planned for 2018. Gemini Lake was planned for November 2017, Cannon Lake for mid-2018 and Ice Lake for 2019. Intel said initial 10nm shipments would begin near year-end, ramping up in early 2018.

The Housing Authority of the City of Santa Barbara won a Gold Nugget Award for Best Affordable Project for Bradley Studios, a 54-unit development built in 2012. Serving low-income residents with special needs, it offers community spaces and on-site support services. Judges praised its California Craftsman styling, environmentally responsible design and community focus.

The “Drive & Kick” offense uses a three-player weave from a 3-2 spread alignment. Players drive for layups while avoiding offensive charges. When penetration is denied, the handler passes outside and replaces the receiver, continuing the weave. Corner passes maintain continuity when baseline players zone, while back cuts offer scoring opportunities when baseline defenders help. The offense can run time off the clock before a set play.

Acting CDC director Jim O’Neill called for replacing the combined measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine with three separate shots, echoing President Trump. No evidence shows that separating the vaccines improves safety or effectiveness. Single-disease vaccines are no longer available in the U.S., and developing them would likely require years of clinical trials and regulatory review.

Experts warn that separate shots could leave children more vulnerable to infection and that officials’ rhetoric could discourage vaccination. A 2017 study found higher vaccination-series completion among children receiving combination vaccines. The MMR vaccine is highly effective, with minimal side-effect risks, including a small increased risk of febrile seizures. Research has found no link between MMR vaccination and autism.

Three Illinois men were shot and killed at point-blank range during an event attended by 15,000 people at Great Lakes Dragaway near Union Grove, Wisconsin, on Aug. 13, 2017. Authorities identified the victims as David L. Watson, 30; Khalid R. Howard, 30; and Derek K. Edwards, 26. Sheriff David Beth said their confirmed gang affiliations led investigators to suspect gang-related killings, though the motive remained unknown. Authorities were searching for the gunman, who fled in a vehicle. The pistol used was not recovered. Private security worked the event, but spectators were not screened for weapons.

The Department opposes dividing the General Assembly into regional sections, fearing decentralization would complicate the international organization’s establishment and weaken its effectiveness. It recommends postponing decentralization discussions until the organization is firmly established.

The Mexico City Conference, convening February 21, will discuss matters of mutual interest among American republics, possibly including Argentina. The United States seeks discussion and support for the Dumbarton Oaks proposals without undertaking inconsistent commitments, continuing its approach in meetings with Latin American ambassadors.

The Dumbarton Oaks proposals establish an international court as the organization’s principal judicial organ, with a statute based on the existing Permanent Court’s statute. All organization members would be parties; nonmembers could join under specified conditions. Legal and practical complications arise because the existing court remains in being and affected states include prospective nonmembers. The recommended procedure is to convene approximately fifteen technically qualified jurists, selected by four-power agreement, when conference invitations issue, to draft a statute and alternative implementation procedures.

A study examined self-reported empathy among 206 teachers in education faculties at a Spanish university using the Interpersonal Reactivity Index. Participants showed high overall empathy, with strong perspective taking, fantasy and empathic concern, and moderate personal distress.

Female participants scored significantly higher overall and across all four dimensions. Empathy did not differ significantly by degree programme taught, campus, contractual status or length of teaching experience. Previous non-university teaching experience was associated with higher perspective taking, fantasy and empathic concern, but not significantly higher overall empathy. Teachers with only university experience reported greater personal distress.

The authors highlight the importance of university educators modelling empathy and developing skills for empathic interactions with students. Limited sample size and possible social desirability bias restrict generalisation of the findings.

UNC Chapel Hill placed Professor Dwayne Dixon on leave while investigating his “alleged advocacy of politically motivated violence,” potentially leading to dismissal. The action followed Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet’s demand that Dixon be fired over his past involvement in Redneck Revolt, which Kolvet linked to controversial fliers at Georgetown University.

Dixon said he left his Redneck Revolt chapter in 2018; the organization disbanded in 2019. UNC declined to say whether Kolvet’s post or related news coverage prompted its investigation.

A reinstatement petition drew more than 900 signatures. North Carolina and UNC Chapel Hill American Association of University Professors representatives condemned the suspension, calling the connection between Dixon and the fliers unsubstantiated. Dixon previously remained employed through controversies involving his political activism.

This preprint examines immune-regulatory microenvironments in dermal leishmaniasis lesions using spatial transcriptomics, single-cell imaging, and immunohistochemistry. Analyses included cutaneous leishmaniasis (CL) biopsies from Sri Lanka and Brazil and post kala-azar dermal leishmaniasis biopsies from India.

Myeloid cells expressing the immune checkpoints IDO1 and PD-L1 (encoded by CD274) clustered in lesion cores and deeper T-cell-rich regions. Mature dendritic cells showed the highest proportion of cells with abundant expression of both checkpoints, while CCL18-positive macrophages were prominent within these microenvironments. Nearby cells commonly included CD8-positive memory T cells and regulatory T cells, which were major sources of IL-32. Immunostaining confirmed close proximity between CD8-positive T cells and checkpoint-expressing cells.

Across the three disease forms, five genes—IL32, LYZ, GBP1, IFI30, and FTH1—consistently correlated with IDO1 and CD274 expression. IL32β and IL32γ were the most strongly upregulated IL-32 isoforms in lesions compared with healthy skin.

Among 25 Sri Lankan patients treated with sodium stibogluconate, lower densities of IL-32-positive cells and IL-32-positive CD8 T cells were associated with earlier cure. Corresponding age- and sex-adjusted hazard ratios were 3.5 and 2.78. IL-32-positive regulatory T-cell abundance was not significantly associated with cure rate.

The authors propose that IL-32-producing T cells help generate or maintain checkpoint-expressing myeloid niches that suppress effector T-cell activity and constrain immune-dependent treatment. Limitations included restricted biopsy sampling, small patient groups, unmatched reference datasets for cell identification, and an inability to functionally characterize lesion-derived cells. The findings identify IL-32-positive CD8 T cells as a prognostic marker of treatment response in Sri Lankan CL.

A federal appeals court granted a stay allowing the Education Department to fire 276 of its Office for Civil Rights’ 550 employees. The decision followed a Supreme Court ruling permitting broader departmental layoffs. Although the appeals court acknowledged concerns about OCR’s ability to enforce civil rights laws, it found insufficient differences between the cases to reach a contrary result at this preliminary stage.

Coach Quenneville and Stan Bowman discussed their team’s development, playoff performance and upcoming series. Quenneville described the opposition as disciplined, positionally strong and capable offensively, emphasizing the need to play to their own strengths, challenge the opposing goalie at the net and spend time in the offensive zone. Bowman praised Corey’s consistent goaltending and gradual development within the organization, along with Bryan’s progress and contributions. He credited organizational success to scouting, coaching and player development rather than any individual.

Quenneville said the experienced core could support younger teammates and noted increased enthusiasm and improvement throughout the playoffs. He also praised Sharp’s productivity and two-way play, discussed possible lineup adjustments and reflected on his time with the Windsor Spitfires.

The AMD Secure RNG library simplifies access to hardware-generated random numbers through the x86 RDRAND and RDSEED instructions. RDRAND returns random values, while RDSEED returns conditioned random values.

The library provides APIs for individual 16-, 32-, and 64-bit values, arrays of 32- or 64-bit values, and byte arrays. It abstracts low-level instruction handling, checks for hardware failures, supports configurable retry attempts, and reports success or failure. Applications should first verify instruction support using the CPUID-based is_RDRAND_supported and is_RDSEED_supported APIs.

Applications include Monte Carlo simulations, communication protocols, gaming, cryptographic key generation, and seeding software pseudo-random number generators (PRNGs).

RDRAND and RDSEED access the cryptographic co-processor through memory-mapped I/O, which is relatively slow compared with software PRNGs. For latency-sensitive applications, the passage recommends seeding a software PRNG with a hardware-generated value to improve performance while retaining security benefits.

Carolina Herrera appointed Lisa Arnold vice president of retail and Thea Terenik vice president of global merchandising. Both report to president Emilie Rubinfeld in New York. Arnold will oversee global retail and client service, while Terenik will lead brand positioning and product strategy for luxury ready-to-wear and bridal, with expanding global distribution among her goals.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere architecture, is designed for AI training and inference, high-performance computing (HPC), and data analytics. It combines increased computational throughput, expanded memory and cache capacity, GPU partitioning, faster interconnects, and CUDA 11 programming features.

**Compute architecture and performance**
- Manufactured using TSMC’s 7nm process, the GA100 chip contains 54.2 billion transistors. The A100 implementation includes 108 streaming multiprocessors, 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, and 432 third-generation Tensor Cores.
- Tensor Cores support FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. TF32 accepts FP32 input and produces FP32 output while using reduced internal precision.
- Compared with V100, A100 delivers up to 2.5 times the dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision Tensor Core performance and FP64 performance. TF32 operations provide up to 10 times V100’s standard FP32 throughput, increasing to 20 times with sparsity.
- Fine-grained structured sparsity uses a pattern of two nonzero values per four entries. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zeros to double computation throughput. The described inference workflow trains dense weights, prunes them, and fine-tunes remaining weights, with virtually no accuracy loss in evaluated networks. Training acceleration without accuracy loss remains an active research area.

**Memory and data movement**
- A100 provides 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per streaming multiprocessor.
- Compared with V100, HBM2 bandwidth increases by 73%, L2 capacity grows nearly sevenfold, and L2 read bandwidth increases 2.3 times.
- Cache residency controls prioritize reusable data. Compute Data Compression can improve DRAM and L2 bandwidth by up to four times and effective L2 capacity by up to twice.
- Asynchronous copying transfers data directly from global to shared memory without intermediate register storage. Asynchronous barriers allow computation and data transfers to overlap.

**GPU sharing and reliability**
- Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources.
- Isolated memory paths provide predictable throughput and latency, quality of service, and fault isolation for workloads sharing a physical GPU.
- GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, enabling independent context execution. MIG supports multi-tenant services, shared workgroups, and multiple applications belonging to one user.
- ECC protection and enhanced error detection, attribution, isolation, and containment improve reliability.

**Connectivity and software**
- Third-generation NVLink provides 12 links and 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections and supports SR-IOV virtualization.
- NVSwitch, Mellanox networking, and Magnum IO support multi-GPU and multi-node scaling.
- CUDA 11 supports A100’s Tensor Core formats, sparsity, MIG, cache controls, asynchronous operations, and hardware-accelerated reductions. CUDA Task Graph optimizations reduce launch overhead and execution latency for repeated workflows.
- Additional hardware includes JPEG decoding, five video decoders, and an optical flow accelerator.

**DGX A100**
The DGX A100 integrates eight A100 GPUs connected through six NVSwitches, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance in a 6U system. MIG enables up to 56 isolated GPU Instances. Mellanox networking supports large clusters, while the DGX software stack and NGC provide frameworks, applications, and development tools for deployment.

The bearish engulfing candlestick pattern consists of a bullish candle followed by a larger bearish candle whose body completely engulfs the first. Typically appearing during an uptrend, it is interpreted as a potential shift toward bearish sentiment and a possible downward reversal. Unlike bullish engulfing, which signals a potential upward reversal, bearish engulfing may prompt traders to close long positions or consider short positions.

The passage emphasizes that the pattern does not guarantee a reversal. Confirmation may involve other technical indicators, changes in momentum or price action, and the broader trend. RSI, MACD, moving averages, and oscillators can supplement analysis.

The passage reports a stock-market win rate of 55–65% and 311 occurrences in the S&P 500 since 1993, making it the third most frequent of 75 candlestick patterns examined. Despite its conventional bearish interpretation, it also describes the pattern as frequently bullish or a continuation signal in stocks. One reported backtest buying the pattern and selling after eight trading days produced 258 trades averaging a 0.73% gain. Requiring a five-day RSI above 60 reduced trades to 58 and increased the average gain to 0.88%.

Risks include false signals, changing market conditions, volatility, and amplified losses from leverage. Other limitations include subjectivity, unclear signals, and unsuitability for some time frames. Suggested risk-management methods include stop-loss orders, position sizing, risk/reward assessment, diversification, hedging, and a defined trading plan.

The passage recommends backtesting clearly defined rules and evaluating profitability rather than relying solely on win rates.

The 50 EMA strategy uses the 50-day exponential moving average to identify medium-term trends and generate trading signals. Prices above an upward-sloping EMA indicate an uptrend; prices below a downward-sloping EMA indicate a downtrend. Traders commonly enter long positions above the EMA and short positions below it, using indicators such as RSI or MACD for confirmation.

The passage emphasizes backtesting to select timeframes, settings, and complementary indicators. It discusses stop-loss orders, take-profit orders, and diversification, while noting that the authors rarely find stop-loss orders improve backtested strategies.

Reported backtests show mixed results:
- A moving-average crossover system performed poorly across multiple assets.
- An S&P 500 test returned 6.8% annually versus 7.3% for buy-and-hold, with maximum drawdowns of 32% and 56%, respectively, excluding dividends.
- Using the 50 EMA as a filter with a second indicator produced QQQ annual returns of 11.5% versus 9.8% for buy-and-hold, with a 22% maximum drawdown versus 83%. Slippage and commissions were excluded.
- The modified strategy returned 8.9% annually on SPY versus 9.9% for buy-and-hold, with a 16% maximum drawdown.
- TLT averaged 0.18% per trade, which the passage describes as too small.

U.S. manufacturing has nearly 390,000 job openings but faces a shortage of qualified workers as automation and advanced technology require more education and specialized skills. Workers displaced by factory closures and offshoring struggle to qualify, while those with in-demand skills benefit.

Liberal nonprofits are preparing for potential investigations and other actions by the Trump administration, considering emergency funds, mergers, legal challenges, relocation abroad, and surrendering nonprofit tax status to operate as businesses.

After Charlie Kirk’s murder, administration officials and allies intensified allegations linking nonprofits to political violence. Trump announced that he was designating “antifa” a terrorist organization and recommended investigating its funders. Justice Department officials are drafting plans for a potential investigation of Open Society Foundations, which rejected the accusations and said its work is peaceful and lawful.

Nonprofit leaders say preparations have been underway for months. Organizations are reviewing financial and legal compliance, while foundations are accelerating grants to address funding gaps and strengthen the sector’s readiness. Republican legislative efforts have also targeted organizations accused of supporting terrorism or riots.

Alternative structures carry risks: becoming a business could reduce financial transparency, while relocating abroad could complicate funding US operations. Sector representatives warn that legal battles could drain resources and damage reputations even if nonprofits ultimately prevail. Some organizations are already removing website content, prompting concerns that funding threats could encourage self-censorship and changes to programming.

The Texas Instruments MSPM0C1105/6 are low-power, 32-bit Arm Cortex-M0+ microcontrollers operating at up to 32MHz, with supply voltages of 1.62–3.6V and a temperature range of −40°C to 125°C. They provide up to 64KB flash, 8KB SRAM, and software-configurable peripherals accessed through memory-mapped registers.

- **Processing and memory:** The CPU subsystem includes instruction prefetch/cache, a 24-bit SysTick timer, and interrupt management with four programmable priority levels. Flash supports 1KB erase sectors, up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on the first 32KB, and up to 10,000 cycles on remaining flash. SRAM offers zero-wait-state access and configurable write protection.
- **Power and clocks:** Five operating modes—RUN, SLEEP, STOP, STANDBY, and SHUTDOWN—and two power domains balance performance and consumption. SRAM is retained except in SHUTDOWN. The power management unit supplies internal regulation and brown-out monitoring. Clock sources include internal 32kHz and 32MHz oscillators and external crystal or clock inputs.
- **Data movement and events:** A three-channel DMA controller transfers data without CPU intervention. An event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals.
- **Analog functions:** Features include a 12-bit ADC operating at up to 1.6Msps, a temperature sensor with factory calibration, and a comparator with an 8-bit reference DAC. The shared voltage reference provides selectable 1.4V or 2.5V references and supports external references; internal-reference ADC operation is supported up to 515ksps.
- **Digital peripherals:** Devices provide up to 45 GPIOs, configurable pin multiplexing, three UARTs, two I2C interfaces, and one SPI interface. I2C supports rates up to 1Mbps, while SPI supports up to 16Mbit/s. Timing resources include four 16-bit general-purpose timers, one advanced timer with deadband and clocking up to 64MHz, independent and windowed watchdogs, and a real-time clock.
- **Security and debugging:** Features include code/data firewalls, CRC-16, a two-wire serial debug interface, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Read-only factory memory contains device identification, capabilities, and trim information.

Application guidance recommends nearby 10µF and 0.1µF supply-decoupling capacitors, a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown capacitor on NRST, and pullup resistors for open-drain outputs. Relevant package thermal pads must be soldered to the circuit board.

TI provides development tools, software, training, reference documentation, and support forums. The September 2025 revision updates specifications, removes DGS32 package information, adds debug-subsystem documentation, and revises identification tables. Emory University researchers found that mice fed the probiotic Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG (LGG) for two weeks had an improved liver antioxidant response after receiving high doses of acetaminophen, protecting against oxidative damage. The study identified the protein Nrf2, which regulates genes involved in fighting free radicals, as important to this protection. Further studies are needed to determine whether these findings apply to humans. Probiotics are not a substitute for medicine, and the passage recommends consulting a doctor before starting a new supplement.

The 1-2-2 zone is effective against outside shooting, supports fast breaks, and can protect late-game leads against three-point attempts. Its initial alignment places one defender at the top of the circle, two at the elbows, and two above the blocks. Defenders keep their arms extended and shift while passes are airborne.

The point guards the ball out front and protects the high post when it moves to a wing or corner. Wings alternate between guarding the ball and covering the middle, with weakside rebounding responsibilities on corner possessions. Baseline defenders coordinate coverage of corners, the low post, and the basket. All defenders collapse when the ball enters the middle.

Adjustments include having wings deny return passes or help defend the low post, trapping corner ball handlers, and switching to a 2-1-2 zone on the first pass. The defense can also extend into a half- or full-court press.

Kenyatta National Hospital (KNH) enforced Kenya’s national referral guidelines on July 1, 2021, to reduce inappropriate referrals and prioritize complex cases. Referring facilities were required to obtain concurrence from KNH’s referral office and provide official referral letters.

A retrospective pre-post study examined 468 orthopaedic and trauma referral records, comparing February–June with August–December 2021. Most referrals originated from Nairobi and neighbouring counties, and government facilities supplied the majority.

After enforcement, referrals from tiers 2 and 3 declined, while those from tiers 4–6 increased. Differences by facility tier were statistically significant (p=0.002), whereas differences between government and private facility referrals were not (p=0.411). Forty-three facilities stopped referring patients directly to KNH; 67.4% were private, and 81.4% were tiers 2–4.

Factors associated with referrals included inadequate staffing, infrastructure, equipment and implants, financial considerations, and patient preference. Staffing capacity and availability were the leading factors in both government and private facilities. Patient preference was more frequently recorded among private-facility referrals.

The study concluded that enforcing referral guidelines reduced direct referrals from lower-tier facilities. Its retrospective, quasi-experimental design limited causal conclusions, and COVID-19 potentially affected referral patterns. Recommendations included strengthening staffing, regularly educating facilities about referral requirements, developing standard operating procedures, and training KNH staff and referring facilities to support adherence.

In Closson v. Billman, Closson sought to foreclose a material supplier’s lien for $863.35 in lumber used to build a house. He had also signed the contractor’s $1,500 bond guaranteeing performance of the building contract. The defendants argued that his liability under the bond barred recovery on the lien.

The court held that the bond and contract must be read together. The contractor’s obligation to furnish materials and complete the residence included paying for those materials and delivering the house free of material liens. Completing construction according to the plans and specifications alone did not fulfill that obligation.

Closson was a guarantor, not a surety, because he guaranteed performance of the separate building contract. His resulting liability provided a sufficient defense to his foreclosure action, avoiding separate litigation over the same obligation.

Notice of acceptance was unnecessary because the guaranty was executed contemporaneously with, and as part of the consideration for, the underlying transaction. Closson bore the burden of pleading and proving any failure to notify him of default and resulting damage. The judgment for the defendants was affirmed.

Texas Tech University removed an FAQ clarifying restrictions on teaching about transgender identity after three days, without explaining why to faculty. The guidance applied only to its flagship campus and stated that research was unaffected. It advised faculty to omit pronoun language and LGBTQ allyship statements from syllabi, while allowing relevant classroom discussions of differing views without instructor advocacy.

At the university’s Health Sciences Center, an anonymous faculty member reported verbal prohibitions on terms including “transgender” and “gender-affirming care,” but no written guidance. Health-care instructors worry students will lack preparation for transgender patient care covered in some licensing exams. The Texas conference of the American Association of University Professors criticized the restrictions and urged policies protecting academic freedom and involving faculty participation.

The Sustainable Development Goals and the Incheon Declaration establish a vision of inclusive, equitable, quality education and lifelong learning for all by 2030. Education is presented both as a goal and as a prerequisite for achieving other development goals. Despite decades of expansion, education systems faced substantial deficiencies in participation, quality and equality before COVID-19. Globally, 258 million school-age children were out of school, while inequalities persisted across socioeconomic, gender and racial or ethnic groups.

Pandemic-related institutional closures affected approximately 91% of the global student population. The shift to online and home-based learning disrupted access and quality, disproportionately affecting disadvantaged students. However, the pandemic also compelled education systems to adopt technologies they had previously resisted, creating opportunities to advance educational goals.

The paper argues that Comparative and International Education should examine pandemic damage and technology-based responses across different educational and societal contexts. Such comparisons could guide the effective use of technology and support recovery beyond pre-pandemic conditions.

This work could also address weaknesses within the field, including inadequate responsiveness to emerging opportunities, insufficient attention to classroom teaching and learning, reliance on theories from other disciplines, limited university presence, persistent Northern dominance and weak demonstrable influence on practice and policy. The author calls for a reinvigorated field that uses pandemic experiences to help build better education systems and advance the 2030 vision.

NVIDIA’s shading advancements include mesh shading, which shifts object processing from CPUs to GPUs and supports advanced geometry and detail management. Variable Rate Shading dynamically adjusts shading effort to improve efficiency and frame rates. Texture-space shading caches results for reuse, reducing duplicate work or improving quality. Multi-View Rendering enables multiple views with different origins or directions to be rendered in a single pass.

Delta Insurance is expanding its presence in the South Island’s growing technology sector, joining Canterbury Tech and offering technology and cyber liability coverage. South Island underwriter Karl Samson brings 12 years of industry experience and local broker knowledge.

W. T. Hay appealed the refusal to stay execution against real estate conveyed through his brother to his wife before his bankruptcy. Deposit National Bank sought execution on a pre-bankruptcy judgment, alleging the conveyance was fraudulent, despite Hay’s subsequent discharge.

The court held that Hay lacked standing because he neither owned nor claimed the property, and execution had been permanently stayed against him personally and any property he owned. The proposed sale therefore affected none of his rights. Questions concerning the bank’s authority to proceed and whether the sale would convey valid title could not be raised by Hay, though his wife could raise them if a purchaser sought to eject her. The appeal was dismissed at Hay’s costs.
A study shows live ants and their bacteria acidify and thicken milk into yogurt, a traditional practice in Bulgaria and Turkey.

The passage proposes intensified U.S.-Soviet dialogue in 1983 while maintaining established policy standards. Priorities include verifiable arms reductions, military equality, stability, and Western Alliance cohesion; diplomatic pressure on regional conflicts; and improvements in Soviet human rights through private diplomacy. Economic initiatives should neither strengthen Soviet military power nor subsidize its economy, and bilateral exchanges should ensure reciprocity and broader access to Soviet society. The disclosure describes systems, methods, devices, and computer-readable media for vehicle route planning, particularly for automated guided vehicles (AGVs), using maps modified according to other vehicles’ motion status.

The planning process obtains a vehicle’s start location, destination, and a map containing nodes and their information. Node information may include location, weight, passability, turning capability, adjacency, and connectivity. The system obtains information identifying other vehicles as stationary or moving, modifies relevant map nodes, and determines a route using the modified map.

Map preprocessing may occur in two stages. The first modifies nodes within regions occupied by or surrounding stationary vehicles, assigning high weights, restricting turns, or marking nodes as impassable. A candidate route is then calculated. If that route conflicts with moving vehicles’ routes, a second preprocessing stage also modifies nodes along portions of those vehicles’ planned routes that they have not yet traversed, and route planning is repeated. These stages may also be performed separately.

Start and destination nodes may be selected as the nearest available nodes that are neither barriers nor occupied by other vehicles. Route selection evaluates node costs combining accumulated costs, node weights, travel distances, turning costs, and estimated distance to the destination. Examples use Manhattan distance and a weighted change in angle. An iterative search maintains open and closed node sets, selects minimum-cost nodes, and reconstructs the route through parent nodes. A binary heap may support minimum-cost selection. Disclosed planning algorithms include A-star, modified A-star, Dijkstra, Floyd-Warshall, and rapidly-exploring random trees.

The scheduling system may also allocate tasks according to vehicle availability. Tasks assigned to a specified vehicle wait until it becomes idle; unspecified tasks may be assigned to the idle vehicle nearest the destination. Map information may be updated periodically or upon request.

An example implementation includes a server, network, vehicles, terminal devices, and storage. Processing may occur locally, remotely, on an onboard computer, or through a cloud platform. Vehicles can transmit motion information and receive tasks and routes, while terminal interfaces allow users to view information and issue instructions. The stated objectives are improved route-planning accuracy and efficiency and avoidance of collisions with stationary and moving vehicles.

The issuance was conducted under a November 6, 2017 underwriting agreement and an April 29, 2013 indenture with The Bank of New York Mellon Trust Company, N.A., as trustee.
