The Jerusalem Post seeks reader support through a $5 monthly subscription while keeping journalism accessible without a paywall. Benefits include reduced ads, premium content, Ivrit magazine, Jerusalem Report content, and a daily ePaper.

Best Buy offers the Lenovo Legion 7i Gen 10 for $1,650, a $220 discount. It features a 2,560 × 1,600 OLED display with a 165-Hz refresh rate, a 115-watt RTX 5060 GPU, and a well-rated keyboard and trackpad. Battery life was under five hours in video playback testing. Despite the discount, it remains more expensive than some lower-wattage RTX 5060 laptops priced near $1,000.

Amazon.com, Inc.’s Form 8-K dated February 1, 2018 reports the announcement of its fourth-quarter and full-year 2017 financial results. The filing incorporates Exhibit 99.1, the earnings press release, and Exhibit 99.2, information regarding non-GAAP financial measures. Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Brian T. Olsavsky signed the report.

The study investigated Cu-doped nickel oxide (NiO) thin films for liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) sensing using ultra-fast spray pyrolysis. Undoped and Cu-doped films were deposited on ITO-coated glass at 450 °C in 1.5 minutes. The doped precursor contained 7 wt% copper chloride dihydrate relative to nickel chloride hexahydrate.

Structural characterization indicated Cu incorporation into the cubic NiO lattice. Doping increased the lattice parameter from 4.18 to 4.20 Å and reduced crystallite size from 21 to 20 nm. Raman measurements showed vibrational shifts and disappearance of the TO mode, indicating structural distortion. Cu doping also enhanced visible-light absorption, narrowed the optical bandgap from 3.70 to 3.65 eV, and reduced photoluminescence intensity, suggesting additional defect states and non-radiative recombination centers.

Gas-sensing measurements used approximately 1 vol% LPG. At 5 V, current increased from 249 to 327 mA for undoped NiO and from 265 to 480 mA for Cu-doped NiO under LPG exposure. Sensitivity, defined as the gas-exposure current divided by the ambient-air current, increased from 1.3 for NiO to 1.8 for Cu-doped NiO.

The authors attribute the improved sensing response to modified charge transport, increased adsorption sites, and enhanced surface reactivity, identifying rapid deposition combined with Cu doping as a promising approach for low-cost NiO-based gas sensors.

U.S. airlines canceled 1.17 percent of domestic flights in 2016, a record low. Mishandled baggage and involuntary passenger bumping also reached record-low rates. On-time arrivals improved to 81.4 percent, with Hawaiian Airlines ranking first among 12 major carriers. Transportation Department complaints fell 11.3 percent to 17,904.

Alek Minassian, 25, was charged with 10 counts of first-degree murder after allegedly driving a rental van into pedestrians in Toronto, killing 10 people and injuring 15. His motive remained unclear. Officials said the attack posed no national security threat and had not changed Canada’s threat level or G7 security preparations. Prime Minister Justin Trudeau urged Canadians to stand united with Toronto. Mourners left flowers and messages, while flags were lowered to half-staff. The officer who arrested Minassian was praised for doing so peacefully.

Oregon Health & Science University researchers report that a technique that produced healthy mice from lab-created eggs using skin-cell DNA has been mostly unsuccessful with human cells. The team developed “mitomeiosis,” a process to reduce chromosome numbers, but major obstacles remain before clinical testing. If refined, the approach could help treat infertility, prevent heritable diseases, and enable same-sex couples to have genetically related children.

A study of 19 mothers and their babies suggests dopamine plays a role in mother-infant bonding. Brain scans showed mothers released more dopamine when watching videos of their own babies than other babies. Higher dopamine release was associated with more responsive caregiving and greater sensitivity to infants’ needs, while less responsive mothers released less dopamine.

Researchers suggested these processes may continue as children grow and could support other close caregiving relationships. Further research is needed to determine whether fathers and other caregivers experience similar responses. The study’s small size limits its generalizability, and it cannot establish whether mothers are predisposed to stronger bonding before childbirth.

The National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) entered 2020 with growing interest following the U.S. women’s national team’s 2019 World Cup victory, but remained financially vulnerable. Founded in 2012 after two predecessor leagues failed, it prioritized stability through a single-entity structure, spending controls, and financial and operational support from U.S. Soccer.

Lisa Baird became commissioner on March 10, 2020, just before COVID-19 disrupted professional sports. Her initial plans to expand staffing, sponsorships, and fan engagement shifted toward preserving a season while protecting players’ health. A Paycheck Protection Program loan funded non-allocated players’ compensation, and owners committed to maintaining all players’ pay and health insurance throughout the year, including those who opted out of competition.

Baird organized workstreams addressing medical protocols, finances, competition format, facilities, player concerns, childcare, and social justice. These efforts produced the Challenge Cup, held near Salt Lake City from June 27 to July 26. Eight teams participated after Orlando withdrew because of COVID-19 cases. The tournament cost $1.8 million, recorded no positive cases across more than 2,000 tests, and ended with Houston defeating Chicago. More than 650,000 viewers watched the final on CBS, setting a league record.

The NWSL subsequently organized an 18-game Fall Series, securing broadcast opportunities opened by postponed college football. New CBS and Twitch agreements and sponsorships from Google, Verizon, and P&G/Secret supported the league’s commercial development. Television viewership increased 493% over 2019, while social and traditional media mentions also rose. Players used the season to support racial justice, including wearing Black Lives Matter shirts and kneeling during the national anthem.

Despite these gains, the league faced limited mainstream coverage, uneven attendance, low player salaries, and competition from European clubs. Its dedicated fans relied heavily on social media and supporter communities.

Entering 2021, priorities included expansion, deeper fan engagement, increased revenue and media exposure, improved player compensation, a planned rebrand, and collective bargaining negotiations with the NWSL Players Association. Following its December 2020 separation from U.S. Soccer’s management, the league also needed to establish governance arrangements and redefine that partnership while balancing investment with financial sustainability.

AMC management proposes doubling authorized shares to 1.1 billion, risking further shareholder dilution. Despite debt refinancings and adjustments, net debt remains above $3 billion, while third-quarter box office revenues were weak. The passage attributes AMC’s steep valuation discount to peer CNK to ongoing losses, negative equity, and persistent cash burn. AMC also struggled during the pandemic as attendance plunged and releases were delayed.

Improving farmers’ conditions requires practical education, cooperative organization, and government support, though farmers must primarily rely on their own efforts. Education should develop work skills, citizenship, and cooperation. The Department of Agriculture assists farmer associations, coordinates with state agricultural and educational authorities, and helps organize efforts against the boll weevil and cattle fever tick. Irrigation and forest preservation have benefited the Rocky Mountains and Great Plains; national action is also urged to preserve White Mountain and Southern Appalachian forests.

The passage recommends congressional funding for preliminary work on a memorial amphitheater at Arlington to honor military dead and support Memorial Day observances. It also advocates national authority over marriage and divorce to address abuses arising from differing state laws, and federal power to deal with polygamy regardless of broader marriage-law reform.

Researchers created experimental human egg cells by replacing donor egg nuclei with skin cell nuclei, then using fertilization and the chemical roscovitine to trigger chromosome reduction. Some developed into early embryos, but none had the correct chromosome sets and all were nonviable. Development was limited to about six days.

The proof-of-concept technique could eventually help people with infertility or allow male same-sex couples to have genetically related children. However, it remains inefficient, high-risk and dependent on donor eggs. Researchers are working to improve chromosome division and estimate at least a decade before potential clinical trials.

The passage presents Robert Stuart’s allegations that the BBC Panorama documentary “Saving Syria’s Children” included fabricated footage. The footage concerned an alleged incendiary attack on a Syrian school on August 29, 2013, and aired as the UK Parliament prepared to vote on military action against Syria.

The author cites questions about visible injuries, reported casualty counts ranging from 25 to 50, and conflicting accounts of the attack’s timing. The passage also scrutinizes the military background of Dr Saleyah Ahsan and alleged political connections involving Dr Rola Hallam’s father. It argues that these issues suggest possible fabrication and raises broader questions about reporting used to justify Western military intervention.

Trauma can affect postsecondary students’ attendance, academic performance, memory, concentration, relationships, and well-being. An estimated 50%–70% have experienced at least one adverse childhood experience. Healthcare students also face risks of secondary traumatic stress and vicarious trauma through educational and clinical activities. Studies of occupational therapy (OT) students describe disruptions to daily routines and learning, alongside reluctance to disclose trauma because of stigma.

This literature review examines trauma-informed care (TIC) frameworks, educational models, and strategies for health professions education, particularly OT. SAMHSA’s framework emphasizes safety; trustworthiness and transparency; peer support; collaboration; empowerment, voice, and choice; and recognition of cultural, historical, and gender-specific issues. Implementation involves institutional leadership, faculty, staff, and students, supported by training, policies, resources, safe environments, and ongoing evaluation.

Recommended educational practices include:
- Providing advance notice of potentially triggering content without removing challenging material.
- Using clear communication, predictable routines, flexible teaching, and student collaboration.
- Incorporating self-care activities, emotional check-ins, peer support, and referrals to appropriate services.
- Creating culturally responsive learning environments and involving trauma survivors in planning and evaluation.
- Offering faculty development and assessing educators’ knowledge and attitudes toward TIC.

TIC education remains limited in OT curricula. Studies of the simulation-based PATH model reported improvements in students’ knowledge of adverse childhood experiences and TIC, with some reporting increased self-efficacy. The review recommends introducing trauma education early and reinforcing it throughout professional training.

Trauma-informed practices may support student engagement, satisfaction, and academic participation. Increased retention, graduation, and degree attainment are identified as possible long-term outcomes. OT educators are encouraged to reflect on whether their teaching methods and policies support students with trauma histories.

AGESA firmware integration covers processor and memory initialization, UEFI coordination, platform configuration, diagnostic services, and suspend/resume operations.

- **UEFI coordination:** PPIs signal completion of early processor initialization and memory initialization. A memory-information HOB describes available memory after AmdInitPost, except during S3 resume. Memory is unavailable for general system use until the standard EfiMemory PPI is published. A reset-coordination PEIM handles warm-reset requests from AMD modules. DXE drivers expose generated information tables and control integrated-GPU VGA decoding according to host requests.

- **Build integration:** AGESA supports binary-module builds and source integration. Platform option files customize build defaults, while UEFI control files and environment variables establish build locations and requirements. Only published entry functions are assured to remain available.

- **Stack and cache requirements:** Provided assembly macros establish and remove pre-memory Cache-As-RAM stacks. The host must not modify SS, ESP, or cache controls during the specified Cache-As-RAM period. Early initialization requires host-allocated parameter storage. AARCH64 APUs with the Platform Security Processor do not use the early stack macros; the PSP initializes DRAM.

- **Initialization sequence:** AmdInitReset performs minimal processor initialization and configures execution-cache regions. AmdInitEarly performs fuller processor, interconnect, and power-management configuration and may request a warm reset. AmdInitPost initializes system memory and transfers pre-memory data into main memory. AmdInitEnv moves artifact data into permanent host-managed buffers before PCI enumeration. Subsequent graphics configuration occurs after resource allocation and before the video BIOS call. AmdInitLate generates operating-system information tables and prepares processor power states for OS entry.

- **Configuration and services:** Settings cover processor power limits, voltage regulators, PCIe topology, graphics, chipset controllers, memory timing, interleaving, ECC, training, UMA allocation, and memory-context restoration. Service functions allocate and release parameter structures, retrieve processor addresses and identities, report execution-cache capacity and DIMM data-eye results, locate memory devices associated with system addresses, update MMIO mappings, and read event-log entries.

- **Suspend and resume:** Ready-To-Boot processing saves processor and silicon context but does not initiate suspend. The host preserves memory-critical data in nonvolatile storage and other context in retained memory or nonvolatile storage. Resume procedures restart memory, restore registers after PCI restoration, and perform final preparation for OS handoff. The host initiates OS restart.

- **Required host call-outs:** The host supplies buffer allocation, deallocation and lookup, system reset, applicable DIMM SPD reads, and application-processor task execution. Runtime allocations must remain reserved. SPD-reading requirements differ for newer PSP-equipped APUs that perform memory initialization. Many AGESA services require an established stack, preserved artifact data, and unobstructed interprocessor communication.

- House appropriators proposed FY2002 discretionary allocations totaling $661.3 billion, generally following President Bush’s requests but providing more for Labor-HHS, VA-HUD, and Energy and Water. House leaders intended to hold FY2001 supplemental spending to Bush’s requested level despite demands for additional defense funding.

Deletions of the *Plasmodium falciparum pfhrp2/3* genes can cause false-negative results in HRP2-based malaria rapid diagnostic tests (RDTs), threatening malaria control. By 2023, deletions had been reported in 40 of 47 surveyed countries, with false-negative rates reaching 80% in the worst-affected settings. Alternative RDTs face limitations in sensitivity and availability.

This study updated an individual-based malaria transmission model using surveillance data and estimates of malaria prevalence, diagnostic practices, treatment-seeking, parasite fitness and HRP3 cross-reactivity. It developed two measures aligned with WHO’s 5% threshold for clinically relevant infections misdiagnosed because of deletions:
- **Innate Risk:** how quickly misdiagnosis would rise from 1% to 5% once deletions are established, assuming HRP2-based RDT use.
- **Prospective Risk:** projected spread incorporating reported deletion frequencies, current RDT use and simplified movement between neighbouring regions.

Globally, an estimated 63.5% of pfhrp2-deleted samples also carried pfhrp3 deletions. Model fitting to Eritrean and Ethiopian data estimated deleted parasites’ relative fitness at 96.4% and HRP3 cross-reactivity producing a positive HRP2-based RDT at 29%.

Malaria prevalence was the strongest modelled determinant of deletion selection, with lower prevalence generally favouring faster increases. Under the Innate Risk scenario, 73 of 106 modelled countries had at least one region predicted to reach the 5% misdiagnosis threshold within 20 years. Prospective modelling indicated that 29 of 49 African countries had at least one region already at, or expected to reach, that threshold within 20 years. Continued reliance on HRP2-based diagnosis was projected to favour spread southward from the Horn of Africa through East Africa, alongside increases in parts of West Africa, particularly Senegal and Mali.

Projections carry substantial uncertainty from incomplete and inconsistent surveillance, uncertain malaria prevalence and fitness estimates, simplified geographical spread, and assumptions that transmission and treatment practices remain constant. Very-low-transmission settings also face greater randomness in whether deleted strains spread or disappear.

The study provides interactive risk maps to support surveillance priorities and decisions about alternative diagnostics. It highlights Senegal, Zambia and Kenya among surveillance priorities outside regions already using alternative frontline RDTs, while emphasising that accurate local data are needed before switching tests.

Gas colic is common in horses and, although described as the least serious form of colic, can lead to displacement or twisting of the large colon. It occurs when gas produced during hindgut fermentation accumulates rather than passing normally.

Potential contributors include insufficient forage, confinement, stress, ulcers, intestinal inflammation, inadequate exercise, dehydration, and abrupt feed changes. Restricting forage can encourage rapid eating and interfere with digestion, while confinement reduces intestinal movement and gas clearance. Stress-related inflammation can further increase colic risk.

The article recommends:
- Providing continuous access to forage, including overnight.
- Increasing pasture turnout or outdoor exercise, with hay and water available.
- Introducing new hay over approximately one week and new concentrated feeds over two to three weeks.
- Feeding hay before concentrated meals.
- Avoiding unfamiliar, occasional bran mashes; introducing them gradually and feeding consistently if used.
- Keeping slow feeders full to simulate grazing and encourage self-regulated eating.

It also discusses prebiotics, B vitamins, yeast, and colostrum as digestive-support supplements, and recommends reducing ingredients it identifies as inflammatory, particularly sugar and soy products. Its central recommendation is to align feeding and management with horses’ grazing behavior, making incremental improvements where extensive pasture access is unavailable.

The lecture explores protein folding through fixed-angle linkages: mechanical chains with fixed edge lengths and joint angles that move by rotation around edges. This simplified model ignores energy and biological folding forces to study which configurations and motions are geometrically possible.

Four main problems are examined:
- **Span:** Minimizing or maximizing the distance between endpoints in planar configurations is NP-hard. The general three-dimensional problems remain open, while maximum span for orthogonal chains can be computed in linear time.
- **Flattening:** Determining whether a chain has a planar configuration without self-intersections is weakly NP-hard. Cases with equal or polynomially bounded edge lengths remain unresolved.
- **Flat-state connectivity:** Whether every fixed-angle open chain can move between all its planar configurations without self-intersection is open. Positive results cover several classes, including orthogonal chains, obtuse chains, and chains with equal acute angles. Some more constrained linkages have disconnected planar states.
- **Locked chains:** Fixed-angle chains can have locked configurations. Whether locking occurs when chains simultaneously have equal edge lengths, equal angles, and obtuse angles remains open.

The lecture then introduces **producible protein chains**, motivated by proteins emerging progressively from a ribosome. The ribosome is modeled as a cone that the emerging chain cannot penetrate; the chain also cannot intersect itself.

Under the specified relationship between chain turn angles and cone angle, all producible configurations belong to one connected component of configuration space, together with all planar configurations. The proof constructs a canonical, helix-like configuration inside a narrower cone. Reversing a chain’s production motion while organizing its inserted portion into this canonical form gives an algorithm for connecting producible states.

These results identify a geometric constraint that permits folding algorithms despite the existence of locked configurations elsewhere. Whether such algorithms describe biological folding remains unresolved.

The July 31, 2001 IEP news compilation focuses on California’s energy crisis, financial conflicts involving Gov. Gray Davis’ advisers, and electricity deregulation.

- The SEC reportedly opened a preliminary inquiry into whether Davis’ energy consultants used inside information to trade power-company stocks. Five consultants were dismissed over possible conflicts of interest. Davis spokesman Steve Maviglio disclosed a $12,000 Calpine stock purchase and denied wrongdoing.
- Communications consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo payment for state work under a lawsuit settlement concerning their simultaneous ties to Southern California Edison.
- Davis’ proposed Edison rescue remained stalled as an August 15 legislative deadline approached. Competing proposals differed over utility losses and state acquisition of transmission assets; some legislators and consumer advocates preferred bankruptcy.
- A commentary by Kathleen Connell and Peter Navarro criticized California’s $43 billion in long-term electricity contracts, arguing that their prices and provisions would impose unnecessary costs. Other coverage raised concerns about the contracts’ reliance on fossil fuels.
- State officials said federal refund restrictions could reduce potential electricity refunds from $9 billion to roughly $3.9 billion. The order excluded purchases before October 2000 and direct Department of Water Resources purchases. Davis planned an appeal.
- San Francisco voters would consider two November measures establishing public-power entities. Supporters anticipated greater local control and lower rates; PG&E opposed the proposals.
- Maryland regulators examined whether Baltimore Gas and Electric’s proposed corporate separation would leave it financially vulnerable. Texas prepared to begin a delayed electricity-choice pilot before broader deregulation.
- California’s crisis involved high wholesale prices, constrained supplies and transmission problems. PG&E had filed for bankruptcy, while the state had spent more than $8 billion purchasing electricity for financially troubled utilities.

Tesla issued an additional $127.5 million in 2.375% Convertible Senior Notes due March 15, 2022, on March 30, 2017, after underwriters fully exercised their purchase option on March 27.

In connection with the issuance, Tesla paid approximately $26.6 million for additional note hedge transactions intended to reduce potential stock dilution and/or offset certain cash payments upon conversion.

Tesla also received approximately $6.9 million from selling additional warrants to hedge counterparties. These warrants permit the acquisition of approximately 0.8 million common shares at a strike price of $655 per share, subject to adjustments. They could dilute common stock if its market value exceeds the strike price, unless Tesla elects cash settlement under the applicable terms. The warrants are separate from the notes, and noteholders have no rights concerning them.

The University of Manchester’s Students’ Union launched Earth Week with climate campaigners Asad Rehman and Martin Empson. Rehman highlighted climate-related deaths and displacement, unequal responsibility for emissions, and the need for legal protection for displaced people. Empson encouraged involvement through protests, petitions, contacting MPs and donations. Both advocated cooperation between environmental and migration movements.

European wholesale power prices fell as wind supply increased and demand eased. German and French Wednesday baseload prices dropped 16 percent and 20 percent, respectively. Forward contracts tracked lower coal prices. Traders expected continued weakness amid improved French nuclear supply and sharply lower demand next week.

The American Cancer Society recommends beginning colorectal cancer screening at age 45 for average-risk adults, citing rising incidence among younger adults and modeling showing a favorable balance of benefits and screening burden. Colorectal cancer incidence among people under 50 has increased 51% since 1994.

The recommendation for ages 45–49 is “qualified” because direct evidence is limited; screening for adults 50 and older remains a strong recommendation. Screening should continue through age 75 for average-risk adults in good health with more than 10 years of life expectancy. Decisions for ages 76–85 should be individualized, and screening is discouraged after 85.

Recommended options include annual fecal immunochemical or high-sensitivity guaiac-based stool tests, stool DNA testing every three years, colonoscopy every 10 years, and CT colonography or flexible sigmoidoscopy every five years. The guideline does not prioritize one test over another, emphasizing patient preferences and availability. Positive results from non-colonoscopy tests should be followed by timely colonoscopy.

American Girl will release its first male doll, Logan Everett, on Thursday. A drummer for fellow contemporary character Tenney Grant, Logan reflects fans’ longstanding requests for a boy character. Felicity Merriman also returns Thursday, while filmmaker Z Yang and World War II-era Hawaiian character Nanea will debut later in 2017. Dolls cost $115 each.

Canada’s Privacy Commissioner is investigating Uber’s 2016 breach, which exposed personal information of over 57 million riders and drivers. Uber concealed the breach for over a year and paid thieves $100,000 to destroy the data. The number of affected Canadians remains undisclosed. Other jurisdictions have launched investigations. The commissioner cannot impose fines or binding orders but can seek compliance through Federal Court.

In People v Helzer, Richard Helzer was convicted of two gross indecency offenses and, in a subsequent proceeding before the same jury, of being a sexually delinquent person. He received concurrent sentences of ten years to life. The Court of Appeals ordered a new trial on all charges because he had been allowed only five peremptory jury challenges rather than 20.

The reviewing court held that sexual delinquency is an alternate sentencing provision, not merely a penalty enhancement or an element of the principal offense. It requires conviction of the principal offense and separate proof of sexual delinquency beyond a reasonable doubt.

Because sexual delinquency proceedings involve broad jury discretion, potential prejudice, and possible life imprisonment, a separate jury must decide that charge unless the defendant waives a jury. The defendant receives 20 peremptory challenges when selecting that jury, but only the number appropriate to the principal offense when selecting the initial jury.

The sexual delinquency charge must be brought before trial begins, although pretrial amendments are permitted. The jury deciding the principal offense must not learn of the sexual delinquency charge; such disclosure would henceforth warrant a mistrial or reversal.

The court upheld Helzer’s gross indecency convictions and remanded only for a new sexual delinquency hearing if the prosecutor pursued that charge. Otherwise, or following acquittal, Helzer would be resentenced solely for gross indecency. The court deferred his constitutional claims. Chief Justice Kavanagh dissented, considering the sexual delinquency statute unconstitutionally vague.

Terry Rozier scored a career-high 31 points in his second NBA start, and Jayson Tatum added a career-high 27 as the short-handed Boston Celtics defeated the Atlanta Hawks 119-110. Rozier replaced injured Kyrie Irving, one of four sidelined Celtics. Jaylen Brown contributed 19 points and Al Horford had 17 points and seven assists.

Boston overcame a two-point halftime deficit by outscoring Atlanta 41-20 in the third quarter, earning its fourth win in five games. Taurean Prince led Atlanta with a career-high 31 points and eight rebounds, while Dennis Schroder scored 25. The Hawks lost for the fifth time in six games.

On January 2, 2017, President-elect Donald Trump criticized the cover image of CNN’s book, “Unprecedented: The Election That Changed Everything,” calling it the worst photo of himself while expressing hope that the book would do well. The photo shows Trump pointing; a commemorative inaugural edition featured a different cover image. His tweet prompted users to post awkward photos and criticize his attention to his appearance. Other recent Twitter activity attracting attention included briefly following “Emergency Kittens,” claiming he anticipated his election victory when Hillary Clinton’s campaign canceled fireworks, and retweeting Ivanka Trump’s New Year photo montage.

Radical-pair spin relaxation is relevant to quantum computing, spintronics, quantum biophysics, and avian magnetoreception. Its simulation faces three main challenges: averaging over initially mixed nuclear-spin configurations, exponentially growing state spaces, and stable propagation over nanosecond-to-microsecond timescales. Classical nuclear-spin approximations reduce computational demands, but full quantum treatments are needed for quantitative accuracy across diverse systems.

The work introduces tensor-network methods to spin chemistry, explains radical-pair modelling challenges, and highlights avian magnetoreception. The radical-pair Hamiltonian includes Zeeman, hyperfine, exchange, dipolar, and spin-selective Haberkorn relaxation terms. Electronic-state populations are key observables.

Three tensor-network representations are introduced: stochastic matrix product states (MPS), vectorised matrix product density operators (vMPDO), and locally purified MPS. Stochastic MPS uses spin-coherent-state sampling and reduces wavefunction storage from exponential scaling to a form governed by system size, local dimension, and bond dimension. Density-operator approaches enable deterministic evaluation without extensive stochastic sampling. Vectorisation reshapes an MPDO into an MPS-like structure for superoperator-based evolution. Time-dependent variational-principle methods support tensor-network propagation with long-range interactions.

Twelve boys and their soccer coach were found alive 1.2 miles inside Thailand’s Tham Luang Nang Non cave after nine days trapped by flooding. A cave rescuer with more than 30 years of experience describes the operation as one of the toughest he has seen.

Waiting for floodwaters to recede is usually the safest approach, but monsoon rains could keep this cave flooded for months. Its relatively warm temperature helped the group avoid hypothermia, while nine days without food left them weak and requiring gradual feeding.

Rescue possibilities include diving them out, drilling an entrance, finding another entrance, or waiting while pumping water. Diving is the most dangerous option because of strenuous conditions, tight passages and the group’s lack of training. Drilling requires heavy equipment and precise mapping, and searches have not found another entrance.

If their location remains safe from further flooding and divers can deliver supplies and care, the group can remain inside. Otherwise, a diving evacuation may be necessary.

The Arizona Supreme Court held that A.R.S. § 13-4033(B) bars direct appeals of contested post-judgment restitution orders entered pursuant to noncapital plea agreements that contemplate restitution and cap its amount. Defendants must seek appellate review through Rule 32 post-conviction relief proceedings.

Frank Hoffman pleaded no contest to driving under the influence and agreed to pay restitution up to $53,653.45. Following a contested hearing, the city court ordered restitution of $40,933.45. The superior court dismissed his direct appeal.

The Supreme Court concluded that the restitution order was part of Hoffman’s sentence and arose directly from his plea agreement, even though he contested the amount. Treating such orders as appealable separately would undermine the legislative goal of limiting direct appeals involving plea agreements and create a burdensome dual-track review system. The general authorization to appeal post-judgment orders affecting substantial rights did not override the plea-agreement exception.

The court affirmed the dismissal and emphasized that Rule 32 must preserve pleading defendants’ constitutional right to appellate review.

Apple Inc.’s July 31, 2018 Form 8-K reports the issuance of a press release and related data sheet covering financial results for its third fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018. These documents are attached as Exhibits 99.1 and 99.2. The report’s information is not deemed filed under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act or incorporated into other filings unless expressly referenced. Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer Luca Maestri signed the report.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint describes a blood-based test intended to support diagnosis of glial malignancies in patients with intracranial lesions. Standard diagnosis requires tissue obtained through surgery or biopsy, which can carry procedural risks.

The test enriches circulating glial cells from peripheral blood and identifies them through GFAP and OLIG2 expression using immunocytochemistry. Analytical validation found a detection limit of 1 cell per 5 mL and a quantitation limit of 6 cells per 5 mL. Clinical samples could be stored at 2–8°C for up to 48 hours with no more than 15% cell loss.

Clinical evaluations included two case-control studies and two prospective studies:
- The first case-control study’s blinded test set achieved 100% sensitivity and specificity.
- The second distinguished glial malignancies from benign brain tumors, epithelial malignancies with brain metastases, and healthy individuals with 100% sensitivity and specificity.
- Prospective studies involving 68 and 31 patients reported sensitivities of 100% and 92.9%, respectively, with 100% specificity in both.

EGFR findings in circulating glial cells and matched tumor tissue were fully concordant in the evaluated glial malignancy cases. The authors reported overall clinical sensitivity above 99% and specificity of 100%.

The test is intended to support clinical decision-making, not determine tumor subtype or grade. It does not detect rarer malignancies such as CNS lymphoma and gliosarcoma. Datar Cancer Genetics Private Limited funded the entire study; several authors were company employees, and one was its founder.

The Bank of Japan is unlikely to rush an exit from ultra-loose monetary policy despite strong economic growth, sources say, because of low inflation and fears that tightening could trigger a sharp yen appreciation. Any increase in yield targets next year would likely be modest and isolated rather than begin a rate-hiking cycle. Political pressure, an impending leadership change and concerns about stock prices further complicate normalization. NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, artificial intelligence, and new shading techniques to improve graphics performance and image quality.

- **Memory:** Turing introduces GDDR6 memory operating at 14 Gbps, with a stated 20% power-efficiency improvement over Pascal’s GDDR5X. Larger caches and improved lossless compression contribute to approximately 50% higher effective memory bandwidth for the RTX 2080 Ti compared with the GTX 1080 Ti. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice that of GP102.

- **Displays, video, and connectivity:** Turing supports two 8K displays at 60 Hz, DisplayPort 1.4a, Display Stream Compression, native HDR processing, and tone mapping. Its NVENC encoder supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps, with bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. USB-C and VirtualLink hardware support combines VR headset power, display, and data connections into one connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI, providing up to 100 GB/s and 50 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, respectively.

- **Ray tracing:** Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding volume hierarchy traversal and ray–triangle intersection testing, freeing shader processors for other work. Combined with denoising and hybrid rendering, these cores enable real-time ray tracing on a single Turing GPU. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where efficient and ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, and shadows. The passage reports ray-tracing performance approximately ten times faster than Pascal.

- **AI-based graphics:** NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for image enhancement. Deep Learning Super-Sampling, or DLSS, targets image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work. DLSS training uses reference images rendered with 64× supersampling; a separate DLSS 2X mode prioritizes higher image quality. Other NGX features include image inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and image or video upscaling.

- **Rendering efficiency:** Mesh shading introduces task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rates within 16×16-pixel regions, enabling content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading stores and reuses shading results across pixels, views, and frames. Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass, reducing repeated geometry work for VR, shadows, and other applications.

- **GPU variants:** TU104 incorporates Turing’s RT Cores, Tensor Cores, and shader architecture and is used in products including the GeForce RTX 2080, Tesla T4, and Quadro RTX 5000. Tesla T4 targets inference applications. TU106 powers the GeForce RTX 2070 and includes 2,304 CUDA Cores, 288 Tensor Cores, and 36 RT Cores, but lacks NVLink and SLI support.

The passage also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-weighted metric combining tensor, floating-point, ray-tracing, and integer operations to characterize hybrid-rendering performance.

Carleton University in Ottawa is establishing a research and teaching chair in the “conjuring arts” to investigate perception, deception and the history of magic. Named after magic enthusiast Allan Slaight, the position is funded by a $2 million Slaight Family Foundation grant matched by Carleton. Responsibilities include developing programs for undergraduate and graduate students and connecting global magic resources through a digital archive. About 80 people have applied.

The passage also describes a University of London experiment involving 120 participants that examined explanations for a card trick. Results suggested that constructing an initial explanation can make people less able to abandon their assumptions and find another solution.

Adam Henrique and Travis Zajac described the Kings as a deep, physical team with puck-moving defensemen and strong goaltending. They said their own team began nervously and tentatively, giving away pucks and failing to execute its forecheck, but improved as the game progressed. Apple’s fiscal first quarter ended December 25, 2021, generated net sales of $123.9 billion, up 11% year over year, primarily driven by iPhone, Services and Mac. Net income increased to $34.6 billion from $28.8 billion, while diluted earnings per share rose to $2.10 from $1.68.

- **Products and services:** iPhone sales increased 9% to $71.6 billion; Mac increased 25% to $10.9 billion; Services increased 24% to $19.5 billion; and Wearables, Home and Accessories increased 13% to $14.7 billion. iPad sales declined 14% to $7.2 billion.
- **Geographic performance:** Sales increased 11% in the Americas, 9% in Europe, 21% in Greater China and 19% in the Rest of Asia Pacific. Japan sales declined 14%.
- **Profitability:** Gross margin increased to 43.8% from 39.8%. Operating income reached $41.5 billion, compared with $33.5 billion a year earlier. Operating expenses increased to $12.8 billion from $10.8 billion.
- **Financial position:** Apple held $202.6 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities. Total assets were $381.2 billion, total liabilities were $309.3 billion and shareholders’ equity was $71.9 billion. Outstanding term debt totaled $117.8 billion, with another $5.0 billion in commercial paper.
- **Cash flow and shareholder returns:** Operating activities generated $47.0 billion. Apple repurchased $20.4 billion of common stock and paid $3.7 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents. Remaining share-repurchase authorization was approximately $40.5 billion.
- **Operations and risks:** COVID-19 continued to affect staffing, retail operations and suppliers, with supply shortages affecting sales worldwide. Manufacturing purchase obligations totaled $47.6 billion, primarily payable within 12 months.

Management concluded disclosure controls were effective and reported no material changes to internal financial-reporting controls or risk factors.

The Sixth Circuit affirmed Dr. Howard W. Ellzey’s convictions for conspiracy and eleven counts of illegally distributing controlled substances. He received concurrent three-year prison terms, except for one count carrying three years’ probation, and $18,000 in fines.

Ellzey routinely prescribed amphetamines during brief visits with little examination. Separate records at his two offices allowed patients to obtain two prescriptions in one day. A DEA survey found he wrote 29,000 of 39,000 schedule II prescriptions filled at six Memphis-area drugstores.

The court found substantial evidence supporting the convictions and upheld admission of the prescriptions as evidence of intent and wilfulness. It rejected the argument that the indictment improperly charged “distributing” rather than dispensing, finding his prescribing activities outside accepted medical practice. The court also rejected challenges to testimony, jury instructions, and juror questioning.

Former U.S. Sen. Mark Begich’s entry into Alaska’s governor’s race has raised concerns among some Democrats and independents that he and independent Gov. Bill Walker could split the vote, helping Republicans win. Begich says he believes he can win, and state Democratic leaders support his candidacy.

A.J. Brown addressed frustration with limited production, saying he wants the ball to help Philadelphia’s struggling offense and welcomes pressure in decisive moments. Panic attacks are bursts of intense fear that typically last fewer than 30 minutes, often peaking around 10 minutes. Unlike persistent anxiety, attacks associated with panic disorder can occur without an apparent trigger. Panic disorder affects two to three percent of Americans.

Symptoms include a pounding heart, sweating, trembling, breathing difficulties, chest discomfort, nausea, dizziness, numbness, feelings of unreality, and fear of dying or losing control. Professionals recommend learning these signs and getting a physical exam to rule out other problems.

Alongside professional guidance, suggested coping strategies include:
- Keeping written reminders that panic attacks are not life-threatening and using realistic rebuttals to catastrophic thoughts.
- Visualizing sensations as waves that rise and subside.
- Using smartphone games, relaxing music, or guided relaxation as distractions.
- Practicing slow, deep breathing daily so it is easier to use during an attack.

A laboratory study found that bumblebee queens exposed to thiamethoxam, a neonicotinoid pesticide, were 26 percent less likely to lay eggs than unexposed queens. Researchers warned that reduced reproduction could cause exposed wild populations to decline and eventually die out, though the pesticide’s impact relative to other threats remains uncertain. Neonicotinoids applied to crop seeds can reach pollen consumed by bees. The findings may strengthen calls for pesticide restrictions as the European Union considers making its temporary moratorium permanent. Pesticide companies and some farmers oppose restrictions, citing lower canola yields and increased use of other pesticides.

The study used the 2019 National Survey of Early Care and Education to examine how families search for child care and early education (CCEE). Its sample included 1,190 households that had searched within the previous 24 months for a child under age six, not yet in kindergarten, and considered more than one provider.

Latent class analysis identified five search types, named for their two leading information sources:
- Child Care Resource & Referral agencies (CCR&Rs) or friends/family.
- Internet searches or social media.
- Known providers or friends/family.
- Social media or friends/family.
- Friends/family or internet searches.

The survey recorded only the first two sources mentioned: 51% of families reported one source and 49% reported two. Friends and family with children were the most commonly used source, followed by internet searches.

Regression analyses found significant differences related to:
- **Information about type of care:** Compared with the friends/family–internet group, the CCR&R–friends/family group was more likely to seek this information, while the internet–social media group was less likely. No relationships were found for six other categories of information.
- **Children’s care-related conditions:** The adjusted proportion of children with conditions affecting care provision was 19% in both the CCR&R–friends/family and known-provider–friends/family groups, compared with 5–10% in other groups.
- **Region:** The known-provider–friends/family group was more likely than other groups to include Western households. The friends/family–internet group was more likely to include Northeastern households than three other groups.

Overall, the study found more similarities than differences in family and child characteristics across search types. The exploratory, correlational analyses could describe associations but not explain why search types varied.

Limitations include recording only two information sources and excluding households without a recent search involving multiple providers. The analytic sample had higher incomes and was more likely to include English-only households and two-parent households with both parents working, limiting how well findings reflect other families’ experiences.

The lecture examines web security vulnerabilities caused by untrusted input, complex parsing rules, and interactions among software components.

- **Shellshock:** Malicious HTTP headers can become environment variables that exploit Bash parsing to execute attacker-controlled commands. The demonstration server also contained a separate command-execution vulnerability.
- **Cross-site scripting (XSS):** Inserting untrusted content directly into HTML can execute attacker-supplied code. Reflected attacks use content supplied through requests, while persistent attacks store malicious content, such as website comments.
- **XSS defenses:** Browser filters, HTTP-only cookies, separate domains for untrusted content, content sanitization, restricted markup languages, Content Security Policy, and disabling content sniffing offer protections with limitations. Complex browser behavior and tolerance of malformed content make reliable sanitization difficult.
- **SQL injection and path traversal:** Untrusted values incorporated into database queries or file paths can alter commands or access unintended files. Framework-provided sanitization and higher-level interfaces help reduce these risks.
- **Authentication:** Cookies commonly contain session identifiers, making theft and manipulation sensitive security issues. Alternatives include authenticating individual requests with message authentication codes, storing authentication information in DOM storage, and using client certificates. These approaches introduce concerns involving key protection, replay, revocation, implementation, or usability.
- **Parsing inconsistencies:** Different interpretations of URLs can undermine origin checks. GIFAR files combined valid images with Java archives, allowing executable content to pass image validation and, with XSS, run under a victim site’s authority.
- **Browsing-history attacks:** Link styling and timing differences involving cached resources, DNS resolution, and rendering can reveal previously visited sites. Hiding visited-link colors from JavaScript addresses one technique but does not eliminate the others.

The lecture emphasizes that individual defenses are often incomplete and that seemingly helpful browser features can expose security-sensitive information.

The lecture examines Hadamard-transform realizations of Reed–Muller codes and introduces the sum-product algorithm for decoding codes on graphs.

Over the binary field, the Hadamard transform uses a universal Reed–Muller generator matrix constructed through tensor products. These matrices are self-inverse. Reed–Muller codes are generated by selecting rows of sufficient weight, equivalently allowing selected transform inputs to vary while fixing others to zero.

Recursive graphical realizations use binary variables and simple equality and zero-sum constraints. Reducing the transform graph for the (8, 4, 4) code produces a realization with 12 simple constraints, but with cycles. Agglomerating constraints and combining variables yields a cycle-free trellis realization with higher state and branch complexity. This illustrates the trade-off between simple cyclic representations and more complex cycle-free representations.

The sum-product algorithm computes a posteriori probability (APP) vectors for symbol and internal variables. On cycle-free graphs, it provides exact APP decoding in finite time; on trellises, it becomes the BCJR algorithm. On graphs with cycles, it is iterative and approximate, with convergence and stopping questions. Large cycles generally support better performance than short cycles.

Bitwise maximum-APP decisions minimize bit-error probability, whereas maximum-likelihood sequence decoding minimizes whole-sequence error probability. Independent bitwise decisions need not form a valid codeword. APP outputs are especially useful as soft information exchanged between component decoders in larger systems, including turbo codes.

For equiprobable codewords transmitted over a memoryless channel, APP computation becomes a sum of products of symbol likelihoods. The contribution from a symbol’s own observation is called intrinsic information; contributions from other observations are extrinsic information. Efficient computation exploits cycle-free structure: cutting an edge separates past and future portions, whose probability contributions can be combined for each fixed state value.

Only problem 8.1 remains due Wednesday; problem 8.2 requires additional background, and 8.3 is deferred because BCJR decoding was not reached.

This retrospective multicentre study investigated whether deep learning applied to structural brain MRI could distinguish multiple sclerosis (MS)-specific damage from healthy brain ageing. The medRxiv preprint, posted January 3, 2024, had not been certified by peer review.

Researchers used data from 4,392 patients across 15 European centres to model disease duration (DD) and MS-specific chronological age. An external longitudinal cohort included 252 patients with early disease, 749 imaging sessions, and an average follow-up of 4.5 years. The brain-predicted DD gap—the difference between predicted and actual disease duration—was compared with the conventional brain-age gap (BAG) and an MS-specific age gap.

Patients’ brains appeared approximately eight years older than their chronological age on average. The DD model achieved a mean absolute error of 5.63 years and explained 34% of disease-duration variance. DD gap and BAG were weakly correlated, suggesting largely independent information. Lesion filling affected DD predictions but did not significantly affect conventional brain-age predictions.

Both DD gap and BAG were associated with physical disability measured using the Expanded Disability Status Scale. Adding DD gap to BAG significantly improved explanations of disability severity and longitudinal worsening. Annual changes in disability correlated with changes in BAG and DD gap. Although the MS-specific age model predicted age accurately, its gap measure did not significantly improve disability models beyond BAG.

The authors concluded that DD gap could complement brain-age measures as a biomarker of MS-specific damage, severity, and progression. Limitations included uncertainty in clinical disease-onset dates, potential treatment confounding, disease-duration-related prediction bias, and the need for broader clinical validation before use in patient stratification.

The paper uses non-Markovian Situation Calculus to formalize a taxonomy of obligations, motivated by domains such as smart contracts, where contractual compliance requires explicit representations of obligations.

Situation Calculus specifies dynamic systems through actions, situations, and fluents whose values change through action execution. Reiter’s successor state axioms address the frame problem by describing both changes and persistence. Markovian theories determine action preconditions and effects from the current situation, whereas non-Markovian theories allow dependence on past situations.

The sequential and temporal framework includes actions, situations, time, and objects. Situations represent finite action histories. Basic action theories combine action precondition axioms, successor state axioms, unique names axioms, initial-state descriptions, and foundational axioms. Non-Markovian theories extend these using bounded formulas that can reference earlier situations. A door-opening example illustrates actions, preconditions, and changing properties, including locking, movement, credential-based button pressing, and manager notification.

Obligations are represented through a fluent, O(s′, s), expressing that situation s′ is deontically accessible from s. An agent is obliged to bring about a condition when that condition holds in every deontically accessible situation. The paper builds on an existing framework combining obligations with time and accounting for actions that change an agent’s obligations. Later sections address obligation types, their properties, and interactions between violations and compensation.

The discovery of Richard III’s remains beneath a Leicester car park changed the lives of several people connected to the project.

Dominic Smee, whose scoliosis closely resembled Richard’s, trained in combat and horse riding for a documentary exploring the king’s physical capabilities. The experience helped him overcome insecurity about his condition and gain confidence in public speaking.

Michael Ibsen, a descendant of Richard’s sister Anne, supplied DNA that helped confirm the remains’ identity. He also made Richard’s coffin and attracted considerable media and public attention.

Car park attendant Mike Mistry witnessed the excavation and welcomed visitors from around the world. He had painted the “R,” meaning “reserved,” on the parking space above the grave. After being made redundant in 2016, he missed interacting with visitors.

Musician Ian Churchward was inspired by a documentary about the discovery to write songs about Richard III. His folk-rock band, The Legendary Ten Seconds, produced five Richard-themed albums, with a sixth underway, and received invitations to perform at festivals, battlefields and a US Richard III Society event.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture to accelerate AI, deep learning, and high-performance computing workloads through increased compute capability, memory bandwidth, workload partitioning, and CUDA enhancements.

- **Memory and cache:** A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1555 GB/sec bandwidth, over 1.7 times that of Tesla V100. Its 40 MB L2 cache is 6.7 times larger and provides 2.3 times the L2 bandwidth. SECDED error correction protects HBM2, caches, and register files. Compute Data Compression offers up to fourfold improvements in DRAM and L2 read bandwidth and up to twice the effective L2 capacity.

- **Tensor Core efficiency:** A100 has 108 streaming multiprocessors, compared with V100’s 80. Its third-generation Tensor Cores support peak mixed-precision performance 16 times higher than standard FP32 FMA operations. Broader thread-level data sharing and larger matrix instructions reduce instruction counts and register accesses. Asynchronous global-to-shared memory copies avoid intermediate register storage, while asynchronous barriers enable overlapping transfers and computation. Maximum shared-memory allocation increases to 164 KB per multiprocessor.

- **Multi-Instance GPU:** MIG partitions an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, isolated memory paths, predictable bandwidth, and fault isolation. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, which support independent context switching and Multi Process Server functionality. MIG supports multi-tenant services, virtual machines, and concurrent applications. Migration between equivalently sized instances can consolidate workloads or permit GPU servicing. MIG is restricted to compute mode.

- **Interconnects and resilience:** Twelve third-generation NVLink connections provide 600 GB/sec total bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 provides 31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16 connections, and SR-IOV supports sharing a PCIe-connected GPU among processes or virtual machines. Improved error attribution, isolation, containment, and NVLink recovery mechanisms help prevent faults from disrupting unrelated workloads.

- **Additional hardware:** A100 includes a five-core JPEG decoder, five NVDEC video-decoding units, and an optical-flow accelerator supporting optical flow and stereo disparity. FP16 and FP32 atomic-operation throughput improves by 11 times and 2.7 times, respectively, over V100. A100 does not include display connectors, RT Cores, or an NVENC encoder.

- **CUDA improvements:** CUDA 11 supports Ampere’s Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, asynchronous copies and barriers, and cache-residency controls. CUDA Graph optimizations reduce launch overhead and execution latency for repeated workflows. Programmers can prioritize persistent data in L2, although L2 cache set-aside functionality is disabled in MIG mode. Cooperative Groups adds asynchronous-copy collectives and hardware-accelerated reductions.

- **DGX A100:** The system combines eight A100 GPUs through six NVSwitches, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 isolated MIG instances. InfiniBand networking supports larger deployments. Its software stack includes CUDA, container tools, and GPU-optimized applications distributed through NGC.

- **Structured sparsity:** Pruning removes low-contribution neural-network connections to reduce computation and memory traffic. A100’s fine-grained structured sparsity balances workloads while preserving parallel execution. The passage reports virtually no accuracy loss across evaluated popular networks using NVIDIA’s sparsification methods.

Beijing ordered 15 online real estate portals to remove misleading information, false advertising, feng shui content and financing advice to help cool soaring housing prices. The restrictions follow higher minimum down payments for second homes and the suspension of individual mortgages exceeding 25 years. Third-property purchases were already banned.

Researchers led by the Okinawa Institute of Science and Technology combined fossil evidence with 17 horizontal gene transfers to estimate that the common ancestor of living fungi existed roughly 1.4–0.9 billion years ago, well before land plants emerged around 470 million years ago. These gene transfers provided relative timing constraints, helping address gaps in fungi’s sparse fossil record.

The findings suggest fungi diversified hundreds of millions of years before plants and may have partnered with algae in early terrestrial communities. By breaking down rock and recycling nutrients, ancient fungi could have helped create primitive soils and prepare Earth’s surface for plant colonization.

The passage argues that U.S. military superiority helped avert war during the 1962 Cuban missile crisis, but subsequent policymakers underestimated Soviet military ambitions. It claims the Soviet Union overtook the United States in most strategic military categories and criticizes the Carter administration’s responses to Soviet actions in Cuba and Afghanistan as inconsistent and ineffective. It also attributes declining allied confidence and American credibility to weakened defenses and unclear policies.

The passage advocates restoring military strength through prudent investment in conventional forces, troop deployments, and strategic deterrence. It calls for firm opposition to terrorism, closer consultation with allies, stronger alliances, and an unequivocal commitment to American principles and freedom, presenting these measures as essential to preserving peace.

MusConv is software for transferring playlists between music streaming platforms, including Spotify and Amazon Music. Its Basic, Professional and Ultimate subscriptions offer unlimited songs and playlists per session and CSV export. Higher tiers add batch importing, Apple Music and priority support, lifetime updates, and duplicate-track deletion.

China’s top official in Hong Kong warned against activities threatening national sovereignty, challenging central authority or undermining mainland stability amid an emerging independence movement. The ousting of two pro-independence lawmakers and detention of five booksellers have heightened concerns over Beijing’s controls and erosion of Hong Kong’s autonomy. Leader Leung Chun-ying will not seek another term; former security chief Regina Ip’s candidacy has raised opponents’ fears of further tightening.

United Airlines emphasized uncrowded lounges and seatback entertainment as part of its premium strategy, contrasting with Delta’s lounge crowding and American’s preference for passengers’ personal devices. United said screens are installed on more than 146,000 seats across 765 aircraft.

Delta has raised lounge fees, restricted some access, and introduced higher-end lounges to address crowding. American says over 90% of customers bring devices and prioritizes connectivity and streaming entertainment.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and accommodate buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

- **Duty-cycle control:** Compatible devices support a 100% maximum duty cycle with DCL connected to VLDO or 75% with DCL floating. Only TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5004-SP support the 50% limit with DCL connected to AVSS; OUTB/SRB operate only in this configuration. TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%. A 50%-duty-cycle external synchronization clock provides the most precise limiting.
- **Current sensing and protection:** CS_ILIM senses transformer primary-side current for PWM control and overcurrent protection. Outputs turn on with the clock and turn off when the sensed signal reaches COMP/2; the comparator signal includes a 150-mV offset. A nominal 1.05-V current-limit threshold initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting. Persistent overcurrent charges the HICC capacitor until switching stops, followed by a timed restart through soft-start. The capacitor controls both delay and restart timing; at least 3.3 nF is recommended.
- **Fault and thermal shutdown:** FAULT provides externally implemented protection. A qualifying signal above approximately 0.6 V stops switching. After FAULT falls below approximately 0.5 V, restart follows a delay of about 15 switching cycles plus internal logic delay. Thermal shutdown occurs above a typical 175°C junction temperature, with power-up restarting below 160°C.
- **Compensation:** Resistor-programmed slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation associated with peak-current-mode operation above 50% duty cycle. The recommended compensation equals the inductor’s falling current slope. Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported; Type 2A adds high-frequency noise attenuation.
- **Design example:** A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull converter uses GaN devices, 500-kHz switching, a 5-V output, approximately 25-ns dead time, and approximately 7.5-ms soft-start. Selected components include a transformer turns ratio of 2.5, 40-µH primary inductance, a 0.47-µH output inductor, and approximately 2.3-mF output capacitance. Overcurrent limiting targets roughly 35 A. Component selection accounts for transient voltage stress, radiation-induced output transients, and testing-based optimization.
- **Supply and layout:** Controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes short switching loops, separation of sensitive signals from switching nodes, single-point connection of analog and power grounds, and nearby bypass, filtering, and compensation components.

Application guidance is not part of TI’s component specifications; customers are responsible for suitability assessment, design validation, and testing. The passage also provides documentation references, revision history, ESD precautions, packaging information, and warranty disclaimers.

Valid writes require at least 32 SCLK cycles per transfer frame. Read protocols include single-SDO SPI, dual-SDO SPI, and source-synchronous protocols.

The device defaults to SPI-00-S after power-up or asynchronous reset. Selecting another SPI protocol requires programming SDI_MODE[1:0] using SPI-00-S for the initial write and setting SDO_MODE[1:0] to 00b. RVS remains low during SPI transfers.

Short frames allow reading selected most-significant bits from the 32-bit output word. Long frames with SDO_CNTL_REG[7:0] = 00h enable daisy-chain operation.

Setting SDO1_CONFIG[1:0] to 11b enables dual-SDO mode, repurposing ALARM/SDO-1/GPO as SDO-1 and launching two data bits per SCLK launch edge.

Blockchain adoption requires interdisciplinary coordination and technical, social, methodological, and personal competencies. Enterprise knowledge gaps motivate this study of blockchain education at US universities with AACSB-accredited business schools.

In March 2024, researchers reviewed university websites and catalogs, identifying 361 blockchain-related courses at 151 of 533 universities, approximately 28%. Courses were classified by topic, scientific field, and connections with emerging technologies, with independent reviews reconciled through author discussion.

Key findings include:
- Undergraduate courses accounted for 72% of offerings, graduate courses 23%, and courses available at both levels 5%.
- Computer Science and Information Systems departments offered the most courses, while Business was the largest broader scientific field.
- Fundamentals and Overview dominated course content with 140 courses, followed by Digital Assets and Cryptocurrencies with 71 and Technical Development with 66.
- Public universities offering blockchain courses outnumbered private universities, but a greater proportion of private universities offered them.
- Larger undergraduate populations generally corresponded with greater likelihood of blockchain course availability.
- Courses also addressed connections with emerging technologies, including artificial intelligence, machine learning, and the Internet of Things.

The study emphasizes holistic competency development and recommends further research comparing curricula with industry and job-level competency needs, alongside replication in five years to assess changes in offerings.

The book aims to make distributed system design more systematic by identifying common patterns and practices. It begins with single-node patterns because groups of colocated containers form foundational elements of distributed systems.

Splitting applications into multiple containers provides resource isolation, clear team ownership, and separation of concerns. Resource boundaries help prioritize user-facing services over background tasks. Modular containers enable reuse across environments and allow teams to own focused components. They also simplify testing, updates, and deployment, reducing dependencies and supporting more reliable rollouts and rollbacks.

These single-node patterns assume tightly coupled containers that can be reliably scheduled together on one machine and optionally share filesystems, network namespaces, and shared memory. Kubernetes calls this grouping a pod, though the concept applies more broadly.

The passage describes a surgical robotic wrist designed to improve instrument mobility and measure externally applied forces. Conventional wrists with two roll joints separated by one pitch joint can require rapid joint movement near a straight configuration and offer limited directional force sensing.

The proposed wrist places two transverse rotational axes between proximal and distal roll joints. Its intermediate articulation may use a universal joint, paired revolute joints, or a spherical joint. Torque sensors measure torque about the two transverse axes; additional sensors may measure torque about the roll axes. A processor combines sensor outputs and may use motor inputs to distinguish externally applied torque from torque caused by driven motion. Measurements can support haptic feedback through the surgeon’s controls.

The wrist may be installed at the end of a robot arm to support a surgical instrument, or at the distal end of an instrument to support an end effector. The arrangement permits movement through a hemispherical space while avoiding the high-speed joint movement associated with conventional wrist configurations. Aligning the terminal roll axis with the instrument shaft allows the instrument to rotate without lateral shaft movement.

The passage also describes robot arms using alternating roll and pitch joints, optional lateral joint offsets, and alternative joint sequences. These configurations seek to provide mobility while limiting size, weight, and workspace requirements, helping multiple arms operate near one another.

Torque sensing may use resistance-based, piezoelectric, or magnetostrictive gauges, with wired or wireless communication. Joint drives may be local or remotely coupled through cables or linkages, and control may be manual or computer-directed. During surgery, coordinated wrist rotation and arm translation can move the end effector about a point at the patient’s incision to avoid enlarging it.

The disclosure describes noninvasive physiological monitoring devices and methods that combine raw or minimally processed optical sensor data from multiple patient measurement sites to generate a single measurement of a physiological parameter. Unlike systems that process each site independently, these monitors combine signals before calculating measurements.

Sensors emit light at multiple wavelengths and detect light attenuated by tissue. Measurement sites may include the nose, earlobe, fingers, hands, feet, or other locations, including sites with different tissue types. Signal processors combine features such as amplitude, phase, wavelength ratios, and tissue or site information to estimate parameters including oxygen saturation, pulse rate, perfusion index, pleth variability index, hemoglobin-related measurements, and glucose. Processors may also calculate individual-site measurements and compare or average them with the combined measurement.

The disclosure also describes sensors with multiple photodetectors arranged in three-dimensional configurations conforming to the measurement site's anatomy. These detectors may be distributed throughout a sensor’s contact area in a finger clip or adhesive sensor. Their locations provide different light paths through tissue and may supply topological information to help determine whether the sensor is positioned correctly.

Combining multi-site data and spatially distributed detectors may improve measurement robustness, support cross-checking, reduce sensor-specific errors or noise, and provide information unavailable from a single measurement site. The described configurations can be used separately or together, and not every embodiment necessarily achieves every stated advantage.

The “Combo” defense combines aggressive outside pass denial with two inside zone defenders to counter spread offenses relying on dribble penetration.
