The study reports water-permeable structural defects where aligned graphene flakes merge on single-crystal Cu(111)/sapphire, challenging the expectation that single-orientation graphene forms a continuous, impermeable film.

Graphene was grown by ambient-pressure chemical vapor deposition and examined using electron microscopy, atomic-force microscopy, Raman spectroscopy, and scanning tunneling microscopy. Some merging regions appeared seamless, while others showed distinct merging lines. Atomic-resolution measurements confirmed that these lines can occur between flakes with the same crystallographic orientation.

Immersion in 90°C water for two hours revealed water-permeable regions through oxidation of the underlying copper into Cu₂O. Among 122 merging regions examined across 145 flakes, 55—approximately 45%—showed defective merging, while 67—approximately 55%—remained unoxidized and were considered likely seamless stitches.

Scanning tunneling microscopy identified some merging lines as overlapping junctions, where one graphene edge lies atop another rather than forming a continuous lattice. Such junctions occurred between both aligned and misaligned flakes. Height measurements and experiments that tore and folded the upper graphene layer supported this interpretation. The researchers propose that copper surface steps contribute to overlap formation.

The study classifies merging behavior as seamless stitching, defective stitching, or overlapping junctions. Its findings indicate that aligned growth does not guarantee defect-free graphene and suggest potential applications for permeable merging structures in nanofiltration, water desalination, and molecular sieving.

The 1-4 “Slice” zone offense combines a high alignment, inside post attacks, outside shooters, and quick ball reversals to keep zone defenses moving. Entry passes can go to either post or wing, triggering a weakside post’s cut to the basket. Cutters adjust their routes to defenders’ positioning and post up if they do not receive the ball.

Scoring options include high/low feeds, baseline feeds, cross-court skip passes, outside shots, and drives. Weakside players use extra passes or screens to create open shots. When no good shot or post feed is available, skip passes and give-and-go actions reverse the ball and maintain continuity. Against overplayed entry passes, pump fakes trigger back cuts, with direct feeds, lob passes, or passes through another player.

Mayor Bill de Blasio urged state lawmakers to extend the School Zone Speed Camera program until 2022, add cameras at 150 school zones and broaden coverage to nearby streets. He also announced a redesign of Ninth Street in Park Slope, where two children were killed in March. Planned changes include improved pedestrian access, protected bike lanes and revised loading regulations, with installation scheduled for summer following community input.

AutoPrune is a training-free framework that adapts visual token pruning to individual samples and tasks while meeting a specified token or FLOPs budget. It addresses limitations of fixed pruning schedules, which cannot accommodate changes in token importance across images, queries, and decoder layers.

Inspired by neuroscience and observations of cross-modal attention, AutoPrune estimates input complexity using mutual information between early-layer visual and textual tokens. Higher mutual information triggers aggressive early pruning, while lower mutual information leads to more conservative, later pruning. These policies follow logistic retention curves rescaled to satisfy the computational budget.

The framework integrates with models including LLaVA-1.5, LLaVA-NeXT, and the autonomous-driving model Senna. Experiments across vision–language and autonomous-driving tasks report improvements over existing training-free methods. On LLaVA-1.5-7B, AutoPrune removes 89% of visual tokens and reduces inference FLOPs by 76.8% while retaining 96.7% of original average accuracy, a reported 9.1% improvement over PDrop.

The method formulates pruning as joint optimization of token allocation, selection, and revival under a global computational constraint.

Russia agreed to proposed Syria peace talks with the US and UN in Geneva on April 24, pending Washington’s confirmation. The meeting would be the first such contact since Donald Trump became president. Regional tensions escalated after US missile strikes on a Syrian air base in response to a chemical attack attributed to Assad’s regime. Russia and Iran threatened military retaliation against further US attacks.

British newspaper reports, unverified by Reuters, highlighted concerns over Tesco’s Booker acquisition, Reckitt Benckiser’s business review, Arcadia’s nearly £1 billion pension deficit, and warnings against treating deferred prosecution agreements as routine. Other stories covered Twitter’s pay-TV ambitions, Cortexica’s £4 million fundraising, Babcock’s prospective £340 million Navy support deal, Co-op’s expected bank-stake write-down, and Michael Fallon’s call to link trade and security in EU negotiations.

New Zealand authorities closed Farewell Spit’s beach while removing more than 300 whale carcasses, citing health risks and fears of explosions from decomposition gases. Workers punctured the bodies before transporting them to an inaccessible location. An estimated 666 pilot whales stranded in two pods; about three-quarters of the first pod died, while survivors and the second pod were refloated. No fresh strandings were found Tuesday, but wildlife officers remained on alert.

This Agreement governs software use and remains enforceable if provisions are invalidated. California and controlling federal law apply, with exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County courts. Exports must comply with applicable regulations. Waivers and amendments require authorized signatures from both parties. Licensors may enforce terms as third-party beneficiaries.

In Arthur C. C. Hill v. Jacob Levine, the plaintiff sought specific performance of a written agreement to purchase Boston real estate. The defendant refused to accept title because of a deed provision requiring subdivided lots to have at least fifty feet of frontage. The Superior Court dismissed the suit, finding reasonable doubt about when that restriction expired.

On appeal, the court held that the deed’s twenty-year limitation applied to the frontage restriction, which therefore expired in 1916. It also found that the provision was a personal agreement between grantors and grantee, not a restriction benefiting other lots or creating an equitable easement enforceable by their owners.

The possibility of future litigation did not justify denying specific performance because the deed’s construction presented no reasonable doubt. The court reversed the dismissal and ordered specific performance, permitting the plaintiff to seek an assessment of damages in the Superior Court.

Siqi Zheng’s lecture examines how public policy can make sustainable real estate financially viable while balancing environmental, social, and profit goals. It reviews three market failures: information gaps, addressed through building certifications; split incentives between landlords and tenants, addressed through green leases; and externalities, addressed through incentives and enforcement.

Green buildings generate societal benefits, such as reduced carbon emissions, that developers cannot fully capture financially, resulting in undersupply. Subsidies, tax incentives, and density bonuses—“carrots”—can improve project returns. Carbon taxes, emissions penalties, disclosure requirements, and energy codes—“sticks”—make environmentally harmful practices more costly. Both approaches can change a project’s financial feasibility, but identifying appropriate policy levels is difficult and behavioral responses can produce unintended consequences.

Examples include European renovation funding, Massachusetts energy-efficiency incentives, and density bonuses in Arlington, Virginia. Heat-pump adoption illustrates that subsidies alone may not overcome installation costs and information barriers. Density bonuses must balance developer incentives against increased energy use, embodied carbon, and infrastructure demands.

Research on Massachusetts energy-code changes examines tensions between sustainability and housing affordability. Higher construction costs passed to households may outweigh utility savings and push some income groups above the 30% housing-cost threshold. The lecture advocates considering incentives alongside mandates, including zoning changes and expedited permitting.

Enforcement examples include mandatory energy disclosures, UK restrictions on leasing inefficient properties, New York City’s Local Law 97, Boston’s BERDO, and proposed Cambridge emissions requirements. Cambridge’s baseline-based approach could disadvantage buildings renovated before the baseline years. MIT’s near-term net-zero plans involve carbon offsets, whose credibility requires scrutiny.

The lecture also explores continued migration and development in climate-risk areas and the unequal capacity to finance adaptation. Miami illustrates a positive cycle of resilience investment, continued development, and tax revenue; Fair Bluff, North Carolina, illustrates declining resources, departures, and reduced capacity to recover.

Federal resilience funding raises concerns about unequal access and moral hazard: expectations of government protection may encourage continued development in risky locations. Managed retreat offers an alternative that could preserve communities through organized relocation, but its political and social trade-offs remain unresolved.

The passage describes electronic devices, including smartphones and tablets, with glass enclosures covering multiple sides or substantially the entire exterior. Transparent front, back, and peripheral surfaces may allow displays and touch- or force-sensitive controls on several or all sides.

Displays may use a folded flexible component or multiple coordinated panels. Different surfaces can present distinct content, such as a primary interface, device controls, or status information. Alternatively, images and interfaces may extend continuously across surfaces, allowing scrolling around the device. Display regions may change according to the device’s operating context.

Some embodiments support use in multiple orientations without a fixed front, back, top, or bottom. The primary interface surface may be selected through sensing, user choice, application requirements, or timing. Symmetrically positioned speakers, microphones, cameras, and other components may support this functionality.

Enclosures may consist of a single glass member or multiple joined members. Described designs include varying wall thicknesses, textured input regions, overlapping tapered joints, and openings for audio or component access. Joining methods include glass frit bonding, adhesives, fusion bonding, ultrasonic welding, and mechanical interlocks. Seam placement, transparent bonding materials, and finishing techniques may reduce interference with display visibility.

Manufacturing and assembly approaches include additive manufacturing, inserting components through openings, and closing openings with glass members, caps, or plugs. Some components may be folded or compressed for insertion and expanded inside. Alternative enclosure shapes include cylinders, elliptic cylinders, and octagonal prisms. Not all embodiments require every surface to be transparent or associated with a display.

Manchester United reportedly have approval for a £50m bid for Fulham’s Ryan Sessegnon, with Fulham seeking a replacement amid interest from United and Tottenham. Jose Mourinho has also reportedly held talks with Marouane Fellaini about extending his contract, which expires at the end of the season.

Maldives President Yameen Abdul Gayoom said he was willing to hold an early presidential election amid unrest following a Supreme Court order to release and retry political prisoners, including former President Mohammed Nasheed. The court also reinstated 12 opposition lawmakers, threatening Yameen’s parliamentary majority. Parliament’s opening was indefinitely postponed. Yameen said authorities were examining how to implement the ruling and dismissed a second police chief since the order. Police dispersed opposition protests demanding compliance. UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres urged the government to respect the ruling and supported all-party talks. Nasheed said he would challenge for the presidency after his conviction was overturned.

Scientists created hybrid rhino embryos using stored sperm from the last northern white rhino male and southern white rhino eggs. Two embryos were frozen, but implantation procedures remain undeveloped. Researchers await permission to collect eggs from the two remaining northern white rhino females, hoping to produce a calf within three years. Other approaches could take longer. Conservationist Terri Roth warned that reliance on reproductive technology could encourage complacency about existing conservation efforts.

Microsoft plans Windows 10 accessibility updates, including reorganized Ease of Access settings, options to enlarge and brighten content, improved Narrator responsiveness and voice-based text styling, and enhanced eye control. Some features are available in Insider previews, with further accessibility additions promised later in the year.

The passage examines how assumptions about free will shape autonomy, authenticity, and moral responsibility in education. It argues that philosophy of education commonly relies on a libertarian conception of freedom requiring alternative possibilities and self-initiation of actions. These assumptions create difficulties under both determinism, which excludes alternative action, and indeterminism, which introduces randomness without ensuring personal control.

The author presents Harry Frankfurt’s thought experiment and hierarchical theory of the will as an alternative. Frankfurt’s scenario suggests that a person can be morally responsible despite being unable to act otherwise, provided the circumstances blocking alternatives do not cause the actual action. His hierarchical theory locates responsibility in the relationship between first-degree desires to act and second-degree aspirations concerning which desires should govern one’s will.

On this account, reflexive self-assessment and identification with effective desires provide the volitional control relevant to responsibility. The author argues that such control can exist regardless of determinism or indeterminism, without requiring control over the origins of desires or access to alternatives. Rational reasons are not the sole basis for responsibility; identification with emotional or irrational motives can also reveal a person’s values and preferences.

The proposed educational implication is to emphasize young people’s understanding and evaluation of their will, rather than whether they could have acted differently. Educators should help them recognize responsibility for actions, omissions, and consequences through their attitudes toward motivating desires and unavoidable circumstances. The passage concludes that this internal account offers a way to address the paradox of moral education, while acknowledging that its adequacy as a replacement for established conceptions of autonomy remains open.

Marine heatwaves are prolonged periods of unusually warm water that can occur in any season, damaging ecosystems, fisheries and aquaculture. Globally, marine heatwave days increased by 54 per cent between 1925 and 2016. Comparing 1925–1954 with 1987–2016, their frequency rose 34 per cent and duration increased 17 per cent, trends explained by rising ocean temperatures.

Recent events have caused lasting kelp forest losses, seagrass declines, fishery disruptions, marine mammal strandings and harmful algal blooms. Human-caused climate change made the 2016 tropical Australian heatwave 53 times more likely and the 2015–2016 Tasman Sea heatwave over 300 times more likely.

Continued warming is expected to increase marine heatwaves, threatening biodiversity and livelihoods. Scientists aim to quantify future changes and develop forecasts to support fisheries, aquaculture and conservation management. Forecasting can help manage risks, but urgent greenhouse gas reductions remain necessary to limit warming.

The Carolina Panthers ended their 2016 season with a 17-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, finishing 6-10. A failed two-point conversion with 17 seconds remaining sealed the defeat. Cam Newton completed 56% of his passes and threw three interceptions, while Graham Gano missed three field goals with a broken bone in his plant foot. Carolina allowed 300 yards of offense. Younger players contributed, including David Mayo with seven tackles and James Bradberry with an interception. The Panthers secured the eighth pick in the next NFL draft, their first top-10 selection since 2012.

An MIT study suggests 3,000 four-person shared taxis could serve 98% of Manhattan ride demand, reducing congestion and pollution. Passengers would face average waits of 2.8 minutes and trip delays of 3.5 minutes. Alternatively, 2,000 ten-passenger vans could suffice. However, many riders and drivers resist shared rides, and switching entirely to them could leave thousands of drivers without work.

LeBron James and Stephen Curry remain the NBA’s defining stars, but no clear successor has emerged. Becoming the league’s next face requires elite performance alongside popularity, charisma, visibility and compelling narratives.

Victor Wembanyama is presented as the leading candidate because of his talent and potential, although his position and international background distinguish him from most previous faces of the league. Anthony Edwards offers a different path as a charismatic, versatile scoring guard in the mold of Michael Jordan and Kobe Bryant.

Luka Doncic’s move to the Lakers strengthens his candidacy through the franchise’s visibility. He led NBA jersey sales in 2025, ahead of Curry and James, and a championship in Los Angeles could further elevate his profile.

Other possibilities include Jalen Williams, Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Cooper Flagg. Zion Williamson and Ball are less conventional candidates whose potential rests on overcoming limited NBA success or injuries while capitalizing on their appeal.

The article also emphasizes rivalries as a route to prominence. Repeated playoff encounters between emerging stars could help establish the next generation’s leading figures, much as rivalries elevated Magic Johnson, Larry Bird, James and Curry.

Amazon.com, Inc. reported that on August 15, 2017, it announced the pricing of a previously announced private placement offering of $16.0 billion in aggregate principal amount of senior unsecured notes. The Form 8-K incorporates the announcement’s press release as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Vice President and Treasurer Kurt H. Zumwalt.

- **Interrupt handling:** The ARM Cortex-A8 interrupt controller supports up to 128 requests with programmable priorities. General-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. The C674x DSP controller combines up to 128 device events into 12 prioritized interrupts, with selectable multiplexed event sources.

- **Timing and board design:** Timing specifications apply at device pins and exclude board-routing delays. TI recommends IBIS models for timing analysis, while DDR interfaces have specific routing rules. For 3.3-V I/O, the timing reference voltage is 1.5 V.

- **DCAN and EDMA:** Two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0 parts A and B, programmable message handling, self-test modes, and interrupts. EDMA transfers data between memories and peripherals through up to 64 channels, with events assignable to any of 512 parameter entries.

- **Debugging:** Advanced Event Triggering provides hardware breakpoints, data watchpoints, counters, and state sequencing. Real-time trace captures execution, timing, and data-access information without affecting system execution. JTAG supports testing and emulation; TRST initialization requirements depend on the controller used.

- **Ethernet:** A three-port gigabit switch connects one internal port and two external PHY ports, supporting hardware flow control and quality of service. External ports support 10/100 Mbps half- or full-duplex operation and 1000 Mbps full-duplex operation through MII, GMII, RMII, or RGMII. PHY interfaces must use 3.3-V signaling. MDIO configures and monitors multiple PHYs over a shared two-wire bus.

- **GPIO:** Four 32-channel modules provide up to 128 configurable 1.8-V/3.3-V pins, depending on device configuration. Features include input/output register control, interrupt generation, and debouncing.

- **External memory:** GPMC interfaces with NOR Flash, NAND Flash, SRAM, Pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic. It supports 8-/16-bit multiplexed buses and up to 512 MB across eight chip selects. The Error Locator Module locates BCH errors at 4-, 8-, or 16-bit levels per 512-byte block.

- **HDMI and video:** The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports digital video, up to eight uncompressed audio channels, DDC, and CEC. TMDS routing requires controlled impedance and careful layout; external ESD protection is required. HDVPSS provides two display-processing pipelines, video conversion up to 1080p60, capture interfaces, digital and analog outputs, and three graphics layers. Analog video outputs support internal-amplifier and external-amplifier modes.

- **I2C and imaging:** Four I2C modules support 10–400 Kbps operation, seven- and ten-bit addressing, multimaster modes, noise filtering, and 32-byte FIFOs. Their pins lack fail-safe buffers. The imaging subsystem captures parallel or CSI2 inputs and provides image correction, compression, scaling, exposure-related data collection, and flash/shutter control.

- **DDR2/DDR3:** Two memory interfaces support 16- or 32-bit data paths, devices from 64 Mb to 4 Gb, independent chip selects, and interleaving. DDR3 clock frequency is limited to 533 MHz. Supported board designs must follow specified routing rules covering placement, stackup, impedance, termination, reference planes, keepout regions, and bypass capacitors. DDR2 clock/address routing uses balanced-T topology; data routing is point-to-point. DDR3 guidance emphasizes short return-current paths and careful planning of high-speed bypass capacitors.

The United Nations Conference met in San Francisco from April 25 to June 26, 1945, to draft a world security organization’s charter. Delegates from fifty governments unanimously approved the UN Charter, the International Court of Justice Statute, and interim arrangements for a Preparatory Commission on June 25. The Charter was signed the next day by 153 delegates, with space reserved for Poland.

The U.S. Senate consented to ratification on July 28, and President Truman ratified the Charter and Statute on August 8. The Charter entered into force on October 24 after ratification by the five major powers and twenty-four other signatories.

Using the Dumbarton Oaks Proposals and subsequent submissions, four commissions, twelve technical committees, and four general committees organized the Conference’s work. Technical committees drafted the Charter in closed meetings, with recommendations proceeding through commissions to plenary sessions. Principal conference records were published in a 22-volume series, primarily in English and French; final documents appeared in five official languages.

Danica Patrick acknowledged she should have kept walking rather than confronting fans who booed her at Pocono Raceway. She said she declined to sign for a fan restrained by security because she did not want to reward disrespect toward the guard. Her statement that signing autographs was not her job sparked debate among NASCAR drivers. Kevin Harvick called it a driver’s responsibility, while Ryan Blaney said drivers should sign despite it not being part of their job. Dale Earnhardt Jr. said Patrick brought negative attention upon herself and described fan interactions as a source of encouragement.

At the World Economic Forum, President Trump encouraged investment in the United States, citing economic growth, stock market gains, job creation, and declining unemployment. He highlighted corporate tax cuts from 35 percent to 21 percent, worker bonuses, Apple’s announced investment plans, and regulatory reductions as reasons businesses should expand in America.

Trump said “America first” did not mean “America alone,” arguing that American prosperity benefits other countries. He advocated fair, reciprocal trade, enforcement against intellectual property theft and other practices he described as unfair, and mutually beneficial trade agreements, including possible negotiations with countries in the TPP. He also emphasized expanding energy production and reforming government bureaucracy.

On security, Trump discussed military investment and urged allies to contribute more to defense. He outlined efforts to denuclearize the Korean Peninsula, counter Iran’s support for terrorism and nuclear ambitions, defeat ISIS, and prevent Afghanistan from becoming a terrorist haven. He proposed replacing extended-family immigration with merit-based admissions and emphasized workforce development.

During questions from Klaus Schwab, Trump credited tax reform with encouraging corporate investment and employee bonuses. He described his business experience as useful preparation for the presidency, defended deregulation, criticized media coverage of his political career, and characterized himself as a promoter of the United States.

The disclosure describes methods and systems for detecting, processing, and responding to speech commands across multiple networked data modules, such as loudspeakers. Modules detect an activation command, or “Hot Word,” and compute scores based on factors including signal power, recognition confidence, user location, and audio processing. These scores determine which modules provide recorded speech for server interpretation.

In a centralized approach, a group leader collects scores, selects higher-scoring modules, activates their microphones, and sends their audio, optionally combined, to an external server. The leader receives the requested action and distributes it to the group. Playback may be paused or muted during command capture, and modules may provide audible confirmation.

In a decentralized approach, modules broadcast their scores and compare them with other modules’ scores. Higher-ranking modules independently submit audio to the server, then exchange confidence levels for the returned action to determine which modules act.

The system can also combine portions of a spoken command captured by different modules, selecting higher-quality segments as a user moves. Synchronized module clocks enable comparisons of signal-to-noise ratios between segments.

The architecture supports dynamically changing Player, Follower, and Renderer roles. Players retrieve and distribute content, Followers forward content within local systems, and Renderers play it. Group configurations and roles may change during operation, with leader selection considering processing capabilities, codec availability, and network conditions. The disclosure also describes synchronized playback, hardware and software implementations, and optional controls over personal-information collection and use.

A year after Loper Bright overturned Chevron’s framework of deference to agency interpretations of ambiguous statutes, three developments warrant attention:

- **Textualism:** Courts must independently identify a statute’s single best meaning, shifting justifications for agency actions toward text, grammar, dictionaries, and statutory structure rather than broader goals and practical considerations.
- **“Shadow Skidmore”:** The Supreme Court has used longstanding agency interpretations to reinforce its own readings without citing Skidmore’s persuasion-based standard. Lower courts remain divided over its role. Agency consistency may continue as an interpretive tool or fade as judges become more accustomed to resolving technical questions independently.
- **Major questions doctrine:** The presumption against implicit delegations of major economic and political decisions remains intact. However, Justice Brett Kavanaugh has proposed excluding national security and foreign policy, citing presidential powers and congressional practice. That proposed exception could matter in litigation challenging the administration’s tariff authority.

The 2025–26 term may clarify how these approaches shape judicial review of agency action.

No. 10 Alabama leads No. 16 Vanderbilt in the third quarter of their Week 6 SEC matchup. Alabama’s Ty Simpson threw touchdown passes of 14 yards to Ryan Williams and 27 yards to Germie Bernard. Conor Talty made a 30-yard field goal and missed a 47-yard attempt.

Vanderbilt’s Sedrick Alexander scored on a 65-yard run and a four-yard pass from Diego Pavia. Martel Hight intercepted Simpson for his first interception of the season. Alabama’s defense recovered a Pavia fumble and intercepted him through Keon Sabb.

Vanderbilt entered undefeated at 5-0, while Alabama returned to the top 10 after beating Georgia following an opening loss to Florida State. The preview highlighted playoff implications, both quarterbacks’ performances and Vanderbilt’s ability to pressure Simpson as key storylines.

This retrospective single-center study examined predictors of rebleeding in 226 adults admitted to Rennes University Hospital with aneurysmal subarachnoid hemorrhage between January 2020 and December 2022. Rebleeding occurred in 33 patients (15%).

Time elapsed since initial symptoms and higher World Federation of Neurosurgical Societies (WFNS) scores were independently associated with rebleeding. In univariate analysis, each additional hour was associated with a 0.7% increase in rebleeding odds; this association remained significant after adjustment. Other previously identified predictors, including admission systolic blood pressure, aneurysm size and location, and intracerebral or intraventricular hemorrhage, were not independently associated with rebleeding.

Two-thirds of rebleeding events occurred more than 24 hours after symptom onset. Rebleeding occurred before aneurysm securing in 9% of patients treated within 24 hours, compared with 21% treated later. Patients with rebleeding also had longer delays before hospital admission.

Overall Glasgow Outcome Scale results at one and six months did not differ significantly between groups, although a six-month subgroup analysis found more scores of 5 among patients without rebleeding.

Limitations included the retrospective design, limited number of rebleeding events, and uncertainty about whether some episodes attributed to rebleeding reflected other causes of neurological deterioration. The authors conclude that elapsed time from headache onset should inform treatment planning and that their findings support securing aneurysms as early as possible. The passage is from a preprint not certified by peer review.

Scaling in means gradually building a trading position according to a predetermined plan rather than reacting to losses. Its uses differ by trader:

- **Long-term investors** buy as prices decline to lower their average entry price, assuming prices will recover.
- **Day traders** begin with small positions and add when the market moves favorably, limiting initial exposure while potentially increasing profits.
- **Institutional traders** split large orders to reduce market impact and avoid attracting traders who might front-run them.
- **Swing traders** may add at potential reversal levels under mean-reversion strategies or add to winning positions under trend-following strategies.

Scaling in requires discipline and ongoing assessment. Buying during declines can produce losses if prices do not recover. Adding to winning trades creates exposure to sudden reversals. Traders may also fail to build their intended position before prices move away.

The passage distinguishes planned scaling in from double-down and Martingale strategies, which add to losing positions to seek breakeven. Martingale doubles the existing position size with each additional trade.

Scaling out means exiting a position gradually. It can secure partial profits while leaving remaining positions open for further gains and can reduce the market impact of large sales.

The described backtest produced lower compound annual growth and final equity with scaling in. However, the authors preferred it because they considered its capital use more efficient and its risk-adjusted returns better relative to time spent in the market.

Backtests of TLT, an ETF tracking 20-year Treasury bonds, from 2004 through August 2021 identified weak returns during the first seven trading days of each month and stronger returns afterward.

Combining end-of-month long positions with early-month short positions produced a reported annual return of 10.2%, versus 3.8% for buy-and-hold, with maximum drawdowns of 24% and 48%, respectively. A modified short strategy returned an average 0.6% per trade and a 5.5% compound annual growth rate.

Buying at the close of the seventh trading day and selling at month-end reportedly doubled buy-and-hold returns while maintaining market exposure roughly two-thirds of the time. The article notes that the 2021–23 bear market affected this strategy and explains the inverse relationship between TLT prices and interest rates.

Menière’s disease (MD) involves recurrent vertigo, hearing loss and other aural symptoms that impair daily functioning and quality of life. This multicenter study evaluated whether the German 17-item Speech, Spatial and Qualities of Hearing Scale (SSQ17) can assess hearing-related disability in unilateral MD.

The analysis included 97 patients from a prospective registry at two German academic centers. Participants underwent vestibular assessment, pure-tone and speech audiometry, and completed the SSQ17. Mean age was 56.2 years, 56.7% were female, and 51.6% used hearing aids.

Hearing was substantially worse in affected ears: mean pure-tone thresholds were 51.9 dB HL versus 19.3 dB HL in unaffected ears, while monosyllabic speech recognition averaged 33.9% versus 86.6%. The mean SSQ17 total score was 6.0 out of 10, with subscale scores of 5.3 for speech hearing, 5.1 for spatial hearing and 7.2 for hearing qualities. SSQ17 scores did not differ significantly between diagnostic categories.

Internal consistency was excellent, with Cronbach’s alpha of 0.960 overall and 0.904–0.956 across subscales. After excluding two audiometric outliers, worse pure-tone thresholds correlated with lower scores across all subscales and the listening-effort item. Better speech recognition correlated with better speech-hearing, spatial-hearing and listening-effort scores.

The authors concluded that SSQ17 is a viable addition to clinical testing for assessing hearing disability, particularly in challenging listening conditions. However, it does not capture vertigo or the full burden of MD. Fluctuating hearing symptoms and differences in hearing-aid use complicate comparisons with other populations. The study was presented as a preprint not certified by peer review.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examines inflammation-related treatments for depression through a review of animal research and a scoping review of clinical trials. Inflammation is associated with depression and may affect neurotransmitter metabolism, neuroplasticity, and neuronal signalling.

The animal literature review included 31 studies investigating pharmacological and non-pharmacological interventions targeting pathways such as NLRP3, NF-κB, and P2X7R. Drugs, natural extracts, nutritional supplements, acupuncture, exercise, and photobiomodulation showed potential to reduce neuroinflammation and depressive-like behaviours. However, most studies were short-term, with insufficient evidence about sustained effects, safety, individual differences, and translation to human treatment.

The clinical review searched PubMed, screened 1,057 articles, and included 11 articles published between 2008 and 2024, collectively reporting 907 patients. Treatment periods ranged from two to eighteen weeks. Interventions included infliximab, minocycline, ketamine, antidepressants, and adjunctive treatments. Commonly assessed inflammatory markers included CRP, hs-CRP, IL-6, and TNF-α.

Clinical findings varied. Some interventions improved depressive symptoms or inflammatory measures, while responses appeared related to baseline inflammation. Minocycline showed no substantial overall advantage over placebo, although patients with hs-CRP levels of at least 3 mg/L responded more favourably. Higher baseline inflammatory markers were also associated with better infliximab responses. The review identifies unclear definitions of inflammation, frequently undetectable cytokines, uncertain biomarker selection, reliance on depression rating scales, safety concerns, and testing costs as barriers.

The authors recommend validating inflammatory biomarkers, investigating long-term effects and personalised treatment, and improving research transparency. They also propose future AI-assisted monitoring and micro-robot applications. They conclude that current anti-inflammatory drug strategies have limited feasibility and advocate greater emphasis on non-pharmacological approaches, including exercise and positive thinking, alongside lower-cost, broadly applicable research.

Digital laggards struggle to connect goals with strategy, creating organizational misalignment. Entrenched habits, skill gaps, and insufficient leadership focus hinder efforts to align behavior with data-driven ambitions.

Digital leaders emphasize learning, transparent data access, clear metrics, and consistency between leadership beliefs, company values, and employee actions. Data-driven objectives help employees understand their contributions to company goals, while shared data models and access support collaboration across teams. Successful transformation requires changing ingrained mindsets and embedding learning, risk-taking, transparency, and measurement into daily practices.

Organizations commonly follow four patterns:
- **Data novice:** Recognizes the need for data-driven decisions but lacks enabling culture and systems.
- **Insight ready:** Encourages risk-taking but lacks advanced analytical capabilities.
- **Tech enabled:** Has necessary technology and data but discourages experimentation.
- **Data reliant:** Has digital maturity and a learning mindset but may rely on data enough to discourage critical thinking.

Each group can build on existing strengths and address specific weaknesses to develop a stronger data culture.

- **Locking and write protection:** Force erase excludes the secure area. The card remains locked, with Temporary and Group Write Protection retained, until all user-area erasure is complete; it then unlocks and clears those protections. Locked cards reject ACMD6, preventing bus-width changes. Hosts must issue CMD42 using the card’s current bus width. Lock/unlock behavior varies by card type and specification version.

- **Application-specific commands:** CMD55 causes the following command to be interpreted as an application-specific command, where defined. Undefined ACMDs are treated as regular commands, but hosts must not use them as regular commands. Command acceptance depends on the card’s current state. APP_CMD response status generally identifies application-command interpretation, with special handling for ACMD41.

- **Function switching:** CMD6 controls access mode, command-system extensions, driver strength, and power limits. It is mandatory for cards compliant with Version 1.10 and later and operates in Transfer State. Mode 0 queries supported functions and maximum current/power consumption; Mode 1 switches functions. Only one function per group can be active. Invalid selections cancel all requested changes, while busy functions retain their current settings. CMD6 returns an R1 response and a 512-bit status block.

- **Power and speed:** The default power limit is 0.72 W, which may restrict performance. Hosts select limits according to power-supply, heat-release, and connector capabilities and should verify consumption before switching functions. In UHS-II, power-limit support is mandatory, command-system support is optional, and access-mode and driver-strength groups are unused. Optional High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/sec interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires a one-to-one host/card connection.

- **Initialization and addressing:** CMD8 checks supply-voltage compatibility during initialization of Version 2.00-or-later cards and must precede ACMD41 in Idle State. A compatible card echoes the voltage range and check pattern in R7. ACMD41 identifies SDSC versus SDHC/SDXC capacity types. SDSC memory commands use byte addressing and CMD16-defined block lengths; SDHC/SDXC use fixed 512-byte block addressing, prohibit partial and misaligned access, and do not support write-protected groups.

- **Clock control and error protection:** Hosts may reduce or stop the bus clock subject to initialization and transaction-completion requirements, including eight additional clocks after the final transaction. Cards can finish programming without the host clock but need a clock edge to release busy signaling. CRC7 protects commands, most responses, and CID/CSD registers; CRC16 protects data blocks and is calculated separately for each data line in wide-bus mode. Invalid commands or command CRC failures leave card state unchanged and set error-status bits.

- **Timeouts:** SDSC read and write timeouts depend on access/program timing parameters, capped at 100 ms and 250 ms respectively. Hosts should allow at least 100 ms for SDHC/SDXC reads. SDHC write busy periods are limited to 250 ms; specified SDXC cases allow 500 ms. UHS-II permits up to one second of busy time after a Data Burst. Hosts are strongly advised to use write timeouts exceeding 500 ms. Erase timeout parameters in SD Status should be used when available.

- **Commands, responses, and status:** Commands have fixed 48-bit formats and are grouped into functional classes whose support is reported through card registers. UHS-II changes some command behavior and normally uses packet length to terminate transfers. Card Status reports command errors and state; the 512-bit SD Status reports extended capabilities; Task Status reports queued-task status. SD Status includes speed classes, allocation-unit sizes, erase timing, application performance, and command-queue support.

- **Recording performance:** Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class specify performance methods for real-time recording; all three are optional in this specification version. The user area is organized into Allocation Units (AUs), subdivided into Recording Units (RUs). Fragmented-AU performance considers writing free RUs and moving used RUs, whereas Class 10 performance is defined for entirely free AUs. File-system updates introduce timing and buffering requirements.

- **SDXC Speed Class:** SDXC recording requires sequential RU writes to completely free AUs and does not support performance-move calculations. AUs may reach 64 MB; performance for AUs larger than 4 MB is measured over each 4 MB sub-unit. SDXC defines exFAT FAT, bitmap, directory-entry, and Continuous Information update procedures. Speed Class requirements apply to cards formatted according to the specified SD File System rules.

A Seattle Public Utilities (SPU) study found that extreme rainstorms have become more frequent and intense over the past 15 years, while the city’s typical drizzle and short showers remain largely unchanged. Based on updated modeling, a storm delivering 4 inches of rain in 24 hours, previously considered a once-in-a-century event, can now be expected every 25 years.

SPU collected rainfall measurements from 17 locations across Seattle over roughly four decades. The updated data will guide drainage and wastewater projects, including pipe sizing, to reduce flooding and polluted overflows. Much of Seattle’s existing infrastructure was designed for a different climate.

SPU meteorologist James Rufo-Hill acknowledged that recent changes could reflect variability but said scientific evidence suggests long-term changes will continue with climate change. The study aligns with National Weather Service data, and officials say its findings underscore the need for better flood preparation throughout Western Washington.

The 1942 Foreign Relations series comprises six numbered volumes and a previously published China volume. Its Belgium section covers U.S.-Belgian mutual aid and military service agreements and negotiations among the United States, United Kingdom, and Belgium concerning Belgian Congo trade.

In March 1942, the United States sought information on renewing the Anglo-Belgian economic agreement, which had expired in August 1941, and considered participating in discussions. Negotiations had been delayed by a Belgian official’s death, difficulty finding a successor, and pricing disputes. Belgium wanted British supplies, particularly mining machinery, but had not submitted a comprehensive requirements program. Kerberos authenticates users and services across an untrusted network using cryptographic keys and tickets. Designed for MIT’s Athena distributed computing environment, it remains in use at MIT and underlies Microsoft’s Active Directory. The lecture explains its architecture, trust assumptions, and weaknesses in Kerberos 4 addressed by later designs.

A trusted Key Distribution Center (KDC) maintains mappings between principal names and secret keys shared with users or services. Users must also trust their workstations, which handle passwords and tickets. Kerberos establishes identity; individual services determine access rights through authorization mechanisms such as access-control lists. Reusing principal names can inadvertently grant new users permissions associated with previous owners.

Authentication proceeds in stages:
- A client requests an initial ticket, typically for the Ticket Granting Service (TGS). The response is encrypted with a key derived from the user’s password.
- After decrypting that response, the client can discard its password-derived key and use the time-limited TGS ticket to request service tickets.
- A service ticket contains identities, validity information, and a session key, encrypted with the service’s secret key. The client receives a separate copy of the session key and presents the ticket to the service.

This arrangement avoids transmitting the password during ordinary ticket acquisition and limits the usefulness of stolen session credentials to their tickets’ lifetimes. Ticket validity requires loosely synchronized clocks. Authenticators, generated by clients and checked against timestamps and cached requests, help prevent replay attacks.

The lecture identifies several security problems:
- Kerberos 4 treated encryption as if it also guaranteed message integrity. Kerberos 5 explicitly authenticates messages.
- Initial encrypted responses permit offline password guessing. Expensive password derivation and salting increase attack costs; preliminary authentication restricts arbitrary requests but does not eliminate attacks on observed traffic. Password-authenticated key-exchange protocols offer stronger protection.
- Kerberos 4 fixed its encryption scheme to DES, whose 56-bit keys became vulnerable to brute force. Kerberos 5 supports multiple encryption schemes.
- Authenticators must be tied to the commands they accompany to prevent attackers from combining new authenticators with old commands.
- Using the same key in both communication directions enables reflection attacks. Direction-specific keys or explicit direction information prevent this confusion.
- Client IP-address restrictions provide limited protection and are largely optional in Kerberos 5.

The KDC is central to security but does not carry application traffic. An outage prevents new logins and ticket issuance, while existing tickets remain usable. Read-only replicas improve availability. Compromising the KDC enables widespread impersonation, making its software, administration, and physical protection important.

A compromised service’s secret key must be replaced. Otherwise, attackers can decrypt subsequent tickets and traffic or forge tickets impersonating users to that service. Account registration and recovery may require trusted, out-of-band identity verification.

A shared login server cannot safely authenticate a password merely by decrypting an apparent KDC response: an attacker could forge that response using a chosen password. The server must also obtain and verify a ticket for itself using its own secret key.

Password changes require tickets obtained directly through password-based authentication, rather than through the TGS, so stolen ordinary tickets cannot permanently take over an account. The described older password-changing protocol also lets an attacker recover successive passwords from recorded exchanges after learning an old password. The lecture presents Diffie–Hellman key exchange as the mechanism for establishing a new secret that prevents this chain of disclosure.

Mapbox, which supplies mapping data for other companies’ apps, is partnering with Microsoft, ARM and Intel’s Mobileye to expand its self-driving car tools. Its Microsoft partnership will combine road-vision software with Azure cloud processing to improve navigation algorithms. ARM will help optimize recognition of lanes, pedestrians and signs. Reports dated November 29, 2001, describe Enron nearing a potentially record-setting bankruptcy after credit downgrades and Dynegy’s withdrawal from its proposed acquisition. Enron had more than $15 billion in debt, less than $2 billion in cash as of the previous week, and substantial upcoming obligations. Its European holding company and some operating businesses entered administration. Overseas assets, partnership obligations and complex derivatives contracts were expected to complicate any bankruptcy proceedings.

Senate Majority Leader Tom Daschle called for Congress to investigate Enron’s collapse and assess its broader implications for the energy industry. Enron’s earlier accounting disclosures had prompted lawsuits, an SEC investigation and earnings restatements.

Key developments included:
- NYMEX required written clearing-member authorization for Enron orders, while several European power exchanges suspended its trading.
- EnronOnline reopened on a limited basis to help customers unwind positions and manage credit exposure. Rival InterContinental Exchange reported trading volume up 65% from October.
- U.S. electricity and natural-gas markets remained generally orderly, although some gas markets experienced increased volatility. British day-ahead electricity prices fell sharply, and German power prices fluctuated.
- Administrators reported serious buyer interest in Enron’s metals business. Dynegy asserted its right to acquire Enron’s Northern Natural Gas pipeline, which Enron said it would contest.
- Credit Suisse First Boston estimated Bank of America, Citigroup and J.P. Morgan Chase each had $500 million in direct loan exposure, excluding potentially significant counterparty obligations.
- Many European energy companies and investment funds reported limited exposure or earlier reductions in their holdings. Four Japanese money-management funds fell below par because of Enron bond losses and faced substantial redemption requests.
- Reliant Resources described its approximately $80 million exposure as manageable. Williams expected net exposure below $100 million and reaffirmed earnings targets. NewPower said it had sufficient cash and credit through the second quarter.
- Enron’s troubles delayed a $108 million Houston office development, pressured bank bonds and contributed to demand for U.S. Treasuries.

Enron shares traded around 41 cents, and bond prices near 22 cents on the dollar reflected expectations of bankruptcy. Shareholders were considered likely to lose their investments, while creditor recoveries remained uncertain.

The passage describes a vehicle driving assistance system that uses cameras and other sensors, including radar, lidar and ultrasonic sensors, to detect surrounding vehicles, their speeds and directions. To mitigate or avoid collisions with faster vehicles approaching from behind, the system may accelerate the equipped vehicle to match the approaching vehicle’s speed, change lanes, or combine these maneuvers.

The system supports scenarios such as passing a slower vehicle while accommodating faster traffic in an adjacent lane, or moving right to allow a faster rearward vehicle to pass. After passing, it may return the vehicle to its original lane and speed. Actions may be autonomous, driver-triggered, or communicated through visual, audible or haptic alerts and instructions.

Maneuver selection may consider available space, surrounding traffic, relative speeds, speed limits, upcoming exits, driver comfort, time loss, safety and emergency vehicles’ priority. Adaptive cruise control may incorporate desired and maximum speeds, with limits based on road restrictions, vehicle conditions, trailer characteristics and driver licensing.

Image processing supports object detection and optional camera displays. The system may also exchange information through vehicle-to-vehicle and vehicle-to-infrastructure communications.

The study demonstrates solid-state near-infrared-to-visible photon upconversion using a DIB-SQ:PCBM donor–acceptor bulk-heterojunction sensitizer coupled to rubrene or DBP-doped rubrene. The system repurposes triplet charge-transfer states, typically considered a loss channel in photovoltaics, to populate rubrene triplets and drive triplet–triplet annihilation (TTA).

A 1:3 DIB-SQ:PCBM weight ratio provided optimal upconversion output. Increasing PCBM content reduced DIB-SQ aggregation and promoted charge-transfer-state formation. Unlike neat sensitizer layers, the blend supported upconversion under low-intensity incoherent excitation.

Doping rubrene with 0.5 vol.% DBP shifted the emission peak from 562 to 605 nm and improved performance. The optimized device achieved a saturated upconversion quantum yield of 1.36% above 69.7 mW/cm², with a threshold intensity of 60.5 mW/cm² under 690 nm excitation.

Time-resolved spectroscopy identified charge-transfer states and molecular triplets as intermediates that transfer energy to rubrene, directly or through PCBM triplets. Magnetic-field measurements further supported the TTA mechanism: upconverted emission decreased by nearly 10% at 300 mT. The findings establish a route for using donor–acceptor sensitizers to harvest low-energy photons for solid-state upconversion.

In Payton v. County of Kane, six former detainees challenged bail fees imposed as a condition of release, alleging violations of the Eighth and Fourteenth Amendments under 42 U.S.C. § 1983. They sought to represent people affected by the practice in 19 Illinois counties, although the named plaintiffs had paid fees only in Kane and DuPage Counties. The district court dismissed the entire action for lack of standing and denied class certification as moot.

The Seventh Circuit reversed. It held that the named plaintiffs had standing to pursue individual claims against Kane and DuPage Counties because their payments constituted monetary injuries traceable to county policies and redressable through litigation. Any inability to represent a class would warrant denial of certification, not dismissal of their individual claims.

The court also reinstated the proposed class claims. It concluded that the absence of named plaintiffs directly injured by the other 17 counties did not automatically preclude a class action because the challenged fees arose from a common state statute. The plaintiffs might represent a class suing all 19 counties if they satisfied Rule 23. In this case, class certification should be considered before assessing standing with reference to the class as a whole.

The court remanded for consideration of certification requirements and the possible effects of related litigation involving Kane and DuPage Counties. It did not decide whether the fees were constitutional or whether the proposed class should be certified.

NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture introduces changes to ray tracing, neural rendering, GPU scheduling, video processing, displays, and power management.

- **Mega Geometry:** Cluster-level acceleration structures group up to 256 triangles, reducing processing for subsequent bounding volume hierarchy (BVH) builds by two orders of magnitude compared with triangle-based methods. GPU-driven, batched APIs minimize CPU overhead. Partitioned top-level acceleration structures update only changed partitions rather than rebuilding entire scenes. Mega Geometry also supports accelerated ray tracing of animated subdivision surfaces and is supported on RTX GPUs starting with Turing.

- **Ray tracing improvements:** Blackwell’s fourth-generation RT Cores provide geometry and BVH compression and up to twice the ray-triangle intersection rate of third-generation cores. Hardware-supported Linear Swept Spheres represent strand-like geometry; common hair-rendering workloads are approximately twice as fast as Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips while requiring about five times less geometry memory. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 doubles core reordering efficiency.

- **GPU scheduling:** The AI Management Processor uses a dedicated RISC-V processor to offload GPU-context scheduling from the CPU. It coordinates graphics and AI workloads, reducing scheduling latency and supporting more predictable execution.

- **Video and displays:** Ninth-generation NVENC adds H.264 and HEVC 4:2:2 encoding and improves AV1 and HEVC quality. AV1 Ultra High Quality mode provides additional quality improvements at increased processing time. Sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed and adds H.264 and HEVC 4:2:2 decoding. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps, including 8K at 165 Hz or 4K at 480 Hz with display stream compression.

- **Power efficiency:** Advanced clock, power, and rail gating reduce consumption during idle periods. Separate GPU-core and memory power rails allow independent control. Clock frequencies adjust to workloads 1,000 times faster than previous architectures, and the deepest sleep state is entered ten times faster than on Ada. A small-language-model inference example shows power savings of up to 50%.

- **DLSS 4:** Multi Frame Generation creates up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. The new frame-generation model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than its predecessor. Hardware Flip Metering moves frame pacing to the display engine. Transformer-based Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and Deep Learning Anti-Aliasing improve temporal stability, lighting detail, and detail in motion.

- **Neural shaders:** Cooperative Vectors APIs enable graphics shaders to access Tensor Cores. Applications include neural material approximation, texture compression, indirect-lighting estimation through Neural Radiance Cache, subsurface scattering through RTX Skin, and generative face rendering through RTX Neural Faces.

- **GPU family:** GB202 underpins the GeForce RTX 5090, GB203 supports the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti, and GB205 supports the RTX 5070. Their full-chip implementations contain 92.2 billion, 45.6 billion, and 31 billion transistors, respectively.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change and provides the materials without warranties, subject to usage and liability limitations.

The Marin Nail Trail 6 is a £1,100 aluminium trail hardtail available with wheel sizes matched to frame size. Its specification includes a 120mm RockShox Recon fork, SRAM GX 1×11 drivetrain with a Sunrace cassette, Shimano Deore hydraulic brakes and Schwalbe tyres. In Valentine Vredenburg et al. v. W. J. Behan et al., the court denied a motion to dismiss the defendants’ devolutive appeal, with costs. The plaintiff alleged an incomplete transcript, failure to include or cite necessary parties, omission of a deceased defendant’s representatives, and acquiescence in the judgment by several appellants.

The court held that three transcripts filed under the same docket number, collectively certified to contain the complete proceedings, evidence, and documents, substantially complied with the law. A new consolidated transcript was unnecessary.

Appellants were not required to name each appellee in their petition; requesting citation was sufficient, with issuance and service assigned to the clerk and sheriff. Acquiescence by some appellants could not deprive others of their appeal rights. Any omission involving the deceased defendant’s representatives did not justify dismissal as to appellants who apparently fulfilled their legal obligations, though that irregularity could still be raised.

The Woodland Trust’s Nature’s Calendar recorded 42 spring indicators at over a thousand UK locations in early 2017. Fewer sightings than in 2016 were attributed to colder January temperatures. Public observations help researchers monitor seasonal changes and climate change’s effects on plants and wildlife.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended July 26, 2015 reported revenue growth alongside lower earnings, restructuring charges and costs associated with a tablet recall.

- **First-half results:** Revenue increased 4% to $2.304 billion, while net income declined to $160 million from $265 million. Operating cash flow increased to $409 million from $247 million.
- **Business segments:** Quarterly GPU revenue increased 9% to $959 million, primarily reflecting growth in high-end GeForce gaming products. Tegra Processor revenue decreased 19% to $128 million as lower smartphone and tablet sales outweighed growth in automotive products, development services and SHIELD devices. Intel patent licensing revenue remained $66 million.
- **Icera restructuring:** NVIDIA began winding down its Icera modem operations after failing to identify a viable buyer. It recorded $89 million in restructuring and other charges and expected an additional $15 million to $25 million during the remainder of fiscal 2016. The restructuring was expected to affect approximately 5% of its global workforce and be substantially completed by fiscal year-end.
- **Tablet recall:** On July 31, 2015, NVIDIA announced a voluntary recall of SHIELD 8-inch tablets sold between July 2014 and July 2015 because their batteries could overheat and pose a fire hazard. Associated charges totaled $21 million for the first half, including $15 million in the second quarter.
- **Expenses and taxes:** Quarterly operating expenses increased 22% to $558 million. Sales, general and administrative expenses rose amid litigation-related legal fees and higher compensation costs. The quarterly effective tax rate increased to 64.0% from 17.2%, with tax charges related to the Icera wind-down among the contributing factors.
- **Financial position and shareholder returns:** At July 26, NVIDIA held $435 million in cash and cash equivalents and $4.070 billion in marketable securities. Total assets were $6.979 billion, and long-term debt was $1.399 billion. During the quarter, NVIDIA made a $400 million accelerated share repurchase payment and paid $52 million in dividends.

It began construction of a new headquarters building financed through an off-balance-sheet lease arrangement, with banks committing up to $380 million. Tesla’s 2017 annual report describes two reportable segments: automotive and energy generation and storage. **Products and operations**
- Tesla sold Model S sedans, Model X SUVs and Model 3 sedans. Model 3 deliveries began in July 2017, with production still ramping. Tesla planned a $35,000 variant and substantially higher volumes than Model S or Model X. Future vehicle plans included the Tesla Semi, Model Y and a new Roadster.

**Technology and regulation**

Tesla’s development activities covered battery packs, electric powertrains, vehicle software, self-driving technology and integrated energy systems. Its vehicles supported over-the-air updates. Government incentives supported manufacturing, electric vehicles, solar energy and storage. Tesla also earned and sold tradable regulatory credits. **Principal risks**

It targeted production of 5,000 Model 3 vehicles per week by the end of the second quarter of 2018, while noting limited experience with manufacturing, delivering and servicing vehicles at that scale.

Ángel Bracero sought damages from S. Ramírez & Co. after bags of rice fell on him in a Ponce shop. The defendant denied owning or controlling the shop and argued that Bracero was an employee whose claim belonged under the Workmen’s Compensation Act. The court upheld findings that Bracero was an independent contractor and that the shop was the defendant’s branch.

The majority nevertheless reversed the judgment, finding no negligence attributable to the defendant at the time of the accident. It rejected reliance on res ipsa loquitur because Bracero and other workers had removed bags from the pile, and Bracero had not established that their intervention was harmless. Earlier testimony warning of defective stacking did not, in the majority’s view, establish the pile’s condition when it fell. The court also criticized deficiencies in both parties’ briefs.

Chief Justice Del Toro, joined by Justice Hutchison, dissented. He considered the evidence sufficient to support the trial court’s findings of defective stacking and failure to warn. He emphasized testimony that the defendant had been warned the pile might fall but merely propped it with another pile rather than rebuilding it. He would have affirmed the judgment, concluding that negligence was established and that the trial court’s resolution of conflicting evidence should stand.

In 2011, Akamai, the world’s largest content delivery network, faced growing competition in non-U.S. markets despite its global scale. Its decentralized infrastructure comprised more than 100,000 servers across 78 countries, accelerating Internet content delivery by locating servers near users. International markets generated 29% of revenue.

Charley Dublin and Akamai’s international leadership team were tasked with addressing its “localization challenge.” Local competitors offered simpler, cheaper services that could match or exceed Akamai’s performance within individual markets. The study introduces an evolutionary hypergame framework in which individuals have unequal access to strategies because of differences in knowledge, experience, or perception. It examines a prisoner’s dilemma with three options: cooperation (C), defection (D), and opting out as a loner (L). Players either possess one of three two-strategy sets or any of the seven nonempty subsets.

Evolution occurs on two timescales. On the fast timescale, players adjust actions within fixed strategy sets through introspection, with stronger introspection making higher-payoff choices more likely. On the slow timescale, strategy sets evolve according to their relative success. Pairwise interactions are modeled as Markov chains, whose stationary distributions determine average payoffs. Strategy-set evolution is examined in well-mixed populations and spatial lattices.

Tournament results show that performance depends on introspection strength and the benefit-to-cost ratio. Under weak introspection, defection-containing sets or unconditional opting out generally prevail. With stronger introspection and sufficiently favorable cooperation benefits, {C, L} becomes more successful. Players using this set sustain mutual cooperation among themselves while switching to opting out when facing exploitation. Theoretical analysis shows that stronger introspection improves both their cooperative payoffs and their resistance to defectors.

Evolutionary simulations similarly show transitions toward cooperation as introspection increases. In well-mixed populations, strong introspection favors {C, L}. Spatial populations exhibit additional transitions, including coexistence and, at some intermediate introspection levels, dominance by unconditional cooperators. At higher introspection levels, {C, L} ultimately dominates.

The framework extends conventional evolutionary models by allowing both actions and available strategy sets to evolve, highlighting how heterogeneous strategic access and introspective adaptation shape cooperation.

- **Power management:** Core Logic Voltage Domains support independently selectable Operating Performance Points (OPPs), defined by maximum module frequencies and supply-voltage ranges. Lower-frequency OPPs reduce power consumption. Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling changes OPPs without reset, subject to supported combinations and device restrictions. DDR access must stop before changing DDR frequency. Adaptive Voltage Scaling is marked unsupported.

- **Low-power operation and supplies:** SRAM shutdown removes power and loses stored data. SRAM in switchable domains automatically shuts down when its domain turns off. Standby mode turns off switchable domains, runs the ARM Cortex-A8 in an idle loop at its lowest frequency, and gates unused functional blocks. Selected I/O supply groups independently support 1.8 V or 3.3 V; DDR interfaces independently support 1.5 V or 1.8 V. PHYs must enter power-down mode before their controller’s power domain is switched off.

- **Power sequencing and board design:** Supplies must follow specified power-up and power-down sequences. The 3.3-V supplies must never exceed the 1.8-V supplies by more than 2 V. PLL and analog supplies require noise filtering. Recommended decoupling includes small-package 0.1-µF capacitors and bulk capacitors near the device. Excessive capacitance must not disrupt sequencing, and reset must remain asserted until supplies are stable.

- **Reset behavior:** Reset sources include power-on, external warm, emulation, watchdog, software global, test, and local resets. Power-on reset resets the entire chip; warm resets preserve specified logic and configurations. Local resets affect only their associated modules. PCIe supports subsystem reset isolation, while Ethernet-switch isolation can preserve switching traffic during supported resets other than power-on reset. Most I/O pins enter high impedance during reset, with stated exceptions. After reset, the ARM Cortex-A8 executes from Boot ROM.

- **Clocking:** Device clocks come from external references, PLLs, and dividers. DEV and optional AUX inputs support crystals with internal oscillators or external 1.8-V LVCMOS clocks. DEV normally requires 20 MHz, with 20–30 MHz permitted under specified conditions; AUX supports 20–30 MHz. PCIe requires a low-jitter, AC-coupled differential reference. PLLs start in bypass mode, and programmed frequencies must satisfy PLL, system-clock, and module limits. PLL_USB must operate at 960 MHz when USB is used.

- **Interrupts, transfers, and debugging:** The ARM interrupt controller supports up to 128 requests with programmable priorities; general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. The DSP controller combines up to 128 events into 12 prioritized interrupts. EDMA supports 64 channels and mapping to 512 parameter entries. Debug facilities include hardware breakpoints, watchpoints, counters, state sequencing, real-time trace, and JTAG.

- **Peripheral interfaces:** Two DCAN interfaces support CAN 2.0 A/B. Four GPIO modules provide up to 128 configurable pins. The Ethernet subsystem includes a three-port gigabit switch, two external ports, MII/GMII/RMII/RGMII interfaces, and shared MDIO management; Ethernet PHY interfaces must use 3.3-V signaling. GPMC connects external flash, SRAM, pseudo-SRAM, and custom logic, with up to 512 MB addressing. The Error Locator Module supports BCH-based error location.

- **Timing and HDMI:** Timing analysis must account for board-routing delays. The HDMI 1.3a transmitter supports digital video, DVI-compatible RGB, and up to eight uncompressed audio channels. InVirtuoGen is a continuous-time discrete flow model for fragment-based molecular generation. It operates on fragmented SMILES with explicit attachment points, refining all sequence positions simultaneously rather than generating tokens sequentially or permanently unmasking them. This allows coordinated molecular updates and separates sampling steps from sequence length.

The representation extends SAFE, uses revised BRICS fragmentation, randomly shuffles fragments to reduce ordering bias, and employs a 204-token vocabulary. A diffusion transformer provides bidirectional attention. The model is pretrained on ZINC and UniChem, containing roughly one billion molecules.

Evaluation covers de novo generation, fragment-constrained design, target property optimization, and lead optimization. In de novo generation, InVirtuoGen achieves a better quality–diversity trade-off than the compared baselines, with finer sampling timesteps improving performance. Across five fragment-constrained tasks, it achieves competitive quality and diversity and higher average uniqueness, but lower average validity than GenMol. Required fragments are preserved by overwriting their positions at each timestep, restricting holistic refinement. Comparisons with GenMol use published results because the authors could not run its pretrained model directly.

For property optimization, the framework combines a genetic algorithm with PPO-based reinforcement learning adapted to discrete flows. Recombined fragments provide starting sequences for refinement, while reinforcement learning uses Monte Carlo estimates over perturbed states. The passage reports state-of-the-art PMO benchmark results and improved lead optimization over prior baselines.

The lecture reviews stopping trials, Wald’s equality, and their applications to renewal theory and queueing systems.

- **Wald’s equality:** For IID random variables with mean \(\bar X\) and a stopping trial \(J\) with finite expectation, \(E[S_J]=\bar X E[J]\). A stopping decision must depend only on observations already available. Generalized stopping trials can incorporate additional variables, such as service times, provided the necessary independence conditions hold.

- **Elementary renewal theorem:** If \(N(t)\) counts renewals through time \(t\), then \(E[N(t)]/t\to1/\bar X\). The appropriate stopping trial is \(N(t)+1\), since identifying the last arrival before \(t\) requires observing the next arrival. Wald’s equality gives a lower bound; truncating interarrival times supplies an upper-bound argument.

- **Queue regeneration:** In a G/G/1 queue with independent IID interarrival and service times, arrivals to an empty system initiate new renewal cycles, assuming the system eventually empties and restarts. Departures do not generally form a renewal process because idle periods interrupt service. The instant the system empties is not generally a regeneration point, since the remaining interarrival time depends on elapsed time.

- **Little’s theorem:** The integral of the number of customers in the system over complete renewal cycles equals the sum of their times in the system. Taking suitable long-run averages yields \(L=\lambda W\): average occupancy equals arrival rate times average customer delay. The main mathematical issue is establishing that these averages exist.

- **Pollaczek–Khinchin formula:** For an M/G/1 queue with Poisson arrival rate \(\lambda\), IID service times \(V\), and utilization \(\rho=\lambda E[V]\),
  \[
  E[W_q]=\frac{\lambda E[V^2]}{2(1-\rho)}.
  \]
  The derivation combines residual service time, service required by customers already waiting, and Little’s theorem. Waiting increases as utilization approaches one and as the service-time second moment grows. An infinite second moment can produce infinite expected waiting even when utilization is below one. Deterministic service gives less waiting than exponential service with the same mean.

The study investigates generating and detecting magnetic monopole fields on three-dimensional topological insulators using scanning tunneling microscopy and spectroscopy (STM/STS). Although magnetic-monopole-like quasiparticles have been constructed, no fundamental magnetic monopole particle has been directly observed.

The proposed mechanism uses the STM tip’s radial electric field to induce circulating surface currents through the topological magnetoelectric effect. These currents produce fields represented by image magnetic monopoles. Their interaction with orbital magnetic moments is predicted to split image potential states (IPS), hydrogen-like energy levels formed by electrons and induced image charges. In the ideal two-dimensional limit, opposing surface currents cancel.

Researchers compared topologically trivial √3-Bi, two-dimensional topological insulator Bi(110), and three-dimensional higher-order topological insulator Bi(111), grown on silicon substrates. IPS peaks in √3-Bi and Bi(110) followed Gaussian distributions and generally narrowed with increasing principal quantum number. In contrast, Bi(111) exhibited broadened, asymmetric higher-level peaks, including two distinguishable components at n = 2. A smaller n = 2 splitting was also observed in seven-quintuple-layer Bi₂Se₃.

The authors examined alternative explanations, including symmetric and antisymmetric IPS series, quantum well states, and quantum confinement. They argued that the observed splitting patterns, lack of thickness dependence, and large terrace sizes did not support these explanations.

A simplified electron–dyon model reproduced the splitting’s dependence on principal quantum number. The measured n = 2 splitting was approximately 400 meV, compared with a theoretical estimate of 204 meV. Changing the tunneling current altered the electric field and continuously modulated the splitting, consistent with the proposed mechanism.

The authors interpret these experimental and theoretical results as strong evidence for electrically induced magnetic monopole fields in a solid-state system and propose extending the method to other topological insulators and heterojunctions.
