The passage recommends confirming signals with other indicators or price analysis and managing risk through stop-loss orders, diversification, appropriate position sizing, and ongoing monitoring.

Jane Goodall warned that conservation is increasingly urgent, identifying climate change as wildlife’s greatest long-term threat. Cautiously optimistic about efforts to address it, she hopes the documentary Jane deepens understanding of chimpanzees and inspires action before environmental damage becomes irreversible.

A video of Tennessee middle school student Keaton Jones describing bullying drew more than 18 million views and support from athletes and entertainers. Keaton said students mocked his appearance, poured milk on him and put ham down his clothes. A crowdsourcing page raised over $29,000 for his future education, while celebrities offered friendship, visits and a game invitation.

This retrospective observational study examined whether glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) were associated with improved cardiovascular outcomes in adults with cancer therapy-related cardiac dysfunction (CTRCD). Using TriNetX electronic health records, researchers identified 12,410 patients treated between 2012 and 2023. After propensity-score matching, 1,223 GLP-1 RA users were compared with 1,223 nonusers, all receiving guideline-directed medical therapy.

Over one year, the composite outcome of heart failure exacerbation, death, or hospital/emergency department admission occurred in 55.7% of GLP-1 RA users versus 68.9% of nonusers (odds ratio 0.566; 95% confidence interval 0.480–0.668). GLP-1 RA use was also associated with significantly lower mortality, heart failure exacerbations, and hospital admissions. Differences in atrial fibrillation/flutter, ventricular tachycardia, and gastroenteritis were not statistically significant.

The findings suggest GLP-1 RAs may offer benefits for patients with CTRCD, but the observational design cannot establish causality. Limitations include potential residual confounding, reliance on clinical documentation, incomplete information about treatment adherence and chemotherapy combinations, limited demographic diversity, and short follow-up. Randomized controlled trials are needed to validate the results. The study was posted as a preprint and had not undergone peer review.

CeeDee Lamb has missed two games with a high-ankle sprain but is progressing in rehabilitation, including resistance-band work at practice. ESPN’s Todd Archer suggested a Week 7 return against Washington is possible. Lamb is likely to miss Week 6 unless his practice participation increases.

A study published in Future Oncology found that non-progression and tumor shrinkage during avelumab treatment correlated with improved health-related quality of life in patients with metastatic Merkel cell carcinoma. Researchers analyzed data from the Phase II JAVELIN Merkel 200 trial, assessing patient health using generic and skin cancer-specific quality-of-life measures.
Kirigami-inspired Mylar parachutes unfurl as objects fall and could be useful for humanitarian aid drops or package delivery.

SEV-ES and SEV-SNP protect guest register state by encrypting it during world switches, preventing direct hypervisor access or modification. The Guest-Hypervisor Communication Block (GHCB) standardizes selective information sharing, required exit handling, and special operations such as interrupt handling and multiprocessor booting.

The GHCB occupies a 4 KB, page-aligned area mapped decrypted or shared by the guest. Automatic Exits do not require exposing guest register state; Non-Automatic Exits allow the guest to control which state is shared. Guests handle relevant #VC exceptions, populate required GHCB fields, and invoke VMGEXIT. Both guest and hypervisor identify valid fields through VALID_BITMAP. Software should disable interrupts and preemption while accessing the GHCB around VMGEXIT and protect its contents during NMI handling.

The GHCB MSR protocol supports communication before a shared GHCB page is available, including protocol negotiation, CPUID requests, page-state changes, feature discovery, and termination requests. Hypervisors must not intercept access to the GHCB MSR. SEV-SNP guests must register each GHCB guest physical address before first use; supplying an address inconsistent with the registered address requires guest termination.

Version 2 adds initial SEV-SNP support and hypervisor feature advertisement through a 52-bit bitmap. Later revisions address 64-bit guest-request sequence numbers, error reporting, certificate identification, APIC ID retrieval, multiple VMPL levels, SEV-ES page-state changes, trusted I/O, and Secure AVIC. The specification also defines communication of secrets and CPUID pages from EFI firmware to the operating system.

Supported operations include I/O, MSR and MMIO handling; private/shared page transitions; firmware requests; certificate retrieval; application-processor creation; VMPL switching; and guest termination. SNP firmware requests use separate shared request and response pages. Extended requests can return certificates alongside attestation reports. Page-state changes track progress so interrupted requests can resume. SEV-TIO supports trusted-device setup and retrieval of measurements, certificates, and attestation data. Secure AVIC uses private, guest-owned APIC backing pages that must remain present in nested page tables while their vCPUs run.

Multiprocessor booting requires special handling because the hypervisor cannot modify encrypted, measured register state. AP reset-hold mechanisms and jump tables support startup and transitions between operating environments. SNP AP Creation allows guest-supplied VMSA pages and supports vCPU hotplug. NMI handling uses a guest “NMI Complete” notification. Hardware debug handling depends on DebugVirtualization support. SMM is unsupported in this specification version, and nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

Restricted Injection uses a shared #HV doorbell page to communicate interrupts and non-maskable events. PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields support notification, acknowledgment, and end-of-interrupt processing. Hosts must maintain APIC-style interrupt semantics. Guests enter HLT with interrupts disabled and examine pending events immediately after resuming.

Youth and Sports Minister Solomon Dalung said Buhari’s 2015 victory showed Nigerians could win elections without money and signalled resistance to political “god-fatherism.” Speaking in New York, he described “Not too Young to Run” as a challenge to entrenched political leaders and urged youths to understand the political system. He claimed Nigeria was progressing in infrastructure, the economy and security, called for unity, and advocated engagement with neighbouring countries to curb armed herdsmen’s cross-border movement.

Enron replaced Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow with Jeffrey McMahon on October 24, 2001, amid an informal SEC inquiry into partnerships Fastow managed while serving as CFO. Chief Executive Kenneth Lay said the change was necessary to restore investor confidence, a day after publicly defending Fastow. Fastow took a leave of absence.

The partnerships raised conflict-of-interest concerns and were linked to a $35 million third-quarter loss and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity. McMahon, formerly Enron’s treasurer and head of its industrial markets group, reportedly had objected to Fastow’s involvement in the partnerships.

Enron shares fell 17% to $16.41 on October 24, roughly halving their value since the company’s October 16 earnings announcement. Other energy-trading stocks also declined. Prudential Securities recommended selling Enron shares, while other analysts downgraded their ratings.

Investors and analysts criticized Enron’s complex financial arrangements and inadequate disclosures. Concerns included additional losses, obligations associated with off-balance-sheet partnerships, possible credit downgrades, and potential share dilution. Several analysts said replacing Fastow alone would not resolve these uncertainties.

Enron denied wrongdoing and maintained that its operations were functioning normally and its finances remained strong. Shareholder lawsuits alleged misleading disclosures, conflicts of interest, and insider trading by executives.

Germany’s Federal Cartel Office is investigating whether Temu restricts independent merchants’ pricing freedom through internal policies, algorithms and pricing tools. Authorities suspect the platform may pressure sellers to maintain uniform or higher prices across platforms, potentially breaching competition laws. Temu says it complies with European competition law and is cooperating with investigators. The retailer serves about 19 million users in Germany and more than 100 million across Europe. Confirmed violations could result in financial penalties or changes to merchant terms. The investigation forms part of broader European scrutiny of digital marketplaces’ competition, transparency and consumer protection practices.

A cross-sectional study in Nigeria examined associations between HIV infection, occupational chemical exposure, and biomarkers of apoptosis, oxidative damage, antioxidant protection, and immune function. Researchers recruited 248 adults—128 HIV-positive and 120 HIV-negative—and divided them into four groups according to HIV status and occupational exposure.

HIV-positive participants exposed to workplace chemicals had significantly lower p53 and bcl2 levels than HIV-negative unexposed participants, but differences from the other groups were not significant. They also had significantly higher malondialdehyde (MDA) levels than both HIV-negative groups. Differences in superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity were not significant.

Levels of p53 and bcl2 correlated positively with 8OHdG and SOD. After adjustment for sex, age, body mass index, and smoking, HIV status and SOD activity were significantly associated with p53 and bcl2; occupational exposure was not independently associated with either marker. HIV-positive participants had lower CD4 counts regardless of occupational exposure, and CD4 counts correlated negatively with MDA.

The authors suggest that oxidative stress and altered apoptosis regulation may contribute to cancer susceptibility among HIV-positive workers exposed to hazardous chemicals. However, the cross-sectional design limits causal conclusions, and the study did not assess specific cancers or long-term cancer outcomes. Longitudinal research and preventive interventions were recommended.
The Third Circuit found no error after reviewing the record and appellants’ arguments and affirmed the district court’s judgment.

Scientists led by Arizona State University physicist Steven Desch propose installing wind-powered pumps across the Arctic to spray seawater onto its surface, where it would freeze and thicken sea ice. The team estimates that adding one metre of ice in a winter could reduce the risk of ice-free summers.

Covering 10 percent of the Arctic Ocean would require approximately 10 million pumps; covering the entire region would require about 100 million. The project has an estimated cost of US$500 billion and would require substantial steel production and funding from multiple governments.

The proposal responds to rapid Arctic warming and concerns that efforts to reduce fossil fuel use will not prevent summer sea ice loss. Disappearing ice threatens local species and reduces Earth’s ability to reflect solar radiation. Researchers are also investigating links between Arctic warming, changes in the jet stream, and persistent extreme weather. The project is outlined in *Earth’s Future*.

Washington’s coach describes reaching the Stanley Cup finals as energizing rather than exhausting. He views defending champion Detroit as a patient, resilient opponent and praises Scotty Bowman’s adaptability across teams and generations of players. Washington respects the Red Wings but, as an experienced team, does not feel intimidated.

The coach and George McPhee emphasize leadership, character and experience alongside skill. Veterans Brian Bellows and Tikkanen have helped teammates stay relaxed and confident, particularly in overtime. The coach credits strong support from management and assistants for an enjoyable season and describes efforts to foster teamwork, humor and open communication.

An Apollo analogy highlighted the importance of supporters behind the team, prompting players to dedicate games to family members. The coach also emphasizes teammates’ loyalty to Dale Hunter and the role of luck in winning championships.

Washington plans to remain flexible with defensive assignments rather than settle immediately on whom Tikkanen should target. The coach considers the goaltending matchup closely balanced, praising Olie’s season-long performance and Chris Osgood’s improvement while acknowledging that both have allowed soft goals.

The disclosure describes respiratory assistance systems that identify gas sources and adjust heating and humidification to account for differences between ambient air and dry gas supplies. The systems aim to improve patient comfort, maintain desired humidity, and reduce condensation.

A system includes a gas source, liquid-containing humidification chamber, chamber heater, inspiratory conduit, patient interface, sensors, and a controller. Optional components include an expiratory conduit and conduit heaters. The systems can support invasive ventilation, non-invasive ventilation, high-flow therapy, and positive airway pressure therapy.

The controller determines gas-source type and system configuration using combinations of:
- Mean and bias flow rates, breathing patterns, and pressure changes.
- Reverse-flow or rebreathing detection.
- Temperature and optional humidity measurements.
- Electrical signals indicating connected components, such as expiratory heater wires.
- User input, which can be checked against sensor-derived information.

Rebreathing detection can involve comparing inlet and outlet flow profiles, identifying double peaks, correlating sensor signals, or comparing inspiratory and expiratory phase durations. Heated-bead sensors or thermistors may measure both temperature and flow. Detection thresholds can vary with sensor characteristics, sampling rates, and system geometry.

Based on the detected source and therapy, the controller can modify temperature set points, heater power, or duty cycles. Some embodiments lower the set point for room-air-entraining sources because incoming air already contains humidity, while maintaining it for dry gas sources. Temperature may serve as a proxy for humidity when direct humidity measurement is unavailable or unsuitable.

The system may operate automatically or with user confirmation, display detected sources and settings, alert users to inconsistent selections, and use default or safety settings before configuration is confirmed. Some embodiments identify supply conditions without direct communication between the humidifier and gas source.

Tesla introduced Model Y and Model 3 Standard variants priced at $39,990 and $36,990, respectively—about $5,000 below Premium versions, but less than the canceled $7,500 federal EV tax credit. Cost reductions include fewer luxury features and no rear touchscreens; the Model Y also has reduced power and range.

Edmunds analyst Joseph Yoon questioned whether the price cuts would attract new EV buyers, suggesting a price closer to $30,000 could be more compelling. Tesla’s supervised driver-assistance feature remains available for an additional $8,000.

Tesla’s global sales are down 6 percent from last year. A separate affordable-car initiative was reportedly canceled as Elon Musk prioritized autonomous vehicles and robotics, which he describes as central to Tesla’s future.

This study examines how employment status, working time and job satisfaction relate to subjective survival probabilities (SSP) among people aged 50 and over in Japan. SSP reflects individuals’ perceived chances of reaching specified ages and predicts mortality independently of self-rated health. Previous research links SSP to socioeconomic position and identifies gender differences, but its relationship with work and employment remains poorly understood.

Japan’s pension reforms have raised pension eligibility ages while many companies retain mandatory retirement at 60. Companies frequently bridge this gap through non-regular reemployment contracts. Other late-career situations include self-employment, domestic work and part-time employment. Research suggests that job satisfaction, workplace support and working conditions are associated with health; in Japan, long working hours have negative health effects particularly among workers reporting low job satisfaction.

The study distinguishes employment status from the tasks and conditions of work. It investigates differences in SSP across employment categories, associations with working time and job satisfaction, and whether these relationships change after adjustment for demographic, socioeconomic and health factors.

Data come from four waves of the Japanese Study of Aging and Retirement, collected in 2007, 2009, 2011 and 2013 across ten cities. The full sample comprises 16,932 observations from 7,082 respondents. Participants repeatedly estimated their percentage chances of surviving to specified ages from 75 to 110. Responses cluster at particular percentages rather than following a normal distribution, with higher survival expectations for age 80 and lower expectations for age 90.

This retrospective, non-peer-reviewed study examined successive SARS-CoV-2 Omicron lineage replacements in Connecticut from January 2022 to January 2023. Researchers combined genomic surveillance, patient and vaccination records, viral RNA measurements, and epidemiological modeling to assess how transmissibility and immune escape contributed to variant fitness.

Successive Omicron waves sustained high transmission throughout 2022. Modeling estimated approximately 1.5 million BA.1 infections, over 2.1 million combined BA.2, BA.4, and BA.5 infections, and 0.4 million XBB infections through January 2023. Lineage replacement slowed: BA.1 increased from 5% to 50% frequency in 10 days, compared with 20 days for BA.2 and 59 days for XBB.

Analysis of 6,856 Omicron samples showed that viral RNA copy numbers, used as a proxy for intrinsic transmissibility, only partly explained replacement patterns. Incoming BA.2 and XBB samples had higher viral copy numbers than their predecessors, whereas BA.4 and BA.5 replaced BA.2 despite lower copy numbers.

Vaccination-linked analyses found increased odds of BA.1 rather than Delta infection among people with at least two vaccine doses whose most recent vaccination was over five months earlier. BA.2 showed no overrepresentation among breakthrough infections. Observed vaccination-related associations for BA.5 and XBB did not reach statistical significance.

The authors proposed a conceptual model in which lineage advantages depended on changing population immunity and differing combinations of transmissibility and immune escape. They interpreted BA.2’s advantage primarily through enhanced transmissibility, BA.4/BA.5’s through immune escape, and XBB’s through both.

The study emphasizes linking sequencing with clinical, laboratory, and epidemiological data to evaluate emerging variants. Limitations include restricted applicability to populations with different characteristics, sample selection based on diagnostic cycle thresholds, and uncertainty about how viral RNA measurements reflect infectious virus.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 documentation describes peripheral capabilities, implementation requirements, development resources, and packaging guidance.

- **Analog functions:** A temperature sensor provides a linear voltage output to an ADC channel, with factory calibration data for temperature estimation. VREF offers selectable 1.4V and 2.5V internal references or an external reference. The comparator supports low-power wakeup, timer fault handling, selectable inputs, and an 8-bit reference DAC.
- **Low-frequency operation:** The LFSS includes a real-time clock and independent watchdog, using a typically 32kHz clock. RTC features include calendar counting, alarms, periodic interrupts, and calibration for crystal error and temperature drift.
- **Security and data checking:** Features include code and data firewalls, CRC-16 with custom-polynomial support, and a CRC module supporting CRC16-CCITT and bit reversal.
- **Communications:** Three UART peripherals support configurable parity, baud rates, LIN mode, FIFOs, and loopback. I2C supports 7-bit and 10-bit addressing, speeds up to 1Mbps, DMA, SMBus 3.0, address-match wakeup, and glitch filtering. SPI supports controller and peripheral operation up to 16Mbits/s, programmable frame sizes, DMA, and multiple formats.
- **Watchdogs and timers:** The independent watchdog generates a power-on reset if software fails to service it within the programmed time. The windowed watchdog can generate a reset or interrupt and also operate as an interval timer. General-purpose and advanced timers provide 16-bit counters, prescalers, synchronization, and peripheral triggering; advanced timers add PWM, dead-band insertion, and fault handling.
- **I/O and debugging:** IOMUX controls peripheral selection, input/output paths, and shutdown wakeup. The two-wire SWD debug subsystem supports processor and device-state debugging, configurable peripheral behavior during halts, mailbox communication, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Read-only factory memory stores device identification, capabilities, and trim information.
- **Implementation:** TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic supply-decoupling capacitors close to the pins. NRST requires a 47kΩ pullup resistor and 1000pF pulldown capacitor. External crystals require bypass capacitors, and 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs require pullups to produce logic-high signals.
- **Support and qualification:** Development resources include configuration tools, software libraries, training, debugging tools, and support forums. “X” identifies experimental devices intended for evaluation; “MSP” identifies fully qualified production devices. ESD precautions are required.
- **Revision and packaging:** The September 2025 revision removed DGS32 package information, updated specifications and identification tables, and added the debug-subsystem section. Packaging guidance covers thermal-pad soldering, optional vias, stencil design, marking, and ordering information.
- **Responsibility and limitations:** Application guidance is not part of TI’s component specification. Customers are responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance. Technical resources are supplied “as is” and may change without notice.

This preprint investigated sodium homeostasis in structural brain connectivity hubs in drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Researchers combined 7-Tesla anatomical, diffusion and sodium MRI with stereoelectroencephalography in 23 patients and compared imaging findings with 21 healthy controls. Brain regions were classified by structural hub status and involvement in seizure generation or propagation.

Total sodium concentration (TSC) was higher in patients than controls, averaging 54.6 versus 51.3 mM. This increase occurred across epileptogenic and non-epileptogenic regions and correlated with the extent of the epileptogenic network. Structural hubs had higher TSC than non-hub regions in both groups.

The sodium signal fraction, f, was increased specifically within epileptogenic zones compared with corresponding control regions, but decreased in other patient regions. Unlike TSC, f did not differ between hubs and non-hubs. Thus, the findings did not support the hypothesis that structural hubs exhibit distinctive epilepsy-related sodium signal fraction alterations.

Ten patients had overlap between structural hubs and epileptogenic zones. Patients without overlap showed a greater TSC increase. Observed associations between hub involvement and postoperative seizure recurrence were not statistically significant.

The authors suggest that TSC may reflect diffuse microstructural changes, whereas f may be more closely associated with regional homeostasis and epileptogenicity. Its physiological basis remains unclear. Limitations include possible cerebrospinal-fluid partial-volume effects, difficulty separating hub status from anatomical characteristics, and limited applicability to other epilepsy syndromes. The preprint had not been peer reviewed.

GAO examined comprehensive support and improvement (CSI) schools, their improvement plans, and the Department of Education’s monitoring of state oversight under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (ESEA).

In 2019–2020, about 5,200 CSI schools enrolled approximately 2.5 million students, or 5 percent of public school students. Compared with all Title I schools and all public schools, CSI schools more commonly served predominantly low-income and Black student populations, had substantially lower math and reading proficiency rates, and had slightly higher student-teacher ratios. School and district officials identified teacher shortages and turnover as barriers to improvement.

Based on a nationally generalizable sample, GAO estimated that 42 percent of CSI plans appeared to address all three selected required elements: a school-level needs assessment, identification of resource inequities, and interventions. Specifically:
- 73 percent contained or referenced a needs assessment.
- 52 percent discussed resource inequities or stated that a review had occurred.
- 86 percent included at least one intervention aimed at improving student or related outcomes.

GAO did not independently assess legal compliance or whether interventions met ESEA’s evidence-based definition. An estimated 58 percent of plans included an intervention supported by a high-quality study reviewed by Education’s What Works Clearinghouse; 18 percent included interventions shown ineffective by studies it reviewed. The Clearinghouse does not cover all interventions or all evidence allowable under ESEA.

Some school and district officials reported difficulty conducting needs assessments, identifying resource inequities, and selecting evidence-based interventions. Plans varied in quality, and some focused on circumstances outside schools’ control rather than school-based resources or actionable causes.

Education identified compliance deficiencies through routine and targeted monitoring and required corrective actions. However, it allowed monitored states and districts to select CSI plans for review, limiting its ability to assess state oversight independently.

GAO recommended that Education independently select improvement plans for monitoring. Education agreed and stated it would begin doing so in spring 2024.

Coach DeBoer said a major injury forced the team to test young players in different roles, revealing organizational depth and needs that informed deadline acquisitions. He focuses on energy and execution rather than motivational speeches for a veteran group playing in the Stanley Cup finals.

He attributed power-play difficulties partly to limited opportunities and said the team needed to keep moving and draw more penalties. He praised Melker’s intelligence, competitiveness and consistency, noting that increased confidence and a higher lineup position offered more offensive opportunities.

DeBoer described leadership decisions as difficult because of the many qualified players, but said everyone set aside egos and supported an inclusive approach. He praised the team’s resilience through extensive travel and rejected criticism of its character and leadership, calling its leaders among the best he had worked with.

Periyar University released April 2017 UG and PG examination results, available at periyaruniversity.ac.in or students’ colleges. Online access requires registration number and date of birth. Re-totalling and revaluation applications are due within 10 days of declaration, costing Rs 200 and Rs 250 respectively. Answer-sheet copies cost Rs 250.

Frank Schilbach introduces MIT’s Psychology and Economics course, also called Behavioral Economics. The field integrates insights from psychology and other disciplines into economics to make models more realistic, improve predictions, and inform policy. Schilbach’s research examines how poverty and associated conditions, including financial constraints, sleep deprivation, and mental health problems, affect behavior and economic outcomes.

Standard economic models commonly assume stable, well-defined preferences; expected-utility maximization; narrowly defined self-interest; perfect self-control; exponential discounting; preferences over final outcomes rather than changes; and optimal processing of information. They also generally assume information matters for decisions rather than directly affecting well-being.

The lecture discusses departures from these assumptions:
- Limited self-control can prevent people from following plans and create demand for commitment devices that restrict future choices.
- People may avoid useful health information or favor beliefs that make them feel better.
- Defaults can substantially influence decisions, as illustrated by differences in organ donation participation under opt-in and opt-out systems.
- Medication reminders and attention experiments illustrate limitations in memory and attention.
- Charitable giving and peer influences demonstrate that people care about others’ welfare, actions, and opinions.
- Preferences may depend on expectations, available alternatives, and how choices are presented.

Behavioral economics seeks to identify which departures matter, rather than merely document that standard assumptions are imperfect. Useful models should be simple, tractable, insightful, generalizable, testable, empirically consistent, and predictive. The field builds on standard economics rather than replacing it: markets, incentives, mathematical models, and empirical evidence remain central. An energy-use experiment illustrates that financial incentives can have persistent effects while appeals to morality fade.

Classroom laptop use provides a policy example. Laptops support note-taking and expand students’ choices, but may distract others, encourage temptation, consume attention, and interact with overconfidence about multitasking. A cited randomized study found that allowing computers reduced test scores by 0.18 standard deviations; flat tablets also performed worse than pen-and-paper note-taking. The course will use an opt-in laptop section at the front on one side of the classroom to limit distractions and permit supervision.

Course topics include time, risk, and social preferences; emotions; projection and attribution biases; attention; beliefs and learning; narrowly bracketed choices; malleable preferences; happiness and mental health; discrimination; policy and paternalism; and poverty. Policy discussions will consider defaults, framing, and nudges, including their welfare effects and ethical implications. Students are assigned sections one and two of Matthew Rabin’s paper on psychology and economics for the next class.

Telltale Games plans to develop an original IP, though it is not among its immediate projects and no genre or story details were disclosed. Communications head Job Stauffer highlighted interest in VR and streaming services and said the studio plans to expand onto devices beyond consoles, mobile, and PC, with details expected this summer. Telltale has up to 400 employees and can work on four projects simultaneously. It is developing more Game of Thrones, Minecraft, and Guardians of the Galaxy episodes, with additional announcements planned for the summer.

IDT’s September 29, 2025 earnings call introduced discussion of financial and operational results for the quarter and fiscal year ended July 31, 2025. Management cautioned that forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties and noted that reconciliations of non-GAAP measures appear in the earnings release. The excerpt contains no financial results.

A notice transcribed by the Tong-Hâk condemns Japanese and foreign interference in Korea, invokes past grievances and duties of loyalty, and calls for united action to expel foreigners under patriotic leadership. Following reports that Tong Hâk members are approaching Seoul, Japanese Consul Sugimura urges Japanese residents to prepare to evacuate women and children to Chemulpo. A further message to the Japanese consulate invokes moral and religious principles, condemns interference in another nation, recalls Japan’s 1592 invasion, and warns Japan to choose between danger and peace.

Britain’s first carbon-neutral new-build church, the Roman Catholic Church of the Annunciation in Walsingham, was built in 2006 with solar panels and a deep bore heat exchange system. Sheffield’s Christ Church Central planned a PassivHaus building but bought a nightclub instead because of funding constraints. The passage notes one PassivHaus church in the United States and two under construction in Canada.

Via Browser is a lightweight, fast, customizable Android browser available from developer Lakor in the Google Play Store. It supports web searches and URL navigation, selectable search engines, and an optional pull-to-refresh gesture. Do Not Track and ad blocking are enabled by default, while location access is disabled. An Incognito Mode is also available. Tabs are managed through a numbered icon that opens a list of active tabs. The author recommends Via for its balance of speed, features, and simplicity.

High Prairie Elementary students are learning to access ebooks through Overdrive. Grade 6M elected Shayla Grey class prime minister. Classes are planting seeds, studying biographies and the Famous Five, conducting science experiments, preparing for the Christmas concert, and exchanging postcards internationally. Grade 5 students sold out their Kids Sense Book Sale and organized assemblies and charitable activities. Automatic Local bus clock gating can prevent an edge-configured PIC input from returning to Idle, causing missed interrupts and potential system hangs or unexpected behavior. Recovery requires the clock to be on or turn on while the interrupt source is low.

The passage describes traditional Russian sunburn remedies: dairy products for redness; egg whites, nettle decoction, and watermelon juice for pain; sea buckthorn oil for peeling and chafing; potatoes, carrots, and pumpkins for itching; and sauerkraut for swelling. Other suggested treatments include soda dissolved in water, soaked oatmeal, and a sour cream mask with lemon juice. These remedies are presented as ways to soothe or restore sunburned skin.

Glenn Ellison’s lecture examines firm entry, its welfare implications, and models of firm learning and reputation.

- **Entry and market structure:** In a two-stage model, firms pay a fixed entry cost and then compete. Equilibrium entry depends on whether operating profits cover entry costs. Lower entry costs generally encourage entry, while competition determines how quickly profits decline as firms enter. Net profits can reflect the discrete number of firms that fit into a market rather than simply the intensity of competition. In several models, larger markets support both more firms and larger firms.

- **Efficiency of entry:** For homogeneous goods, the first-best outcome is one firm pricing at marginal cost. When competitive behavior is taken as given, free entry generally exceeds the socially optimal number under the lecture’s assumptions, subject to a possible one-firm rounding exception. The central mechanism is **business stealing**: entrants gain sales partly by taking customers from incumbents, whereas the social benefit comes from increased total output and reduced deadweight loss.

- **Differentiated products:** Entry can be excessive or insufficient. Business stealing encourages excessive entry, while improvements in consumers’ product matches can generate benefits that entrants do not capture. In the illustrated Hotelling-circle model, equilibrium entry is twice the socially optimal level despite improved matching. Ellison cautions that model assumptions can predetermine welfare conclusions; empirical work should distinguish market expansion from business stealing and allow flexibility in consumer-surplus gains.

- **Vertical differentiation:** Shaked and Sutton’s framework distinguishes natural oligopoly from specialization. If the same highest-quality product is efficient for everyone, the number of firms remains finite even as entry costs approach zero. If different qualities are efficient for different consumers, extensive specialization can occur.

- **Firm dynamics and learning:** Census manufacturing data show substantial entry, exit, and variation in firm growth. In Jovanovic’s model, firms initially do not know their productivity and learn through noisy operating results. Firms expecting low costs produce more; firms with uncertain prospects may remain small while learning; firms sufficiently confident that their costs are high exit. The model explains why small firms grow faster conditional on survival but fail more often, and why larger firms are more profitable. Concentration and profits can be correlated because of cost heterogeneity rather than a causal effect of weaker competition.

- **Ratings and entry:** Vellodi’s model examines how limited reviews impede learning about new firms. Poorly established firms attract few customers and therefore few reviews, slowing reputation development. Some price below cost to encourage purchases and learning. In this model, a consumer-optimal rating platform selectively withholds information about highly rated firms, increasing the reward for attaining a moderately good reputation and strengthening new firms’ incentives to attract customers through lower prices.

Canon’s EOS 77D features a 24.2-megapixel Dual Pixel CMOS sensor, 45-point autofocus, a top status display, an optional beginner interface and Bluetooth connectivity. Positioned between the T7i and 80D, it lacks weather sealing. Canon also introduced a smaller but heavier EF-S 18-55mm f4-5.6 IS STM kit lens, priced at $250. The 77D is scheduled for April 2017 availability at $900 body-only, $1,050 with the new lens or $1,500 with an 18-135 STM lens.

The Supreme Court denied Google’s request to pause court-ordered changes to its Play store policies in an antitrust dispute with Epic Games. A jury found in 2023 that Google unlawfully maintained a monopoly, and an appeals court upheld the verdict and injunction. Google must allow developers to use independent payment systems for in-app purchases later this month; changes involving competing app stores are due by July 2026. Google cited security risks, which Epic said lower courts had already rejected. Google plans to seek Supreme Court review, which could affect the broader changes.

On April 16, 2020, NVIDIA announced that China’s antitrust regulator approved the proposed acquisition of Mellanox by NVIDIA International Holdings, its wholly owned subsidiary. The transaction had received antitrust approvals from the European Commission, Mexico and China, and the U.S. antitrust waiting period expired on May 23, 2019. Closing was expected on or about April 27, 2020, subject to remaining customary conditions.

Brown recorded academic code violation charges against 49 undergraduates and seven graduate students in 2015–16. More than half of violations occurred in computer science, potentially reflecting stronger detection tools. Sanctions ranged from reprimands to suspension or dismissal, while 13 undergraduates received no violation. The Academic Code committee requested expanding faculty membership from five to nine to handle its caseload. Prevention efforts include a mandatory online tutorial, course-specific integrity standards and revised international student orientation. International students and first-years are slightly overrepresented in violations, which administrators attributed largely to differing educational expectations. Officials are considering academic integrity events and an honor code with student-led review panels.

The Rancho Bernardo Kiwanis Club celebrated 50 years of service at StoneRidge Country Club. Founded in 1967, the club sponsors school youth groups and Scouts. In 2016, it donated $50,000 toward a community park tot lot and $40,000 to Rady Children’s Hospital. It also supports transitional homes for Romanian orphans and serves meals at Ronald McDonald House. Its annual pancake breakfast typically raises about $20,000 in profit. President John O’Rourke said the club has helped over 800,000 children.

Lois Riess, 56, was arrested in Texas after a weekslong manhunt. Authorities allege she killed her husband in Minnesota, stole $11,000 from his account, then killed Pamela Hutchinson in Florida to assume her identity.

Riess faces second-degree murder, theft and identity-related charges in Florida, and felony theft in Minnesota, where authorities say a murder charge is pending. A Texas judge authorized extradition to either state.

Florida could pursue the death penalty if a grand jury indicts Riess for first-degree murder, but prosecutors would still need to evaluate aggravating and mitigating factors. Potential death penalty considerations could influence which state tries her first.

Riess also has a history of gambling and alleged misuse of her disabled sister’s funds. Court records show she was ordered to repay her sister but was not charged.

Amazon’s 19 March sale reduces Netgear Arlo’s three-camera security system by 39%, from £409.99 to £249.99. Its waterproof, battery-powered cameras offer motion detection, night vision and a week of free online video storage, with smartphone, browser and Alexa control.

The Trump administration fired most members of the National Council on the Humanities, leaving four, all Trump appointees. The 26-member council advises the National Endowment for the Humanities on grants, policy and funding. Dismissed member Karen Stout expressed disappointment with the firings.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examines how excessive left ventricular trabeculation affects measurements of heart function. A retrospective, single-center study analyzed cardiac magnetic resonance images from 15 adults with excessive trabeculation, separating the compact wall, central cavity, trabeculations, and blood-containing intertrabecular recesses. Four-chamber analyses were expanded to 30 cases using publicly available images.

Intertrabecular recesses had a significantly higher ejection fraction (EF) than the central cavity: 61±17% versus 44±16% (P<0.001). Four-chamber images similarly showed greater systolic area reduction in the recesses. Total EF was not significantly correlated with the extent of trabeculation.

Measurement methods substantially affected ventricular volume and EF estimates. Including trabecular tissue in the blood pool increased end-diastolic and end-systolic volumes and lowered EF without significantly changing stroke volume. Excluding intertrabecular recesses from the blood pool reduced measured volumes, stroke volume, and EF. Compared with including trabeculations in the blood pool, contouring trabeculations halved the number of patients classified with EF below 40% and doubled those with EF above 50%.

The authors conclude that contouring trabeculations improves volume and EF assessment and could influence diagnosis and treatment. Limitations include manual labeling, threshold-related measurement variation, a small single-center sample, and the absence of additional clinical data. The findings require validation in larger studies.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2019 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 27, 2019. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, the company develops GPU-based computing platforms for Gaming, Professional Visualization, Datacenter, and Automotive. Its two reportable segments are GPU and Tegra Processor, supported by a common architecture and CUDA software.

Key products include GeForce gaming GPUs, Quadro professional graphics, Tesla accelerators, DGX AI systems, GRID virtualized graphics, and Tegra-based platforms for autonomous vehicles, robotics, medical instruments, and entertainment. NVIDIA introduced its RTX platform during fiscal 2019, enabling real-time ray tracing. Its DRIVE automotive platform combines hardware, software, training, and simulation tools for autonomous driving.

The company’s strategies emphasize advancing GPU computing, AI, visual computing, autonomous vehicles, and intellectual-property licensing. NVIDIA had invested more than $17 billion in research and development since inception. As of January 27, 2019, it employed 13,277 people, including 9,486 in research and development.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on third-party suppliers for semiconductor fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Sales occur through industry partners, online channels, and direct relationships with cloud providers and enterprise customers. Revenue attributed to billings outside the United States represented 87% of total revenue in fiscal 2019; China, including Hong Kong, represented 24%. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities increased 4% to $7.42 billion at year-end.

Principal risks include rapid technological change, competition, cybersecurity incidents, product defects, supplier dependence, demand forecasting errors, business disruptions, international regulation, employee retention, acquisitions, intellectual-property disputes, privacy requirements, taxation, and litigation. Fiscal 2019 included prolonged channel sell-through of mid-range gaming GPUs and weaker second-half revenue than first-half revenue. Securities and derivative lawsuits alleged misleading statements concerning channel inventory and cryptocurrency mining’s effect on GPU demand.

NVIDIA’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under NVDA. It had 606 million shares outstanding as of February 15, 2019. Through January 27, 2019, the company had repurchased 260 million shares for $7.08 billion, with $7.24 billion remaining authorized. It intended to return $3 billion to shareholders by the end of fiscal 2020, including $700 million in fourth-quarter fiscal 2019 repurchases.

The report cautions that forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties and that actual results may differ materially from expectations.

Harvey Ulfers was sentenced to 33 months for wire fraud and money laundering involving undervalued John Deere scrap metal sales. He was ordered to pay a $111,602 fine and $259,132 restitution. Co-conspirator Patrick Williams received 27 months.

Addressing Congress in an extraordinary session, the President describes the seizure of federal property and suspension of most federal functions in six Southern states at the beginning of his term. These states had declared separation from the Union, organized armed forces, and formed a Confederate government seeking foreign recognition. The administration initially pursued peaceful measures while attempting to retain remaining federal property.

The President recounts military difficulties surrounding Fort Sumter and unsuccessful efforts to reinforce Fort Pickens. After South Carolina was notified of an expedition to provision Sumter, the fort was attacked and captured before supplies arrived. He argues that this attack initiated armed conflict and required the government to use force to preserve the Union. He presents the struggle as a test of whether constitutional government can survive internal attempts at dissolution.

Federal measures included calling 75,000 militia, blockading ports in insurrectionary districts, requesting additional volunteers, and expanding the Army and Navy. The President seeks congressional ratification of emergency measures and defends limited suspension of habeas corpus as constitutionally justified by rebellion and public safety. He requests at least 400,000 men and $400 million to make the conflict short and decisive.

The address describes Virginia’s cooperation with the Confederacy and promises protection for loyal Virginians. It rejects border-state “armed neutrality” as effectively assisting secession.

The President argues that states possess no constitutional right to withdraw unilaterally, that their legal status derives from the Union, and that secession would undermine government and shared financial obligations. He questions whether disunion commands a genuine majority in most seceded states.

Praising volunteers and loyal service members, he portrays preservation of the Union as defense of popular government, opportunity, and constitutional elections against armed reversal. He pledges that, after the rebellion is suppressed, the government will remain guided by the Constitution and laws and respect the rights of states and citizens.

Halimat Oniru’s Haleem Group is headquartered in Abuja and operates in Lagos, Delta, Bayelsa and Cross River. The passage describes it as a major dredging and road construction company, crediting it with creating tens of thousands of jobs and noting Oniru’s humanitarian work.

The President outlined a six-part plan to combat COVID-19 amid the spread of the Delta variant. He cited progress, including more than 175 million fully vaccinated Americans and a 70 percent decline in weekly deaths compared with the week before he took office, while emphasizing that nearly 80 million eligible Americans remained unvaccinated.

The plan includes:

- **Expanded vaccination requirements:** Employers with at least 100 employees would have to ensure workers are vaccinated or tested weekly and provide paid time off for vaccination. Requirements would also cover executive branch federal employees, federal contractors, and 17 million healthcare workers. Overall, the proposed requirements would affect about 100 million Americans.
- **Protection for vaccinated people:** Free booster shots would be available following decisions by the FDA and CDC on authorization and eligibility.
- **School safety:** Nearly 300,000 Head Start educators would be required to get vaccinated. The President urged governors to require vaccination for teachers and staff and supported testing, masking, ventilation, and distancing. He pledged federal support for school officials facing state penalties for protective measures.
- **Expanded testing and masking:** The administration would increase rapid-test production, purchase nearly 300 million tests for free distribution, expand pharmacy testing, and work with retailers to reduce home-test prices. Fines for travelers refusing required masks would double.
- **Economic support:** The maximum available COVID-19 Economic Injury Disaster Loan for small businesses would rise from $500,000 to $2 million.
- **Improved treatment:** The Defense Department would double military health teams supporting hospitals, and shipments of free monoclonal antibody treatments would increase by 50 percent.

The President also pledged an equitable response, continued international vaccine donations, and further details on pandemic preparedness. He urged vaccination and collective action while acknowledging that the measures would take time to have their full effect.

Two Oceans Restaurant in Table Mountain National Park has stopped selling West Coast Rock Lobster after SASSI red-listed it as unsustainable. Sales will remain suspended until the population recovers. SASSI reported less than 2% remaining. SANParks TMNP supports the initiative.

This English cohort study examined the effectiveness of two doses of BNT162b2 and ChAdOx1 COVID-19 vaccines versus no vaccination, with follow-up extending to 50 weeks after the second dose or 31 March 2022.

Third-dose uptake reached at least 90% among adults aged 65+, clinically vulnerable adults aged 18–64, and adults aged 40–64. Individuals remaining with two doses had higher non-COVID-19 mortality than unvaccinated individuals, suggesting selection bias associated with deferred vaccination following infection, illness or frailty. Consequently, the researchers did not interpret COVID-19 effectiveness estimates beyond 26 weeks in these groups. High third-dose uptake also complicated assessment of the omicron variant’s effects.

Among adults aged 18–39, studied only for BNT162b2, third-dose uptake reached 73%, without evidence of increased non-COVID-19 mortality among those remaining with two doses. Estimated protection against COVID-19 hospitalisation declined approximately log-linearly and was negligible by weeks 35–38. Protection against a positive SARS-CoV-2 test appeared negligible by weeks 15–18, but differences in testing behaviour complicated interpretation. The authors tentatively suggested protection might instead persist until weeks 23–26. Waning in this subgroup did not appear affected by omicron’s emergence.

The study highlights the importance of accounting for selective uptake of additional doses, testing policies and testing behaviour when estimating long-term vaccine effectiveness. Reporting non-COVID-19 outcomes may help identify biases.

Linda Ronstadt discusses how Parkinson’s disease ended her singing career and makes daily tasks, talking and travel difficult. Diagnosed in 2013, she exercises daily and remains publicly active through “A Conversation With Linda,” featuring archival material about her career and audience questions.

The passage also highlights the 40th-anniversary expanded edition of her album Simple Dreams, featuring three live recordings from 1980. The original album topped the charts for five weeks beginning in December 1977, produced three Top 40 hits and won a Grammy for Best Recording Package. Her fifth consecutive million-selling platinum album, it sold over 3½ million copies in less than a year in the United States.

The study examines how blockchain companies create and capture value through digital business models. Blockchain uses distributed ledgers, consensus mechanisms, and cryptography to protect transactional records and enable transactions without trusted intermediaries. Despite interest in its business applications, scholars disagree over whether blockchain disrupts existing systems or primarily strengthens their foundations.

Combining digital business model theory with value configurations—value chains, value networks, and value shops—the researchers conducted an exploratory study of five companies in mainland China. All used permissioned consortium blockchains without issuing tokens. Evidence included public archives and 43 interviews with 31 informants conducted between September 2017 and August 2018. Analysis focused on value creation and capture, excluding delivery architecture and stakeholder networks because the researchers considered these broadly comparable across the cases.

The study identifies five business models:

- **Platformer—ChainArchitect:** Improves blockchain architecture and provides an open platform for third-party applications. It seeks to capture value by establishing its technology as a standard for future innovation. Compatibility with existing infrastructure is its principal challenge.
- **Disintermediator—ChainFinance:** Uses blockchain-enabled interbank transfers to displace intermediary functions and reduce transaction costs. It captures value by improving conditions for disadvantaged market participants but faces incumbent resistance.
- **Mediator—ChainSecurity:** Applies blockchain to asset-backed securities, improving information reliability, risk assessment, and coordination. It captures value through participant-specific benefits. Securing cooperation and changing established routines are major obstacles.
- **Transformer—ChainNova:** Develops customized applications, including agricultural product traceability, and seeks to replicate successful solutions across industries. Differences in business practices limit transferability.
- **Co-innovator—ChainDraft:** Collaborates with organizations to develop applications on its proprietary blockchain platform, including electronic drafts. It captures value through licensing, while development and maintenance costs and small-scale adoption constrain returns.

The findings locate blockchain value opportunities at ecosystem, value-chain, and individual-organization levels. They also suggest that blockchain can improve existing arrangements rather than necessarily displacing them.

Generalizability is limited by the five-company sample, its mainland China setting, and the exclusion of two business-model dimensions. The proposed typology is neither definitive nor exhaustive; further research could expand and refine it.

Kyle Busch won the Overton’s 400 for Joe Gibbs Racing, defeating Kyle Larson by 1.162 seconds after a final-lap challenge. It was Busch’s fifth victory of the season, second at Chicago and 48th career NASCAR Cup Series win, tying Buck Baker for 14th on the all-time wins list.

Busch started 16th and struggled with handling, finishing 12th in Stage 1 and 11th in Stage 2. Aric Almirola and Kevin Harvick won those stages, respectively. Adjustments and fast pit stops helped Busch advance in the final stage. He took the lead on lap 210 and led 59 laps overall.

Busch credited his team’s persistence, improved car balance and pit crew performance. His career wins across NASCAR’s top three divisions reached 190.

The next Cup Series event is the Coke Zero Sugar 400 at Daytona International Speedway on July 7.

Amazon reported second-quarter 2021 net sales of $113.1 billion, up 27% from a year earlier. Operating income increased to $7.7 billion from $5.8 billion, while net income rose to $7.8 billion from $5.2 billion. Diluted earnings per share increased to $15.12 from $10.30.

- **Segment results:** North America sales rose 22% to $67.6 billion, International sales increased 36% to $30.7 billion, and AWS sales grew 37% to $14.8 billion. Operating income was $3.1 billion, $362 million, and $4.2 billion, respectively.
- **First-half results:** Net sales reached $221.6 billion, up 35%, with operating income of $16.6 billion and net income of $15.9 billion.
- **Cash flow and investment:** Second-quarter operating cash flow declined to $12.7 billion from $20.6 billion. Cash capital expenditures increased to $13.0 billion from $6.6 billion, primarily supporting fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure. Trailing-twelve-month operating cash flow increased to $59.3 billion, while free cash flow declined to $12.1 billion from $31.9 billion.
- **Financial position:** Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $89.9 billion at June 30, 2021. Long-term debt was $50.3 billion, compared with $31.8 billion at year-end 2020. Amazon issued $18.5 billion of unsecured senior notes in May, including $1.0 billion for green or social projects.
- **Acquisition and legal matters:** Amazon agreed to acquire MGM for approximately $8.5 billion, including debt, subject to customary closing conditions. Luxembourg’s data-protection regulator imposed a €746 million fine in July over alleged GDPR noncompliance; Amazon disputed the decision.
- **Pandemic effects:** Amazon incurred approximately $1.5 billion in COVID-19-related costs during the quarter. It expected sales growth to decelerate in the third quarter and pandemic-related costs, fulfillment-capacity pressures, and supply-chain constraints to continue into all or portions of that period.

The passage describes a patent application for systems and methods that generate near-real-time weather forecasts using diverse, high-frequency data sources, including terrestrial and satellite microwave links, radar, numerical weather models, and stationary or vehicle-mounted sensors. The system estimates precipitation, atmospheric water vapor, liquid water content, fog, and visibility, including runway visual range (RVR), to support transportation planning.

The described architecture separates four functions: information collection and normalization, offline/background processing, modeling and prediction, and information distribution and alerting. Asynchronous collection and preprocessing operate independently of forecast cycles. Precomputed filters, transforms, and trained machine-learning models remove unreliable data and convert measurements into usable weather information. Background processes maintain these tools, while forecasting components blend observations and produce forecasts, maps, reports, and alerts.

Data is organized into repeating “cadence” instances containing geographically organized tile layers for collected, processed, and forecast information. These structures support data sharing, reuse of unchanged information, and updates as new observations arrive. Forecast horizons are configurable, typically spanning two to six hours for high-resolution forecasts and one to ten days for lower-resolution forecasts.

A cadence manager compares new observations with previous forecasts and chooses between complete recalculation and incremental updates. When differences are limited, unchanged tiles are reused, while affected tiles and dependent forecasts are recalculated. Updates propagate through dependent layers until no significant changes remain. This approach reduces unnecessary computation and storage.

The passage reports forecast accuracy improvements of 30–70%, forecast speed improvements of up to 50%, and forecast cycles as short as one minute. Some embodiments use cadence intervals below 15 seconds. Aviation applications include frequently updated fog and RVR forecasts for individual airports, runways, and sensor locations.

President Donald Trump called for Congress to end “chain migration” and strengthen immigration enforcement after an explosion near Manhattan’s Port Authority Bus Terminal. Police identified the suspect as Akayed Ullah, a 27-year-old permanent resident who entered the United States in 2011 on a family immigrant visa. Trump urged Congress to increase immigration enforcement staffing, expand arrest and detention powers, and address immigration fraud. He also called for the strongest legal penalties for convicted terrorists, including the death penalty in appropriate cases.

The Department of Transport has warned that some commercial State companies consider salary rates introduced in 2011 too low to attract or retain suitable chief executives. Government policy also eliminated certain benefits and stopped performance-related bonuses. Some CEOs whose contracts retain bonus clauses are threatening legal action to recover payments, including arrears. The chief executive of Dún Laoghaire Harbour Company has referred unpaid bonuses to the High Court.

Edmonton police seized $3.2 million worth of carfentanil, the department’s largest seizure of the drug, after firefighters discovered suspicious powder in a southwest basement suite on Jan. 28. Investigators confirmed carfentanil in blue and pink powders and believe white powder was caffeine intended to dilute the drug. Police said the drugs were likely destined for street distribution. Alberta Health Services condemned the building over contamination concerns. No arrests have been made, and investigators are seeking to identify and speak with the basement tenant, considered a person of interest. Upstairs tenants, university students who called firefighters, were unaware of the operation.

The application describes blockchain-based digital certificate management methods, apparatuses, and systems intended to reduce security risks arising from compromised or malicious certificate authorities (CAs).

A CA issues a digital certificate to a blockchain node and requests that it be written into the blockchain. Participating nodes verify the certificate, broadcast their results, and determine whether consensus requirements are met. Acceptance can depend on predetermined numbers or proportions of successful verifications, potentially within a specified period. Verification criteria may address certificate validity periods, serial numbers, or customized requirements. Certificates are written into the blockchain only after successful consensus verification and remain invalid before that step.

The same approval process applies to certificate revocation lists, updates to those lists, and individual revocation records. Nodes may store an approved revocation list in their local ledgers or construct and maintain lists from approved revocation records. When processing transactions, nodes compare participants’ certificates against these local lists and accept or reject requests according to applicable transaction rules.

Local verification removes the need to request remote certificate verification from the CA. The application identifies reduced verification costs, improved transaction efficiency, and protection against unauthorized certificate issuance or revocation as intended benefits.

Corresponding apparatuses provide functions for receiving requests, determining consensus results, and accepting or rejecting requests. CA-side apparatuses issue certificates and submit them for blockchain approval. Implementations include processor-and-memory devices, hardware, software, combined hardware/software systems, and computer-readable storage media. An additional workflow stores approved certificates and transaction-identifying data, records execution time, and notifies the CA when a transaction is executed.

This preprint evaluated the modified COVID-19 Yorkshire Rehabilitation Scale (C19-YRSm), a 17-item patient-reported measure of Long Covid symptoms, functional disability and overall health. Data came from 1,314 patients receiving care at 10 UK Long Covid services in the LOCOMOTION study. Participants were predominantly Caucasian (76%) and female (67%), with an average age of 48 years.

The instrument showed good reliability and convergent validity with the FACIT-Fatigue scale. Symptom severity and functional disability scores increased with additional symptom burden and were higher among patients previously hospitalised or admitted to intensive care for COVID-19. Missing responses were uncommon, at under 3%.

Among 263 patients assessed approximately 30 days apart, the scale detected changes over time. Test-retest reliability coefficients were 0.86 for symptom severity and 0.78 for functional disability. Responsiveness was greater than that of the generic EQ-5D-5L health measure, although effect sizes were modest.

Estimated minimally important differences were two points for symptom severity and functional disability and one point for overall health. Estimated minimal clinically important differences were four points for symptom severity and functional disability. These distribution-based estimates require confirmation using patient- and clinician-reported assessments of change. Support for a two-factor structure was limited, with several fit statistics failing to meet predefined thresholds.

The findings support using C19-YRSm to monitor Long Covid trajectories and assess interventions in clinical practice and research. Its brevity may reduce patient burden and facilitate repeated self-assessment. The preprint had not been certified by peer review.

The San Diego County Fair’s “Where the West is Fun” exhibit features Kumeyaay cultural displays and tribal members performing songs in their native language at 12:30 p.m. Wednesdays. Special craft projects are planned for Kids’ Day on June 27. Organizer Vanessa Christman says the tribe’s presence helps counter misconceptions that Kumeyaay people no longer exist. The exhibit also examines Hollywood’s portrayal of cowboy life and offers daily entertainment.

Ruth Negga said she resented how teachers spoke to her and wanted her school days to end. The Ethiopian-Irish actress described acting as freeing despite its rigorous schedule and credited luck with an important role in her success. She received her first Oscar nomination, for Best Actress, for Loving, which tells the story of an interracial couple whose case led the US Supreme Court to overturn laws against interracial marriage.

The passage describes peripherals, implementation requirements, development resources, and packaging guidance for TI MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers.

- **Watchdogs:** The independent watchdog uses a system-independent clock and generates a power-on reset if software fails to reset it within the programmed period. It offers eight periods from 2 ms to 2 hours. The windowed watchdog can generate resets or interrupts, stop automatically during sleep, and operate as an interval timer.
- **Timers:** General-purpose and advanced timers support programmable prescalers, synchronization, cross-triggering, and interrupt/DMA generation. Selected general-purpose timers provide shadow registers and encoder interfaces. Advanced timers add complementary PWM, programmable dead band, repeat counters, and fault handling.
- **Analog and I/O:** Enabling DAC_OUT connects it to PA15; external signals on PA15 are not recommended during its use. IOMUX selects digital peripheral functions and controls input, output, and shutdown wake-up paths. Available features vary by pin.
- **Debugging and programming:** A two-wire serial wire debug interface provides debugging access. The boot strap loader supports UART or I2C programming and configuration, protected by a 256-bit user-defined password. It is enabled by default but can be disabled. Invocation can occur through a hardware condition, an unprogrammed reset vector and stack pointer, or an application command.
- **Factory information:** A read-only, memory-mapped FACTORY region contains device capabilities, identification, hardware revision, and factory trim data. Identification and revision information also appear in package markings.
- **Implementation:** TI recommends 10 µF and 0.1 µF supply decoupling capacitors near the supply pins, plus a 47 kΩ pullup and 10 nF pulldown capacitor on NRST. SYSOSC frequency correction requires an external 100 kΩ, 0.1% resistor with a temperature coefficient of 25 ppm/°C or better. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47 µF capacitor and must not connect to other circuits. Open-drain outputs require pullups to output high.
- **Development and support:** Resources include software libraries, examples, configuration tools, training, IDEs, compiler toolchains, documentation updates, and support forums. “X” identifies experimental devices; “MSP” identifies fully qualified production devices. TI recommends only qualified devices for production and appropriate ESD precautions.
- **Revisions and packaging:** The April 2025 revision updates peripheral descriptions, electrical specifications, operating-mode information, package options, and other details. Packaging guidance addresses dimensions, thermal-pad soldering, vias, stencil design, and material information. Automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions are listed.
- **Responsibilities:** Application guidance is not part of TI’s component specification. Customers are responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance; technical resources are provided “as is” and may change without notice.

The passage provides push-pull converter design guidance for Texas Instruments TPS7H500x-SP controllers, including component selection, protection, compensation, power supply requirements, and PCB layout.

- **Transformer:** The design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle below the controller’s 50% limit to accommodate efficiency effects and load transients. It uses a turns ratio of 2.5 and primary inductance of 40 μH rather than the calculated 33 μH. Magnetizing current was initially targeted at 6% of output current, balancing transformer size and efficiency.
- **Switching devices:** Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a maximum input of 36 V. Secondary synchronous rectifier GaN FETs are rated at 80 V despite approximately 20 V expected stress, allowing for transient spikes. Parallel Schottky diodes can reduce soft-start current through the FETs and reverse-conduction losses.
- **Clamp and output filter:** An RCD clamp limits switch-node voltage and requires optimization through testing. The selected output inductor is 0.47 μH, targeting 40% ripple current. Calculations require at least 1.3 mF output capacitance for ripple and load-transient limits; approximately 2.3 mF was used to help mitigate radiation-induced single-event transients. An additional output filter can reduce ripple, with damping added if necessary.
- **Protection and compensation:** Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A, using a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover frequency, with selected components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF. A 102-kΩ resistor sets slope compensation.
- **Controller supply:** Operation requires a regulated 4–14 V supply and at least 0.1 μF bypass capacitance between VIN and AVSS. Ceramic capacitors should be close to the controller; additional bulk capacitance is recommended for distant supplies.
- **PCB layout:** Keep sensitive signals away from switching nodes and magnetics, minimize switching-loop paths and switch-node copper area, separate analog and power grounds with a single-point connection, and use short, wide high-current traces. Bypass, filtering, and compensation components should be close to their associated pins.

The passage also lists supporting documentation, revision updates, ESD precautions, packaging information, and disclaimers. TI provides design resources without warranties and assigns product selection, application validation, testing, and compliance responsibilities to developers.

Eisenhower accepts the Republican nomination for President, endorses Nixon, and urges supporters to promote the administration’s record, register voters, and ensure turnout in November 1956.

He presents five reasons for calling Republicans the “Party of the Future”: adherence to long-term principles, attention to current and future problems, national unity, progress through individual initiative, and dedication to peace. He defends agricultural conservation and income policies, collective bargaining without government interference, and the preservation of state and local authority. He identifies education, infrastructure, housing, health, urban development, and peaceful atomic energy as priorities.

Eisenhower cites advances against discrimination while acknowledging continuing needs among older people, workers, farmers, American Indians, women, and small businesses. He advocates federal leadership combined with private initiative rather than centralized control.

For lasting peace, he outlines three requirements: maintaining American moral, economic, and military strength; strengthening collective security through international cooperation; and cautiously expanding exchanges with people under communist rule without weakening defenses. He also supports peaceful nuclear cooperation and effective disarmament measures. He concludes that cooperation among free Americans and friendly nations can produce greater prosperity, justice, understanding, and lasting peace.

The passage interprets statistical independence (SI) as the requirement that random sampling yield representative samples. In Bell experiments, this means measurement settings must not systematically select systems with different underlying properties. The authors define superdeterminism as systematic failure of this requirement, allowing theories to preserve local causality while explaining quantum correlations.

They distinguish three forms:
- **Fine-tuned initial conditions:** Deterministic theories produce correlations through atypical starting conditions.
- **Statistical flukes:** Unrepresentative observations arise through improbable event distributions in deterministic or indeterministic theories.
- **Nomic exclusion:** Physical laws prevent certain combinations of measurement settings and underlying states, concealing outcomes inconsistent with quantum predictions.

The authors argue that superdeterminism therefore need not involve determinism or fine-tuned initial conditions. They examine Leibnizian Quantum Mechanics as an example with simple but atypical initial conditions and a complex ontology, while questioning whether its SI violation has been adequately demonstrated under the frequency interpretation. Hypothetical “goblin” models illustrate how nomic exclusion could operate through local mechanisms without fine-tuning or flukes.

The passage also begins arguing that retrocausal theories need not violate SI when interpreted through causal rather than temporal order. It announces further arguments that invariant set theories are not necessarily superdeterministic, that some compatibilist accounts imply superdeterminism restricts free will, and that superdeterministic theories contain a conspiratorial element. The authors characterize superdeterminism as pre-scientific rather than necessarily destructive of scientific methodology.
