Anthony Scaramucci told ABC News that elements in Washington, including the White House, were trying to undermine and remove President Trump. Fired as communications director after 10 days following comments about Reince Priebus, Scaramucci said he had believed his recorded call with journalist Ryan Lizza was off the record.

Washington Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers after missing two games with a sprained left knee. Medically cleared Wednesday, he practiced fully all week and will wear a knee brace that he says does not restrict his movement.

Washington will again be without two of its top three receivers. Backup Marcus Mariota helped the offense score 61 points from scrimmage during Daniels’ absence. Daniels said he will not alter his playing style but acknowledged the importance of being smart about taking hits.

The passage outlines a moderately conservative Stay Rich Portfolio for wealth preservation, emphasizing that preserving wealth may require different strategies than building it. It distinguishes temporary market drawdowns from permanent capital loss and argues that no asset class avoids drawdowns over long periods.

The proposed approach uses liquid, broadly diversified ETFs, including US and foreign stocks, inflation-protected Treasury securities (TIPS), and corporate bonds. Global diversification is presented as a way to reduce, but not eliminate, drawdowns. TIPS provide inflation protection, while corporate bonds may offset their weaker performance during low inflation.

The portfolio has approximately 75% US and 25% foreign exposure, with additional international exposure through US companies. The passage references backtesting but provides no specific results or detailed asset weights.

The passage argues that revolutionary Communist regimes generate mass refugee flight through sweeping demands for social change, citing displacement of Chinese inhabitants in Vietnam and refugee figures from Marxist-governed countries. It contends that traditional autocracies offer greater prospects for gradual democratization than radical totalitarian regimes. It recommends U.S. support for incremental liberalization, except when governments face violent threats to survival, and warns that Marxist-led insurgencies are likely to produce totalitarian rule. It distinguishes democratic revolutionaries by their commitment to popular consent and elections, urges treating groups declaring hostility toward the United States as enemies, and rejects accusations of American racism, colonialism, genocide, and expansionism.

AAPL is Apple Inc.’s stock ticker on Nasdaq, where it began trading on December 12, 1980. Apple produces consumer electronics, software, and online services. The passage attributes the stock’s popularity to the company’s fundamentals, recognizable products, dividends, and share-price appreciation.

Investors can buy AAPL through brokers. Regular trading hours are 9:30 a.m.–4:00 p.m. ET, with trading also available before and after those hours. Shares do not expire and can be held indefinitely. Trading approaches include day trading, swing trading, scalping, and options, although the passage describes scalping and options trading as particularly difficult.

Trading requires market knowledge, analysis, discipline, and risk management. Strategies, indicators, and time frames should suit the trader’s abilities and risk tolerance. The passage recommends backtesting while noting that it is not foolproof, and warns that becoming wealthy through trading is difficult and unlikely.

Selling decisions should consider financial goals, valuation, diversification, company fundamentals, market conditions, taxes, and personal circumstances. Stock sales are subject to capital gains taxes, and dividends may face withholding taxes.

The passage reports an annual dividend of $0.82 per share, subject to board discretion, and an approximately 16.1% average return over the preceding five years.

Dutch-speaking Mechanical Engineer sought for a 12-month assignment in Genk, Belgium, starting within 1–4 weeks. Requires modelling, thermal and mechanical experience; chemical processing is an alternative industry background.

Biogetica partnered with Research Needs to conduct clinical trials and research on multidisciplinary natural medicine, including evaluating and combining plant medicines from different cultures. Plans for 2018 included trials and observational studies for HPV, herpes, trigeminal neuralgia, vertigo, tinnitus, and cataract. The partnership aims to validate Biogetica’s protocols through an evidence-based approach.

The NIH announced funding for 13 autism research teams, with a focus on environmental factors, although autism is considered mostly genetic. Researchers caution that measuring simultaneous environmental exposures is complex. The agency also announced an $87 million initiative supporting organoids, miniature cell cultures that mimic human organs, as part of efforts to reduce animal research.

The FDA approved Evita Solutions’ low-cost generic mifepristone, prompting opposition from anti-abortion groups and politicians aligned with the Trump administration. The company submitted its application four years earlier.

The Trump administration postponed for another year a policy addressing a loophole that allows drugmakers to avoid Medicare price negotiations by combining ingredients.

In an opinion piece, Boston University professor Shoumita Dasgupta argues that the administration’s autism rhetoric dehumanizes autistic people and echoes early 20th-century eugenic thinking.

SpaceX’s Falcon Heavy is targeting a February 6 launch at 1:30 p.m. Eastern, following a successful engine test. The company plans to land all three first-stage boosters. Despite the rocket’s capabilities, CEO Elon Musk is tempering expectations, acknowledging it might not reach orbit. SpaceX has received an FAA launch license, with February 7 as a backup date. Further delays could lead to indefinite postponement because federal funding expires February 8, and a government shutdown would prevent launches on government property.

Larry Connors and Cesar Alvarez’s Double Seven strategy buys when the close is above the 200-day moving average and at a seven-day low, then sells at a seven-day high. This mean-reversion strategy uses no stop loss.

Backtesting SPY since 1993 produced 154 trades, an average gain of 1.18%, an 82.5% win rate, and a 33% maximum drawdown versus 55% for buy-and-hold. Annualized growth was 6.3%, compared with buy-and-hold’s 10.1%, while market exposure was approximately 26%.

A broader ETF portfolio generated 1,189 trades averaging 0.63% before costs, with 6.3% annualized growth; almost all gains occurred before 2010. A SPY-and-QQQ portfolio failed because of overlapping trades. Shorting with the reversed strategy performed poorly on the S&P 500.

The article concludes that Double Seven still performs on major stock indices, but other mean-reversion strategies offer better results.

The passage argues that Andropov may favor an arms control agreement to constrain US defense programs, ease Soviet economic pressures, and counter domestic political competition. It recommends prioritizing INF negotiations, where timing provides US leverage, while sustaining the defense buildup. A private channel is preferred because of Andropov’s secrecy and concerns about leaks and ideological opposition within the US administration. The proposed opening is a brief letter acknowledging fundamental disagreements and renewed confrontation while expressing interest in peace and nuclear arms reductions, rather than presenting a complete proposal.

The lecture develops mathematical tools for physics in curved spacetime and derives the geodesic equation governing freely falling test bodies.

Covariant derivatives preserve tensorial transformation properties, while Lie derivatives describe transport along vector fields. Killing vectors characterize metric symmetries and connect to conserved quantities.

Tensor densities differ from tensors by determinant factors in their transformation laws. Multiplying a density of weight \(w\) by \(|g|^{w/2}\), where \(g\) is the metric determinant, converts it into a tensor. This constructs the Levi-Civita tensor and covariant volume elements.

The metric determinant also simplifies contracted Christoffel symbols:
\[
\Gamma^\mu_{\mu\alpha}=\partial_\alpha\ln\sqrt{|g|}.
\]
Consequently, a vector’s covariant divergence becomes
\[
\nabla_\alpha V^\alpha
=\frac{1}{\sqrt{|g|}}\partial_\alpha\!\left(\sqrt{|g|}V^\alpha\right),
\]
which facilitates Gauss-type integrals in curved spacetime. General tensor divergences retain additional connection terms, although antisymmetry can eliminate them in special cases. Local stress-energy conservation does not generally imply global energy-momentum conservation, because comparing vectors at different points requires transport that can be path dependent.

An ideal test body has mass but no charge, spin, or spatial extent. In a freely falling, locally Lorentz frame, it moves inertially. Geometrically, its trajectory parallel-transports its tangent vector, yielding
\[
\frac{d^2x^\mu}{d\lambda^2}
+\Gamma^\mu_{\alpha\beta}
\frac{dx^\alpha}{d\lambda}
\frac{dx^\beta}{d\lambda}=0.
\]
Charge interactions, finite size, and spin can introduce corrections to this leading description.

The equation uses an affine parameter, corresponding to uniformly spaced increments in a local Lorentz frame. Proper time is a suitable choice for timelike trajectories. Nonaffine parameterizations introduce a tangent-proportional term that can be removed by reparameterization; linear transformations preserve affine parameterization.

A second derivation uses a stationary-action principle based on accumulated proper time. It identifies timelike geodesics with extremal aging as well as generalized straight lines. Null trajectories and the derivation of conserved quantities from Killing vectors are deferred to subsequent discussion.

The Tennessee Biorepository and Integrative Genomics (BIG) Initiative links genomic data, electronic health records, and environmental information to support research involving underrepresented Mid-South populations. It has consented over 42,000 participants and collected more than 15,000 biosamples; 87% of participants are younger than 18.

Analysis of genetic data from 13,152 individuals identified substantial diversity: approximately 20% aligned with African reference populations and 30% had admixed ancestry. Ancestry showed geographic stratification, with African ancestry more common in urban areas and European ancestry in suburban regions, highlighting potential geographic confounding in association studies.

Researchers identified 6.8 million high-confidence variable sites, including 771,717 novel single-nucleotide variants absent from major reference databases. Novel variants were predominantly rare and ancestry-specific, with approximately twice the rate of predicted high-impact consequences compared with known variants. Ancestry-specific differences in rare deleterious variant burden require further investigation.

Minority groups had higher odds ratios for obesity and asthma. Preliminary geographic analyses found elevated prevalence of both conditions in three suburban areas around Memphis, suggesting an environmental component. Comparisons of self-reported race with inferred ancestry revealed discrepancies, including different racial identities among genetically related individuals, illustrating limitations of race as a proxy for genetic ancestry.

BIG incorporates community advisory boards and genomics education to support engagement. Future priorities include expanding recruitment across age groups toward 100,000 Tennesseans and adopting pangenomic analyses to better represent genetic diversity. The study is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed and should not guide clinical practice.

The study introduces a Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) framework to improve four-dimensional variational data assimilation (4D-Var), which estimates initial model states from sparse observations. The FNO learns an approximation to the inverse Hessian operator, using observations embedded through an adjoint-model calculation.

Experiments estimate initial conditions for a linear advection equation, with 5,400 training samples and 5,400 test samples spanning different background states, error correlations, and observation configurations. Although the standalone FNO generally produces less accurate estimates than conjugate gradient (CG), its predictions provide useful initializations for CG.

The combined FNO-CG method reduces average relative error by 62% and iteration count by 17% compared with standard CG initialized from the background state. Average relative error decreases from 0.0426 to 0.0161, while average iterations fall from 127 to 105. Improvements are most pronounced in ill-conditioned problems. Future work will extend the approach to nonlinear PDEs, particularly chaotic systems.

A commodity trading advisor (CTA) provides advice or manages investments involving futures, commodity options, forex contracts, or swaps. CTAs may manage individual accounts or operate managed futures funds. They must register with the CFTC and join the NFA, and typically charge management and performance-based fees.

Many CTAs use systematic trading algorithms based on technical indicators or fundamental data, while others use discretionary approaches. Trend following is the predominant strategy, seeking medium- to long-term trends. Momentum strategies may buy recent outperformers and sell recent underperformers across multiple asset classes.

The passage emphasizes combining strategies with low correlations rather than selecting solely for high returns. Such diversification can reduce portfolio volatility and improve risk-adjusted performance.

An illustrative backtest buys the S&P 500 when it closes above its 200-day moving average and exits below it. It produced a 6.73% compound annual growth rate versus 7.16% for buy-and-hold, with a maximum drawdown of 28%; dividends were excluded.

CTA strategies face potential losses, market volatility, unreliable data, capital requirements, and specialized knowledge needs. The passage argues that complexity does not necessarily improve results and that correlation and risk management are central to constructing a CTA portfolio.

Darren McGregor described Hibs’ 3-2 comeback victory over Rangers at Ibrox as “character-building,” praising his team’s determination amid an exceptionally loud atmosphere. Hibs recovered from an early deficit through Simon Murray’s equaliser, a James Tavernier own goal and Vykintas Slivka’s strike. McGregor supported Ryan Jack’s dismissal following an incident with Anthony Stokes, while acknowledging it benefited Hibs. He also praised Murray’s workrate and ten goals in seven competitive matches. Controversy over Neil Lennon’s celebration and refereeing decisions overshadowed Hibs’ performance.

Soccer coaches should prepare contingency plans rather than improvise when problems arise. Plans should be developed collaboratively with coaches, players and parents, documented, and communicated to everyone involved.

Key planning areas include:
- Routine and emergency communications, technology failures, cancellations, location changes and designated backups.
- Player health, injuries, eligibility, registration, financial hardship, behavior and responses to coaching.
- Practice adjustments, difficult parent interactions and varying field or weather conditions.
- Pre-game readiness, including officials, equipment, uniforms, player passes, medical authorizations and transportation.
- In-game emergencies, including injuries, hospital transport, severe weather, fighting, disciplinary decisions and coaching absences.
- Post-practice or post-game pickup and vehicle problems.
- Long-term coaching absences and succession planning.

Coaches should use “what if” questions and checklists, delegate responsibilities, ensure backups have necessary information and equipment, and teach players to prepare for contingencies. Because not every problem can be anticipated or controlled, ready assistance is essential.

Nova Scotia Community College faculty and support staff ratified six-year collective agreements covering 2014–2020, including a seven-per-cent wage increase. Faculty voted 55 per cent in favour, while support staff voted 64 per cent in favour.

Enron faced declining investor confidence amid losses, questions about its financial structure and an SEC inquiry into partnerships formerly overseen by CFO Andrew Fastow. A $1.01 billion charge contributed to a $618 million third-quarter loss, compared with a $292 million profit a year earlier. Enron replaced Fastow with Jeff McMahon to restore confidence, but analysts continued requesting greater transparency about off-balance-sheet transactions.

On October 25, 2001, Enron shares closed at $16.35, down approximately 80 percent for the year. Standard & Poor’s affirmed its ratings but changed its outlook to negative, citing reduced financial flexibility. Moody’s and Fitch placed Enron’s credit under review for possible downgrades. Investors also questioned approximately $3.3 billion in potential liabilities tied to affiliated entities.

Most major trading partners reported little or no change in dealings with Enron, despite heightened monitoring of credit exposure. EnronOnline maintained strong trading activity. Participants warned that disruption at Enron, which handled about one-quarter of U.S. power and natural-gas trading, could affect markets and counterparties.

Enron said it had sufficient operating funds and access to roughly $3.4 billion in bank credit lines. It planned asset sales to reduce debt. S&P reported no immediate liquidity threat or significant deterioration in trading operations, while warning that failure to strengthen the balance sheet could trigger a downgrade.

Kenneth Lay resigned from i2 Technologies’ board to concentrate on his renewed responsibilities as Enron CEO. Analysts differed over whether management changes and asset sales would restore confidence.

The passage specifies SD Memory Card operation, command handling, data transfer, protection, function switching, and timing requirements.

- **Identification and selection:** Hosts must use fOD frequency throughout Card Identification Mode and may use fPP during Data Transfer Mode. CMD9 retrieves card-specific data, while optional CMD4 configures driver stages. CMD7 selects one card for Transfer State; selecting another card deselects the previous one. Data communication is point-to-point between the host and selected card.

- **Reading and writing:** CMD17 reads a single block; CMD18 reads consecutive blocks until CMD12 stops transmission. CMD12 can abort reads and writes, and writes must be stopped before deselection. CRC checks protect transferred data, and failed write CRC checks prevent erroneous data from being programmed. Address, block-length, alignment, and write-protection violations generate errors. Multiple-block writes and pre-erasure settings through ACMD23 can improve write performance. ACMD22 reports the number of successfully written blocks.

- **Programming and busy states:** Cards may buffer block writes and indicate busy conditions by holding DAT0 low. Read and parameter-setting commands are prohibited during programming. Deselection does not terminate programming or erase operations, but resetting can terminate programming and destroy data. CMD13 reports card status and readiness for additional data.

- **Erase operations:** Erasure uses CMD32 and CMD33 to identify a range, followed by CMD38. Protected sectors remain intact. DISCARD permits partial or complete deallocation, with discarded contents treated as unspecified. Full User Area Logical Erase (FULE) logically erases the entire user area. DISCARD and FULE require support checks, apply only to SDHC and SDXC cards, and are unavailable through SPI. Their busy timeouts are 250 milliseconds and one second, respectively.

- **Write protection and passwords:** Protection methods include a host-enforced mechanical switch, optional internal write protection, and password locking. Locked cards permit specified control commands but prohibit data access. CMD42 manages passwords and locking; passwords persist across power cycles, and cards with passwords automatically lock at power-up. Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password (FEP). Setting FEP disables ordinary Force Erase and password clearing and requires COP Unlock after reset. FEP Force Erase requires the matching FEP, erases user data and the lock password, but preserves FEP. Force erase does not erase the secure area.

- **Bus width and function switching:** ACMD6 changes between one-bit and four-bit operation but is rejected while locked. CMD55 identifies the following command as application-specific when defined. CMD6 queries or switches functions, including access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Hosts must verify support, readiness, and power requirements before switching. The default power limit is 0.72 W. Optional High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires a one-to-one host-card connection.

- **Initialization and capacity differences:** CMD8 checks supply-voltage compatibility before ACMD41 during initialization. SDSC uses byte addressing and block lengths set by CMD16. SDHC and SDXC use block addressing with fixed 512-byte memory-access blocks and do not permit partial or misaligned accesses.

- **Clock, CRC, and timeout handling:** Hosts may slow or stop the clock subject to specified restrictions and must provide eight clocks after transactions before shutdown. CRC7 protects commands, most responses, and identification registers; CRC16 protects data blocks. Invalid commands or command CRC failures leave card state unchanged and set error status. Read and write timeouts depend on capacity type and operating mode. SDHC write busy is limited to 250 milliseconds; specified SDXC cases allow 500 milliseconds, and UHS-II allows one second after a Data Burst. Fixed write timeouts are recommended.

A TeamLease survey across nine cities found Delhi had the highest job loss risk, followed by Bengaluru and Hyderabad, while Pune had the lowest. Industrial manufacturing and allied sectors faced the greatest risk, followed by construction and real estate, and BPO and IT-enabled services. Healthcare and telecom ranked lowest in job loss risk.

This systematic review examines empirical evidence on the applications, evaluation methods, risks, and mitigation strategies associated with large language models (LLMs) in education. A PRISMA-guided search across five databases identified 69 studies published between 2023 and 2025; one additional study brought the total to 70. Three included studies addressed broader AI systems rather than LLMs specifically. Most studies evaluated GPT models, particularly GPT-3.5.

The review organizes educational applications into three categories:

- **Operational effectiveness:** Feedback generation, data processing, domain knowledge, and teaching capabilities. LLMs can complete many academic tasks and support instructional work, but studies report superficial understanding, inconsistent responses, hallucinations, knowledge limitations, and privacy concerns. Compared with educators, LLM-generated feedback often lacks contextual sensitivity, indirect guidance, and pedagogical depth. Human-like fluency can encourage excessive trust and complicate the identification of AI-generated assignments.
- **Personalized applications:** Grading, content generation, progress monitoring, and recommendations. Bias is the predominant reported risk. Studies identify differences in scores, instructional content, and recommendations associated with demographic characteristics, alongside cultural and linguistic misalignment. Some conventional bias-mitigation approaches fail to improve fairness or worsen disparities.
- **Interactive learning tools:** Student engagement, cognitive development, and academic performance. LLM assistance can improve task completion, grammatical accuracy, and some performance measures. However, these gains do not consistently translate into deeper learning. Reported risks include reduced verification, weaker critical thinking and reflection, memory difficulties, over-reliance, diminished motivation, and reduced student agency. Targeted assistance benefits some learners and tasks, while effects vary with learners’ competence and usage patterns.

Evaluation approaches include comparisons with human feedback and grading, statistical analyses, qualitative investigations, quasi-experimental classroom studies, surveys, linguistic analysis, and measures of neural activity. The review connects system-level shortcomings with their educational consequences and situates them within broader societal concerns, including unequal access and skills, data colonialism, environmental costs, and regulatory gaps.

Proposed safeguards involve multiple stakeholders. Educators should retain oversight, verify generated materials, protect sensitive information, establish clear usage policies, and emphasize higher-order learning. Developers should improve robustness, assess bias continuously, involve diverse stakeholders, and provide transparent, learner-centred systems. Students should verify outputs and use LLMs as support rather than substitutes for independent work. Governments should strengthen data governance and stakeholder collaboration.

The paper introduces a conceptual, not empirically validated, **Interaction–Monitoring–Outcome model** describing how risks can accumulate across learning cycles. It identifies opportunities for planning support, verification prompts, source transparency, reflection, and tools that make reliance patterns visible.

Limitations include the rapidly changing technology, English-language selection, and the predominance of short-term evidence. Future priorities include longitudinal research, cross-cultural comparisons, updated evaluation measures, and safeguards embedded in everyday educational use. The review argues that responsible implementation must support autonomy, meaningful learning, equity, transparency, and learner wellbeing rather than technical performance alone.

Low volatility investing focuses on stocks with smaller price fluctuations than the overall market, often identified by a beta below 1. These stocks commonly occur in utilities, consumer staples, and healthcare and may offer steadier returns and reduced risk.

Investors can implement the strategy through low volatility ETFs or mutual funds, or build diversified portfolios using historical price data and companies with stable earnings, consistent dividends, predictable businesses, and lower debt. Portfolios require periodic review and rebalancing, and the strategy generally needs a time horizon of years or decades.

The passage cites research showing that low volatility stocks have historically outperformed highly volatile stocks in U.S. and international markets. Kenneth French’s research found particularly poor performance among the most volatile stocks during market declines. Research on Berkshire Hathaway attributed its returns partly to leverage and selecting inexpensive, safe, high-quality stocks.

Low volatility investing still carries risks and can experience prolonged underperformance. Returns may be lower over some periods, backtests provide only estimates, and past performance does not guarantee future results. Suitability depends on investors’ financial goals and risk tolerance.

David Wybron, headteacher at Lord Williams’s School in Thame, is urging government action on examinations, teacher recruitment and funding. He argues that state school students face greater examination pressures than independent school pupils and calls for revised GCSE content and structures, with no league-table penalties for schools choosing IGCSEs. He says immigration controls hinder overseas recruitment and supports adding teachers in all subjects to the shortage occupation list. Despite planned funding increases, he says his school faces rising costs and will receive over £1,000 less per pupil than schools in well-funded authorities, before deprivation funding.

Players praise a retiring Swedish hockey star as a professional role model and an icon whose achievements include four Stanley Cups and seven Norris Trophies. Adam Larsson says young Swedish players look up to him. Henrik Tallinder calls him the best Swedish player in the league, praising his offensive and defensive abilities. Johan Hedberg highlights his consistency, durability and importance to his team over two decades. Tallinder also says he feels physically ready to play after practicing for two to three weeks, pending the coach’s decision.

VentureWire’s September 14, 2000 issue reports private-company financing, acquisitions, venture funds, and leadership changes.

- Inktomi agreed to acquire FastForward Networks for approximately $1.3 billion in stock. FastForward will become Inktomi’s media division, led by Abhay Parekh.
- Bertelsmann announced eBertelsmann, a venture fund targeting $1 billion for media, Internet, and technology investments.
- Algorithmics raised $60 million in second-round financing and acquired collateral-management software supplier Sentry Financial Systems for undisclosed terms.
- Artisan Entertainment launched Artisan Digital Media, including iArtisan, a fund planning to invest up to $50 million in rich-media technology companies.
- Privista raised $17 million in first-round funding and appointed Eric Gertler president and CEO.
- Other financing included $67.5 million for Pax Clearing, $51 million for Circadence, $27 million for Epoch Internet, $16 million for Industry to Industry, $12.5 million for OnePage, and $12 million each for Prefer Network and iMedica. The Triple RSI trading strategy is a mean-reversion approach inspired by Larry Connors’ R3 strategy. It uses four key variables, three based on RSI, with conditions involving RSI readings, the 200-day moving average, and entry and exit signals.

A backtest on SPY, the ETF tracking the S&P 500, produced 83 trades since 1993, averaging a 1.4% gain per trade with a profit factor of 5. The passage reports the win rate as both 90% and 91%.

The strategy trades infrequently. The passage suggests adjusting its rules to increase trading frequency or using it to complement a long-term buy-and-hold portfolio, potentially with a small amount of leverage in a margin account.

The ADS9803 is an eight-channel, 20-bit, 2MSPS data acquisition system with a built-in analog front end. Its configuration, operating modes, application guidance, and register descriptions include:

- **Data interface:** Supports two- or four-lane operation with single-data-rate or double-data-rate signaling, selected through SPI. Conversion results are transmitted most-significant-bit first in 24-bit packets. The ADC supplies data and capture clocks; clock frequency depends on sampling speed, data rate, and lane count.
- **Output processing:** An optional randomizer XORs conversion data with either its least significant bit or an appended PRBS bit to reduce interference associated with ground bounce. Simple averaging improves SNR while halving output data rate; moving averaging does not change output data rate.
- **Interface testing:** Fixed, digital-ramp, and alternating test patterns replace conversion data for debugging. Patterns are configured separately for channel groups CH[4:1] and CH[8:5].
- **Initialization and operation:** Register-write initialization is required after power-up or reset, with a free-running sampling clock connected. Normal operation also requires this clock. Speed-boost mode samples a selected channel pair at up to 8MSPS while the other six channels remain idle.
- **SPI configuration:** The device has three banks of 16-bit registers with 8-bit addresses. Bank 0 remains accessible regardless of bank selection. Multiple devices can share a daisy-chain SPI connection; register writes require 24 clock cycles per device.
- **Configurable functions:** Registers control data format, averaging, randomization, test patterns, speed boost, gain-error correction, analog bandwidth, power-down, reference selection, output lanes, and common-mode range. Reserved fields should retain their default values.
- **Application performance:** An ATE example reports post-calibration total unadjusted error of 0.0015% at 25°C ±5°C. Low-noise bandwidth reaches 22.7kHz, while wide-bandwidth operation reaches 700kHz and settles to 99.95% of full scale in 7.5µs for multiplexed signals.
- **Power and layout:** Three supplies—AVDD_5V, VDD_1V8, and IOVDD—require no specific power-up sequence. Guidance calls for separate supply decoupling, nearby bypass and reference capacitors, and separation of analog paths from digital lines and noise sources.
- **Support and limitations:** TI provides development resources, documentation notifications, and support forums. ESD precautions are recommended. Application guidance is outside the component specification; customers are responsible for component suitability, design validation, testing, and compliance.
Naughty Dog showcased Uncharted: The Lost Legacy, featuring Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross, at E3 2017. Its full team began development weeks after completing Uncharted 4: A Thief’s End.

Defensive tackles line up inside the defensive line and play key roles in stopping runs and pressuring quarterbacks. They penetrate the backfield, shed blocks, tackle ball carriers, and absorb double teams to free teammates to make plays. Their contributions often receive little statistical recognition.

Pass rushing is challenging because defensive tackles operate in tight spaces and frequently face multiple blockers. Their pressure can disrupt quarterbacks, free edge rushers, and allow defenses to keep more players in coverage rather than blitzing.

The position requires strength, agility, recognition, and toughness. Defensive tackles typically have thick, sturdy builds, with estimated heights of 6’2–6’4 and weights of 300–335 pounds. They may also be called nose tackles or nose guards, especially when aligned over the center.

Notable players include Aaron Donald, credited with three NFL Defensive Player of the Year awards, and “Mean” Joe Greene, who earned two such awards and helped Pittsburgh win four Super Bowls.

Machine-learning models offer efficient alternatives to computationally costly Density Functional Theory for material-property prediction, but their performance depends on crystal representations. Existing graph-based approaches—including pairwise, angular, and periodic-vector encodings—can map distinct crystal structures to identical representations because local encodings fail to capture long-range interactions.

The passage introduces PRDNet, a framework combining graph embeddings with learned pseudo-particle diffraction representations in reciprocal space. Unlike conventional probes with fixed form factors, its learned probe incorporates chemical-environment dependence to better distinguish atoms and structural environments. The framework generates synthetic diffraction patterns invariant to crystal rotations, reflections, and translations.

Crystals are described through atomic types, positions, and periodic lattice vectors. Diffraction maps atomic arrangements into reciprocal space through structure factors, providing information about periodic structural directions. PRDNet uses this information to capture long-range correlations for crystal-property regression and classification.

Evaluations on Materials Project, JARVIS-DFT, and MatBench reportedly show state-of-the-art performance across multiple crystal-property prediction tasks.

Funding concerns affected 40.1 percent of surveyed manufacturers, while small-firm activity contracted. Renewed U.S. tariff threats added uncertainty. Services growth edged higher, while construction growth slowed. Economists expected China’s economic growth to decline to 6.5 percent in 2018 from 6.9 percent in 2017.

MIT and the Carnegie Institution for Science released nearly 61,000 measurements of over 1,600 nearby stars to help the public search for exoplanets. Gathered over 20 years at Hawaii’s W.M. Keck Observatory, the dataset includes open-source software and an online tutorial. The passage introduces Truthful Text Summarization (TTS), a framework designed to improve LLM-generated summaries while encouraging sources to report truthfully. It argues that summarization systems must address source incentives alongside hallucinations, conflicting claims, and adversarial manipulation.

TTS evaluates sources before generating a final summary. For each source, it constructs atomic claims using only other documents, extracts whether sources support, contradict, or abstain on those claims, and scores informative peer agreement. The scoring rule rewards agreement on the same claim while subtracting agreement across different claims, discounting generic overlap. Sources below an inclusion threshold are filtered out. Visibility in the resulting summary, rather than monetary payments, provides the incentive.

Under stated assumptions—including independent claim blocks and a positive average informative peer margin—the analysis shows that truthful reporting maximizes expected scores. It establishes asymptotic informed truthfulness, stronger guarantees against significant deviations under additional conditions, and finite-sample bounds that improve as the number of claims increases.

Experiments use 300 queries each from Natural Questions and ClashEval, with generated source pools containing four reliable and two unreliable documents per query. TTS achieves answer accuracy of 70.7% on Natural Questions and 74.3% on ClashEval, compared with 34.0% and 14.0% for the majority-claims baseline. It also improves claim-level precision, recall, and F1 scores. Additional tests show decreasing scores as truthful sources flip more stances and near-zero scores for coordinated, uninformative sources.

The authors propose future extensions involving reputation priors, retrieval integration, and multilingual or streaming settings.

The Opportunity Project (TOP), a nonprofit serving about 600 children ages 1 to 5 at three centers in Wichita and Derby, provides early education for children living in poverty and support for their families.

A study published in the Journal of Research in Childhood Education found that TOP graduates outperformed comparable children who had not attended TOP in academics, social skills and attendance at nearly every grade level studied. Graduates were 19 percent more likely to read at grade level by third grade and 107 percent more likely by eighth grade.

TOP uses a child-directed learning approach, offers scholarships through public and private funding, and connects families with food, clothing, health care and educational assistance. Its Parent Cafe workshops cover childhood development, community resources and school advocacy.

Single father William Eckels credits TOP with educating both his son and himself. After attending workshops, he advocated for high-quality preschool with Kansas Gov. Sam Brownback and began considering an education degree.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture improves gaming, professional visualization, and data-center workloads through enhanced shading, ray tracing, AI processing, memory bandwidth, and storage access. NVIDIA reports up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI compared with the previous generation.

- **DLSS and ray tracing:** DLSS uses Tensor Cores and a neural network to combine details from multiple frames into images comparable to native resolution while improving performance. Ampere’s third-generation Tensor Cores and 9x Super Resolution scaling enable 8K gaming at 60 fps in supported ray-traced games. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance and accelerate ray-traced motion blur.
- **GDDR6X memory:** Developed with Micron, GDDR6X uses four-level PAM4 signaling to transmit two bits per clock edge. GA10x implementations support rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec. Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding addresses signal-quality challenges. Error Detection and Replay retries failed memory transactions, potentially revealing excessive overclocking through plateauing performance, though crashes remain possible.
- **RTX IO:** Working with Microsoft DirectStorage, RTX IO enables GPU-based asset loading and lossless decompression, reducing CPU workloads and storage bottlenecks. It supports faster loading, texture streaming, and access to large rendering datasets. NVIDIA reports up to 100x higher I/O performance compared with hard drives and traditional storage APIs.
- **Professional GPUs:** The A40 targets data-center visual computing, simulation, AI, and virtual workstations. It includes 48GB of memory, expandable to 96GB across two GPUs using NVLink, and supports NVIDIA vGPU software and the EGX platform. The RTX A6000 provides 48GB of GDDR6 for professional workstations, with similar dual-GPU memory expansion, hardware-accelerated motion blur, and AI denoising.
- **Displays and video:** Ampere supports 4K at 120Hz and 8K at 60Hz through advanced display interfaces, including HDMI 2.1 and DisplayPort 1.4a. Fifth-generation NVDEC provides hardware decoding for multiple codecs, including AV1 at up to 8K60 HDR with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads video encoding and supports H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K.
- **GeForce models:** The RTX 3090 uses GA102 with 10,496 CUDA cores and 24GB of GDDR6X. The RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, supports GA10x architectural features except NVLink, and is described as outperforming the RTX 2080 Ti.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change and provides the materials without warranties, placing responsibility for application suitability and testing on customers.

In his farewell address, President Truman welcomes the peaceful transfer of power to General Eisenhower and urges Americans to support their new president regardless of party. He reflects on the presidency’s responsibilities and his succession after Franklin Roosevelt’s death in April 1945, including decisions concerning the United Nations, the atomic bomb, and the transition from war to peace.

Truman identifies the Cold War as the dominant issue of his presidency. He credits international cooperation, economic assistance, and defense alliances with strengthening the free world and preventing another world war. He highlights resistance to Soviet pressure in Iran, assistance to Greece and Turkey, the Marshall Plan, the Berlin airlift, and intervention in Korea. He describes the Korean intervention as his most important presidential decision, arguing that resisting aggression there prevented greater conflict later.

Rejecting calls for all-out or atomic war, Truman emphasizes peace, justice, and freedom as American goals. He expresses confidence that a stronger, more united free world will eventually bring change within the Soviet system. He envisions scientific advances and peaceful development reducing poverty and suffering worldwide.

Domestically, Truman points to high employment, improved incomes, insured-bank stability, and growing awareness of civil rights. He concludes that he has done his best in public service and thanks Americans for their support in strengthening the free world and preserving peace.

The March 2006 specification update documents hardware issues, implications, and workarounds for the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device, silicon revision A3. Issues affect timers, interrupts, DMA, storage, power management, USB, UARTs, LPC, SMBus, GPIO, and debugging features.

- **Timers and interrupts:** PIT behavior differs from expected counter-latch and count-loading operation. Automatic end-of-interrupt handling can generate duplicate interrupts. PIC clock gating can cause missed interrupts and system hangs. Simultaneous interrupt requests can delay SSMIs, making CS5535-generated synchronous traps unreliable.
- **DMA and storage:** UART accesses during block or demand DMA can be discarded or return all ones; LPC I/O is also unreliable during these DMA modes. Single-transfer DMA is recommended. UDMA writes can suffer CRC errors following certain host-terminated reads; the documented workaround uses UDMA I/O blocking. IDE command packets should precede bus-master enable. ATAC drivers should use DWORD-aligned PRD addresses to avoid hangs.
- **Prefetching:** ATA and audio PRD prefetching can introduce errors when software changes descriptors during active transfers. ATA descriptors should be defined before operation, and audio descriptor changes should remain at least two tables ahead.
- **Power management:** Several wake inputs do not work from ACPI S3; PWRBTN# is the recommended alternative. Byte accesses to PM1_EN and PM1_STS hang, while incorrectly sized PMC writes can corrupt register contents. Sleep-control delays must be shorter than PM_SED to restore external circuitry and PCI/IDE signaling. LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to record a low-battery event.
- **Clock gating:** USB register reads can fail when controller clock gating is enabled. UART CEIR operation and GLIU statistics-generated ASMIs also have clock-gating limitations.
- **Interfaces:** PCI I/O addresses at or above 10000h can hang the system and should not be used. USB requires external over-voltage protection. LPC-to-ISA bridge transactions may abort prematurely; a programmable-logic workaround is described. The SMB NEGACK issue requires a two-write clearing sequence. GPIO high-bank feature registers require full-register read-modify-write operations after suspend.
- **Emulation and debugging:** Keyboard emulation status and snoop-mode behavior require software workarounds. The debug port hangs the system and should not be used; several other debug features fail without operational impact.

Some issues have no resolution, while others are described as having negligible, diagnostic-only, or no expected real-world impact.

Seattle’s Smith Tower is automating its manually operated elevators after 103 years. Owner Unico Properties says the modernization will improve safety, reliability, accessibility and service while preserving the elevators’ historic appearance, including ornate glass doors.

Work began in June, and operators will no longer be required by mid-2018. Unico plans to retain at least one operator to honor the building’s history and says existing operators will be supported during and after the transition.

Hamilton Beale, an elevator operator since 1999, plans to return to Virginia to be closer to family, partly because of automation. He says he will most miss the tenants. Tenant Hal Mueller describes the operators’ familiar greetings and the elevators’ distinctive operation as valued parts of working in the building.

The executrices of Diedrick Grafing’s estate sought to recover $2,000 deposited in his name in trust for Catharine Heilmann, arguing that he intended to retain ownership during his lifetime and have Heilmann distribute the funds after his death.

The court upheld the trust. Grafing’s retention of the bank books and use of the interest during his lifetime were consistent with creating a valid trust. Payment of part of the funds to Heilmann recognized her ownership; there was no evidence of a loan. The transaction was a trust, not a gift, and postponing receipt until Grafing’s death would not make it testamentary because Heilmann’s interest vested when the deposits were made.

Any persons claiming that Heilmann had promised to distribute funds to them had to pursue their own remedies against her. The judgment dismissing the executrices’ complaint was affirmed, with costs.

- Command legality depends on whether a command is accepted in the card’s current state. Hosts should ignore APP_CMD status in CMD11 and CMD3 responses following ACMD41.

- **Function switching:** CMD6 switches or expands card functions and is mandatory for cards compliant with specification Version 1.10 or later. It operates in Transfer State and supports six function groups, with four defined for access mode, command system, driver strength, and power limit. Only one function per group can be active. Mode 0 queries support and maximum current/power consumption; Mode 1 changes functions. Function 0 selects defaults, while 0xF preserves the current selection. Invalid Mode 1 selections cancel all requested changes; busy functions retain their current settings.

- CMD6 returns an R1 response and a 512-bit status block containing supported functions, selections, consumption information, and busy status. Hosts should verify power capability before switching and use Mode 0 to check readiness. Functions return to defaults through a power cycle, CMD0, or appropriate CMD6 selections. Switching completes within eight clocks after the status data ends; a status-data CRC error requires a power cycle.

- **Power and interface modes:** The default power limit is 0.72 W and may restrict performance. Hosts select higher limits according to supply, thermal, and connector capabilities. UHS-II requires Power Limit support, does not use the access-mode or driver-strength groups, and optionally supports command-system extension. Optional High-Speed mode provides a 25 MB/s interface using a 50 MHz clock and requires a one-to-one host/card connection.

- **Initialization and addressing:** CMD8 checks supply-voltage compatibility for Version 2.00 or later cards and must precede ACMD41 in Idle State. Compatible cards echo the voltage range and check pattern in R7; incompatible cards remain idle without responding. ACMD41’s CCS bit distinguishes SDSC from SDHC/SDXC. SDSC uses byte addressing and CMD16-controlled block lengths; SDHC/SDXC memory accesses use fixed 512-byte blocks and do not support partial or misaligned access.

- **Clocking and error protection:** Hosts may reduce or stop the bus clock subject to specified restrictions, including eight additional clocks after transactions. During ACMD41 initialization, hosts must provide continuous 100–400 kHz clocking or poll at intervals below 50 ms when stopping the clock. CRC7 protects commands, most responses, and CID/CSD registers; CRC16 protects data blocks, separately on each data line in wide-bus mode. Commands with CRC errors or illegal commands receive no response, leave card state unchanged, and set error-status bits.

- **Timeouts:** SDSC read and write timeouts depend on access/program timing, capped at 100 ms and 250 ms respectively. SDHC/SDXC reads require a minimum 100 ms host timeout. SDHC write busy periods are limited to 250 ms; specified SDXC cases allow 500 ms. UHS-II permits up to one second of busy time after a Data Burst. Hosts are strongly advised to use write timeouts exceeding 500 ms. Erase timeouts should use SD Status parameters when available.

- **Commands and status:** Commands have a fixed 48-bit format, and supported command classes are recorded in CSD. Application-specific commands are preceded by CMD55. UHS-II changes several command behaviors and normally uses packet transfer length to end transfers. Cards provide Card Status, 512-bit SD Status, and queued Task Status. SD Status reports performance classes, allocation-unit sizes, erase parameters, and performance-enhancement support.

- **Recording performance:** Speed Class, UHS Speed Grade, and Video Speed Class support real-time recording; all three methods are optional in Version 6.00. Allocation Units (AUs) divide the user area, and Recording Units (RUs) subdivide AUs without crossing their boundaries. Performance requirements account for sequential writes, reads, fragmentation where supported, and filesystem updates. Class 10 performance is defined only for entirely free AUs.

- SDXC Speed Class recording requires sequential writes to completely free AUs, supports AU sizes up to 64 MB, and measures larger AUs in 4 MB subunits. CMD20 distinguishes recording, directory updates, and Continuous Information updates. UHS Speed Grades 1 and 3 require at least 10 MB/s and 30 MB/s respectively; higher grades must satisfy lower-grade requirements.

Toronto Blue Jays star Vladimir Guerrero Jr. comes from a family with extensive baseball connections. Born in Montreal in 1999, he moved to the Dominican Republic with his mother, Riquelma Ramos, as a child and spent summers with his father in the United States.

Guerrero Jr. married Nathalie Guerrero in March 2023 after five years of dating. They have two daughters, Vlaimel and Vlaishel, born in 2017 and 2018. He has cited Vlaimel’s affection for Toronto as a major reason for signing his contract there.

Father and son have each won an All-Star Game MVP award and a Home Run Derby, hit postseason grand slams and recorded 40-home-run seasons.

Other family baseball connections include:

- **Half-brother Vladi Miguel Guerrero:** Joined the New York Mets organization in 2024.
- **Uncle Wilton Guerrero:** A former MLB player whom Guerrero Jr. credits with teaching him baseball.
- **Uncle Julio Guerrero:** Played four minor-league seasons in Boston’s system.

The 123 reversal pattern is a three-swing price formation indicating a potential trend reversal. A bearish pattern develops when an uptrend forms a lower high and then breaks below the preceding swing low. A bullish pattern, also called a 123 bottom, develops when a downtrend forms a higher low and then breaks above the preceding swing high.

Trading rules include:
- Entering at the breakout bar’s close or the next bar’s opening after price breaks point 2; a large breakout bar may warrant waiting for a retest.
- Placing a stop loss beyond point 3, or beyond point 1 in highly volatile markets.
- Estimating a profit target by measuring the distance between point 2 and the midpoint of the line connecting points 1 and 3, then projecting that distance from the breakout point. Partial profits and trailing stops are alternatives.

The pattern can be applied to stocks, forex, commodities, and Bitcoin. Its somewhat subjective rules make backtesting difficult. Tests on the gold ETF GLD found that a bullish strategy with a 20-day exit had a profit factor of 2.22; the bearish strategy performed worse. The passage describes the results as somewhat promising and suggests additional parameters could improve performance.

Hajime, a rival to Mirai malware, has infected an estimated 100,000 IoT devices worldwide. Both exploit weak usernames and passwords, but Hajime uses a decentralized peer-to-peer network, making it harder to disrupt than Mirai’s command-server-based botnets. Researchers have observed no Hajime DDoS attacks, and its operators and purpose remain unknown. Hajime infects ARM-based devices, while Mirai variants target more platforms. Their overlapping targets have created competition, limiting some of Mirai’s expansion. Researchers recommend patching vulnerable devices, but inconsistent vendor support means both malware threats could persist unless affected devices are retired.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, and AI-based processing through a hybrid rendering model. Its principal features include:

- **Ray tracing acceleration:** Dedicated RT Cores perform Bounding Volume Hierarchy traversal and ray–triangle intersection testing, freeing other GPU resources for shading and computation. Combined with denoising and hybrid rendering, these cores enable real-time reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. The passage reports approximately tenfold ray tracing performance compared with Pascal.
- **AI-based graphics:** NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores to accelerate pretrained neural networks. Features include Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), image inpainting, slow-motion frame interpolation, and image or video upscaling. Standard DLSS targets image quality similar to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X prioritizes higher image quality.
- **Geometry and shading improvements:** Mesh shading introduces cooperative task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rates within 16-by-16-pixel screen regions, enabling content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading stores and reuses shading results independently of screen-space visibility calculations.
- **Multi-view rendering and VR:** Turing supports up to four hardware-rendered views per pass, with up to 32 views at the API level. This supports stereo displays, wider-field-of-view headsets, shadow rendering, and other multi-view workloads. USB-C and VirtualLink hardware support combines headset power, display, and data connections into one connector.
- **Video processing:** The enhanced NVENC encoder supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 frames per second, with bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit decoding and supports VP9 10/12-bit HDR.
- **GPU interconnection:** TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI, providing total bidirectional bandwidth of 100 GB/s and 50 GB/s respectively. Three-way and four-way SLI are unsupported; TU106 supports neither NVLink nor SLI.
- **Products and resource management:** TU104 is used in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and the inference-focused Tesla T4. TU106 powers GeForce RTX 2070. Turing also supports expanded bindless resource access and more flexible resource heaps.

The passage introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted performance metric incorporating Tensor, FP32, ray tracing, and integer operations. It also explains how ray tracing, acceleration structures, and denoising work together to improve lighting effects while limiting computational demands. NVIDIA’s accompanying notices disclaim warranties, limit liability, and reserve the right to change specifications.

Assuming the Presidency under extraordinary circumstances without having been elected to the office, the speaker asks Americans for their prayers and pledges to serve all people. He emphasizes constitutional legitimacy, bipartisan cooperation, and addressing urgent national needs, and plans to consult Congress on priorities. He promises openness, honesty, and an uninterrupted pursuit of peace while maintaining American strength.
