The disclosure describes cooperative monitoring networks that temporarily connect otherwise independent monitoring systems to monitor and respond to events across multiple properties or a wider community.

A monitoring application server, central alarm station server, or monitoring control units may detect an event at an individual system, evaluate it against associated rules, and select other systems to participate. Selection may depend on geographic proximity, camera coverage, occupancy, user preferences, and participant consent. Participating systems can share sensor data, images, video, and alerts, while coordinating cameras, lighting, and other devices.

Applications include tracking intruders, locating missing people or animals, responding to medical emergencies, and assisting mobile users who activate a panic button. Networks may expand through cascading notifications until someone acknowledges responsibility for an alarm. They may also add or remove monitoring systems as an entity moves, using image recognition and, in some implementations, machine-learning route predictions. Public cameras and street lighting may participate.

Combined data can help distinguish property-specific problems from wider events, including power failures, telephone outages, radio-frequency communication failures, and abnormal solar-panel output. Different classifications may produce different responses, including identifying possible jamming or treating shared abnormalities as false alarms.

Users may configure event definitions, responses, potential participants, and network adaptation rules through an interface. Cooperative networks may be modified according to event location and timing or disbanded when an issue is resolved, tracking is lost, or related and unrelated events can no longer be adequately distinguished. The techniques may be implemented through hardware, software, firmware, or combinations of these.

On November 27, 2000, Jennifer Cutaia forwarded a widely circulated chain email about a purported seven-year-old named Amy Bruce. The message claims she has severe lung cancer from secondhand smoke and a brain tumor from repeated beatings, and that her family cannot afford treatment. It urges recipients to forward it, claiming the Make A Wish Foundation will donate seven cents for every name on the list.

The passage advocates expanded education and vocational training on Indian reservations, emphasizing English proficiency, individual aptitudes, and native industries. It calls for adequate pay, high standards, and strong penalties for misconduct among government officials dealing with Indians. It praises scientific agricultural assistance, including disease prevention, new crops, range restoration, and improved fruit storage and shipping. It recommends support for Smithsonian museum plans and preservation of records and threatened animals. Washington should model effective sanitation, housing, charitable and correctional systems, and labor legislation. Proposed protections include employer-liability laws, railroad safety requirements, and improvements to the 1893 safety-appliance law.

The UCLA High Post Rub Offense contributed to John Wooden’s championship teams and is used at all basketball levels. Built on court spacing and coordinated execution, it combines inside and outside attacks and suits teams with a skilled passing and shooting post player rather than a traditional low-post specialist. A 1–4 alignment is favored against pressure defenses, with interchangeable positions and entries from either side.

The basic action begins with a point guard passing to a wing and cutting off a high-post screen for a layup or post-up. Counters depend on defensive positioning:
- Against trailing defenders, the guard cuts toward the basket.
- Against outside denial, the guard cuts inside.
- Against defenders going behind the screen, the guard pops out for a shot.
- Against show-and-recover coverage, the screener slips toward the basket.
- Against switches, players exploit mismatches through post rolls or perimeter isolation.

Low-post options include power layups, baby hooks, face-up attacks, lobs against fronting, and pressure releases against double teams. Post feeds can also lead to two-player cutting actions or post splits.

If the initial action produces no good shot, the offense moves into quick ball reversal and down screens. Players counter defensive coverage with curls, baseline fades, back cuts, screen-and-roll actions, slips, or isolation opportunities. Denied passing lanes create additional options through dribble clears, backdoor cuts, high-post feeds, lobs, and alternative entries.

Implementation emphasizes footwork, timing, communication, defensive reads, and coordination among passer, screener, and receiver. Suggested preparation includes breakdown drills, scrimmages, and individual skill development. Coaches should scout opponents, monitor defensive adjustments, vary alignments and entries, and attack weaker defenders.

Troll Cakes, a New York City bakery/detective agency, anonymously sends chocolate chip brownie cakes decorated with internet trolls’ insults to the commenters. Cakes cost $35 to make and ship, plus $25 if the company must locate the recipient’s address. Its $30 “Tiny Hands Special” sends a cake featuring a chosen Trump tweet to the White House.

The speaker hopes team depth will limit the impact of Dallas’s heat and emphasizes correcting mistakes after a loss. The team succeeded in the first game by getting the puck deep, but struggled through the neutral zone in the second, allowing Dallas’s transition attack to create scoring opportunities and neutralize its speed. Consistent puck placement, cycling, finishing checks and winning individual battles are identified as priorities. The speaker notes a tendency to abandon effective habits after dominant wins despite repeated discussions. Strong road play has helped throughout the playoffs, with the team staying relaxed and doing small things needed to win. Returning to a simple, consistent approach is emphasized.

Travis Zajac emphasized creating more traffic and shots against a quick goalie, elevating play to secure a first win, and drawing confidence from previous series comebacks against Florida and the Rangers. He stressed focusing on winning the next game.

The speaker describes entering a Stanley Cup final with five minutes remaining, gaining confidence through saves, and making a mistake by holding the puck too long. They emphasize preparation and believe they can help the team.

This study examined associations between maternal and child gut microbiomes and early childhood neurodevelopment in 116 mother–child pairs from the Vitamin D Antenatal Asthma Reduction Trial. Researchers analyzed stool microbial composition, metabolites, and short-chain fatty acids collected during the third trimester of pregnancy and from children at 3–6 months, one year, and three years. Neurodevelopment was assessed annually from ages one to three using the Ages and Stages Questionnaire, covering communication, motor, problem-solving, and personal-social skills.

The maternal gut microbiome showed stronger associations with children’s first-year neurodevelopment than either the infant or one-year child microbiome. Maternal microbial composition predicted first-year developmental scores with an average cross-validation Q² of approximately 0.21, compared with approximately 0.096 for infant microbial composition. Predictive power generally weakened for second-year development, and neither maternal nor child microbiomes predicted third-year outcomes.

Children’s gut microbiota became increasingly similar to their mothers’ with age, but this similarity did not correspond to stronger developmental associations. Some shared microbial taxa, including Fusobacteriia and Fusobacteriota, showed divergent associations with developmental scores when measured in mothers versus infants, suggesting potentially different prenatal and postnatal roles.

The findings suggest pregnancy may be an important period for microbiome–neurodevelopment associations. Limitations include the small sample, limited pregnancy sampling, and very low abundance of some implicated bacteria. Larger studies, validation, and mechanistic research are needed. The passage is a preprint that had not been peer reviewed.

Researchers found that 14 of Centaurus A’s 16 satellite galaxies orbit in a common plane, contrary to the random orbital directions predicted by the lambda cold dark matter model. Located 13 million light-years away, this is the first such observation outside the Local Group. Study author Marcel Pawlowski suggested the finding could indicate missing elements in simulations or flaws in the model. Other astrophysicists argue that these arrangements may be statistical anomalies and that replacing the model would require stronger evidence. Large-scale dark matter filaments offer another possible explanation. Observations of more distant galaxies could help determine whether these orbital patterns extend beyond local exceptions.

Andrew Lo reviews alternatives to net present value (NPV) for capital budgeting while recommending NPV as the primary decision criterion. Adjusted present value (APV) incorporates additional considerations such as taxes, project interactions, strategic alternatives, and optionality.

- **Payback period** measures how long an investment takes to recover its initial cost. It ignores the time value of money and cash flows after repayment. Discounted payback addresses the first problem but not the second. Payback can highlight uncertainty, liquidity needs, and managers’ career concerns, although these issues should be incorporated more explicitly into valuation.
- **Profitability index** divides the present value of future cash flows by the initial investment. An index above one indicates positive NPV, but ranking mutually exclusive projects by this measure can be misleading because it ignores scale.
- **Internal rate of return (IRR)** is the discount rate that makes NPV zero. It can agree with NPV under specified conditions, including an initial outflow followed by nonnegative cash flows, evaluation of a single project, and a constant opportunity cost of capital used as the hurdle rate. Otherwise, IRR may have no real solution, multiple solutions, or misleading rankings. Borrowing arrangements require reversing the usual preference for higher IRRs. IRR also ignores scale and is widely used in bonds and private equity.

Lo emphasizes that return-based investment theory assumes investors are small enough not to affect prices or returns. Corporate projects and very large investments can violate this assumption: increasing investment may reduce returns. Capital budgeting therefore requires attention to dollar value and investment scale.

Recommended practices include accepting positive-NPV projects, choosing the highest NPV among mutually exclusive alternatives, evaluating project interactions separately, using after-tax cash flows rather than accounting earnings, and applying risk-adjusted discount rates that reflect changes in risk over time. More advanced analysis addresses competitive responses, capital constraints, and allocation across multiple years. Political, social, cultural, and implementation considerations also influence decisions and cannot be replaced by financial analysis alone.

The lecture then introduces efficient markets and the importance of understanding when market prices can be trusted. Lo describes a study of stock-price reactions to the Challenger disaster: Morton Thiokol’s shares suffered the largest sustained decline on the day of the explosion, months before an official report identified its O-ring as the cause. He presents this as an example of markets aggregating information rapidly, while noting that subsequent discussion will examine failures of market efficiency.

Michael Barnard argues that hurricanes and wildfires will increase voter acceptance of climate change and its political importance. He predicts migration from affected areas will alter voting patterns, weaken Republican electoral advantages and benefit Democrats. Barnard contends that continued warming and extreme weather will intensify these shifts, eventually removing Republicans from leadership unless they change their position on climate change.

Offensive corner kicks should include a planned play, a designated target, and an appropriate service from a selected kicker. Coaches should choose options suited to players’ abilities.

Common types include:
- **Far post:** A lofted kick targeting a strong header, with inward or outward curve.
- **Near post:** An accurate delivery exploiting weak near-post defense; the receiver may shoot or redirect it.
- **Medium:** A lofted delivery into central areas to challenge defenders or the goalkeeper.
- **Top-of-the-arc:** A pull-back delivery to space 18 yards from goal, allowing a shot or pass.
- **Short:** A pass to a nearby teammate, often intended to draw defenders away before a cross.
- **Skip header:** A near-post receiver flicks the ball across goal toward a back-post target.
- **Direct score:** A bending kick intended to enter the goal untouched; rarely attempted or successful.
- **Floated-ball:** A high delivery near the center of goal that tests the goalkeeper’s ability to claim it.

Kickers need suitable distance, height, and accuracy; receivers often need aggressiveness and heading ability. Coaches should teach all players the positions and movements, progressing from unopposed practice to live defenders and game conditions.

Teams should adjust for strong wind, coordinate signals and timing, prepare for rebounds and clearances, and guard against counterattacks. The original kicker cannot touch the ball again until another player does.

On June 10, 2015, Tesla Motors, Inc. and Tesla Motors Netherlands B.V. entered into a $500 million senior secured asset-based revolving credit agreement with seven banks. Subject to conditions, commitments may increase to $750 million. The agreement includes a $100 million letter-of-credit subfacility and a $40 million swingline loan subfacility.

Proceeds may fund working capital and general corporate purposes. The facility matures June 10, 2020, and had no outstanding borrowings at closing. Availability depends on eligible inventory, receivables and equipment, less reserves. Borrowings carry floating interest rates plus margins of 1% for LIBOR loans or 0% for base-rate loans; unused commitments carry a 0.25% annual fee.

The borrowers guaranteed obligations and pledged specified assets as collateral. The agreement includes reporting requirements, restrictions on dividends, debt, liens and stock repurchases, and a minimum fixed-charge coverage ratio under certain circumstances. Defaults may permit lenders, subject to customary cure rights, to demand immediate repayment and foreclose on collateral.

Microsoft Corporation’s Form 8-K dated April 24, 2019, reports that the company issued a press release announcing financial results for the fiscal quarter ended March 31, 2019. The release is furnished as Exhibit 99.1. The report and exhibit are not deemed “filed” for purposes of Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act and are not incorporated by reference into other filings unless expressly specified. Chief Accounting Officer Frank H. Brod signed the report.

Workers in Gainesville, Florida, began removing the Confederate statue “Old Joe” after months of relocation efforts. It will be returned to the United Daughters of the Confederacy. Near Tampa, authorities reported red paint and derogatory comments at a Confederate memorial park. Hillsborough County commissioners also planned to discuss relocating a separate monument, amid broader debates and recent violence in Charlottesville, Virginia.

A longitudinal study examined pneumococcal carriage and household transmission among 121 adults aged 60–86 from 61 households during 2020–2022. Participants provided saliva samples every two weeks over 10 weeks; 62 participated in both study seasons. Culture-enriched saliva was tested using qPCR, with the piaB gene used to determine pneumococcal positivity.

Overall, 52 of 1,088 tested samples (4.8%) were positive, and 27 participants (22.3%) carried pneumococcus at least once. Carriage prevalence was similar across seasons. Estimated detectable colonization lasted an average of 17.7 days, with approximately one detected acquisition episode per year.

Contact with young children was associated with increased carriage and acquisition. Recent contact with children under 10 was associated with a threefold higher acquisition rate, while daily contact or contact every few days was associated with a sixfold higher rate compared with no contact. Although both adults carried pneumococcus in some households, the study found no clear evidence of adult-to-adult transmission.

Saliva qPCR detected carriage more sensitively than conventional culture-based nasopharyngeal sampling, but several serotyping assays produced nonspecific results, and some samples could not be serotyped. All urine antigen tests were negative.

Limitations included the small study population, predominantly white and highly educated participants, pandemic-related contact patterns, and diagnostic constraints. The authors suggest adult pneumococcal vaccination may primarily provide direct protection, particularly for adults exposed to children, rather than substantially reduce transmission between adults. The study was conducted collaboratively by Yale and Pfizer and reported in a preprint not certified by peer review.

Europe is set to launch Sentinel-3B on Wednesday, adding a seventh satellite to the Copernicus Earth-monitoring constellation. Alongside Sentinel-3A, it will monitor ocean conditions, pollution, sea ice, coastal vegetation, river and lake heights, and wildfires, delivering data within three hours. Funded by the EU and European Space Agency, Copernicus provides free environmental data and supports disaster response. Brexit’s impact on Britain’s participation remains uncertain.

Osteoarthritis (OA) involves cartilage degradation and low-grade joint inflammation, and no molecular diagnostics are currently approved. This study investigated whether glycosylation of lubricin, a protein involved in joint lubrication, differs between plasma and synovial fluid and between OA patients and controls.

Researchers developed a fluorescent immuno-lectin assay (FILA) using five lectins to measure lubricin glycoforms. Validation included spike-and-recovery, dilution linearity, reproducibility testing, and comparison with quantitative mass spectrometry. The methods generally agreed, although higher spike concentrations showed signal suppression.

In matched samples from 19 OA patients, lubricin glycoform concentrations were one to three orders of magnitude higher in synovial fluid than in plasma. Plasma lubricin showed relatively greater sialylation and lower Tn-antigen content, suggesting different tissue origins.

Among 183 non-obese OA patients awaiting knee replacement and 38 controls, SNA-binding plasma lubricin glycoforms were significantly reduced in OA (p=0.0023). Other measured glycoforms did not differ significantly. The SNA/MGL ratio was also lower in OA. The authors suggest that reduced SNA binding could contribute to a combined biomarker assay but would not suffice alone.

Higher BMI correlated with increased sialylation and glycan complexity. In OA patients, increasing age correlated with reduced sialylation and increased Tn-antigen expression. These findings indicate that plasma lubricin glycosylation varies with OA, age, and BMI. The origin and biological basis of the OA-associated changes require further investigation. The passage is from a preprint not certified by peer review.

The “Double Stack” offense counters a Triangle & Two defense by positioning shooters behind mid-post screeners, creating space and a head start for open shots. Shooters can pop out, curl, fade or back cut depending on defensive reactions; switches create post-up opportunities against smaller defenders. Entries include crossing, fake crossing and single/double screens, with transitions into base-screen or side-screen actions. Effective execution requires coordinated screening, strong post-ups, defensive recognition, communication and timing. Teams should anticipate defensive responses, monitor adjustments, vary alignments and attack weaker defenders. The Triangle & Two defense uses three zone defenders and two “chasers” focused on denying designated opponents the ball.

A phase 2 trial found that adding abatacept to standard treatment reduced severe acute graft-versus-host disease (GvHD) after mismatched unrelated donor stem cell transplants. Among 43 patients receiving abatacept, 3 percent developed grade III–IV acute GvHD within 100 days, compared with 32 percent and 22 percent in two national database control groups.

One-year overall survival was 85 percent with abatacept, versus 57 percent and 68 percent in controls; disease-free survival was 79 percent, versus 50 percent and 63 percent. Patients receiving abatacept had intact immune reconstitution, no major uncontrolled infection and no increase in disease relapse.

A second, randomized double-blind cohort involving 140 patients receiving matched unrelated donor transplants completed enrollment in November 2017, with results expected within six months.
Geoff Cameron says Stoke must beat Hull on Saturday to end a five-game winless run. Stoke sit 13th, eight points above relegation, while 17th-placed Hull have not won away in the league since August.

A Milwaukee woman reported that intruders broke through her front door around 11 p.m. on New Year’s Eve but fled when her alarm sounded. Police told her they had received similar calls on her street. The damaged door required boarding up, and blood was left behind. She plans to improve her home security.

The AEGEAN study randomized 1,162 subjects to Primary SOC (583) or an Additional Educational Program (579); 1,160 received study drug. Overall, 1,054 completed the 24-week visit and 1,003 completed the 48-week visit. At the second randomization, 524 subjects were assigned to Secondary SOC or Continued Additional Educational Program groups.

Baseline characteristics were comparable across groups. Median age was 74 years, 59.9% were male, and 96.4% had atrial fibrillation. Most subjects received apixaban 5 mg twice daily.

At 24 weeks, mean treatment adherence was 91.64% in Primary SOC and 91.88% in the Additional Educational Program group, with no significant difference (p=0.8117). Between weeks 24 and 48, mean adherence ranged from 87.51% to 88.41% across the three groups, without significant differences. Adherence declined significantly over time within groups.

Treatment persistence was 91.7% versus 91.3% at 24 weeks and ranged from 85.2% to 87.8% at 48 weeks, with no significant between-group differences. The proportion remaining fully adherent was approximately 27–28% at 24 weeks and 15% at 48 weeks. Mean compliance, assessed as the percentage of prescribed drug taken, exceeded 95% through week 24 and 94% at week 48.

Safety endpoints were similar across groups. Before week 24, adverse events affected 51.2% of Primary SOC subjects and 52.0% of Additional Educational Program subjects; bleeding events affected 6.5% and 9.0%, respectively. Between weeks 24 and 48, adverse-event rates ranged from 33.8% to 40.8%, and bleeding-event rates ranged from 3.2% to 4.1%. Three fatal bleeding events and 24 deaths were reported overall.

The study reported high adherence and persistence through 48 weeks, but the educational program provided no additional adherence or persistence benefits.

Childs Farm Baby Moisturiser, priced at £3.99 and available at retailers including Boots and Asda, has attracted praise on Facebook from people reporting improvements in psoriasis and eczema. Laura Gray claimed her psoriasis disappeared within 24 hours of using it. Paige Sweeney reported that her daughter’s eczema began clearing within days after other treatments had failed; her post was shared more than 40,000 times. Another mother, Joanne, said her daughter Kelisha’s skin cleared after four weeks of use. The company’s dermatologist, Dr Jennifer Crawley, said regular moisturising helps soothe and hydrate eczema-affected skin and recommended frequent application in severe cases.

The President addresses Syria’s civil war, which has killed over 100,000 people and displaced millions, and attributes an August 21 chemical weapons attack that killed over a thousand people to Assad’s government. He argues that allowing chemical weapons use to go unanswered would undermine international prohibitions, threaten U.S. security and allies, and encourage other governments and terrorists to acquire such weapons.

He advocates a targeted military strike to deter further chemical attacks and reduce Assad’s capabilities, while ruling out ground troops, an open-ended campaign, or forcibly removing Assad. He explains his decision to seek congressional support and acknowledges Americans’ concerns about further military involvement after Iraq and Afghanistan.

However, a Russian-backed initiative to secure Syria’s surrender of its chemical weapons offers a possible diplomatic alternative. Assad’s government has acknowledged possessing these weapons and expressed willingness to join the Chemical Weapons Convention. The President has asked Congress to postpone an authorization vote while diplomacy proceeds, emphasizing that any agreement must include verification.

The administration will pursue international cooperation and a U.N. Security Council resolution requiring Syria’s chemical weapons to be surrendered and destroyed under international control. Meanwhile, U.S. forces will remain positioned to maintain pressure and respond if diplomacy fails. The President frames action against chemical weapons as a matter of national security, international law, and American leadership.
