- Equal access, treatment suited to individual needs, and waiting-time standards, with explanations and alternatives when standards are not met.
- Safe care from qualified staff and continuous improvement in care quality.
- Access to NICE-recommended treatments when clinically appropriate, evidence-based funding decisions, and routine vaccinations.
- Informed consent, the ability to accept or refuse treatment, and protection of personal information.
- Choice of GP practice, involvement in treatment decisions, and openness, apologies and support when something goes wrong.
- Proper investigation of complaints, escalation to the Ombudsman, judicial review of unlawful decisions, and compensation for harm caused by negligence.

Patients are expected to look after their health where possible, respect staff and other patients, keep appointments, follow treatment plans or discuss difficulties, and participate in vaccination and screening programmes.

The Charter provides a framework for accountability, fairness and shared responsibility amid NHS waiting lists, staffing shortages and financial pressures.

On February 8, 2022, NVIDIA, SoftBank Group Capital Limited and SVF Holdco (UK) Limited mutually terminated their September 2020 share purchase agreement involving Arm Limited because of significant regulatory challenges. The sellers will retain NVIDIA’s $1.25 billion prepayment, while NVIDIA will retain its 20-year Arm license. NVIDIA intends to record a $1.36 billion charge in the first quarter of fiscal 2023, including the prepayment, due to the termination.

A retrospective cohort study reviewed 267 records of children admitted with clinically diagnosed measles to Mulago National Referral Hospital, Uganda, in 2018. It assessed treatment outcomes and costs to the healthcare delivery system amid recurring outbreaks despite free vaccine availability.

The median patient age was one year, and the median hospital stay was four days. Thirty children (11%) died during admission. Multiple complications occurred in 185 patients (69.3%), with severe pneumonia the most common, followed by gastroenteritis and conjunctivitis.

The estimated average cost of managing a measles case was US$114.50, comprising US$33.13 in direct healthcare costs and US$81.37 in overhead costs, principally staffing. Higher direct healthcare costs were associated with male patients, co-morbidities, longer hospital stays, and death during admission. Treatment costs substantially exceeded the estimated US$0.86 cost of immunizing a child.

Limitations included reliance on retrospective records, clinical rather than laboratory-confirmed diagnoses, inability to verify whether documented treatments were received, and exclusion of family and societal costs. Findings from one public referral hospital may not apply to private facilities. The authors recommend promoting measles immunization to reduce mortality and healthcare expenditure.

AQTWM, Inc. (Aqua Terra) filed a preliminary prospectus for an initial public offering of common shares in all Canadian provinces except Québec. TD Securities, Canaccord Genuity and RBC Capital Markets will co-lead the underwriting syndicate. Share quantity and pricing remain undetermined, and completion is not assured. The prospectus is available on SEDAR and remains subject to amendment or completion. There will be no U.S. public offering. Aqua Terra provides oilfield water management, logistics and disposal services to onshore oil and natural gas producers in Canada and the United States.

The High/Low zone offense combines a three-player perimeter passing attack with two interior players rotating between high and low positions. Its continuity is relatively simple, can begin from various alignments, and creates matchup problems through constant interior movement. When defenders collapse toward the middle, outside shooters gain opportunities. Sharp, accurate passing and weakside attacks are central to its success.

The basic sequence begins with a point-to-wing pass. The wing looks for a post player rolling to the basket, posting up, or moving to the short corner, then for the other post flashing into the middle. If neither receives the ball, the flashing post steps outside to reverse the ball and repeat the action on the opposite side.

Post options include shots, baseline feeds, high/low passes, and kickouts or skip passes to perimeter shooters. Entry variations include Dribble Clear, 1-4 Slice, Mid Screen, and Horns.

For late-clock situations or after timeouts, the offense can transition into quick-hitting plays: Pin Down uses down screens, Weakside Double frees a shooter with a double screen, and Vegas combines a post roll with a high double screen and cross-court pass.

The disclosure describes recommendation-model training methods and related apparatus designed to improve sampling efficiency and top-N ranking performance in large-scale recommendation systems. It addresses problems associated with large datasets, including overfitting, resource consumption, slow training, and imbalances between positive and negative samples.

Samples contain user features, object features, and labels identifying positive or negative samples based on predefined user actions. Sample sets may represent objects displayed together in one recommendation result. Training can begin by retaining sets containing at least one positive sample and adding some or all positive samples to a training set.

Negative samples receive sampling probabilities calculated using one or more relationships with positive samples:
- Differences between estimated scores representing positive or negative tendencies.
- Distances between sample feature vectors.
- Changes in ranking indicators when positive and negative samples exchange ranking positions.

The method assigns higher sampling probabilities to negative samples considered more influential for training. Selection may use descending probability order or comparisons with random numbers. An optional correction divides probabilities by their maximum value, preserving relative values while increasing selection likelihood.

The selected samples train a recommendation model using algorithms such as FTRL, logistic regression, or field-aware factorization machines. Trained models can generate scores for subsequent sampling rounds, allowing sampling and training to proceed iteratively.

During recommendation, the model scores candidate objects using user and/or object features, ranks them in descending score order, and recommends a predefined number of highest-ranked objects.

The disclosure also covers sampling and training units, processor-and-memory apparatus, storage media, and computer program products. Tests using a HUAWEI APPGALLERY dataset reportedly improved NDCG@5, NDCG@10, P@5, and P@10 compared with no sampling, random sampling, dynamic negative sampling, and optimized logistic-regression sampling.

BlinkRx, an online prescription delivery company with Donald Trump Jr. on its board, plans to host drugmakers and senior administration officials at a December summit. Some pharmaceutical representatives worry the event signals White House pressure to work with BlinkRx. The company could benefit from President Trump’s push for direct-to-consumer drug sales and the planned TrumpRx website.

Meanwhile, Pfizer’s drug-pricing agreement with the administration has prompted other major drugmakers to pursue deals. Whether these agreements will lower prescription prices remains unknown, and Pfizer’s deal details remain private.

A New York panel also recommended that state Medicaid pause coverage of a Sarepta Duchenne drug.

The paper presents a proof-of-concept system for analyzing instant messaging data in criminal investigations, developed within an Italian national project and tested on two investigations involving fraud and corruption. It addresses the time and effort required to examine large chat collections, particularly audio messages, and the limited search and integration capabilities of investigators’ existing tools.

The system combines:
- A Neo4j knowledge graph containing chats, participants, messages, metadata, and extracted entities.
- Whisper speech recognition to transcribe audio messages.
- A named entity recognition and linking pipeline that identifies, links, and clusters entity mentions.
- Neo4j graph exploration and DAVE, a web application supporting keyword search, entity-based filtering, document navigation, and annotation correction.

In an evaluation using 500 Italian audio files with added distortions, Whisper Large achieved a BERT F1 score of 0.908 and a word error rate of 0.282. In the second investigation, the entity extraction pipeline processed 1,296 of 1,442 chats; failures involved very long chats. Audio transcripts contained, on average, four times more entities than text messages, and 2,361 person mentions were linked to participants in the chat graph.

Preliminary entity recognition results were unsatisfactory: exact-match F1 was 28.8%, rising to 47.0% when partial matches were accepted. The authors identify messaging-specific language, abbreviations, and inconsistent capitalization as challenges requiring in-domain fine-tuning.

Investigators valued graph visualizations, combined textual and relational searches, audio transcription, and entity-based navigation. However, Neo4j querying required expertise. Simplified query and conversational interfaces were at an early prototype stage.

The system is intended to support, not replace, human decision-making. It retains keyword search, allows annotation correction, and supports verification against original evidence. Future work includes improving entity extraction, evaluating interfaces, and extending enrichment to images and videos.

UNC Chapel Hill reinstated professor Dwayne Dixon after a threat assessment found no basis that he threatened the university community or violated university policy. Dixon had been placed on leave Monday. Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet called for his firing over his counterprotest activities and former Redneck Revolt affiliation.

Hetzner now peers directly at NAP Africa in Isando through a 10Gbps circuit, expanding its connections with content distribution networks and Internet service providers. Together, its NAP Africa and JINX connections carry over 65% of its local traffic, reducing reliance on costly transit links. Hetzner contributes more than 4Gbps of traffic to these exchanges and supports settlement-free peering to reduce connectivity costs and latency while improving network resilience. The company hosts over 330,000 websites and encourages network operators to connect through exchange points or directly.

The gold/silver ratio measures how many ounces of silver equal the value of one ounce of gold, calculated by dividing gold’s price by silver’s price using the same currency and weight units. A high ratio indicates gold is relatively expensive compared with silver; a low ratio indicates the reverse.

Traders commonly use mean-reversion strategies, buying silver and shorting gold when the ratio is high, and reversing those positions when it is low. These strategies can involve futures, options, or ETFs. Appropriate trading thresholds require backtesting.

Historically, governments fixed the ratio for monetary stability. It now fluctuates, averaging 47:1 during the 20th century and reaching 114.77 in 2020.

Despite describing the ratio as a useful trading signal, the passage reports unsuccessful backtests. A gold strategy had positive expectancy but an erratic equity curve. A pair trade buying GLD and shorting SLV when the five-day RSI exceeded 75, then exiting below 50, showed flat performance. The authors found no robust gold/silver strategies or meaningfully profitable equity-market risk strategies based on the ratio.

The GHCB protocol defines communication between SEV-ES or SEV-SNP guests and hypervisors through MSR requests, shared GHCB pages, and VMGEXIT.

- **Initialization and registration:** Guests negotiate protocol versions, determine the memory-encryption bit position, and establish a shared GHCB. CPUID requests can retrieve individual register values before a GHCB exists, but do not support non-zero sub-leaves or function 0x0000_000d. GHCB GPA registration is supported and required only for SEV-SNP guests. Registering a new address unregisters the previous one; using an address that differs from the registered address requires guest termination.

- **Exit handling:** Non-automatic exits generate #VC exceptions for SEV-ES guests. Guests provide required state through GHCB fields, invoke VMGEXIT, and process returned results. Both sides identify valid fields using VALID_BITMAP and should clear it before preparing requests or responses. Software should disable interrupts and preemption while preparing and accessing the GHCB. Hypervisors report errors through SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2.

- **Memory and I/O operations:** String I/O and MMIO operations use decrypted shared buffers and may require multiple VMGEXIT calls. Page State Change requests support private/shared transitions and optional page-splitting or combining hints. The shared buffer holds up to 253 entries. Progress fields support interrupted requests; a zero SW_EXITINFO1 alone does not establish successful completion.

- **Firmware requests:** SNP Guest Requests use separate shared request and response pages. Hypervisors manage response-page ownership around firmware processing and return firmware status. Rate limiting may request retries, which guests must perform before sending another request to avoid reusing an AES-GCM IV with a new payload. Extended requests can return certificate data alongside attestation reports.

- **Processor management:** SNP AP Creation supports creating, updating, or removing AP state through guest-prepared VMSA pages and enables vCPU hotplug. Restricted Injection requires this mechanism rather than AP Reset Hold. APIC ID requests provide processor identifiers, while Run VMPL requests switch the current vCPU to a VMPL with an associated VMSA. Traditional AP startup requires preserving measured register state and coordinating reset vectors, including through an AP jump table.

- **Additional facilities:** SEV-SNP secrets pages convey message sequence numbers and AP jump-table information between operating environments. EFI configuration tables can communicate secrets and CPUID pages to the OS. SEV-TIO supports trusted-device setup and requests involving certificates, measurements, and attestation data. Secure AVIC uses private per-vCPU APIC backing pages that must remain present in nested page tables while their vCPUs run.

- **Interrupt delivery:** Restricted Injection uses #HV notifications and shared doorbell pages containing pending-event and EOI-assist fields. Hypervisors emulate APIC interrupt lifecycle behavior. Guests acknowledge events atomically, validate interrupt vectors, and either use EOI assistance or explicitly request an EOI. Guests should halt with interrupts disabled and examine pending events after resuming.

- **Other requirements:** NMI injection relies on guest “NMI Complete” messages before another NMI can be injected. Debug-register handling depends on hardware virtualization support. Guests may request termination, with an HLT loop or SHUTDOWN recommended afterward. SMM is unsupported in this specification version, and nested virtualization is unsupported under SEV-ES and SEV-SNP.

Deborah Jones of Cougar Creek Streamkeepers opposes a proposed 35-storey development at Scott Road and 75A Avenue, arguing it conflicts with North Delta’s six-storey area plan and stormwater management policies. She says its underground parking would prevent groundwater infiltration, while lost tree cover would increase environmental damage and vulnerability to flooding and drought. She also argues the project does not qualify for incentives requiring low environmental impact and could encourage speculative development.

Jones says Delta should consider the proposal only with significant environmental mitigation, including a reduced underground footprint and at least 15 per cent open space for large trees and rainwater infiltration. She recommends requiring all multi-family developments to reserve at least 15 per cent of their land as fully permeable ground, supporting urban forests, groundwater supplies and resilience to floods and drought.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU uses the Ampere architecture and TSMC’s 7nm process to accelerate AI and high-performance computing. Its GA100 implementation includes 108 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), 6,912 FP32 CUDA cores, 432 third-generation Tensor Cores, and five HBM2 memory stacks.

- **Tensor Core performance:** A100 supports FP16, BF16, TF32, FP64, INT8, INT4, and binary operations. It provides twice the dense Tensor Core throughput per SM of V100, reaching up to 312 TFLOPS for dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision operations and 19.5 TFLOPS for FP64 Tensor Core operations. Both GPU-level figures are approximately 2.5 times V100’s corresponding performance. TF32 accepts FP32 inputs and produces FP32 outputs while using reduced internal precision; FP16 and BF16 mixed precision offer higher training throughput.

- **Structured sparsity:** A100’s 2:4 sparsity pattern allows two nonzero values in each four-entry vector. Compressing these weights halves their storage and bandwidth requirements, while sparse Tensor Core instructions double computational throughput by skipping zeros. NVIDIA’s inference workflow trains dense networks, prunes weights, and fine-tunes the remaining weights. Evaluated networks showed virtually no inference accuracy loss; training acceleration without accuracy loss remains an active research area.

- **Memory architecture:** A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/sec, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. Compared with V100, HBM2 bandwidth increases by more than 1.7 times, L2 capacity by 6.7 times, and L2 bandwidth by 2.3 times. Compute Data Compression can further improve effective bandwidth and cache capacity. ECC protects HBM2 and key on-chip memory structures.

- **Programming and execution:** CUDA 11 supports A100’s new formats, sparsity, partitioning, and memory controls. Asynchronous copies transfer data directly from global to shared memory without intermediate register storage. Asynchronous barriers enable overlap between transfers and computation. Task graph acceleration reduces launch and dependency overhead, while cache residency controls prioritize reused data. Hardware-supported reductions and improved atomic operations provide additional acceleration.

- **GPU sharing and reliability:** Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable bandwidth, and fault isolation. Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances. Migration supports workload consolidation and GPU servicing. Improved error detection, attribution, containment, and recovery aim to reduce disruption across applications and connected GPUs.

- **Connectivity and additional accelerators:** Twelve third-generation NVLink connections provide 600 GB/sec aggregate bandwidth, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/sec per direction for x16 connections, while SR-IOV supports virtualized sharing. A100 also includes a five-core JPEG decoder, five video decoders, and an optical-flow accelerator.

The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs with six NVSwitches, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting up to 56 MIG instances. Its networking and software stack support larger deployments, with GPU-optimized containers, frameworks, libraries, and development tools provided through NVIDIA’s software ecosystem.

Charlie Tillett explains how entrepreneurs can use financial projections to understand their businesses, manage cash, attract investors, and plan equity ownership. Drawing on his experience financing NetScout Systems and Reveal Imaging, he emphasizes that building a financial model is valuable even when forecasts prove inaccurate: it exposes assumptions, identifies business drivers, and helps determine funding needs.

**Financial planning and business models**
- Maintaining sufficient cash is a central responsibility of the CEO. Financial plans help connect financing rounds with achievable milestones and anticipate when additional funding will be necessary.
- Tillett describes a business model as an income statement expressed in percentages once the company reaches critical mass. Entrepreneurs should examine revenue potential, gross margins, departmental expenses, operating profit, and revenue per employee.
- Comparisons with similar companies help test assumptions. Differences are not necessarily wrong, but entrepreneurs should understand and explain them.
- Cost of goods sold includes production materials, labor, manufacturing facilities, support, and warranty obligations. Product development belongs in R&D; other major expense categories are sales and marketing and general and administrative expenses.
- Pricing should leave customers a compelling share of the value created. Distribution choices affect revenue, expenses, profitability, and speed to market.

**Building projections**
- Tillett recommends constructing the model directly rather than relying on software that automatically generates a plan. Understanding the formulas allows founders to diagnose problems and revise assumptions.
- Sales forecasts should be built from concrete activities—sales staffing, customer visits, conversion rates, and order sizes—rather than an assumed percentage of a large market. Actual sales data can then refine the model.
- Begin with detailed first-year hiring and spending needs, extend into year two, and connect these projections to a plausible mature business model. Quarterly projections over four years provide a manageable starting point.
- Staffing drives much of a technology company’s spending. Projections should include salaries, benefits, raises, and related expenses. Formula-based costs can adjust automatically when staffing or revenue changes.
- His spreadsheet links sales, production costs, staffing, and departmental expenses to quarterly and annual profit-and-loss statements.
- Cumulative operating losses plus capital expenditures provide a rough funding estimate. Cash planning should also account for delayed customer payments and expenses payable immediately.
- Investors should receive one best-estimate forecast, although founders should still consider contingencies.

**Financing and equity**
- Venture investors seek substantial returns over a five-to-seven-year horizon, meaningful ownership, and rapid growth. A profitable smaller business may not fit their investment requirements.
- Investor ownership equals the investment divided by pre-money valuation plus the investment. Subsequent financing rounds dilute existing shareholders.
- Employee option pools also affect founders’ ownership. Venture investors generally receive preferred shares with additional rights and board representation.
- Financial planning can support milestone-based financing and help reduce dilution. Tillett’s Reveal example illustrates how equipment financing extended the company’s runway.
- Equity should incentivize future contributions, not merely reward past work. Tillett recommends vesting for founders and employees, typically over three or four years, to protect those who remain if someone leaves.
- An experienced CFO or financial adviser can help founders prepare for fundraising, anticipate financing needs, and negotiate ownership outcomes.

The lecture presents ongoing research on hot embossing thermoplastic polymers for low-cost microfluidic devices. Polymers offer low cost, transparency, and mechanical toughness. Hot embossing uses a patterned stamp to shape heated polymer, generally followed by cooling under load and stamp removal. Important variables include temperature, force, loading duration, hold time, material properties, substrate thickness, and pattern geometry.

Thermal nanoimprint lithography uses a similar process on very thin polymer layers to transfer submicron patterns. Uniform residual polymer thickness is important because thickness differences affect subsequent etching. Microembossing involves thicker substrates and different mechanical conditions.

The research seeks computationally efficient models that predict replication quality and support process and pattern design. Variability occurs at substrate, device, and individual-feature scales. Experiments particularly examine how feature dimensions, spacing, and neighboring patterns affect cavity filling.

For short-duration embossing, a simplified linear-elastic model with a fitted Young’s modulus closely reproduced measured surface topographies and pattern interactions. Carefully designed test patterns enabled material characterization across temperatures. Adding a linear viscous component approximated time-dependent deformation, although it underestimated filling rates for narrower features.

Tests examined PMMA and the cyclic olefin polymers ZEONOR and TOPAS. A fractional factorial experiment on TOPAS found significant effects of temperature, force, and hold time; the loading-rate effect was uncertain because of experimental aliasing. TOPAS samples also showed substantial orientation-dependent deformation attributable to the material rather than the stamp.

Cooling and demolding pose major challenges in microembossing. Differential thermal contraction can damage stamps and distort polymer features, while surface irregularities can cause mechanical locking. Friction-reducing treatments can help release but do not eliminate lateral forces. Carefully controlled demolding near the glass transition reduced defects in PMMA experiments, but excessive temperature or delayed cooling caused recovery and distortion. Process selection therefore requires balancing filling performance, cycle time, thermal stresses, and sensitivity to temperature.

The closing discussion addresses project presentations, weighted objectives for multiple outputs, and comparing one-factor-at-a-time optimization with response-surface methods.

Illnesses from mosquito, tick and flea bites have tripled in the U.S. since 2004, according to the CDC. Venice’s canals and wetlands provide potential mosquito breeding sites. West Nile Virus is endemic throughout Los Angeles County, where reported human cases peaked at 300 in 2015. About 80 percent of infected people show no symptoms; fewer than one percent develop severe neuroinvasive disease. Local vector control officials manage standing water to prevent breeding and recommend using insect repellent outdoors between dusk and dawn. Residents should also eliminate standing water in their yards, including small containers that hold water for more than five days.
Weston Public Library will offer free solar viewers Aug. 14, a pinhole-projector workshop Aug. 15, and NASA’s eclipse livestream Aug. 21, when Weston will see approximately 70% coverage.

The lecture examines coding for bandwidth-limited additive white Gaussian noise channels, where multilevel constellations and Euclidean distance replace the binary-code and Hamming-distance emphasis of power-limited channels.

Lattice constellations combine a discrete lattice with a finite shaping region. For moderate-complexity codes dominated by nearest-neighbor errors, an approximate union-bound expression separates coding gain from shaping gain. Normalizing signal-to-noise ratio by spectral efficiency enables comparisons across constellation sizes. Integer lattices shaped by cubes provide the baseline, with both gains equal to one.

Shaping minimizes a region’s normalized second moment. Spherical regions are optimal, providing approximately 0.2 dB of gain in two dimensions and approaching a maximum of 1.53 dB as dimensionality increases. A 16-dimensional sphere provides about 1 dB. Although shaping cannot close most of the gap to the Shannon limit, it is necessary to approach that limit. Practical techniques include trellis shaping and shell mapping; the latter provides approximately 0.8 dB in the V.34 modem. High-dimensional spherical shaping produces approximately Gaussian distributions in lower-dimensional components.

Denser lattices offer increasing nominal coding gains, but their large numbers of nearest neighbors reduce effective gains. Examples include the hexagonal lattice, D4, E8, Barnes–Wall lattices, and the 24-dimensional Leech lattice. Barnes–Wall lattices use recursive constructions analogous to Reed–Muller codes. Despite impressive density, the larger lattices discussed provide effective coding gains of roughly 4 dB or less.

Ungerboeck’s trellis-coded modulation introduces redundancy by enlarging the constellation rather than expanding bandwidth. Set partitioning divides constellation points into subsets with progressively larger minimum squared distances. A convolutional code selects subsets, while uncoded bits select points within them.

A four-state, two-dimensional example doubles the constellation size and achieves approximately 3 dB coding gain. Its overall minimum squared distance is limited by errors within a subset, which the convolutional code cannot protect against. Decoding first identifies the closest point in each subset, then uses those distances as metrics in a Viterbi decoder. Further gains require deeper partitioning as well as more complex codes. Larger trellis codes can approach 6 dB effective coding gain.

Four-dimensional trellis coding reduces constellation expansion per two dimensions. Wei’s eight-state code provides approximately 4.2 dB nominal coding gain and was adopted in V.34 and ADSL. Increasing complexity eventually yields diminishing improvements. Practical trellis coding combined with shaping generally remains approximately 2–3 dB from the Shannon limit.

Higher-performance approaches include turbo codes, sequential decoding, multilevel coding, and bit-interleaved coded modulation. Multilevel coding treats partition levels as separate binary channels with different capacities and protection requirements. In principle, capacity-achieving codes at each level can attain the aggregate channel capacity. The least reliable levels require stronger codes, while higher levels can use high-rate algebraic codes. Bit-interleaved coded modulation distributes one code’s interleaved bits across levels and uses reliability information during decoding.

The lecture concludes that coding for traditional Gaussian and binary-input channels is mature and close to fundamental limits. Remaining research includes iterative-decoding convergence, code structure, and very low error probabilities, while substantial activity has shifted toward networks and multi-user channels.

The speaker emphasizes preparing for Dallas’s strongest performance rather than dwelling on past games. Dallas was expected to respond to an opening loss with more aggressive forechecking and physical play. Forwards and defensemen must work together to limit the time available to skilled players such as Modano, Hull and Nieuwendyk.

After the next game, the speaker criticizes poor puck decisions, turnovers, individual efforts and failure to follow the game plan. Dallas forechecked more aggressively, but the team remained competitive despite what the speaker considered its worst performance in several games. An alleged missed offside before Hull’s goal was not blamed for the loss.

With the series tied 1–1 heading to Dallas, the speaker sees no reason to panic and urges a return to the team’s successful approach. Health concerns were limited, with Madden’s injury less serious than initially feared. The speaker also notes that playoff competition builds rivalries and that playing in June reflects a deep postseason run.

Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) provides measurements for attestation and does not modify AMD firmware when attestation schemes prohibit updates. Update packages must match installed firmware and patch levels, satisfy dependencies, and complete validation before applying updates. Packages should not be applied if any portion cannot fully update.

SFS patches do not persist across warm or cold reboots. Customers may apply them during boot, immediately afterward, or during system operation. Packages are versioned binary objects aligned with AGESA releases.

A customer-provided deployment agent constructs a command buffer and update package in DRAM, optionally adds customer co-signing information, and submits the request through the ASP mailbox interface. The command buffer requires 2 MB alignment; output data or update packages begin 4 KB after its address.

ASP checks memory protection, verifies applicable customer and mandatory AMD signatures, executes the patch, updates patch-level information, and returns status. Its interface also reports firmware versions and patch levels.

Updates run alongside x86 and DMA traffic and are designed to minimize performance impact and avoid system resets, although some activities may require brief quiescence. SEV and SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates; SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating.

CBCT supports daily image guidance in radiotherapy but suffers from artifacts and inconsistent Hounsfield Unit (HU) values. Conventional CT provides better soft-tissue contrast and reliable HU calibration but typically cannot capture daily anatomical changes. Generating synthetic CT from CBCT aims to combine these advantages, improving dose calculation, anatomical monitoring, segmentation, and adaptive treatment planning without repeat CT scans.

Existing synthesis approaches include deformable registration, intensity correction, GANs, CNNs, transformers, and hybrid architectures. Their limitations include dependence on prior anatomy, unstable training, hallucinated structures, limited interpretability, and computational demands. Diffusion models offer improved training stability, although computational cost and generalization remain challenges.

The work introduces EqDiff-CT, a conditional denoising diffusion framework for head-and-neck CBCT-to-CT synthesis without deformable priors or adversarial training. Its time-conditioned U-Net incorporates discrete rotational equivariance and self-attention to capture long-range spatial relationships. The model processes two-dimensional axial slices, concatenating the CBCT condition at each denoising timestep. Training combines mean squared error and structural similarity losses on predicted noise, alongside an HU-preserving processing pipeline.

Evaluation used the SynthRAD2025 Head & Neck dataset with an 80/20 patient-wise split and slice- and volume-level metrics. The attention-enhanced model outperformed a diffusion baseline without attention and a CycleGAN baseline across SSIM, PSNR, MSE, and MAE, while preserving structures including the mandible, airway, and cervical spine.

SteelSeries Arctis GameBuds, rated 9/10 by WIRED, are discounted to $128 on Amazon. Xbox- or PlayStation-compatible versions also support Switch, PC, and smartphones. Features include low-latency 2.4GHz audio through a USB-C dongle, Bluetooth, active noise cancellation, physical controls, and game-specific equalizer settings through a mobile app. Battery life reaches approximately 10 hours per charge and 40 hours with the case. The reviewer highlights their portability, comfort, and suitability for gaming and everyday use.

James Harden recorded the NBA’s first 60-point triple-double as the Houston Rockets defeated the Orlando Magic 114-107. He added 10 rebounds and 11 assists, surpassing Calvin Murphy’s franchise single-game scoring record of 57 points, set in 1978. Harden scored 18 points in the fourth quarter, including six straight after the game was tied at 107.

Houston played without injured Chris Paul and Trevor Ariza and lost Eric Gordon to lower back stiffness in the second quarter. Harden played a season-high 46 minutes, 26 seconds. Mario Hezonja and Marreese Speights led Orlando with 17 points each as the Magic suffered their third consecutive loss.

Researchers developed a model to interpret influenza A H5 RNA detections in wastewater by estimating potential contributions from humans, cow milk, poultry feces, and wild bird feces. Although wastewater influenza A measurements have generally been associated with human infections, H5N1 outbreaks in dairy cattle introduced milk as another potential source. Infected cows shed virus in milk, and discarded milk and dairy-processing waste can enter sewers. Bird feces may enter through stormwater runoff or exposed treatment facilities.

The study retrospectively analyzed 110 wastewater solids samples collected from September 1, 2023, to May 13, 2024, at Southeast San Francisco’s treatment plant, which serves 750,000 people and receives combined stormwater and sanitary sewage. Researchers measured total influenza A and H1, H3, and H5 subtype RNA using droplet digital RT-PCR, with laboratory controls.

The objectives were to identify the first H5 detection during a period of circulating human influenza and estimate source inputs needed to explain measured H5 concentrations. The model calculates daily H5 RNA flux in wastewater solids and liquids using measured concentrations, partitioning assumptions, treatment-plant flow, and suspended solids. The passage provides background and methods but no study results.

Effective early offense and press breaks require precise execution, spacing, timing, footwork, and coordination. Use the “Whole-Part-Whole” method: demonstrate player responsibilities, walk through options and defensive reads, practice progressive breakdown drills, then compete at game speed against strong defense. Include press breaks in every practice.

Coaching goals include building confidence against pressure, making sound outlet passes, advancing quickly with controlled passing, attacking double teams and outnumbered situations, and flowing into early offense when no good shot emerges.

Push the ball on every possession, transition without hesitation, and anticipate opponents’ defensive tactics and adjustments. Tough defense supports early offense, while immediate defensive pressure can disrupt opponents’ transitions and create steals and baskets.

The speaker praises a goalie’s composure and strong recovery after losses or bad goals. Bergeron and Ryan O’Reilly are described as hardworking, strong defensively and skilled at faceoffs. Both teams emphasize defense, forechecking and physical play, with similarities in overall style. The speaker stresses disciplined, clean physicality aimed at winning the puck, avoiding confrontations after whistles, and putting the team first. Scheduling and travel make two good goalies necessary, though their usage depends on circumstances.

Apple’s Form 10-Q for the fiscal quarter ended June 30, 2018 reported:

- **Quarterly results:** Net sales increased 17% year over year to $53.265 billion, primarily driven by iPhone, Services and Other Products. Net income was $11.519 billion, compared with $8.717 billion a year earlier, and diluted earnings per share were $2.34 versus $1.67. Operating income reached $12.612 billion.
- **Nine-month results:** Net sales increased 15% to $202.695 billion. Net income totaled $45.406 billion, diluted earnings per share were $8.99, and operating cash flow was $57.911 billion.
- **Product performance:** Quarterly iPhone revenue increased 20% to $29.906 billion, primarily reflecting higher average selling prices, while unit sales increased 1%. Services revenue rose 31% to $9.548 billion, including a $236 million favorable one-time item from lawsuit resolutions. Other Products revenue increased 37% to $3.740 billion. iPad and Mac revenue each declined 5%.
- **Geographic performance:** Quarterly sales increased across all reportable regions: Americas, 20%; Europe, 14%; Greater China, 19%; Japan, 7%; and Rest of Asia Pacific, 16%. Foreign currency strength favorably affected overall sales.
- **Margins and expenses:** Quarterly gross margin was 38.3%, down from 38.5%, primarily because of higher product cost structures, partly offset by favorable sales mix and currency effects. Operating expenses totaled $7.809 billion, including $3.701 billion for research and development.
- **Financial position and capital returns:** Cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities totaled $243.743 billion, including $8.8 billion restricted from general use. Outstanding term-debt principal was $104.1 billion, and commercial paper totaled $12.0 billion. Apple repurchased $20.0 billion of shares and paid $3.7 billion in dividends and dividend equivalents during the quarter. It completed its previous repurchase program and began a newly authorized $100 billion program.
- **Taxes and contingencies:** The quarterly effective tax rate declined to 13.3% from 22.9%. Apple reduced its provisional tax-reform expense estimate to $900 million and its deemed repatriation tax payable estimate to $37.0 billion. Apple and Ireland appealed the European Commission’s state-aid decision; Apple had funded €4.5 billion into escrow by quarter-end. The filing also described VirnetX and Qualcomm litigation and risks associated with component availability and concentrated outsourced manufacturing.

The passage describes networked exercise equipment and methods for delivering live and on-demand instructor-led classes, with treadmills as a principal example. The system supports communication among instructors and users, shared performance metrics, competition, and gamification. Backend servers, storage, recording studios, and communications networks support content creation, distribution, and participation from remote locations.

Example treadmills include a deck with a continuous slatted belt, separate motors controlling belt speed and deck incline, supporting posts and arms, an adjustable display, and two separate rotary controls for different functions. A manufacturing method includes assembling opposing arms and crossbars, attaching rotary controls, and connecting them to a controller.

Rotary controls may feature a rotating outer portion, a central input device, sensors or encoders, and detents for incremental adjustments. They can provide visual, tactile, and audible feedback. Rotation may adjust speed, incline, or other functions, while central inputs may start or stop the belt, select classes, or change operating modes. Some embodiments use linear touch controls instead. A magnetic emergency-stop device can stop the belt when its clip is removed.

Sensors may measure machine operation and user performance, including speed, incline, distance, energy expenditure, heart rate, and other physical metrics. These measurements can be stored, analyzed, and displayed or shared.

Display interfaces allow users to manage accounts, browse featured classes, search archived classes, view live schedules, and access “just run” options. Class information may include instructors, duration, ratings, body focus, and required equipment. During exercise, interfaces may show instructional video alongside performance metrics, scorecards, leaderboards, and segmented timelines representing portions of the class.

Kentucky valedictorian Christian Bales and student council president Katherine Frantz delivered graduation speeches by bullhorn outside their commencement after the Diocese of Covington barred them from speaking during the ceremony. The diocese said the speeches were submitted late, political and inconsistent with Catholic teaching. Bales’ speech emphasized young people’s power to effect change, citing student gun-law advocates from Florida’s Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School. He said the rejection ultimately brought his message a wider audience through national media attention.

Federal prosecutor hiring has slowed despite the Trump administration’s plans to add more than 400 attorneys to US Attorneys’ Offices. LinkedIn data showed 42 people reporting new assistant US attorney jobs from January through August, less than half the number in the same period in each of the previous four years. The data is not comprehensive.

Current and former prosecutors attributed the slowdown to budget constraints, hiring freezes, higher staffing costs, political turmoil and concerns about ethically questionable assignments. Departures and firings have worsened staffing shortages, while some offices are increasing recruitment.

New hires continue to have strong credentials, including experience at prominent law firms and prosecutors’ offices. Former prosecutors differ on recommending government service: some emphasize training opportunities and qualified leadership, while others warn that political interference could affect new attorneys.

The study developed metal inorganic-organic complex (MIOC) crystals and glasses using a ligand-tuning strategy that introduces chloride into zeolitic imidazolate framework systems. Two zinc-based compounds, MIOC-4 containing imidazole and MIOC-7 containing benzimidazole, were synthesized by slow evaporation and converted into transparent glasses by melt-quenching.

Both crystals contain hydrogen-bonded networks, while MIOC-7 additionally features extensive π-π interactions and an interdigitated structure. MIOC-4 and MIOC-7 melted at 440 and 508 K, respectively, and their glasses exhibited glass-transition temperatures of 282 and 359 K. Structural analyses showed that melting involves slippage and distortion of hydrogen-bonded structures followed by hydrogen-bond breaking, without disrupting metal-ligand coordination. During quenching, disordered N-H···Cl hydrogen-bond networks form. The glasses retain intramolecular correlations but lose medium- and long-range intermolecular order and exhibit short-range structural disorder.

Mixed-ligand synthesis produced binary mixtures of MIOC-4 and MIOC-7 crystals with reduced melting temperatures, reaching a minimum of 415 K. Increasing benzimidazole content enabled approximately linear adjustment of glass-transition temperatures from 282 to 360 K. The strategy was also extended through metal substitutions involving cobalt and copper and anion substitution involving thiocyanate. Hydrogen-bond strength and network topology were identified as stronger determinants of thermal behavior than metal-node selection.

MIOC-7 glass displayed stronger photoluminescence than its crystalline counterpart, with excitation-dependent emission colors ranging from blue to yellow. Its internal photoluminescence quantum yield was 3.4%, compared with 1.2% for the crystal. These optical properties were linked to distinct molecular conformations frozen within the disordered glass network, suggesting potential anti-counterfeiting applications.

The speaker describes supporting an overtime scoring play and using a delayed penalty to seek a clean chance. They praise the shooter, express excitement about returning home, and credit fans’ support. They emphasize avoiding penalties against an effective opposing power play, maintaining intensity, clearing the puck and making quick changes. Despite losing key players, they remain confident teammates can step in and contribute.

Socket 940 specifications cover construction, markings, contacts, actuation, inspection, and electrical performance.

- **Construction:** The base and cover use Liquid Crystal Polymer rated UL 94 V-0. Cover thickness must not exceed 1.17 mm, including the recess, and flatness must remain below 0.25 mm. A removable overlay supports vacuum pick-and-place without outgassing or leaving residue.
- **Markings:** Required identifiers include “SOCKET 940,” locking directions, pin A01 orientation, the supplier’s UL-approved symbol, and lot traceability.
- **Contacts and mounting:** High-strength copper-alloy contacts require at least 1.27 µm nickel plating and 0.76 µm gold on mating areas. Mating areas must contain no lubricants. SMT attachment uses 0.76 mm tin-lead solder balls, with solder barriers and a 0.20 mm coplanarity requirement.
- **Actuation:** A stainless-steel lever enables toolless operation. Open-position insertion and extraction forces must not exceed 2 kgf; closed-position extraction requires at least 0.013 kgf per pin. Lever operation requires less than 3.6 kgf, and pin displacement must remain below 1.0 mm.
- **Inspection:** Solder balls, contacts, housing, and lever must meet specified condition and assembly requirements.
- **Electrical performance:** Contacts require a 1.5 A rating with less than 30°C temperature rise. Initial and final resistance must not exceed 25 mΩ per contact with Kovar pins. Requirements include single-pin inductance below 4 nH, capacitance below 1 pF, differential impedance of 100 Ω ± 10%, dielectric withstand of at least 650 Vac, and insulation resistance of at least 1000 MΩ.

A study tracking 20 million U.S. children and their parents found that black boys earn less as adults than white boys from similar socioeconomic backgrounds in 99 percent of neighborhoods. Black and Native American children had the lowest upward economic mobility. About 11 percent of white children raised in the bottom income fifth reached the top fifth, compared with 2.5 percent of black children. The black-white income gap was driven almost entirely by men; controlling for parental income, black women earned slightly more than white women. Disparities persisted among wealthy families and in affluent neighborhoods. Neighborhoods where black and white children reached similar adult outcomes tended to have lower racial bias among white residents and higher proportions of present black fathers.

The Average Directional Movement Index (ADX), developed by Welles Wilder and published in 1978, measures trend strength on a scale of 0–100. It is a lagging indicator used alongside positive and negative directional indicators (DI+ and DI-). Wilder classified readings below 15 as non-trending and above 20 as trending.

The article’s backtests found limited standalone performance:
- A 10-day directional-indicator crossover strategy on the S&P 500 produced a 5.4% compound annual growth rate (CAGR), a 0.42% average trade return, and a 1.71 profit factor, excluding commissions and slippage.
- An optimized ADX breakout strategy achieved a 3.03% CAGR versus 9.9% for buy-and-hold, but reduced drawdown to 13.76% versus 55%.

Adding an ADX filter to an undisclosed mean-reversion strategy reduced market exposure and improved average returns per trade. On SPY, CAGR fell from 9% to 7.3%, while exposure dropped from 24% to 7%; average trade returns increased from 0.54% to 0.73%, and maximum drawdown decreased slightly. The filtered strategy achieved a 12.5% CAGR on QQQ with 8% market exposure.

The article concludes that ADX is more useful alongside other indicators than alone and recommends independent backtesting.

The paper studies conditions under which strategic interactions in multi-agent reinforcement learning admit finite-length satisficing paths from any initial joint strategy to an equilibrium. Satisficing paths follow a “win-stay, lose-shift” constraint: players currently achieving a best response retain their strategies, while others may change them. The paper introduces grouped satisficing paths, in which a group must retain its strategies when all its members achieve best responses. Singleton groups recover ordinary satisficing paths.

Using a topological approach, the paper establishes two main results:
- Under convex, compact strategy sets and continuous, partially analytic payoff functions, a local minimum of the best-response group count occurs exactly when every currently best-responding group remains best-responding after any admissible strategy update. This supports reducing the original game to a sub-game.
- If these conditions hold and every sub-game has an equilibrium, every initial joint strategy admits a finite-length grouped satisficing path ending at an equilibrium.

Corollaries establish satisficing-path existence for certain continuous games, finite-strategy mixed games, and finite-state stochastic games with finite strategy sets, including stationary strategies and strategies using finite histories.

The results concern path existence rather than convergence guarantees for particular update algorithms. They do not impose the regularity or uncoupledness restrictions considered in prior impossibility results.

Open questions include identifying necessary and sufficient conditions, extending the main results to approximate best responses, and determining whether path existence persists when strategy changes are restricted to neighborhoods of current strategies.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture enhances graphics, ray tracing, AI processing, memory bandwidth, and data loading for gaming, professional visualization, and data-center workloads.

- **Concurrent processing:** GA10x supports simultaneous RT Core and graphics or compute workloads, plus two concurrent compute workloads within each streaming multiprocessor. Software controls allow different workload priorities.
- **Ray tracing and motion blur:** Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection throughput compared with Turing. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates motion blur for moving and deforming geometry, enabling up to eightfold faster ray-traced motion blur rendering. NVIDIA reports a fivefold improvement in one Blender demonstration using an RTX 3080 versus an RTX 2080 Super.
- **Rendering performance:** In a Wolfenstein: Youngblood frame example, the RTX 2080 Super takes 51 milliseconds using shaders alone, 20 milliseconds with RT Cores, and 12 milliseconds with Tensor Core-enabled DLSS. The RTX 3080 renders the same frame in 6.7 milliseconds.
- **Tensor Cores and AI:** Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support and structured sparsity. Sparse operations skip zero-valued weights, doubling per-SM throughput compared with Turing while dense throughput remains unchanged. A 2:4 pruning and retraining process reduces weight storage and bandwidth requirements with virtually no inference accuracy loss in NVIDIA’s evaluations. Enhanced DLSS combines information from multiple frames and supports a new scaling factor for 8K gaming.
- **Memory:** GDDR6X uses four-level PAM4 signaling to transmit two bits per clock edge. GA10x supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/s. Error Detection and Replay retries failed memory transmissions; excessive overclocking can reduce useful bandwidth through repeated retries and can still cause crashes.
- **RTX IO:** Working with Microsoft DirectStorage, RTX IO enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression of compressed assets, reducing CPU work and storage overhead. It is intended to improve loading, streaming, and handling of large game and professional datasets.
- **Professional GPUs:** The A40 targets data-center visual computing, AI, and virtualized workloads. The RTX A6000 targets professional workstations, rendering, and large datasets. Both provide 48 GB of memory and support linking two GPUs through third-generation NVLink for 96 GB combined memory.
- **Displays and video:** Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz, subject to interface and compression requirements. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding, including up to 8K60 HDR playback. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads video encoding and supports H.264 up to 4K and HEVC up to 8K.
- **Product distinctions:** The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X memory. The RTX 3070 uses GDDR6 and lacks NVLink.

NVIDIA provides the specifications without warranties of accuracy or completeness and reserves the right to change them.

E-mini futures are electronically traded contracts representing a fraction of standard futures contracts. Introduced by the Chicago Mercantile Exchange in 1997 for the S&P 500, they now cover indexes, commodities, currencies, and some individual stocks. The S&P 500 E-mini remains the most actively traded.

Their smaller size, liquidity, and leverage allow traders with less capital to speculate or hedge investments. However, leverage magnifies losses as well as gains. Trading requires a futures brokerage account and an understanding of margin requirements, contract specifications, and risk management. Capital requirements vary by contract, exchange, broker, and volatility.

The passage presents an S&P 500 E-mini strategy tested using a compounding equity backtest rather than a futures test:
- **2000–2021:** 163 trades, averaging a 0.89% gain, with a 79% win rate and a profit factor of 2.
- **2022:** 13 trades, averaging a 0.18% gain, compared with a 15% S&P 500 decline at the time of writing.

The author discourages scalping because of competition, commissions, and slippage, and emphasizes written trading plans, backtesting, discipline, and recordkeeping. Educational resources include books, courses, videos, and broker-provided materials.

The study examines Songyang Academy’s history, educational philosophy, and relationship to modern general education through documentary research, fieldwork, interviews, and observations.

Originating as a Buddhist temple in 484 CE, Songyang Academy developed into an influential center of Confucian learning. It flourished during the Northern Song Dynasty with imperial support and prominent scholars, including Cheng Hao and Cheng Yi. Subsequent periods brought decline, restoration, and eventual collapse in the late Qing Dynasty.

The academy emphasized moral education, character development, practical learning, and the integration of knowledge and action. It welcomed learners regardless of region or social status and encouraged academic exchange. Its student-centered teaching promoted independent reading, self-study, questioning, and debate, with teachers serving as guides. Management combined academic and administrative leadership, while some students held supporting roles.

The authors connect these principles to general education’s emphasis on broad knowledge, independent judgment, social responsibility, and well-rounded development rather than narrow specialization or examination performance. They argue that Songyang Academy’s traditions offer resources for contemporary educational reform.

The study recommends preserving the academy’s cultural heritage and adapting its educational principles to modern needs through improved teaching methods, international perspectives, practical applications, interdisciplinary integration, and personalized education.

The passage examines competencies needed for digital transformation leadership in education through bibliometric analysis, connecting Education 4.0 with Thailand’s Digital Thailand strategy. It describes digital disruption and the COVID-19 pandemic as drivers of changes in teaching, learning, and institutional operations.

The analysis identifies five key areas:
- **Digital literacy:** Understanding, accessing, and using digital technologies, including cybersecurity, digital media, and online collaboration.
- **Digital readiness:** Preparing people, infrastructure, strategies, and processes for technological change.
- **Digital culture:** Building collaborative, innovative organizations that use data for decisions while maintaining data security.
- **Digital mindset:** Replacing traditional approaches with adaptable thinking, openness to innovation, and teamwork.
- **Digital leadership:** Establishing a clear vision, supporting professional development, communicating effectively, and guiding organizational change.

Education 4.0 emphasizes innovation, project-based learning, independent learning, and remote or hybrid instruction. Educators must support students’ critical thinking, creativity, and social and emotional development while adapting institutional practices and infrastructure.

The passage concludes that successful transformation requires coordinated changes in leadership, organizational culture, skills, and digital teams. These changes should be adapted to educational contexts, with teachers retaining an essential role. The findings provide directions for further research on preparing future digital education transformation leaders.

Kobe University researchers found that seeds of four orchid species germinated only near decaying logs, relying almost exclusively on wood-decaying fungi for carbon. Seedlings partnered with nearly the same fungi as adult orchids retaining coral-shaped rhizomes. Researchers suggest that maintaining these partnerships into adulthood may have facilitated the evolution of orchids that depend entirely on fungi rather than photosynthesis. The findings reveal a carbon pathway from deadwood to plants and indicate that conserving wild orchids requires protecting deadwood and its fungi.

Virtual education can offer flexible schedules, individualized instruction, expanded course access, credit recovery, and accommodations for some students’ needs. Potential challenges include unreliable internet access, limited interaction, difficulty maintaining motivation, and barriers to providing special education accommodations.

A study conducted during the 2020–21 school year examined Indiana public school leaders’ perceptions of virtual education and its growth during COVID-19. Surveys were sent to 290 superintendents and 77 virtual program administrators, with responses from 96 and 36, respectively. Eleven volunteers participated in follow-up interviews. Most survey respondents represented rural districts.

COVID-19 concerns were the leading factor in adopting and maintaining virtual programs, followed by credit recovery. Among responding superintendents, 79.2% rated pandemic-related parental concerns as very important to adoption. Among program directors, 84.8% agreed or strongly agreed that these concerns motivated continued operation.

Both groups most frequently identified maintaining enrollment during the pandemic, credit recovery, and learner convenience and flexibility as benefits. Maintaining enrollment was cited by 90.1% of superintendents and 88.6% of program administrators. Interviewees also described students who succeeded virtually after struggling in traditional classrooms and opportunities to personalize learning.

Student engagement and ensuring curriculum and instructional quality were the most frequently reported challenges. Engagement concerned 80.5% of superintendents and 97.1% of program administrators; instructional quality concerned 79.2% and 85.3%, respectively. Staffing and professional development were additional concerns.

Interviews highlighted effects on districts, teachers, and students. Districts accelerated technology plans and expanded virtual offerings while seeking to retain enrollment and funding. Teachers developed technology skills but experienced stress, abrupt assignment changes, and insufficient training. Students faced difficulties with attendance, independent learning, time management, peer relationships, and social-emotional well-being. Participants emphasized parental support, especially for younger learners.

Financial competition and student retention were prominent in interviews but less prominent as motivations in survey responses. Participants generally assessed program success in terms of maintaining enrollment, engagement, and family choice during the health crisis rather than demonstrating equivalent instructional effectiveness.

The study recommends designing programs around family needs, addressing engagement and instructional quality, and providing virtual-specific teacher development. It calls for research on post-pandemic program changes and the characteristics of successful virtual students and educators. Its findings represent a snapshot of Indiana during 2020–21 and do not establish the pandemic’s lasting effects on virtual education.

The lecture examines theoretical protein folding and interlocked three-dimensional chains.

The hydrophobic–hydrophilic (HP) model represents a protein as a sequence of H and P nodes folded onto a lattice. Its objective is to maximize adjacent H–H contacts beyond those already imposed by the chain. This models hydrophobic clustering but omits other forces involved in actual protein folding.

Finding an optimal HP folding is NP-hard on both two-dimensional square and three-dimensional cubic lattices. The lecture presents a one-third approximation algorithm for the square lattice, using parity constraints and loops that align hydrophobic nodes. Uniquely optimal foldings exist for closed chains of every even length and open chains whose lengths are divisible by four. Other lengths, uniqueness on other lattices, and designing sequences that fold uniquely into prescribed shapes remain open questions discussed in the lecture.

For three-dimensional chains with universal joints, individual chains can be unlocked yet interlock with one another. Chains are separable if they can move arbitrarily far apart without intersection. Key results include:
- Any finite collection of two-bar chains, or hairpins, can separate.
- Two three-bar chains, or one four-bar chain, can separate even with arbitrarily many additional hairpins.
- Three three-bar chains can interlock, as can a three-bar chain with a four-bar chain.
- A hairpin can interlock with an eleven-bar chain; whether eleven is minimal remains conjectural.

Separability proofs use scaling motions that preserve required bar lengths, with extended end bars shortened back to their original lengths. Interlocking proofs use geometric constraints or topological arguments involving links.

Lubiw’s problem asks how many vertex cuts are needed to unlock an arbitrary chain of \(n\) bars. The lecture gives worst-case bounds of approximately \(n/4\) to \(n/2\); the exact constant remains unknown.

Interlocked chains also provide rigid infrastructure in a proof that deciding whether one three-dimensional chain configuration can move to another is PSPACE-complete. The complexity of deciding whether a given chain can straighten remains open.

Marjory Stoneman Douglas High School reopened February 28, 2018, two weeks after a shooting killed 17 students and teachers. Heavy police security, grief counselors, therapy animals and volunteers greeted returning students. Some students expressed unease about the armed presence and emotional difficulty returning. Classes began with the period interrupted by the shooting, while the building where it occurred remained closed.

Students continued organizing against gun violence, including preparations for a national school walkout. Dick’s Sporting Goods announced it would stop selling assault-style rifles and guns to anyone under 21.

Florida legislative committees advanced school-safety proposals that included raising the minimum age for buying long guns to 21 and allowing trained, deputized teachers to carry concealed weapons with district approval. Broward’s superintendent opposed arming teachers. Governor Rick Scott sought legislation before the session ended but declined to say whether he would veto a package containing that provision. An NRA lobbyist opposed gun-ownership restrictions, while victims’ relatives urged legislative action.

The speaker felt honored by recognition despite disappointment over missing a rookie trophy nomination. They delayed joining the Flyers to prepare mentally and physically in Europe. Hard training, veteran teammates’ work ethic, and growing confidence after a difficult first five games helped them improve.

The author’s 21-year-old daughter has strengths suited to becoming a literature professor, but scarce full-time faculty jobs make that career difficult to recommend. The author argues that rising costs, demographic pressures, generative AI and political hostility make an academic hiring recovery unlikely. Journalism, publishing and web-based publications also offer limited opportunities amid industry struggles. The daughter is interested in librarianship, which the author encourages because of information science’s flexible applications. Seeking broader options for talented young people who might otherwise pursue academic careers, the author invites readers to suggest alternatives.

The passage covers support, handling precautions, revision history, packaging guidance, and disclaimers for Texas Instruments MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 devices.

- TI E2E forums provide engineering support. Contributor content is supplied “AS IS” and does not constitute TI specifications.

Changes include two ADCs across all variants, selectable 32kB flash sectors for high-endurance operation, support for up to four keys, and additional DMA and timer documentation.
- Mechanical and packaging information is subject to change. Assembly guidance addresses thermal-pad soldering, vias, solder coverage, dimensions, and stencil design.

- Automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions are listed.
- TI provides technical resources without warranties. Developers remain responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements. Resource use is restricted to developing applications using the described TI products; product sales remain governed by applicable terms.

This study examined attitudes toward inclusive education among 30 purposively selected teachers from four public elementary schools in Liloan District, Cebu Province, Philippines. Using a descriptive correlational design and the Modified Scale of Teachers’ Attitudes Toward Inclusion, it assessed perceived advantages and disadvantages, professional issues, philosophical issues, and logistical concerns.

Most respondents had limited inclusion-specific experience and training: 90% had taught learners with special educational needs for one to five years, and 80% had attended only one or two inclusive education training sessions.

Teachers demonstrated positive attitudes toward inclusion’s advantages and disadvantages, professional issues, and philosophical principles, with mean scores of 3.50, 4.08, and 4.03, respectively. They recognized social benefits and supported equal access and differentiated instruction, but remained uncertain about some academic outcomes. Logistical concerns received a neutral mean score of 3.23, reflecting concerns about resources, instructional time, materials, assistive technology, and specialist access.

Statistical tests found no significant relationships between attitudes and the examined teacher or classroom characteristics, including age, marital status, education, teaching experience, and learners’ numbers or disabilities.

The study recommended sustained, practical professional development, mentorship, smaller classes, additional qualified personnel, adequate funding and materials, and stronger specialist and parent collaboration. It proposed an evidence-based Teacher Inclusion Support Plan, with continued monitoring and school-specific adjustments to translate positive attitudes into sustainable inclusive practices and reduce potential burnout risks.

The court unanimously affirmed dismissal of Brian O’Loughlin’s defamation action against the Patrolmen’s Benevolent Association and others, without costs. PBA president Phil Caruso had publicly described O’Loughlin and eight other officers as having “no feelings” and being a “disgrace” after they requested refunds of contributions toward a police memorial. O’Loughlin had proposed using his contribution for officer safety equipment instead. The court held that Caruso’s remarks were vague, unverifiable expressions of personal opinion, not actionable factual statements or mixed opinion. Their language, context and intended readership indicated that they expressed Caruso’s negative assessment of the officers’ refusal to support the memorial contribution effort.

The global vertical farming market is projected to reach approximately USD 6 billion by 2022, growing at a 21% CAGR during 2016–2022. Growth drivers include increasing population, food demand, improved food quality and technological adoption. High initial investments and artificial-lighting energy consumption hinder growth. North America holds the largest market share, while Asia-Pacific is expected to grow rapidly, supported by urbanization, limited fertile land and investment. The market is segmented by component, farming type, crop type and region.

Kayleigh Gray donated 25 pairs of acrylic turtle doves to Royal Preston Hospital’s neonatal unit, which cared for her daughter Emilia after her birth at 27 weeks. Designed by Kayleigh and produced by her employer, Sign Build, the paired doves allow parents to take one home while the other stays with their baby.

A study examining a hypothetical 40 percent reduction in the National Institutes of Health’s budget found that more than half of drugs approved in the 21st century were linked to research that would have risked losing funding. The analysis connected lower-priority NIH grants from 1980–2007 to drugs with new active ingredients approved between 2000 and 2023.

Of 557 drugs, 40 had patents directly acknowledging NIH funding, and 14 cited at-risk grants. Drugs linked to at-risk research received FDA priority review more frequently and had higher average market values than unlinked drugs.

Researchers cautioned that the analysis cannot establish whether particular drugs would have been developed under reduced funding. Co-author Matt Clancy said the study understates potential effects because it excludes some indirect pathways from research to treatments. The findings come amid warnings about proposed NIH budget cuts.

Population growth and rising food consumption are increasing demand for grain and cereal crop protection products. Herbicides dominate the market, supported by low costs, research investments, and new active ingredients. North America is the leading regional market, while Asia Pacific is expected to expand rapidly. Crop rotation helps maintain soil nutrients and reduce pest attacks, but excessive crop protection chemical use can harm the environment, human health, and soil productivity. The market includes local, regional, and international suppliers competing on factors including price, quality, innovation, and distribution.
