The author examines Justice Barrett’s defense of originalism in relation to a Supreme Court challenge to Louisiana’s second majority-Black congressional district, created to avoid violating the Voting Rights Act.

The author argues that precedents subjecting districts drawn predominantly on racial grounds to strict scrutiny lack support in the original public meaning of either the 14th or 15th Amendment. According to the essay, the 14th Amendment’s equal protection clause was not originally understood to regulate elections, while the 15th Amendment cannot support claims involving racial sorting without denial or abridgment of voting rights.

Although adherence to precedent can coexist with originalism, the author contends that the racial-predominance doctrine warrants reconsideration because it is difficult to apply and conflicts with enforcement of Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act. Remedies for minority vote dilution often require deliberately considering race when drawing districts.

The author concludes that an originalist Court should abandon this constitutional doctrine rather than weaken Voting Rights Act protections. Congress could separately prohibit such districting by statute. The essay urges Barrett and her colleagues to address these tensions consistently with her stated interpretive principles.

The paper argues for adopting cooperative education (co-op) in Nigeria to strengthen young people’s technical and soft skills, improve employability, and ease school-to-work transitions. It defines youth as people aged 15–24 to enable international comparisons.

Nigeria’s youth unemployment, historically lower than that of many regions, increased in recent years and was at least twice total unemployment for much of 1991–2021. In 2019, 28% of Nigerian youth were outside employment, education, or training, compared with 13% in OECD countries. Informality, gender disparities, limited social protection, and inadequate labor-market data complicate assessment of employment conditions.

Co-op integrates academic curricula with workplace learning through coordinated relationships among educational institutions, employers, and governments. Programs may alternate academic and work terms or combine school and work within the same day. Reported benefits include improved employment outcomes, earnings, career clarity, and alignment between education and occupational needs. Evidence comes mainly from developed countries, and the literature acknowledges research-quality limitations and the importance of program design and implementation.

Nigeria’s existing initiatives include the Students Industrial Work Experience Scheme (SIWES), Subsidy Reinvestment and Empowerment Programme, and National Social Investment Programme, including N-Power. Evaluations report benefits alongside problems such as inadequate funding, weak supervision, poor placement matches, and complex administration. The paper distinguishes co-op from SIWES through stronger curricular integration and closer institutional-employer collaboration.

The proposed approach is a federally championed co-op initiative linked to existing SIWES or N-Power infrastructure, initially tested through pilots. Governments could provide placements and support participation through employer tax credits, institutional grants, or increased public funding. The recommended alternating model would provide multiple work terms and at least one year of career-related experience before graduation.

The paper emphasizes that training alone cannot resolve youth unemployment. Broader interventions addressing labor demand, labor supply, and economic and institutional conditions are also necessary. Further research is recommended on co-op governance, suitable models for different institutions and programs, and applicability beyond tertiary education.

This preprint examines the introduction and spread of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron BA.1 in England from November 2021 through January 2022, combining 48,615 English genomes with global genomic, epidemiological and anonymized human mobility data.

Researchers inferred at least 6,455 independent introductions into England, with the earliest estimated between 5 and 18 November 2021. Approximately 70% had no onward local transmission observable in the dataset. Eight large transmission lineages accounted for more than 60% of sampled English genomes; six were inferred to have arrived before restrictions on travel from southern Africa began. Introductions before those restrictions ended represented approximately 6% of all introductions but collectively accounted for about 80% of reported BA.1 infections through January.

Importations increased exponentially through mid-December despite travel restrictions. Although early imports likely came mainly from South Africa, estimated weekly importation intensity from the United States was approximately four times that from South Africa during the restriction period. The findings indicate that geographically targeted restrictions were largely ineffective at reducing overall importation intensity.

Greater London played a central role in early domestic spread. Long-distance viral movements increased in early December, predominantly from London toward other English regions. Around New Year, movements from the Midlands and East of England increased while London’s relative contribution declined. Epidemic peaks occurred earlier in London and surrounding areas than in most other local authorities.

Mobility fell approximately 20–50% from mid-December to early January, potentially reflecting restrictions, holidays and responses to rising case numbers. Statistical modelling associated each additional weekly COVID-19 case per 100 people in an urban hub with approximately 12% fewer trips between that hub and connected home areas. Shorter-distance travel showed larger reductions.

Limitations include uneven international sequencing, unsampled genetic diversity, possible aggregation of separate transmission lineages and residual sampling biases. The authors recommend further research on interactions between transmission risk and behaviour, alongside coordinated infrastructure integrating genomic and epidemiological data.

The United States advanced to the Davis Cup quarterfinals with a 3-0 victory over Serbia, sealed by Ryan Harrison and Steve Johnson’s doubles win. Kazakhstan also advanced, defeating Switzerland 3-0. Serbia and Switzerland were without Novak Djokovic and Roger Federer, respectively.

Hungary’s doubles victory kept its tie against Belgium alive at 2-1. France, Croatia, Spain and Germany also took 2-1 leads over the Netherlands, Canada, Britain and Australia, respectively. Italy led Japan after winning the doubles.

The TLV321/2x comparator family consumes 40µA per channel and provides 40ns propagation delay. TLV321x devices have push-pull outputs; TLV322x devices have open-drain outputs that support pull-up voltages up to 5.5V independently of the comparator supply.

- **Inputs:** The input range extends 200mV beyond either supply rail without phase inversion. Input current must remain at or below 10mA; series resistors are recommended for transient protection. Applying input signals without supply voltage is not recommended. Unused inputs must maintain at least 50mV differential voltage rather than being tied together.
- **Hysteresis and timing:** Internal hysteresis is 1.8mV. External positive feedback can add hysteresis to reduce chatter near switching thresholds. Smaller input overdrive increases propagation delay, particularly below 100mV.
- **Outputs:** Push-pull outputs must not connect to another output, and unused outputs must float. Open-drain outputs support logical OR connections and level translation; recommended pull-up current is 100µA–1mA. Unused open-drain outputs may float or connect to V−. Output shorts can cause thermal runaway and device destruction.
- **Startup:** Power-on reset holds the output low for up to 32µs after the supply crosses the 1.65V POR threshold. After the delay, with adequate supply voltage, the output reflects the differential input.
- **Applications and layout:** A low-side current-sensing example uses an amplifier and comparator to signal when amplifier output exceeds 1.1V. Single or split supplies are supported. TI recommends a low-ESR 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitor at each device, stable supplies, high-speed PCB routing, and minimized input-output coupling to prevent ringing, false triggers, and oscillation.
- **Documentation and responsibility:** The passage includes support resources, ESD precautions, packaging guidance, and legal notices. Application information is not part of TI’s component specifications; customers are responsible for component suitability, design validation, testing, and compliance.

TI provides resources “as is,” disclaims warranties and responsibility, and limits use to developing applications with specified TI products. Developers bear product-selection, testing, compliance, and indemnification responsibilities. Resources may change without notice; other reproduction and display are prohibited. Product terms and warranties remain unchanged.

Four people, including a suspect wearing a homemade explosive device, suffered non-life-threatening injuries in an explosion near New York City’s Port Authority and Times Square on Monday morning. Police said the device malfunctioned or did not detonate as planned. The suspect was taken into custody. The explosion, reported around 7:30 a.m., prompted a major emergency response, subway evacuations and service disruptions, and bus diversions. President Trump was briefed on the incident.

The Investors Intelligence Sentiment Index, developed by AW Cohen in 1963, surveys over 100 independent market newsletters weekly, classifying investment advisors’ views as bullish, bearish, or expecting a correction. It is used as a contrarian indicator, particularly at extreme readings.

Bullish readings above 55% suggest excessive optimism and potentially negative market conditions; readings below 35% indicate excessive pessimism and are considered positive. The report also tracks stocks above their 10-week and 30-week moving averages to assess shorter-term and major market turns.

Investor sentiment describes investors’ mood about the broader market. Unlike Investors Intelligence, which focuses on advisors and commentators, the AAII Sentiment Survey measures individual investors’ expectations for the next six months.

Chartcraft publishes the Investors Intelligence index, available through subscriptions on its website. The passage recommends backtesting before using it in trading strategies.

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted Turkey to suspend in-person education and introduce virtual instruction, including EBA TV. Students with disabilities in inclusive settings faced challenges involving technology access, engagement, individualized support, and family involvement.

This qualitative phenomenological study examined primary school teachers’ perspectives on these students’ participation in virtual lessons, completion of activities and homework, and possible solutions. Ten general education teachers from two provinces in Turkey’s Marmara region participated voluntarily. Each taught at least one student with an officially diagnosed disability. Researchers conducted recorded, in-person semi-structured interviews in 2021, lasting 28–35 minutes, and analyzed them using content analysis. Reported transcription reliability was 98%, and intercoder reliability was 90.17%.

Findings covered six themes: teaching practices, attendance, inclusion and educational monitoring, activities and homework, teacher-parent cooperation, and solutions. Teachers used EBA, Zoom, WhatsApp, supplementary instruction, and combinations of virtual and in-person teaching. They also requested videos of home learning to assess and guide family support.

Most teachers reported high attendance among students with disabilities, particularly when families provided support and adequate equipment was available. Other students attended infrequently or not at all. Reported barriers included internet and device problems, parents’ limited literacy or technological skills, insufficient supervision, and preference for rehabilitation-center instruction. Some students attended only core subjects on medical advice.

Teachers described difficulties with social interaction, homework monitoring, student engagement, cameras being switched off, and reliance on parental assistance. Large classes restricted individual attention, while unsuitable home environments, limited communication, and parental fatigue complicated instruction. Some teachers reported no substantial difficulties, citing consistent family cooperation, daily communication, and EBA’s tracking tools. Some students completed assignments successfully and achieved high examination scores after returning to school.

Applied solutions included flexible support sessions, hybrid instruction, telephone guidance, and feedback on recorded home activities. Teachers recommended stronger family-school cooperation, device and internet assistance, social-development activities, access to school settings, and coordination with rehabilitation centers.

The study recommends preparing teachers, parents, and students for virtual education, providing accessible instructional materials, improving technological infrastructure, and adapting content to students’ characteristics and families’ support capacities. Proposed future research includes examining other educational settings and grade levels, comparing students with and without disabilities, and quantitatively investigating factors affecting virtual education.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere GPU architecture updates programmable shading, ray tracing, AI processing, memory, storage access, and display capabilities compared with Turing.

- **SM architecture:** Each streaming multiprocessor contains 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, and 128 KB of combined L1 cache/shared memory. FP32 processing on both primary datapaths doubles peak FP32 throughput per SM. Shared memory bandwidth doubles, while combined L1/shared memory capacity increases by 33%.
- **GA102 organization:** The full GPU has a 384-bit memory interface, 6144 KB of L2 cache, and 112 ROPs. Moving ROPs into graphics processing clusters increases raster throughput and improves anti-aliasing, pixel fillrate, and blending.
- **Ray tracing:** Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection testing throughput. GA10x supports concurrent ray tracing with graphics or compute, as well as simultaneous compute workloads. A new Interpolate Triangle Position unit accelerates ray-traced motion blur for moving and deforming geometry, with reported improvements of up to eight times over Turing.
- **Tensor processing:** Third-generation Tensor Cores add TF32 and BF16 support. Structured sparsity uses a two-nonzero-values-per-four pattern to reduce weight storage and bandwidth requirements and double effective matrix throughput. Dense Tensor throughput per SM remains equivalent to Turing. Tensor Cores support applications including DLSS, denoising, and AI-based audio and video effects.
- **Memory and efficiency:** GDDR6X uses four-level PAM4 signaling to transmit two bits per clock edge, supporting rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec. Error Detection and Replay retries faulty memory transmissions. NVIDIA reports up to 1.9 times Turing’s power efficiency at equal performance.
- **RTX IO:** Integration with Microsoft DirectStorage enables GPU-based loading and lossless decompression, reducing CPU workload and storage-transfer overhead. It is intended to improve asset streaming and loading for games and professional applications.
- **Display and video:** Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, and configurations including 4K at 120 Hz and 8K at 60 Hz. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds AV1 hardware decoding, including 8K60 HDR playback. Seventh-generation NVENC supports hardware encoding up to 4K H.264 and 8K HEVC.
- **Products:** The RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X; the RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6. The A40 targets data-center visual computing, while the RTX A6000 targets professional workstations. Both provide 48 GB of memory, support virtualization, and can pair through NVLink for 96 GB of combined GPU memory.

Archaeologists in Mexico plan to clear Maya-sealed tunnels at Chichen Itza to seek access to a hidden cenote beneath the El Castillo pyramid. Team leader Guillermo de Anda expects the excavation to take about three months. The European Union announced a €545 million ($636 million) package for renewable energy and electrification in Africa, where nearly 600 million people lack electricity. Projects include transmission infrastructure, rural electrification, wind and hydropower, and mini-grids.

The funding forms part of Global Gateway, the EU’s infrastructure initiative aimed at expanding electricity access, reducing fossil fuel dependence, and countering China’s Belt and Road Initiative. The EU estimates the investment program could create 38 million green jobs in Africa by 2030.

Competition also centers on Africa’s critical minerals and supply chains. China has invested heavily in African energy infrastructure and increased solar panel exports, while Western initiatives include renewable energy projects and a railway linking mineral deposits in Zambia and the Democratic Republic of the Congo to Angola’s Atlantic coast. The policy brief uses Afghanistan to argue for replacing the out-of-school children (OOSC) indicator with an out-of-education children (OOEC) indicator encompassing formal, informal, and non-formal learning.

OOSC measures formal school enrollment but overlooks alternative pathways, including madrasas, community-based education, apprenticeships, and technology-based learning. Enrollment also does not establish whether children attend or learn. Incomplete population data, chronic absenteeism, and reported schools or students that cannot be verified further limit its accuracy.

Afghanistan illustrates how educational exclusion reflects interconnected political, cultural, economic, and geographic barriers. Conflict and ideological competition have shaped its education systems, while the Taliban’s ban on girls’ secondary education has intensified exclusion. Rural children, nomadic populations, working children, and children with disabilities face particular obstacles, including distance, mobility, poverty, inaccessible facilities, and inflexible schooling.

The proposed OOEC indicator would treat education as an activity within an interconnected ecosystem rather than equating it with enrollment in one institution. The brief argues that recognizing complementary learning pathways could support culturally relevant responses to exclusion, more flexible provision, and education-system transformation.

Implementation would require:
- Data systems capturing learning activities, curricula, engagement, and educator competencies across pathways.
- Credentialing mechanisms that validate diverse learning experiences and assure quality.
- Collaboration among policymakers, educators, researchers, employers, technology providers, and communities.
- Equitable financial and technical investment, supported by better information on costs and resource allocation.

The brief presents this transition as a fundamental change in how education is measured, valued, and organized, with relevance beyond Afghanistan.

Passport applicants must swear allegiance to the United States, provide a physical description, and submit certification from a credible witness. Additional requirements apply to applicants born abroad to native-citizen fathers, naturalized citizens, women, children claiming citizenship through naturalized parents, and residents of insular possessions. These include evidence of citizenship, family relationships, immigration, residence, or loyalty, as applicable.

Passports expire after two years and require a new application. An eligible wife, minor children, and servant may share the applicant’s passport; a woman’s passport may include her minor children and servant. Professional titles are excluded. Insular chief executives may refuse applications involving suspected unlawful or improper purposes or noncompliance with the rules.

The passport fee is $1, with separate 50-cent fees for preparing duplicate applications and administering the oath in duplicate. The rules are dated July 19, 1902, and signed by Theodore Roosevelt.

Laboratory tests show jostling air and methane microbubbles can create tiny electrical sparks, potentially explaining what ignites swamp will-o’-the-wisps.

AMD Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables datacenter operators to apply firmware fixes for selected high-priority issues without rebooting. Updates run at runtime, do not persist across resets, and must be reapplied after reboot. SFS and optional customer co-signing require BIOS configuration; both are disabled by default.

SFS tracks three categories of version information:
- **SFS Patch Level (SFSPL):** Identifies the applied update package and must increase to prevent rollback.
- **Component firmware and Security Patch Level versions:** Track individual components; later patches may revert previously introduced functionality.
- **System Patch Level (SYSPL):** Tracks run-once code executed since the last reboot and increases monotonically.

Packages verify existing firmware versions, patch levels, and operational state before applying changes. They can modify registers, replace complete firmware images, or update firmware portions. Multiple packages must be applied sequentially, and all package parts must pass validation before updates begin.

AMD cryptographically signs every package. The AMD Security Processor (ASP) verifies signatures before execution. Customers may require co-signing to approve deployments, supplying an RSA public key during early boot that cannot be changed afterward. Customer key maintenance remains the customer’s responsibility.

A customer-provided deployment agent submits packages through the ASP interface using specified memory alignment and buffer layouts. The ASP checks memory protection, verifies required signatures, executes the patch, updates version information, and returns status. Firmware and patch levels are available through SFS commands.

Updates must match the system’s firmware and patch-level combination. Packages check dependencies to avoid inconsistent firmware states and should not apply if any portion cannot complete.

SFS automatically commits SEV updates, preventing rollback to previous images without rebooting. SEV and SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating. Update design aims to minimize performance impact and avoid OS quiescence where possible.

A take-a-knee chart helps football coaches determine when an offense can kneel to run out the clock and preserve a late lead. The quarterback kneels after the snap in a “victory formation” designed to minimize mistakes and turnovers. The passage offers a free chart in PDF and Google Sheets formats. Effective clock management requires practicing endgame situations and coordinating with coaching staff. Coaches must account for timing rules and play selection, since incomplete passes stop the clock and can give opponents time to regain possession and score.

The COVID-19 pandemic prompted Greece to introduce distance education in preschools to maintain students’ contact with learning. Implementation faced barriers including inadequate digital infrastructure, unequal access to technology, limited teacher training, and young children’s dependence on adult assistance.

A quantitative study examined kindergarten teachers’ experiences and views on integrating distance education into preschool education beyond the pandemic. An anonymous online questionnaire collected responses from 82 teachers in Epirus, Greece, between May 5 and June 4, 2021.

Before mandatory implementation, approximately 76% of respondents had little or no familiarity with distance education, and 91.5% had not incorporated it into teaching. Synchronous education was preferred by approximately 65%; Webex was used by nearly 89%, and email by about 61%. Teachers holding advanced ICT certification reported significantly greater prior familiarity with distance education than those without certification. No statistically significant relationship was found between years of service and ICT familiarity.

Teachers’ views on integrating distance education into kindergarten were predominantly negative:
- Approximately 93% reported limitations on psychomotor activities.
- About 90% considered adult supervision necessary.
- Approximately 87% regarded distance education as less effective than conventional education for developing social skills.
- Some 78% reported difficulties with children independently using technological tools.
- Approximately 73% identified inadequate internet and technology access, while 66% reported significant school infrastructure problems.

Respondents also expressed reservations about student engagement, individualized learning, and participation by children with disabilities. Distance education was generally viewed as an emergency option when face-to-face teaching was unavailable, rather than a routine preschool approach.

The authors recommend improving school and household technological resources, providing teacher professional development, supplying age-appropriate interactive materials, and supporting families’ supervisory roles. They urge caution about preschool integration because children’s young age intensifies digital inequalities. Findings cannot safely be generalized beyond Epirus; further studies involving larger populations and other regions are recommended.

The 9 EMA trading strategy uses a 9-period exponential moving average to identify short-term trends, generating buy signals when prices cross above the average and sell signals when prices cross below it. It can be applied across stocks, forex, commodities, and cryptocurrencies, but the passage’s backtests indicate better performance in trending assets than in mean-reverting stock markets.

A Bitcoin crossover backtest produced 284 trades averaging 2.65% gains per trade, with a maximum drawdown of 83%. Adding a 200-day moving average trend filter reduced trades to 153 and increased the average gain to 4%. The filter improved S&P 500/SPY results, but the passage still deemed the strategy untradable.

RSI, Bollinger Bands, MACD, volume, and other tools can provide signal confirmation. Suggested risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, diversification, defined exits, and avoiding excessive leverage and emotional trading.

Effective law enforcement often depends on legislation that receives little public attention but faces opposition from interested parties. The Government has supplemented civil enforcement in trust and interstate commerce cases with criminal prosecutions, achieving successes that deter violations through imprisonment and substantial fines.

Judge Holt emphasized the seriousness of deliberate railroad rebate violations. In one case, clear evidence showed a railroad repeatedly granted a shipper discriminatory rates that could drive competitors out of business. He stressed that educated business leaders and corporations enjoying public privileges have obligations to obey the law and treat citizens equally. Because such offenses are secretive and difficult to prove, prosecutions had been rare despite repeated legislation. Holt argued for penalties proportionate to the offense, with the principal penalty imposed on the corporation rather than its traffic manager, who presumably acted for his employer without personal gain.

The Konektadong Pinoy Act, enacted August 24, 2025, aims to reduce barriers to competition in the Philippine telecommunications market. New entrants, including Virtual Network Operators, could further weaken PLDT’s declining profitability and slowing growth. The author argues that additional investment in an already mature, highly penetrated industry could depress profitability and favors staying on the sidelines despite PHI’s attractive valuation.

ML²B is a benchmark for evaluating large language models on complete machine-learning pipeline generation from multilingual descriptions. It contains 30 Kaggle competitions—24 public and six without publicly available code—across 13 languages, producing 390 evaluation instances covering tabular, text, and image tasks in 12 domains. It addresses the English-only scope of existing end-to-end ML benchmarks.

Task descriptions and standardized data cards undergo human review, while GPT-4o translations are validated by native speakers with computing backgrounds. Evaluation uses isolated Docker environments and directly executes submitted code. A modular submission format separates training, validation-data preparation, and prediction to reduce preprocessing leakage. Results are normalized using Kaggle leaderboard percentiles.

Evaluation across AIDE and ML-Master configurations reports 15–45% performance degradation on non-English tasks. Performance varies by language, domain, modality, and metric. Low-resource languages exhibit more failures, particularly in tabular classification and regression. Hybrid systems partially reduce these disparities, but no model performs best universally. Common failures include inconsistent preprocessing, altered function signatures, global dependencies, and invalid library calls.

Static analysis initially flagged potential leakage in 61 of 554 modular submissions. Further examination left 33 submissions, or 5.9%, with potential leakage, indicating a need for additional auditing. Proposed future work includes expanding private tasks, improving domain balance, and developing multilingual alignment strategies.

On November 29, 2000, Enron’s Mark Palmer circulated a class-action complaint against electricity generators, noting that a reporter said Enron’s suit would look similar.

Gordon against Reliant Energy, Southern Company, NRG Energy, Dynegy, AES, Williams Energy, Duke Energy North America, and unnamed defendants. Gordon alleges that defendants manipulated California’s wholesale electricity markets by sharing and exploiting confidential operational data, withholding generating capacity, coordinating outages, creating transmission congestion, and exporting electricity for resale into California at inflated prices. The claims concern antitrust violations, unfair business practices, consumer protection violations, and unconscionable pricing. Requested relief includes class certification, damages potentially trebled where applicable, restitution, disgorgement of profits, injunctions, interest, and attorneys’ fees.

Passports expire after two years and require a new application for replacement. Eligible wives, minor children, and servants may share an applicant’s passport under specified conditions. Louisiana registered nurse Joy Williams is joining the International Nurses Association and will appear in Worldwide Leaders In Healthcare. She began nursing in 2009 and earned a Bachelor of Science in Nursing from Dillard University in 2016.

Amazon.com’s 2018 Form 10-K describes its businesses, financial performance, liquidity, and principal risks. The company operates through three segments—North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS)—serving consumers, sellers, developers, enterprises, and content creators. Its offerings include online and physical retail, electronic devices, digital content, Prime memberships, fulfillment, advertising, and cloud services. Whole Foods Market’s results have been included since its acquisition on August 28, 2017.

**2018 financial results**
- Net sales increased 31% to $232.9 billion from $177.9 billion in 2017.
- Operating income rose to $12.4 billion from $4.1 billion.
- Net income increased to $10.1 billion from $3.0 billion; diluted earnings per share rose to $20.14 from $6.15.
- North America sales reached $141.4 billion, with operating income of $7.3 billion.
- International sales reached $65.9 billion, with an operating loss of $2.1 billion.
- AWS sales increased 47% to $25.7 billion, with operating income of $7.3 billion.

Operating cash flow increased to $30.7 billion from $18.4 billion. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $41.3 billion at year-end. Cash capital expenditures were $11.3 billion, primarily supporting fulfillment capacity and technology infrastructure. Amazon believed its operating cash flows, available balances, and borrowing arrangements would meet anticipated operating cash needs for at least 12 months.

Amazon’s financial strategy emphasizes long-term growth in free cash flow through increased sales, operating efficiency, working-capital management, and investment in infrastructure and new offerings. Operating expenses totaled $220.5 billion, including $139.2 billion in cost of sales. Shipping costs increased to $27.7 billion.

At December 31, 2018, Amazon employed approximately 647,500 full-time and part-time workers and operated 520 physical stores in North America and seven internationally. Fourth-quarter revenue represented 31% of annual revenue.

Principal risks include intense competition, rapid expansion, fluctuating operating results, international regulation and foreign exchange, fulfillment and inventory management, acquisition integration, personnel retention, cybersecurity and system interruptions, intellectual-property disputes, taxation, supplier dependence, payment processing, product liability, and unlawful seller activities. Google launched Gemini Enterprise, a business AI platform offering Gemini Ultra models, Google Cloud deployment, and tools for security, data governance, and regulatory compliance. Businesses can customise models with proprietary data while using explainability features and access controls.

Competing with Microsoft, Amazon, and OpenAI, Google emphasises transparency, privacy safeguards, and compliance for regulated sectors. Mother appealed a dissolution judgment awarding $31 monthly support for each of two children and abating father’s obligations during visitation. The children spent about half their time with father. The 4-3 defense uses four defensive linemen, three linebackers and four defensive backs, emphasizing smaller, athletic players in the front seven. Tom Landry introduced it to the NFL, Jimmy Johnson modernized it, and the early-2000s Tampa Bay Buccaneers popularized its use with Tampa 2 coverage.

Key positions include the 3-technique defensive tackle, who can generate interior pressure, and the Mike linebacker, who must defend both runs and passes. The nose guard typically absorbs double teams, while defensive ends handle individual gaps and contain the quarterback.

Its strengths include:
- Strong run defense with seven defenders in the base box.
- Defined gap responsibilities that reduce reading requirements.
- Flexibility to use multiple pass coverages.

Its weaknesses include vulnerability to spread formations, unfavorable linebacker coverage matchups and outside runs. Defenses often replace the Sam linebacker with an additional defensive back to counter spread offenses.

Pressure options include a weak-side linebacker edge blitz and a zone blitz that drops a defensive end into coverage. Common coverages include Tampa 2, where the Mike drops deep between the safeties, and Cover 3, featuring three deep defenders.

Successful examples include the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, the 2006 NFC champion Chicago Bears and Montini Catholic High School under Mike Bukovsky.

Ray Dalio and Bridgewater Associates developed the All Weather Portfolio to balance risk across economic conditions, including inflation, deflation, and stagflation. It combines stocks, bonds, and commodities, using diversification to smooth returns and reduce drawdowns rather than maximize growth.

The strategy has substantial bond exposure and a relatively small stock allocation. Its risk-parity approach adjusts allocations according to volatility, although the article’s simplified backtests do not incorporate this adjustment.

In a backtest beginning in July 2007, the portfolio produced a 4.5% compound annual growth rate with daily rebalancing, compared with 6.7% for the S&P 500. Both figures exclude reinvested dividends. Annual rebalancing reduced the portfolio’s return to 4.15%.

The portfolio experienced smaller losses than stocks during major selloffs:
- **2008–09 financial crisis:** approximately 17% maximum drawdown.
- **2020 Covid-19 selloff:** approximately 6%, versus 33% for stocks.
- **2022 bear market:** approximately 12%, as commodities partly offset losses in stocks and bonds.

Using 1.5-times leverage increased the backtested annual growth rate to 6.5% and maximum drawdown to 25%, excluding borrowing costs and dividends.

The article suggests rebalancing annually or semiannually, preferably in a tax-deferred account. It presents the portfolio as potentially suitable for conservative investors and retirees, while emphasizing lower long-term returns than stocks and no guarantee of future performance.

The Atlas of Human-AI Interaction is an open-source framework that uses large language models to synthesize empirical research into a navigable knowledge graph. It addresses fragmentation in a rapidly expanding field by connecting findings rather than organizing papers solely by topics, keywords, or citations.

Researchers collected 1,888 abstracts from ACM Digital Library, IEEE Xplore, Springer Nature Link, and ArXiv in September 2025 using the query “human-ai interaction.” Claude Opus 4.1 extracted 2,037 empirical findings from 1,124 papers and represented them as [cause, relationship, effect] triplets. Semantic embeddings, synonym merging, and clustering supported construction of a graph containing 1,310 nodes and 3,908 edges, with links to original findings and source papers.

The interface provides three complementary views:
- **3D Graph View:** explores research themes, connections, and potential gaps.
- **Cause-Effect View:** displays directional relationships through Sankey diagrams.
- **Paper View:** supports searching and examining individual papers and extracted findings.

Analysis identified substantial research attention to educational contexts, explanations, trust, design, and decision support. Network analysis found 126 research communities and highlighted large language models, generative AI, trust, chatbots, and autonomous agents as opportunities for cross-community synthesis. Longitudinal effects, reciprocal human-AI adaptation, and non-professional contexts remained comparatively underexplored.

A study with 20 expert users found that Atlas supported early-stage exploration, relationship discovery, and gap identification. Participants valued its complementary visualizations but reported insufficient detail in paper summaries, ambiguity in interpreting relationship labels, limited applicability to mathematical or formula-based research, and concerns about coverage and missing temporal analysis. The tool was positioned as a complement to existing literature-review workflows rather than a replacement.

Proposed improvements include continuous literature updates, richer relationship types, stronger extraction verification, methods for reconciling contradictory findings, and more advanced network analysis.

Please, Continue (Hamlet), by theatre-makers Yan Duyvendak and Roger Bernat, stages Hamlet’s trial for killing Polonius using real legal professionals and actors playing Hamlet, Ophelia and Gertrude. Presented at Melbourne Festival, the production has played in 12 countries since its 2011 Swiss premiere, adapting to each jurisdiction’s laws. Twelve audience members are selected after closing arguments and given 20 minutes to reach a verdict.

Inspired by concerns about the Guantanamo trials, the creators sought to reveal how local justice systems work. They combined the Hamlet scenario with evidence and social circumstances from a real case involving a young man accused of killing his girlfriend’s father.

The creators’ opposing views of that case helped shape the production’s exploration of differing judgments. Duyvendak says audience members often change their opinions during performances, while some jury participants report becoming more critical of heavy sentences after experiencing the complexity of deciding a case.

Small group differentiation tailors instruction to students’ readiness, interests, abilities, linguistic needs, and cultural backgrounds. The passage presents it as a promising approach for improving learning outcomes and inclusion in elementary and higher education, benefiting students across achievement levels.

The study reviewed literature published from 2000 to 2023 using five databases. Constructivist and sociocultural theories guided the research, emphasizing learning through prior experience, social interaction, collaboration, and teacher scaffolding.

Differentiation can modify content, instructional processes, student products, and learning environments. Key principles include flexibility, ongoing assessment, respectful and challenging tasks, collaboration, and student responsibility. Suggested practices include instructional-level materials, progressively challenging assignments, visual supports, open-ended questions, and regular adjustment based on student progress.

Implementation differs by educational setting. Elementary students generally require more teacher guidance and foundational instruction, while higher education involves more specialized content, changing student groups, and greater independence. Small groups can support participation, dialogue, peer relationships, skill practice, and personalized feedback. Inclusive, culturally responsive materials and clear classroom expectations can also encourage engagement.

Challenges include substantial planning time, large classes, limited administrative support, and the need to understand individual students thoroughly. Higher education faculty also face competing research responsibilities. Increasing linguistic diversity and students’ disability-related needs reinforce the importance of flexible instruction.

The review identifies significant evidence limitations. Insufficient comparable data prevented analysis across educational settings, and available studies made relationships among small group instruction, learning outcomes, benchmarks, and test scores difficult to assess. Research gaps remain concerning effective strategies in graduate education.

The passage recommends varied individual and group assessments, clear proficiency criteria, and ongoing instructional adjustments. Order affirmed with costs; Thomas dissented over denial of the plaintiff’s statutory right to reply.

Michigan officials encourage residents and businesses to join a voluntary statewide tornado drill at 1 p.m. Wednesday during Severe Weather Awareness Week. Nearly all state facilities will participate. Residents should identify safe shelter, practice drills, monitor weather broadcasts, understand tornado watches and warnings, and prepare 72-hour emergency kits. Tornadoes can develop with little warning. If severe weather occurs April 19, the drill will move to 1 p.m. Thursday.

The Navy’s free Pier Pressure app promotes responsible drinking among Sailors through interactive gaming and tools exploring potential health and career impacts. Part of the Keep What You’ve Earned campaign, it includes a drink calorie counter and Uber and Lyft integration. It is available on iTunes and Google Play.

The Dow fell 424.56 points, or 1.74 percent, amid interest-rate concerns and Caterpillar’s warning that first-quarter performance would mark its yearly peak. The S&P 500 dropped 1.3 percent and Nasdaq 1.7 percent. Caterpillar and 3M shares declined, while the 10-year Treasury yield exceeded 3 percent for the first time in four years.

Chinese police shot dead three knife-wielding attackers who killed five people and injured 10 in Xinjiang’s Pishan County. Authorities said order had been restored and an investigation launched. They did not disclose the ethnic backgrounds of the attackers or victims.

Security researcher Michael Myng discovered a disabled-by-default keylogger in Synaptics touchpad drivers affecting more than 450 HP device models. The debugging trace could monitor keystrokes if activated through a registry change requiring administrative privileges. HP confirmed the issue and released patches, urging affected users to update promptly. HP said neither it nor Synaptics had access to customer data through the vulnerability. A separate keylogging issue involving debugging code in Conexant audio drivers had affected HP laptops earlier that year.

Johnny Juzang is making a case for a Timberwolves roster spot on a non-guaranteed contract following Nickeil Alexander-Walker’s departure. He scored 20 points in 14 minutes in a preseason game and has made 9 of 15 preseason three-pointers. His outside shooting fits Minnesota’s style, though the team still needs to determine how to retain him.

This study reviews research on the metaverse in education, examining publication trends, leading countries, influential journals and articles, major themes, and research gaps. It uses systematic review and descriptive bibliometric methods, following PRISMA standards, to analyse 270 English-language journal articles retrieved from Scopus. The search covered January 2015 to July 2024, and VOSviewer was used to map citations and keyword relationships.

Research activity increased substantially after 2021. The study reports four publications each in 2020 and 2021, 36 in 2022, 131 in 2023, and 91 by July 2024. South Korea led publication output with 40 articles, followed by China with 35 and the United States with 31. South Korea also received the most citations, followed by the United Kingdom and China. IEEE Transactions on Learning Technologies ranked first in article output, while Sustainability (Switzerland) received the most journal citations. Dwivedi and colleagues’ 2022 multidisciplinary article on the metaverse was the most cited article, with 890 citations.

Keyword analysis identified virtual reality, augmented reality, and artificial intelligence as prominent themes. Research broadly addresses two areas: developing virtual educational environments and investigating students’ and teachers’ perceptions of metaverse adoption. Applications discussed include medical simulations, educational games, virtual universities, and collaborative learning environments. Reviewed studies report opportunities to support immersion, engagement, motivation, and practical learning.

The Technology Acceptance Model provides a framework for understanding adoption through perceived usefulness and ease of use. Other reported influences include innovativeness and enjoyment. Although teacher and student attitudes are described as mainly positive, technical training and platform complexity can affect willingness to adopt metaverse tools.

Potential areas for further exploration include extended reality, blockchain, sustainability, and gamification. The study identifies a shortage of longitudinal research assessing sustained educational effectiveness and scalability. It recommends long-term evaluations across classroom, online, and hybrid settings, alongside comparative studies examining different cultural contexts, educational systems, pedagogical practices, and institutional infrastructures.

In Hemsell v. Summers, the Texas Court of Civil Appeals reviewed a $30,890 judgment awarded to J. W. Summers’s widow, children, and mother following his death in an automobile collision with Clennon C. Hemsell. The plaintiffs alleged that Hemsell’s negligence caused the collision and that his employer, Columbian Fuel Corporation, was also liable.

The court found several errors in the damages instructions. Instructions treating the deceased’s life expectancy as 34½ years and his mother’s as approximately twenty years improperly removed factual questions from the jury. Mortality tables were evidence, not conclusive determinations. The widow’s recovery should reflect pecuniary benefits she reasonably expected to receive, rather than the cost of maintaining her accustomed and expected lifestyle. The mother’s award also required consideration of the present value of future contributions.

For the children, recoverable damages could include the monetary value of nurture, care, and education, but not love, companionship, sorrow, or grief. An instruction specifically allowing college expenses improperly assumed facts not sufficiently supported by the testimony. The jury should also have been instructed to exclude sorrow and grief.

The court rejected appellants’ challenges concerning omitted sole-proximate-cause and new-and-independent-cause issues. It additionally held that plaintiffs’ counsel improperly criticized defense counsel for introducing admissible divorce records and that the trial court should have instructed the jury to disregard those remarks.

The judgment was reversed and the case remanded.

Borek Dockal contributed a goal and two assists as Philadelphia extended its unbeaten run to four matches, conceding only twice during that stretch and remaining in the playoff race. Ilsinho scored after beating Bastian Schweinsteiger. In another MLS match, Teal Bunbury’s late penalty earned New England a 1-1 draw after Josef Martinez scored.

Johns Hopkins and Mayo Clinic researchers developed a guideline to eliminate creatine kinase-myocardial band (CK-MB) testing for suspected heart attacks, citing evidence that it adds no diagnostic value beyond cardiac troponin testing. Despite previous recommendations, a 2013 survey found that 77 percent of nearly 2,000 U.S. laboratories still used CK-MB.

Published in JAMA Internal Medicine, the report recommends hospitalwide education, removing CK-MB from standardized order sets, creating computerized alerts when clinicians order it, and measuring test use and patient safety outcomes before and after implementation. It is the first in a series of High Value Practice Academic Alliance guides aimed at reducing unnecessary medical practices.

Effective March 11, 2021, Jerome Guillen transitioned from President, Automotive, to President, Tesla Heavy Trucking. He will lead all aspects of the Tesla Semi program, including charging and servicing networks, as Tesla prepares to enter the heavy trucks market. Since September 2018, Guillen had overseen Tesla’s vehicle programs, supply chain and service infrastructure.

Effective basketball transition defense begins with careful ball handling, good shot selection, offensive rebounding, and defensive balance. It requires deliberate practice rather than occasional reminders during games.

Players should sprint back immediately while maintaining sight of the ball, stay ahead of it, protect the basket, and establish defensive positions. They should prioritize preventing team scoring over following assigned opponents, pressure the ball handler, force extra passes to allow teammates to recover, and box out to prevent second chances.

Defending outnumbered situations requires communication and specific techniques:
- On breakaways, pursue the dribbler, attempt a low block with the near hand, and remain ready to rebound.
- In two-on-one situations, contain the dribbler and delay the attack rather than reaching for a steal.
- In three-on-two situations, use tandem positioning, pressure the ball, and rotate according to the pass.

After missed shots or blocked shots, the nearest defender should disrupt the rebounder’s outlet pass while another denies the primary ball handler and teammates retreat to protect the basket. If the outlet succeeds, pressure the ball toward a sideline and slow its advance. Trapping is an option; deep outlets require recovery into half-court defense. Made baskets and free throws provide opportunities to establish pressure defenses.

After turnovers, players must immediately recover. Following an intercepted pass, the passer should contain the ball handler while teammates pursue and protect the basket. Following a dribble steal, the dispossessed player should sprint back and pursue.

Coaches should assign rebounding and defensive responsibilities within offensive plays, scout opponents’ early offense, and address failures to sprint back. Instruction should use whole-part-whole teaching, breakdown drills, and full-court scrimmages that consistently include transition defense. New concepts should be introduced before execution is refined in a subsequent practice.

The study tests how accurately molecular line observations measure collapse velocities in prestellar cores by combining hydrodynamical simulations, time-dependent chemistry, and radiative transfer to generate synthetic observations.

Infall velocities estimated using the Myers et al. (1996) method consistently underestimate the simulation’s true mass-weighted velocities. Estimates based on CS reach approximately half the true value, while those based on HCO+ are often an order of magnitude lower. Results depend on the molecular tracers and measurement aperture. Despite substantial physical evolution between two simulated timesteps, similar line profiles produce similar inferred velocities.

The discrepancy arises because constant-velocity, two-slab models do not represent realistic, radially varying collapse velocities. Self-absorption features generally trace slower-moving outer regions rather than the faster inner material. Mass accretion rates calculated from these inferred velocities are therefore subject to comparable underestimation.

In these simulations, non-thermal velocity dispersions measured from optically thin lines are typically within a factor of two of the true mass-weighted infall velocity and may offer a better diagnostic. However, this interpretation may not apply to more complex, turbulent environments.

The passage specifies GHCB communication requirements and supported non-automatic events (NAEs) for SEV-ES and SEV-SNP guests.

- **GHCB state and VMGEXIT:** Guests and hypervisors must mark supplied fields in VALID_BITMAP and should clear the bitmap before setting event-specific bits. Guests must mark SW_EXITCODE, SW_EXITINFO1 and SW_EXITINFO2; hypervisors must mark the latter two. Software should disable interrupts and preemption during GHCB updates and access surrounding VMGEXIT. Nonzero SW_EXITINFO1[31:0] indicates a hypervisor-returned error.

- **Instruction handling:** Guests may handle intercepted instructions through #VC or invoke VMGEXIT directly through paravirtualization. String I/O and specified MMIO operations require decrypted buffers identified by SW_SCRATCH. Multiple VMGEXIT calls may transfer larger amounts of data. MSR faults require identifying reads versus writes, while hypercall register requirements depend on the hypervisor.

- **Page state changes:** Supported guests can request private or shared page states. SEV-SNP guests can also provide optional hints to split or combine RMP entries. The GHCB shared buffer holds up to 253 requests. Progress fields support interrupted operations and retries; zero SW_EXITINFO1 alone does not establish successful completion.

- **SNP firmware requests:** Requests require separate shared request and response pages. The hypervisor assigns the response page to firmware, reclaims it afterward and returns the firmware status. Rate limiting may request a retry, which the guest must complete before issuing another request to prevent IV reuse. Extended requests can return certificates in shared, guest-contiguous pages, with required capacity reported when supplied space is insufficient.

- **Trusted devices:** SEV-TIO allows guests to bind trusted devices within their private address space. Requests exchange device identifiers, MMIO information and interface status, and can return measurements, certificates and attestation reports. An optional nonce can trigger fresh device measurements.

- **Processor management:** SNP AP Creation supports creating, changing or removing vCPU state through guest-prepared VMSA pages. It enables vCPU hotplug and provides an alternative AP boot method. APIC ID List requests retrieve guest processor identifiers. SNP Run VMPL requests switch the current vCPU to another VMPL level, which must have an associated VMSA.

- **Interrupt facilities:** Restricted Injection uses shared #HV doorbell pages to notify guests of pending events. Related NAEs configure doorbells, send IPIs and provide emulated APIC timers. Secure AVIC uses private per-vCPU APIC backing pages that must remain present in nested page tables while their vCPUs run.

- **Booting and platform requirements:** Hypervisors must expose CPUID information identifying SEV-ES support. Traditional AP startup requires special handling because measured, encrypted registers cannot be modified by the hypervisor. AP reset-hold protocols and jump tables support startup without SNP AP Creation; Restricted Injection requires SNP AP Creation. NMI handling uses guest “NMI Complete” messages. Debug-register handling depends on hardware virtualization support. SMM and nested virtualization are unsupported.

- **Termination and unsupported events:** Guests can request termination with reason codes and additional information. An HLT loop or SHUTDOWN after the request is recommended. NAEs outside the negotiated protocol version should use the Unsupported Event exit code.

The doorbell protocol defines PendingEvent and NoEoiRequired fields aligned with APIC interrupt behavior. Hosts present interrupt vectors and non-maskable events, track acknowledgment and service state, and manage notification suppression. Guests must atomically retrieve and clear event information before acting on vectors and validate that vectors represent legitimate, expected interrupts. Clearing NoEoiRequired can complete an EOI without VMGEXIT; otherwise an explicit APIC EOI write is required. Guests should halt with interrupts disabled and inspect pending events upon resuming. Non-cooperative behavior can cause lost notifications or denial of service.

The passage describes a micro light emitting diode (LED) device and manufacturing method intended to improve the reliability of connections between light emitting materials and electrodes.

The device includes a thin film transistor substrate, two diode electrodes, passivation layers, micro LEDs, and two conductive bridge patterns connecting the LEDs to the electrodes. Each micro LED may have a cylindrical inorganic light emitting material containing sequential p-type semiconductor, intermediate, and n-type semiconductor layers, surrounded by an insulating protective layer. Its opposite ends remain exposed for electrical contact.

The micro LEDs rest on a first passivation pattern whose sidewalls align with their exposed ends to form substantially continuous planes. This arrangement reduces steps in the bridge patterns and helps minimize breakage. Additional passivation layers insulate the bridges and protect underlying components. Alternating parallel electrode lines and reflective barrier ribs may also be included.

Manufacturing involves forming the substrate, electrodes, and first passivation material layer; placing and electrically aligning the micro LEDs; and depositing a second passivation material layer. A single mask process incorporating two etching stages forms the passivation patterns. The first etch is longer and relatively more anisotropic, while the second is shorter and relatively more isotropic, uses an oxygen-containing additive gas, and completes the aligned sidewalls. Bridge patterns and an intervening insulating layer are then formed.

The device may be incorporated into a luminescent panel controlled by scan and data drivers, a power supply, and a timing controller. An example light emitting unit uses three transistors and a storage capacitor, although other circuit configurations are permitted.

Researchers analyzed pretreatment tumor biopsies from 67 patients with diverse sarcoma subtypes enrolled in three immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) combination trials to investigate associations between immune infiltration, transposable element (TE) expression, epigenetic regulators, and treatment outcomes.

RNA sequencing identified two groups: immune-hot tumors with greater immune cell infiltration and immune-cold tumors with lower infiltration. Immune-hot tumors had a significantly higher overall response rate than immune-cold tumors (30% versus 8.1%) and longer median progression-free survival (3.65 versus 1.7 months). The progression-free survival association remained significant after accounting for sarcoma subtype.

Expression of selected TEs and the chromatin-interacting transcription factor IKZF1 predicted immune classification. Higher TE scores and IKZF1 expression correlated with antiviral and inflammatory pathways, antigen processing, CD8+ T-cell activity, and PD-L1 expression. Both were associated with longer progression-free survival: 4.4 versus 1.8 months for high versus low TE scores, and 5.3 versus 1.8 months for high versus low IKZF1 expression. Higher IKZF1 expression was also associated with a significantly higher response rate; the response-rate difference by TE score was not statistically significant.

Analysis of an independent cohort of 190 sarcoma samples reproduced associations between TE and IKZF1 expression, immune infiltration, and immune pathway activation. Immune-hot classification and higher TE or IKZF1 expression were associated with longer overall survival. However, this cohort predominantly comprised primary tumors from patients who had not received systemic therapy and did not validate outcomes following ICI treatment.

Limitations included the small treatment cohort, heterogeneous sarcoma subtypes and treatment regimens, and sequencing methods that limited detection of non-polyadenylated TEs. The authors propose TE scores and IKZF1 expression as potential biomarkers requiring further validation. Mechanistic relationships remain unresolved, and functional studies are needed. Pharmacologically promoting TE expression through epigenetic targeting is suggested for preclinical investigation.

This exploratory mixed-methods study examined physics teachers’ attitudes towards physics education research, defining science scepticism as doubt about its potential positive impact on teaching practice. It addressed an underexplored aspect of the theory–practice gap: whether teachers perceive research findings as relevant and usable.

The study combined interviews with 13 purposefully selected physics teachers in Germany and a convenience-sample survey of 174 physics teachers in Germany and Austria. Interview findings informed 22 survey items. Analyses included exploratory factor analysis, latent profile analysis, and multinomial logistic regression.

Interviews revealed seven main attitudes, including recognition of research’s practical relevance and intrinsic value, alongside concerns about implementation and cooperation with researchers. Eleven interviewees expressed that research findings played a minor role compared with personal experience, and eleven expressed that findings could not be implemented in practice. Reasons included limited time, overly theoretical findings, curriculum misalignment, and perceived irrelevance to particular school settings. Some teachers expressed both positive and sceptical attitudes.

Survey analysis identified four dimensions: personal relevance, classroom feasibility, relevance to teaching generally, and cooperation between research and schools. Four teacher profiles emerged:
- **The Sceptical Ones (14%)** questioned research’s value and practical applicability.
- **The Uncertain Ones (27%)** acknowledged personal relevance but expressed largely neutral views on other dimensions.
- **The Undersupplied Ones (41%)** valued research but considered its findings insufficiently applicable and cooperation with schools inadequate.
- **The Research Advocates (18%)** valued research and considered its findings usable, while remaining less positive about research–practice cooperation.

Among the professional variables examined, only instructional-journal reading frequency significantly predicted profile membership. More frequent reading was associated with membership in the Uncertain or Research Advocate profiles rather than the Sceptical profile. Teaching experience, teacher education, school type, and doctoral qualifications were not significant predictors.

The authors recommend stronger research–practice collaboration, improved communication of findings, and greater integration of research into teacher education and professional development. Findings remain exploratory because of nonrepresentative samples, possible participation and response biases, small profile sizes, classification uncertainty, and limitations in measuring journal-reading frequency.

The lecture concludes free scalar field theory and introduces interactions and scattering.

- **Propagators:** Two-point functions describe field correlations and can heuristically represent particle transition amplitudes. The Feynman propagator is time-ordered. Retarded, advanced, Feynman, and reverse-time-ordered functions correspond to different contour prescriptions around poles. Infinitesimal shifts of the poles—the epsilon prescription—allow integration along a fixed contour.
- **Free-field correlations:** General correlation functions can be calculated using creation and annihilation operators. Vacuum n-point functions factorize into sums of products of two-point functions through all possible pairings.
- **Composite operators:** Products of fields at the same spacetime point, including quantities such as the Hamiltonian density and stress tensor, can exhibit singularities. These divergences require renormalization.
- **Interactions:** Adding higher-order terms, such as a quartic field term, introduces interactions. The coupling controls their strength. The resulting nonlinear equations cannot be solved exactly by the earlier free-field method; weak coupling permits perturbative expansion. Path integrals are introduced as an approach to treating interactions.
- **Scattering and the S-matrix:** Scattering experiments probe particle interactions. The S-matrix describes transition amplitudes between initial and final states idealized as infinitely separated particles at infinite past and future times, where interactions can be neglected. Initial and final particle numbers need not match.
- **S-matrix properties:** The S-matrix is unitary and equals the identity for a free theory. Writing \(S=I+iT\) separates interaction effects. Factoring out the energy-momentum-conservation delta function defines the scattering amplitude.
- **Correlation functions and scattering:** The LSZ theorem relates scattering amplitudes to time-ordered correlation functions evaluated in the interacting theory’s vacuum, distinguishing it from the free-theory vacuum.

The application describes sidelink positioning methods and apparatuses for determining a terminal device’s relative or absolute position using reference signals exchanged with another terminal device. It addresses positioning errors that increase with terminal-to-network distance and latency associated with core-network-controlled positioning.

A network device provides positioning configurations to two terminal devices. One or both terminals transmit sidelink positioning reference signals and measure angle of arrival, receive–transmit time differences, or both. The first terminal or the network device determines the first terminal’s position using these measurements and the second terminal’s position.

Configurations specify signal time-frequency resources, sequences, and measurement reporting methods, with optional port, beam, and power information. Supporting information may include terminal position, orientation, speed, and measurement time. Measurements can be reported directly between terminals through a PC5 interface or exchanged with the network device through a Uu interface.

The embodiments cover mutual measurements, one-way angle-of-arrival measurements, and two-way timing measurements. Where the first terminal cannot measure sidelink reference signals, the second terminal performs the measurements and reports them directly or through the network.

The described approach improves accuracy by using terminal reference devices at shorter distances than the network device. Measurement information need not pass through the core network, reducing positioning latency. The network device may host positioning following core-network authorization or preauthorization.

The application also describes corresponding terminal and network apparatuses, processors, memories, chips, computer programs, storage media, and communication systems. The methods apply to communication systems including LTE, 5G, NR, V2X, IoT, and future-generation networks.

AI could enhance human cognition, learning, creativity, and productivity, but its effects depend on design, deployment, and use. The passage examines opportunities, risks, and responses across four areas:

- **Cognition and education:** Over-reliance on AI may weaken critical thinking, independent knowledge retention, and skill development. Suggested responses include selectively delegating routine tasks, encouraging active learning, and designing AI to augment rather than replace human capabilities. Personalized learning pathways and interactive assessments could improve education.
- **Work and collaboration:** LLMs may reduce knowledge barriers, blur occupational boundaries, expand gig work, and enable flexible partnerships across individuals and organizations. These changes could improve efficiency and innovation while increasing inequality, employment instability, and pressure on specialized middle-class roles. Proposed measures include equitable AI access, new employment opportunities, labor protections, and adaptable education and welfare systems.
- **Social science research:** LLMs offer potential for generating synthetic research data, automating analysis, and developing hypotheses. Limitations include biased or oversimplified representations of people, uncertain data authenticity, and concerns about theoretical originality and validity. Human oversight and interdisciplinary collaboration remain important for research rigor and responsible use.
- **Governance:** Generative AI creates challenges involving misinformation, malicious deepfakes, discrimination, and risks that emerge during real-world use. Existing government and corporate initiatives face communication gaps, inconsistent national regulations, and rapidly evolving technology. The passage advocates forward-looking governance combining cooperation among industry, academia, and policymakers with developer and user reporting, transparent investigation, and timely regulatory updates.

Across these areas, coordinated research, institutional reform, and public participation are presented as ways to support human well-being while mitigating AI-related harms.

In June 2014, Hertz disclosed that it would restate and correct three years of financial results, revealing broader accounting problems than previously anticipated. Its stock fell about 9%. Auto industry analyst Abby Devins investigated whether the problems involved rental-fleet depreciation and could affect future vehicle purchases.

The U.S. car rental industry generated approximately $36 billion in revenue in 2013. Enterprise, Avis Budget, and Hertz together held 71% of the market. Hertz operated almost 12,000 rental locations across 145 countries and had more than 700,000 rental cars. Acquisitions and new brands expanded its operations beyond its original business-traveler focus into leisure rentals, commercial fleet services, and other markets.

Hertz reported record revenue and EBITDA in 2013. Between 2011 and 2013, revenue increased roughly 30%, and net income attributable to Hertz more than doubled. Depreciation averaged approximately 25% of total expenses, while revenue-earning equipment represented more than half of total assets in 2012 and 2013.

Hertz depreciated rental equipment using the straight-line method, relying on estimated holding periods and residual values. Management reviewed depreciation rates quarterly and adjusted them for changing market conditions. Estimated car useful lives ranged from 5–16 months in 2006 to 4–36 months in 2013.

Program cars carried manufacturer repurchase or depreciation guarantees, whereas non-program cars exposed Hertz to residual-price risk. Program cars declined from 61% of U.S. purchases in 2006 to 18% in 2013.

Devins assembled Hertz’s and Avis Budget’s equipment and depreciation data for 2006–2013 to assess depreciation’s potential significance. The passage does not establish whether depreciation caused Hertz’s accounting problems.

The passage provides operating, protection, application, and layout guidance for TI’s TLV32xx comparators.

- **Unused inputs:** Do not tie inputs together, as internal noise can cause high-frequency chatter. Connect them to voltages within the specified input range with at least 50mV differential.
- **Hysteresis:** The family includes 1.8mV internal hysteresis. External positive feedback adds hysteresis to reduce chatter near switching thresholds. Inverting configurations use three resistors; non-inverting configurations use two resistors and a voltage reference.
- **Push-pull outputs:** TLV321x outputs source and sink current without an external pull-up resistor. Never connect them to another output. Leave unused outputs floating.
- **Open-drain outputs:** TLV322x outputs sink current and support external pull-up voltages from 0V to 5.5V, independently of supply voltage. They support logical OR connections and level translation. Recommended pull-up current is 100µA–1mA. Unused outputs may float or connect to V−.
- **Protection:** Output shorts can cause thermal runaway and destruction; series current-limiting resistors are recommended where shorts are possible. Internal ESD circuits protect inputs and outputs. Input voltages are limited to 0.2V beyond the supply rails; limit input clamp current to 10mA or less.
- **Startup:** Power-on reset holds the output low for up to 32µs after the supply crosses 1.65V. After the delay, with adequate supply voltage, the output reflects the differential input.
- **Timing:** Propagation delay depends on input overdrive; smaller overdrive produces longer delays, particularly below 100mV.
- **Application example:** A low-side current-sensing circuit amplifies the voltage across a shunt resistor and changes comparator output at an overcurrent threshold. The stated design requires a logic-high alert above 1.1V amplifier output.
- **Supply and layout:** Use a low-ESR 0.1µF ceramic bypass capacitor close to each device’s supply and ground pins. Maintain stable supplies, solid grounding, and separation between input and output traces. Single or split supplies are supported within recommended input limits.
- **Documentation:** TI provides support resources and mechanical information. Application guidance requires customer validation; technical resources are supplied “as is,” and designers remain responsible for product selection, testing, and compliance.

President Andrew Johnson submitted correspondence to the House of Representatives concerning General U. S. Grant’s departure as Secretary of War ad interim following the Senate’s refusal to concur in Edwin M. Stanton’s suspension.

In his February 10, 1868, letter, Johnson accused Grant of violating an understanding to retain the office pending judicial proceedings or resign early enough for Johnson to appoint a replacement. Johnson argued that Grant had accepted the position intending to prevent Stanton’s exclusion while leading Johnson to believe otherwise. He also accused Grant of insubordination over instructions requiring presidential authorization for War Department orders purportedly issued by the President’s direction.

Johnson enclosed recollections from five Cabinet members concerning their January 14 discussion. Gideon Welles, Hugh McCulloch, and Alexander Randall supported Johnson’s account. Orville Browning described Grant’s explanation that closer examination of the law had convinced him he could not remain after the Senate’s action without risking penalties. William Seward reported that Grant’s acknowledgment of Johnson’s account was qualified rather than explicit. The accounts described an anticipated Monday conference that did not occur.

In his February 11 reply, Grant declined to accept statements contradicting his earlier accounts and denied intending to disobey any clearly communicated legal presidential order. He characterized Johnson’s instructions as ambiguous and said he had explained his interpretation without receiving an objection until Johnson’s February 10 letter. Grant enclosed departmental correspondence showing Treasury and Post Office officials recognizing Stanton as Secretary of War and requesting military assistance or information through him.

The authors argue that community-based organizations, including summer camps, mentoring programs, sports leagues and after-school clubs, should complement families and schools in addressing youth mental health needs. These organizations foster trusted relationships that position staff to recognize distress, provide basic support and connect young people with professionals, without becoming clinics.

However, staff often handle urgent needs without adequate training, resources or institutional support. The authors call for investment in mental health planning, response protocols, resource directories, staff training, partnerships with mental health providers and referral systems. They also urge support for frontline workers experiencing stress and burnout. Stronger funding and collaboration, they contend, could create a more sustainable and coordinated youth mental health support network.

Avoyelles Parish’s projected 2017–18 state and local school funding is $8,123 per student, ranking 68th among Louisiana’s 69 districts, compared with a statewide average of $9,015.
