NVIDIA’s RTX Blackwell architecture introduces AI, ray-tracing, video, display, and power-management enhancements for GeForce RTX 50 Series GPUs.

- **Memory and AI computation:** GDDR7 includes always-enabled, on-die single-bit error correction without a performance penalty, alongside Enhanced CRC and Error Detection and Replay support. Fifth-generation Tensor Cores add FP4 and FP6 operations and a second-generation FP8 Transformer Engine. FP4 reduces AI model memory requirements; the FLUX.dev example falls from over 23GB at FP16 to under 10GB.

- **Ray tracing:** Fourth-generation RT Cores provide up to twice the ray-triangle intersection rate of third-generation cores. Mega Geometry enables full-fidelity ray tracing with cluster-based level-of-detail systems, reduces acceleration-structure construction work, and supports real-time animated subdivision surfaces. Partitioned acceleration structures allow updates to changed scene partitions rather than complete rebuilds. Mega Geometry supports RTX GPUs starting with Turing through DirectX 12, Vulkan, and OptiX APIs.

- **Strand rendering and scheduling:** Hardware-supported Linear Swept Spheres accelerate geometry such as hair, with common use cases approximately twice as fast and requiring five times less geometry memory than Disjoint Orthogonal Triangle Strips. Shader Execution Reordering 2.0 improves reordering efficiency. A dedicated RISC-V AI Management Processor offloads GPU-context scheduling from the CPU to improve workload coordination and latency.

- **Video and displays:** Blackwell adds hardware H.264 and HEVC 4:2:2 encoding and decoding. Ninth-generation NVENC improves encoding quality and introduces AV1 Ultra High Quality mode; sixth-generation NVDEC doubles H.264 decoding speed. DisplayPort 2.1b supports up to 80 Gbps, enabling 8K at 165Hz or 4K at 480Hz with Display Stream Compression.

- **Power efficiency:** Advanced clock, power, and rail gating reduce idle consumption. Frequency switching is 1,000 times faster than previous architectures, while entry into the deepest sleep state is ten times faster than Ada.

- **DLSS 4:** Multi Frame Generation produces up to three additional frames per traditionally rendered frame. Its new frame-generation model is 40% faster and uses 30% less VRAM than the previous method. Transformer-based Super Resolution, Ray Reconstruction, and DLAA improve temporal stability, lighting detail, and detail in motion. Enhanced hardware Flip Metering manages frame pacing.

- **Neural rendering:** Cooperative Vectors APIs expose Tensor Cores to graphics shaders. Applications include neural materials, texture compression, real-time indirect-light estimation through Neural Radiance Cache, and generative facial rendering. RTX Skin brings subsurface scattering into real-time path tracing.

- **GPU lineup:** GB202 powers the RTX 5090, GB203 powers the RTX 5080 and RTX 5070 Ti, and GB205 powers the RTX 5070. Their full-chip implementations contain 92.2 billion, 45.6 billion, and 31 billion transistors, respectively.

NVIDIA states that specifications may change and provides the materials without warranties concerning accuracy, completeness, or suitability for particular uses.

The article surveys connections between transformer expressivity, logic, automata, and circuit complexity, highlighting established results and open problems. It treats transformers as formal language recognizers and focuses on models without chain-of-thought feedback. Its main distinctions concern attention mechanisms, positional information, and computational precision.

Unique Hard Attention Transformers (UHATs) select the leftmost position with the maximum attention score. Even with positional embeddings, their expressive power lies strictly within AC⁰, excluding PARITY and MAJORITY. They can express first-order logic extended with unary numerical predicates, all regular languages in AC⁰, and palindromes. Masked UHATs without positional embeddings recognize exactly the star-free languages. Their verification problems are decidable and EXPSPACE-complete.

Average Hard Attention Transformers (AHATs) average all positions attaining the maximum attention score. They can recognize MAJORITY and are bounded by TC⁰. Counting Linear Temporal Logic with unary numerical predicates is expressible by AHATs with positional embeddings, while its past-counting fragment, Kt[#], is expressible by masked AHATs without positional embeddings. Complete characterizations of these broader AHAT models remain unavailable. Without masking or positional embeddings, AHATs recognize exactly permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images; checking whether their recognized language is nonempty is undecidable.

The relationship between hard-attention models and practical softmax transformers remains incompletely understood. Softmax transformers with positional embeddings can express PARITY, so UHATs do not subsume them. Uniform-attention AHATs can be simulated by softmax transformers, establishing that softmax models recognize Kt[#] languages and permutation-invariant languages with semi-algebraic Parikh images.

The article also distinguishes expressibility from trainability. PARITY is expressible by softmax transformers but difficult to learn accurately, with sensitivity identified as a cause. Research on length generalization has produced a formal framework involving limit transformers and Kt[#], supported by theoretical and empirical results. Whether Kt[#] captures all concepts that permit transformer length generalization remains open.

The 3 Days Down Overnight Trading Strategy buys SPY after three consecutive declining closes and exits at the next day’s open. Backtesting produced 661 trades, averaging a 0.13% gain, with a 65% win rate and 8% maximum drawdown, excluding slippage and commissions.

Exiting at the next day’s close increased average gains to 0.24%, but lowered the win rate to 61% and increased maximum drawdown to 17%.

A community-based study in England explored barriers to care and stigma among people with probable Long Covid who reported no known clinical diagnosis. Co-produced with a Community Advisory Board, the study recruited participants in Camden, Merton and Derbyshire through community outreach. Researchers conducted 23 semi-structured interviews between August 2022 and May 2023 and analysed them thematically. Sharing study materials through voluntary organisations was the most effective recruitment approach.

Four main themes emerged:
- **Uncertainty and awareness:** Some participants were unfamiliar with Long Covid or did not associate their symptoms with it. Others attributed symptoms to ageing, menopause, stress or existing conditions. Limited awareness of available support and self-doubt discouraged help-seeking.
- **Healthcare barriers:** Participants described difficulty obtaining appointments, short consultations, fragmented assessment of symptoms and reluctance to burden the NHS. Fluctuating, multi-system symptoms and attribution to other conditions could hinder recognition and follow-up.
- **Stigma and discrimination:** Participants reported perceived dismissal, ageism, gender discrimination and limited understanding from healthcare professionals, employers and social contacts. Anticipated disbelief or judgement discouraged disclosure and care-seeking. Some experienced shame, reduced self-worth and concerns about employment.
- **Support:** Just under half sought treatment or support outside the NHS. Participants valued social and community support, flexible working and potential financial assistance. They wanted accessible, longer consultations, attentive listening, appropriate referrals and dedicated Long Covid services, sometimes without requiring GP access.

The authors interpreted the findings as consistent with epistemic injustice, involving difficulties understanding or communicating symptoms and having personal accounts discounted. They concluded that community-based case finding can engage people who have not previously sought support, and called for greater awareness, stigma reduction and earlier access to help.

Participants had symptoms consistent with Long Covid rather than confirmed diagnoses, so alternative explanations remained possible. The study did not include people under 29. The passage is a preprint that had not been peer reviewed.

The ADS868xW is a fully differential, 16-bit SAR data acquisition device with an integrated analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and buffered precision reference.

- **Conversion operation:** A rising edge on CONVST/CS moves the device from acquisition to conversion. Conversion uses an internal clock, and further CONVST/CS transitions are ignored until completion. Before starting another operation, the host monitors RVS for a low-to-high transition or waits for the maximum conversion time.
- **Data transfers:** Frames begin when CONVST/CS falls and end when it rises. A 32-clock frame provides a valid command. Shorter frames permit partial reads but invalidate writes, producing a NOP command. Longer frames use the final 32 input bits as the command. Configuration commands execute on the rising edge of CONVST/CS.
- **Programming and output:** Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power, interface protocols, output formatting, input ranges, and alarms. Programming supports byte and half-word operations; half-word commands ignore the address’s least significant bit. Output can contain fixed patterns, requested register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result, with optional device-address, range, alarm, and parity information.
- **Interface protocols:** The multiSPI interface supports four SPI-compatible protocols, single or dual data outputs, and source-synchronous reads. SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or asynchronous reset. In source-synchronous mode, RVS supplies an output clock synchronized with data, using an internal or external clock source.
- **Alarms and applications:** Input alarms have programmable high and low thresholds and hysteresis; AVDD alarms are also provided. An industrial input-module example combines the ADS8681W with an eight-channel differential multiplexer for software-configurable voltage or current inputs. A thermistor example demonstrates temperature monitoring and hysteresis for improved noise immunity.
- **Power management:** Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies serve internal circuitry and the digital interface. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. Power-down disables analog blocks while retaining register contents and an active interface. Protected reset and power-control writes require writing 69h to address 05h first.
- **Implementation guidance:** Recommendations include supply and reference decoupling, separation of analog and digital routing, short ground connections, and ESD precautions. Application information is outside the component specification; customers are responsible for design suitability, validation, and testing.

In 1886, the United States successfully opposed a proposed $2 million Hawaiian loan managed by an English syndicate, citing privileges under the reciprocity treaty. In 1887, Secretary Bayard withheld approval of a proposed Hawaiian-Samoan political alliance.

Britain subsequently proposed an international guarantee of Hawaiian neutrality and equal access to its ports. Bayard declined, citing existing treaty arrangements and affirming that the Pearl Harbor concession did not impair Hawaiian sovereignty.

In 1888, Britain formally protested the United States’ exclusive use of Pearl Harbor as a coaling and repair station, invoking British treaty rights and warning that preferential concessions threatened Hawaiian independence. Britain also acknowledged assurances that the concession transferred neither territory nor property, preserved Hawaiian jurisdiction, granted no commercial exclusivity, and would terminate with the reciprocity treaty.

The lecture examines persistent gender gaps in earnings and career advancement, focusing on discrimination, biased beliefs, identity norms, and workplace task allocation. Studying these differences matters for fairness, economic efficiency, and understanding how preferences develop.

Women’s labor market outcomes have improved through expanded education, technological innovations, shifts toward service employment, and reduced discrimination. Nevertheless, substantial earnings gaps remain, including after accounting for work time and education.

Research discussed illustrates several mechanisms:
- **Hiring practices:** Blind orchestra auditions increased impartiality and women’s representation, although some estimates were imprecise and comparisons complicated by selection across audition rounds. A separate résumé study found that white-sounding names received 50% more callbacks than African-American-sounding names.
- **Biased performance evaluations:** Female surgeons received stronger referral penalties after adverse patient outcomes and smaller rewards after favorable outcomes than male surgeons. Negative outcomes also reduced referrals to other female surgeons. Such patterns can restrict opportunities and prevent biased beliefs from being corrected.
- **Technology’s limitations:** Algorithms trained on biased human decisions can reproduce discrimination, although explicitly incorporating equity objectives may help reduce it.
- **Gender identity norms:** Research links expectations that husbands should earn more than wives to marriage formation, divorce, women’s reduced paid work, and greater household responsibilities. Studies of MBA students suggest that marriage-market incentives can discourage single women from publicly expressing career ambition.
- **Parenthood and policy:** Danish evidence shows a long-run maternal earnings penalty of nearly 20% following the first child. Gender-neutral tenure-clock extensions in economics departments increased male tenure rates while reducing female tenure rates.
- **Nonpromotable tasks:** Women more frequently volunteer for work that benefits organizations without advancing their careers. Experiments found higher female volunteering in mixed-gender groups but no gender difference in single-gender groups. Women were also more likely to accept requests and therefore more likely to be asked, reinforcing unequal task allocation.

The lecture concludes that understanding biased beliefs, identity concerns, and these demand–supply feedback mechanisms can inform efforts to reduce gender inequality.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI-based image processing, and new shading techniques to improve graphics and computational performance.

- **Memory subsystem:** Turing introduces GDDR6 memory with 14 Gbps signaling and 20% greater power efficiency than Pascal’s GDDR5X. Larger, faster caches and improved lossless compression increase effective memory bandwidth by approximately 50%. TU102 includes 6 MB of L2 cache, twice that of GP102.

- **Display and video:** DisplayPort 1.4a and Display Stream Compression support two 8K displays at 60 Hz. The display pipeline includes native HDR processing and tone mapping. Enhanced NVENC supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps, with bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 decoding support.

- **Connectivity:** USB-C and VirtualLink combine VR headset power, display, and data connections into one connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI, offering up to 100 GB/s and 50 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, respectively. TU106 does not support NVLink or SLI.

- **Ray tracing:** Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding-volume hierarchy traversal and ray–triangle intersection tests, freeing shader resources for other work. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where efficient and ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, and shadows. Denoising reduces the number of rays required. NVIDIA reports ray-tracing performance approximately ten times faster than Pascal.

- **AI graphics:** NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for image enhancement. Deep Learning Super-Sampling produces output comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work; DLSS 2X prioritizes image quality. Other NGX features include image inpainting, slow-motion frame interpolation, and image or video upscaling.

- **Rendering efficiency:** Mesh shading introduces cooperative task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rates within 16-by-16-pixel regions, enabling content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading stores and reuses shading results across views and frames. Multi-View Rendering supports four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API.

- **GPU implementations:** TU104 incorporates Turing’s RT Cores, Tensor Cores, and streaming-multiprocessor changes, serving products including GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4. Tesla T4 targets inference workloads in datacenters, enterprises, and edge devices. TU106 powers GeForce RTX 2070 and retains the principal Turing rendering features.

The passage also introduces RTX-OPS, a workload-weighted performance metric combining Tensor, floating-point, ray-tracing, and integer operations. Its ray-tracing overview explains how acceleration structures, denoising, hybrid rendering, and dedicated hardware work together to enable real-time effects.

A prolonged heat wave has broken records across Canada, the United States, Europe and the Middle East. Montreal reached 37 C, with officials linking at least 11 deaths to the heat and humidity. Ottawa recorded its highest humidex, 47, while Denver tied its all-time high of 40 C. Scotland recorded 33.2 C, its highest temperature ever. In Oman, Quriyat stayed above 42.6 C for 51 hours, setting a record for the highest nightly low. Climate scientist Blair Feltmate linked the duration and extremeness of heat waves to climate change.

In a December 31, 1842 message to Congress, the U.S. President emphasized the Hawaiian Islands’ importance to Pacific commerce, particularly American whaling vessels. American ships constituted five-sixths of annual vessel visits. He supported Hawaiian independence, disclaimed exclusive control or special advantages, and opposed potential foreign colonization or displacement of the native government. He recommended funding the resident consul to address complaints involving American citizens and property.

The message also discussed the treaty ending British military operations against China, which opened four additional ports to British merchants. Because the treaty neither admitted nor excluded other nations’ ships, the President highlighted the need to determine American access and seek appropriate commercial arrangements with China.

The double-down trading strategy adds an equal-sized position to a losing stock trade, lowering the average entry price so a smaller recovery can achieve breakeven. However, continued price declines increase losses, and focusing on the average entry price can reflect anchoring rather than a planned strategy.

The passage distinguishes doubling down from:
- **Scaling in:** a planned approach that reserves capital for additional purchases.
- **Martingale:** adding larger trades after losses, substantially increasing risk.
- **Repair strategies:** using call options to help a losing position reach breakeven faster.

Backtests suggest results depend on the asset’s behavior. For SPY, presented as mean-reverting, doubling down increased the average gain per trade from 0.56% to 0.97%, while reducing trades from 518 to 236 and lowering overall earnings. For HYG, presented as trending, the average loss per trade worsened from 0.19% to 0.22%.

The passage concludes that doubling down may work in mean-reverting assets but perform poorly in trending assets. A single large loss can cause severe damage. Trading decisions should emphasize risk management, overall strategy, and probability of success rather than recovering a particular entry price.

The low-side current sensing circuit uses an amplifier to amplify the voltage across a shunt resistor and a high-speed comparator to produce a logic-high alert when the amplifier output exceeds 1.1 V.

Reliable operation requires a stable, low-noise supply and a low-ESR 0.1 µF ceramic bypass capacitor placed directly at each device’s supply and ground pins. Minimize output-to-input coupling to prevent oscillations. An output series resistor below 100 Ω can damp ringing on long traces; controlled-impedance traces with back-termination can improve edge shapes.

The devices support single or split supplies, with inputs kept within recommended ranges. With split supplies, the low output swings to the negative supply rather than ground.

The author argues that tariffs rarely create monopolies but supports reducing duties that foster harmful monopolies and removing the anthracite coal tariff to help during crises. Additional financial legislation should promote an elastic monetary system, with banks supplying adequate circulation for commerce and industry and all money interchangeable and convertible into gold. Corporations and labor unions can benefit society or cause harm; criticism should target misconduct rather than organization itself. Both should obey the law, respect individual freedom, deal fairly, and align their interests with the public good. The author condemns political class animosity, advocates judging individuals by their conduct rather than wealth or background, and urges the National Government to exercise its constitutional powers consistently with these principles.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 documentation describes peripheral functions, application requirements, development resources, and packaging guidance.

- **Watchdog timers:** The independent watchdog (IWDT) has independent power and clock sources and generates a POR reset if software fails to reset it within the programmed time. It includes a 25-bit counter and eight selectable periods. The windowed watchdog (WWDT) generates resets or interrupts, supports automatic stopping during sleep, and offers interval timer operation.
- **Real-time clock:** RTC_B provides calendar counters, alarms, periodic interrupts, binary or BCD formats, leap-year correction for 1901–2099, calibration, temperature-drift compensation, and clock output for calibration.
- **Timers:** General-purpose timers support 16-bit counting, programmable prescaling, quadrature encoder inputs, synchronization, and peripheral triggers. Advanced timers additionally provide clock doubling, repeat counting, shadow registers, asymmetric PWM with dead-band insertion, fault handling, and additional capture/compare channels.
- **I/O and debugging:** IOMUX selects digital-pin peripheral functions and controls output drivers, input paths, and shutdown wake-up logic. Pin capabilities vary. The two-wire SWD interface and DEBUGSS support processor and device-state debugging, configurable peripheral behavior during debug halts, mailbox communication, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging.

- **GPU architecture:** The full GA102 contains seven Graphics Processing Clusters, 42 Texture Processing Clusters, 84 Streaming Multiprocessors (SMs), and 112 raster operators. Each SM includes 128 CUDA Cores, four third-generation Tensor Cores, one second-generation RT Core, and 128 KB of combined L1 cache/shared memory. - **Connectivity and memory:** Third-generation NVLink provides 112.5 GB/sec of total bidirectional bandwidth between two supported GPUs. Nuclear binding energy describes what holds nuclei together and is calculated from the difference between the summed masses of their constituents and the nucleus’s mass. Average binding energies are generally 7.5–9 MeV, except for light elements, and peak around iron. Both nuclear fusion and fission can release energy by moving toward more energetically favorable states.

The semi-empirical mass formula, also discussed through the liquid-drop model, parameterizes binding energy using five terms:

- **Volume:** The dominant contribution, proportional to mass number, is about 16 MeV per nucleon and indicates a short-range nuclear force.
- **Surface:** Surface nucleons have fewer neighbors, reducing binding energy in proportion to nuclear surface area.
- **Coulomb:** Electrical repulsion between protons reduces binding energy.
- **Asymmetry:** Unequal neutron and proton numbers increase energy, explained through the Pauli exclusion principle.
- **Pairing:** Even neutron and proton numbers favor lower energies, while nuclei with both numbers odd have the least favorable pairing state.

Together, these terms reproduce the binding-energy maximum around iron.

An overlap in soccer sends a defender forward past a midfielder, usually near the sideline, to create an unmarked attacker. The runner may receive the ball and cross from near the end-line; if marked, another attacker may become free. Unlike a positional switch, the midfielder remains in the attack. Overlaps require space and are less common in congested central areas.

An underlap takes the defender inside the midfielder, often creating a shooting opportunity. In either case, the defender returns to their original position once the attacking play changes. Coaches can vary these runs but should consider whether adding another attacker will overcrowd the attack.

In Nelson v. John, decided August 25, 1906, Ross Nelson appealed a judgment rejecting his action to enforce an 1892 agreement with John and Chekudakai Salerhand to convey allotted Puyallup reservation land.

The court held that restrictions on alienating the land were valid under the governing treaty and federal policy. It rejected Nelson’s argument that the restrictions were incompatible with the grant, explaining that the government’s policy treated the Indians as wards and expressly limited their power to transfer allotted lands.

The court also held that legislation conferring citizenship did not impliedly repeal the restrictions. Washington’s 1890 law removing restrictions depended on congressional consent. Congress’s March 3, 1893 act followed the agreement and withheld alienation rights for lands not selected for sale by the authorized commission until March 3, 1903.

Because conveyances made contrary to the restrictions were void, the court affirmed the judgment for the defendant.

The passage examines how global information and communication technology (ICT) firms are restructuring business models for an Internet of Things (IoT)-based society. Although IoT offers new services, efficiencies, and revenue opportunities, the authors identify a potential productivity paradox: technological investment may not translate into measured productivity gains.

The authors describe ICT’s “two-faced nature.” Innovation develops new functionality that can increase technology prices, while Internet characteristics—including free services, easy copying, and standardization—reduce prices. They define “uncaptured GDP” as benefits that provide utility and happiness beyond economic value but are not measured by conventional GDP accounting. Free digital services, consumer surplus, and difficult-to-measure innovations illustrate these measurement challenges.

An empirical analysis of 500 global ICT firms during 2005–2016 uses logistic growth models, with adjustments for exceptionally large firms. It reports contrasting patterns: highly R&D-intensive firms experience declining marginal ICT productivity as R&D increases, while less R&D-intensive firms experience rising marginal productivity. The reported number of firms in the declining-productivity group increased from 16 to 25.

The authors argue that leading firms respond by developing “self-propagating” functionality, which expands growth capacity as development proceeds. This relies on “soft innovation resources,” including unused resources, trust, past experiences, memories, future aspirations, and preferences extending beyond economic functionality.

Reviews of Samsung, Intel, Google, Microsoft, Huawei, Apple, and Amazon illustrate shifts toward platforms, connected services, personalized experiences, and integration of physical and digital activities. The passage also reports that ICT firms occupied nine of the top 15 positions by market capitalization in 2016.

The authors recommend integrating ICT and business strategies, developing trust-based disruptive business models responsive to social demand, and using soft innovation resources effectively. Proposed future research includes additional company case studies, closer examination of Amazon’s business model, and improved approaches to measuring digital-economy benefits beyond conventional GDP.

The article analyzes an SEIR-like model for SARS-CoV-2 transmission, focusing on estimating a time-dependent transmission rate from reported daily infections. It motivates this approach by noting that transmission changes with mobility and within-host pathogen dynamics, while excessive model complexity can impair forecasting.

The model comprises nine compartments: susceptible, exposed, vaccinated, asymptomatic infectious, mildly infectious, severely infectious, critically infectious, recovered, and deceased. To reduce unknowns, transmission rates for hospitalized, critically ill, and asymptomatic individuals are fixed at 10%, 1%, and 58% of the mildly infectious transmission rate, respectively. Other parameters describe vaccination, disease progression, recovery, hospitalization, ICU admission, and mortality. Hospitalization and death rates are derived from seven-day moving averages of reported data with specified delays.

Under assumptions of continuous, strictly positive parameters and suitable initial conditions, the passage establishes positivity or non-negativity of compartment populations and existence and uniqueness of solutions on finite time intervals. With bounded parameters, it states that a unique non-negative solution exists for all non-negative times.

The parameter-to-solution operator maps the transmission rate in a Sobolev space to the model’s compartment trajectories. The passage establishes that its admissible domain is closed and convex with non-empty interior, and that the operator is well defined, injective, continuous, and sequentially closed under weak convergence. It also states Fréchet differentiability within the domain’s interior, with the derivative characterized by a linearized differential-equation system.

The introduction outlines a subsequent inverse-problem analysis using Tikhonov-type regularization to provide sufficient conditions for existence, stability, and convergence of transmission-rate estimates, alongside a numerical example using real data.

Researchers at Washington University School of Medicine identified an alternative heat-producing pathway in mouse brown fat involving cellular structures called peroxisomes. Researchers are exploring dietary interventions and drugs that could activate this pathway to support weight control and metabolic health. Although some human evidence suggests potential relevance, the findings are from mice, and benefits of targeting the pathway in people remain to be tested.

Choked gamma-ray bursts occur when relativistic jets launched during massive-star collapse cannot escape the stellar envelope. Although gamma-ray emission is suppressed, these systems may produce high-energy neutrinos and electromagnetic transients from cocoon-driven shock breakout.

This study uses relativistic magnetohydrodynamic simulations to investigate jet propagation and shocks in supergiant progenitors. A preliminary survey of 39,000 one-dimensional jet models identified scaling relations for breakout and choking times, with stellar radius dominating breakout time. A shock-identification algorithm locates potential particle-acceleration sites using flow convergence, pressure jumps, temperature–density gradient alignment, and relativistic Mach numbers.

The detailed simulation follows a weakly magnetized jet in a blue supergiant with a radius of 50 solar radii and mass of 15 solar masses. The jet has a luminosity of 10⁵¹ erg/s, an initial Lorentz factor of seven, and a five-second engine duration. During injection, it develops external cocoon, termination, and internal collimation shocks. After shutdown, the collimation shock fades while the cocoon shock accelerates through decreasing stellar density. No choking occurs during the simulated 30 seconds; the study reports a choking time of approximately one minute after launch.

The evolving shocks may support particle acceleration, with dominant sites shifting outward after shutdown. Future work will calculate photon and neutrino spectra and light curves and explore additional blue- and red-supergiant models, jet properties, and viewing angles to assess detectability.

The lecture examines rapidity divergences and factorization in soft-collinear effective theory (SCET), focusing on applications to collider processes.

For the Sudakov form factor, dimensional regularization must be supplemented by a rapidity regulator. Renormalization introduces two scales, μ and ν, whose evolution is needed to resum large logarithms. Hard, collinear, and soft functions have different natural scales, but their combined scale dependence cancels in the physical observable. Evolution in the μ–ν plane is path independent, imposing consistency relations among anomalous dimensions. Counterterms remove regulator poles, and the resulting evolution kernels resum logarithms.

Higgs production at small transverse momentum provides another application. Its factorization theorem contains a hard function, transverse-momentum-dependent parton distribution functions (PDFs), and a soft function. Soft and collinear radiation have comparable transverse momenta, producing rapidity divergences and requiring both μ and ν evolution. Jet broadening in electron–positron collisions is another SCET II example.

The lecture then distinguishes three Drell–Yan configurations:
- **Inclusive:** Hard radiation is unrestricted. Factorization involves a hard function and ordinary PDFs; establishing the result also requires addressing Glauber exchange.
- **Threshold:** Nearly all collision energy enters the lepton pair, restricting remaining radiation to low energies. A separate soft function appears, and evolution resums threshold logarithms.
- **Isolated:** Measurements constrain small momentum components in two beam hemispheres, allowing collinear initial-state jets and ultrasoft radiation without requiring threshold kinematics.

Isolated Drell–Yan introduces beam functions, which describe both the incoming proton and initial-state jet radiation. They measure large and small momentum components, unlike ordinary PDFs. When the jet scale is perturbative, beam functions factorize into perturbative matching coefficients and standard PDFs. They also appear in exclusive jet-production factorization theorems.

The PSY-COVID study examined predictors of intention to follow COVID-19 preventive measures after confinement among 15,131 adults residing in Spain during the first pandemic wave. Participants were predominantly female (66.8%), university educated (75%), and residents of Catalonia (63.65%); their average age was 38.4 years.

Self-efficacy and outcome expectations were the strongest predictors of post-confinement preventive intentions. Other significant predictors included general adherence, time spent seeking pandemic information, previous preventive behavior, perceived vulnerability, proxy control attributed to scientists, and social norms. Perceived pandemic severity moderated the relationships of infection-avoidance adherence and perceived vulnerability of others with future preventive intentions.

Region of residence had a small but statistically significant influence. Preventive intentions were highest in the Canary Islands and lowest in Aragón and the Balearic Islands. Trust in scientists was substantially higher than trust in government.

Limitations included non-probabilistic sampling, exclusion of people without internet access, low reliability for some measures, and a focus on Spain during a specific pandemic period. The authors recommend strengthening confidence in performing preventive behaviors, providing clear and consistent public communication, and addressing regional differences in preventive behavior and healthcare resources.

The paper proposes a weighted expectation-maximization (EM) algorithm for estimating transition probability matrices in Markov cohort-state-transition models when observations have unequal intervals or missing transitions. Unlike the existing uniformly weighted approach, it assigns optimized weights to estimated one-step transition counts to reduce output variance. Weights are selected computationally through grid search, with bootstrapping used to estimate uncertainty.

A fictitious three-state model compares “SuperDrug” with placebo using monthly transitions among Healthy, Unhealthy, and Death states. Missing observations produce one-, two-, and three-month transition count matrices. Weight optimization targets variance in the incremental cost-effectiveness ratio (ICER), with uncertainty attributed solely to the estimated transition probabilities.

Across 5,000 bootstrap samples, optimized weighting reduced ICER variance by 15.2% and increased the probability of cost-effectiveness at £20,000 per quality-adjusted life year by three percentage points, while producing similar mean ICERs. The method does not necessarily increase estimated cost-effectiveness.

The authors caution that transition counts may need to come from the same or similar studies to avoid estimation bias. They recommend assessing whether data can be pooled and comparing weighted and unweighted approaches for precision and accuracy. Further validation using large clinical trials or real-world data is needed.

NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI-based image processing, and new shading techniques for games, professional graphics, and VR.

Memory and compression improvements give the RTX 2080 Ti approximately 50% higher effective bandwidth than the Pascal-based GTX 1080 Ti.

- **Display and video:** The display engine supports DisplayPort 1.4a, Display Stream Compression, two 8K displays at 60 Hz, native HDR processing, and tone mapping. NVENC supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps, with bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 decoding. Turing’s encoder improves streaming quality while reducing CPU utilization.

- **Connectivity:** VirtualLink combines VR headset power, display, and data connections through one USB-C connector. TU102 and TU104 replace earlier SLI interfaces with second-generation NVLink, providing up to 100 GB/s and 50 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, respectively. They support two-way SLI, but not three- or four-way configurations.

- **Ray tracing:** Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding volume hierarchy traversal and ray–triangle intersection testing, freeing shader resources for other work. Combined with denoising and hybrid rendering, they enable real-time ray tracing on a single Turing GPU. Rasterization handles tasks such as visibility, while ray tracing supplies reflections, refractions, shadows, and indirect lighting. The passage reports ray-tracing performance approximately ten times faster than Pascal.

- **AI graphics:** NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for graphics and image processing. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) targets image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work. DLSS 2X emphasizes higher image quality. Other NGX features include image inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and image or video upscaling. NGX does not support architectures preceding Turing.

- **Rendering efficiency:** Mesh shading introduces task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rates within 16×16-pixel regions, enabling content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading separates shading from visibility sampling and reuses computed results across views or frames. Multi-View Rendering supports four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API.

- **Products and resource support:** TU104 incorporates Turing’s major features and serves products including GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4. Tesla T4 targets inference workloads. TU106 powers GeForce RTX 2070 and includes RT and Tensor Cores but lacks NVLink and SLI. Turing also expands bindless resource access and permits different resource types within shared memory heaps.

The passage introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted measure combining Tensor, floating-point, ray-tracing, and integer operations, rather than simply adding their peak throughputs. NVIDIA provides the specifications without warranties and reserves the right to change them.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine supports moving pages between memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses. It offloads copying and mapping updates, pauses DMA traffic for safe migration, and can migrate guest pages protected by SEV or SNP. TMPM requires IOMMU enablement; software can check availability through the ENGINE_READY bit.

- **Migration commands:** PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO migrates pages targeted by concurrent DMA operations and requires the relevant IOMMU host page table entry location. It also migrates Hypervisor-state pages in SNP systems. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages from Guest-Valid or Guest-Invalid source pages to Pre-Migration destination pages. Afterward, sources become Pre-Migration pages and destinations inherit the sources’ original states.
- **Multi-page operations:** Commands support up to 128 pages, which need not be adjacent and may belong to multiple guests. Entries and commands must have no order dependencies. PM_SUCCESS means all pages migrated; PM_PARTIAL_SUCCESS requires checking individual statuses. Other overall return codes mean no migrations executed. PM_RMP_NOTEXCLUSIVE permits retry after a conflict is resolved.
- **Performance:** AMD testing found higher bandwidth with at least 16 pages per command and maximum performance with 128. Keeping the command ring buffer populated and limiting interrupt requests can improve throughput.
- **Restrictions:** Certain IOMMU structures, vIOMMU buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages cannot migrate. PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO source pages must be DMA-mapped through a single IOMMU host page table per physical page. Host software must avoid concurrent changes to referenced entries because TMPM may modify them non-atomically and set Access and Dirty bits.

The lecture examines coding gains, signal constellations, and the motivation for binary block codes.

For equally likely signals in additive white Gaussian noise, minimum-error decoding is equivalent to maximum a posteriori, maximum-likelihood, and minimum-distance decoding. Minimum-distance decision regions are convex Voronoi regions. Because exact error probabilities are difficult to calculate, the lecture uses the union-bound estimate:
\[
P_e\approx K_{\min}Q\!\left(\frac{d_{\min}}{2\sigma}\right),
\]
where \(K_{\min}\) is the average number of nearest neighbors.

In the power-limited regime, effective coding gain measures the reduction in required \(E_b/N_0\) relative to uncoded 2-PAM at a fixed bit-error probability, taken as \(10^{-5}\). At this error rate, 2-PAM requires approximately 9.6 dB. The estimated bit-error probability is
\[
P_b\approx K_bQ\!\left(\sqrt{2\gamma_c E_b/N_0}\right),
\]
with nominal coding gain \(\gamma_c=d_{\min}^2/(4E_b)\) and \(K_b=K_{\min}/\log_2M\). A rule of thumb is
\[
\gamma_{\mathrm{effective,dB}}\approx\gamma_{c,\mathrm{dB}}-0.2\log_2K_b.
\]
Thus, doubling the nearest-neighbor count per information bit costs approximately 0.2 dB.

Examples show that increasing minimum distance alone does not guarantee coding gain. Both 4-QAM and a two-point diagonal subset have zero gain relative to 2-PAM. A four-point subset of a three-dimensional cube provides approximately 1 dB of effective gain.

Orthogonal signal sets contain \(M\) equal-energy, mutually orthogonal signals. Their nominal gain is \(\tfrac12\log_2M\), while their nearest-neighbor count per bit is \((M-1)/\log_2M\). Although nominal gain grows without bound, effective gain remains bounded and approaches approximately 11.2 dB, corresponding to the ultimate Shannon limit of −1.59 dB. Practical drawbacks include spectral efficiency \(2\log_2M/M\), which rapidly approaches zero, and decoding complexity exponential in the number of transmitted information bits. Binary codes can provide the same effective gain with higher spectral efficiency. Related constructions include simplex sets, obtained by subtracting the orthogonal set’s mean, and bi-orthogonal sets, obtained by adding each signal’s negative.

In the bandwidth-limited regime, performance is measured by error probability per two dimensions against normalized SNR, using M-PAM as the baseline. Effective gain is estimated similarly, with nearest neighbors normalized per two dimensions.

The lecture concludes by introducing binary block coding: \(K\) information bits are mapped to \(N\ge K\) coded bits, then modulated as \(+\alpha\) or \(-\alpha\). This separates coding from modulation. Binary signaling limits spectral efficiency to two bits per two dimensions, but near one bit per two dimensions its fundamental penalty relative to unconstrained signaling is at most approximately 0.2 dB. This motivates studying binary block and convolutional codes in the power-limited regime.

A short squeeze occurs when a heavily shorted stock rises unexpectedly, forcing short sellers to buy back shares and pushing prices higher. Short sellers face potentially unlimited losses because stock prices have no theoretical upper limit.

Short squeezes are rare and typically last two to four weeks, though their duration depends on short interest, trading volume, and brokers’ actions. Notable examples include Volkswagen in 2008 and GameStop in 2021.

The passage reports no successful results from attempts to backtest short squeeze strategies. High short interest alone does not indicate an imminent squeeze, and stocks with high short interest underperformed those with low short interest in the cited backtests.

Suggested exit tactics include monitoring price momentum and short interest, setting stop-loss orders, and using trailing stops before prices reverse sharply.

Short squeezes can occur naturally, but schemes that manipulate stock prices or availability to cause a squeeze are illegal in the United States.

The study presents a multi-criteria integer model for selecting ambulance station locations that balances population coverage within two travel-time thresholds while ensuring all demand points remain reachable within a legally permitted maximum. It addresses the trade-off between rapid coverage in densely populated urban areas and more evenly distributed coverage across urban and rural areas.

The model was applied to relocating outdated ambulance stations in Southwest Germany. In the detailed example, four stations were selected from 17 potential locations, alongside 13 fixed neighboring stations. The study covered 70 municipalities, more than 450,000 inhabitants, and 20,444 road segments. Travel times were calculated using a detailed road network and ambulance speed profiles derived from emergency operations.

The objectives maximized population coverage within five and ten minutes, with mandatory coverage of every road segment within fifteen minutes. The analysis identified 16 Pareto-optimal solutions. Maximizing five-minute coverage favored urban locations, while maximizing ten-minute coverage produced a more even distribution, including rural locations. Compromise solutions offered substantial improvements in one objective with relatively small losses in the other.

The model assumes ambulances are always available at their stations. Consequently, its results served as an initial decision-support stage, followed by expert review and discrete-event simulation of promising alternatives. Decision-makers, rather than the model, determine the balance between urban and rural coverage. Proposed extensions include investment costs, multiple coverage, and simultaneous optimization of station locations and vehicle provision.

This study investigated whether brief resting-state stereoelectroencephalography (SEEG) recordings could identify the seizure-onset zone (SOZ) and predict treatment outcomes in 43 patients with drug-resistant focal epilepsy. Researchers analyzed 10-minute interictal recordings without epileptiform activity, measuring directional connectivity within and across frequencies and estimating excitation–inhibition balance from power-spectrum slopes. Clinical outcomes were assessed more than one year after treatment.

Information flow predominantly traveled from non-SOZ regions toward the SOZ across frequencies. SOZ electrodes received stronger inward information flow and had more negative power-spectrum slopes, suggesting lower excitability than non-SOZ regions. Greater within-frequency directional asymmetry—stronger non-SOZ-to-SOZ flow and weaker flow in the opposite direction—was associated with seizure freedom. Comparable outcome-related differences were not found in cross-frequency connectivity.

A balanced random forest classifier using within-frequency connectivity identified SOZ electrodes with 85% accuracy and an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.94. Seizure-outcome prediction achieved 77% accuracy and an AUC of 0.78 using clinician-identified SOZ, versus 72% accuracy and an AUC of 0.75 using model-estimated SOZ.

Limitations included using clinical SOZ as a proxy for the epileptogenic zone, relying on short recordings that may not capture temporal or behavioral-state variation, and excluding clinical variables from outcome prediction. The authors suggest that resting-state connectivity could supplement conventional SEEG interpretation and potentially reduce prolonged seizure monitoring, but prospective validation is needed. The passage is from a preprint not certified by peer review.

The statistical analysis plan specifies plasma glucose measurements, pharmacodynamic and safety analyses, reporting formats, and programming quality-control requirements.

- **Glucose and pharmacodynamics:** Plasma glucose is measured before dosing and at scheduled times through 45 minutes, with an additional 60-minute measurement for patients weighing at least 21 kg. The pharmacodynamic endpoint is the area under the glucose effect curve above baseline from 0–30 minutes, calculated using SAS. Concentrations, changes from pre-dose, pharmacodynamic metrics, and individual and mean concentration-time curves are presented by treatment group.
- **Efficacy reporting:** Planned outputs include time-to-glucose-recovery summaries, Kaplan–Meier curves, sensitivity analyses addressing rescue IV glucose, and analyses using interpolated recovery times. Recovery is defined as a plasma glucose increase of 20 mg/dL within 45 minutes without IV glucose. Additional analyses assess recovery and glucose changes at 10, 15, 20, and 30 minutes.
- **Exposure and safety:** All safety analyses use the safety set. Listings and summaries cover prior insulin administration, hypoglycemia induction, trial medication, rescue glucose infusion, injection-site tolerability, adverse events, laboratory tests, vital signs, ECGs, and immunogenicity. Time to first post-treatment IV glucose infusion is summarized descriptively only for patients receiving an infusion, without statistical testing.
- **Adverse events:** Most summaries are restricted to treatment-emergent adverse events, including events arising after dosing or existing events that worsen. Events are coded using MedDRA version 21.0 or higher and summarized by treatment group, system organ class, and preferred term. Possibly or probably related events are classified as related; unresolved missing causality assessments are also treated as related. Missing severity is not imputed. Uncertain onset dates are handled conservatively unless available information indicates that an event was not treatment-emergent.
- **Laboratory and ECG assessments:** Laboratory summaries include descriptive statistics, reference-range categories, categorical results, and changes from screening to follow-up. ECG reporting includes investigator assessments and QTcF thresholds above 450, 480, and 500 milliseconds, plus increases from baseline above 30 and 60 milliseconds.
- **Immunogenicity:** ADA occurrence is analyzed descriptively without statistical tests. Overall incidence combines patients becoming ADA-positive after a negative baseline and baseline-positive patients with at least fivefold increases in ADA titer, using evaluable patients as the denominator.
- **Protocol changes:** The primary efficacy analysis wording was revised, sensitivity and supportive analyses were added, and secondary efficacy terminology changed from recovery “within” specified times to recovery “at” those times.
- **Reporting and quality control:** Appendices define table, figure, and listing formats, rounding conventions, handling of incomplete dates, and calculation rules. Quality control covers SAS programs and logs, output accuracy, dataset validation, source-data checks, consistency of counts and percentages, figure verification, and documentation of findings and resolutions. Planned reporting includes efficacy, safety, pharmacokinetic, pharmacodynamic, and individual-patient outputs.

Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where efficient and ray tracing for reflections, refractions, shadows, and other effects. Denoising reduces the rays needed for useful image quality. NVIDIA reports ray tracing performance approximately ten times faster than Pascal.

- **AI-enhanced graphics:** NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks for graphics and image processing. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS) reconstructs images from fewer input samples to reduce shading work; DLSS 2X emphasizes image quality using target-resolution inputs. Other NGX features include image inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and image or video upscaling.

- **Rendering efficiency:** Mesh Shading introduces cooperative task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support flexible geometry processing. Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rates within 16-by-16-pixel regions, enabling content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading stores and reuses shading results independently of screen-space visibility, including across frames and stereo views.

- **Multiple views and resource management:** Multi-View Rendering supports up to four hardware views per pass and 32 views through the API, sharing geometry processing where possible. Applications include VR, character instances, and shadow maps. Turing also extends DirectX 12 resource binding and memory-heap support.

The architecture spans TU102, TU104, and TU106 products. NVIDIA introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted metric combining Tensor, floating-point, ray-tracing, and integer operations rather than simply adding their peak throughputs.

The passage presents variadic nominal anti-unification, a method for identifying structural similarities while abstracting differences in expressions containing variable binders and variable-length argument lists. Motivated by code clone detection, it addresses limitations of simpler techniques that struggle with inserted or deleted statements and overemphasize differences in local variable names.

The framework distinguishes bound atoms from substitutable variables. Individual variables represent single terms, while hedge variables represent finite, possibly empty sequences of terms. Permutations handle atom renaming, and freshness constraints restrict which atoms may occur freely in substitutions. Generalization is restricted to a finite set of atoms because unrestricted freshness constraints can prevent least general generalizations from existing.

The rule-based VNAU algorithm maintains unresolved problems, stored differences, freshness constraints, and a substitution representing the developing generalization. Its rules eliminate trivial matches, decompose terms and sequences, handle abstractions, solve differences, merge related problems, and narrow hedge variables to individual variables. The passage establishes termination, soundness, and completeness. Because some computed generalizations are not least general, subsequent minimization using matching is needed.

Code examples illustrate how the method accommodates bound-variable renaming, changed types, deleted statements, and additional function arguments. Stored differences support reconstruction of the original expressions, while freshness constraints describe restrictions on abstracted fragments.

The main limitation is excessive nondeterminism: exhaustive branching produces numerous alternatives and makes the basic algorithm impractical. A proposed refinement introduces a rigidity function to control which similarities are retained and reduce nondeterminism. Potential applications extend beyond clone detection to program analysis, refactoring, symbolic reasoning, and structural comparison in linguistic or mathematical domains.

The lecture introduces Lebesgue integration and measure theory as foundations for Fourier analysis and communication theory, particularly when working with irregular functions and random processes.

Riemann integration partitions the input axis, while Lebesgue integration partitions function values and measures the sets of inputs associated with each range. Lebesgue integration agrees with Riemann integration whenever the latter exists, but also accommodates functions that are not Riemann integrable.

An interval’s measure is its length, regardless of whether its endpoints are included. Measures add over countable collections of disjoint intervals. Sets that can be covered by intervals with arbitrarily small total measure have measure zero. The rational numbers provide a countable example, while a construction using ternary expansions illustrates an uncountable set of measure zero. Such sets contribute nothing to Lebesgue integrals.

A function is measurable when the input sets corresponding to its value intervals are measurable. Increasingly fine lower approximations establish that every nonnegative measurable function has an integral that is either finite or infinite. For example, the function equal to one at rational points and zero at irrational points on the unit interval has Lebesgue integral zero, although its Riemann integral does not exist.

The lecture defines:
- **L1 functions:** measurable functions with finite integrals of their absolute values.
- **L2 functions:** measurable functions with finite integrals of their squared magnitudes, interpreted as finite energy.

A function may belong to either class, both, or neither. However, every finite-duration L2 function is also L1. Complex functions are measurable when their real and imaginary parts are measurable.

For finite-duration L2 functions, Fourier coefficients exist and are finite. Their Fourier-series approximations converge in the mean: the energy of the approximation error approaches zero as more terms are included. This is emphasized as more useful for engineering approximation and quantization than equality at every individual point. Conversely, a coefficient sequence with finite total squared magnitude determines an L2 function in this limiting sense.

An arbitrary L2 signal can be divided into finite time segments, each expanded into a Fourier series. The resulting functions form an orthogonal expansion across both time segments and frequencies. This provides a conceptual basis for voice compression and represents changing frequency content over time. The lecture concludes by introducing Fourier-transform relationships and postponing precise conditions for their validity.

AMD’s Tiered Memory Page Migration (TMPM) engine supports moving pages between memory tiers while preserving guest physical addresses. It extends System Encryption, SEV, and SNP capabilities, requires IOMMU enablement, and exposes readiness through the ENGINE_READY status bit.

- **Migration capabilities:** TMPM pauses DMA traffic while copying pages and updating IOMMU mappings, allowing migration of pages actively used by I/O devices. It also migrates protected guest pages inaccessible to the hypervisor or operating system.
- **Commands and page states:** PM_PAGE_MOVE_IO handles DMA-targeted pages and hypervisor-state pages. PM_PAGE_MOVE_GUEST migrates SNP guest pages into Pre-Migration destinations. After guest migration, source pages enter Pre-Migration state, and destinations inherit the original source states.
- **Batching and status:** Commands support up to 128 pages, including nonadjacent pages and pages from multiple guests, without order dependencies. Partial success requires checking individual page statuses; certain conflicts permit retries.
- **Performance:** AMD testing found higher bandwidth with at least 16 pages per command and maximum performance at 128. Keeping the command ring buffer supplied and limiting interrupt frequency can improve throughput.
- **Restrictions:** Certain IOMMU structures, pinned backing buffers, the ring buffer, and argument pages cannot migrate. Software must avoid concurrent modifications to IOMMU host page table entries referenced by TMPM operations.
- **Firmware reload:** Reloading requires stopping operations and tearing down the ring buffer. Replacement firmware must have the same or a higher version. Reload procedures vary by EPYC family, identified through PM_GET_CAPABILITIES; software must check engine readiness before communicating with firmware.

This study examines how people use prompting strategies when seeking information from ChatGPT, how its communication styles adapt to prompts and issue controversy, and how responses influence users’ AI perceptions and issue-specific attitudes.

A nationally representative sample of 937 U.S. adults participated in a November 2024 experiment covering controversial and noncontroversial health, science, and policy topics. Participants were instructed to interact with GPT-4o for at least five turns. Researchers analyzed 747 valid conversations, measuring five communication styles—self-revealing, information-seeking, fact-oriented, action-seeking, and cognitive complexity—alongside citations, response structure, and prompting strategies.

The study reports that 19.1% of users employed at least one prompting strategy, with adoption predicted by education and party affiliation. Issue controversy affected ChatGPT’s communication styles and citation counts, while users’ communication styles remained consistent across controversy levels. Users evaluated cognitively complex AI responses less favorably but experienced more positive issue-relevant attitude changes with those responses.

The ADS868xW family comprises fully differential, 16-bit SAR data-acquisition devices with an integrated analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and precision reference.

- **Commands and data transfer:** Writes are synchronized to SCLK. Programming operations support one-byte or two-byte transfers; half-word commands ignore the least significant address bit. Register-configuration commands are 32 bits long and execute on the rising edge of CONVST/CS. Valid writes require at least 32 SCLK cycles per frame. Commands support reading, writing, setting, and clearing register bits.

- **Output data:** Each frame’s output depends on the preceding command and DATA_VAL settings. Output can contain a fixed pattern, eight- or sixteen-bit register data followed by zeros, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional appended information includes device identification, input range, supply and input alarm flags, and parity; unused output bits are zero.

- **Interface protocols:** The multiSPI interface supports four legacy SPI protocols, single- or dual-SDO outputs, and source-synchronous operation. SPI-00-S is the default after power-up or asynchronous reset. Protocol changes require an initial write using that default. Dual-SDO mode outputs two bits per launch edge. Source-synchronous mode supplies a data-synchronized clock through RVS, using a selectable internal or external clock source.

- **Registers:** Nine configuration registers control device identification, reset and power management, input and output protocols, output formatting, reference and input ranges, alarm status, and alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Device identification supports up to 16 devices. Writes to reset and power-control settings require first writing the protection key 69h to address 05h.

- **Application example:** An industrial eight-channel input module combines the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 differential multiplexer. Channels are software-configurable for current or voltage inputs. The ADC provides settling to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs and supports signals up to ±12.288 V on one analog supply. Programmable alarm thresholds and hysteresis support monitoring applications such as thermistor-based temperature sensing.

- **Power and layout:** Separate AVDD and DVDD supplies serve internal circuitry and the digital interface. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. Power-down disables analog blocks while retaining register contents and interface operation. Wake-up timing must be observed before conversions resume. Layout guidance emphasizes analog/digital separation, supply and reference decoupling, short ground connections, and capacitors close to device pins.

TI states that application guidance is outside the component specification and requires customer validation. The May 2025 revision changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data.

The study examined knowledge, attitudes, and uses of artificial intelligence in Hungarian education, alongside AI tools’ effectiveness in programming tasks. Interviews involved 14 high school teachers and university lecturers, while questionnaires were completed by 53 university students.

Respondents knew a range of AI applications, with ChatGPT recognized by all participants. Reported uses included debugging, generating code and practice tasks, explaining concepts, finding information, and summarizing materials. Most respondents (91%) viewed AI’s educational integration positively. Identified benefits included time savings, immediate answers, faster debugging, and support for independent learning. Concerns included cheating, excessive reliance, reduced learning effectiveness and critical thinking, and legal issues involving data use.

Programming assessments compared freely available, multilingual versions of Gemini, ChatGPT, and Microsoft Copilot. Reported overall accuracy was 64% for Gemini, 92% for ChatGPT, and 74% for Copilot. None achieved complete accuracy. In more complex programming tests, all three eventually completed HTML, JavaScript, and combined JavaScript/PHP tasks, sometimes requiring corrective prompts. Only ChatGPT completed the longer C programming task; the others supplied incomplete solutions and useful advice.

The study concludes that AI can support teaching preparation, practice, and assessment, but incorrect or incomplete responses limit its usefulness for learners without sufficient background knowledge. Critical thinking and prior subject knowledge help users identify errors and use these tools effectively.

The passage describes computer-implemented methods and systems for automatically generating orthodontic treatment plans using dental professionals’ individual or group preferences. These systems combine patient dentition information, such as digital scans, with treatment instructions and a preference database linking users, textual preferences, and corresponding clinical behaviors.

Preferences may be explicitly supplied or identified from historical instructions and approved treatment plans. Text analysis can use machine learning, similarity searches, or both to recognize different expressions of clinical preferences. Techniques include modified bag-of-words models and word-by-word Damerau-Levenshtein distance measures. Candidate preferences and associated behaviors may undergo manual or semi-automatic verification before inclusion in the database.

Statistical preference analysis identifies consistent clinical behaviors, including preferences not explicitly expressed in instructions. For measurable features, such as treatment stages for extractions or attachment removal, clustering methods can identify recent changes and multiple recurring behavior patterns. Analysis may be restricted to periods reflecting the user’s current practices.

The planning engine applies recognized preferences to patient-specific treatment plans, which users may review, modify, and approve before appliance production. User modifications can update the preference database. Monitoring tools compare automatically applied options with accepted plans, report detection performance, and identify incorrect or outdated preferences. One described example reports a reduction in treatment plans requiring changes from 12.48% to 8.5%.

The TPS7H500x-SP family comprises radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters. They require external gate drivers, support switching frequencies up to 2 MHz, and accommodate buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge topologies.

**Protection and compensation**
- The FAULT pin enables externally implemented protections. A voltage above 0.6 V typical triggers shutdown when sustained for the required minimum pulse width of 0.4–1.4 µs. Shutdown discharges SS and stops switching. Once FAULT falls below 0.5 V typical, soft-start resumes after approximately 15 switching cycles plus an internal logic delay. A renewed fault during this delay restarts the sequence.
- Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical junction temperature of 175°C; the power-up sequence restarts below 160°C typical.
- Slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation associated with peak-current-mode operation above 50% duty cycle. The minimum compensation is half the inductor’s falling current slope; the recommended value equals that slope. A resistor between RSC and AVSS sets compensation.
- Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation can be used. Type 2A adds a capacitor for high-frequency noise attenuation. Component selection depends on crossover frequency, power-stage transconductance, the dominant pole, and optionally the output-capacitor ESR zero.

**Synchronous push-pull design example**
The TPS7H5001-SP example uses GaN devices, a 500-kHz switching frequency, and a 5-V output. Selected parameters include:
- 205-kΩ frequency-setting resistor and 10-kΩ/1.4-kΩ feedback divider.
- Approximately 25-ns dead time and an initial 50-ns leading-edge blanking interval.
- 33-nF soft-start capacitor, producing approximately 7.5-ms soft-start.
- Transformer turns ratio of 2.5 and actual primary inductance of 40 µH.
- A targeted 35% maximum operating duty cycle, with the controller limited to 50%.
- 170-V primary GaN FETs and 80-V synchronous-rectifier GaN FETs.
- 0.47-µH output inductor and approximately 2.3-mF output capacitance.
- Approximately 35-A cycle-by-cycle current limiting, a 1:100 current-sense transformer, and a 7.5-Ω sense resistor.
- 3.3-nF hiccup capacitor, 10-kHz target crossover frequency, and Type 2A compensation using 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF.
- 102-kΩ slope-compensation resistor.

Output capacitance must satisfy ripple and load-transient requirements, with additional capacitance potentially needed to mitigate radiation-induced single-event transients. Optional output filtering reduces ripple, while an RCD clamp limits switch-node voltage. Blanking, clamp, and compensation values may require adjustment during testing.

**Supply and layout**
The controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least 0.1 µF of input bypass capacitance. Ceramic bypass capacitors should be close to the controller with low-impedance AVSS connections. Layout guidance includes minimizing switching-loop paths and switch-node copper, separating sensitive signals from switching traces, keeping high-current traces short and wide, and connecting analog and power grounds at one point. Compensation and filtering components should be placed near their associated pins.

Application guidance is not part of the component specification; customers are responsible for component suitability and design validation. The passage also provides documentation references, ESD precautions, revision history, packaging information, and warranty disclaimers.

The Affordable Care Act (Obamacare) changed Medicare, employer-sponsored insurance, individual coverage and Medicaid. President-elect Donald Trump and congressional Republicans pledged to repeal it, beginning with spending and revenue provisions, while potentially retaining coverage for children under 26 on their parents’ plans.

- **Medicare:** Full repeal would likely raise premiums, deductibles and cost-sharing, eliminate free preventive benefits and restore the prescription-drug coverage gap. The Congressional Budget Office estimated repeal would increase Medicare spending by $802 billion over 10 years.
- **Employer coverage:** Repeal would end the insurance mandate for larger employers. Some workers could lose coverage or free preventive services. Small-business employees could lose protections concerning pre-existing conditions, required benefits and age-based premiums.
- **Individual insurance:** Obamacare established exchanges and subsidies, required coverage of pre-existing conditions and essential benefits, prohibited annual and lifetime benefit caps, and limited out-of-pocket spending and premium differences.
- **Medicaid:** Expansion extended eligibility to low-income adults in participating states. Repeal would leave millions without insurance.
- **Uninsured:** Repeal would eliminate the requirement that nearly all Americans obtain insurance or pay a penalty.

BioRecall is a cross-sectional pilot study designed to supplement biobank records with lifestyle and environmental exposure data to support research on non-communicable diseases and gene–environment interactions. It will invite 1,386 potentially eligible Central Finland Biobank donors who have type 2 diabetes, available genome-wide genetic data, and consent to research recontact.

Participants will access a 30–40-minute electronic questionnaire through MyBiobank, provide consent, and complete the survey using REDCap. The questionnaire covers physical activity, diet, alcohol and substance use, body measurements, weight loss history, health, reproductive history, work, emotional states, sleep, residential environment, and socioeconomic characteristics. Postal codes will link responses to environmental and socioeconomic datasets. Pseudonymized survey responses will be combined with genetic and clinical records.

Participants will receive automated feedback on physical activity, diet, waist circumference, work stress, and sleep in relation to relevant recommendations. The study will also compare participants and nonparticipants using biobank information.

Data collection is scheduled to begin in February 2025. Because the primary aim is to pilot the operational model, no formal sample size calculation or detailed statistical analysis plan has been developed. Limitations include a restricted sample from one regional biobank, possible low participation because of questionnaire length, and the absence of wearable-device data.

The protocol received a favourable ethics statement and biobank approval. With participants’ consent, collected data will return to the biobank for future approved research, with access applications through Fingenious. If successful, the approach may expand to other donors and Finnish biobanks. The passage reports a study protocol, not research findings, and is a preprint that has not been peer reviewed.

Hong Liu introduces a graduate course on holographic duality. There is no textbook, recitation, or exam. Five problem sets account for 75% of the grade, and an 8–10-page final project accounts for 25%. The outline is flexible, and students are encouraged to ask questions and pursue independent reading.

The lecture contrasts gravity with other interactions, which are described by gauge theories on fixed spacetime. Classical gravity describes dynamical spacetime, while its quantum formulation raises unresolved questions about spacetime’s structure, black holes, and the universe’s beginning.

Holographic duality proposes that quantum gravity and a quantum field theory without gravity can be different descriptions of the same quantum system. This suggests that gravity and dynamical spacetime can emerge from nongravitational degrees of freedom. The course aims to explain this relationship, develop a dictionary between the descriptions, and explore its applications.

Liu reviews earlier ideas of emergent gravity and explains why massless spin-2 particles are central to this discussion. He introduces the Weinberg–Witten theorems: a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved current cannot contain charged massless particles of spin greater than one-half, and a theory with a Lorentz-covariant conserved stress tensor cannot contain massless particles of spin greater than one. These restrictions apply to elementary and composite particles.

QED, Yang–Mills theory, and general relativity are consistent with these theorems because their particles or conserved quantities do not satisfy all the relevant conditions. Holographic duality avoids the restriction on emergent gravity because its gravitational description occupies a different, higher-dimensional spacetime.

The lecture concludes with a proof based on Lorentz symmetry, helicity, conserved quantities, and the transformation of current and stress-tensor matrix elements under rotations.

DNA origami uses DNA base-pairing to assemble predefined nanostructures. DNA-PAINT uses dye-linked strands that bind transiently to complementary sequences, producing blinking signals that reveal binding sites. Assembly proved robust across varied physical conditions, but strand incorporation depended on position within the structure, and some sites remained unoccupied. Additional staple strands improved efficiency. The findings offer guidance for optimizing DNA nanostructure construction, while the researchers suggest potential applications in measuring labelling efficiency in quantitative structural biology.
