The paper studies modal extensions of lattice-based logics and how modal validities characterize lattice properties. It primarily interprets necessity as the greatest lower bound of a formula’s values across accessible worlds. The framework is motivated by interpreting one logic’s truth values within another and supporting communication between different logical systems, although this study restricts worlds to a single lattice semantics.

The authors distinguish regular modal extensions, where necessity means truth in all accessible worlds, from normal extensions defined through greatest lower bounds. For a complete lattice, the normal extension is regular exactly when the designated values form a filter containing their greatest lower bound. For finite lattices, being a filter suffices. Infinite examples demonstrate that normal extensions need not be regular.

The paper establishes connections between algebraic conditions and modal formulas:
- Validity of \((\Box\varphi \lor \Box\psi)\to\Box(\varphi\lor\psi)\) across all frames characterizes implicative designated values.
- With strictly deductive implication, validity of axiom K characterizes linearity outside the designated set.
- With implication defined as \(-a+b\), anti-monotone, involutive negation and down-distribution connect axiom K to implicativity.

An application to restricted twist algebras identifies designated sets supporting axiom K in paraconsistent semantics. Future research includes models accommodating different logics across worlds and conditions ensuring the finite-model property for computational applications.

Sony approached the PlayStation 3’s November 2006 launch facing strong competition despite the PlayStation 2’s market dominance. Microsoft’s Xbox 360 had a one-year head start, while Nintendo’s forthcoming $249.99 Wii targeted a broader audience with motion-sensitive controls. Sony’s premium PS3 cost $599, creating a potential barrier to adoption, although its built-in Blu-Ray player was cheaper than standalone players. The console also supported Sony’s effort to establish Blu-Ray against Toshiba’s competing HD-DVD format.

The industry’s history illustrated changing competitive advantages. Atari’s early success ended amid market saturation and poor-quality software. Nintendo subsequently dominated through quality controls, licensing restrictions, and popular games, before facing competition from Sega and Sony. Sony’s original PlayStation benefited from three-dimensional graphics, inexpensive CD production, and a broad game library. The PS2 combined gaming with DVD playback and held 55% of the console market by early 2006.

Console manufacturers generally sold hardware below cost and earned money through software sales and licensing royalties. Rising development budgets and increasingly blockbuster-driven sales encouraged publishers to acquire independent development studios, securing talent and reducing royalty payments. Sony’s game-business revenue increased in 2006, but operating income declined sharply.

Internet connectivity became central to the new console generation. Microsoft’s Xbox Live offered a unified online service, social features, subscriptions, and downloadable content. Nintendo planned online access to classic games, while Sony’s PlayStation Network would support multiplayer gaming, communication, and purchases. These services expanded competition beyond consoles toward connecting living rooms to the Internet.

Sony and Microsoft focused on experienced, predominantly young adult male gamers. Nintendo instead sought players across ages and genders through accessible games and intuitive controls, building on the success of its Nintendo DS handheld.

The industry also faced criticism over violent content and the accuracy of its voluntary ratings system. Legal restrictions encountered constitutional challenges, while proposed federal legislation sought to restrict sales of mature-rated games to minors.

Some analysts forecast continued Sony leadership, and PS2 sales remained strong immediately before the PS3 launch. Nevertheless, Sony faced pricing challenges, established competition, and uncertainty about whether its previous success would carry into the new generation.

Satish Gupta identifies housing finance and liquor as sectors receiving “astrological support” and claims financial astrology can guide investment timing. He promotes early subscriptions to his Samvat 2074 sector forecasts, citing claimed past successes in dyes, chemicals and sugar, including stock gains exceeding 500%. Moneycontrol.com states that these views belong to the contributor and advises consulting certified experts before making investment decisions.

The passage develops a Bayesian approach combining dynamic mode decomposition (DMD) with Gaussian process (GP) regression to model nonlinear dynamical systems from noisy measurements and estimate uncertainty in multi-step predictions.

DMD approximates infinite-dimensional transfer operators using finite-dimensional representations, enabling spectral analysis, forecasting, control, and dimensionality reduction. Kernel methods construct functional bases implicitly from data, while GP regression provides probabilistic predictions and a framework for model selection.

The proposed method gives a Bayesian interpretation of the embedded Perron–Frobenius operator and is a special case of extended DMD, inheriting some of its limitations. It integrates measurement noise, hyperparameter optimization, and sparse dictionary learning within one inference framework. To address the cubic computational costs of kernel-based DMD, the authors aim to apply the variational free energy method, balancing computational complexity and generalization without using every training input as a dictionary element.

The formulation assumes isotropic measurement noise on training targets and extends GP regression to outputs in a reproducing kernel Hilbert space using an operator-valued kernel. It begins by approximating noisy lifted observations as latent noise-free values plus zero-mean GP noise.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU uses the Ampere architecture to accelerate deep learning, high-performance computing (HPC), and data analytics through expanded Tensor Core capabilities, improved memory systems, workload partitioning, and faster interconnects.

- **Tensor Core performance:** A100 contains 108 streaming multiprocessors (SMs) and 432 Tensor Cores, delivering up to 312 TFLOPS of dense FP16/FP32 mixed-precision performance—2.5 times Tesla V100’s mixed-precision Tensor Core performance. Its Tensor Cores add TF32, BF16, and FP64 support alongside existing floating-point and integer formats. TF32 accepts FP32 input and produces FP32 output while using reduced internal precision, enabling Tensor Core acceleration without user-script changes. FP16 or BF16 mixed-precision training provides up to twice TF32’s throughput.

- **HPC acceleration:** FP64 Tensor Core operations deliver peak throughput of 19.5 TFLOPS, 2.5 times V100’s FP64 performance. Mixed-precision iterative refinement in cuSOLVER accelerates linear-system solutions while targeting FP64 accuracy. Across 37 test problems, TF32 achieved a geometric-mean speedup of 2.0 times over the reference FP64 solver and was the fastest and most robust Tensor Core mode tested.

- **Structured sparsity:** A100 supports a 2:4 pattern allowing two nonzero values in every four-entry vector. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zero-valued entries, doubling compute throughput while compressed weights halve their data footprint and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA’s inference workflow trains dense networks, prunes weights, and fine-tunes the remaining weights, with virtually no accuracy loss reported across evaluated networks. Training acceleration without accuracy loss remains an active research area.

- **Memory and data movement:** A100 provides 40 GB of HBM2 memory with 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per SM. Compared with V100, HBM2 bandwidth exceeds 1.7 times and L2 bandwidth reaches 2.3 times. Compute Data Compression offers up to fourfold improvements in DRAM and L2 bandwidth and up to twice the effective L2 capacity. ECC protects major memory structures.

- **Programming efficiency:** CUDA 11 supports A100’s Tensor Cores, sparsity, Multi-Instance GPU, cache controls, and asynchronous operations. Direct global-to-shared-memory copies avoid intermediate register storage, while asynchronous barriers enable overlapping transfers and computation. CUDA Graph optimizations reduce launch and execution-dependency overhead. L2 residency controls prioritize reused data, although cache set-aside functionality is disabled in MIG mode.

- **Workload isolation:** Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) partitions one A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources, predictable bandwidth, and fault isolation. GPU Instances can contain smaller Compute Instances and support MPS. MIG supports multi-tenant services, concurrent applications, and workload migration for utilization and maintenance.

- **Connectivity and additional hardware:** Twelve third-generation NVLink connections provide 600 GB/s aggregate bandwidth per GPU, twice V100’s. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction over an x16 connection and supports SR-IOV. Other additions include hardware JPEG decoding, five video decoders, optical-flow and stereo-disparity acceleration, faster atomics, and improved fault containment.

The DGX A100 system combines eight A100 GPUs through six NVSwitches, offering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and up to 56 isolated MIG instances. Its networking and software stack support deployments ranging from individual systems to large GPU clusters.

Baidu is incorporating NVIDIA Tesla P40 GPUs and deep learning software into Baidu Cloud. The companies are also partnering on a cloud-to-car autonomous vehicle platform. Baidu’s Autonomous Driving Unit is developing Level 4 technologies, targeting commercialization by 2018 and mass production by 2020.

The American Indian College Fund announced a two-year study funded by a $600,000 grant from Strada Education Network to assess the economic and social impact of five tribal colleges and universities in North Dakota. Working with the North Dakota Association of Tribal Colleges, the project will examine graduate well-being, employment, and institutional return on investment. It will include a Gallup College Values survey of 5,000 College Fund scholars and a pilot study on tribal colleges’ roles in preserving languages and culture and strengthening American Indian nations. Scheduled to conclude in September 2019, the project’s findings will be published and shared with state and federal policymakers.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 documentation describes device peripherals, implementation requirements, development support, and packaging information.

- **Power and clocks:** The power management unit regulates core supplies, monitors external voltage, and supports low-power operation. Clock sources include internal 32kHz and 32MHz oscillators, external 32kHz sources, and external high-frequency sources from 4MHz to 32MHz.
- **Data movement and events:** DMA transfers data without CPU intervention using two full-feature channels and one basic channel. The event manager routes peripheral events to the CPU, DMA, or other peripherals through static and programmable connections.
- **Memory:** Flash supports 1KB erase sectors, up to 100,000 program/erase cycles on 32 selected sectors, and up to 10,000 cycles elsewhere. SRAM provides zero-wait-state access, retains contents in RUN, SLEEP, STOP, and STANDBY, and loses contents in SHUTDOWN. SRAM write protection operates at 1KB resolution.
- **Digital and analog peripherals:** Devices support up to 45 GPIO pins and configurable pin multiplexing. The 12-bit ADC supports up to 1.6Msps with 10.6-bit ENOB using an external reference. Internal references are selectable between 1.4V and 2.5V and support ADC operation up to 515ksps. A temperature sensor includes factory calibration data. The comparator supports low-power wakeup, timer fault handling, and an 8-bit reference DAC.
- **Communications and timing:** Three UART peripherals support asynchronous communication and LIN. I2C supports rates up to 1Mbps and SMBus 3.0; SPI supports up to 16Mbits/s. Independent and windowed watchdogs supervise execution. The real-time clock provides calendar, alarm, periodic wakeup, and calibration functions. General-purpose and advanced timers support synchronization and peripheral triggers; advanced timers additionally provide PWM, dead-band insertion, and fault handling.
- **Security and debugging:** Features include code/data firewalls, CRC-16, and a two-wire Serial Wire Debug interface. Debug controls include peripheral halt behavior, mailbox communication, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. Read-only factory memory contains identification, capability, and trim information.
- **Implementation:** TI recommends nearby 10µF and 0.1µF supply-decoupling capacitors. NRST requires a 47kΩ pullup and 1000pF pulldown capacitor. External crystals require capacitors, and 5V-tolerant open-drain outputs require pullups for logic-high output. Specified package thermal pads must be soldered to the board.
- **Support and qualifications:** TI provides development tools, software, training, documentation, and support forums. “X” identifies experimental devices; “MSP” identifies qualified production devices. The September 2025 revision updates specifications and identification information, adds debug-subsystem documentation, and removes DGS32 package information. TI supplies design resources “as is”; customers remain responsible for component selection, design validation, testing, and compliance.

More than 400 Black-owned coffee shops and tea houses are expected to participate in National Eat at a Black Coffee Shop Day on May 29, 2018, when Starbucks closes over 8,000 U.S. locations for diversity training. Organized under The Black Star Project, the initiative seeks to attract customers and retain market share. Shops are also encouraged to host economic empowerment forums supporting a campaign to increase spending within Black communities.

Business planning is a dynamic process aimed at creating and capturing value. Entrepreneurs should ask why their opportunity matters, why now is the right time, why their team is suited to pursue it, and why it might fail.

Entrepreneur Bob Jones emphasizes that customers are essential to business success. Companies must understand what they are really selling, who wants it, who pays, and how to reach those buyers. An offering should be both unique and important to a specific customer group.

Jones contrasts two nutrition-product launches:

- **Regain**, a nutrition bar for dialysis patients, failed initially despite favorable clinical results and enthusiastic clinician feedback. Jones had surveyed clinicians rather than the patients who would purchase and consume it. Patients did not want it or could not afford it, taste was an issue, and retail pharmacy distribution required costly slotting fees. The company later obtained Medicaid reimbursement in 40 states and sold the business, recovering its investment.
- **NiteBite**, developed to address nighttime low blood glucose in people with diabetes, benefited from direct conversations with patients and parents. These revealed concerns about dying during sleep and a preference for discreet, nonmedical branding. Jones identified the central benefit as peace of mind.

NiteBite built demand through advertising, free samples, follow-up calls, and relationships with diabetes educators. Educators valued a product patients liked and would use. Demonstrated customer demand helped the company secure pharmacy and wholesaler distribution without paying slotting fees. The business was eventually sold to a pharmaceutical firm.

Jones recommends identifying actual buyers and their influencers, understanding each stakeholder’s motivations, and selling benefits rather than product features. Businesses should focus first on customers most motivated to buy, investigate existing alternatives, and distinguish between what people need and what they want.

Direct conversations and observation are important; surveys and emails alone are insufficient. Entrepreneurs should test a basic prototype, obtain customer feedback, change direction when assumptions fail, and establish evidence of willingness to pay before investing heavily in branding, packaging, or expansion.

Cadillac sold 35,020 vehicles globally in September 2017, up 16.5 percent, marking 16 consecutive months of growth. Year-to-date sales reached 256,613, up 20.9 percent. September sales increased 37.6 percent in China and 1.1 percent in the United States. The XT5 led sales with 103,645 deliveries worldwide in 2017. Cadillac remained on pace to exceed its 2016 sales total.

On November 29, 2016, NVIDIA’s Board amended and restated its bylaws, effective immediately, to implement proxy access and revise advance-notice provisions. A stockholder or group of up to 20 stockholders holding at least 3% of outstanding voting power continuously for three years may include director nominees in annual meeting proxy materials, subject to specified requirements. Nominees may constitute the greater of two directors or 20% of the Board.

Beginning with the 2018 annual meeting, non-proxy-access director nominations require notice 90–120 days before the prior meeting’s anniversary, replacing the previous 120–150-day window. Alternative deadlines apply when meeting dates shift by more than 30 days or no meeting occurred the previous year. The amendments also include administrative and conforming changes.

AMD shares rose more than 20% in premarket trading after announcing a multiyear agreement to supply OpenAI with AI accelerators, beginning with its MI450 series. OpenAI will receive warrants to acquire up to 10% of AMD’s equity, contingent on production and performance milestones. Analysts say the partnership could generate tens of billions of dollars in revenue if demand scales as projected, strengthening AMD’s challenge to Nvidia. However, production complexity, supply-chain bottlenecks, margin management and sustained demand remain risks. The agreement follows AMD’s previously announced $6 billion share buyback plan.

The study develops an Atomic Cluster Expansion (ACE) machine-learning potential for YBa₂Cu₃O₇ (YBCO) to model oxygen defects, diffusion, and its orthorhombic-to-tetragonal structural transition. Understanding these processes is important for high-temperature superconducting devices, particularly in radiation environments, because oxygen stoichiometry and defects influence superconducting properties.

The potential was trained on density functional theory (DFT) data comprising 1,368 configurations, including defect-free structures, vacancies and interstitials of all species, disordered environments, oxygen Frenkel pairs, and approximate transition states. It achieves energy and force errors of approximately 10 meV/atom and 70 meV/Å, respectively. Validation shows improved agreement with DFT compared with an existing Buckingham+Coulomb potential, particularly for lattice parameters, oxygen-defect formation energies, and migration barriers. Selected oxygen migration barriers agree with DFT within 20 meV.

Molecular dynamics simulations involving approximately 25,000 atoms and durations up to 75 ns reproduce the structural transition near 800 K, compared with approximately 1,000 K experimentally. The transition occurs as oxygen migrates from basal-plane CuO chains, and to a lesser extent apical sites, into sites between chains. This redistribution disrupts chain order and makes the two basal-plane directions equivalent.

The simulations indicate that the transition is entropy-driven and facilitated by thermal expansion, which lowers oxygen Frenkel-pair formation energies. Comparisons with experimental transition temperatures are complicated by oxygen loss in experimental samples, whereas the simulations conserve particle number. The potential’s underestimated formation energy for one oxygen Frenkel pair also contributes to the lower simulated transition temperature.

Further development requires variable oxygen contents and simulation methods accessing experimentally relevant timescales. The potential supports investigations of oxygen transport and may help optimize annealing strategies for restoring superconductivity in radiation-damaged tapes.

This non-empirical literature review examines artificial intelligence’s impact on inclusive education, addressing a shortage of studies explicitly connecting the two. Conducted from September 2023 to March 2024, it followed PRISMA guidelines and searched Web of Science, ScienceDirect, and IEEE Xplore.

Inclusive education seeks equitable opportunities for all students, regardless of background or disability. It requires more than shared classrooms: teaching, assessment, curricula, and environments must accommodate diverse needs and foster belonging. Barriers include inadequate teacher training, inaccessible materials, overcrowding, insufficient infrastructure and resources, discriminatory labeling, and limited family and community support.

The review identifies several potential benefits of AI:
- Personalized instruction, adaptive learning, timely feedback, and continuous assessment.
- Assistive features such as text-to-speech, speech-to-text, writing support, and word prediction.
- Greater student engagement, independent learning, and access to educational resources.
- Automation of grading, scheduling, data management, and other administrative tasks.

These benefits depend on appropriate implementation rather than technology alone. Educators should participate in designing, testing, evaluating, and managing AI tools, alongside students, parents, researchers, developers, and policymakers. AI can support educators but cannot replace their emotional support, creativity, or understanding of complex human experiences.

Limitations include biased data and outputs, implementation and maintenance costs, potential job losses, privacy and security concerns, and excessive technological dependence. Overreliance may weaken critical thinking and overlook learning’s emotional, social, and cultural dimensions. Some technologies also require training and may cause physical discomfort.

The discussion recommends accessible syllabi, assistive technologies, Universal Design for Learning, flexible mentoring arrangements, and asynchronous or offline materials. It emphasizes student-centered teaching, active participation, safe learning environments, inclusive curricula, and ongoing professional development.

The study lacks empirical data, fieldwork, and participants’ direct perspectives. Its literature coverage was limited and did not examine minority or marginalized groups’ sociocultural circumstances in depth. Further research should incorporate empirical methods, broader literature, and these groups’ experiences.

The lecture compares ion and neutral-atom trapping and explains radio-frequency ion traps and the Cirac–Zoller quantum gate.

Neutral atoms are confined using magnetic or optical forces, whereas ions experience much stronger confinement through electric forces, allowing room-temperature ions to be trapped. Both platforms support precision clocks, quantum information processing, and simulations of many-body systems. Sideband cooling, commonly used for ions, also applies to tightly confined neutral atoms.

Static electric fields alone cannot confine ions in every direction. Penning traps combine axial electrostatic confinement with radial confinement through cyclotron motion in a magnetic field. Paul, or radio-frequency, traps rapidly alternate between confining and anti-confining potentials. Although the force averages to zero at a fixed position, an ion’s driven micromotion produces a net restoring force when averaged along its trajectory. The kinetic energy of micromotion appears as an effective trapping potential for slower secular motion.

Quantum algorithms can be constructed from single-qubit rotations and two-qubit gates. A controlled-NOT gate flips a target qubit when the control qubit is 1. A controlled-phase gate changes the sign of the state in which both qubits are 1; single-qubit Hadamard operations connect these two gate types.

The Cirac–Zoller scheme uses shared center-of-mass vibration as a data bus between ions. After cooling this motion to its ground state, a sideband pulse transfers one ion’s internal qubit information into the vibrational state. A laser pulse through an auxiliary level then applies a conditional phase shift to another ion. Transferring the vibrational information back restores the control ion and resets the data bus.

The scheme illustrates how shared motion enables gates between selected ions. Its limitations include requiring ground-state cooling and restricting gate speed through the center-of-mass vibrational period. Other ion-gate approaches have therefore become more popular.

Judges are sanctioning lawyers for faulty legal citations linked to AI. In Puerto Rico, law firms will share $24,492 in fees after opposing counsel submitted at least 55 defective citations. The sanctioned lawyers denied using AI, but the judge questioned that denial. In California, attorney Amir Mostafavi was ordered to pay $10,000 to the court for AI-generated fake quotes and irrelevant cases in appellate briefs. Opposing counsel received no fees because they failed to detect the errors.

This non-peer-reviewed study examined racial differences in associations between blood pressure (BP) and cognitive decline among 2,284 Black and White adults aged 55 or older from three aging and dementia cohorts. Participants were classified as having normal, high, or variable systolic BP based on repeated annual measurements. Cognitive assessments measured global cognition and five domains. Analyses accounted for age, sex, education, and baseline diagnosis.

White participants with variable BP declined faster in global cognition and all five cognitive domains than Black participants across all BP categories. Among participants with high BP, White adults declined faster than Black adults in global cognition, processing speed, semantic memory, and working memory, but not episodic memory or visuospatial ability. Normal-BP groups generally showed similar decline, although White participants declined faster in working memory than Black participants with normal BP.

Results remained consistent when analyses accounted for cohort differences and alternative modeling of individual cognitive trajectories. Exploratory analyses indicated that lower baseline cognitive performance did not explain the slower decline observed among Black participants.

The authors discuss autonomic regulation and lifetime stress exposure as possible explanations for racial differences. Limitations include not accounting for medication adherence or comprehensive medication histories, which could influence BP classification and cognition. The findings highlight differences in BP-associated cognitive decline and the potential value of targeted interventions.

Stranger Things regulars reportedly secured season-three pay raises to $150,000–$350,000 per episode, with some earning up to 12 times their previous salaries. Millie Bobby Brown reportedly negotiated separately. Netflix declined comment; actors’ representatives did not immediately respond.

Addressing Congress after Franklin Delano Roosevelt’s burial, the new president calls for national unity and pledges to uphold Roosevelt’s ideals. He commits to continuing the war against Germany and Japan until unconditional surrender, retaining existing military leadership and strategy, and punishing war criminals.

He promises continued efforts to improve ordinary Americans’ lives and preserve democratic freedoms. Honoring military sacrifices, he stresses that lasting security depends on law, justice, and international cooperation rather than geographical barriers or temporary peace.

The president confirms that the San Francisco Conference will proceed and urges support for a strong United Nations Organization capable of settling international disputes and maintaining peace. He argues that nations must unite to defend peace under law, with powerful states serving rather than dominating others.

He appeals for congressional and public cooperation, advocates expanded international trade to increase production, employment, and living standards, and concludes by praying for wisdom to serve faithfully.

University of Birmingham academic Dr Chris Bradley said drains coped well during Sunday’s flooding. Birmingham City Council attributed flash floods to extreme rainfall rather than blockages, although a blocked grate was photographed on Tuesday. The Met Office issued a yellow weather warning for Birmingham and the West Midlands for Thursday, with thunderstorms, further flooding, frequent lightning and large hail possible.

Audi, BMW, Volkswagen and Volvo have discontinued several manual models locally amid low demand. Cuts include Audi’s A4 1,4T FSI, selected BMW 1 and 2 Series variants, Volkswagen’s Polo GTI and certain Scirocco and Jetta versions, and Volvo’s S60 T3 Kinetic. Porsche supports manuals, while Jaguar SA added manual F-Type versions.

Belgium agreed to facilitate potential development activities to increase Congo supplies. The United States requested that Congo supply and requirements data be sent simultaneously to British and American authorities for allocation by two combined boards in Washington. It also proposed considering restrictions on increases in Congo export duties. Postponement of the tripartite agreement was accepted, but negotiations ended without agreement after continuing through 1943; existing mechanisms handled supplies and purchases, and an informal Tripartite Supply Committee was established. The passage also references recognition of war with Hungary, Bulgaria, and Rumania; a July 1942 U.S.–Czechoslovak mutual-aid agreement; and U.S. efforts to prevent further Finnish participation in war against the Soviet Union alongside Germany.

The ETF rotation strategy ranks SPY (S&P 500), TLT (20-year Treasury bonds), and EEM (MSCI Emerging Markets) by their previous month’s performance, then holds the best-performing ETF for one month. Trades occur at month-end closes.

The backtest beginning in 2003 reported an 11% compound annual growth rate, with dividends reinvested and commissions, slippage, and taxes excluded. The strategy initially outperformed buy-and-hold with lower drawdowns, but its maximum drawdown rose from 22% before 2022 to 41% in 2022. Performance has been weaker over the last five to six years. Frequent trading makes a tax-deferred account preferable, according to the article.

Ineos shut down the 450,000-barrel-per-day Forties Pipeline System after a crack widened, warning repairs could take weeks. The pipeline carries nearly 40 percent of UK North Sea oil production and supports the Brent benchmark. Brent prices rose nearly 2 percent above $64.50 per barrel, reaching a two-year high. The outage could force offshore production shutdowns and disrupt up to 10 million barrels over three weeks. Replacement purchases could tighten Atlantic Basin supplies, while a wider Brent-WTI price gap could boost demand for U.S. crude exports and accelerate inventory declines.

Charlie Javice, founder of financial-aid startup Frank, was sentenced to 85 months in prison for defrauding JPMorgan Chase, which acquired the company for $175 million in 2021. Frank had fewer than 300,000 real customers, while millions of additional identities were fabricated.

A jury convicted Javice and chief growth officer Olivier Amar on three fraud counts and one conspiracy count. Javice also received three years of supervision, $22.36 million in forfeiture and $287 million in restitution to JPMorgan. She will remain free on bail during her appeal.

Javice expressed remorse and requested forgiveness. Prosecutors had sought 12 years in prison, while Judge Alvin Hellerstein emphasized the need to deter others. JPMorgan failed to verify Frank’s claimed customer numbers before the acquisition.

The S&P 500 fell 2.36% last week and 3.33% from Thursday’s record high over two days, closing Friday at its lowest level since early July. A roughly 0.5% rebound was expected Monday, though the article warns that a deeper correction remains possible. The VIX reached 21.90, its highest level since June 23.

Crude oil dropped 2.79% Friday and another 2.1% Monday after OPEC+ announced a September production increase of 547,000 barrels per day. Higher supply and weakening demand indicators could pressure prices, while potential U.S. measures against Russian oil buyers could reduce supply.

Upcoming earnings, tariff uncertainty, seasonal weakness and stretched valuations are highlighted as reasons for careful position management and potentially more defensive positioning.

The Scripps National Spelling Bee includes 113 returning competitors this year. Finalists Erin Howard, 13, Cameron Keith, 12, and Naysa Modi, 12, devote hours to daily preparation, sometimes sacrificing social activities. Erin studied more trademarked words after misspelling one last year, while Cameron says experience has reduced his competition stress. Naysa’s father credits years of intense effort for her progress and says preparing together has strengthened their relationship. For these repeat competitors, participation involves not only pursuing victory but also appreciating words, language and hard work.

The S&P 500 reached a 9.1% return as strong earnings contrasted with signs of economic slowing. July added 73,000 jobs, below expectations, while May and June totals were revised down by 258,000. June data had been largely positive, with 12 of 20 key indicators exceeding expectations.

S&P 500 second-quarter earnings growth estimates rose from 7.7% to 11.2% during the week, while sales growth increased from 4.5% to 5.6%. AI has supported market performance, but elevated valuations and economic weakness remain concerns.

After July’s 11th consecutive annual gain, the market faces the historically weaker August–October period. The passage anticipates possible near-term weakness while noting that an economic slowdown does not necessarily mean a recession.

Most Southeast Asian stock markets fell Thursday amid concerns that Federal Reserve plans to reduce its $4.5 trillion balance sheet could trigger regional capital outflows. Investors also remained cautious ahead of a meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping. Indonesian shares bucked the trend, closing at a record high for a fourth consecutive session of gains, led by financials. Philippine shares fell 0.3 percent, with financial and property stocks leading declines. Vietnam and Thailand markets were closed for holidays.

The Seattle Mariners beat the Texas Rangers 2-1 for their ninth win in 10 games and major league-leading 16th one-run victory. Marco Gonzales pitched 6 2/3 innings without allowing an earned run, extending his streak to 19 1/3 innings. Nelson Cruz and Kyle Seager hit RBI singles in the sixth after a defensive miscue helped Seattle’s rally. Texas scored its only run on a passed ball. Alex Colome pitched a scoreless eighth inning, and Edwin Diaz earned his 19th save. Denard Span went 0 for 4 in his Mariners debut.

In Wiechmann v Wiechmann, the Michigan Court of Appeals affirmed a divorce judgment granting the parents joint legal custody of their four children, with physical custody of the two older children awarded to the father and the younger twins to the mother. The mother appealed, seeking custody of all four children and arguing that the siblings should remain together. A custody specialist had recommended awarding her custody of all four.

The trial court evaluated the statutory best-interest factors and found the parents essentially equal, except that stability and continuity slightly favored the father. The appellate court held that courts should seriously consider sibling bonds and the potentially harmful effects of separation. Although keeping siblings together generally serves their interests, each child’s individual best interests control when those interests conflict with keeping siblings together. The court found no palpable abuse of discretion or legal error in the custody arrangement.

Later temporary custody orders gave the father custody of the twins, but the appellate court lacked a permanent custody-change order and declined to treat the appeal as clearly moot.

FCA survey data shows 70% of adults planning to access defined contribution pensions within two years had not been asked by providers about their plans. Some 67% had not received advice from their pension provider. Among those who had not taken retirement-planning advice, 40% felt able to decide independently. One-third expected the state pension to be their largest retirement income source, while 44% had a good idea of their expected annual retirement income.

Taxify will launch in Sydney on Tuesday, its first Australian market, offering half-priced fares for one month. More than 4,000 drivers have registered. The company charges drivers a 15 per cent commission, almost half Uber’s rate, and operates in 20 countries. Public-holiday surge pricing will be capped at 1.5 times normal fares.

Officials broke ground Wednesday on the Mauka Concourse at Daniel K. Inouye International Airport. The $220 million project will add gates capable of handling larger aircraft and 260,000 square feet of space. Completion is expected by late 2020, as part of a $1.3 billion airport modernization project.

Index Markets Research’s Global Plastic Granules Market report examines market size, trends, growth drivers, competition, revenue forecasts, manufacturing costs and production capacity. It covers North America, China, Europe, Southeast Asia, Japan and India, with historical data and forecasts spanning 2012–2022. Product types include PP, HDPE, PPCP, LLDPE, LDPE and others; applications include plastic products and clothing. The report assesses market volume and value, leading companies’ strategies, emerging opportunities and development challenges. It also includes new-project SWOT analysis, investment assessments and recommendations for companies.

AMD’s Seamless Firmware Servicing (SFS) enables secure, non-persistent updates to selected running firmware and settings without a BIOS reflash or system reset. It addresses priority runtime issues in AMD-provided binary firmware, including ASP firmware, modules, and register settings. It does not update x86-executed BIOS components or boot-time run-once code. Patches serve as interim measures between BIOS releases and must be reapplied after every reboot.

Customers must enable SFS through BIOS configuration, test and validate patches in their environments, and provide an SFS Deployment Agent to initiate and track updates through the PSP/ASP driver. Packages target specific firmware and patch levels and must be applied sequentially.

SFS tracks the overall SFS Patch Level, individual firmware versions and Security Patch Levels, and a System Patch Level for changes made by SFS run-once code. SFS and System Patch Levels increase monotonically. Packages check existing versions and system state before applying updates.

AMD cryptographically signs every package, and the ASP verifies signatures before execution. Optional customer co-signing provides additional deployment control. When enabled, the customer’s public key must be supplied during early boot and cannot be changed afterward. Customers are responsible for maintaining their keys.

The deployment agent prepares an aligned memory buffer and submits commands through the ASP interface. The ASP checks memory protection, verifies required signatures, executes the patch, updates version information, and returns status. Updates are not applied until package validation completes.

Packages can modify registers, replace firmware images, or update firmware components. Updates are designed to minimize performance disruption while x86 and DMA traffic continue. SEV or SEV/ES virtual machines must stop and restart for SEV firmware updates, while SEV/SNP virtual machines can continue operating. Reverting an SFS-updated SEV firmware image requires a system reboot.

Research suggests that air filters and improved school ventilation can raise test scores and reduce absenteeism at relatively low cost. Following a California gas leak, schools receiving air purifiers saw math gains equivalent to about three months of learning, with similar English improvements. Costs were approximately $30 per student, far below those of a class-size reduction intervention producing comparable gains. Further research is needed to confirm these effects.

Other studies reported a 12.5% reduction in student absenteeism with air purifiers and a 55% decline in illness-related absences at Swedish daycare centers. Cleaner air may support cognition, reduce respiratory illnesses and particularly benefit students in low-income communities exposed to greater pollution and poorer building conditions.

The author recommends restarting unused air cleaners, replacing filters and piloting broader installation. Schools should track academic and health outcomes, while philanthropies, advocates and researchers support equipment access, air-quality standards and larger trials.

Research identifies sudden, potentially irreversible changes across Australian ecosystems caused by the combined pressures of gradual climate change and extreme weather. Rising temperatures, more frequent heatwaves, fires and droughts, and shorter recovery intervals are overwhelming natural resilience.

Six case studies document changes including kelp forests becoming seaweed turfs, wildfire destruction of Gondwanan refugia, floodplain forest dieback, alpine forests converting to shrubland, arid-zone population fluctuations, and widespread mangrove dieback. Only one ecosystem had previously experienced substantial human disturbance, indicating that relatively undisturbed systems are also vulnerable.

Ecosystem collapse threatens biodiversity, fisheries, forest resources, carbon storage, tourism and water supplies. Predicting collapses is extremely difficult. Targeted interventions may help but are costly, face declining chances of success as extreme events become more frequent, and may have unintended consequences. The researchers suggest that risks of inaction may increasingly outweigh those of intervention.

The Bengals will start Joe Flacco against the Packers after acquiring him from the Browns for a 2026 fifth-round draft pick, with Cincinnati also receiving a sixth-round selection. Coach Zac Taylor said Flacco will take all practice reps before Sunday’s game.

Cincinnati is 2-3 after losing three consecutive games with Browning starting in place of Joe Burrow, who is recovering from surgery for a left-foot turf toe injury. Browning will return to the backup role, and Burrow’s return timetable remains uncertain.

Flacco, 40, led Cleveland to a 13-10 win over Green Bay in Week 3. Taylor said that experience should help Flacco prepare as Cincinnati seeks to end its losing streak and remain in playoff contention.

Iamgold Corp (NYSE:IAG) closed at $4.90, unchanged in its latest session. Thirteen analysts projected an average 12-month price target of $7.65, ranging from $6.25 to $9.05. Recommendations included 3 Buy, 6 Outperform, 6 Hold and 2 Underperform ratings, with no Sell ratings. Its average brokerage recommendation was 2, and its industry ranked 194 of 265. The stock’s ATR-14 was 0.20, weekly volatility 3.09%, monthly volatility 3.60% and RSI 30.76. Market capitalization totaled $2.29 billion, with 468.31 million shares outstanding. The Covid-19 pandemic prompted widespread adoption of distance education, highlighting the need for alternative educational systems and effective infrastructure. This literature review examines artificial intelligence (AI) as a possible component of education during emergencies and ordinary circumstances.

Advances in machine learning, deep learning and artificial neural networks allow computers to learn from large datasets. Educational applications include personalized instruction, assessment, student support, administration and game-based learning. Intelligent Education Systems adapt instruction to learners’ needs and progress through domain, pedagogy and learner models, using analysis and feedback to guide subsequent activities. Existing systems depend on human-defined models and activities; the passage also considers systems that independently determine educational content and methods.

Three approaches are proposed:
- AI-supported face-to-face teaching by humans.
- Face-to-face teaching delivered by AI through robots or screens.
- AI-led education in simulated environments.

These approaches may use human-supervised algorithms or self-training AI that develops personalized curricula. Simulated education could involve virtual reality equipment or, potentially, connections between computers and biological neural networks, although the latter integration is not yet fully possible.

Potential benefits include individualized instruction at scale, improved learning and motivation, richer learning experiences, reduced training costs and risks, and more efficient educational management. The passage cites studies reporting improvements in scientific reasoning, prediction performance and students’ emotions. Fully controlled simulations might also reduce bullying and classroom discipline problems.

Potential risks include diminished human interaction, isolation, educator unemployment, privacy breaches, manipulation, cyberattacks and psychological difficulties. Immersive simulations could affect personality development, adjustment to everyday life and distinctions between virtual and real experiences. Whether machines can educate people more effectively than humans remains unresolved.

The review concludes that AI-based education warrants further research and serious ethical, social and philosophical discussion. Although computers have not reached human mental capacity, technological developments may substantially change educational roles and institutions.

El neuromarketing aplica conocimientos y técnicas neurocientíficas al estudio del consumidor y complementa los métodos tradicionales de investigación de mercados. En el sector audiovisual se utiliza para analizar contenidos, promociones y bloques publicitarios, con el objetivo de mejorar la competitividad y el retorno de la inversión.

El estudio examina su implantación en España mediante 18 entrevistas realizadas entre junio y septiembre de 2015 a consultoras, representantes del sector audiovisual, neurocientíficos y académicos. Los resultados indican que estudiar al consumidor audiovisual mediante estas técnicas es viable, pero presenta limitaciones éticas, de representatividad de las muestras y de interpretación y aplicación de los datos. La investigación requiere equipos multidisciplinares con formación en neurociencia, marketing y comunicación, así como protocolos basados en el método científico.

Su implantación española es incipiente y se concentra principalmente en Atresmedia y Mediaset España. Las cinco consultoras entrevistadas habían trabajado para la industria audiovisual, que representaba, en promedio, el 33% de su volumen de trabajo y el 38% de su facturación. Entre las barreras señaladas figuran el desconocimiento, la desconfianza, las malas prácticas, la escasa disposición a innovar, los costes y la limitada aplicabilidad de algunos resultados.

Mediaset emplea registros de actividad electrodérmica, complementados con encuestas, para evaluar ficción y fundamentar cambios durante la producción. Atresmedia mantiene estudios sobre atención y memoria en bloques publicitarios, pero abandonó una experiencia de análisis de contenidos por dificultades para identificar las causas de los resultados. Según su antiguo proveedor, TVE dejó esta investigación por motivos económicos.

Las productoras cinematográficas y televisivas muestran interés creciente, aunque los bajos presupuestos, la falta de personal intermediario y la escasa cultura investigadora dificultan su incorporación. Los entrevistados prevén una evolución positiva, condicionada al desarrollo y la estandarización tecnológica, la mejora interpretativa, el abaratamiento de los estudios y la demostración de su eficacia. Actualmente, estas metodologías no responden a todas las preguntas de los principales grupos mediáticos españoles.

IES Holdings’ shares have nearly doubled year to date, outperforming infrastructure and Russell 2000 stocks. Despite challenges in its residential division, data center projects are supporting growth in its next two largest divisions. Backlog exceeds $2 billion, growing more than 20% year over year, alongside improved cash flow and record cash balances. The article recommends waiting for a pullback, citing the stock’s overextended position, subpar free cash flow yield and increased insider selling.

This retrospective cohort study used survey and electronic health record data from the All of Us Research Program to examine how social determinants of health predict healthy aging among approximately 100,000 adults aged 50 and older. Healthy aging was defined using age thresholds and a composite measure of comorbidities, cognitive impairment, and assisted-living status. About 44% of the primary cohort met the criteria.

Researchers compared logistic regression, multi-layer perceptron, and XGBoost models. XGBoost with random oversampling performed best, achieving an AUROC of approximately 0.79 in the primary cohort and 0.86 in a secondary cohort using a higher age threshold. Positive and negative predictive values were similar across the assessed race and sex groups.

Health insurance type was the strongest predictor, followed by employment status, substance use, and insurance coverage. Substance and alcohol use were unexpectedly positively associated with healthy aging; the authors suggested selection bias and behavioral changes as possible explanations.

Limitations included an incomplete definition of healthy aging, restricted coverage of comorbidities, potential volunteer-selection bias, limited generalizability, and unmeasured confounders. The findings emphasize health insurance’s association with healthy aging and the potential value of incorporating social determinants into prediction models and public health strategies. The passage is a preprint that had not been peer reviewed.

Institute manager Kevin Deery expressed frustration after a draw with Larne extended his side’s run to three consecutive draws. He blamed missed chances, poor decision-making in both penalty areas and bad luck, noting their last two goals were own goals. Despite remaining outside their desired position, Institute were still in the top six with 13 games remaining. Deery maintained confidence in his players.

Virginia defeated North Carolina 71-63 to win the ACC Tournament championship, ending the tournament’s two-year run at Barclays Center. The Cavaliers began the season unranked and picked to finish sixth in the conference. North Carolina beat Duke to reach the final. Other coverage highlighted Marvin Bagley III’s performance and Clemson’s win over Boston College.

On October 22, 2001, Enron shares fell 21% to $20.65 after the company disclosed an SEC request for information about related-party transactions involving partnerships formerly run by Chief Financial Officer Andrew Fastow. Enron characterized the request as an informal inquiry, pledged full cooperation, and said its auditors, attorneys and board had reviewed the arrangements.

The partnerships drew scrutiny over potential conflicts of interest and their financial impact. Enron reported a $35 million partnership-related charge and a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholders’ equity associated with unwinding arrangements. The company also reported $1.01 billion in third-quarter charges, largely involving failed investments.

A shareholder derivative lawsuit alleged that Enron’s board breached its fiduciary duties by allowing Fastow to operate the partnerships. A separate securities class action alleged that Enron and certain executives concealed or misrepresented partnership transactions, artificially inflating its stock price.

Investors expressed concerns about additional financing obligations, potential shareholder dilution and credit-rating downgrades. Moody’s placed Enron’s debt under review for a possible downgrade, while AG Edwards lowered its stock recommendation from “buy” to “hold.”

Broader U.S. stock indexes rose as several companies reported earnings exceeding reduced expectations, despite anthrax concerns and signs of economic weakness.

Separately, UniPrime Capital announced a letter of intent to acquire a partial interest in a California wind park ground lease owned by Enron Wind Development.

Former Maui County Councilmember and 2018 mayoral candidate Mike Victorino struck two teenagers, ages 18 and 15, while driving on April 13. Both sustained nonlife-threatening injuries. Victorino stopped and waited for emergency responders. Police did not believe speed or alcohol contributed. Their initial investigation indicated the pedestrians were outside a crosswalk, but the older teenager’s mother said her son reported they were in one.

The study evaluates replacing internal combustion vehicles with battery electric vehicles (BEVs) using one year of telematics data from 10,441 private car users in Asti, Italy. After cleaning, the dataset contains approximately 10.1 million trips covering 98.9 million kilometres. Simulations replicate existing trips without changing routes or schedules, comparing four BEV models and four charging policies: workplace, low-battery AC, overnight AC, and low-battery fast DC charging.

Workplace-only charging performs worst, enabling users to complete an average of 64–88% of trips depending on the vehicle. Fast DC charging performs best. With the largest-battery model, the Audi A6 e-tron, 95% of users can complete at least 99% of their trips, while 72% can complete every trip without changing driving habits. Overnight charging makes the smaller Fiat 500e suitable for 35% of users under the 99% threshold.

Charging policies also affect charging frequency and remaining battery charge. For the Audi, low-battery AC and fast DC policies require nearly half as many charging sessions as overnight charging. Overnight charging produces the highest average post-trip state of charge, exceeding 70% for every model.

The results indicate that current BEVs can meet many users’ mobility needs but cannot accommodate everyone’s unchanged travel patterns. The simulations assume accessible charging infrastructure, constant charging power, and energy consumption unaffected by external conditions. They exclude costs and lack precise user and charger locations. Applying the method elsewhere would help assess generalizability.

CSU’s Board of Governors reviewed the first two on-campus stadium gamedays. Student government plans rebranding and pre-game programming to increase awareness and use of the student tailgating lot. Attendance was 37,583 at the first game and 27,038 at the second, with entry and concession congestion improving. Transportation planning generally worked well: 7,000 attendees used transit at the first game, exceeding the predicted 5,000, and post-game traffic was not overwhelmed. About 50 vehicles were towed from campus gameday lots each weekend, with similar numbers towed from surrounding neighborhood parking zones.

The Canadian dollar rose nearly 2 per cent from the previous week to almost 75.50 U.S. cents Wednesday, supported by strong economic data and expectations of a Bank of Canada interest rate increase. Lower oil prices and a widening Canada-U.S. interest rate gap had weighed on the currency. The bank appears to favour a weaker dollar to support exports, but recent statements from officials suggested tightening could come sooner than expected. CIBC now forecasts a rate increase in the fourth quarter rather than 2018. Economist Andrew Grantham attributed the loonie’s perceived volatility to its lack of clear direction.

Linebackers typically line up 3–5 yards behind the defensive line, relay coaches’ calls, organize defensive positioning, and defend against both runs and passes. The position requires toughness, athleticism, intelligence, tackling, block shedding, strength, and coverage skills. Its name reflects its location behind the defensive line and its original role supporting run defense.

Linebacker roles include Sam (strong side), Mike (middle), Will (weak side), and Jack (usually a second middle linebacker in a 3–4 front). Notable players include Hall of Famers Ray Lewis, Chuck Bednarik, and Lawrence Taylor.

Although passing-oriented offenses have reduced the value of inside linebackers relative to edge defenders and defensive backs, versatile linebackers remain valuable. Their ability to rush passers, cover receivers, and stop runs allows defenses to disrupt offenses and adapt to different matchups.

The Great Southern Storm have named an initial 45-player colts squad for next month’s carnival in Kulin. New coach Glynn Verbruggen replaces Phil Gilbert, who has moved to Perth. The squad includes State 16 players Heath Spinks and Jacob Blight, plus eight players who have represented State Country colts this season. North Albany has the largest representation with 12 players. Training sessions will be held at Railways on June 4 and 11 before the final travelling team is selected.

Discussing his memoir “Misunderstood” on ESPN’s “First Take,” Allen Iverson described his 2013 divorce from Tawanna Turner as his lowest point, prompting deep self-reflection. The divorce coincided with his retirement from basketball. Iverson confirmed that he and Turner are back together. Reflecting on his journey to sobriety, he said he recognized alcohol as a problem associated with negative experiences. He also discussed his influence on younger NBA players, saying he helped them feel comfortable expressing themselves.

The February 6, 2002 news compilation covers investigations into Enron’s collapse, its bankruptcy proceedings, and broader concerns about corporate accounting.

- Congressional committees expanded hearings and subpoenaed former chairman Kenneth Lay. Representative Billy Tauzin expected former chief executive Jeffrey Skilling to testify Thursday without invoking the Fifth Amendment. Former chief financial officer Andrew Fastow was reportedly seeking immunity.
- Internal investigator William Powers testified that Enron’s partnerships concealed losses, inflated earnings by $1 billion over 15 months, and enriched executives. He said senior management failed to provide oversight and should have understood the risks, but declined to characterize the conduct as fraud. Investigators also reported threats against employees who challenged partnership dealings.
- Arthur Andersen chief executive Joseph Berardino faced criticism over auditing failures and document destruction. He maintained that Enron withheld information and disputed claims that Andersen actively established the partnerships.
- Hearings examined employees’ retirement losses, executive bonuses, and restrictions on retirement-account trading during Enron’s stock decline. Labor Secretary Elaine Chao was scheduled to discuss stronger retirement protections.
- Enron’s proposed bankruptcy financing, initially projected at $1.5 billion, was expected to shrink to $250 million–$500 million. Banks were reluctant to participate, while Enron’s lawyer cited stronger-than-expected cash holdings.
- County officials said Enron’s broadband unit owed approximately $440,000 in back taxes. Enron opposed the Houston Astros’ effort to end their stadium naming agreement, arguing that the rights could retain value for creditors.
- Spain’s energy regulator planned to investigate Enron’s distribution operations. Other coverage described accounting fears affecting corporate bonds, debated professional responsibility and whistleblowers’ career prospects, and presented satire about Enron’s accounting and political connections.

The study examined whether role-taking and literacy interventions could reduce demographic and appearance-based biases in trust and risk-taking decisions related to social engineering. Such attacks exploit psychological cues, including perceived age, gender, ethnicity, and attire, rather than technical vulnerabilities.

An online experiment involved 139 participants identifying with Arab cultural traits, divided into persuader, persuadee, literacy, and control groups. Before and one week after the interventions, participants evaluated 16 personas offering mobile internet hotspots, rating their willingness to accept and their perceptions of security risk. Role-taking participants completed three sessions involving financial-advisor and lettings-agent scenarios. Literacy participants completed two sessions examining stereotypes and alternative perspectives; controls received no intervention.

Neither role-taking nor literacy significantly reduced demographic or appearance-based biases in trust or risk-taking. Bayes Factors provided moderate to strong support for the absence of intervention effects. Adjusting for age, self-esteem, and self-efficacy largely preserved these findings, although self-esteem showed a small interaction with changes in attire-related trust. Willingness to discuss appearance-based influences also showed no significant change. Issue involvement showed a significant time-by-group interaction, but follow-up comparisons found no significant differences between specific groups.

Participant feedback described the interventions as engaging and conducive to self-reflection, despite the absence of measurable debiasing effects. Limitations included hypothetical scenarios, short intervention duration, static comic-based materials, possible socially desirable responses, and potential difficulty transferring lessons between contexts. The authors recommend investigating longer-term, more immersive and interactive approaches to address persistent biases.

The passage argues that Germany’s control of Middle Europe depends on subordinating the Poles, Czechs, South Slavs, and Bulgaria. It distinguishes economic and cultural integration from imperial domination, proposing that United States policy oppose the latter rather than regional unity itself.

The ruling powers in Berlin, Vienna, Budapest, Sofia, and Constantinople are linked by interests in political supremacy, territorial preservation, and German support. Postwar debts are expected to strengthen Germany’s influence.

Two principal sources of leverage are identified. First, control over raw materials, markets, and trade routes could pressure Germany into concessions, since economic exclusion would obstruct industrial recovery and demobilization and increase domestic unrest. Second, nationalist discontent within Austria-Hungary could weaken its ruling coalition and dependence on Berlin.

The proposed policy combines encouragement of nationalist pressure with rejection of Austria-Hungary’s dismemberment. Offering security through disarmament and a league of nations could encourage its rulers to preserve the empire by pursuing greater independence from Germany.

In separate murder cases, a Zhob court sentenced Shehzado to death and fined him Rs. 200,000. Brothers Ajab Khan and Fateh Khan received 25-year terms and Rs. 200,000 fines each; Dilbar Khan received 25 years and a Rs. 105,000 fine.

Texas will replace STAAR with three shorter exams administered at the beginning, middle and end of the school year starting in 2027-28. The law aims to reduce stress, monitor academic growth and preserve instructional time by banning practice tests. Scores must be released within about two days to help teachers adjust instruction.

Parents, educators and policy experts worry the changes could increase testing time and anxiety without reducing the importance of end-of-year results in school accountability ratings. A required study on reducing testing’s weight in those ratings is not due until 2029-30, and the Texas Education Agency is not obligated to implement its findings.

Schools will choose the first two exams from agency-approved assessments; the agency will create the third. Testing protocols remain undecided, prompting concerns that restrictive STAAR-style procedures could apply to all three exams.

Some educators want assessments they already use, such as MAP, which measures student growth and is administered with fewer disruptions. They also seek teacher input in test development and less restrictive testing environments. Supporters say the overhaul will reduce over-testing, while critics argue that pressure will persist as long as accountability ratings rely heavily on test results.

Chipotle launched queso on Sept. 12, drawing Twitter complaints about its price and taste. Chips and queso cost $3.95 for a small order and $6.25 for a large. A spokesman said 63% of test-market customers who tried queso reported greater likelihood of visiting more often, and ingredient costs meant no planned price reductions.

The passage presents a construction of strong pseudorandom unitaries (PRUs) in the quantum Haar random oracle model (QHROM), where all parties can query a Haar-random unitary and its inverse. Strong PRUs remain indistinguishable from Haar-random unitaries even when adversaries have inverse access.

The construction has the form \(G^U(k)=X_{k_3}UX_{k_2}UX_{k_1}\), requiring two queries to the Haar oracle. The work states that security against adversaries making polynomially many queries can be achieved using \(O(\log^{1+\epsilon}(n))\) random bits for any constant \(\epsilon>0\). This extends earlier results establishing PRUs in the inverseless model.

The security proof builds on Ma–Huang’s path-recording framework, replacing Haar-random oracles with operators that record queries. An approximate isometry merges independent query databases while simulating keys. Query-by-query operator-norm bounds show that the real construction and two independent Haar-random oracles yield statistically close adversarial views. The analysis uses Haar-measure invariance, unnormalized operators, and independent forward and inverse recording registers to simplify calculations.

The passage also reviews quantum pseudorandomness and idealized cryptographic models. It motivates QHROM through applications to random circuits and black-hole dynamics, while noting that security in an idealized model does not necessarily guarantee security for real-world implementations.

LAPIS is an extensible compiler framework designed to combine performance, portability, and productivity while integrating Python-based machine learning with C++ computational science applications. It uses MLIR to compile high-level programs into parallel Kokkos C++ source code that can be incorporated directly into scientific applications, reducing the need for manual Python–C++ interfacing.

The framework accepts dense and sparse tensor programs through torch-mlir and MPACT frontends. Its principal contributions include a custom Kokkos dialect, representations of Kokkos Kernels linear algebra operations, accelerator-supporting lowering passes, a portable memory model, and a C++ code emitter. The memory model incorporates Kokkos DualView concepts to manage data across host and accelerator memory.

LAPIS maps parallel loops to Kokkos execution policies according to nesting depth, estimates parallelism to select execution parameters, and inserts synchronization operations. Its dialect represents hierarchical parallelism, synchronization, and library calls for dense matrix multiplication and matrix-vector multiplication.

The work demonstrates one sparse and two dense linear algebra operations matching hand-optimized implementations, alongside coupling computational science and machine learning in SciML and image-processing applications. Performance portability is demonstrated on AMD MI300A and NVIDIA H100 GPUs and Intel Granite Rapids CPUs.

Paul Clement is set to become Swansea manager after Bayern Munich granted permission for talks. Swansea hope to finalise a deal until 2019 and provide a £30million transfer budget. Clement would replace Bob Bradley, sacked after a 4-1 defeat to West Ham. Swansea sit 19th in the Premier League, having conceded 44 goals in 19 games.

U.S. District Judge Jeannette A. Vargas dismissed Drake’s lawsuit against Universal Music Group over Kendrick Lamar’s “Not Like Us,” ruling that lyrics calling Drake a “certified pedophile” were nonactionable opinion in a heated rap battle. The dismissal covered defamation, harassment and deceptive acts claims. Drake plans to appeal.

Hungary’s 1956 revolt arose amid discontent with Communist rule, economic failure, repression and developments suggesting greater independence from Soviet control might be possible. A Budapest demonstration on 23 October escalated after state security police fired into the crowd. Revolutionary councils formed nationwide, demanding nationalism, neutrality and Soviet withdrawal.

The Hungarian leadership recalled Imre Nagy as prime minister while requesting Soviet troops. Soviet tanks entered Budapest on 24 October, provoking resistance, then withdrew on 29 October. Soviet representatives promised respect for Hungarian sovereignty while forces prepared an invasion.

As the Suez crisis diverted international attention, Soviet forces surrounded Budapest on 1 November and attacked at midnight on 3–4 November. Hungarian resistance was defeated by 30 November. Approximately 25,000 Hungarians and 7,000 Soviet soldiers were killed. The revolt’s suppression marked a turning point for the Soviet Union and NATO.

Peggy Mahoney forwarded Energy Central’s August 25, 2000 Competition and Deregulation Forum to Enron colleagues. The forum posed a new question about encouraging natural gas exploration and production on federal lands and the continental shelf. It stated that natural gas supplied 25% of U.S. electricity but was expected to fuel almost 95% of planned power plants, while shortages had prompted forecasts of record winter gas prices.

Published responses addressed whether generators were manipulating wholesale electricity prices affecting San Diego Gas & Electric customers and whether price caps should protect ratepayers.

Respondents offered conflicting explanations:
- Many attributed price spikes to supply shortages, high demand, hot weather, rising fuel costs, inadequate generation and transmission investment, or flaws in California’s deregulation framework.
- Others alleged collusion, withholding of generation, utility mismanagement, or market rules that encouraged excessive profits.
- Many opposed price caps, arguing they would discourage investment, conservation, and additional supply while increasing shortage risks.
- Some supported temporary caps, cost-based pricing with limited profits, mandatory generation to meet local needs, or re-regulation.

Proposed alternatives included expanding generation and transmission, removing barriers to market entry, improving demand management, and using contracts or financial instruments to stabilize electricity costs. Several contributors emphasized assessing prices over a full year rather than focusing solely on summer spikes.

Springfield Officer Conrad Lariviere faces disciplinary action for a Facebook comment praising a car striking counter-protesters at a white supremacist rally in Charlottesville, killing Heather Heyer and injuring 19 others. Police launched an internal investigation, and Mayor Domenic Sarno condemned the comment. Lariviere apologized, denied being racist and said he would never want anyone murdered.

Williams & Connolly confirmed that hackers accessed a small number of attorney email accounts through a zero-day attack. The firm reported no evidence of further access to its IT system or extraction of confidential client data from other systems. It believes the hackers are affiliated with a nation-state actor linked to attacks on other firms and companies. The firm said it took steps to block the attackers and found no ongoing unauthorized network traffic.

Video output signals carry the eight most significant bits of video data. G/Y/YC carries green, Y, luma, or multiplexed Y/Cb/Cr depending on mode. B/CB/C carries blue or chroma data and is unused in BT.656 mode. R/CR carries red data in RGB mode.

The State Bar of Michigan’s May 23, 2001 e-Journal presents case summaries, attorney referral listings, classified advertisements, employment opportunities, and bar event information.

Key case summaries include:
- **In re Hood:** The Sixth Circuit Bankruptcy Appellate Panel affirmed that the Tennessee Student Assistance Corporation lacked sovereign immunity in a student-loan dischargeability action because states ceded sovereignty over bankruptcy discharge matters.
- **Thakur v. Department of Corrections:** Summary disposition for defendants was affirmed because the plaintiff failed to rebut nondiscriminatory reasons for not interviewing him or connect racial disparities to a neutral employment practice.
- **People v. Byars:** Dismissal of criminal charges for delayed discovery was reversed; no prejudice was shown, and a continuance could have alleviated harm.
- **Other criminal cases:** Decisions were affirmed involving jury-instruction waiver, ineffective-assistance claims, routine destruction of police videotapes, justification for a vehicle stop, and joint representation.
- **Slawick v. Detroit Newspaper Agency:** A former employee’s defamation judgment was affirmed. Federal labor law did not preempt the claim, and evidence supported actual malice and the damages awarded.
- **Family law:** Termination of parental rights was affirmed in three cases involving substance abuse, failures to provide care, domestic violence, or noncompliance with treatment plans.
- **Van Reken v. Michigan Basic Property Insurance Association:** Land-contract vendors could not recover under an ordinary loss-payable clause when policy exclusions barred recovery by the insured purchasers.
- **Moton v. Oakwood Healthcare:** Striking an untimely supplemental witness list was upheld.
- **Domine v. Township of Grosse Ile:** Denial of a zoning variance was reinstated because evidence supported the decision and the property owner had created the practical difficulty.
- **Negligence cases:** Defense judgments were affirmed based on the fireman’s rule, insufficient evidence of hospital negligence, and an open and obvious ladder defect.

The issue also lists legal services across numerous specialties, expert witnesses, litigation financing, office space, and attorney and paralegal vacancies. Announced programs address Social Security disability and probate and post-mortem planning for legal assistants.

Indianapolis Public Schools is seeking public input on a proposal to close three high schools by 2018–2019. All seven high schools are under capacity, with five less than half full. A taskforce recommended operating four schools to accommodate potential population shifts. Public meetings will continue through April and May, with closure recommendations likely in June and a board vote in September.

Coppin State University, a historically Black institution in Maryland, has expanded enrollment through its Expand Eagle Nation program, which offers in-state tuition to students from 41 states and territories without an HBCU, plus Washington, D.C. Enrollment from qualifying locations rose from 81 before the program to 195 in 2024 and 416 this fall, out of an incoming class of 1,000. Overall enrollment increased 26 percent this year.

The university supported recruitment through high school visits, advertising, community college transfer partnerships and outreach to college-search organizations. Officials say the program also increased recognition among local students.

Coppin’s growth coincides with increased interest in HBCUs and broader college efforts to recruit beyond their home states. To accommodate growth, the university coordinated course and faculty availability, maintains six off-campus apartment facilities and is constructing a dorm scheduled to open next fall. Officials report that some prospective students struggle to believe the tuition offer is genuine.

The White House said it was not defending Roseanne Barr’s racist tweet, which led ABC to cancel her sitcom. President Trump and press secretary Sarah Sanders nevertheless sought an apology from ABC for derogatory comments about the administration. Trump criticized Disney president Bob Iger for apologizing to Valerie Jarrett without apologizing to him. Sanders cited attacks on Trump by television personalities as evidence of a media double standard and said the President remained focused on other issues.

DAWN-PLASMA was a randomized, open-label, phase 2 multicenter trial evaluating convalescent plasma plus standard care versus standard care alone in adults hospitalized with COVID-19. Researchers hypothesized that early administration of high-volume plasma with high neutralizing-antibody titers would reduce mechanical ventilation requirements.

Participants were randomized 2:1 to plasma plus standard care or standard care alone. Plasma recipients received 800–1,000 mL across four units. The first two units were administered within 12 hours of randomization, and the remaining two 24–36 hours after completion of the first infusion. Plasma with neutralizing-antibody titers below 1:160 was prohibited.

The primary endpoint was the percentage of patients alive without mechanical ventilation at Day 15. Secondary assessments included clinical status, improvement, ventilation or death, transfusion-related effects, adverse events, quality of life, laboratory results and vital signs.

Eligibility required adults with COVID-19 meeting specified clinical criteria. Exclusions included mechanical ventilation before or at randomization, unacceptable safety risks, documented severe plasma allergy, treatment restrictions preventing ventilation or intubation, and anti-CD20 therapy during the preceding year.

Ethics committees approved study documentation, and the study followed Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice guidelines. Consent procedures were specified. Five patients withdrew consent and one was excluded for a non-COVID diagnosis before intervention; all six were replaced. No patients were lost to follow-up after intervention.

CEMEX grew from a Mexican cement company into a global building-materials supplier through acquisitions and a continuously refined integration approach known as the “CEMEX Way.” By 2007, it employed 65,000 people, operated in 50 countries, and generated $21.7 billion in annual revenue.

Under CEO Lorenzo Zambrano, appointed in 1985, CEMEX strengthened its domestic position, sold non-core assets, and invested in communications and information systems. Increased foreign competition in Mexico and U.S. trade penalties helped drive international expansion.
