In 1992, CEMEX acquired two Spanish cement companies for $1.8 billion. The acquisitions provided access to lower-cost financing and opportunities to transfer operational expertise. Applying Mexican practices increased the Spanish operations’ margins from 7% to 24%, while learning from their use of petroleum coke improved CEMEX’s energy efficiency elsewhere.

Subsequent acquisitions across Latin America and Asia helped develop the CEMEX Way. Difficulties retaining local talent during integration in Colombia demonstrated the importance of learning from acquired companies rather than simply imposing existing systems. The approach combined standardized processes, technology, and organizational structures with some local operational flexibility.

Multinational teams of functional specialists implemented established practices while identifying improvements from acquired businesses. Selected practices became company-wide standards. Integration time declined from 25 months for the Spanish acquisitions to less than five months for Southdown. Applying the integration process to Mexican operations in 1996 identified $85 million in savings.

Changes in strategic analysis supported further expansion. Evaluating U.S. regions separately helped justify acquiring Southdown, while emphasizing return on investment rather than margins increased the attractiveness of ready-mix concrete and aggregates. CEMEX acquired RMC for $5.8 billion in 2005, broadening its geographic and product reach and delivering more than $200 million in synergy savings within one year.

The $15.3 billion Rinker acquisition in 2007 expanded CEMEX further but added substantial financial leverage. Its share price fell sharply in 2008 amid the global downturn and credit crisis. Analysts also questioned whether Rinker offered integration benefits comparable to RMC’s.

CEMEX’s expansion occurred in an increasingly consolidated but largely localized industry, where high transportation costs limited international cement trade. Its growth relied on operational capabilities, knowledge sharing, innovation, and continuous improvement rather than cost arbitrage.

The transfer of the presidency and Congress to Democratic control represents a national desire for change beyond party victory. The speaker praises the nation’s wealth, enterprise, moral strength, and governmental institutions while criticizing resource waste, industrial suffering, and the use of government for private interests.

The proposed task is restoration: correcting abuses without undermining achievements and aligning national life with justice and fair opportunity. Priorities include reforming tariffs, banking and currency, and industrial practices; improving agricultural efficiency, scientific support, and credit; and conserving natural resources. Government must also protect health and establish sanitary, food, and labor standards to shield people from harmful conditions they cannot individually control, while safeguarding property and individual rights.

Reform should proceed gradually, guided by facts, consultation, and justice rather than partisanship or haste. The speaker presents the moment as one of dedication rather than triumph and calls for public counsel and support.

Kyle Shanahan described practice as competitive, with both offense and defense showing improvement and areas needing work. He said his father reviews film and offers trusted advice but is not part of the coaching staff. As a first-time head coach balancing offensive and broader responsibilities, Shanahan values additional perspectives that identify things he might miss. He plans to disconnect and spend time with family before training camp. Shanahan emphasized that play-action puts defenses in difficult positions, reduces pressure on the offensive line and quarterback, and creates opportunities for explosive plays while keeping defenses honest.

The passage introduces LG-CD, a language-guided model for remote sensing change detection. Traditional methods are sensitive to environmental interference, while existing deep-learning approaches face limitations involving contextual modeling, data scarcity, annotation costs, and reliance on visual information alone.

LG-CD combines a pretrained SAM2 encoder for visual feature extraction with CLIP for text encoding. SAM2 extracts multi-scale features from images acquired at two different times. Lightweight convolutional adapters refine these features, which are then concatenated across channels.

A Text Fusion Attention Module aligns visual features with textual prompts using multi-head cross-attention, directing attention toward task-relevant changing regions. CLIP supplies word-level and global text embeddings. A visual-semantic fusion decoder integrates visual and semantic information to produce change detection masks.

The paper reports that incorporating natural-language guidance improves semantic understanding, detection accuracy, robustness, and generalization. Its principal contributions are the multimodal LG-CD architecture, multi-level adapters for SAM2, and dedicated text-attention and visual-semantic fusion components.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin ruled that Nirvana’s 1991 album cover depicting a naked baby underwater is not child pornography, dismissing Spencer Elden’s 2021 lawsuit. Elden, photographed at 4 months old, sought civil remedies under federal law. Olguin found that nudity alone did not establish lasciviousness, comparing the image to a family photograph of a child bathing.

Prof. Cyril Dim describes cervical cancer as a malignancy of the neck of the womb, caused in almost all cases by human papillomavirus (HPV), particularly high-risk types such as HPV 16 and 18.

Precancerous changes usually have no symptoms and can be detected through Pap screening and treated before invasive cancer develops. Early cervical cancer may also be symptomless. Later symptoms include bleeding after sex, abnormal vaginal bleeding, foul-smelling discharge and pelvic pain. Advanced disease can affect surrounding organs, causing weakness, weight loss and loss of bladder or bowel control. Confirmation requires tissue biopsy and histology.

Treatment depends on the disease’s stage. Early-stage cancer may be cured through radical surgery or radiotherapy. Late-stage treatment focuses on prolonging life, generally using radiotherapy, sometimes with chemotherapy. Prognosis worsens with advanced disease.

Dim identifies inadequate structured screening as a major contributor to Nigeria’s cervical cancer burden. He cites estimates of about 15,000 new cases and 10,000 deaths annually in Nigeria, where cervical cancer ranks second to breast cancer among cancers affecting women.

Regular screening, treatment of precancerous lesions and vaccination against cancer-associated HPV types are emphasized as preventive measures. Listed risk factors include HPV infection, multiple sexual partners, smoking, birth control pill use and early sexual contact.

California lawmakers debated competing plans to prevent Southern California Edison from entering bankruptcy under more than $3.5 billion in debt. Proposals included purchasing its transmission lines, obtaining an option to buy them, or financing debt repayment through customer charges. Consumer groups questioned the costs, while business groups sought greater freedom to buy electricity directly.

PG&E sued California for compensation over electricity contracts Governor Gray Davis seized in January. The state acknowledged owing compensation but disputed the contracts’ value. Separately, the state’s consumer advocate criticized a proposed $1 billion purchase of San Diego Gas & Electric’s transmission lines as excessive.

California was selling surplus electricity after cool weather and reduced demand left it with more power than needed. Traders reported sales far below contract purchase prices. Officials defended the contracts as protection against shortages; daily state power costs had fallen from more than $100 million in May to under $26 million in July.

Other reports covered Contra Costa County’s proposed $1.7 million energy-efficiency upgrades, efforts to waive solar-installation fees in San Diego County, and tribal land-preservation concerns involving a proposed power line. National consumer prices rose 0.2% in June. Duke Energy reported second-quarter net income of $419 million, up 27%, driven by trading and wholesale-power businesses.

A player expressed surprise and gratitude after Pat returned him to the lineup following two weeks out. He credited hardworking teammates and planned to discuss his future with his family, saying there could be no sweeter way to leave. Reflecting on three cups in nine years, he described a difficult season, praised Madden and Marshall’s additions after Holik’s departure, and said the team had built a solid foundation. He credited Pat’s demanding, focused coaching with preventing complacency.

The speaker believes Ottawa is better than its performance in the first two games against Anaheim but must prove it through improved play. Anaheim has capitalized on mistakes, defended effectively and supported its centers better on faceoffs. Pahlsson’s line has limited Ottawa’s offensive players through physical play, puck protection and possession.

Ottawa needs fewer turnovers and risky passes, better faceoff support, more patient puck control and greater speed attacking Anaheim’s defense. Its goaltender has generally provided opportunities to win, while Ottawa has not sufficiently tested Giguere, particularly in the second game.

The speaker expects key forwards to improve at home and plans to use the fourth line more for its hitting, speed and energy. An emotional home crowd is expected to help, though players must avoid becoming overly excited. Chris Neil received the day off because his wife was having a baby. The speaker also praises Rob Niedermayer’s strength, skating, adaptability and playoff contributions.
Quantum-state moments determine Rényi entropies and underpin entanglement and coherence measures, as well as randomness certification protocols.

The TPS7H500x-SP family consists of radiation-hardness-assured, fixed-frequency, peak-current-mode PWM controllers for space-grade DC-DC converters, including buck, flyback, forward, active-clamp forward, push-pull, and full-bridge designs. External gate drivers are recommended.

- **Enable and voltage regulation:** The EN pin supports connection to VLDO, external control or sequencing signals, or a resistor divider for programmable startup and undervoltage lockout. UVLO must be approximately 75% or less of input voltage for reliable turn-on. An internal 1.23-V reference generates the 0.613-V error-amplifier reference, regulated within +0.7%/−1% across line, load, temperature, and total ionizing dose. REFCAP requires a 470-nF capacitor. A resistor divider programs output voltage.
- **Soft start and switching frequency:** An external capacitor controls gradual output startup. Synchronous rectifier outputs activate when SS exceeds 1 V. Switching frequencies range from 100 kHz to 2 MHz. Controllers support an internal oscillator, external synchronization, and primary-secondary operation. External synchronization requires RT floating and a 200-kHz-to-4-MHz clock at twice the desired switching frequency, with 40%–60% duty cycle. Primary-secondary operation supports synchronized independent converters or parallel interleaved phases.
- **Outputs and timing:** Available primary and synchronous rectifier outputs vary by device and have approximately 150-mA peak capability. TPS7H5001-SP and TPS7H5002-SP offer programmable dead times; TPS7H5003-SP has typical fixed 50-ns dead time and leading-edge blanking. Other devices have programmable leading-edge blanking. Pulse skipping addresses minimum-on-time limitations, occurring when COMP is below 0.3 V at the system-clock rising edge and the previous duty cycle was below 25%. Maximum duty-cycle options depend on the device; TPS7H5004-SP supports only 50%.
- **Protection and compensation:** CS_ILIM provides current sensing and overcurrent protection. A nominal 1.05-V threshold initiates cycle-by-cycle limiting, followed by hiccup shutdown and restart timing controlled by an external capacitor; at least 3.3 nF is recommended. FAULT enables externally implemented protections. Thermal shutdown stops switching above a typical 175°C and restarts power-up below a typical 160°C. Resistor-programmed slope compensation mitigates subharmonic oscillation, and Type 2A or Type 2B frequency compensation is supported.
- **Design example:** A TPS7H5001-SP synchronous push-pull converter uses GaN devices, 500-kHz switching, and a 5-V output. Selected parameters include approximately 25-ns dead time, 50-ns initial leading-edge blanking, 7.5-ms soft start, a 2.5 transformer turns ratio, 40-µH primary inductance, 0.47-µH output inductance, and approximately 2.3-mF output capacitance. Current limiting targets roughly 35 A, with a 10-kHz compensation crossover target. Component values may require optimization during testing.
- **Supply and layout:** Controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least 0.1-µF input bypass capacitance. Layout guidance emphasizes short switching loops, separation of sensitive signals from switching nodes, separate analog and power grounds joined at one point, and nearby bypass and compensation components.

Application guidance is not part of the component specification. Customers are responsible for component suitability, design validation, and testing. The passage also provides documentation references, revision history, packaging information, ESD precautions, and legal disclaimers.

An analysis of campaign contributions from lawyers and staff at 100 top-grossing firms and 50 larger plaintiffs-side firms found that 92.45% went to Democrats in 2023–2024. Democratic-affiliated groups received about $52 million, versus $4 million for Republican-affiliated groups. The roughly 12-to-1 ratio doubled from 2017–2020. Among top-grossing firms, Cleary Gottlieb had the highest Democratic contribution share at 99.7%, followed by Fried Frank and Mintz. Nelson Mullins had the lowest at 66.4%, followed by Lewis Brisbois and Ogletree Deakins.

This position paper examines how artificial intelligence (AI) can transform higher education through teaching and learning, research, institutional management, and external relationships. It draws on documentation collected from B-ON and SCILIT and reflection informed by the authors’ university teaching experience.

Potential applications include personalized learning and tutoring, automated grading, student support, translation, plagiarism detection, predictive analytics, and immersive learning environments. AI can also assist researchers with literature reviews and data analysis and streamline administrative tasks such as enrolment and scheduling.

The paper identifies challenges involving equitable access, disability inclusion, bias, privacy, data security, costs, staff training, students’ learning needs, institutional conservatism, and the concentration of control among a few entities. Its integration may also raise concerns about professional autonomy and alter teachers’ roles and interactions with students.

The authors advocate participatory implementation involving the whole institution, supported by transparent data policies and AI literacy beyond digital literacy. Teachers need competencies to assess AI critically, interpret data, and understand its educational benefits and limitations. The paper also emphasizes complementary skills such as communication, teamwork, creativity, leadership, and problem-solving. It concludes that higher education should engage with technological change while preserving academic freedom in teaching and research.

U.S. stock index futures rose Thursday as earnings started strongly and oil prices rebounded. Of 57 S&P 500 companies reporting, 75.4 percent beat expectations; quarterly profits were estimated to rise 10.8 percent, the strongest growth since 2011. U.S.–North Korea tensions, France’s presidential election and doubts about President Trump’s pro-growth agenda tempered risk-taking. Dow futures gained 41 points, S&P futures 6.5 points and Nasdaq futures 17.5 points.

Will Ma’s lecture explains postflop poker strategy through hand examples, emphasizing hand ranges rather than individual cards. Decisions depend on position, effective stack size, board texture, and opponents’ likely holdings.

- **Continuation betting:** Players commonly check to the preflop aggressor because that player’s range includes strong hands such as large pocket pairs. Ma suggests betting roughly half the pot on the flop, with larger proportions on later streets. Very small bets can unnecessarily give opponents an opportunity to check-raise.
- **Value bets, bluffs, and checks:** Strong hands should generally bet to receive calls from worse hands; weak hands can bluff to make better hands fold. Medium-strength hands often benefit from checking because betting drives out weaker hands while retaining stronger ones. Bluffing is less attractive on highly coordinated boards or against many opponents.
- **Responding to bets:** Many missed flops and weak draws should be folded. Moderate hands often warrant calling rather than raising, particularly when raising would attract action mainly from stronger hands. In “way-ahead, way-behind” situations, calling avoids forcing out hands that have little chance of improving.
- **Stack size and position:** At approximately 40 big blinds or deeper, Ma generally recommends two pair or better for committing an entire stack, while noting exceptions. Shorter stacks justify committing with weaker hands. Earlier-position raises usually indicate stronger ranges than button raises.
- **Leading into the aggressor:** Betting first can be appropriate when the flop favors the caller’s range. However, this is an advanced strategy requiring balance so that checking does not consistently reveal weakness.
- **Implied and reverse implied odds:** Immediate equity is sufficient for evaluating an all-in call, but remaining betting changes the calculation. Speculative hands can profit from future payments when they improve; difficult-to-play hands can lose additional money even after making a pair. Set mining requires enough potential winnings to compensate for infrequent success.
- **Bluffing with draws:** Good bluff candidates retain outs against hands that call. Draws can support aggression while balancing strong value hands. Stack depth affects whether raising risks being forced off a useful draw.
- **Continuing or abandoning bluffs:** Players should consider both their improvement chances and the strong hands their actions plausibly represent. A missed draw may justify further bluffing, especially when another draw completes. Conversely, an unfavorable card that strengthens the opponent’s range and weakens the bluff’s credibility can make giving up appropriate.

Ma presents these recommendations as practical guidelines drawn from experience and calculations, rather than mathematical proofs of every example.

The court affirmed Bradford Washington’s convictions under both indictments. His challenges to a detective’s testimony and the jury instruction on consciousness of guilt were unpreserved and without merit. The court also rejected his claim that the prosecutor changed the prosecution’s theory during summation, finding that the prosecutor consistently identified him as the gunman. Washington raised no independent claim concerning his separate guilty-plea murder conviction.

Darren Osborne, 48, was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum term of 43 years for murder and attempted murder after driving a van into worshippers outside mosques in Finsbury Park, London, last June. He killed Makram Ali and injured nine others. Ali’s family welcomed the guilty verdict. Prosecutors said Osborne had been radicalized into Islamophobia, and police released footage documenting his planning and attack. Police counterterrorism commander Dean Haydon praised the community’s unity afterward.

Quantbot Technologies LP increased its stake in Zoe’s Kitchen by 114.5% in the second quarter, acquiring 9,106 shares for a total holding of 17,056 shares worth $203,000. Several other institutional investors also increased holdings or established positions. Director A Alexander Taylor II purchased 3,100 shares for $39,897 on August 22.

Zoe’s Kitchen had a consensus analyst rating of “Hold” and a target price of $17.55. Shares opened Friday at $12.39, with a market capitalization of $242.04 million.

The restaurant operator reported quarterly earnings of $0.06 per share, exceeding analysts’ estimates of $0.02. Revenue rose 12.1% year over year to $74.30 million but fell below the $75.11 million estimate. Analysts projected a full-year loss of $0.09 per share.

Several major hedge funds reduced healthcare holdings in the second quarter as the sector rose 6.7 percent, outpacing the S&P 500’s 2.6 percent gain. Jana Partners exited nine healthcare companies, while Third Point reduced stakes in Humana and Baxter International. Third Point, Jana and Omega Advisors also exited energy holdings as that sector fell 7 percent. Hedge funds overall gained 1 percent. Quarterly holdings disclosures appear 45 days after quarter-end and may not reflect current positions.

Facebook is introducing Trending News on iOS and Android through the Explore tab. It ranks stories by how many publications cover them, letting users access headlines from multiple sources, videos, photos, and related Facebook posts.

The lecture examines parity, time reversal, and charge conjugation in quantum field theory, then introduces Grassmann calculus for fermionic path integrals.

Time reversal must be anti-linear to reverse the sign of \(i\) in the Schrödinger equation while commuting with the Hamiltonian. Its quantum implementation is anti-unitary, requiring complex conjugation in the definitions of adjoints and preserved inner products.

For complex scalar fields, parity reverses spatial coordinates, time reversal reverses time, and charge conjugation exchanges particles and antiparticles. Parity phases of \(+1\) and \(-1\) distinguish scalars from pseudoscalars. Both parity and time reversal reverse momentum.

For Dirac fields, discrete transformations also act on spinor components through matrices. Requiring the transformed field to satisfy the Dirac equation constrains these matrices. The parity matrix is proportional to \(\gamma^0\). A charge-conjugation matrix exists because the negative transposes of the gamma matrices satisfy the same Clifford algebra. The time-reversal matrix is related to charge conjugation and \(\gamma^5\). Parity and time reversal are independent discrete transformations, not related by Lorentz boosts.

Fermionic path integrals require anti-commuting variables rather than ordinary classical fields. Berezin’s approach uses Grassmann variables, which satisfy \(\theta^2=0\). Consequently, a function of one variable has the form \(f(\theta)=f_0+f_1\theta\), and functions of several variables have finite expansions. Left and right derivatives can differ by signs; the lecture adopts left derivatives.

Grassmann integration is defined by linearity, vanishing integrals of total derivatives, and the normalization \(\int d\theta\,\theta=1\). Thus, \(\int d\theta\,1=0\) and \(\int d\theta\,f(\theta)=f_1\), matching differentiation for one variable. Integration measures anti-commute with Grassmann variables. Under rescaling \(\theta'=a\theta\), the measure transforms inversely: \(d\theta'=a^{-1}d\theta\).

Released shortly after the 1987 Black Monday stock market crash, Oliver Stone’s *Wall Street* remains influential 30 years later. The passage attributes its longevity to its blend of a rags-to-riches story, the Hero’s Journey, and a cautionary fairy tale, alongside its vivid portrayal of 1980s wealth and excess. Bud Fox’s rise under financier Gordon Gekko explores ambition, success, and their costs. Michael Douglas’s Oscar-winning performance made Gekko an enduring symbol of financial greed and success who reportedly inspired some viewers to pursue finance careers. The film’s memorable dialogue, period details, and charismatic antagonist contribute to its lasting cultural impact.

In Coleman v. Coleman (1972), the court upheld Ohio’s requirement that plaintiffs reside in the state for one year before filing for divorce or annulment, except in actions for alimony alone. The appellant had not satisfied the requirement when she filed.

The court distinguished divorce from welfare assistance and voting, which were addressed in decisions invalidating durational residency requirements. It concluded that obtaining a divorce was neither a basic need nor, in this case, an urgent necessity, and that Ohio’s requirement did not penalize the constitutional right to interstate travel.

The court also found a compelling state interest in overseeing marriage and divorce, preserving marital stability, and ensuring that Ohio’s divorce laws were not applied to nonresidents. It considered the one-year requirement the least restrictive means of establishing domicile, given the difficulty of determining an individual’s intention to make Ohio a permanent home. Actions for alimony alone remained available without the waiting period.

The judgment was affirmed. Justice Schneider concurred based on the particular facts, while leaving open reconsideration in circumstances where grounds for divorce arose after residence was established in Ohio.

On August 17, 2022, Apple’s Compensation Committee approved an Executive Cash Incentive Plan for executive team members and other designated employees. Awards depend on achievement of committee-established performance goals, generally measured over fiscal years. The committee determines award terms and payouts. Participants who leave before payment generally forfeit their awards unless the committee decides otherwise.

Apple’s Board also adopted amended and restated bylaws, effective immediately. Changes include:
- Allowing special Board meetings on less than 48 hours’ notice when necessary or appropriate.
- Expanding procedural and disclosure requirements for certain shareholder nominations and proposals, including updated disclosures and nominee interviews.
- Clarifying authority over shareholder meeting locations, conduct and adjournment.
- Revising procedures for shareholder-requested special meetings and record dates for written consent.
- Requiring shareholders soliciting proxies to use nonwhite proxy cards.
- Allowing reduced Board procedural requirements during emergencies defined by California law.

The Form 8-K includes the incentive plan and amended bylaws as exhibits and was signed on August 19, 2022.

The passage describes systems, devices, and methods for spatially and temporally synchronizing a rotating LIDAR sensor with one or more cameras to improve the combination of their sensor data.

The LIDAR emits light pulses and detects reflections to collect information about an environment. Cameras detect external light using adjacent rows of sensing elements aligned with the LIDAR’s rotation axis. In a rolling-shutter configuration, these rows are exposed and read sequentially, following an order similar to the LIDAR’s scanning pattern. Exposure periods for successive rows may overlap.

A controller can adjust camera exposure timing, pixel acquisition order, and delays between rows based on the LIDAR’s pointing direction, rotation speed, rotation direction, and pulse emission order. Alternatively, LIDAR operation can be adjusted to match camera acquisition. These arrangements seek to capture image pixels and LIDAR measurements from similar viewing directions during similar time periods.

Example camera arrangements include a stationary ring of cameras surrounding the rotation axis, with adjacent or overlapping fields of view providing 360-degree coverage. Another arrangement places sensing elements along a curved surface around the axis. Where camera and LIDAR scanning durations differ, exposure can be synchronized for selected image regions, such as image centers. Overlapping camera views can provide aligned pixels in place of less well-aligned measurements.

The collected data can be associated through timing and viewing-direction comparisons. Applications include assigning depth values to image pixels, adding colors to LIDAR point clouds, generating three-dimensional environmental representations, and mapping both datasets into a shared coordinate system.

The passage also describes supporting components, including controllers, power supplies, actuators, rotating and stationary platforms, optical elements, housings, and optional displays. Although the examples emphasize LIDAR and cameras, alternative implementations may employ other active or passive sensors, including RADAR, SONAR, microphones, and temperature sensors.

The passage describes an electronic smoking device with a coil-less atomizer using one or more woven fiber tubes that combine liquid transport and electrical heating. Tube ends contact a liquid supply, while an electrically conductive heating section vaporizes liquid delivered through the hollow interior by capillary action and through the porous tube walls. This arrangement eliminates the need for separate heating wires and wicking elements.

The tubes may use carbon fibers, metals, ceramics, or composite materials selected for electrical conductivity, liquid transport, and strength. They can have various shapes, diameters, and arrangements. Multiple tubes may supply liquid to a central heating tube or provide staged aerosol delivery through different heating rates. Liquid supplies may contain free-flowing liquid, liquid held in porous material, or both.

Electrical leads or surface contacts connect the heating section to a power source. Selective coatings can lower resistance outside the heating section, concentrating heat where vaporization occurs. Surface treatments may also improve liquid transport or alter electrical and thermal properties. A described manufacturing process mounts tubes on a board, masks the heating section, coats exposed sections with a conductive material, and removes the mask.

Device embodiments include airflow-sensor or manual-switch activation, disposable or rechargeable batteries, and refillable or replaceable liquid supplies. The passage presents these heating elements as suitable for compact designs and controlled-resistance manufacturing.

The Massachusetts Bankruptcy Court determined damages arising from Randall Fincke’s false statement in Access Cardiosystems’ October 2002 Business Plan that patent counsel had advised that its product did not infringe known patents.

The court denied Fincke’s motion to reconsider liability under Massachusetts securities law. Its earlier finding rested on the absence of any such advice, formal or informal, and the statement’s materiality to a reasonable investor.

Although investors sought recovery of their investments, the court held that each securities sale had to be linked to the misstatement. Proof of reliance or loss causation was unnecessary, but the investors’ testimony that the Business Plan influenced every subsequent investment was not credible.

Only Joseph Zimmel’s October and November 2002 stock purchases, totaling $1.5 million, were sufficiently connected to the Business Plan, which was used to solicit those purchases. The April 2003 investments resulted from a new company overview and extensive financing negotiations, rather than the earlier misstatement. No evidence established additional stock purchases after April 2003.

The court directed judgment against Fincke:
- For Zimmel: $1.5 million, plus six percent annual interest from May 25, 2007, and costs.
- For Access: $281,534.62 for fiduciary-duty breaches involving repayment of Fincke’s loans, plus twelve percent annual interest from July 6, 2004, and costs.

Both awards would accrue federal postjudgment interest. The request for attorneys’ fees was waived because no supporting evidence was presented.

The proposed BIRDS workshop aims to connect digital library and GLAM practitioners with computational researchers to develop practical, innovative digital library systems. It addresses a gap between practitioners’ knowledge of collections and user needs and researchers’ technical expertise, while considering constraints such as limited computing resources and restrictions on sharing materials.

The full-day, in-person workshop prioritizes collaboration rather than paper submissions. Planned activities include introductions, a keynote showcasing successful practitioner–researcher collaboration, scientific speed-dating, a panel, and breakout discussions. Suggested discussion topics include large language models, OCR, interface evaluation, and effective access paths to digital libraries.

Goals include identifying shared challenges, discussing preliminary ideas and ongoing work at TPDL, establishing a continuing workshop series, and publishing a SIGIR Forum report. The workshop welcomes participants from all backgrounds, particularly practitioners, researchers, students, and library representatives, and expects around 25 attendees. It is organized by Christin Katharina Kreutz and Hermann Kroll.

Developer B-S-G modified Google Camera to enable HDR+ on Android phones with Snapdragon 820, 821 or 835 processors. Amazon offers refunds for questionable solar-eclipse glasses. HBO refuses to pay hackers despite leaks including upcoming Curb Your Enthusiasm episodes. Waymo patented technology that would soften car surfaces before pedestrian collisions to reduce injuries.

Evelyn Montiel balanced academic success with demanding work at her family’s ice cream business in East Oakland. After dropping out of an East Coast college amid depression, she received help from Students Rising Above to enroll at USC and secure internships. Graduating during the recession, she returned to the family business before SRA connected her with an interview that launched her finance career. Now a broker at a Silicon Valley startup, Montiel remains rooted in East Oakland and credits SRA’s support with helping her succeed.

The Simons Observatory uses microwave frequency multiplexing and SLAC microresonator radio frequency (SMuRF) electronics to read out superconducting transition-edge sensor detectors. Its large-aperture telescope (LAT), containing nearly 31,000 detectors, has 18 SMuRF systems mounted directly on its receiver. The electronics and external radio-frequency cables experience daily temperature changes that can introduce phase drifts and mimic detector signals.

Researchers measured these drifts using off-resonance “pilot” tones, which pass through the readout system without interacting with detector-coupled microwave resonators. Observations of 290 tones over 22.6 hours showed temperature-correlated time-delay changes of only a few picoseconds.

An analytical conversion based on measured resonator and SQUID properties estimated the equivalent detector-current noise. During a 40-minute scan, this inferred contribution was small compared with on-sky detector noise and remained within the readout noise budget. The researchers therefore do not expect temperature-induced phase drift in the warm cables to affect the LAT’s mapping speed. A future study incorporating flux-ramp demodulation simulations could provide a more accurate conversion.

Electron–photon coupling in optical cavities modifies molecular electronic structure and requires specialized computational methods. The orthonormal, systematically improvable sinc basis represents molecular orbitals on a uniform real-space grid. Although direct evaluation of two-electron integrals scales as O(N⁴), rapidly decaying off-diagonal tensor elements permit sparse or low-rank approximations that reduce computational costs.

Retired Justice Anthony Kennedy’s memoir, released Oct. 14, reflects on judicial decision-making, controversial rulings, and personal experiences. Kennedy emphasizes humility, integrity, and clear reasoning, arguing that the Supreme Court earns respect through thoughtful decisions rather than infallibility. He finds both originalism and pragmatism insufficient as comprehensive judicial philosophies.

Kennedy defends his campaign-finance ruling in Citizens United, emphasizing constitutional limits on government restrictions and voters’ ability to respond to political spending. His reasoning on same-sex marriage included marriage’s changing history and the effects of nonrecognition on children raised by gay couples. He recounts Justice Antonin Scalia’s apology for personal attacks in his dissent, shortly before Scalia’s death.

Kennedy distinguishes his personal opposition to abortion from his judicial obligation to protect constitutional rights. He rejects the “swing justice” label and stresses that protecting free expression can require tolerating offensive conduct.

The memoir also argues that presidents must give proper deference to Supreme Court rulings and opposes courtroom cameras because they could encourage performance rather than substantive discussion. Kennedy describes an unsettling exchange with Vladimir Putin about capital punishment and a destructive attack on his family’s home that police suspected, without proof, was connected to a bail decision involving a Manson family member.

Amazon.com’s 2016 Form 10-K describes its operations, financial performance, liquidity, and business risks for the year ended December 31, 2016.

Amazon operates through three segments: North America, International, and Amazon Web Services (AWS). It serves consumers through retail websites, electronic devices, digital content, and Prime memberships; provides selling and fulfillment services to third-party sellers; offers computing, storage, database, and other services through AWS; and supports content creators through publishing and distribution programs.

**2016 financial results**
- Net sales increased 27% to $136.0 billion from $107.0 billion in 2015.
- Operating income increased to $4.19 billion from $2.23 billion.
- Net income rose to $2.37 billion from $596 million, with diluted earnings per share increasing to $4.90 from $1.25.
- North America sales grew 25% to $79.8 billion, generating $2.36 billion in operating income.
- International sales grew 24% to $44.0 billion, while its operating loss widened to $1.28 billion from $699 million.
- AWS sales grew 55% to $12.2 billion, with operating income increasing to $3.11 billion from $1.51 billion.

Retail growth primarily reflected increased unit sales, including marketplace sales. AWS growth primarily reflected increased customer usage, partly offset by pricing changes. International losses increased primarily because of spending on fulfillment capacity, technology infrastructure, and marketing.

Operating cash flow reached $16.4 billion, compared with $11.9 billion in 2015. Cash, cash equivalents, and marketable securities totaled $26.0 billion. Cash capital expenditures were $6.7 billion, and equipment acquired under capital leases totaled $5.7 billion. Amazon expected available liquidity to cover anticipated operating cash needs for at least 12 months.

Amazon’s financial strategy emphasizes long-term growth in free cash flow, customer experience, cost efficiency, and investment in infrastructure and new offerings. Net shipping costs increased 43% to $7.19 billion. Approximately 32% of annual revenue occurred in the fourth quarter, and Amazon employed about 341,400 full- and part-time workers at year-end.

Disclosed risks include intense competition, rapid expansion, international regulation, foreign exchange fluctuations, fulfillment and inventory challenges, security breaches, system interruptions, intellectual property disputes, tax liabilities, supplier dependence, and payment-related obligations. Amazon also identified ongoing U.S. transfer-pricing litigation and a European Commission investigation concerning Luxembourg tax arrangements.

On November 27, 2001, Dynegy confirmed talks to restructure its proposed acquisition of Enron. Reports indicated the approximately $9 billion stock deal could be reduced by more than 40% to about $5 billion. Negotiations also involved additional financing and extensions of Enron’s debt maturities.

Enron’s energy trading business faced mounting credit concerns. Many counterparties restricted transactions or stopped selling it near-term gas and power. A broker estimated over-the-counter trading volume at roughly 25% of its level a month earlier; Enron disputed that estimate, describing only a slight reduction.

Bankers seeking up to $2 billion for Enron had been rejected by investors including Prince Alwaleed, Blackstone and Carlyle. Enron faced $9 billion in payments before the end of 2002 and had less than $2 billion in cash and credit lines. Moody’s said its Baa3 rating, the lowest investment grade, would remain unchanged that day.

Investors and analysts remained concerned that the merger could fail, potentially leading to bankruptcy. Employee retirement-plan and shareholder lawsuits added uncertainty. Some hedge funds considered positions combining short sales of Enron shares with purchases of its bonds, while many merger traders remained cautious.

Enron shares closed at $4.14, up 13 cents; Dynegy closed at $40.89, up $1.64. Analysts emphasized that stabilizing Enron’s trading operations was essential to preserving the acquisition’s value.

Tesla’s 2022 Form 10-K describes its electric vehicle and energy businesses, technology development, operations and principal risks.

- **Business and products:** Tesla operates two reportable segments: automotive, and energy generation and storage. It manufactures Model 3, Model Y, Model S and Model X vehicles, and began early Tesla Semi production and deliveries in December 2022. Planned vehicles include Cybertruck and a new Roadster. Energy products include Powerwall, Megapack, solar systems and Solar Roof.
- **Technology:** Tesla develops battery cells, powertrains, vehicle software and self-driving technologies. Its Autopilot and Full Self-Driving options currently require drivers to remain responsible for vehicle control. The company also previewed its Optimus humanoid robot in 2022.
- **Sales and services:** Tesla generally sells directly to customers through its website and company-owned stores. It provides vehicle servicing, charging infrastructure, used-vehicle sales, financing, leasing and insurance. Insurance was available in 12 states. Tesla began offering non-Tesla vehicles access to selected Supercharger locations in November 2021.
- **Manufacturing and workforce:** Manufacturing facilities are located in California, Nevada, New York, Texas, China and Germany. Tesla seeks to expand capacity and localize production. At December 31, 2022, Tesla and its subsidiaries employed 127,855 full-time workers worldwide, approximately 29,000 more than a year earlier.
- **Government policy and competition:** Tesla’s products are subject to vehicle safety, self-driving, battery, dealership and energy regulations. Government incentives support electric vehicles and clean energy, including Inflation Reduction Act tax credits. Tesla faces competition from established and emerging vehicle manufacturers, energy-storage providers, solar companies and utilities.
- **Principal risks:** Identified risks include pandemic disruptions, rising interest rates, production delays, supplier shortages, battery-cell and raw-material availability, factory expansion challenges, uncertain demand and increasing competition. Other risks concern service and charging capacity, product defects and liability, financing exposure, international operations, regulatory restrictions, cybersecurity and employee retention. Tesla states that it is highly dependent on Elon Musk, who does not devote his full time to the company.

The report cautions that forward-looking statements involve uncertainties and actual results may differ materially from expectations.

VentureWire’s September 26, 2000 issue reports private-company financing, partnerships, acquisitions, and executive appointments.

- **Major funding:** Optical networking company Chiaro Networks secured more than $100 million in third-round financing, while fiber-optics component developer Novalux raised $109 million. Nexsi and Netigy each raised $75 million. Other rounds included Nonstop Solutions ($50 million), Epylon ($47 million), Predictive Networks ($45 million), Telecruz ($35 million), and Artesia Technology ($26 million).
- **Partnerships and investments:** Bertelsmann and iSyndicate agreed to establish an equally owned European content-syndication venture; Bertelsmann will also acquire 4% of iSyndicate. Sun Microsystems launched a $50 million Asia-Pacific investment program, with local co-investments intended to bring the total to $250 million. Motorola, through Metrowerks, agreed to acquire 8% of Lineo for $22.5 million.
- **Closure:** Online jewelry retailer Miadora shut down after raising $20 million in May and previously acquiring Jewelry.com.
- **Energy marketplaces:** Myutility.com secured undisclosed seed funding for website development. FuelSpot.com launched its petroleum marketplace after securing $7.8 million from Internet Capital Group and another $5 million from Zero Stage Capital.
- **Products and acquisitions:** SmartPipes introduced a beta version of its Global IP Services, and PocketPass.com launched a prepaid online payment system. Autodaq purchased Market Wise, DeepBridge acquired Online Communications, and Findel planned to merge Burley House Weddings with Confetti Network.
- **Personnel and venture funds:** Mayfield Fund appointed Jennifer Jones as marketing partner, and Matrix Partners hired former 3Com Ventures president Edgar Masri as a partner. Venturelab Partners launched a $100 million second fund. Net Value Holdings renamed itself Stonepath Group.
- **Clarifications:** Sharing Technologies’ $15 million financing comprised $9 million in equity and a $6 million IBM Global Financing bridge loan. VentureWire also corrected its previously reported investor list for epipeline.com.

The DAWN-plasma study was a randomized, open-label, multicenter phase 2 trial evaluating convalescent plasma added to standard care in adults hospitalized with COVID-19. It received ethics approval and followed Declaration of Helsinki and Good Clinical Practice guidelines.

Between May 2020 and January 2021, 489 patients were randomized in a 2:1 ratio to plasma plus standard care or standard care alone. After six exclusions, the full analysis set included 320 plasma recipients and 163 controls. Patients receiving mechanical ventilation at randomization were excluded. The intervention comprised four plasma units totaling 800–1,000 mL, administered early after randomization. Approximately 81% of administered units had neutralizing-antibody titers of at least 1/320.

The primary endpoint—being alive without mechanical ventilation on day 15—was similar between groups: 83.7% with plasma versus 84.1% with standard care alone (odds ratio 0.99; p=0.976). No statistically significant differences were found in mortality or other secondary endpoints. Per-protocol results were similar.

Adverse events occurred in 28.13% of plasma-group patients and 30.06% of controls. Serious and fatal adverse events were also similar between groups. Fourteen adverse events in 12 patients and seven serious adverse events in seven patients were considered treatment-related. Transfusion-related side effects occurred in 19 of 320 patients (6.0%); no TRALI cases were reported.

Neutralizing-antibody titers increased between baseline and day 6, but plasma treatment did not influence that increase. Higher baseline and day-6 titers correlated with better outcomes. Overall, early administration of high-volume, high-antibody-titer convalescent plasma did not improve the measured clinical outcomes.

A nationally representative study analyzed 2009–2020 National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey data from 32,498 US adults to examine dietary patterns by cardiovascular disease (CVD), socioeconomic vulnerability, and Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) participation.

Researchers identified four dietary patterns:
- **American:** Higher intake of refined grains, meats, dairy, fats, and added sugars; followed by 33.7% of adults.
- **Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy:** Higher intake of fruits, whole grains, soy protein, nuts/seeds, milk, and yogurt; followed by 27.9%.
- **Prudent:** Higher intake of vegetables, meat, poultry, seafood, eggs, and oils; followed by 22.6%.
- **Legume:** Higher intake of vegetables and legumes; followed by 15.8%.

The American pattern had the lowest Healthy Eating Index score, while Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy had the highest. After adjustment, adults with CVD were more likely to follow the American pattern than those without CVD (37.1% versus 33.3%); alignment with other patterns was similar.

Greater socioeconomic vulnerability was associated with greater alignment with American and Legume patterns and less alignment with Prudent and Fruit/Whole Grain/Dairy patterns. SNAP participants were more likely to follow the American pattern and less likely to follow the Prudent pattern than income-eligible nonparticipants and noneligible adults. Associations involving socioeconomic vulnerability and SNAP varied by race and ethnicity, whereas CVD associations did not differ significantly.

The authors recommend considering naturally occurring dietary patterns when designing nutritional support and clinical or policy interventions for at-risk populations. Limitations include the cross-sectional design, which limits causal inference, self-reported health and socioeconomic information, and dietary assessment based on two 24-hour recalls.
A study examines how age gaps in online images shape AI perceptions of employees, finding evidence of discrimination against older women.

A player’s stable personality, skill, size and strength are credited with helping him score important playoff goals under pressure. The team aims to pressure opposing defenders, maintain short-term focus and overcome deficits without concern for historical odds. Defensive adjustments and renewed offense have built confidence. After feeling in control of the latest game, particularly five-on-five, the team hopes to repeat that performance but stops short of claiming control of the series.

The State Bar of Michigan’s June 4, 2001 e-Journal summarizes Sixth Circuit and unpublished Michigan Court of Appeals decisions across business, civil rights, contracts, criminal, employment, family, litigation, and tort law.

Key decisions include:
- **Helwig v. Vencor:** Securities-fraud allegations concerning misleading financial projections and the Balanced Budget Act were sufficient to survive dismissal; the case was remanded.
- **Kiphart v. Saturn:** Evidence supported an employee’s favorable ADA verdict concerning disability, job rotation, and reasonable accommodation; reversed and remanded.
- **Anchrum v. Airtouch Cellular:** Rejection of a racial-discrimination claim was affirmed because the employee failed to establish disparate treatment or rebut the employer’s stated reason for discharge.
- **Sudul v. Donnell:** Evidence supported an excessive-force claim, but governmental immunity barred a bystander emotional-distress claim. The case was remanded for reconsideration of excessive damages.
- **Rock Construction v. Onyebuchi:** Failure to obtain financing did not establish impossibility, but recovery of a $13,000 down payment was upheld.
- **United States v. Mader:** Withdrawal of an unaccepted guilty plea required a fair and just reason, which the defendant failed to provide.

Other decisions affirmed juvenile placement, criminal convictions and sentences, termination of parental rights, and dismissal under res judicata.

The issue also contains attorney referral listings, advertisements for legal and support services, employment openings, office space, links to archived issues, and subscription and contact information.

Microsoft reported in a Form 8-K that co-founder Bill Gates resigned from its Board of Directors effective March 13, 2020. The filing includes the company’s press release announcing Gates’ plans as Exhibit 99.1 and was signed by Assistant Secretary Keith R. Dolliver.

Wham is a complementary football run play similar to Trap, using a tight end or fullback rather than a guard to kick out a defensive lineman. It creates favorable blocking angles quickly and can surprise defenses that rarely practice against it.

Its drawbacks include complicated blocking assignments, installation time, and the need for a powerful blocker. Teams often use specific formations to obtain predictable defensive fronts.

Against 3-4 and 4-3 fronts, the fullback identifies and kicks out the first defensive lineman outside the center, while other blockers secure gaps and engage linebackers. The tailback aims inside the kickout block.

Variations include Gun H-Back Wham RPO, which targets the nose tackle and gives the quarterback passing options, and Shotgun Influence Wham, which uses a pulling guard to draw a defender wider before the fullback blocks him.

Santa Barbara County detectives are investigating a Tuesday robbery at Summerland Antique Collective. A man threatened and duct-taped two female employees, stole cash and merchandise, and fled. A customer found the employees about 20 minutes later; neither appeared seriously injured.

President Donald Trump has nominated Travis Hill, a senior adviser at the Treasury Department, to chair the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation, according to Bloomberg News. The nomination requires Senate confirmation and comes amid tighter credit conditions, elevated interest rates, and concerns about smaller lenders.

Hill is expected to balance financial stability with lighter regulatory burdens, consistent with Trump’s deregulatory approach. If confirmed, he would oversee deposit insurance, bank assessments, and responses to bank failures. His nomination is likely to face congressional scrutiny over his institutional experience and potential regulatory leniency.

NVIDIA’s fiscal 2017 Form 10-K covers the year ended January 29, 2017. Headquartered in Santa Clara, California, the company develops GPU-based visual and accelerated computing platforms, with an expanding focus on artificial intelligence and deep learning.

NVIDIA operates through two reportable segments, GPU and Tegra Processor, serving four principal markets:
- **Gaming:** GeForce GPUs, GeForce NOW cloud gaming, SHIELD devices, and software supporting gaming and virtual reality.
- **Professional Visualization:** Quadro GPUs and software for design, engineering, rendering, and digital content creation.
- **Datacenter:** Tesla GPUs, DGX systems, CUDA software, and related technologies for AI, scientific computing, and virtualized graphics.
- **Automotive:** DRIVE PX computing platforms and DriveWorks software for autonomous driving and driver assistance.

The company’s strategies include extending its AI and visual computing capabilities, expanding GPU parallel processing, supporting mobile and cloud applications, and licensing intellectual property. NVIDIA had invested more than $13 billion in research and development since inception. Fiscal 2017 research and development expenses were $1.46 billion, compared with $1.33 billion in fiscal 2016. Of its 10,299 employees, 7,282 worked in research and development.

NVIDIA uses a fabless manufacturing model, relying on outside suppliers for wafer fabrication, assembly, testing, and packaging. Sales are conducted through a partner network and direct retail channels. ASUSTeK Computer accounted for 12% of fiscal 2017 revenue. Customers outside the United States and Other Americas accounted for 80% of revenue. Consumer products historically generated stronger revenue in the second half of the fiscal year.

Cash and marketable securities increased 35% to $6.80 billion at fiscal year-end. NVIDIA issued $2 billion in notes during September 2016, while $827 million in convertible-note principal remained outstanding at January 29, 2017.

The filing identifies risks involving competition, changing market requirements, manufacturing yields, supplier dependence, cybersecurity, product defects, customer concentration, inventory forecasting, international operations, intellectual property disputes, acquisitions, indebtedness, and shareholder dilution. Revenue recognition under NVIDIA’s Intel licensing agreement was scheduled to continue through the first quarter of fiscal 2018; failure to replace that income could adversely affect results.

NVIDIA paid $261 million in dividends during fiscal 2017 and increased its quarterly dividend to $0.14 per share in November 2016. By year-end, cumulative share repurchases totaled 245 million shares costing $4.59 billion, with $2.73 billion of authorization remaining through December 2020. The company intended to return $1.25 billion to shareholders in fiscal 2018 through dividends and repurchases. Its common stock trades on NASDAQ under NVDA, with 589 million shares outstanding as of February 24, 2017.

Namibia’s Mining Expo & Conference will take place April 25–26 at the Windhoek Show Grounds, themed “Maximising the multiplier effect from Namibia’s mining sector.” Nedbank Namibia’s Corporate and Investment Banking Mining and Resources team will showcase financing capabilities, discuss foreign investment opportunities and provide a networking lounge. Team leader Dominic Shikola highlighted its funding services and commitment to supporting mining development and sustainability. According to Shikola, mining contributes about 11 percent of Namibia’s GDP and provides employment, foreign exchange and tax revenues.

Nunavut MLA George Hickes raised concerns that senior government managers were threatening public servants and directing them not to speak with their MLAs. Repeating a warning he issued in 2014, Hickes emphasized constituents’ right to communicate with elected representatives without fear of repercussions.

Minister David Akeeagok said the Public Service Act does not prohibit such communication and that he was unaware of directives discouraging it. He said employees’ rights are protected and encouraged staff to contact an ethics officer if needed.

Hickes said MLAs can help when complaint processes fail and rely on constituents’ feedback. He noted that fear of repercussions may be greater in small communities where complainants are more easily identified.

A descriptive cross-sectional study at CUSP health center in Huye district, Rwanda, assessed HCV prevalence, associated risk factors, and transmission awareness among household members living with HCV-positive patients. Data collection and analysis took place from January 2 to February 2, 2021. Although the planned sample was 180 participants, 148 people from 30 families participated. Screening used HCV antibody rapid tests, with positive samples tested by ELISA.

Sixteen participants (10.8%) tested positive, compared with the reported general HCV prevalence of 4% in Rwanda. Significant associations were reported between HCV positivity and HBV history, HIV history, and unprotected sex. Blood transfusion was not significantly associated with positivity. Transmission awareness was low: 139 participants (93.9%) answered incorrectly, although awareness was not significantly associated with test results.

The authors recommend early screening of household members, follow-up and treatment monitoring for positive patients, and education about transmission and prevention. The cross-sectional design could not establish whether infections originated within households. Further research, including phylogenetic studies and broader geographic coverage, was recommended to investigate infection origins and household transmission.

European shares rose despite Britain formally starting Brexit proceedings. The STOXX 600 gained 0.4 percent to its highest close in nearly 16 months, while Germany’s blue-chip index also rose 0.4 percent. EU regulators blocked the proposed London Stock Exchange–Deutsche Boerse merger, but both companies’ shares advanced. Banks fell 0.2 percent amid signals that ECB easy-money policies would continue. Broker upgrades boosted Engie and 3I Group. Scout24 dropped 8.9 percent after disappointing results and guidance, while Aurelius slumped more than 35 percent as investors remained unconvinced by its rebuttal of a short-seller’s report.

Paulo Dybala expects to play against Barcelona in the Champions League quarter-final return leg after resuming team training. He also confirmed his Juventus contract renewal until 2022 was his choice.

The speaker describes physical play and fights as normal parts of playoff hockey, emphasizing the need to respond physically. A turnover after an offensive faceoff win led to a penalty and an opposing power-play goal, which the speaker identifies as the game’s turning point. Missed scoring chances, uneven play and an ineffective power play contributed to lost momentum. The focus is on winning the next game and responding throughout a series.

Faceoffs matter for puck possession, while scoring first helps establish momentum. The speaker favors lineup chemistry over depth-chart rankings, credits Pratt’s contributions and says using seven defensemen provides flexibility and has worked well.

Rusty benefited from a grinding role and a mental adjustment about where he needed to play to score goals. Marty St Louis used his opportunity to prove doubters wrong, which the speaker considers a strong motivation.

Expiring patents have enabled inexpensive desktop 3D printers, while industrial systems remain costly because they serve demanding applications requiring specialized materials and performance. Technologies include fused deposition modeling, stereolithography, and powder bed fusion, with materials ranging from plastics and ceramics to metals.

Industrial additive manufacturing offers large build volumes and throughput that can compete with traditional manufacturing for short production runs, without requiring molds. Applications include aircraft components, dental crowns, automotive spare parts, jewelry, and propulsion systems. GE’s printed LEAP engine fuel nozzles are lighter and longer-lasting, while its CT7 helicopter engine redesign reduced part counts, weight, and cost.

As industrial patents expire, entrepreneurs make these processes more accessible. The annual Wohlers Report documents additive manufacturing technologies, materials, software, and markets.

For Luccis Losers, Duce Staley was expected to start but share carries with Correll Buckhalter. Sebi allowed debt issuers to request rating reviews by committees comprising a majority of independent members. To improve transparency and accountability, credit rating agencies must disclose non-accepted ratings on their websites for 12 months and publish half-yearly rating summaries within 15 days. Disclosures must separately cover securities and other financial instruments.

Mississippi charity treasurer Melinda Rosetti-Spence was sentenced to 10 years in prison for embezzling about $266,600 from Pink Hearts Fund. She was ordered to repay about $181,000, with her family paying the balance. Prosecutors said she wrote herself 132 checks from March to July 2016. She pleaded guilty in April.

China has become a leader in the clean energy transition, investing $625 billion last year—nearly a third of global spending—and helping lower green technology prices through research and widespread adoption.

At the UN Climate Summit, President Xi Jinping pledged to reduce greenhouse gas emissions by 7–10 percent by 2035, moving beyond China’s previous promise to peak emissions by 2030. The projected annual reduction remains slower than that of many industrialized countries.

Xi also committed to reaching 3,600 gigawatts of installed wind and solar capacity by 2035, achieving an energy mix with more than 30 percent renewables, making electric vehicles prevalent in sales, and expanding carbon emissions trading to additional emissions-intensive sectors.

China’s commitments come amid weakened or divided climate action elsewhere. Its large domestic market and renewable technology development are reshaping global markets, though questions remain about whether its emissions targets are ambitious enough.

English councils are entitled to full refunds after an administrative error caused the Ministry of Justice to overcharge them about £9m annually since 2013-14 for council tax recovery applications. Each application was overcharged by £2.50. The ministry said it would urgently reduce fees to the correct level and announce refund arrangements. Councils issued about 3.5 million summons for council tax arrears last year.

LG’s webOS TVs, launching later this month, will support Sky’s EPG, allowing users to browse Sky content and control viewing with LG’s remote. The Today menu combines viewing options from apps, online platforms and live TV, while webOS enables quick switching between inputs.

enGene hired Hussein Sweiti as chief medical officer. He previously served as global medical head of oncology clinical development at Johnson & Johnson. The appointment appears in STAT’s regular feature highlighting pharmaceutical industry personnel changes.

The U.S. government froze around $18 billion in funding for New York City infrastructure projects, including the Second Avenue Subway extension and Hudson River Tunnel, over concerns that contract awards used unconstitutional diversity, equity and inclusion criteria. The Department of Transportation suspended a $300 million payment pending review under a new rule limiting race- and gender-based funding preferences.

City officials criticised the freeze as politically motivated, warning of job delays, construction disruptions and cost overruns. A federal shutdown has further complicated contract management. Funding could resume if projects are cleared, while violations could require renegotiated agreements or result in lost funding.

Cryotherapy, a growing wellness trend, exposes people to temperatures as low as 180 degrees below zero. Enthusiasts claim benefits including faster muscle recovery, reduced inflammation and pain, and improved mood. Developed in the 1970s to treat arthritis, it is now offered at Polar Brrr Cryo in West Michigan, attracting athletes and other clients. Scientific support for its benefits is limited, and it is not FDA-approved; the agency warns of frostbite, burns and eye injuries. Polar Brrr supervises its three-minute sessions and requires clients with conditions such as heart problems or hypertension to consult a doctor first.

Archaeologists discovered a 2,100-year-old chalk bowl fragment engraved with the Hebrew name “Hyrcanus” in Jerusalem’s City of David. Found in 2015 beneath an ancient Jewish ritual bath complex near the Akra fortress remains, it is among Jerusalem’s earliest chalk vessels. Researchers cannot determine whether it belonged to either of two Hasmonean rulers named Hyrcanus or another person, as the name was common. The rarity of engraved vessels from this period also leaves its purpose uncertain.

Apple’s Form 8-K reported results from its March 1, 2019 annual shareholders meeting. Shareholders elected eight directors: James Bell, Tim Cook, Al Gore, Bob Iger, Andrea Jung, Art Levinson, Ron Sugar and Sue Wagner. They approved Ernst & Young LLP as the company’s independent auditor for 2019 and an advisory resolution on executive compensation. Shareholder proposals titled “Shareholder Proxy Access Amendments” and “True Diversity Board Policy” were not approved. The report was signed on March 4, 2019, by Katherine Adams, Senior Vice President, General Counsel and Secretary.

The Council of Regional Accrediting Commissions (CRAC), representing seven agencies overseeing 3,000 degree-granting institutions, is encouraging colleges to use artificial intelligence to improve transfer-credit evaluations. Its nonbinding statement says AI can help reduce credit loss, accelerate decisions and ease administrative workloads without conflicting with accreditation standards.

A 2024 Public Agenda survey found that 58 percent of adults who attempted to transfer credits lost some credits, while 20 percent had to repeat a class. Transfer difficulties led 16 percent to abandon pursuing a degree or credential. Manual evaluations can involve inconsistent guidelines and bias.

AI can compare course descriptions and learning outcomes to identify additional course equivalencies. A pilot involving 59 institutions is testing this approach. CRAC urges institutions to apply credits toward program completion unless evidence shows required learning outcomes are unmet.

Supporters emphasize that AI should assist, not replace, human judgment. Questions remain about reliability at scale, and academic oversight is still needed. Implementing changes will depend on individual institutions.

Amazon is developing an AI chip for Alexa, whose “Alexa Loses Her Voice” commercial led YouTube views on Super Bowl Sunday. Other reports cover CES reveals, likely losses from Amazon and Google speaker discounts, Echo Dot holiday sales, Apple’s delayed home speaker, an Alexa device playing loud music while its owner was away, and plans for Alexa-powered Big Mouth Billy Bass.

An open-label randomised controlled trial in western Cambodia compared total primaquine doses of 3.5 mg/kg and 7.0 mg/kg, both administered over 14 days, for preventing Plasmodium vivax recurrence. Conducted between November 2021 and February 2024, the study allocated 156 patients to treatment groups. Of these, 119 patients with normal glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) activity were randomised to low-dose, high-dose or no primaquine; 37 G6PD-deficient patients were assigned to no primaquine. All received seven days of artesunate and were relocated to a malaria transmission-free area for 90 days to prevent reinfection.

In the primary per-protocol analysis, recurrence within 90 days occurred in:
- 81.4% of patients receiving no primaquine;
- 24.4% receiving 3.5 mg/kg;
- 4.7% receiving 7.0 mg/kg.

The difference between primaquine regimens was statistically significant. The hazard ratio for high versus low dose was 0.17 (95% CI 0.04–0.79). Higher efficacy of the 7.0 mg/kg regimen remained evident through day 180.

Both primaquine regimens were well tolerated in G6PD-normal patients, with no serious adverse events reported. Increased methaemoglobin was more common with high-dose treatment but was asymptomatic and resolved after treatment. No patient developed severe anaemia during primaquine administration.

Limitations included failure to reach the planned sample size, a single-centre open-label design, inability to definitively distinguish relapses from recrudescence, and tightly supervised conditions that differed from routine practice. The authors recommend adopting the 7.0 mg/kg regimen in Cambodia and suggest its use elsewhere in Southeast Asia, while calling for further regional studies. The report is a preprint that had not been peer reviewed.

The holiday effect is a seasonal stock-market pattern involving returns around non-trading holidays. The passage examines S&P 500 data using SPY and earlier index data, concluding that Independence Day, Thanksgiving, and Christmas show the most tradeable patterns.

Reported backtest results include:
- **Independence Day:** 1.01% average gain across 28 trades, with a 68% win rate.
- **Thanksgiving:** 0.82% average gain across 28 trades, with a 65% win rate. A retail-sector fund performed slightly better.
- **Christmas/year-end:** 1% average gain across 60 trades, with a 67% win rate.
- **Other holidays:** Martin Luther King Jr. Day and President’s Day produced negative average returns; Memorial Day and Labor Day showed weak effects. Easter is described as one of the better holiday effects.

Possible explanations include reduced liquidity, holiday optimism, fewer macroeconomic announcements, and price recovery after pre-holiday selling. The passage emphasizes comparing holiday results with broader monthly seasonality.

Post-holiday backtests found stronger returns on the second trading day after holidays. A strategy incorporating an undisclosed additional variable produced a 0.56% average gain across 100 trades, a 71% win rate, and a 3.5% annual return while invested 1% of the time. However, the FAQ gives conflicting statements about whether a post-holiday effect exists.

The passage characterizes holiday effects as small potential additions to trading strategies rather than a guaranteed route to substantial profits.

Scottish councils can raise basic council tax rates by up to 3% following the end of the government’s tax freeze. Individual councils decide whether to increase rates when setting their budgets.

Separately, higher multipliers for bands E to H will increase bills from April regardless of local decisions, affecting almost 700,000 homes, or 26% of Scottish households. Average increases range from about £2 weekly for band E to £10 for band H, before any council-approved rise. The changes should raise £100m annually, which will now be spent locally rather than distributed nationally to schools.

The impact varies significantly: 56% of homes in East Renfrewshire fall within the affected bands, compared with 18% in East Ayrshire.

Council tax bands remain based on April 1991 property values. Research suggested 57% of properties would have changed bands following a 2014 revaluation. The government opposes revaluation, citing costs, timescales and potentially substantial bill changes.

Councils receive most funding through government grants. A budget agreement with the Greens added £160m in direct local authority funding, but political disagreement remains over whether this offsets planned reductions.

Bollinger Bands, developed by John Bollinger in the 1980s, measure price volatility and help identify potential trading opportunities. They typically consist of a 20-period simple moving average and upper and lower bands positioned two standard deviations away. The bands widen as volatility increases and narrow as it decreases. Traders can adjust the moving-average period, type, and standard-deviation settings.

The passage describes several approaches:
- **Squeeze, Pinch Play, and Volatility Contraction:** Identify narrowing bands and consolidation that may precede breakouts.
- **Breakouts:** Interpret moves above or below the outer bands as potential trading signals.
- **Bounce and Reversal:** Use band touches or breaches to identify possible oversold or overbought conditions and reversals.
- **Band Walks and Double Bollinger Bands:** Track strong trends using price positioning relative to the bands.
- **%B and Band Width:** Measure relative price position and the distance between bands.
- **RSI-based and Triple strategies:** Combine indicators or multiple band settings to assess trading opportunities.

Band touches do not necessarily indicate reversals; prices can remain near an outer band during strong trends. False breakouts, delayed signals, and misleading overbought or oversold readings limit reliability. Shorter timeframes generate more signals but potentially more false positives, while longer timeframes reduce noise. The passage emphasizes confirmation through other indicators and risk management through stop-loss orders, position sizing, and diversification.

Reported testing produced mixed results. A stock-market mean-reversion example underperformed buy-and-hold since 1993 and lost money after 2018. Some breakout approaches showed promise in gold but performed poorly in gold miners or failed in stocks. The authors report finding no useful strategies for stock indices. No single setting, timeframe, or accompanying indicator works across all markets; profitability depends on the strategy and asset.

India’s top 1% receives 22% of national income, up from 6% in the early 1980s and the highest share since income tax began in 1922, according to economists Lucas Chancel and Thomas Piketty. Inequality declined during the 1950s–1970s under strong market regulations and progressive taxation, then rose as pro-business policies developed in the mid-1980s. The paper says “Shining India” reflects prosperity among the top 10%, rather than the middle 40%, with growth also unevenly distributed within the top group.

Russia is intensifying attacks on Ukrainian drone pilots, treating them as high-value targets because of their battlefield effectiveness. Ukrainian soldiers and operators report rising pilot casualties and extensive strikes on suspected positions. Drones conduct attacks, gather intelligence, and assist artillery targeting; recent assessments attribute around 70% of casualties on both sides to drones. Ukraine also targets Russian drone operators. To reduce their exposure, Ukrainian pilots are building stronger shelters, working deeper underground, and changing positions frequently.

An October 29, 2001 collection of news reports describes Enron’s declining investor confidence, falling share price and efforts to secure additional financing following investment losses and disclosures about partnerships managed by former CFO Andrew Fastow.

- Moody’s cut Enron’s senior unsecured debt rating from Baa1 to Baa2, two levels above junk, and warned of further downgrades. Its commercial-paper rating was also placed under review.

- Enron sought additional bank financing, reportedly $1 billion to $2 billion, after drawing roughly $3 billion from existing credit lines and using about $2 billion to repay commercial paper. Analysts expected lenders to demand higher interest rates, collateral or other restrictions.
- Investor concerns centered on substantial investment charges, a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity and insufficient disclosure of off-balance-sheet transactions. The Securities and Exchange Commission was examining partnership transactions, and Fastow had been removed.
- Major U.S. energy companies reported normal trading with Enron while monitoring their exposure. Several European companies had suspended or restricted dealings because of credit concerns.
- Analysts differed over Enron’s prospects: some warned that declining confidence threatened its trading business, while GimmeCredit considered a junk rating unlikely. A newsletter reported possible Royal Dutch/Shell takeover interest, without company confirmation.
