The free Fantastic Fountain Square Home Tour will take place in Indianapolis on June 16–17, 2018, from noon to 5 p.m. Homes on Woodlawn Avenue, Cottage Avenue and Laurel Street will showcase modern designs and varied floor plans. Food, maps, guided tours and prizes will be provided.

The Washington Court of Appeals affirmed Vernon Clausing’s convictions for delivery and possession with intent to deliver legend drugs. After his medical license was revoked for negligent prescribing, Clausing continued distributing Soma and Nubain. Police obtained drugs from him through a sting operation and found substantial supplies at his home and clinic.

Clausing argued that an unlicensed person could lawfully deliver legend drugs to someone with a valid prescription. The court distinguished delivery from dispensing: an unlicensed person may physically deliver drugs, but unless delivered by a practitioner acting within the scope of a license, the drugs must first be prepared for delivery by a licensed practitioner pursuant to a valid prescription. Clausing produced no evidence supporting his claim that the recipient had a valid prescription.

The court upheld the challenged jury instructions, finding that they accurately stated the law and did not reduce the State’s burden of proof. It also found the charging document sufficient under liberal construction and concluded that Clausing demonstrated no resulting prejudice.

A Board of Pharmacy official testified that revocation of a physician’s license invalidated existing prescriptions, although no Washington authority supported that opinion. The court found any admission error harmless because the jury was instructed not to treat the testimony as law and Clausing supplied no corroborating prescriptions or medical records. The court also rejected his prosecutorial-misconduct claims.

The Simons Observatory in Chile will study the cosmic microwave background using three small-aperture telescopes and one large-aperture telescope across six frequency bands. This study reports laboratory characterization of 25 ultra-high-frequency (UHF) detector modules operating at 220 and 280 GHz, with over 36,000 transition-edge sensor (TES) devices tested.

Each module contains 1,720 antenna-coupled TES bolometers and 36 dark calibration devices, read out through microwave SQUID multiplexing. Testing measured detector yield, critical temperature, saturation power, noise, response time, and optical efficiency.

Key results include:
- Average operable TES yield was 83%, with every module exceeding the 70% baseline requirement.
- Median critical temperature was 163 mK in both frequency bands.
- Median saturation powers were 24 and 26 pW at 220 and 280 GHz, respectively. Twenty-three modules met saturation-power performance requirements.
- Median dark noise-equivalent powers were 39 and 42 aW/√Hz, with approximately 89% of detectors performing better than noise requirements.
- Median optical efficiencies were 0.62 and 0.63.
- Average usable resonator-channel yield was 86%, with frequency-spacing limitations responsible for the largest losses.

Two modules were rejected for unsuitable saturation powers, and another will not be deployed because of low optical efficiency associated with wafer re-annealing. Future detector wafers will avoid re-annealing.

The measured noise levels indicate that detectors should achieve background-limited performance on the sky. Nineteen selected modules will populate the observatory: thirteen have already been deployed, and six are planned for a large-aperture telescope upgrade. All instruments have achieved first light; subsequent papers will report on-sky detector characterization.

Erik Demaine presents a cell-probe lower bound for dynamic connectivity: the maximum of update and query costs must be Ω(log n), even when every connected component is a path. The stated theorem applies to amortized and randomized algorithms, although the lecture focuses on the worst-case proof.

The construction arranges vertices in a √n-by-√n grid, with perfect matchings between consecutive columns representing permutations. Block updates replace individual permutations, while block queries verify proposed prefix compositions. Each block operation requires O(√n) ordinary graph operations.

The proof uses random permutation updates ordered by a bit-reversal sequence and a balanced binary tree over operation times. At every tree node, update positions in the left subtree interleave with query positions in the right subtree. This forces information from earlier updates to be available to later queries. Reads are charged to the lowest common ancestor of their execution time and their last write, avoiding double counting.

An information-theoretic argument first establishes a lower bound for queries that compute prefix compositions. Encoding the addresses and contents of cells written on the left and read on the right permits simulation of the queries and reconstruction of the random updates. Since those updates require many bits to encode, sufficiently many cell probes are necessary.

Verification queries require an additional step: the decoder tries every candidate permutation. Incorrect candidates may access cells absent from the actual execution, so the encoding includes a compact separator constructed using perfect hashing. This lets the decoder reject unsuitable simulations safely.

The encoding bound forces either substantial information transfer across subtrees or sufficiently many total reads and writes. Combining these bounds yields Ω(log n) per ordinary operation. The technique also supports update–query tradeoffs and establishes matching lower bounds for dynamic-tree structures.

Deep brain stimulation (DBS) of the thalamic ventral intermediate nucleus treats tremor, but its mechanism remains unclear. Identifying neural biomarkers recorded through the stimulation lead could support self-adjusting DBS without additional electrodes or external sensors.

Researchers recorded thalamic local field potentials (LFPs) and hand acceleration in 34 surgical patients with essential tremor, multiple sclerosis, or Parkinson’s disease. A subgroup of 16 received DBS at frequencies from 2 to 130 Hz. Analyses assessed LFP spectral power, coherence with acceleration, tremor classification, and stimulation-related changes.

Tremor correlated moderately with theta- and alpha-band LFP power and strongly with peak coherence between LFPs and acceleration. LFP-based decoding of postural tremor achieved an area under the curve of approximately 0.7. High-frequency DBS, approximately 130 Hz, reduced low-frequency LFP power relative to baseline, and postural tremor could also be decoded during stimulation.

A computational model represented three thalamic nuclei using 5,000 thalamocortical relay neurons with bursting, regular, or random firing. Simulated low-frequency LFP power varied considerably with electrode location, tremor-cell distribution, and the proportion of tremor cells. These sensitivities may help explain differences in recorded LFP power across participants and its moderate correlation with tremor.

While President Muhammadu Buhari reported improved electricity supply across Nigeria, his hometown, Daura, and neighbouring towns faced a 10-day blackout after a windstorm felled a newly erected power tower. Businesses were reportedly shutting down. Kano Electricity Distribution Company said repairs were underway and promised restoration within 48 hours. Infrastructure damage had also left parts of Lagos and Ondo without electricity for months.

- Enron-controlled Dabhol Power Co. issued a political force majeure notice amid a dispute with Maharashtra State Electricity Board over unpaid power bills. Reports described the notice as potentially paving the way for interrupted supplies or withdrawal from the $3 billion Indian project. MSEB disputed the notice and pursued penalties for alleged technical underperformance, which Enron rejected.
- India’s finance minister, Yashwant Sinha, said the government agreed to conciliation. Enron had sought London arbitration over 1.02 billion rupees owed for December electricity purchases. Maharashtra was also reviewing the project’s contract.
- Consultant and anti-Enron activist Pradyumna Kaul proposed treating Dabhol as a failed business model, reducing equity and debt and deferring interest. Separately, a state government seeking additional electricity from India’s Central Grid said it had abandoned proposed Enron purchases because of the price.
- E.ON announced plans to acquire Powergen for €8.2 billion in cash and assume €7.1 billion in debt. The transaction would create the world’s second-largest utility by electricity sales volume and expand E.ON into the United States through Powergen’s LG&E subsidiary. Regulatory approvals and asset sales remained significant challenges.
- Houston Area Water Corp.’s board selected Montgomery Watson for negotiations on a water plant contract worth up to $150 million, rejecting City Hall staff’s preferred bidder, Enron affiliate Azurix. Montgomery Watson’s bid was approximately $17 million lower; City Council approval remained necessary.
- American Airlines completed its acquisition of TWA’s assets, becoming the world’s largest air carrier. Allegheny Energy planned a stock sale to help finance its $1.03 billion purchase of three Enron power plants.

The passage describes container and distributed-system patterns for separating responsibilities, improving reuse, and scaling services.

- **Ambassador containers** manage how applications communicate with external services while presenting a localhost interface. They can route requests to storage shards, discover and broker services across environments, or split traffic between production and experimental systems. Examples use twemproxy for sharded Redis and memcached, and nginx for directing 10% of traffic to experiments. Keeping this logic separate allows ambassadors to be reused across applications.

- **Adapter containers** translate application interfaces into standardized interfaces for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Examples include exporting Redis metrics to Prometheus, using fluentd to normalize logs and capture Redis slow queries, and testing MySQL health through application-specific queries. Separate adapters support independent updates, resource allocation, and reuse without modifying third-party application images.

- **Microservices** divide applications into independently running components that communicate through defined APIs. This supports smaller teams, independent releases, and service-specific scaling. However, distributed communication makes debugging and architectural design harder. Established patterns provide reusable approaches to these challenges.

- **Replicated load-balanced services** use interchangeable servers to provide redundancy and horizontal scaling. Readiness probes distinguish applications that are running from those ready to handle requests. Session tracking directs a user’s requests to the same replica; application-level mechanisms such as cookies are preferred when external IP addresses or intermediary caches make IP-based tracking unsuitable. Consistent hashing reduces reassignment when replica counts change.

- **Caching and edge layers** extend replicated services. A separate caching tier permits independent scaling and avoids duplicating cached content across numerous small caches. Reverse proxies can also enforce rate limits. The examples combine application replicas, Varnish caches, and nginx servers for SSL termination, using Kubernetes Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and Secrets.

- **Sharded services** divide requests or data among servers rather than making every replica responsible for everything. Sharding increases usable storage capacity, but shard failures and upgrades can reduce cache effectiveness and overload backend services. Replicating each shard improves resilience and allows heavily loaded shards to scale independently. Shared shard-routing services simplify client deployment but introduce additional network traffic, latency, and scaling responsibilities.

- **Sharding functions** should be deterministic and distribute load uniformly. Keys must reflect the information that determines a response: overly specific keys waste cache capacity, while overly general keys can return inappropriate results. Consistent hashing limits key reassignment when shard counts change. Cache-dependent systems should be tested both with and without caches.

- **Scatter/gather** distributes portions of a request across multiple workers and combines their results. It supports parallel computation and searches over sharded data. Benefits are limited by request-handling overhead and slow workers, because complete responses depend on the required leaf results. Replicating each leaf shard supports availability, upgrades, and greater processing capacity.

- **Function-as-a-service (FaaS)** supports event-driven applications through simplified deployment, automatic scaling, and failure recovery. Its independent, stateless functions complicate dependency tracking, monitoring, and debugging. FaaS is generally poorly suited to long-running background processing, large in-memory datasets, or sustained workloads where per-request pricing becomes unfavorable. Event-driven computing and serverless computing are distinct concepts. One FaaS pattern decorates requests or responses by transforming them before passing them to another service.

Under CEO Dan Schulman, PayPal adopted a mission in 2015 to democratize financial services and improve financial health. Its strategy combined services for consumers and merchants with partnerships, acquisitions, and product development. Accelerated adoption of digital payments during the pandemic contributed to growth, and PayPal reached 426 million active accounts by the end of 2021.

Despite paying at or above market rates, PayPal discovered substantial financial insecurity among its employees. Assessments conducted in 2018–2019 found that nearly two-thirds of surveyed customer service employees ran out—or nearly ran out—of money between paychecks. Half of global customer service employees had only 4–6% of their pay remaining after basic living expenses, before accounting for dependents. Financial difficulties also contributed to absenteeism and departures.

PayPal developed estimated net disposable income, or eNDI, to measure income remaining after taxes and typical living costs. In October 2019, it announced a four-part Employee Financial Wellness Initiative targeting hourly and entry-level employees:
- Wage increases where appropriate.
- A 60% reduction in U.S. healthcare premiums for eligible employees, plus company-funded health reimbursement accounts.
- Equity grants averaging $3,100 for approximately 8,600 employees who had not previously received equity.
- Financial education, digital resources, and confidential individual coaching.

The initiative cost tens of millions of dollars in its first year. Leadership and the board supported it as consistent with PayPal’s mission and expected it to improve retention, productivity, and customer service, although the financial return was uncertain.

During the pandemic, PayPal avoided pandemic-related layoffs, provided remote-work equipment and stipends, and introduced crisis leave. It subsequently expanded financial wellness support through additional equity grants and services allowing employees to access earned wages before payday without fees or interest.

Early results indicated improvements. In 2020, 76% of surveyed employees intended to stay at PayPal for at least five years, compared with 51% in 2018. Customer service turnover declined from 19.4% in 2019 to 7.3% in 2020, while productivity, customer loyalty, and employee engagement improved. By January 2021, minimum eNDI for U.S. hourly and entry-level employees reached 11%; PayPal’s global goal was 20%.

PayPal also sought broader corporate participation through the Worker Financial Wellness Initiative, whose members committed to assessing workers’ financial health. By the end of 2021, 11 companies had joined.

The paper studies popular matchings in house allocation, marriage, and roommates problems, allowing strict preferences or ties and weighted or unweighted agents. A matching is popular if, against every alternative matching, the total weight of agents strictly preferring it is at least the weight preferring the alternative. Such matchings do not always exist.

To address nonexistence, the paper introduces **popular winning sets**: collections of matchings evaluated by each agent’s best assignment across the collection. A collection wins if its weighted support is at least that of every alternative matching. The **popular dimension** of an instance is the minimum size of such a collection; for a class of instances, it is the maximum of these minimum sizes.

The main results are:
- **House allocation:** The popular dimension is exactly 2 in all four combinations of weighting and preference types.
- **Marriage:** The dimension is 1 for unweighted agents with strict preferences. With weights or ties, it is between 2 and 3.
- **Roommates:** The dimension is exactly 2 for unweighted agents with strict preferences. With weights or ties, it is between 2 and 3.

The proofs provide polynomial-time algorithms achieving these upper bounds. For house allocation, the algorithm constructs an allocation that decomposes into two matchings. For unweighted roommates with strict preferences, a greedy procedure constructs two matchings. For general roommates instances, the algorithm transforms the problem into house allocation and decomposes the resulting edges into three matchings; this also supplies the general marriage upper bound.

Popular winning sets satisfy a stronger condition than Condorcet winning sets because indifferent voters do not count toward their support. Consequently, the results also establish Condorcet dimension at most 3 for these matching problems.

Determining whether the dimension is 2 or 3 for marriage and roommates problems with weights or ties remains open. The authors conjecture that the general marriage problem has popular dimension 2.

This study examines how climate-induced displacement affects K–12 learners’ education in lower- and middle-income countries (LMICs), where limited resources, infrastructure, and social services heighten vulnerability. Drawing on 73 English-language academic and grey-literature sources, it combines a Human Rights-Based Approach to education with Education in Emergencies research to assess immediate and long-term effects on educational access, quality, and learning environments.

Before displacement, sudden disasters damage schools and transportation or turn classrooms into emergency shelters. Slow-onset crises undermine household income and food security, making education unaffordable and increasing children’s work responsibilities. Heat, malnutrition, disease, and psychological trauma can impair learning and development. Although some studies report increased attendance during disasters, this does not necessarily improve academic performance.

After relocation, learners encounter additional financial pressures, restrictive registration and documentation requirements, curricular differences, discrimination, and social exclusion. Distance education faces limitations involving technology access, connectivity, teacher training, certification, funding, and reduced social interaction. Inadequate institutional preparedness and unreliable data further constrain support. Displacement-related trauma and disrupted family and community connections can undermine well-being and educational engagement.

Girls face heightened barriers as climate pressures reinforce existing gender inequalities. Families may prioritize boys’ schooling, while girls assume additional domestic responsibilities or face menstrual hygiene difficulties, early marriage, and cultural restrictions on attendance.

The study recommends sustainable financial assistance, simplified enrollment, academic and mental health support, inclusive learning environments, stronger monitoring systems, and gender-responsive policies. It identifies research gaps concerning climate displacement within emergency education, long-term educational outcomes, and proactive policy development. It advocates integrating education into climate adaptation strategies and replacing short-term responses with sustained, rights-based support.

In Mock v. Watson, the court affirmed an order setting apart a widow’s interest in her deceased husband’s real estate despite unpaid estate debts and insufficient other assets. The heirs argued that her share could be assigned only after creditors were paid.

The court held that the widow’s statutory interest was not subject to the husband’s debts. Although the Code abolished dower, the wife’s interest attached when marriage and the husband’s ownership coincided and became vested upon his death. Unlike the heirs’ interest, her share was not made subject to estate charges.

Statutes authorizing sales of real estate to pay debts applied only to the estate’s interest, excluding the widow’s share. Restrictions against prejudicing creditors did not subordinate her interest to their claims, but prevented her receiving more than the prescribed one-third in value.

Industrial simulation, modeling, and analysis increasingly require complex calculations, creating trade-offs between speed and accuracy when computing capacity is limited. In an IDC survey, 42% of respondents reported outdated or inaccurate simulations, and half said iterations and calculations took too long. High demand for high-performance calculations was expected to rise from 8% of respondents to almost half within two years.

High-performance computing (HPC) uses technologies including parallel processing across connected systems to perform complex calculations efficiently. It enables faster, higher-quality simulations, more iterations, new applications, and quicker development of products, processes, and data-based services. Among respondents, 81% viewed HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation, rising to 96% among enterprises already using it. More than a quarter already used professional HPC infrastructure, while another 39% were planning or piloting deployment.

External infrastructure is prominent in deployment plans. Among current HPC users, 87% preferred external infrastructure for existing workloads or planned to use it; 74% operated or planned their own infrastructure in colocation facilities. Only 6% had HPC infrastructure in an on-premises datacenter, while 28% planned its use within two years.

HPC adoption faces several challenges:
- Security concerns were important to 72% of respondents.
- Energy consumption and sustainability were key issues for 58%.
- A lack of internal and external expertise affected 42% of HPC users.
- Investment, operating and licensing costs, insufficient capacity, downtime, and infrastructure complexity also constrained use.

IDC expects public cloud HPC to become the most important architecture among surveyed manufacturers using or planning HPC, followed by hybrid cloud approaches. Cloud-based HPC and HPC as a Service (HPCaaS) offer scalable capacity, flexible spending, access to current technologies, and reduced infrastructure-management requirements. Hybrid architectures can retain sensitive workloads internally while using public cloud resources for demand peaks or non-critical work. However, cloud HPC still requires skilled personnel to configure systems, program calculations, and interpret results.

HPCaaS can also support shared engineering environments, collaboration, and new business models without large upfront infrastructure investments. Of respondents already using HPC, 81% intended to implement HPC-based business models.

IDC recommends integrating virtual development into digital transformation, establishing a common data foundation, selecting operating models according to utilization, budget, performance, security, and skills, and prioritizing scalability and energy efficiency. It also recommends seeking external expertise where necessary.

The findings came from a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Uber suspended self-driving vehicle testing in the U.S. and Canada after one of its vehicles struck and killed Elaine Herzberg, 49, in Tempe, Arizona. Police said she was walking outside a crosswalk when the Volvo, operating autonomously with a human operator behind the wheel, hit her. It was the first fatality involving a fully autonomous test vehicle. Uber said it was cooperating with local law enforcement.

Indian press reports dated April 27, 2001, described an escalating dispute between Enron-promoted Dabhol Power Company (DPC) and the Maharashtra State Electricity Board (MSEB) over unpaid bills, penalties and electricity tariffs.

DPC’s board authorised management to issue a preliminary notice terminating its power purchase agreement with MSEB. The resolution passed six votes to one, with IDBI opposing and MSEB excluded from voting as an interested party. Authorisation did not mean immediate termination; reports described further contractual procedures, including a six-month consultation period.

Domestic lenders favoured renegotiation and expressed concern about their loans. Reports differed on international lenders’ positions: some said they opposed immediate termination, while others said they supported withdrawal and were withholding further funding for the nearly completed second phase.

MSEB paid Rs 134 crore under protest toward its Rs 146.64-crore March bill, disputing the remaining Rs 12.64 crore. Earlier unpaid bills remained contested alongside MSEB’s Rs 401-crore penalty against DPC for alleged supply failures.

Maharashtra opposed termination and planned a committee to renegotiate the agreement, particularly its tariffs. Union Power Minister Suresh Prabhu said termination would cost the Centre Rs 2,840 crore. DPC officials generally declined public comment on board proceedings.

HDFC Mutual Fund decided to wind up HDFC FMP 378D March 2014 (1) with unit-holder approval after net assets fell below Rs 10 crore, making management unviable. Its corpus is invested in cash and cash equivalents.

Following the September 11, 2001 terrorist attacks, Enron and other energy companies suspended trading, closed offices and sent nonessential employees home. The New York Mercantile Exchange evacuated safely and remained closed September 12. U.S. power trading largely stopped, and several telecommunications-bandwidth trading operations also shut down.

Energy companies increased security at power plants, pipelines and refineries. The Nuclear Regulatory Commission ordered heightened security at all 104 U.S. nuclear reactors. Major suppliers reported continued electricity and natural-gas deliveries and normal refinery operations, although some storage and distribution facilities closed temporarily.

Oil and gasoline prices rose amid fears that possible U.S. retaliation could disrupt Middle Eastern supplies. Consumers queued for gasoline, while Exxon Mobil reported ample supplies and urged normal purchasing. OPEC said it was prepared to act to prevent price spikes. Natural-gas traders warned of volatility and potential short covering.

Enron announced it would resume North American gas and electricity trading on September 12 through EnronOnline and telephone transactions until noon Houston time. It said physical infrastructure remained secure and operational and saw no reason for those markets to become unstable. Markets outside North America would follow normal schedules.

Houston businesses experienced widespread voluntary closures and evacuations, with many planning to reopen September 12 under increased security. Foreign energy companies also reviewed South Asian security arrangements; Enron India reported precautions to protect its installations, employees and offices.

Separately, Enron’s 65%-owned Dabhol Power Co. warned that financial constraints arising from its payment dispute with the Maharashtra State Electricity Board would impair debt repayment and plant preservation. Its first phase had been idle since May, and second-phase construction had stopped at 97% completion. BJP leader Gopinath Munde opposed proposed Maharashtra tariff increases and load shedding, urging purchases of Enron power at reasonable rates.

The study presents two all-optical thermometry methods using silicon-vacancy (SiV) centers in diamonds: multi-feature regression (MFR) and two-stage multi-feature regression (2SMFR). Both combine temperature-dependent SiV photoluminescence and diamond Raman signals to predict temperatures of previously unseen diamonds, reducing the need for individual sensor calibration.

Experiments used eight approximately 1-µm diamonds measured between 25 and 85 °C at seven temperature set points. Up to nine spectral features were tracked, including intensity, peak position, and linewidth. Models were trained on subsets of diamonds and evaluated on independent test sets, producing generalized performance metrics rather than estimates based on training data.

MFR evaluates all 511 nonempty combinations of nine features to select the best-performing subset. Its strongest combination comprised SiV zero-phonon-line wavelength, SiV linewidth, and Raman linewidth. The best MFR performance was an accuracy error of 1.7 K and resolution of 1.2 K·Hz⁻¹/², representing approximately 26% better accuracy than the best single-feature model. Calibration gains diminished substantially beyond approximately three diamonds and a few temperature set points.

2SMFR combines partial least squares regression, Lasso feature selection, and spline-based bias correction. It requires more calibration data but achieved the strongest overall performance when trained on seven diamonds and seven temperatures: 0.7 K accuracy error and 0.6 K·Hz⁻¹/² resolution. These represent approximately 70% better accuracy and 50% better resolution than the best single-feature model. Its reported relative sensitivity was 0.04 K⁻¹, approximately seven times that of the best single-feature model.

The methods offer different trade-offs between calibration effort and predictive performance. Reported generalized metrics should not be directly compared with literature values evaluated on calibration data. The study also cautions that assumed linear feature–temperature relationships may not hold over wider temperature ranges, and predictions outside the training range may be unreliable.

Thai Prime Minister Prayuth Chan-ocha said Thailand had no trade with North Korea and complied with U.N. resolutions. U.S. envoy Joseph Yun was expected in Bangkok to discuss increasing pressure over North Korea’s weapons programs. Thailand’s foreign ministry previously reported trade with North Korea had fallen by as much as 94 percent over the preceding year.

Josephine Slosson’s father granted her a lifetime interest in trust income and power to dispose of the principal by will. She exercised that power through bequests, directions to pay her debts, and distribution of the balance to her surviving issue. Her three children sought to take under their grandfather’s will instead.

The court held that Slosson validly exercised the power, making the beneficiaries’ interests subject to transfer tax. Her children could not take under their grandfather’s alternative provision because it applied only if she failed to dispose of the fund by will. Since they had not renounced their legacies, the consequences of renunciation were not before the court. Transfers from the trust to pay Slosson’s debts were also taxable.

The court modified the tax order to exclude $682.04 from Alice Slosson’s taxable bequest because that amount reimbursed advances used to settle creditors’ claims, rather than a debt owed to her at Slosson’s death. Otherwise, the tax order was affirmed.

The quarterback is regarded as football’s most important position, serving as the offense’s leader and playing a central role in every offensive play. Responsibilities include receiving the snap, handing off or throwing the ball, occasionally running, communicating plays, ensuring correct formations, reading defenses, and changing plays when necessary. Preparation involves studying the playbook, scouting reports, and opponent film.

Key quarterback skills include:
- **Football IQ and decision-making:** Understanding plays, recognizing defensive coverages, and avoiding risky passes.
- **Accuracy:** Completing passes that allow receivers to maintain momentum and protect themselves from big hits.
- **Leadership:** Inspiring confidence, holding teammates accountable, and preparing thoroughly, whether starting or serving as a backup.
- **Footwork, athleticism, and arm strength:** Supporting effective passing, escaping defensive pressure, and gaining yards when opportunities arise.

Quarterbacks vary in size and athletic ability, and coaches adapt offensive systems to their strengths. Although tall, strong players were traditionally preferred, smaller, more athletic quarterbacks have become more common.

The position is also called “Signal Caller,” “Field General,” or “QB”; “Gunslinger” describes quarterbacks associated with strong arms and aggressive passing.

The passage highlights Otto Graham, Peyton Manning, Dan Marino, Joe Montana, and Tom Brady among notable quarterbacks. Their achievements include Graham’s 10 consecutive championship appearances, Manning’s two Super Bowl titles, Marino’s passing milestones, Montana’s four Super Bowl titles, and Brady’s record for Super Bowl championships by a quarterback.

The UC1825B-SP PWM controller supports high-frequency power supplies using current- or voltage-mode control. Features include input-voltage feed-forward, current limiting, shutdown, soft start, undervoltage lockout, jitter-free logic, and high-current totem-pole outputs.

Carol Christ, 73, becomes UC Berkeley’s first female and oldest chancellor amid sexual harassment scandals, budget problems, housing shortages and free speech disputes. A former Berkeley professor and administrator who later led Smith College, she succeeds Nicholas Dirks with faculty expressing optimism about her leadership.

Christ’s priorities include addressing Black student underrepresentation, campus sexual assault and a fractured sense of community. She plans to designate 2017–18 a “free speech year,” featuring debates between speakers with differing views.

To ease the housing shortage, Christ wants partnerships with Berkeley and Oakland. She says homelessness and safety must be addressed before considering student housing at People’s Park.

Berkeley must halve its $110 million budget deficit this year. Christ has proposed increased private philanthropy and administrative cuts. She also advocates a larger role for UC campuses in Sacramento amid lawmakers’ concerns about financial transparency. Across these challenges, she emphasizes dialogue among campus groups and plans to attend student events to strengthen community ties.

Zimbabwean nurse and epidemiologist Chenai Mathabire received an International AIDS Society prize for research showing that health facilities in Malawi and Mozambique could implement rapid tuberculosis testing for HIV-positive patients.

Working with Doctors Without Borders, her team found that the urine-based test delivered results in less than an hour, potentially allowing same-day treatment. Conventional testing took an average of two to four days, with delays sometimes lasting months. Staff could learn to administer the rapid test within hours, health workers found results easy to interpret, and patients welcomed it.

The findings prompted some Doctors Without Borders-supported health centers to adopt rapid testing and could encourage wider use. Mathabire continues working for the organization and is considering further HIV and tuberculosis research.

Players discuss responding to strong opposition, improved first-period play and limiting shots. One player describes an unexpected move from Toronto to Detroit that provided a playoff opportunity, thanking Jimmy Devellano and Scotty Bowman. Detroit’s championship is credited to a total team effort, including key contributions from five Russian players. A player says the team improved throughout the playoffs and expected to outplay opponents, though winning four straight games was unexpected.

A study in The American Journal of Psychiatry tracked 33,908 Norwegian adults over 11 years. Participants reporting no exercise were 44 percent more likely to experience depression than those exercising one to two hours weekly. Researchers estimated that small amounts of exercise could have prevented 12 percent of reported depression cases.

Irish soccer player Megan Connolly posted a viral video of her frightening amusement ride in Myrtle Beach, featuring teammate Dallas Dorosy laughing at her reaction and the Fray’s “How To Save A Life.”

Options expiry is when an options contract becomes void. The passage describes U.S. expiration as the third Saturday of the expiration month, with trading generally ending the preceding Friday or Thursday if Friday is a public holiday. Expiration periods are associated with increased trading volumes and slightly higher volatility, particularly during quarterly “quad witching” expirations.

The passage recommends developing strategies through research, backtesting over at least 15 years or different market cycles, and forward-testing under current conditions. Its backtests focus on stocks and ETFs rather than options because of options’ complexity and unavailable data.

Reported results include:
- S&P 500 ETF (SPY) expiration-week trading: 0.3% average weekly gain, with January and July negative.
- Healthcare ETF (XLV) strategy: approximately 0.7% average gain per trade.
- SPY overnight strategy: 0.46% average gain.
- SPY expiration-day short strategy: 0.18% average gain across 306 trades.

Some trading rules are not disclosed. The authors consider expiration-related seasonality strategies potentially robust and suitable for further development.

Liberal leader Andrew Wilkinson blamed Premier John Horgan’s tax increases for rising gasoline prices and called for a gas-tax cut. Horgan attributed a nine-cent overnight increase to corporate profiteering, not taxation, and said increasing domestic refining capacity could help address supply issues and benefit consumers.

Google’s Project Fi is adding the $199 moto G6, $740 LG G7 ThinQ and $899 LG V35 ThinQ to its limited phone lineup. The service lacks Apple and Samsung phones, which may constrain customer growth. Launched in April 2015, Fi uses major carriers and Wi-Fi, automatically selecting the strongest available network. It charges $20 monthly for unlimited calls and texts, plus $10 per gigabyte of data up to 6GB, without charging for unused data. Google has not disclosed subscriber numbers but claims a healthy user base and high satisfaction. Analyst Roger Entner cites limited handset choice and little advertising as obstacles.

Apple Inc.’s Form 8-K dated October 27, 2022, reports that the company issued a press release announcing financial results for its fourth fiscal quarter ended September 24, 2022. The press release is attached as Exhibit 99.1. The report’s information is not deemed “filed” under Section 18 of the Securities Exchange Act or incorporated by reference into other filings unless expressly specified. The report was signed by Luca Maestri, Senior Vice President and Chief Financial Officer.

The Texas Court of Civil Appeals affirmed a judgment denying the Wilson appellants damages from a head-on collision. The jury found that Wilson negligently drove north into the western lane of a three-lane highway and that this negligence was the sole proximate cause of the collision.

The appellants challenged the submission and omission of jury issues and opposing counsel’s argument. The court held that objections to the jury charge were waived because appellants neither objected nor timely submitted written requests in accordance with procedural rules. They also failed to object when opposing counsel made the challenged argument. Because any harmful effect could have been cured by an instruction, the argument did not warrant reversal. The court found no reversible error.

The speaker accepts the Democratic presidential nomination, endorses the party’s platform on civil and economic rights, and thanks running mate Lyndon Johnson and other party leaders. Addressing concerns about his religious affiliation, he affirms separation of church and state and pledges to make public policy decisions independently in the national interest.

He criticizes Richard Nixon and Republican leadership while arguing that Democrats must offer more than attacks on their opponents. He identifies international challenges including expanding Communist influence, poverty, shifting alliances, and weapons capable of destroying humanity. Domestic concerns include agricultural surpluses, overcrowded schools, inadequate housing, racial discrimination, insecurity among older citizens, job displacement through automation, and declining ethical standards.

Calling for a new generation of leadership, he presents the “New Frontier” of the 1960s as a set of challenges rather than promises. These encompass science and space, peace and war, ignorance and prejudice, and poverty and surplus. He asks Americans for courage, innovation, sacrifice, and commitment to the common good.

The speaker frames the election as a choice between progress and complacency, public interest and private comfort, and national greatness and decline. He urges Americans to demonstrate that their free society can meet Communist competition and asks for their help and votes.

North Tyneside’s cabinet unanimously backed progressing the North of Tyne devolution deal, covering Newcastle, Northumberland and North Tyneside. The deal includes an elected mayor and £600m over 30 years, with 10,000 jobs projected. Mayor Norma Redfearn said councils south of the Tyne could seek government approval to join later. The authority was expected to launch in summer 2018, with mayoral elections in May 2019. Newcastle leader Nick Forbes rejected concerns that it would be under-powered, citing higher investment per person and health and housing provisions. A vote to split the existing North East Combined Authority was postponed until mid-April.

Coach Bylsma restored confidence through a new philosophy. Winning the first three games of a five-game road trip and acquiring Billy and Adams marked a season turnaround. Sid’s leadership comes through playing within the team’s system and balancing offense with defensive responsibility. Jordan’s offensive talent and responsible two-way play are also valued. The speaker praises talented leaders for their effort and admires an organization’s sustained dominance despite losing significant players after success. Personally, the speaker hopes for a championship ring rather than many mementos.

A soccer penalty kick is awarded for a defender’s foul inside their own penalty area that would otherwise warrant a direct free kick. Taken from a mark 12 yards from goal against the opposing goalkeeper, it requires accurate technique, composure, and consistent practice.

**Rules and responsibilities**
- The ball must be stationary, with part touching or overhanging the penalty mark’s center, and the kicker must be identified.
- Other players must remain outside the penalty area, behind the mark, and at least 10 yards away until the ball is kicked.
- The goalkeeper must face the kicker and, at the moment of the kick, have part of one foot touching, in line with, or behind the goal line.
- The kicker must wait for the referee’s whistle and kick forward. Feinting during the approach is permitted, but faking the kick after completing the approach is not.
- The kicker may shoot again after a goalkeeper’s save, but cannot immediately replay a rebound from a post or crossbar without another player touching it.
- Coaches are responsible for teaching the rules, preparing teammates, and selecting primary and alternate kickers before matches.

**Developing the kicker**
Selection should reflect scoring success, confidence, and composure. A designated kicker who feels unprepared or uncomfortable should be able to request an alternate without criticism.

Players should experiment with kicking techniques, target locations, starting positions, and approaches, then establish a repeatable routine. This routine should cover ball placement, relaxation, the run-up, body position, the strike, and follow-through. Kickers should avoid changing their intended shot at the last moment.

Accuracy takes priority over maximum power, although sufficient pace is needed to beat the goalkeeper. Inside-of-the-foot kicks generally offer accuracy, instep drives offer power, and instep-face kicks can produce rising or bending shots. Lower corners are generally preferred because upper-corner attempts risk going over the crossbar.

**Mental preparation and practice**
Kickers should practice remaining calm and blocking out distractions through focus, measured breathing, visualization, confidence, and positive thinking. Goalkeeper movements should not disrupt their routine.

Training should progress from target-based practice to work with goalkeepers, coaching feedback, and simulated match conditions. Players should practice on the surfaces they compete on, rehearse the complete routine regularly, and take kicks during scrimmages and when tired. Coaches should also prepare teammates to respond to rebounds without entering early.

**Advanced preparation**
More experienced kickers can develop multiple reliable shots, study goalkeepers’ habits, and refine legal deceptive approaches. Advanced options include changing the apparent kicker and tapping the ball forward for an approaching teammate to shoot. These require coordinated preparation.

Coaches should support players after misses, prohibit teammate criticism, and ensure penalty-taking assignments are clear rather than improvised when a kick is awarded.

The passage provides push-pull converter design guidance, power supply requirements, and PCB layout recommendations for TPS7H500x-SP controllers.

- **Timing:** Approximately 25 ns dead time, set with 20.5-kΩ resistors, reduces GaN reverse-conduction losses. Initial leading-edge blanking is approximately 50 ns using 49.9 kΩ and may require adjustment for ringing, PCB parasitics, and gate-driver delay. A 33-nF soft-start capacitor produces approximately 7.5 ms soft-start.
- **Transformer:** The design targets a 35% maximum duty cycle below the controller’s 50% limit. Selected transformer turns ratio is 2.5; actual primary inductance is 40 μH versus a calculated 33 μH. Magnetizing current involves a size-efficiency trade-off.
- **Switching devices:** Primary GaN FETs are rated at 170 V for a maximum 36-V input. Synchronous rectifier GaN FETs are rated at 80 V despite approximately 20-V expected stress, allowing transient margin. Parallel Schottky diodes can reduce soft-start current through the GaN FETs and reverse-conduction losses.
- **Clamp and output components:** An RCD clamp can limit switch-node voltage but requires testing and optimization. The output inductor is 0.47 μH, targeting 40% current ripple. Calculations require at least 1.3 mF output capacitance; approximately 2.3 mF is used to help mitigate radiation-induced single-event transients. Additional filtering can reduce output noise.
- **Protection and compensation:** Cycle-by-cycle current limiting begins near 35 A, using a 1:100 current-sense transformer and 7.5-Ω sense resistor. The hiccup capacitor is 3.3 nF. Type 2A compensation targets a 10-kHz crossover frequency, with selected components of 40.2 kΩ, 15 nF, and 47 pF. The slope-compensation resistor is 102 kΩ.
- **Supply and layout:** Controllers operate from 4–14 V and require at least 0.1 μF input bypass capacitance. Recommendations include short switching loops, minimal switch-node copper, separation of sensitive signals from noisy traces, separate analog and power grounds joined at one point, and nearby bypass and compensation components.

The document also includes related technical resources, revision history, ESD precautions, packaging information, and legal notices assigning application design, validation, and compliance responsibilities to developers.

The study uses density functional theory (DFT) to investigate the structural, electronic, mechanical, thermal, and optical properties of three out-of-plane ordered MAX phases: Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃, Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃, and Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃. Calculations were performed with CASTEP using GGA-PBE and GGA-PBEsol functionals, with particular attention to potential thermal barrier coating applications.

All three compounds have hexagonal structures with the P6₃/mmc space group and 16 atoms per unit cell. Negative formation energies, the absence of negative phonon frequencies, and compliance with elastic stability criteria indicate chemical, dynamical, and mechanical stability. Formation energies are −0.506, −0.349, and −0.386 eV/atom for the Zr-, Nb-, and Ta-containing compounds, respectively.

Electronic band structures and density-of-states calculations indicate metallic behavior and direction-dependent conductivity. Bonding analyses identify a mixture of covalent, ionic, and metallic interactions, including strong metal–carbon bonding.

The compounds are mechanically anisotropic and classified as brittle using elastic-property criteria. In the GGA-PBEsol results, Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃ exhibits the highest Young’s modulus, fracture toughness, and machinability index. Calculated Vickers hardness values are 6.025 GPa for Mo₂Zr₂AlC₃, 6.277 GPa for Mo₂Nb₂AlC₃, and 6.224 GPa for Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃. Corresponding fracture toughness values are 2.67, 2.78, and 2.59 MPa·m½.

Thermal calculations support their potential as thermal barrier coatings. Estimated minimum thermal conductivities are 0.89, 0.90, and 0.74 W/m·K, while estimated melting temperatures are 2064, 2237, and 2131 K, respectively. Thermal expansion coefficients at 300 K are 11.11, 9.90, and 11.47 × 10⁻⁶ K⁻¹. Mo₂Ta₂AlC₃ combines the lowest minimum thermal conductivity with the lowest GGA-PBEsol Young’s modulus, making it particularly relevant to thermal insulation and thermal-shock resistance. Lattice thermal conductivity decreases as temperature rises, while heat capacities approach the Dulong–Petit limit at elevated temperatures.

Optical calculations indicate anisotropic metallic responses, approximately 98% infrared reflectivity near 1 eV, and substantial visible and ultraviolet reflectivity. These computational findings identify the compounds as candidates for high-temperature thermal barrier coatings and solar heat-shielding layers, providing a basis for further theoretical and practical evaluation.

- **ARM Cortex-A8 subsystem:** Integrates a general-purpose processor with Harvard architecture, NEON SIMD, VFPv3 floating-point support, separate instruction and data caches, and hardware/software debugging. Trace data is captured in a 32KB Embedded Trace Buffer rather than exposed through external pins. The interrupt controller prioritizes peripheral requests and generates IRQ or FIQ signals, although general-purpose devices do not support FIQ generation. An embedded PLL generates subsystem clocks. A 128-bit DMM port provides DDR access, while a 64-bit L3 port accesses other device modules.

- **C674x DSP subsystem:** Includes eight functional units, two data paths, and 64 general-purpose 32-bit registers. It combines C64x+ performance with C67x+ floating-point capabilities and supports parallel arithmetic, complex multiplication, packing, sorting, and Galois field operations. Additional features include interruptible software-pipelined loops, compact instructions, exception handling, user/supervisor modes, memory permissions, and a free-running timestamp counter. Listed memories include 32KB L1 program memory/cache with error detection and 256KB L2 RAM/cache with error correction.

- **Memory management:** The system MMU translates C674x MDMA accesses into physical addresses, protects ARM memory regions from accidental DSP corruption, and supports shared user-space buffers. EDMA TC0 and TC1 accesses can optionally use the MMU. A unified memory map provides a consistent resource view where possible. TILER adds 4GB of addressing for rotated and mirrored frame-buffer views; the full extended range is accessible only to HDVPSS and ISS.

- **Media processing:** The Media Controller manages HDVPSS and ISS. HDVICP2 accelerates video encoding, decoding, and transcoding for multiple codec standards, including MPEG, H.264, VC-1, RealVideo, AVS, and VP6.2/VP7. The face-detection module detects and tracks faces in QVGA 8-bit grayscale images and reports face size, position, angle, and confidence.

- **Processor coordination:** A hardware spinlock module provides 128 semaphores for resource synchronization. The mailbox module supports processor communication through message queues, four-message FIFO depth, flexible processor assignment, and interrupt notifications.

- **Pins and interfaces:** Terminal tables describe pin functions, multiplexing, supply sources, pullup/pulldown states, and reset behavior. Boot configuration pins are sampled at reset and subsequently serve GPMC functions. Interfaces covered include DDR2/DDR3, Ethernet, GPIO, HDMI, I2C, McASP, PCIe, SD, SPI, UART, USB, timers, clocks, and video input/output. GPIO pins can also act as external interrupt inputs. Digital video interfaces support RGB and YCbCr configurations; analog outputs support composite and S-Video.

- **Electrical requirements:** The passage specifies external pullups for I2C0, connection requirements for analog video outputs, and instructions for unused or powered-down pins. Several analog supplies must remain connected even when their associated peripherals are unused. Designated pins require 1µF capacitors to ground.

This critical reflection proposes a framework for ethical generative AI use in education, applicable to online, blended, and in-person settings. It argues that AI should support human agency, critical reflection, and meaningful action rather than merely automate assignments and increase efficiency.

The framework draws on five philosophical perspectives:
- **Günther Anders:** Technological capabilities can exceed people’s ability to comprehend their consequences. Critical reflection and imagination help challenge the assumption that whatever technology makes possible must be adopted.
- **Michel Foucault:** AI can shape “regimes of truth,” giving corporations influence over knowledge production. Inconsistent outputs, hallucinations, biases, and opaque processes require critical human assessment.
- **Paulo Freire:** Educational technology can serve humanizing purposes when it promotes dialogue, critical understanding, and collective efforts to transform the world.
- **Bloom’s revised taxonomy:** AI can perform tasks across cognitive levels, although cited research reports stronger performance at lower levels. The taxonomy helps classify learning but does not adequately address its ethical purposes.
- **Hannah Arendt:** Distinguishing labor, work, and action directs attention beyond repetitive consumption toward lasting contributions and public engagement.

The proposed framework places student AI use on a spectrum from **consumptive labor to humanizing action**. Uncritical, impersonal, or erroneous AI-generated assignments fall toward the consumptive end. Uses demonstrating students’ perspectives, critical engagement, and capacity to act fall toward the humanizing end. Cognitive complexity alone does not establish ethical value; even sophisticated content creation may lack meaningful purpose.

Two imagined applications illustrate the framework. In community-based political learning, students use AI to research local issues and candidates while developing their own evaluations and participation plans. In individualized research, AI provides Socratic questioning and research support, while students work with human mentors and share findings through community outreach.

The authors call for educators to redesign objectives, activities, and assessments around humanizing goals, continually reassess AI use, and investigate ethically ambiguous cases through future research.

The disclosure describes a device and methods for implementing fundamental computational primitives using a processor, memory, programmable streaming engines, and a matrix multiplication accelerator (MMA). Applications include speech recognition, industrial control, object recognition, and vision.

The example MMA contains a 1×32 multiplier buffer, two 32×32 multiplicand buffers, and two 32×32 result buffers, all storing 16-bit elements. Background and foreground buffers allow data loading, computation, and result output to overlap. A load-store-execute instruction supports these operations within a single cycle, including direct assignment, addition, or subtraction of multiplication results.

Configurable MMA features include input and output data formatting, fixed-point fractional-bit settings, lookup-table expansion from 4-bit to 16-bit values, per-element row offsets, and optional rectified linear unit activation. The processor supplies additional formatting, including zero padding, replication, known-matrix generation, seam and stride removal, and transposition. Streaming engines retrieve data in programmable multidimensional address sequences. Control software configures these components and executes instruction sequences for each primitive.

Supported implementations include:
- Batched small matrix multiplication using block-diagonal placement, and large matrix multiplication using 32×32 tiles.
- Pointwise multiplication using diagonal matrices and matrix addition using identity matrices.
- Batched vector-matrix multiplication, vector summation, and affine transformations.
- Two-dimensional convolution using tiled feature maps and filters, with formatting to handle seams, strides, and padding.
- Row and column permutations using permutation matrices.
- Small Fourier transforms using discrete Fourier transform matrices, and larger transforms using column transforms, twiddle-factor multiplication, row transforms, and transposition.
- Discrete transforms, one-dimensional convolution, correlation, matrix assignment, and matrix transposition.

Large one-dimensional filters are decomposed into smaller fragments, balancing accelerator throughput against the number of fragments. The disclosure identifies approximately half the accelerator buffer width as the optimal fragment size. Other examples permit different processor types, host-controlled operation, and smaller or larger MMA buffers.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for managing reduced processing time in low-latency wireless systems using configurable or short transmission time intervals (TTIs). Shorter TTIs reduce latency but also reduce the time available to process downlink data, prepare uplink transmissions, and generate hybrid automatic repeat request (HARQ) feedback. Timing advance, which adjusts uplink transmission timing to account for propagation delays, can further reduce available processing time.

A wireless transmit/receive unit (WTRU) may determine its processing capabilities, report them to an eNodeB, and receive a processing capability configuration. Capabilities may include maximum timing advance, maximum receive-transmit time difference, minimum processing time, supported TTI lengths, maximum transport block sizes, and scheduling or HARQ timelines. Their determination may depend on factors including TTI length, symbol count, transport block size, channel and transmission type, allocated resources, coding, transmission layers, waveform, and numerology.

The WTRU may measure a current processing value and report its proximity or headroom relative to a processing capability when specified conditions occur. It may limit timing advance or receive-transmit time difference according to its capabilities for a particular TTI length.

For an uplink grant, the WTRU may determine available processing time between the end of downlink control information and the start of the scheduled uplink transmission. It may transmit when that time meets a capability-based threshold and refrain from transmitting when it does not. HARQ acknowledgment transmission may similarly depend on sufficient processing time after downlink reception.

Responses to processing-limit violations may include capping processing values, suspending or dropping uplink transmissions, stopping time-alignment timers, flushing HARQ buffers, or reporting an error or insufficient headroom. Prioritizing transmission types, channels, or TTIs and dropping lower-priority transmissions may help avoid violations.

The passage also describes supporting wireless-device and network architectures, including LTE, NR, and WLAN examples; scheduling and feedback timing relationships; timing-advance commands and groups; and time-alignment timer operation. The methods may be performed by various wireless communication devices, and described functions may be implemented through emulation devices for testing.

Gunmen attacked U.N. facilities in Timbuktu and Douentza, Mali, on Monday, killing nine people and injuring eight. U.N. troops killed six assailants in Timbuktu; two attackers died in Douentza. Mission chief Mahamat Saleh Annadif called the incidents terrorist attacks. U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres condemned the violence, warning that targeting peacekeepers may constitute war crimes. The U.N. is investigating whether the attacks were connected.

The Treasury Department recommended rolling back Obama-era financial regulations, including Dodd-Frank’s requirement that companies disclose CEO-to-worker pay gaps. Its report, the second of four ordered by President Trump, proposes easing initial public offerings, allowing companies to gauge investor interest privately before filing, and raising the annual crowdfunding limit from $1 million to $5 million. It also urges regulators to simplify and harmonize derivatives rules.

The administration and business groups argue these changes would encourage economic growth. Critics warn that deregulation could weaken safeguards established after the financial crisis and expose taxpayers to future bailouts. Most recommendations could be implemented by regulators, although some require congressional action. Broader Republican efforts to repeal financial regulations have stalled in the Senate.

Arizona ammunition dealer Douglas Haig was charged with manufacturing armor-piercing bullets without a license after unfired rounds bearing his fingerprints were found in Las Vegas gunman Stephen Paddock’s hotel room. Court records did not say whether the ammunition was used in the Oct. 1 attack that killed 58 people. Haig said he sold Paddock 720 rounds of tracer ammunition and noticed nothing suspicious. His identity was inadvertently disclosed in court documents. Haig reported receiving death threats and unwanted media attention and said he had closed his ammunition business.

The National Institute of Standards and Technology revised its password guidelines to recommend long, simple, memorable passwords rather than special characters, mixed capitalization or regular changes. NIST adviser Paul Grassi says longer passwords are harder to break, while traditional requirements frustrate users without substantially improving security. Password managers remain useful but are not necessary, he says.

The NVIDIA A100 Tensor Core GPU, based on the Ampere GA100 architecture, targets AI training and inference, high-performance computing, and data analytics. It builds on the V100 with increased computing throughput, expanded memory and cache capacity, faster interconnects, and GPU partitioning.

Key features include:
- **Third-generation Tensor Cores:** Support TF32, BF16, FP16, IEEE-compliant FP64, and integer formats. Fine-grained structured sparsity can double Tensor Core throughput. TF32 operations process FP32 input/output data at 10 times the rate of V100 FP32 FMA operations, or 20 times with sparsity.
- **Memory:** Includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/sec bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per streaming multiprocessor. Cache residency controls and compute data compression improve memory utilization.
- **Multi-Instance GPU:** Partitions one A100 into as many as seven isolated GPU instances, with separately assigned compute and memory resources to support predictable performance and multi-tenant workloads.
- **Connectivity:** Third-generation NVLink provides 600 GB/sec total bandwidth, twice V100’s bandwidth. PCIe Gen 4 doubles x16 bandwidth compared with PCIe 3.0/3.1. NVSwitch, Mellanox interconnects, and Magnum IO support larger multi-GPU systems.
- **Programming and reliability:** CUDA 11 supports asynchronous memory copies, hardware-accelerated barriers, and task graph acceleration. Enhanced error detection, isolation, and containment aim to improve GPU availability.

GA100 is manufactured using TSMC’s 7 nm process and contains 54.2 billion transistors on an 826 mm² die. A100 supports both shared operation for smaller workloads and interconnected deployment for large-scale computing.

Evaluating AI on unforeseen tasks requires addressing data contamination, static benchmarks, and complex internal mechanisms. Proposed benchmarks should dynamically generate samples, vary task difficulty, and analyze individual capabilities rather than only overall scores. Evaluation should also consider cultural differences, ethnic values, and human-defined safety principles. The DyVal framework dynamically generates evaluation samples at varying complexity levels using directed acyclic graphs, enabling diverse tasks with computable ground truth.

Raja Jackson, 25, son of retired MMA fighter Quinton “Rampage” Jackson, will face felony and misdemeanor battery charges over an August assault at a Los Angeles wrestling event. Jackson slammed wrestler Stuart Smith, known as Syko Stu, to the ground and continued striking him after he appeared unconscious. Smith reported jaw injuries, a serious head injury, a cut lip and lost teeth. Jackson was arrested in September, and his father publicly condemned his actions. The felony charge carries up to four years in state prison; prosecutors are also expected to seek a sentencing enhancement that could increase his prison time.
Stack routines are native assembly macros for establishing or destroying stacks in stackless mode. The host must define the execution environment, include the source, and call the routines.

The passage examines the promise and statistical limitations of using large language models (LLMs) as synthetic agents in social science. Although LLMs can reproduce survey patterns and experimental findings, their outputs reflect learned language patterns rather than samples from a defined human population or calibrated Bayesian posterior distributions.

Research reviewed identifies several risks: predictions can depend on the order of generated observations, drift through self-conditioning, exhibit artificially low variance, and fail systematically across demographic groups or unfamiliar contexts. Fine-tuning can improve task-specific performance without ensuring statistical coherence or generalizable understanding. Success at reproducing familiar main effects does not necessarily extend to interactions, identity-sensitive interventions, or novel scenarios.

The passage recommends treating synthetic agents as domain-specific predictors under explicit conditioning, rather than universal models of human behavior. Researchers should:
- Validate responses against human data and report subgroup accuracy, calibration, and variability.
- Account for mismatch between synthetic and human distributions and limit effective simulation sizes to avoid falsely precise inference.
- Use synthetic data to augment, rather than replace, human measurements.
- Anchor agents in individual-level or task-specific data while recognizing limits to generalization.
- Avoid recycling synthetic outputs into subsequent prompts, test order sensitivity, and standardize decoding settings.
- Stress-test unfamiliar tasks and alternative prompt formulations, disclose failures, and publish reproducible pipeline details.

The conclusion supports carefully validated, specialized applications of LLM agents for prediction, research design, and exploring otherwise difficult scenarios, while cautioning against interpreting predictive mimicry as coherent probabilistic inference about people.

The study assessed early childhood education at 71 Anganwadi centers across 25 villages in Nuh Block, Mewat, Haryana. Researchers collected quantitative and qualitative data through observations, checklists, and worker interviews during August–September 2021.

Findings identified substantial infrastructure, sanitation, resource, and educator-training deficiencies:
- Only 23 centers had safe buildings, and 14 had leveled floors.
- Three centers each had functional toilets, clean drinking water, and safe, clean kitchens.
- No center provided mats, desks, or chairs for children, and learning materials were scarce.
- No center maintained a preschool education timetable.
- Thirty-six of 71 workers had education below the required tenth-grade qualification.
- Workers lacked knowledge of developmental domains and curriculum content; 63% relied on repetition and memorization, while 37% used activity-based teaching.
- Training was infrequent, and parental involvement was limited.

The study connects these findings with broader challenges in rural preschool education, including socioeconomic disadvantage, language and cultural barriers, and weak monitoring. It discusses the National Education Policy 2020’s emphasis on holistic, play-based learning, qualified educators, community participation, and evaluation.

Recommendations include increased investment, standardized infrastructure requirements, adequate learning resources, stronger worker training, parental awareness, and effective monitoring. The authors advocate coordinated implementation by state governments, communities, parents, NGOs, and corporate social responsibility initiatives to improve preschool quality and equity.

Gary Ackerman’s final WPTF newsletter of 2000 reviews California’s electricity crisis, regulatory developments, and industry communications. He advocates clearer public messaging focused on consumers’ electricity bills, emphasizing new generation, greater choice of energy providers, and a provider of last resort.

Key developments include:
- Senator Steve Peace criticized wholesale electricity prices and FERC’s oversight. Ackerman argues that Kaiser Aluminum’s decision to suspend production and resell electricity illustrates demand response.
- Southern California Edison CEO John Bryson called for re-regulating California’s electricity system, restoring utilities’ responsibility for securing sufficient power and charging cost-based rates. Ackerman opposes this approach and highlights utilities’ financial leverage.
- Frozen retail rates, high wholesale costs, and delayed payments created credit problems that discouraged Pacific Northwest suppliers from selling into California.
- The CPUC reopened PG&E’s and Edison’s rate-stabilization applications after previously suspending them.
- Energy Secretary Bill Richardson ordered out-of-state generators and marketers to supply California upon demand and directed BPA and WAPA to maximize deliveries. Ackerman raises concerns about payment terms, future Northwest supplies, and potential salmon impacts.
- WPTF supported the Power Exchange’s emergency request to replace the ISO’s $250/MWh hard cap on adjustment bids, arguing that differing caps diverted transactions from forward markets into real-time trading. The ISO opposed the request.

Correspondents supported stronger consumer-focused public relations. The newsletter announces WPTF’s February 8–9 meeting in Scottsdale and concludes with election-themed humor, a personal account of a conversation with Ackerman’s son, and holiday wishes.

Orthopaedic surgeon Dr Sushrut Babhulkar and Maharashtra Animal and Fisheries Science University veterinarians plan to fit Sahebrao, an eight-year-old tiger at Nagpur’s Gorewada Rescue Centre, with a prosthetic limb. His paw was amputated after a poacher’s trap injured him in 2012. Babhulkar plans to obtain the limb from Germany’s AO Foundation. The passage describes hydrogen peroxide as a household disinfectant with cleaning, whitening and personal-care uses. The AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update documents hardware defects, their effects, and workarounds.

- PIT issues include incorrect counter-latch/read-back sequencing and immediate loading of new mode 3 counts. Software should complete latch commands before read-back and avoid relying on the affected behavior.
- The GLIU debug port hangs the system and should not be used. Other GLIU debug detection and error-reporting features fail without operational impact.
- PIC defects can generate duplicate interrupts with automatic end-of-interrupt enabled. Automatic clock gating can also prevent recognition of subsequent interrupts, potentially hanging the system.
- Legacy DMA priorities do not always rotate correctly, although transfers complete. UART accesses during block or demand DMA are discarded or return all ones; software should wait for completion or use single-byte transfer mode.
- Thermal alarms enter Faulted Standby, but the PMC cannot independently detect alarm clearance while in standby.
- Sleep Clock must be enabled in the PMC when associated sleep options are used; it can instead be disabled at the GPIO.
- PCI I/O addresses at or above 10000h can hang the system and should not be generated. Such LBAR settings should also be avoided.
- USB requires external over-voltage protection.
- ATA and audio PRD prefetching can create hazards when software changes descriptors during active transfers. Workarounds restrict descriptor-update timing.
- UDMA writes can suffer CRC errors following host-terminated reads. The specified workaround enables UDMA I/O blocking to prevent host terminations.
- ATAC SSMI generation during DMA does not block IDE I/O as intended, but the passage states this has no operational impact.

Additional listed issues affect ACPI, PMC registers, PCI timing, USB clock gating, LPC transfers, wake events, GPIO, and standby behavior.

Toll sought to reopen probate proceedings and prevent foreclosure on his home after discovering that Casey and Mrs. McKenzie had replaced an unrecorded deed, concealing the McKenzie children’s half-interest in the property. Mrs. McKenzie had then sold the property to Toll as sole owner.

After Toll learned of the defect, Casey and Mrs. McKenzie agreed to perfect his title through court proceedings without expense to him. Probate and guardianship proceedings followed, but Toll challenged their validity and compliance with the agreement.

The court held that, although the agreement’s literal terms had not been followed, its purpose had been fulfilled. The probate court ultimately received all material facts and approved the transaction. The probate sale was valid, and the transaction, when completed as directed, would provide Toll merchantable title to the McKenzie interests. The court characterized the original deception as constructive fraud because there was no intent to injure the children.

Nevertheless, Casey could not obtain foreclosure relief without fulfilling his corrective obligations. Both judgments were affirmed with modifications allocating costs and requiring Toll to pay the outstanding debt, with six percent interest, less Casey’s contractual obligations, followed by release of the trust deed. On rehearing, the foreclosure case was remanded to implement the judgment, permitting a necessary extension of up to thirty days; rehearing was otherwise denied.

Micro E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures (MNQ) provide exposure to the Nasdaq 100 Index, comprising the largest 100 non-financial companies listed on Nasdaq. They are one-tenth the size of E-mini Nasdaq 100 futures and trade electronically on CME Globex.

Each contract is valued at $2 times the index level. The minimum outright price movement is 0.25 index points, worth $0.50 per contract. Contracts expire quarterly in March, June, September, and December, with cash settlement based on the index’s special opening quotes. Trading ends at 9:30 am ET on the third Friday of the contract month.

Globex trading runs from Sunday evening through Friday afternoon, with a daily maintenance break. Traders need a funded futures brokerage account. Unlike futures, related CFDs have no fixed expiration dates.

Trading strategies may combine technical indicators, fundamental analysis, risk management, and position sizing. The passage describes a proprietary strategy backtested on the longer-established Mini contract using daily, continuous, back-adjusted data, without stops or other risk-management parameters.

Prices are influenced by major component stocks, macroeconomic reports, interest-rate policies, economic conditions, and sociopolitical events. Leverage magnifies losses. The passage reports a historical high of 16,676.50 in November 2021 and a low of 6,628.75 in March 2020.

Former Trump aide Sebastian Gorka endorsed John McCann in New Jersey’s 5th district Republican congressional primary, citing his support for Trump’s agenda. McCann faces former Bogota mayor Steve Lonegan, a former Trump critic who now supports him. The winner will challenge Democratic Rep. Josh Gottheimer in November.

The 6-quart Instant Pot Ultra is on sale for the first time, priced at $120 instead of $150 at Amazon and Sur La Table. Its new “Ultra” setting allows users to control temperature, pressure and cooking time, alongside nine preset options. Unlike DUO models, it provides additional cooking-status information and features a quick-release button. Prices may change.
