The passage describes a high-voltage nanosecond pulsed electric field (nsPEF) generator with feedback control for electrotherapy, including tumor treatment. It reports that nsPEF treatments can induce apoptosis in tumor cells and may stimulate immune responses against similar tumor cells elsewhere in the body.

The system includes a controller, adjustable power supply, pulse generator, treatment electrodes, user interface, and sensors. Users specify characteristics such as pulse amplitude, duration, frequency, quantity, and maximum tissue temperature. Feedback from the generator, electrodes, or sensors enables the controller to adjust power supply and pulse-generation signals so measured characteristics approach desired values. Control methods may include proportional-integral-derivative control, lookup tables, or fixed-step adjustments.

The pulse generator uses a hybrid Marx-generator architecture with series-connected semiconductor switch stacks, including MOSFETs. This arrangement permits charging voltages above individual switch ratings while using relatively few generator stages. Parallel generator circuits increase current capability, while series-connected outputs increase voltage. Pulse duration is controlled by opening and closing the switches. Transformer-coupled drivers provide electrical isolation; lossy transformer cores dissipate residual magnetic flux, and transformer saturation limits excessively long output pulses. Optional snubber circuits and overcurrent protection protect switching components.

Treatment electrodes include needle and two-pole suction designs, with other configurations described for internal access through endoscopes or laparoscopes. Sensors and analog-to-digital converters can measure voltage, current, temperature, and other treatment characteristics. These measurements may also support calculations of tissue impedance, delivered energy, and average power.

The disclosed operating methods repeatedly generate pulses, measure their characteristics or effects, compare results with programmed targets, and modify subsequent operation. Feedback can regulate amplitude and pulse width, verify capacitor charging voltage before pulse generation, and reduce delivered power when temperature, energy, or average-power thresholds are exceeded or approached. Power reduction may involve decreasing pulse width, frequency, or voltage. Tissue temperature may be measured directly or calculated using delivered energy and thermal characteristics.

Scientists documented the first modern case of “river piracy” at Canada’s Kaskawulsh glacier, attributing it to global warming. River gauge data suggest most meltwater abruptly shifted from the Slims River to the Alsek River around May 26 last year after a canyon formed at the glacier’s end. The Slims became shallow and still, while the Alsek grew deeper and faster. Researchers estimated only a one-in-200 chance that the glacier retreat and river diversion occurred naturally without human-caused warming. Outside scientists praised the study as significant.

Average overnight returns were 0.04% for the S&P 500 and approximately 0.03% for gold. Gold miners also showed an overnight bias, contrasting with negative intraday returns. However, these broad patterns alone are insufficient to overcome trading costs; specific strategies are needed.

An overnight strategy published in 2014 remained profitable over seven years of out-of-sample results, including gains exceeding 6% in 2020. A portfolio combining three strategies holding positions for 24 hours recorded 950 trades with an average gain of 0.33%, which the passage describes as sufficient to cover slippage and commissions.

The passage provides hardware guidance, development resources, revision details, and packaging information for TI MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 microcontrollers.

- **Hardware connections:** TI recommends 10µF and 0.1µF low-ESR ceramic capacitors near the supply pins. NRST must be pulled up to VDD; a 47kΩ pullup resistor and 10nF pulldown capacitor are recommended. SYSOSC frequency correction requires an external 100kΩ resistor with 0.1% tolerance and a temperature coefficient of 25ppm/°C or better. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47µF capacitor and must not connect to other circuits. The 5V-tolerant open-drain pins require pullup resistors for high outputs and tolerate applied voltage without VDD.
- **Device status:** “X” identifies experimental devices intended for internal evaluation, while “MSP” identifies fully qualified production devices. TI recommends using only qualified devices in production.
- **Development and support:** Resources include development boards, software libraries, cloud tools, TI Resource Explorer, SysConfig, MSP Academy, GUI Composer, Code Composer Studio, IAR and Keil toolchains, TI Arm-Clang, and GNU Arm tools. Documentation updates are available by subscription, and TI E2E forums provide design support. Appropriate ESD precautions are recommended.
- **April 2025 revisions:** Changes cover peripheral counts, preview package variants, electrical and thermal specifications, supply currents, timing, memory, security, and operating-mode descriptions. Any 32kB flash sectors may be selected for high-endurance operation, and the keystore supports up to four keys.
- **Packaging and terms:** Mechanical and ordering information is subject to change. Applicable package thermal pads must be soldered to the board. Automotive-qualified MSPM0G3518-Q1 and MSPM0G3519-Q1 versions are listed. TI provides technical resources “as is”; developers remain responsible for product selection, application validation, testing, and compliance.

Two clinical trials found that daily oral GLP-1 drugs helped people with obesity lose weight. Participants taking 25 milligrams of oral semaglutide lost nearly 14 percent of their body weight on average over a trial lasting up to 64 weeks. Those taking the highest dose of orforglipron lost about 11 percent over up to 72 weeks.

Pills could simplify manufacturing, distribution and administration compared with injections, potentially improving access and reducing costs. Pricing and insurance coverage remain uncertain.

Both drugs caused gastrointestinal side effects similar to other GLP-1 medications, generally fading over time. Researchers observed no liver toxicity, but longer-term studies in larger populations are needed. Researcher Sean Wharton hopes both pills will reach consumers by 2026, depending on FDA approval.

Tesla, Inc.’s January 29, 2020 Form 8-K reported that the company released financial results for the quarter and year ended December 31, 2019, by posting its Fourth Quarter and Full Year 2019 Update on its website. The update was attached as Exhibit 99.1 and incorporated by reference. Chief Financial Officer Zachary J. Kirkhorn signed the report.

Construction of Los Angeles’ Metro Purple Line extension has uncovered Ice Age fossils since 2014, including remains of rabbits, mastodons, camels, bison and horses. Paleontologist Ashley Leger’s team made a particularly rare discovery: an intact juvenile mammoth skull with both tusks attached, excavated over 15 hours.

The skull was taken to the La Brea Tar Pits and Museum, where it is being studied and can be viewed by the public. Assistant curator Emily Lindsey noted that only about 30 mammoths have been uncovered in Los Angeles.

California environmental laws require scientists at certain construction sites, and paleontologists have staffed Los Angeles subway excavations since the 1990s. Their costs are included in project budgets, and construction shifts elsewhere while fossils are recovered. Similar construction projects in other cities have uncovered fossils and historical artifacts.

Dengue affects an estimated 100–400 million people annually, and no direct-acting antiviral treatment is available. AT-752 is an oral guanosine nucleotide prodrug whose active metabolite, AT-9010, inhibits dengue virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase across all four serotypes.

A first-in-human, randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled Phase 1 study evaluated AT-752’s safety, tolerability, and pharmacokinetics in 65 healthy participants. Single doses ranged from 250 to 1500 mg; repeated regimens included 1000 mg once daily and 750 mg twice or three times daily. The study also assessed food effects and pharmacokinetic differences in Asian participants.

AT-752 was well tolerated, with no serious adverse events or adverse-event-related discontinuations. Treatment-emergent adverse events were mild or moderate and resolved by study completion. Gastrointestinal events occurred mainly at higher doses. No treatment- or dose-related trends appeared in laboratory values, vital signs, or electrocardiograms.

The parent prodrug was rapidly eliminated, while AT-273, a circulating surrogate for intracellular AT-9010, had a substantially longer half-life. With repeated dosing, AT-273 reached approximately steady-state concentrations by Day 3. Only the 750 mg three-times-daily regimen maintained mean trough concentrations above the target corresponding to 90% inhibition of dengue replication in vitro, beginning within the first day.

Comparable pharmacokinetic profiles across ethnic cohorts suggested no need for dose adjustment in Asian participants. Food altered peak concentrations but had limited effects on overall exposure, supporting administration with or without food. These safety and pharmacokinetic findings support dose selection for future clinical studies. The study was funded by Atea Pharmaceuticals and reported in a preprint not certified by peer review.

Japan’s March 2011 earthquake, tsunami and nuclear emergency severely disrupted automotive production and global supply chains. Approximately 80% of Japanese automotive plants suspended production, and industry output fell nearly 60% in March and April compared with 2010. Nissan sustained damage to six production facilities, while about 50 critical suppliers were impaired.

Nissan’s preparedness reflected its emphasis on flexibility, clear responsibility and rapid response. It combined decentralized regional supply chains with strong central coordination during crises. Its simplified product range used build-to-stock production for a few variants and build-to-order production for others. Following its 1999 financial crisis and alliance with Renault, Nissan established formal risk-management responsibilities, business continuity planning, seismic reinforcement and disaster simulations.

Nissan activated its Global Disaster Control Headquarters within 15 minutes of the earthquake and established a Recovery Committee. Its response emphasized:
- **Information sharing:** Regional representatives traveled to Japan to gather information and support coordinated problem-solving.
- **Supply allocation:** Sales, marketing and supply-chain teams prioritized scarce components for higher-margin products and models requiring them.
- **Production management:** Nissan adjusted production around expected bottlenecks, brought forward vacations, sought alternative supplies and used air freight for critical parts.
- **Empowered decisions:** Temporary changes to delegation rules enabled rapid local action, with decisions revised as information improved.

Nissan’s recovery also continued an existing localization strategy intended to reduce currency exposure and costs. In 2012, it announced plans to increase localized production in the Americas from approximately 70% to 90% by 2015 and halve components imported from Japan into North America by the end of fiscal 2013. It also sought stronger continuity planning and better understanding of dependencies beyond first-tier suppliers, acknowledging that supplier recovery and supply-chain rehabilitation remained incomplete.
Wall Street stocks fell Tuesday as banks and healthcare companies declined. Goldman Sachs and Johnson & Johnson missed forecasts, while Cardinal Health issued a weak outlook. Bond prices rose.

Cuba’s provisional government will end after elections and the peaceful inauguration of a new government. The United States seeks Cuban prosperity and independence but warns that fraudulent elections and recurring insurrection could require renewed intervention to protect life and property.

The Third International Conference of American Republics, held in Rio de Janeiro from July 23 to August 29, addressed trade, communication, international barriers, and mutual understanding. Its harmonious discussions produced resolutions and proposed conventions with substantial unanimity, demonstrating improved efficiency over earlier conferences. Brazil’s hospitality was praised.

The Secretary of State attended the conference and visited Brazil, Uruguay, Argentina, Chile, Peru, Panama, and Colombia, conveying peace, friendship, and mutual cooperation. Governments and citizens warmly received his message. Visits to Paraguay, Bolivia, and Ecuador were impracticable because of time and travel constraints.

NTT Docomo installed smartphone wipes in some Tokyo Narita International Airport restrooms until March 15. The wipes promote its wifi service and travel guide app. Cited studies found bacterial contamination on cellphones.

The Supreme Court allowed Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook to remain in office pending January 2026 oral arguments on President Donald Trump’s effort to remove her. It deferred Trump’s request to suspend a lower court injunction blocking her dismissal.

Trump alleges Cook committed mortgage fraud and argues this constitutes legal cause for removal. Cook denies wrongdoing and has not been charged over the mortgage applications. The case could have significant implications for the Fed’s independence from political interference.

The order permits Cook to participate in the Fed’s October and December policy meetings, when officials have indicated further quarter-point interest rate cuts. Cook supported September’s quarter-point reduction and has advocated a cautious approach to easing policy.

California news reports from March 7–8, 2001, describe mounting financial, supply and political problems in the state’s electricity crisis.

- Gov. Gray Davis’s administration reported progress toward rescuing PG&E through a state purchase of its transmission lines, with an offer of at least $7 billion. PG&E and Southern California Edison faced roughly $13 billion in debts after wholesale electricity costs exceeded regulated retail revenues.
- California was spending billions purchasing electricity for the utilities, but repayment remained disputed. Legislative limits and insufficient revenue from existing customer rates threatened plans to issue $10 billion in bonds. State officials maintained that sufficient revenue could be secured.
- Davis announced approximately $40 billion in long-term electricity contracts and tentative agreements, averaging $69 per megawatt-hour. Critics questioned contract secrecy and the risk of paying above-market prices later; supporters defended confidentiality and the negotiated terms.
- Long-term contracts would not eliminate summer shortages or dependence on expensive spot-market purchases. Officials pursued conservation, additional contracts and accelerated power-plant construction, while forecasts warned of rolling blackouts.
- El Paso Energy closed six cogeneration plants producing about 175 megawatts because PG&E had not paid for deliveries. Legislation intended to reduce payments to alternative generators stalled over unequal payment provisions.
- Municipal utilities, including Sacramento’s SMUD, sought relief from obligations to impose blackouts at PG&E’s direction. Regulators also considered whether utility layoffs and relaxed service standards should be permitted.
- Proposals for wholesale price caps, retail-rate changes and expanded generation remained contested. New plants and transmission projects encountered local environmental and land-use objections, although officials approved a temporary 51-megawatt plant at San Francisco International Airport.
- A separate commentary argued that California’s estimated $90 billion infrastructure gap required demand management and coordinated regional planning alongside construction.

Thermoelectric performance requires high electrical power factors and low thermal conductivity, but coupled carrier and phonon transport complicates optimization. Near room temperature, n-type Bi₂Te₃-based materials lag behind their p-type counterparts because of stronger crystallographic anisotropy and intrinsic defects.

This study improved Se-alloyed n-type Bi₂Te₃ polycrystals using melting–hot pressing followed by annealing. Bi₂Te₂.₆Se₀.₄ was identified as the optimal composition, and annealing at 723 K for 100 hours effectively decoupled carrier and phonon transport. Te(Se) volatilization promoted cation vacancies and other atomic defects, reducing carrier density while increasing mobility and the Seebeck coefficient. These changes improved the power factor, while enhanced phonon scattering reduced lattice thermal conductivity.

After annealing, room-temperature carrier density reached 2.43 × 10¹⁹ cm⁻³, carrier mobility reached 295.97 cm² V⁻¹ s⁻¹, and lattice thermal conductivity fell to 0.48 W m⁻¹ K⁻¹. The optimized sample achieved a room-temperature ZT of 0.78, a peak ZT of 1.06 at 373 K, and an average ZT of 0.99 over 300–423 K. Microscopy and elemental analysis showed increased porosity and Te(Se) depletion after annealing.

The findings present annealing as a practical post-synthesis approach for improving n-type thermoelectric materials, with potential applications in cooling and chip-level thermal management.

Schaeffler’s electric Audi RS3, dubbed 4ePerformance, uses four Formula E motors producing 1,180 horsepower. According to Schaeffler, it reaches 124 mph in seven seconds. It features all-wheel drive, torque vectoring and two battery packs totaling 64 kilowatt-hours. Audi is focusing on its upcoming e-tron SUV, while Formula E is attracting additional manufacturers.

The study develops a classification, mathematical model, and methods for evaluating software accessibility, focusing on users with visual impairments. It addresses limitations in ISO 25023, which provides accessibility formulas but lacks methods for determining certain parameters and assigning metric weights.

The proposed framework evaluates four subproperties:
- **Perceptiveness:** alternative text, color contrast, subtitles, and audio descriptions.
- **Operability:** keyboard access and structured navigation.
- **Understandability:** clear instructions, input assistance, and error messages.
- **Localization:** availability of language versions, weighted according to the target audience.

Individual metrics are combined using weighting coefficients to calculate an overall accessibility score. Expert evaluation determines the importance of the indicators.

The methodology was applied to key pages of the Vasyl Stefanyk Precarpathian National University website, using automated tools to assess image alternatives and color contrast. Its overall score was 0.67916, classified as “excellent” on the study’s Fibonacci-based evaluation scale. Keyboard navigation and clear instructions scored 1, while color contrast scored 0.99. However, subtitles and audio descriptions and input assistance scored zero; alternative text scored 0.15, and structured navigation scored 0.47.

Recommended improvements include adding accessible multimedia alternatives, improving image descriptions, implementing input assistance, and strengthening page hierarchy and breadcrumb navigation. The framework supports accessibility assessment while identifying specific areas for improvement.

The Supreme Court agreed to hear five new cases during its 2025–26 term, including a challenge to Hawaii’s prohibition on carrying handguns on private property open to the public without the owner’s permission.

Two cases concern lawsuits under a 1996 law addressing property confiscated by Cuba. Exxon Mobil seeks to sue three state-owned companies, raising questions about foreign sovereign immunity. Havana Docks seeks compensation from cruise lines that used docks after its confiscated concession would have expired.

Another case concerns whether a Michigan estate should receive compensation based on a foreclosed home’s fair market value rather than its auction price, invoking constitutional protections against uncompensated takings and excessive fines.

The fifth case asks whether federal law bars state-law negligence claims against brokers for selecting motor carriers or drivers.

The passage advocates reserving agricultural public lands for resident settlers, reforming laws exploited for large land acquisitions, recognizing grazing settlers’ greater land needs, and ending unlawful fencing of public lands. It recommends congressional investigation or an expert commission to address these issues. For Alaska, it urges laws encouraging permanent settlement, protection of forests, game, and salmon fisheries, regulated timber use by settlers, congressional representation, and an investigative visit. It proposes gradual assimilation of Indigenous peoples, with land allotment and settlement policies adapted to differing tribal conditions, including pastoral village life where appropriate.

HIV disproportionately affects minoritized populations, with social and structural determinants—including racism, stigma, housing instability, transportation barriers, and healthcare access—contributing to disparities in prevention and treatment. Although pre-exposure prophylaxis and antiretroviral therapy are effective, inequities limit their uptake and adherence. Structural interventions address these external conditions, but their implementation in the United States remains understudied.

This systematic review protocol aims to identify barriers and facilitators, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions relevant to structural interventions supporting HIV evidence-based interventions. It will also identify literature gaps and examine distinctions between structural interventions, implementation strategies, and adjunctive interventions.

Searches conducted from May through July 2024 identified 8,098 articles before duplicate removal. Eligible studies must focus on HIV/AIDS, include samples based at least 50% in the United States, present original behavioral or social science research, assess implementation outcomes, and examine interventions targeting external conditions or social determinants of health. Natural language processing screened 8,092 titles and abstracts, identifying 405 articles for inclusion across all classifiers and 4,285 requiring further inspection without exclusion labels. Manual title, abstract, and full-text screening will involve two reviewers per article, with disagreements resolved by senior investigators.

Data extraction will cover populations, settings, study designs, interventions, and implementation outcomes. Barriers and facilitators will be coded using the Consolidated Framework for Implementation Research; implementation strategies using Expert Recommendations for Implementing Change; and adjunctive interventions using the Theoretical Domains Framework and COM-B. Analyses will examine effectiveness, reporting detail, equity considerations, and differences across populations, settings, and intervention types.

At the time of reporting, searches and automated screening were complete, and manual title and abstract review was underway. Full-text review and extraction were scheduled to begin in January 2025, with analyses from June 2025 through June 2026. Dissemination is planned through publications, conferences, and an interactive literature dashboard. The review aims to inform research, policy, and practice supporting equitable implementation of HIV structural interventions.

The Missouri Supreme Court will consider two cases addressing whether the Missouri Human Rights Act prohibits discrimination based on sexual orientation and gender identity, despite not explicitly naming either.

One case concerns a transgender teenager denied access to boys’ restrooms and locker rooms. Lower courts dismissed his sex-discrimination lawsuit against the school district.

The second involves a gay state employee alleging discrimination for not conforming to male stereotypes and a colleague alleging discrimination and retaliation over their friendship. The Human Rights Commission rejected their complaints, but an appeals court disagreed.

The ACLU supports interpreting the act to cover sexual orientation and gender identity. Opponents argue courts cannot add protections not explicitly stated in the law.

Mod-Cam, the first-light and commissioning receiver for the Fred Young Submillimeter Telescope, serves as a testbed for Prime-Cam instrument modules. This study characterizes the thermal stability of its 280 GHz module and the thermal responsivity of aluminum (Al) and titanium-nitride (TiN) kinetic inductance detectors.

Cryogenic upgrades reduced temperature drift at the 40 K stage from 0.2 K/day to below 0.1 K/day. A dilution refrigerator and PID-controlled heater maintained the detector stage near 100 mK. Detector measurements used a cold-load configuration to minimize external radiative loading, while overall cryogenic performance was also assessed in an optically open configuration.

An eight-hour measurement at 100 mK yielded an RMS temperature fluctuation of 3.2 × 10⁻⁵ K. Measurements of 2,409 Al and 1,886 TiN detectors produced median thermal responsivities of 1.995 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹ and −6.081 × 10⁻⁴ K⁻¹, respectively.

Combining these measurements with optical responsivities from prior work gave thermally induced equivalent power fluctuations of 0.20–0.27 fW for Al and 0.11–0.13 fW for TiN under 5–9 pW optical loads. At 5 pW, these correspond to 0.0040% and 0.0023% of the background signal. The study concludes that thermal fluctuations should negligibly affect instrument sensitivity. Future work will directly measure optical responsivity using a cryogenic blackbody source.

Finder.com’s annual America’s Biggest Money Mistakes survey found that 78.3% of respondents reported making a financial mistake. Overspending on shopping, vacations, dining out and other leisure activities was the most common regret, cited by almost 64%.

Women more frequently regretted overspending and letting partners control family finances, while men more often regretted bad investments and excessive gambling. About 20% of both men and women regretted dropping out of college. Bureau of Labor Statistics data showed college dropouts had lower median earnings and higher unemployment than bachelor’s degree holders.

Millennials were more likely to regret leisure overspending, while baby boomers more often regretted bad investments. Other regrets included wedding expenses, online scams and having children. Consumer advocate Jennifer McDermott recommended identifying spending triggers, considering financial consequences and researching career pathways before committing to college studies.

An experiment found that 6-year-olds worked harder and stayed more focused on repetitive tasks when pretending to be Batman or Dora the Explorer. Children who focused on themselves took frequent breaks.

This study examined relationships between mentalization, attachment insecurity, and personality pathology within the DSM-5 Alternative Model for Personality Disorders (AMPD). It distinguished self-mentalizing—understanding one’s own mental states—from other-mentalizing—understanding others’ mental states—and assessed their associations with personality functioning (Criterion A) and maladaptive personality traits (Criterion B).

The sample included 109 adults aged 18–47: 60 psychiatric inpatients and 49 community participants. Overall, 54% met criteria for a personality disorder. Researchers assessed self-mentalizing through a self-report questionnaire and other-mentalizing through a film-based social cognition task, alongside measures of attachment, personality functioning, and maladaptive traits.

Self-mentalizing deficits were associated with impairments in both self- and interpersonal functioning and all five maladaptive trait domains: Negative Affectivity, Detachment, Antagonism, Disinhibition, and Psychoticism. In regression analyses, self-mentalizing deficits were the strongest predictor across outcomes. Correct other-mentalizing independently predicted fewer interpersonal functioning difficulties but did not significantly predict maladaptive traits. Models explained 18%–55% of outcome variance, with the greatest explanatory power for self-functioning difficulties and Negative Affectivity.

Mentalizing also moderated some relationships between insecure attachment and personality pathology:
- Better other-mentalizing weakened the association between attachment anxiety and interpersonal impairment, while greater hypermentalizing strengthened it.
- Self-mentalizing moderated associations between attachment anxiety and both Negative Affectivity and Detachment. Among participants with low attachment anxiety, greater self-mentalizing deficits were associated with higher levels of these traits.
- Better other-mentalizing weakened the association between attachment avoidance and Detachment, whereas undermentalizing and nonmentalizing strengthened it.
- No mentalizing moderation effects were observed for self-functioning impairments.

The authors suggest that self-mentalizing may have broad relevance to personality-disorder treatment, while other-mentalizing may be particularly relevant to interpersonal difficulties and withdrawal. They propose tailoring therapeutic priorities to patients’ attachment patterns and mentalizing difficulties.

The findings require caution. The cross-sectional design cannot establish causality or changes over time. Other limitations include the small, heterogeneous sample, unassessed comorbid symptomatic disorders, and possible effects of using different assessment methods for self- and other-mentalizing. Larger, longitudinal studies and more comparable measurement approaches are needed. The passage is from a preprint that had not undergone peer review.

Denmark’s Systemic Risk Council recommended restricting interest-only and variable-interest mortgages for most Copenhagen and Aarhus borrowers whose debts exceed 400 percent of pretax income. The government has three months to adopt the recommendation or publicly explain its refusal.

Erik Demaine introduces MIT’s Advanced Data Structures course and its first topic, temporal data structures. The course also covers geometry, dynamic optimality, memory hierarchies, hashing, integer data structures, dynamic graphs, strings, and succinct representations.

The lecture uses the pointer-machine model, where constant-sized nodes contain data and pointers. It distinguishes persistence, which preserves old versions when updates create new ones, from retroactivity, which changes past operations and their subsequent effects.

Four forms of persistence are discussed:
- **Partial persistence:** All versions can be queried, but only the latest can be updated.
- **Full persistence:** Any version can be updated, creating a tree of versions.
- **Confluent persistence:** Versions can be combined, producing a directed acyclic graph.
- **Functional data structures:** Existing nodes cannot be modified; changes require new nodes.

Pointer-machine structures with bounded incoming and outgoing pointers can be made partially or fully persistent with constant amortized overhead and constant additional space per elementary change. Partial persistence uses back pointers, bounded modification records, and node copying when records fill. Full persistence additionally requires version-ancestry tests, maintained through a traversal ordering, and splitting full nodes rather than merely copying them. Potential-function arguments establish the amortized bounds.

Partial persistence also admits constant worst-case slowdown; obtaining this for full persistence is presented as an open problem.

Confluent persistence is harder because repeated combinations can make the represented structure grow exponentially. A general transformation has overhead depending on version-path counts and the number of updates. A more restricted transformation achieves logarithmic overhead when combined versions share no nodes. Whether constant overhead is possible when both queries and updates are charged remains open.

Functional examples include balanced search trees using path copying, link-cut trees, and deques supporting concatenation. Constant-time splitting and concatenation of persistent lists is another open problem.

Jim Cramer reversed his bullish stance on Snap, citing its unpopular redesign and concerns that reduced user engagement could drive advertisers away. Snap shares erased their post-earnings gains amid criticism, but Cramer still considers the stock too expensive and risky. He recommends waiting for evidence of the redesign’s impact, while remaining open to buying at a lower price. Snap reports first-quarter results on May 1.

The study proposes an active learning (AL) queue-prioritization algorithm to improve generative AI workflows for scientific discovery. Generative models can produce infeasible candidates, wasting simulation resources and contributing to model decay during iterative retraining. The algorithm uses a surrogate model and customizable acquisition functions to prioritize promising candidates before expensive simulations.

The approach is demonstrated in a workflow for discovering metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) for carbon capture. A fine-tuned DiffLinker model generates organic linkers for cubic zinc-based MOFs, while molecular dynamics simulations evaluate structural stability through internal strain. An XGBoost surrogate predicts strain and uncertainty, is retrained as simulation results accumulate, and reorders candidate queues. Prioritization can also incorporate estimated synthesizability and similarity to known linkers.

Across 1,000 novel candidates, the workflow identified an average of 604 high-performing candidates with AL, compared with 281 without it. Queue prioritization improved candidate quality across different generator fine-tuning fractions and mitigated model decay associated with retraining on unsuitable structures.

Acquisition functions balancing exploration and exploitation performed better than either extreme in the generative workflow. Weak exploration produced the most stable MOFs and the lowest strain-prediction error, whereas pure exploration prioritized outliers that rarely yielded useful structures or improved predictions. Multi-objective tests showed that prioritizing synthesizability alone reduced stable-MOF discovery, while similarity to known linkers improved stability without guaranteeing experimental viability.

AL prioritization added approximately 0.6% to computational resource use, providing substantial improvements with marginal overhead.

Researchers at the NeuroPiano Institute and Sony Computer Science Laboratories demonstrated that pianists can alter timbre through touch, addressing a century-old question. Using high-precision sensors, they recorded all 88 keys’ movements at 1,000 frames per second while 20 professional pianists performed with different intended timbres.

In listening experiments involving 40 participants, both pianists and people without musical experience consistently recognized the intended timbral differences, even when volume and tempo were controlled. Pianists showed greater sensitivity.

Analysis identified specific movement features associated with timbre, including acceleration during escapement and hand synchronization. Experiments varying individual features established a causal relationship between key movement and perceived timbre.

Published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the findings could support evidence-based music instruction by making previously difficult-to-describe techniques measurable and teachable. They also suggest potential applications in neuroscience, rehabilitation, skill transfer, and human interface design.

Assistant U.S. Attorney Will Rosenzweig of the Southern District of Florida was fired by email while observing Rosh Hashanah after conservatives publicized alleged blog posts criticizing President Trump. Rosenzweig joined the office in September 2020 and handled economic crimes cases. The Miami Herald described his dismissal as part of broader firings of federal prosecutors perceived as opposing Trump or his agenda. Three other prosecutors in the district who previously worked with former special counsel Jack Smith were also fired. Smith recently criticized dismissals of career public servants and politically motivated investigations.

Canadian and U.S. stock indexes fell Friday morning, with the TSX down 81.78 points to 15,694.52. UK bank branch closures are increasing as mobile-only banks grow. A survey of 9,076 Which? members suggested that more than half of under-40s would consider a mobile-only account, with willingness substantially lower among older members. Competitive savings rates may attract customers, but an reported Atom Bank app crash highlighted drawbacks of lacking in-branch service. Major banks closed over 1,000 branches between January 2015 and January 2017. Commenters raised concerns about losing personal service and travelling farther to resolve problems or make deposits, while some were open to alternatives.

Tennessee middle schooler Keaton Jones went viral after his mother recorded him describing bullying at school. Celebrities expressed support, including LeBron James and Mark Ruffalo, who invited Keaton to the premiere of *Infinity War*.

A confidential memorandum proposes preparing United States Peace Conference negotiators with concise expert studies on history, commerce, international law, disarmament, arbitration, and political institutions. Specialists would produce pamphlets and supporting appendices, secretly printed and indexed, under centralized supervision. A separate memorandum raises questions about American involvement in European boundaries and colonial redistribution, criteria for territorial settlements, and conditions for guaranteeing colonial possessions. Colonel E. M. House praises the preparatory memorandum and seeks a discussion with Secretary of State Lansing about organizing the work.

Antonio Vasquez and Hector Perez were convicted of possessing burglar’s tools and acquitted of attempted petit larceny and resisting arrest after testimony that they abandoned an attempt to steal a bicycle using bolt cutters. They moved to set aside the conviction, arguing that the jury should have been instructed that renunciation also applied to possession of burglar’s tools.

The court denied the motion, holding that Penal Law § 40.10 authorized renunciation for only four categories of offenses, excluding possession of burglar’s tools. Although troubled that abandoning the theft offered defendants little benefit, the court concluded that expanding the defense required legislative action.

Professor Noelle Selin discusses mercury pollution and the Minamata Convention, signed in October 2013, examining the relationship between scientific evidence, domestic regulation, international negotiations, and business supply chains.

Mercury travels globally through the atmosphere, making national controls alone insufficient. Once deposited, it can become methylmercury, accumulate in food chains, and cause neurological and cardiovascular harm. Major sources include coal combustion, artisanal and small-scale gold mining, industrial processes, and mercury-containing products. Historical mercury releases also continue circulating through soils, oceans, and the atmosphere, complicating estimates of human contributions.

A 2002 global scientific assessment concluded that international action was needed. The United States initially favored voluntary partnerships, while the European Union supported a binding treaty. A change in US administration and developing domestic mercury regulations helped secure agreement to begin negotiations in 2010. The resulting convention closely matched existing US requirements, allowing US acceptance without Senate ratification.

The convention addresses mercury throughout its life cycle, including emissions, mining, trade, products, industrial processes, and waste. Negotiators chose to list restricted products rather than impose a blanket ban. Restrictions, exemptions, and phaseout dates reflected negotiations among countries with different economic interests and regulatory capacities. Dental amalgam was targeted for phased reduction, while mercury-containing vaccine preservatives received an exemption. Waste provisions draw on the Basel Convention.

Artisanal and small-scale gold mining presents particular challenges because mercury supports miners’ livelihoods and often moves through informal or illegal supply channels. The treaty emphasizes capacity building, formalization, and safer practices rather than eliminating the activity. Equipment that captures mercury during gold processing can reduce releases and allow reuse.

Businesses participated mainly as observers, advocating through governments and providing information about alternatives and technical feasibility. Scientific assessments established the case for action, but detailed treaty provisions largely emerged through political bargaining. Gary Gensler’s lecture examines digital identity, identity management, and potential blockchain applications, emphasizing critical evaluation of benefits and limitations.

Identity is distinguished from identifiers and supporting evidence. Attributes include names, ages, addresses, citizenship, and biometrics; claims assert attributes; credentials document them; and attestations provide third-party verification. Identity and access management involves authentication and authorization. Biometric examples involving identical twins illustrate limitations in some identification methods.

Public-key cryptography and certificate authorities help verify website identities. Blockchain-based public-key infrastructure could offer an alternative by enabling agreement on public keys without relying on the existing certificate-authority model.

Major identity-management problems include identity theft, forged credentials, data breaches, privacy risks, and updating personal information. Adoption costs, commercial incentives, and connections among government identification, taxation, banking, and anti-money-laundering requirements complicate reform.

The lecture discusses two government systems that do not use blockchain: Estonia’s electronic identity system and India’s Aadhaar. Aadhaar combines a 12-digit identifier with fingerprints and iris scans to support inclusion and access to services, but the discussion also highlights breaches, errors, and exclusion concerns.

Self-sovereign identity aims to give individuals and entities greater control over identity attributes, direct access, portability, and interoperability. It does not inherently require blockchain. Commercial demands for personal information may limit its practical implementation.

Blockchain could potentially reduce verification costs and fraud, improve provenance tracking, and support privacy. However, distributing personal information across blockchain nodes creates privacy risks, while immutable records raise questions about deletion rights. Discussed approaches include keeping personal data off-chain, recording hashes, and appending updated information. Lost or stolen private keys remain a significant concern.

The class reviews identity startups, standards initiatives, decentralized public-key infrastructure, and MIT’s blockchain-backed diplomas. Gensler stresses distinguishing useful applications from hype rather than assuming blockchain or associated tokens are necessary solutions.

This non-peer-reviewed methodology preprint describes KaviKrishna’s community-based tuberculosis (TB) care and research programme in rural Northeast India. The programme combines Indigenous Knowledge Systems, participatory action research, telemedicine, and molecular and stem cell research to address limitations of centrally controlled TB programmes, including inadequate community participation, diagnostic difficulties, dormancy, relapse, and multidrug resistance (MDR).

In Assam’s Sualkuchi-Hajo region, the Indigenous Kamarupa Information Network connects local temples, student volunteers, clinicians, researchers, patients, and families. It supports screening, contact tracing, education, nutritional supplementation, and long-term monitoring. The authors report screening 300 pulmonary TB cases among 500 suspected cases since 2010, providing follow-up information for 210 patients, and recruiting another 250 patients across Northeast India to investigate stem cells’ role in MDR evolution. Community involvement is described as helping reduce stigma and sustain participation.

Laboratory methods include sputum culture, drug-susceptibility testing, PCR, stem cell isolation, whole-genome sequencing, and assays assessing bacterial viability, drug tolerance, and viable but non-culturable MTB. PCR and sequencing identified non-tuberculous mycobacteria in some samples initially considered pulmonary TB. Strain profiling identified Beijing, CAS/CAS1-Delhi, and orphan strains.

Previous studies reported dormant MTB within bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells of successfully treated patients. Mouse experiments demonstrated that stem-cell-associated dormant bacteria retained reinfection capacity and that coronavirus-associated stress could trigger reactivation. Preliminary findings of rpoB and rpoC mutations in MTB recovered from stem-cell populations led the authors to propose that the stem cell niche may contribute to MDR evolution; further evaluation is planned.

The programme also developed local laboratory infrastructure, trained more than 50 community students since 2010, and established national and international collaborations. Whole-genome sequencing is being incorporated into surveillance of circulating strains and resistance-associated mutations, with a sample dataset deposited in NCBI.

The authors propose that this integrated, community-specific approach could support improved TB control and precision treatment. Several findings remain preliminary or unpublished, and the approach’s broader potential is presented as a subject for further development.

OSCAR is a one-shot causal discovery framework for high-dimensional, multi-label event sequences. Using two pretrained Transformers to estimate event and label distributions, it applies conditional mutual information tests to identify each label’s Markov Boundary from an individual sequence. Parallelized GPU operations support scalable processing, while causal indicators describe changes in label likelihood after observing events.

The method’s theoretical guarantees depend on temporal precedence, bounded lagged effects, causal sufficiency, and perfect distribution estimation. The authors acknowledge that these strong assumptions are unlikely to hold strictly in practice.

Evaluation used a vehicular dataset containing 29,100 diagnostic event types and 474 vehicle-defect labels. In a 50,000-sample comparison, OSCAR achieved 55.26% precision, 31.37% recall, and 40.02% F1 in 11.7 minutes; five comparison algorithms failed to finish within three days. Evaluation references were expert-defined diagnostic rules, approximately 12% of which were missing. The framework is intended to provide sequence-specific explanations and support diagnostic rule refinement.

The passage describes container and distributed-system design patterns, their applications, and operational trade-offs.

- **Ambassadors** separate application logic from external communication. A service-broker ambassador discovers environment-specific services while the application connects through localhost. Ambassadors can also redirect experimental traffic or duplicate requests to test services without returning experimental responses to users. An nginx example routes 90% of traffic to production and 10% to an experiment, using IP hashing for consistent user experiences.

- **Adapters** translate heterogeneous application interfaces into common conventions for monitoring, logging, and health checks. Examples include a Prometheus exporter for Redis, Fluentd adapters that normalize logs or collect Redis slow queries, and a MySQL adapter that runs diagnostic queries and exposes an HTTP health-check interface. Separate adapter containers support independent updates, resource allocation, reuse, and sharing without modifying third-party application images.

- **Microservices** divide applications into independently managed components communicating through defined APIs. This supports smaller teams, independent releases, and service-specific scaling, but complicates debugging and architecture. Established distributed patterns help organize these systems and reuse design experience.

- **Replicated load-balanced services** use interchangeable servers to provide redundancy and horizontal scalability. Readiness probes distinguish applications that can serve requests from those that are merely running. Session tracking directs a user’s requests to the same replica; application-level tracking is preferred over external IP-based tracking where network address translation interferes. Consistent hashing reduces reassignment when replica counts change.

- **Layered serving architectures** can add caching, rate limiting, and SSL termination. A separate caching tier allows caches and application servers to scale differently. Caches can disrupt IP-based session affinity, requiring cookies or HTTP headers instead. Varnish provides caching and throttling, while a separate nginx tier can terminate SSL. Kubernetes Deployments, Services, ConfigMaps, and Secrets support the illustrated implementations.

- **Sharded services** divide requests and data among servers rather than maintaining identical replicas. Sharding increases storage capacity and can improve cache memory utilization, but failed or replaced shards cause cache misses that affect latency and backend load. Replicating individual shards improves availability and enables independent scaling of heavily used shards. Routing can occur through client-side ambassadors or a shared routing service, with trade-offs in deployment complexity, scaling, and network overhead.

- **Sharding functions** should be deterministic and distribute requests uniformly. Keys must reflect information relevant to responses without unnecessarily separating equivalent requests. Consistent hashing limits redistribution when the number of shards changes. Cache-dependent systems should be load-tested both with and without caches.

- **Scatter/gather** distributes computation across leaf nodes and combines partial results at a root. Document-search examples either intersect results for separate search terms or combine matching documents from different data shards. Parallelism can reduce processing time, but request overhead and slow leaf responses limit its benefits. Replicating each leaf shard improves reliability, capacity, and support for upgrades under load.

- **Function-as-a-service (FaaS)** supports event-driven execution with simplified deployment, automatic scaling, and failure recovery. Its strongly decoupled functions complicate monitoring, dependency tracking, and debugging. It is less suitable for long-running background work, services requiring substantial in-memory data, or sustained workloads where per-request pricing becomes unfavorable. Event-driven processing and serverless computing are distinct concepts.

- **FaaS decorators** transform requests or responses around existing services. A defaulting function, for example, supplies missing API fields before forwarding a request. This separates lightweight transformation logic from the underlying service and allows independent scaling.

The lecture introduces iterative methods for solving large sparse linear systems when direct elimination is too costly in time or storage. Sparse matrix–vector multiplication is inexpensive, making repeated approximations practical.

Preconditioners aim to resemble the original matrix while allowing simpler solves. Examples include Jacobi’s diagonal preconditioner, Gauss-Seidel’s lower triangular preconditioner, successive overrelaxation, and incomplete LU factorization, which limits fill-in.

For the stationary iteration
\[
P x_{k+1}=(P-A)x_k+b,
\]
the error satisfies
\[
e_{k+1}=(I-P^{-1}A)e_k.
\]
Convergence for every initial error requires all eigenvalues of the iteration matrix to have magnitude below one. Its spectral radius controls the convergence rate.

For a tridiagonal example with diagonal entries 2 and neighboring entries −1, Jacobi’s iteration has spectral radius \(\cos(\pi/(n+1))\), close to one. Consequently, reducing the error by a fixed factor requires order \(n^2\) iterations. Both the lowest- and highest-frequency error components converge slowly. Weighted Jacobi, with weight \(2/3\), improves high-frequency damping but leaves low-frequency errors problematic.

The lecture distinguishes solution error from residual error: a small residual need not imply a small solution error when the matrix has eigenvalues near zero. Gauss-Seidel uses newly computed values immediately and, for the example, achieves roughly two Jacobi steps’ progress per iteration, but still requires order \(n^2\) iterations. Multigrid is introduced as a way to address slowly decaying low-frequency errors by changing grids.

The ADS868xW devices integrate a 16-bit SAR ADC, analog front end, programmable gain amplifier, ADC driver, and buffered precision reference. The passage describes their digital interface, operating states, programming, registers, application examples, power management, and layout recommendations.

- **Digital interface:** The multiSPI interface supports standard SPI writes and configurable reads using single or dual data outputs or source-synchronous protocols. Source-synchronous operation provides an output clock on RVS, derived from an internal or external clock. SPI-00-S is the default protocol after power-up or asynchronous reset. The host sees the device as a 32-bit input-output shift register.

- **Connection options:** Devices support standalone and daisy-chain configurations. Daisy-chained devices share CONVST/CS and SCLK, use identical configuration values, and transmit data serially through SDO-0 and SDI. An optimal frame for N devices contains 32 × N SCLK capture edges; shorter frames can cause erroneous configuration. The host receives the last device’s data first.

- **Operating states:** RESET, acquisition (ACQ), and conversion (CONV) are controlled by RST and CONVST/CS. Application reset restores configuration defaults, while power-on reset resets internal circuitry. In ACQ, the device acquires the analog input. A rising CONVST/CS edge starts conversion, which uses an internal clock and ignores further CONVST/CS transitions until completion. Before another operation, the host monitors RVS or waits the maximum conversion time.

- **Data transfers:** Frames begin on a falling CONVST/CS edge and end on the subsequent rising edge. A 32-clock frame supports valid read or write commands. Short frames permit partial data reads but not writes. In longer frames, the final 32 input bits form the command. Register operations support byte and half-word access; half-word commands ignore the address’s least significant bit.

- **Output and registers:** Output can contain fixed patterns, requested register data, or the latest 16-bit conversion result. Optional fields include device identification, input range, supply and input alarms, and parity. Nine configuration registers control identification, reset and power, interface protocols, output formatting, reference and input ranges, and alarm thresholds and hysteresis. Reset/power-control writes require an unlocking value of 69h at address 05h.

- **Applications:** An industrial eight-channel input example combines the ADS8681W with the MUX36D08 differential multiplexer for voltage and current measurement. The ADS868xW supports signals up to ±12.288 V on a single analog supply and settles to 1% accuracy in under 5 µs. Programmable input-alarm thresholds and hysteresis support monitoring applications such as thermistor-based temperature sensing.

- **Power and layout:** AVDD powers internal circuitry, while DVDD supplies the digital interface. NAP and power-down modes reduce consumption at lower throughput rates. Power-down disables analog blocks while retaining register contents and an active interface. Recommended layout practices include separating analog and digital routing, placing bypass capacitors close to supply and reference pins, and using short, low-impedance ground connections.

TI states that application information requires customer validation, warns about ESD damage, and provides documentation-update and support resources. The May 2025 revision changed ADS8685W and ADS8689W status from Advance Information to Production Data.

The study examined prospective teachers’ views on a special education course delivered through distance education, including preferences, attendance requirements, technical difficulties, and suggested improvements. Using a qualitative phenomenological approach, researchers collected semi-structured interviews from 45 volunteers at a private university during the 2022–2023 academic year.

Participants expressed mixed views. The abstract and conclusion reported that most were satisfied with distance delivery, while the findings stated that 26 participants preferred traditional instruction. Face-to-face education was valued for effectiveness, clearer understanding, and easier teacher–student communication. Benefits of distance education included flexibility, recorded lessons, home comfort, individualized learning, and affordability. Reported disadvantages included distraction, internet disruptions, limited access to devices, inadequate technical support, and difficulties with practical courses.

Most participants supported compulsory attendance to promote learning and achievement. Others opposed it because of technology barriers, access to recordings, or students’ responsibility for their own learning. Most recommended distance education despite its limitations.

Suggested improvements included developing the learning system, strengthening internet infrastructure and technical support, providing free internet access, and supplying digital materials. The authors recommended further research using quantitative methods, larger samples, and courses beyond special education.

Health savings accounts (HSAs), drawing renewed Republican interest as an alternative to the Affordable Care Act, allow people with high-deductible health plans to invest money with tax-free growth and withdrawals for eligible medical expenses. A 2015 report found about 20 million of 176 million insured people participated.

Limited disposable income and psychological barriers, including financial stress and difficulty prioritizing future needs, hinder saving. Behavioral research suggests loss aversion and automatic enrollment could encourage participation.

Research indicates HSA participants use less health care, but health benefits remain unclear. One study found lower prescription drug costs but increased emergency room visits, particularly among lower-income families. Unclear medical pricing also makes savings targets difficult to calculate. HSAs can help people with money left after daily expenses, but may be less useful for those already struggling to afford insurance.

Each contract represents 10 metric tons, quoted in US dollars per metric ton. The minimum price movement is $1 per metric ton, or $10 per contract. Contracts expire in March, May, July, September, and December.

The passage reports a backtest of 96 trades with a 2.3 profit factor and a 74% win rate. Cocoa futures tend to perform better in summer and worse in spring and fall.

Traders use cocoa futures for speculation, hedging, diversification, and arbitrage. Major risks include leveraged losses from adverse price movements and limited liquidity, which can complicate exits and widen spreads.

As of November 25, 2022, cocoa futures traded at $2,484 per metric ton. The passage cites a historical high of $5,379 in July 1977 and, using TradingView data beginning in 1979, a low of $707 in December 2000.

A Reversal Day is a substantial change in the direction of a stock or market index following an established trend, sometimes accompanied by high trading volume.

- **Bullish Reversal Day:** Prices rise after an extended downtrend, potentially making a low below the previous day’s low before closing above its high.
- **Bearish Reversal Day:** Prices decline after a prolonged rally, potentially making a high above the previous day’s high before closing below its low.

Reversals can result from changes in market sentiment, economic conditions, company-specific news, or geopolitical events. They occur in stock, currency, commodity, and bond markets.

Potential signals include changing price direction, increased trading volume, moving averages, relative strength index (RSI), Bollinger Bands, and divergences between price and RSI or moving average convergence divergence (MACD). Support and resistance levels may also help, although the passage notes that they require discretionary judgment and are difficult to quantify.

The article backtests bullish and bearish reversal strategies in gold (GLD), testing exits after 1–25 trading days. The bullish strategy’s highest average gain per trade was 2.02% with a 24-day exit. Profit factors were described as favorable across most exits, but there were few trades. The bearish strategy produced losses, attributed to gold’s upward overnight drift. The article concludes that its backtests indicate merit in the Reversal Day concept.

A descriptive cross-sectional study investigated burnout prevalence, associated factors, and coping strategies among officers at Ghana’s Nsawam Medium Security Prison. Participants were selected through proportionate stratified random sampling, with data collected between February and May 2023. Of 266 recruited officers, 243 questionnaires were analyzed. Measures included the Maslach Burnout Inventory–Human Services Survey, Work Environment Scale, and Coping Methods Checklist.

Overall burnout prevalence was 9%. High emotional exhaustion affected 42.0% of officers, high depersonalization affected 32.5%, and low personal accomplishment affected 68.7%. Shift allocation was significantly associated with emotional exhaustion, while officer rank was associated with depersonalization. In adjusted analyses, male officers had 69% lower odds of burnout than female officers, and officers with diplomas or certificates had 89% lower odds than those with postgraduate degrees.

Officers identified irregular shifts (71.6%), heavy workload (49.0%), and limited training and development opportunities (47.7%) as perceived causes of burnout. Many reported insufficient recognition, constructive feedback, and supervisory support. However, most expressed pride in their work, felt valued by colleagues, and felt capable of performing their duties.

Common coping strategies included talking to colleagues (62.5%), looking forward to time off (60.1%), and talking to family (54.3%). Alcohol use was reported by 29.2%.

The study recommends addressing irregular shifts and heavy workloads and improving training and development opportunities to reduce burnout among prison officers.

The authors criticize Stanford’s mandatory Program in Writing and Rhetoric (PWR), arguing that it inadequately teaches academic writing through overly broad course topics, limited instruction, and insufficient source analysis. They propose allowing experienced writers to bypass PWR, providing more targeted instruction for less experienced students, and including conservative perspectives among course options. They oppose a proposed PWR minor, arguing that resources should instead improve existing classes.

As an alternative, the authors recommend a standardized, rigorous, source-based course designed by experienced humanities professors and taught by current PWR instructors. Students would analyze texts within a focused subject area to develop skills needed for other academic work.
