NVIDIA’s Turing GPU architecture combines rasterization, real-time ray tracing, AI-based image processing, and new shading techniques for games, professional graphics, and virtual reality.

- **Display and video:** Turing supports native HDR processing and BT.2100 tone mapping. Its NVENC encoder supports HEVC 8K encoding at 30 fps, with bitrate savings of up to 25% for HEVC and 15% for H.264. NVDEC adds HEVC 4:4:4 8/10/12-bit decoding and supports VP9 10/12-bit HDR. Encoding improvements enable 4K streaming with lower CPU utilization than software encoding.

- **Connectivity and multi-GPU support:** USB-C and VirtualLink hardware support combines VR headset power, display, and data connections into one connector. TU102 and TU104 use second-generation NVLink for two-way SLI, providing up to 100 GB/s and 50 GB/s bidirectional bandwidth, respectively. Three-way and four-way SLI are unsupported; TU106 supports neither NVLink nor SLI.

- **Real-time ray tracing:** Dedicated RT Cores accelerate bounding volume hierarchy traversal and ray-triangle intersection testing, freeing shader processors for other work. Hybrid rendering uses rasterization where efficient and ray tracing for effects such as reflections, refractions, and shadows. Denoising reduces the number of rays needed. The passage reports ray-tracing performance approximately ten times faster than Pascal and describes improvements to shadows, ambient occlusion, and reflections.

- **AI features:** NVIDIA NGX uses Turing Tensor Cores and pretrained neural networks to enhance graphics and other applications. Deep Learning Super-Sampling (DLSS), trained against 64× supersampled reference images, targets image quality comparable to temporal anti-aliasing with roughly half the shading work. DLSS 2X prioritizes higher image quality. Other NGX features include image inpainting, interpolated slow-motion video, and image or video upscaling.

- **Geometry and shading:** Mesh shading introduces cooperative task and mesh shaders to reduce CPU draw-call bottlenecks and support flexible geometry processing and level-of-detail selection. Variable Rate Shading adjusts shading rates within 16×16-pixel regions independently of visibility sampling, enabling content-adaptive shading, motion-adaptive shading, and foveated rendering. Texture Space Shading stores shading results in textures for reuse across pixels, views, and frames.

- **Multiple views and resource management:** Multi-View Rendering supports four hardware views per pass and up to 32 views through the API, sharing view-independent processing. Applications include VR, shadow maps, and character instances. Turing also supports DX12 Tier 3 resource binding and Tier 2 resource heaps.

- **GPU implementations:** TU104 incorporates RT Cores, Tensor Cores, and updated streaming multiprocessors and appears in products including GeForce RTX 2080, Quadro RTX 5000, and Tesla T4. Tesla T4 targets inference workloads. TU106 powers GeForce RTX 2070 and retains the principal ray-tracing, AI, and shader improvements.

The passage introduces RTX-OPS as a workload-weighted metric combining Tensor, FP32, ray-tracing, and integer throughput rather than simply adding their peak rates. It concludes with technical explanations of ray tracing and legal notices limiting warranties and liability.

President Donald Trump warned Iran against restarting its nuclear program while discussing the 2015 nuclear agreement with French President Emmanuel Macron. Trump criticized the deal for excluding ballistic missiles and Iran’s involvement in regional conflicts, but said he and Macron could reach an understanding quickly. Iran threatened to expand its nuclear program if the agreement collapsed and might leave a nuclear nonproliferation treaty if Washington withdrew. Macron sought to preserve the agreement, describing it as the best available means of constraining Tehran and preventing nuclear proliferation. Their agenda also included European exemptions from U.S. steel tariffs and the future of U.S. troops in Syria.

Thailand recorded 390 road deaths during Songkran week, an 11 per cent decline from the previous year following a junta road-safety campaign. Earlier crackdowns had shown no reductions. Drunk driving caused 28 per cent of accidents, and authorities seized 5,600 motorbikes and 1,800 cars from drivers over the alcohol limit. Junta chief Prayut Chan-O-Cha said more work was needed to encourage responsible driving.

The Daily Examiner is replacing metered digital access with a premium model to fund journalism. Subscriber-only stories will carry a PLUS symbol, while public safety information and some local stories remain free. Existing subscribers retain unlimited access. Subscriptions include app access, newsletters, breaking news alerts and access to other News Corp sites, with newspaper or digital-only options available.

A holder catches snaps and positions the football for field goals and extra points, placing it precisely at the kicker’s preferred spot and angle with the laces facing away. The role requires soft hands, quick reactions, consistent placement, and coordination with the long snapper and kicker. Holders may also pass, run, or flip the ball during fake field goals.

No particular body type is required. NFL teams often use punters, while high school and college teams may use backup quarterbacks, receivers, or other capable players. Although holding is typically a secondary duty and receives little attention, mistakes can cost scoring opportunities and affect game outcomes. The NFL tracks no holding statistics, and there is no consensus on the best holders.

The Supreme Court of Canada unanimously upheld a ruling that confidential records of residential school abuse claims should be destroyed after 15 years. The court said settlement negotiators intended the compensation assessment process to be private, and claimants and alleged perpetrators relied on confidentiality assurances. Federal bodies hold digital and physical records pertaining to more than 37,000 claims.

The EU is preparing to urge multilateral development banks to align financing more closely with the Paris Agreement, redirect lending from fossil fuels toward low-carbon projects, and expand climate investment. According to a draft policy seen by Reuters, the proposal also seeks greater transparency, local currency financing, investment de-risking, and coordination to attract private capital.

Led by Germany and France, the initiative will feature at upcoming World Bank and IMF annual meetings. U.S. officials oppose the shift, warning that climate targets could distract banks from economic growth and poverty reduction. European leaders argue that climate finance supports sustainable growth and that MDBs’ record $137 billion in climate funding in 2024 remains insufficient. U.S. resistance could hinder consensus.

The study evaluated a streamlined optical genome mapping (OGM) analysis and reporting workflow using Variant Intelligence Applications (VIA) software for myeloid malignancies. Conventional cytogenetic testing often requires multiple methods to assess structural and copy number abnormalities, while OGM offers a single-assay approach.

Ten retrospective cases—nine acute myeloid leukemia cases and one myelodysplastic syndrome/neoplasm case—underwent independent, blinded technologist and laboratory director reviews, with five to six reviews per case. The workflow used customized views, filters, guideline annotations, and variant classifications to support interpretation and reporting.

OGM through VIA detected all abnormalities identified by standard-of-care testing. Six cases had reportable findings, while four were negative by both approaches. In five positive cases, guideline-defined sentinel variants were unanimously reported and classified as Tier 1A. In the sixth, trisomy 21 was detected but omitted from one report, and its classification varied. OGM identified additional findings in five of six positive cases, including copy number losses, chromosomal gains, small deletions, and complex rearrangements. Reporting and classification of non-Tier 1A findings varied among reviewers.

Average technologist review times were 25.2 minutes for negative cases, 28.5 minutes for simple cases, and 47.3 minutes for complex cases. Compared with previous estimates for Bionano Access alone, VIA often reduced analysis time by approximately 50%.

The authors conclude that OGM with Bionano Access and VIA can streamline cytogenomic interpretation and reporting and may support greater standardization, although variation remained in classification and reporting of some findings.

Olean’s Common Council unanimously authorized Mayor Bill Aiello to apply for a $10 million state Downtown Revitalization Initiative grant. Proposed projects include redeveloping the former Manufacturers Hanover building, supporting business incubators, expanding theater options, improving pedestrian access to Lincoln Park and creating a park near Olean General Hospital. Aiello said the city could also qualify for more than $2 million through the Buffalo Billion initiative. Jamestown Community College representative John Sayegh supported the application and said the college would work with the city on upgrading its Cutco Theater.

Former CIA officer Kevin Mallory is on trial in Virginia, accused of giving classified information, including details about human assets, to a Chinese agent for $25,000. Prosecutors cited undeclared cash found after a Shanghai trip, phone messages and secret documents recovered from his home. Defence lawyers say Mallory intended to feed the Chinese fake documents and expose their intelligence operation. Two witnesses testified that he contacted CIA associates before the airport inspection that prosecutors say prompted his cover story. Mallory faces up to life in prison.

Eric Thames hit a two-run homer in the fifth inning to give the Milwaukee Brewers a 2-0 victory over the Minnesota Twins on Tuesday. It was his third home run in six games.

Junior Guerra pitched five scoreless innings, allowing two hits and striking out eight. Josh Hader followed with three hitless innings, and Corey Knebel struck out the side in the ninth for his ninth save.

Twins starter Jake Odorizzi allowed two runs and four hits over five innings, striking out nine and walking four. Minnesota fell to 1-7 on its nine-game road trip.

Twins first baseman Joe Mauer finished the game without a putout or assist, the first such occurrence for a major league first baseman since 2012.

The address calls on Americans to defend the nation and its democratic institutions against external threats, rejecting isolation and inaction. It argues that democracy has survived domestic crisis through decisive action while preserving constitutional government, the Bill of Rights, and free elections.

The speaker presents national strength as dependent on material well-being, an informed public, and, above all, America’s spirit of freedom. Rooted in generations of people seeking liberty and expressed in foundational documents, this democratic ideal requires continued progress in citizens’ security, opportunity, and knowledge. The address rejects both undeserved poverty and self-serving wealth.

Invoking Washington’s charge to preserve liberty, the speaker urges Americans to resist doubt and fear. Protecting the nation’s democratic spirit is presented as the central justification for sacrifices in national defense and for determined action amid unprecedented dangers.

Uber launched a nationwide panic button allowing riders to call 911 from the app and view their real-time location. In select pilot cities, the app automatically sends location information and vehicle details to emergency dispatchers.

The speaker said Detroit was defensively sound and capitalized on a brief letdown to take a two-goal lead. They described the rest of the game as largely even, with improvement in the second and third periods, but said the power play generated no chances. The speaker also expressed disappointment in their own performance and emphasized the need for better team play.

A December 2000 McKinsey update reviews international electricity-sector privatization and restructuring during June–November 2000. Governments were increasingly opening generation markets to foreign investors, unbundling state utilities, and introducing wholesale and retail competition to meet rising demand despite limited public funding. Some international companies were shifting investments toward less risky U.S. and European markets.

- **Western Europe:** EU directives encouraged liberalization, cross-border investment, mergers, and asset sales. Market opening varied considerably. The UK and several Nordic countries already offered full customer choice, while others pursued phased access. Grid-access conditions, incumbent control, and regulatory delays continued to impede competition in some markets.
- **Central and Eastern Europe:** Governments pursued privatization to attract capital and restructuring associated with prospective EU membership or international financing. Progress faced obstacles including price controls, union opposition, inadequate regulation, and payment problems.
- **Asia-Pacific:** Economic recovery revived restructuring plans and electricity demand. Australia was moving toward full customer choice, Japan had opened access for large customers, and South Korea planned to separate and privatize generation businesses. Independent power producers continued to face contract disputes, financially weak state buyers, limited guarantees, and regulatory uncertainty.
- **Latin America:** Privatization had advanced across most major economies, but currency fluctuations, inflation, ownership restrictions, and political uncertainty slowed further sales. Transmission concessions and privatizations were expanding. Heavy reliance on hydropower and prolonged droughts contributed to shortages and investment concerns. Mexico’s incoming administration proposed market opening without privatization.
- **Africa and the Middle East:** Governments increasingly sought foreign investment and private generation, although most reforms remained limited to independent power projects. Some countries considered utility unbundling or partial privatization. Regional transmission links were a prominent development, while drought, subsidized tariffs, and incomplete regulatory frameworks complicated investment.

The update includes country-level developments and references accompanying maps and market-opening timelines.

The study examines how digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth influence sustainable supply chain performance through brand image and supply chain image in Indonesian information and communication technology (ICT) companies. Digitalization supports business and supply chain activities, but companies face financial constraints, technological challenges, and infrastructure limitations.

Researchers distributed 568 questionnaires to employees involved in product distribution and obtained 315 valid responses. Indonesia was divided into 15 clusters, of which 10 were randomly selected; respondents were then randomly selected from ICT companies. Data were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modelling.

Results supported all seven hypotheses:
- Digital customer experience through e-commerce and electronic word of mouth positively affected brand image.
- Brand image positively affected supply chain image.
- Supply chain image positively affected sustainable supply chain performance.
- Brand image mediated the relationships between both digital customer experience and electronic word of mouth and supply chain image.
- Supply chain image mediated the relationship between brand image and sustainable supply chain performance.

The model explained 82.3% of the variance in sustainable supply chain performance. The study recommends that Indonesian ICT companies use e-commerce practices to strengthen digital customer experience, electronic word of mouth, and brand image, thereby supporting supply chain performance.

On February 8, 2021, Apple Inc. completed the issuance and sale of six series of notes:
- $2.5 billion at 0.700%, due 2026.
- $2.5 billion at 1.200%, due 2028.
- $2.75 billion at 1.650%, due 2031.
- $1.5 billion at 2.375%, due 2041.
- $3 billion at 2.650%, due 2051.
- $1.75 billion at 2.800%, due 2061.

Interest is payable semiannually on February 8 and August 8, beginning August 8, 2021. Each series matures on February 8 of its respective maturity year. The notes are senior unsecured obligations ranking equally with Apple’s other unsecured and unsubordinated debt.

The February 1, 2021 underwriting agreement names Goldman Sachs, J.P. Morgan Securities and Morgan Stanley as representatives of the underwriters. The notes were issued under Apple’s November 5, 2018 indenture and Form S-3 registration statement. The filing includes the underwriting agreement, officer’s certificate, note forms and related legal opinion and consent.

The disclosure describes a hybrid gas turbine electric propulsion system and methods for operating it during descent. An electric motor coupled to the low-speed shaft supplements engine power, allowing the gas turbine to be undersized relative to takeoff or climb thrust requirements and configured for maximum turbine inlet temperature during cruise.

During descent, a controller reduces or eliminates thrust from the engine core. The core may be shut down or maintained at a minimum temperature to prevent an additional thermal cycle, which can shorten the life of certain components. Core operation can be limited by reducing fuel or airflow.

Aircraft systems switch from engine-derived power and bleed air to electrical operation. Stored electricity powers systems, including an electric compressor that replaces compressor bleed air used for environmental control and cabin pressurization. Energy may be generated and stored during earlier flight phases.

The fan may windmill during descent, rotating the low-speed shaft and driving the motor as a generator. Generated electricity can power aircraft systems or be stored. Alternatively, stored energy can drive the motor and fan to produce conventional descent thrust or enough thrust to overcome engine drag.

The described approach reduces fuel consumption and emissions during low-power operation and allows aircraft systems to operate independently of the engine during certain operating modes.

The passage assesses prospects for peace in spring 1953, contrasting the hopes of 1945 with eight years of growing fear and military rivalry. It presents U.S. principles of international cooperation, national self-determination, noninterference, and peace through understanding rather than an arms race. It attributes Western rearmament to Soviet expansion and coercion, while affirming willingness to respond to genuine peaceful actions.

It warns that continued rivalry threatens either atomic war or enduring insecurity and military spending that diverts resources from food, housing, education, and health. Stalin’s death and the emergence of new Soviet leadership are presented as an opportunity to change course, provided peaceful intentions are demonstrated through deeds.

Proposed steps include an honorable Korean armistice followed by discussions toward free elections in a united Korea; an end to attacks on Indochina and Malaya; an Austrian treaty; the release of remaining World War II prisoners; European cooperation; German reunification through free elections; and independence for Eastern European nations.

The passage advocates negotiated limits on armed forces and military production, peaceful international control of atomic energy, prohibition of atomic weapons, restrictions on other highly destructive weapons, and safeguards including United Nations inspections. It proposes devoting a substantial share of disarmament savings to international aid and reconstruction, combating poverty through development, trade, and improved living conditions.

It concludes by asking whether Soviet leaders will support genuine peace in Asia, freedom of governmental choice, and enforceable disarmament, emphasizing that actions—not rhetoric—must establish their intentions.

IDC identifies high-performance computing (HPC), simulations, modeling, and data analytics as key tools for manufacturing innovation, productivity, and digital transformation. These technologies can accelerate development and manufacturing, optimize supply chains and energy consumption, and support new digital products, services, and business models.

Cloud-based HPC and HPC as a service (HPCaaS) offer access to evolving technologies and can supplement or replace in-house infrastructure. Among respondents, 52% consider fast, flexible access to advanced analysis methods and hardware a core innovation benefit of HPCaaS.

IDC recommends that manufacturers:
- Integrate virtual product and manufacturing development into digital transformation.
- Establish a holistic data strategy and a shared, consistent database across the product life cycle.
- Select on-premises, cloud, or hybrid HPC models according to utilization, budget, performance, flexibility, security, and available skills.
- Prioritize scalability, security, and energy efficiency.
- Seek external expertise where internal HPC capabilities are insufficient.

The findings draw on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 technology decision makers at industrial enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

IDC’s white paper examines how simulation, modeling, data analytics, and high-performance computing (HPC) support manufacturing innovation and digital transformation. Its findings draw on a December 2021 telephone survey of 200 IT and departmental decision makers at manufacturing enterprises with more than 500 employees in Germany, Austria, and Switzerland.

Manufacturers face geopolitical uncertainty, rising energy costs, material shortages, supply chain disruptions, labor shortages, and sustainability demands. Simulation, modeling, and analytics can accelerate product development, improve quality, reduce costs, and support new digital products, services, and business models. Three-quarters of respondents identify increased innovation as a leading objective, while 57% emphasize improving product and service quality.

Around half of surveyed enterprises already use these technologies in product development and production and process planning. Deployment in these areas and quality management is expected to reach as high as 90% within two years. Applications include virtual prototyping, design optimization, digital verification, and digital twins that connect operational data with product development. IDC emphasizes that fragmented departmental data limits these benefits and recommends a unified information base across the product life cycle.

Increasing calculation complexity creates trade-offs between speed and accuracy. Half of respondents report that calculations and iterations take too long, and 42% use simulations that are outdated or inaccurate. HPC enables complex calculations, faster iterations, higher-quality results, and additional applications. Overall, 81% regard HPC as a game changer for product and process innovation. More than a quarter already use professional HPC infrastructure, and another 39% are planning or piloting deployment.

External infrastructure is prominent: 87% of existing HPC users prefer or plan to use external HPC resources, and 74% use or plan their own infrastructure in colocation datacenters. Challenges include security concerns, cited by 72%; energy consumption and sustainability, cited by 58%; and insufficient internal and external expertise, cited by 42% of HPC users. Costs, computing capacity, availability, and infrastructure complexity also constrain deployment.

Cloud-based HPC and HPC as a Service offer scalable capacity, flexible costs, access to modern hardware and methods, and reduced infrastructure-management responsibilities. Hybrid architectures can retain sensitive workloads internally while using public cloud capacity for other workloads or demand peaks. Cloud HPC still requires trained personnel to configure resources, program calculations, and interpret results. Among existing HPC users, 81% intend to implement HPC-based business models.

IDC recommends establishing virtual development processes, adopting a holistic data strategy, selecting operating models according to utilization, budget, performance, security, and skills, and prioritizing scalability and energy efficiency. It also recommends seeking external expertise when necessary. The paper concludes that integrated data and HPC-supported analysis are important foundations for manufacturing innovation, productivity, and competitiveness.

The March 2006 AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Silicon Revision A3 specification update documents hardware defects, their effects, and workarounds.

- **Clock gating:** Automatic clock gating can prevent edge-triggered PIC interrupts from recovering, potentially hanging the system. It can also cause lost GLIU statistics-counter ASMIs, incorrect UART CEIR operation, and failed USB register reads. Disabling affected clock gating is recommended where specified.
- **IDE and DMA:** A host-terminated UDMA read can leave state that corrupts CRCs during subsequent device-terminated UDMA writes. The workaround uses the ATAC UDMA I/O blocking feature. IDE drivers must send PIO command packets before enabling bus mastering and use DWORD-aligned PRDs to avoid failures or hangs. Certain unexpected IDE interrupts reset the bus master. The ATAC DMA SSMI feature generates an SSMI but fails to block IDE I/O and should not be used.
- **Descriptor prefetching:** ATAC and audio-controller prefetching can create hazards when software modifies active, insufficiently aligned PRD tables. UDMA descriptors should be defined before transfers; audio descriptor changes must remain at least two tables ahead of the current PRD.
- **Power-management registers:** Byte accesses to PM1_EN and PM1_STS hang. WORD and BYTE writes to PMC registers can corrupt subsequent writes. Avoiding unsupported access sizes or using SMI traps provides workarounds.
- **Keyboard and mouse emulation:** KEL cannot distinguish port 060h and 064h writes through CmdData; trap information must be used instead. Snoop mode incorrectly changes HCE registers, requiring software to save and restore state. Reading port 60h incorrectly clears AuxOutputFull; interrupt-based keyboard and mouse handling is recommended.
- **Interrupts and wakeup:** Simultaneous IRQ and SSMI events can delay an SSMI until after the associated I/O completes. Several GPIO wake inputs do not function from ACPI S3; PWRBTN# is the recommended alternative. LOWBAT_FLAG may fail to record a low-battery event.
- **LPC, RTC, and SMB:** Block and demand LPC DMA can interfere with I/O; single-transfer mode is recommended. LPC-to-ISA transactions may abort, with a programmable-logic workaround available. Particular consecutive RTC accesses return incorrect data. SMB NEGACK handling requires a two-write clearing sequence.
- **Other issues:** PCI retry counting includes unrelated retries. After suspend, GPIO high-bank atomic writes require full-register read-modify-write operations. Sleep-exit delay counters must be shorter than PM_SED to restore control signals and PCI/IDE inputs. PIC polling is unsupported.
- **Limited-impact defects:** Simulated back-to-back PCI reads can fail, but no real-world impact is reported. IRDY# and DEVSEL# violate minimum timing specifications without expected system failures. Fixed UDMA acknowledgment timing still satisfies requirements.

U.S. District Judge Fernando Olguin dismissed Spencer Elden’s lawsuit over Nirvana’s 1991 album cover, which depicted Elden naked underwater as a baby. Olguin ruled that the image was not child pornography, finding that nudity alone did not establish lasciviousness and comparing it to a family photograph of a child bathing.

Myrna LaPlante, whose aunt went missing in 2006, supports inquiry chief commissioner Marion Buller despite the Assembly of First Nations’ call for her resignation. LaPlante said her family trusts the current commission and would withdraw its story if the inquiry were reset. She supports extending its deadline by two years. Other Saskatchewan families support Buller’s resignation, citing poor communication, scheduling changes, inadequate support and failure to address community trauma.

Donna Adelson, 75, was sentenced to life in prison plus 30 years for her role in the 2014 murder of her former son-in-law, Florida State University law professor Dan Markel. Adelson maintained her innocence, prompting Judge Stephen Everett to warn that he could consider her “utter lack of remorse.” Prosecutors alleged she plotted the murder with her son, Charlie, motivated by the family’s desire for Markel’s ex-wife, Wendi Adelson, to relocate to South Florida with their children. Wendi has not been charged. Donna’s husband, Harvey, also asserted her innocence.

Sony’s A7Riii firmware update fixes a “Set File Name” issue and improves camera stability. Installation supports Mac OS X 10.10–10.11 and macOS 10.12, but not macOS 10.13 High Sierra. Users experiencing installation problems on High Sierra can try an earlier supported Mac operating system or run Windows on their machine.

Mortgage borrowing power can improve by paying off debt, obtaining a co-signer, changing loan programs, increasing the down payment or changing jobs before applying. Lenders assess recurring payments rather than interest rates; debt payments exceeding 50 percent of monthly pre-tax income can create borrowing challenges. Co-signers share mortgage liability and can only be removed through refinancing or selling the property. Switching loan programs may improve financing eligibility. Larger down payments generally have less impact than paying off debt. Job changes require careful attention from a loan officer, particularly regarding continuity of field and role. These options should be researched for individual circumstances.

NVIDIA’s Form 10-Q for the quarter ended October 30, 2022, reported revenue of $5.93 billion, down 17% year over year and 12% sequentially. Quarterly results varied across markets:
- Data Center revenue increased 31% year over year to $3.83 billion.
- Gaming revenue declined 51% to $1.57 billion.
- Professional Visualization revenue declined 65% to $200 million.
- Automotive revenue increased 86% to $251 million.
- OEM and Other revenue declined 69% to $73 million.

Gaming and Professional Visualization declines reflected reduced shipments to partners to align channel inventories with demand expectations. Macroeconomic conditions and COVID-19 lockdowns in China weighed on consumer demand. Gross margin fell to 53.6% from 65.2% a year earlier, primarily because of a $702 million inventory charge, largely related to lower Data Center demand in China.

For the first nine months, revenue rose 9% to $20.92 billion, while net income fell to $2.95 billion from $6.75 billion. Results included a $1.35 billion charge following termination of the proposed Arm acquisition because of regulatory challenges. Inventory provisions totaled $2.01 billion.

At October 30, NVIDIA held $13.14 billion in cash, cash equivalents and marketable securities, compared with $21.21 billion at January 30. Nine-month operating cash flow declined to $3.39 billion from $6.08 billion. NVIDIA returned $9.29 billion to shareholders through repurchases and dividends during the nine months and had $8.28 billion remaining under its repurchase authorization.

New U.S. export licensing requirements affected certain products sold to China and Russia. Third-quarter revenue losses from these restrictions were largely offset by alternative product sales into China. NVIDIA also cited supply commitments, demand forecasting, product transitions and geopolitical developments as business risks.

The company began shipping H100 GPUs and GeForce RTX 4090 products and announced cloud and AI collaborations. Management stated that available liquidity was sufficient to meet operating requirements for at least the next twelve months and the foreseeable future.
The United Way of Northwest Illinois will launch Carroll County’s Imagination Library on March 28, 2018, at Mt. Carroll Township Public Library, providing books to children ages 0–5.

Which? research suggested lenders raised mortgage costs faster than savings rates after November’s base rate increase from 0.25% to 0.5%. Within five weeks, 48% of 327 instant-access savings accounts and ISAs had unchanged rates, while 21% received the full increase. By year-end, 53% of standard variable rate mortgage providers examined had raised rates for existing borrowers. Which? urged fair treatment of customers. UK Finance said rates reflect multiple factors and most mortgage borrowers’ fixed-rate deals would remain unchanged.

The New York Times reported that U.S. agencies intercepted calls between Russian intelligence officials and Trump campaign associates, including Paul Manafort. Officials cited in the report found no evidence of campaign cooperation with Russian election interference.

The FBI interviewed Michael Flynn about contacts with a Russian official after Trump’s inauguration. Flynn was ousted amid concerns he misled administration officials. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer called for an independent investigation and Attorney General Jeff Sessions’ recusal.

At least six Republican senators withheld support for labor secretary nominee Andrew Puzder pending his confirmation hearing, with questions surrounding delayed tax payments for an unauthorized housekeeper.

Linda McMahon was sworn in as Small Business Administration chief following an 81-19 Senate vote. David Shulkin became Veterans Affairs secretary after unanimous confirmation.

Michael Lewis’ *The Undoing Project* describes a 1968 study in which doctors assessing stomach-ulcer x-rays disagreed with one another and contradicted their own diagnoses when shown duplicates. A simple computer algorithm based on their stated diagnostic methods outperformed every doctor. The author questions how researchers resolved conflicting methods and supplied image data to the computer. The passage considers whether algorithms benefit from consistent rule-following or collective expertise, and whether artificial intelligence’s ability to generate rules could reduce reliance on experts.

The July 31, 2001 IEP news compilation covers California’s electricity crisis, conflicts of interest in Gov. Gray Davis’ administration, utility rescue efforts and deregulation developments.

- The SEC reportedly opened a preliminary inquiry into whether Davis’ energy consultants used inside information to trade power-company stocks. Five consultants were dismissed over possible conflicts of interest. Davis spokesman Steve Maviglio disclosed a $12,000 Calpine stock purchase and denied wrongdoing.
- Communications consultants Chris Lehane and Mark Fabiani agreed to forgo payment and leave the administration under a lawsuit settlement concerning their simultaneous work for Southern California Edison.
- Commentary criticized California’s $43 billion in long-term electricity contracts as excessively costly. Critics also questioned provisions covering generators’ environmental costs and tax increases, and the contracts’ reliance on fossil fuels.
- Davis’ proposed rescue of Southern California Edison remained unresolved ahead of an August 15 legislative deadline. Competing proposals differed over the utility’s required losses and state acquisition of transmission lines.
- Federal refund restrictions could reduce California’s potential recovery from approximately $9 billion to $3.9 billion. The order excluded purchases before October 2000 and direct purchases by the Department of Water Resources. Davis planned an appeal.
- San Francisco voters would consider two November measures establishing public-power entities. Supporters argued for local control and lower rates; PG&E financed opposition.
- Texas prepared to begin a delayed electricity-deregulation pilot before broader implementation scheduled for January 1. Maryland regulators examined whether BGE’s proposed corporate separation would leave it financially capable of serving customers under frozen rates.
- California’s crisis involved high wholesale prices, supply constraints and transmission problems. PG&E had filed for bankruptcy, the state was purchasing electricity for struggling utilities, and regulators had approved substantial rate increases.

Rare wave-like clouds spotted over Bristol on Monday appeared to be Asperitas, a newly classified cloud feature. Also seen in Monmouthshire, Thornbury and Filton, they resemble a rough sea from below. How they form remains uncertain.

William Green discusses numerical solutions of partial differential equations (PDEs) before introducing probability and measurement uncertainty.

A homework problem involves modeling drug diffusion from a patch into flowing fluid using both COMSOL and a student-written finite volume code. Small diffusivity and a large Peclet number produce sharp concentration gradients, requiring careful mesh selection. Green emphasizes that computed results must be checked for convergence and physical consistency by varying mesh spacing and boundary placement rather than trusting software output.

The finite volume method balances incoming and outgoing fluxes with accumulation in each control volume; at steady state, net flux is zero. Boundary conditions include zero flux at impermeable walls and prescribed concentrations at the drug patch, implemented through boundary flux calculations or ghost volumes. The resulting equations are linear and sparse, making sparse solvers appropriate. Adaptive meshes can improve accuracy but introduce programming risks.

For time-dependent PDEs, Green introduces the CFL number, \(u\Delta t/\Delta x\), which relates time steps to spatial resolution and flow velocity. For the straightforward methods discussed, keeping this number near or below one limits how far material travels during a time step. Refining the spatial mesh consequently increases computational cost through both additional cells and smaller time steps.

The probability discussion emphasizes that measurements vary because of instrument noise and intrinsic physical fluctuations. Continuum equations describe averages rather than individual molecular behavior. Repeated measurements, averages, and error bars help communicate uncertainty.

Using coin flips, Green introduces joint and conditional probabilities, independence, and the importance of avoiding double counting. Bayes’ theorem relates the probability of a hypothesis given observations to the probability of those observations given the hypothesis.

For continuous variables, probability densities must be integrated over intervals to obtain probabilities. Densities have units inverse to those of the variable and integrate to one. A cumulative distribution gives the dimensionless probability that a variable is less than or equal to a specified value.

Special education in Singapore has expanded significantly since 2004, shifting from a largely separate welfare-based system toward greater inclusion within national education. Before 2004, voluntary welfare organizations primarily educated students with disabilities in special schools, while mainstream schools emphasized students’ ability to meet existing academic expectations and could refuse admission.

Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong’s 2004 calls for an inclusive society prompted developments in disability services, school support and personnel preparation. Subsequent Enabling Masterplans established national inclusion goals, and Singapore ratified the United Nations Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities in 2013. The Compulsory Education Act of 2019 required students with special educational needs to attend mainstream primary schools or government-funded special schools. Approximately 80% of students with special needs attend mainstream schools, while 20% with higher support needs attend special schools.

The National Institute of Education provides preparation for special school teachers, Special Educational Needs Officers and mainstream teachers. Key programs include:
- A one-year Diploma in Special Education for special school teachers and Special Educational Needs Officers.
- A Certificate in Special Needs Support for mainstream teachers.
- Advanced diploma, master’s and doctoral pathways.
- Compulsory foundational coursework for mainstream trainee teachers and continuing professional development for practising educators.

Mainstream schools increasingly use tiered support systems involving teachers, special needs officers, counsellors and psychologists. Close collaboration among the Ministry of Education, the National Institute of Education and schools, together with continuity in government policy, has supported these changes.

Several challenges remain. Government-funded special schools are still operated by social service agencies, and their teachers generally receive lower salaries than mainstream teachers. Newly recruited, untrained special school teachers require school-based support before formal preparation. Special education training is shorter and less comprehensive than mainstream teacher preparation, and the National Institute of Education offers no undergraduate degree in special education.

Opportunities for students with higher support needs to learn within mainstream environments also remain limited. Partnerships and joint activities connect special and mainstream schools, but special classrooms for students with moderate to severe disabilities within mainstream schools do not exist.

Singapore’s broader educational direction increasingly emphasizes holistic development, lifelong learning and student-centred outcomes rather than academic performance alone. The passage anticipates an expanding partnership between special and mainstream education in preparing teachers to support diverse learners.

Belleville-area residents are advised to avoid touching Hickory Tussock Moth caterpillars, whose venom-bearing hairs can cause skin irritation and occasional allergic reactions. These white, fluffy caterpillars with black markings are most commonly found from July to September. Contact may cause redness, burning, swelling or pain. Public health advice is to wash affected skin, apply calamine lotion or cortisone for itching, and seek medical attention for more serious symptoms or allergic reactions. D-branes become dynamical through open-string fluctuations: massless gauge fields live on their world-volumes, while massless scalar fields describe transverse motion.

A D-brane’s mass is its ground-state energy, identified with the vacuum energy of open strings living on it. This is calculated by summing Euclidean world-sheet surfaces with boundaries, weighted by \(g_s^{-\chi}\), where \(\chi=2-2h-b\). At weak string coupling, the disk contribution dominates, giving D-brane tension proportional to \(1/g_s\).

Interactions between two D-branes offer another perspective. A cylinder diagram represents either tree-level closed-string exchange between branes or a one-loop vacuum diagram of open strings connecting them. This equivalence, called channel duality, provides an indication of the relationship between gravity and gauge theory underlying holographic duality.

For constant scalar gradients and gauge-field strengths, higher-order terms combine into the Dirac–Born–Infeld action. It incorporates nonlinear electromagnetic dynamics and relativistic brane motion; when these quantities vary slowly, additional derivative corrections are suppressed. The transverse scalars are massless because translation invariance forbids a position-dependent potential. They are Goldstone bosons associated with broken translation symmetries. World-sheet topology also implies that the open-string coupling is proportional to the square root of the closed-string coupling.

For \(n\) coincident D-branes, strings can connect every ordered pair of branes, producing \(n^2\) copies of each excitation. Fields therefore become matrices, and string joining produces matrix multiplication. The resulting world-volume theory has \(U(n)\) gauge symmetry and reduces at low energies to Yang–Mills theory with adjoint scalar fields.

Separating branes makes connecting strings massive, with their formerly massless modes acquiring mass equal to string tension times separation. This realizes the Higgs mechanism: separating two branes breaks \(U(2)\) to \(U(1)\times U(1)\). Commuting scalar matrices have vanishing potential and can be diagonalized, with their eigenvalues specifying brane positions. Separating \(n\) branes into coincident stacks of sizes \(n_1,\ldots,n_k\) breaks the gauge symmetry to \(U(n_1)\times\cdots\times U(n_k)\).

The Gann Fan, developed by W.D. Gann, is a technical analysis tool that uses nine diagonal lines drawn from significant price highs or lows to identify potential support, resistance, reversals, and breakouts. It is based on the theory that price movements follow geometric angles relating price to time.

Its main line, the 45-degree or 1:1 line, represents one unit of price movement per unit of time. Other lines represent different price-time ratios. Under Gann’s technique, prices moving along or above the 1:1 line suggest a strong bull market, while a break below may signal bearish conditions. Unlike the Fibonacci fan, which uses Fibonacci ratios, the Gann Fan emphasizes price-time relationships.

Traders use the tool for trend-following and reversal strategies, including forex trading, often alongside trend lines, moving averages, and other indicators. Suggested risk controls include stop-loss orders, position sizing, risk-reward ratios, and clear entry and exit plans.

The passage emphasizes that Gann angles are not consistently accurate: prices need not follow specific angles, and indicated levels may not function as support or resistance. It recommends backtesting while noting that past performance does not guarantee future results. However, the authors report that they could not produce a meaningful backtest because the strategy’s subjectivity prevented sufficiently precise trading rules.

Cover 1 uses man-to-man coverage on receivers with a deep safety protecting the middle. A linebacker or strong safety may also cover short-to-intermediate routes as a “low hole” defender. This scheme allows defenses to bracket receivers, reinforce run defense, or blitz.

Offenses can attack cover 1 on the perimeter, away from the safety’s help. Effective approaches include:
- **Pick plays:** Crossing receiver paths create natural collisions between defenders and separation for receivers.
- **Double moves:** Receivers sell shorter routes before going deep, using combinations such as slant-and-go or hitch-and-go.
- **Routes caught on the move:** Deep crosses, wheels, and outs help receivers transition into gaining yards after the catch.

Examples from college offenses illustrate these approaches through bubble-go concepts, slot fades, out-and-ups, goal-line motion, and scissors or snag-wheel combinations. Results vary, including touchdowns, incompletions, and a catch stopped near the goal line.

The MSPM0C1105 and MSPM0C1106 documentation describes peripheral capabilities, application requirements, development support, and packaging guidance.

- **Low-frequency subsystem:** LFSS combines peripherals requiring a typically 32kHz clock or low-power operation, including a real-time clock and an asynchronous independent watchdog.
- **Analog functions:** VREF offers selectable 1.4V and 2.5V internal references, supports ADC operation up to 515ksps, and accepts external references. The comparator provides digital voltage-comparison output, low-power wakeup, timer fault connections, selectable inputs, and an 8-bit reference DAC.
- **Security and CRC:** Features include code and data firewalls and a CRC module supporting CRC16-CCITT and bit reversal.
- **Communication:** Three UART peripherals support configurable parity, baud rates, LIN, FIFOs, and loopback. I2C supports 7-bit and 10-bit addressing, rates up to 1Mbps, DMA, SMBus 3.0, address-match wakeup, and glitch filtering. SPI supports controller and peripheral operation up to 16Mbits/s, programmable frame sizes, DMA, and multiple formats.
- **Watchdogs and timekeeping:** IWDT uses independent power and clock sources and generates a power-on reset when software fails to service it. WWDT supports reset or interrupt generation, selectable periods, sleep stopping, and interval timing. RTC_B provides calendar timekeeping, alarms, periodic interrupts, leap-year correction, and calibration.
- **Timers:** General-purpose and advanced timers provide 16-bit counting, programmable prescalers, synchronization, and peripheral triggering. Additional features include quadrature sensing for general-purpose timers and clock doubling, asymmetric PWM, dead-band insertion, and fault handling for advanced timers.
- **I/O and debugging:** IOMUX controls peripheral selection, signal paths, and shutdown wakeup. Two-wire SWD supports processor and device-state debugging. DEBUGSS adds configurable peripheral behavior during debug, mailbox communication, SWD lockout, and password-authenticated debugging. A read-only FACTORY region stores identification, capabilities, and trim information.

Application guidance recommends nearby 10µF and 0.1µF supply-decoupling capacitors. NRST requires a 47kΩ pullup resistor and 1000pF pulldown capacitor. Open-drain I/O requires an external pullup to output logic high.

The designation “unskilled” work in the United States has reflected occupational tasks, entry requirements, and worker identity. Alba Edwards’s occupational classification system, introduced in 1917, reserved skill categories for manual work and grouped laborers and servants as “unskilled.” Some technically skilled occupations were classified as semiskilled because many workers were women or children. In 1930, 75% of employed African Americans worked in “unskilled” occupations, compared with 20% of native-born white workers and 30% of foreign-born white workers. By the 21st century, classifications commonly relied on education, experience, and job content.

Historically, these occupations included farm labor, factory labor, domestic service, construction, mining, and sanitation. They frequently involved low wages, dangerous conditions, discrimination, and exploitation of enslaved people, immigrants, women, and children. Mechanization and automation reduced agricultural and manufacturing employment, while service work expanded. Digital platforms created gig work and online microtasks, often organized through independent contracting and performance monitoring. Many jobs labeled “unskilled,” including farmwork and direct care, nevertheless required judgment, experience, physical endurance, and interpersonal abilities.

In 2018, more than half of the U.S. workforce held jobs typically requiring a high school education or less, with a median annual wage of $33,473. Workers in retail, food service, care, and warehousing commonly faced unstable schedules, limited benefits, and injury risks. Education alone did not resolve low pay: in 2012, 45.7% of low-wage workers had attended college or held a college degree.

Government regulation, worker organizing, and employer practices improved some jobs. New Deal legislation established wage, working-time, and organizing protections, but excluded several occupational groups. Unions and advocacy organizations secured wage increases and improved conditions, although declining unionization weakened worker bargaining power. Employers including Toyota, Costco, QuikTrip, and In-N-Out demonstrated approaches combining investment in workers with operational changes to improve job quality and productivity.

During COVID-19, nearly 70% of essential workers held jobs categorized as “unskilled.” Many continued working in person for low wages, sometimes without adequate protective equipment or hazard pay. The pandemic highlighted the importance of food production, delivery, cleaning, and care work to economic functioning. Reports from MIT and California’s future-of-work commissions emphasized job quality, rather than automation-driven job loss alone, as a central challenge. The passage concludes by questioning how historically “unskilled” work should be valued and compensated when it is also essential.

T-Tamer is a model-agnostic framework for balancing two objectives, such as accuracy and latency, in cascaded inference. It formulates model routing and stopping as costly exploration over directed acyclic graphs, representing model dependencies, precedence constraints, prediction losses, and inspection costs. A tunable parameter weights the two objectives, and the framework learns its policy independently of sub-model training.

The work distinguishes no-recall policies, which must return the last inspected model’s prediction, from recall-based policies, which can select any previously inspected model. It proves that no-recall policies cannot achieve a constant-factor approximation to an offline oracle’s expected loss, even with two models and bounded distributions. Recall also does not eliminate this offline approximation gap; the proposed recall-based strategy instead targets the optimal online policy.

Using dynamic programming, T-Tamer computes dynamic indices that guide routing and stopping, returning the lowest-loss inspected model. Under the stated distributional assumptions, the strategy achieves online optimality for directed lines, directed trees, and directed lines permitting ordered skips. Preprocessing is polynomial-time, while inference requires constant time per inspected node and linear time overall.

Evaluations cover synthetic data and early-exit vision and language classification workloads. Reported results demonstrate accuracy–latency trade-offs: one vision configuration reduces latency to 45% of its original level with less than 7% accuracy loss, while language-model experiments show latency reductions of up to 90%. Experimental accuracy is measured relative to backbone-model outputs.

The NVIDIA A100 GPU introduces compute, memory, virtualization, and software features for high-performance computing, deep learning, and data analytics.

- **Mixed-precision computing:** The cuSOLVER Tensor Core Accelerated Iterative Refinement Solver supports A100 formats including TF32. Across 37 test problems, TF32 provided the fastest and most robust results among Tensor Core modes, achieving a geometric-mean speedup of 2× over the FP64 solver and up to 4× for large complex matrices.

- **Structured sparsity:** A100 uses a 2:4 sparsity pattern, allowing two nonzero values in each four-entry vector. Sparse Tensor Core instructions skip zero values, doubling compute throughput and halving weight storage and bandwidth requirements. NVIDIA’s process of dense training, pruning, and fine-tuning produced virtually no inference accuracy loss across evaluated networks. Training acceleration without accuracy loss remains an active research area.

- **Compute efficiency:** A100 has 108 streaming multiprocessors, compared with V100’s 80, and third-generation Tensor Cores. Expanded thread-level data sharing reduces instruction counts and register accesses. Separate FP32 and INT32 cores support simultaneous execution.

- **Memory architecture:** A100 includes 40 GB of HBM2 memory delivering 1,555 GB/s bandwidth, a 40 MB L2 cache, and 192 KB of combined L1 cache and shared memory per multiprocessor. Compared with V100, HBM2 bandwidth increases by more than 1.7× and L2 bandwidth by 2.3×. Compute Data Compression provides up to 4× improvements in DRAM and L2 bandwidth and up to 2× greater effective L2 capacity. ECC protects major memory structures.

- **GPU partitioning:** Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) divides an A100 into as many as seven GPU Instances with dedicated compute and memory resources. Isolation supports predictable performance, fault containment, and multi-tenant workloads. GPU Instances can be subdivided into Compute Instances, which support independent execution and Multi Process Server functionality. Migration supports workload consolidation and GPU servicing.

- **Interconnects and reliability:** Third-generation NVLink provides twelve links and 600 GB/s total bandwidth per A100, twice V100’s total. PCIe Gen 4 supplies 31.5 GB/s per direction for x16 connections, while SR-IOV supports virtualization. Enhanced error attribution, isolation, containment, and recovery help prevent faults from affecting unrelated workloads.

- **Additional accelerators:** A100 includes a five-core JPEG decoder, five video decoding units, and an optical flow accelerator supporting motion and stereo disparity estimation. FP16 and FP32 atomic-operation throughput improves by 11× and 2.7×, respectively, over V100.

- **CUDA support:** CUDA 11 supports A100 Tensor Cores, sparsity, MIG, and cache controls. CUDA Graphs reduce repeated launch and dependency overhead. Asynchronous copies transfer data directly from global to shared memory without intermediate register storage, while asynchronous barriers enable overlapping computation and transfers. L2 residency controls prioritize reused data, although cache set-aside functionality is disabled in MIG mode. Cooperative Groups adds asynchronous-copy and reduction capabilities.

- **DGX A100 platform:** DGX A100 combines eight A100 GPUs through six NVSwitches, delivering up to 5 PFLOPS of AI performance and supporting up to 56 isolated GPU Instances. Networking and software support larger deployments, while the NGC registry provides optimized containers, models, and development tools for AI, analytics, and HPC workloads.
