U.S. District Judge Sara Ellis dismissed a lawsuit accusing the College Board and 40 private institutions of tuition price-fixing. Plaintiffs alleged that considering both parents’ finances for students with divorced or separated parents increased tuition by an average of $6,200. Ellis acknowledged inflated prices but found the complaint did not plausibly establish an agreement among defendants.

Microsoft’s fiscal first-quarter 2021 revenue, for the three months ended September 30, 2020, increased 12% year over year to $37.2 billion. Operating income rose 25% to $15.9 billion, net income increased 30% to $13.9 billion, and diluted earnings per share grew 32% to $1.82.

- **Productivity and Business Processes:** Revenue increased 11% to $12.3 billion, supported by Office Commercial and LinkedIn. Office 365 Commercial revenue grew 21%, LinkedIn revenue increased 16%, and Dynamics 365 revenue rose 38%.
- **Intelligent Cloud:** Revenue increased 20% to $13.0 billion, with Azure revenue growing 48%. Segment operating income increased 39%.
- **More Personal Computing:** Revenue increased 6% to $11.8 billion. Gaming revenue grew 22% and Surface revenue increased 37%, while Windows revenue declined 1% and search advertising revenue fell 10%.

Commercial cloud revenue increased 31% to $15.2 billion. Its gross margin reached 71%, primarily reflecting longer estimated useful lives for server and network equipment. This accounting estimate change increased quarterly operating income by $927 million and net income by $763 million, or $0.10 per share.

COVID-19 supported demand for cloud services, Surface, and Gaming as customers worked, learned, and played remotely. Reduced advertising spending hurt Search, while transactional licensing remained weak across all segments.

Operating cash flow totaled $19.3 billion, compared with $13.8 billion a year earlier. At September 30, Microsoft held $138.0 billion in cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments. Total assets were $301.0 billion, liabilities were $177.6 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $123.4 billion.

Microsoft repurchased $5.3 billion of shares under its repurchase program and declared a quarterly dividend of $0.56 per share. It also agreed to acquire ZeniMax Media, Bethesda’s parent company, for $7.5 billion in cash, with closing expected in the second half of fiscal 2021, subject to customary conditions and regulatory review.

The agreement governs software use under California and U.S. federal law, with exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County courts. Invalid provisions leave the remainder enforceable. The U.N. international sales convention is excluded. Exports require regulatory compliance; waivers and amendments require authorized signatures from both parties.

On October 27, 2004, the U.S. District Court for the Middle District of North Carolina granted summary judgment to all defendants in Melissa Jennings’s lawsuit against the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill, soccer coaches, and university officials.

Jennings, a women’s soccer team member from 1996 until her dismissal in 1998, alleged that coaches Anson Dorrance and William Palladino made sexually inappropriate comments and that Dorrance questioned her about her personal life. She asserted claims under Title IX, § 1983, and North Carolina privacy law, including supervisory-liability claims against university officials.

The court concluded that the alleged conduct, considered in context, was not sufficiently severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive to deprive Jennings of educational opportunities. It therefore granted summary judgment on her Title IX and constitutional sexual-harassment claims. Her constitutional privacy claim failed because she was not compelled to disclose personal information, her decision-making was not impeded, and her refusal to answer did not cause her dismissal. Without an underlying constitutional violation, the supervisory-liability claims also failed. The court found that Dorrance’s inquiries did not constitute the egregious intrusion required for a state-law privacy claim.

The court denied Jennings’s motion to strike the defendants’ amended answer and obtain default judgment, finding no evidence of bad faith. It also denied her motion to exclude team-evaluation exhibits, finding them authenticated and admissible as records of regularly conducted activity. A separate order denied the defendants’ motion to submit specified evidence under seal.

The passage describes an event-based data intake and query system for collecting, storing, indexing, and searching machine-generated data from sources such as servers, applications, networks, sensors, and mobile devices.

Machine data is stored as timestamped events, generally preserving underlying raw data for later analysis. A flexible schema defines how information is extracted from events. When applied at search time, this “late-binding schema” allows users to add, modify, or remove field extraction rules without defining all analytical requirements during ingestion. Common field names can support searches across differently formatted data sources.

The system includes forwarders, indexers, and search heads. Forwarders receive data, attach metadata, and route it for processing; they may also parse, transform, or index data. Indexers identify event boundaries, assign timestamps, associate metadata, optionally mask or remove information, and store events. Client-side monitoring components can collect network, application, and device performance information. Deployment options include on-premises, cloud-based, and hybrid environments.

Search heads can access locally managed indexes and externally managed collections called virtual indexes. External Result Provider processes translate queries into formats supported by external systems and return results. These processes support streaming mode for minimally processed, low-latency results, reporting mode for processed results, or mixed operation that can transition from streaming to reporting.

Events may be organized into time-range buckets and distributed across indexers for parallel searching. Storage arrangements distinguish actively written, less frequently accessed, quarantined, and archived data. Replication can support availability and disaster recovery.

Keyword and field-value inverted indexes associate search terms with event references. Event reference arrays can supply event locations and timestamps. Indexers use filters—including partitions, time ranges, hosts, sources, source types, and keywords—to identify matching events, then group and count them according to categorization criteria. Search heads aggregate these groupings for display.

This qualitative study examines information technology and management strategies in Indonesian language education through literature review, observation, descriptive and comparative analysis, and framework development. It identifies 151 Scopus papers as strongly relevant from 1,010 related manuscripts.

Education 4.0 and the COVID-19 pandemic accelerated digital learning, expanding the use of online platforms, mobile learning, and blended approaches. However, teachers faced limited technological proficiency, difficulties sustaining student engagement, shortages of suitable online materials, and challenges assessing speaking and listening remotely. Students encountered unreliable internet, inadequate devices, reduced social interaction, limited real-time language practice, and difficulties maintaining motivation and self-regulation. International responses varied according to infrastructure, cultural approaches to learning, technological resources, and community support.

Automatic Speech Recognition can provide immediate pronunciation feedback and support vocabulary acquisition through contextual practice. Task-based and game-based learning encourage participation, repeated practice, and vocabulary retention. Combining these approaches offers interactive opportunities to develop language skills.

Recommended management strategies include:
- Integrating platforms for synchronous and asynchronous learning.
- Providing ongoing teacher development and language-support tools.
- Facilitating international collaboration and virtual exchanges.
- Investing in cloud infrastructure and mobile learning.
- Using data to improve teaching and technology provision.
- Establishing inclusive policies that address affordability, accessibility, and underserved learners.

Students generally view educational technology positively, but limited digital literacy, unreliable tools, unequal access, and concerns about replacing face-to-face interaction can hinder adoption. The study emphasizes accessible alternatives, teacher support, and collaborative activities. It concludes that technology can enhance language education when implementation considers pedagogy, management, and student needs, supporting rather than simply replacing existing teaching methods.

A randomized, single-blind, placebo-controlled trial evaluated SA58 monoclonal antibody nasal spray as post-exposure prophylaxis against COVID-19 in healthy adult workers exposed to SARS-CoV-2 within 72 hours. Conducted at 21 Beijing construction sites from November 26 to December 9, 2022, the study ended early after COVID-19 restrictions were lifted and participants left the sites.

The full analysis included 1,222 participants; efficacy analysis excluded 99 who tested positive at baseline. Among baseline-negative participants, symptomatic COVID-19 occurred in 7 of 824 SA58 recipients and 14 of 299 placebo recipients. Estimated efficacy was 80.82% against symptomatic COVID-19 (95% CI 52.41%–92.27%) and 61.83% against SARS-CoV-2 infection (95% CI 37.50%–76.69%). All 21 sequenced positive samples were Omicron BF.7. No severe COVID-19 cases or deaths occurred during monitoring.

Adverse events were reported by 25% of SA58 recipients and 22% of placebo recipients. All were Grade 1, with no serious adverse events or adverse events of special interest reported.

Limitations included a smaller-than-planned sample, median follow-up below three days, possible effects of isolation measures, and enrollment predominantly of healthy working-age men. The authors recommend larger studies with longer follow-up and evaluation in high-risk populations. These preliminary findings were published as a preprint not certified by peer review.

California Gov. Gavin Newsom signed SB 53, requiring major AI companies to publicly disclose safety protocols, report critical incidents, and protect employee whistleblowers. The law also initiates CalCompute, a government consortium developing public computing infrastructure for safe AI research, and establishes civil penalties enforceable by the state attorney general.

Authored by State Sen. Scott Wiener, SB 53 emphasizes transparency rather than liability, unlike an earlier bill Newsom vetoed. Anthropic supported the legislation; OpenAI and Meta expressed qualified approval.

Critics warn that state-level regulation could burden startups and reinforce larger companies’ dominance. Supporters counter that the requirements target large-scale developers, with obligations excluding companies below $500 million in annual revenue. Former OpenAI policy researcher Miles Brundage called the law progress but urged stronger penalties, clearer risk thresholds, and robust third-party evaluations.

Kevin Love approached his fourth consecutive NBA Finals with Cleveland recovering from a concussion that left his Game 1 availability uncertain. His season included a broken hand, uneven playoff performances and public disclosure of his longtime struggles with anxiety and panic attacks.

After teammates questioned his absence from a game and practice, Love explained his condition and later detailed it in a Player’s Tribune essay. Despite concerns about backlash, he received thousands of supportive emails and said sharing his experience strengthened his empathy and relationships.

Love, who has received counseling, said he wants neither sympathy nor excuses and views basketball as an escape. Despite persistent criticism and trade rumors since joining Cleveland in 2014, he considers his time with the Cavaliers worthwhile, including winning a championship.

Black Sabbath guitarist Tony Iommi announced his sponsorship of the BIMM Birmingham Scholarship during a May 25 Q&A. Reflecting on his career, he emphasized maintaining motivation and persevering through rejection in the music business.

Researchers at the University of California, Irvine and other institutions developed a satellite-based drought severity index using NASA’s Gravity Recovery and Climate Experiment data. The GRACE-DSI incorporates groundwater storage changes, supplementing assessments commonly based on precipitation. Satellite gravity observations enable consistent regional and global monitoring, including areas lacking ground readings. Comparisons in the continental United States showed significant agreement with other drought indices. The dataset covers 2002–2014, with extensions planned using current and follow-on mission data. The tool aims to improve hydrological drought assessment and support water management.

Tropical Storm Nate, blamed for at least 17 deaths in Central America, was forecast to cross the eastern Yucatan Peninsula Friday evening and approach the northern Gulf Coast Saturday evening, strengthening into a hurricane Saturday night into Sunday.

Pensacola was within the forecast warning cone and likely to be east of landfall, where higher wind gusts, storm surge and tornadoes were possible. Escambia and Santa Rosa counties faced heavy rain Saturday through Sunday, with 3–5 inches expected. Sunday winds were forecast at 35–45 mph in Escambia, gusting to 65 mph, and 15–25 mph in Santa Rosa, gusting to 35 mph. Both counties were under a tropical storm watch.

Local institutions announced closures, cancellations and postponements. The University of West Florida planned to close from noon Saturday through Monday, and Gulf Islands National Seashore closed its public areas. Residents were urged to gather supplies and follow local updates; Santa Rosa County offered limited free sand at designated locations.

The summer box office was dominated by three well-received superhero films: Guardians of the Galaxy Vol. 2, Wonder Woman and Spider-Man: Homecoming. Most other categories produced only one major success, including Despicable Me 3 in animation, Girls Trip in comedy, Annabelle: Creation in horror and Dunkirk in adult drama. King Arthur: Legend of the Sword and Valerian and the City of a Thousand Planets were major failures, while The Mummy, Transformers: The Last Knight and War for the Planet of the Apes underperformed. Six-year-old Ryan’s toy-review channel, Ryan ToysReview, reportedly earned $11 million in 2017, placing him among Forbes’ top 10 highest-paid YouTube stars. Launched in 2015, it has over 10 million subscribers and recorded over eight billion views during Forbes’ tracking year. His parents say the show will continue only while Ryan enjoys it.

The passage describes medical airway-management systems designed to assist rescuers during intubation, including rapid sequence intubation (RSI), and to verify that an endotracheal tube is correctly placed and remains properly positioned.

The systems combine airway and physiological sensors with a patient-monitoring device, processor, memory, and user interface. Sensors may measure oxygen and carbon dioxide concentrations, airflow, oxygen saturation, transthoracic impedance, acoustic signals, ECG, blood pressure, and patient or rescuer positioning. Sensors may be separate or integrated into an airway module connected to manual or mechanical ventilation equipment.

To verify tube placement, the system may detect airway airflow and start a timer during which physiological measurements must confirm that ventilation has reached the lungs. The interval may default to 5–15 seconds or be user-defined. Verification may use end-tidal carbon dioxide thresholds, trends, desired ranges, impedance changes, or acoustic information. Continued monitoring may compare current measurements with initial or dynamically updated baselines to determine whether the tube remains properly placed. Failed verification may trigger context-sensitive alarms and recommended clinical actions.

The system may also identify intubation stages and transitions from changes in gas, physiological, or positioning measurements, then adjust displayed information and guidance accordingly. Functions may include preoxygenation and procedure timers, hypoxemia warnings, patient-positioning feedback, drug-dose calculations based on entered information, and automatic event recording. Some implementations require rescuers to confirm detected stage changes before feedback changes.

The monitoring device may incorporate a defibrillator or communicate with ventilators, tablets, smartphones, wrist-worn devices, or head-mounted displays. Feedback may be visual, audible, or tactile. Connected devices may provide checklists, retrieve patient information, and generate quality-assurance reports documenting tasks, timing, alarms, and physiological data. The described approach is intended to provide context-sensitive guidance while reducing manual display adjustments during patient care.

Quarter Circle Games announced The Peterson Case, a first-person horror game for PlayStation 4, Xbox One, and PC. Set near Roswell after the 1947 UFO incident, it follows Detective Franklin Reinhardt investigating a missing family while encountering an unearthly presence.

A New York Times survey found widespread dissatisfaction among 65 responding federal judges with Supreme Court emergency docket decisions during President Trump’s second term. Forty-seven said the court had used the docket inappropriately, and 48 said lower courts lacked sufficient guidance. Of 54 answering a question about public perception, 42 said the docket had harmed perceptions of the judiciary.

Nearly all roughly 20 emergency rulings concerning Trump administration policies benefited Trump, and at least seven lacked reasoning, the newspaper reported. Respondents included 28 Republican presidential nominees and 37 Democratic presidential nominees. The Times acknowledged respondents might not represent the judiciary; a Volokh Conspiracy critique raised concerns about response bias and oversampling judges likely to oppose the rulings.

Long-short equity strategies combine long positions in stocks expected to appreciate with short positions in stocks expected to decline. They aim to generate returns from both price movements while managing risk and providing diversification.

Common among hedge funds, these strategies often maintain a long bias, such as 130% long exposure and 30% short exposure. Market-neutral strategies instead hold equal dollar amounts of long and short positions. Portfolio construction requires research to identify underpriced and overpriced stocks, and outcomes remain uncertain: either position can move against expectations.

Long-short funds may use leverage and derivatives to enhance returns, increasing complexity and risk. The passage describes these strategies as more suitable for institutional investors than retail investors and emphasizes diversifying across multiple pairs rather than relying on one or two.

Edward Thorp is presented as a pioneer of quantitative investing. His Princeton Newport Partners fund operated from 1969 to 1988 without a losing year, compounding returns at 19.1%.

An illustrative Coca-Cola–Pepsi backtest reported an average gain per trade of 0.45%, annualized returns of 3.8%, market exposure 42% of the time, and maximum drawdown of approximately 11%. It also experienced extended periods of flat or negative performance. The passage notes that low average trade gains encourage leverage, which increases risk, and that trading multiple pairs is capital-intensive.

Zacks Investment Research upgraded Teck Resources from “hold” to “buy,” setting a $25 price target implying 8.84% upside. The stock’s average analyst rating was “Buy,” with a consensus target of $31.18.

Shares opened Thursday at $22.97, giving the company a market capitalization of $13.27 billion. Quarterly earnings of $0.73 per share exceeded the $0.71 consensus estimate. Revenue reached $2.82 billion, surpassing expectations of $2.75 billion and rising 62% year over year. Analysts expected annual earnings of $3.52 per share.

The passage describes using the PGA848 to drive the ADS8860, a 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC, with single-ended or differential input signals. The example uses ±15V input-stage supplies and a 5.3V output-stage supply shared with the ADC to prevent ADC input overload during PGA overdrive. A REF6250 provides the 5V ADC reference; a precision divider and OPA192 buffer establish the PGA848’s 2.5V reference voltage.

Three filters address input EMI/RFI, amplifier bandwidth, and ADC charge kickback. The nominal front-end bandwidth is 318kHz, decreasing to 277kHz at the high end of feedback-resistor tolerance, while maintaining −0.1dB flatness to 41kHz. C0G capacitors are used for low distortion. The OPA192 reference buffer uses dual feedback for stability and provides an 86° phase margin. Changes to reference bypass capacitance require recalculating stability components and verifying more than 60° phase margin.

Supply voltages above 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Recommended PCB practices include symmetrical input paths, closely placed 0.1µF supply bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive and noisy traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, and reduced thermal junctions. Appropriate ESD precautions are required.

The document also provides simulation-tool information, related documentation, update notifications, support resources, and packaging and ordering guidance. TI supplies technical resources “as is”; developers remain responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements.

After three women accused President Trump of sexual assault on television, CNN’s Brian Karem asked Sarah Huckabee Sanders about her own experiences with sexual harassment and empathy for accusers. Sanders declined to discuss her personal history but expressed empathy for anyone sexually harassed.

The study presents a machine learning-assisted inverse design workflow for identifying diammonium organic spacers that give two-dimensional Dion–Jacobson (DJ) perovskites targeted energy level alignments. Its central feature is an interpretable, invertible 12-digit molecular fingerprint encoding conjugated backbones, ammonium groups, heteroatom substitutions, and side chains.

Starting from 21 reported spacers, molecular morphing generated 4,887,100 hypothetical spacers represented by 21,306 fingerprints. Calculations on 3,239 organic spacers supplied training data for models predicting frontier orbital energies. Linear models achieved R² scores of approximately 0.95 for both HOMO and LUMO predictions; LASSO regression was selected for interpretability. The analysis identified conjugation and tethering ammonium groups as major influences on energy levels.

Synthesis feasibility screening combined the availability of neutral molecules in PubChem with a formability score based on five molecular descriptors. The score correctly classified 27 of 29 reported cases. Selected perovskite structures were subsequently evaluated using density functional theory.

Fingerprint-constrained inverse design identified 56 promising candidates: two with type Ib alignment, 12 with type IIa, and 42 with type IIb. The type Ib candidates featured pentacene backbones; type IIa candidates generally required extended conjugation, while type IIb candidates commonly incorporated nitrogen-substituted aromatic rings to lower LUMO energies.

The workflow enables targeted exploration beyond exhaustive molecular enumeration and offers structural design rules for underexplored alignments. Limitations include restricted molecular representation and heuristic synthesis screening that excludes solubility and experimental conditions. Experimental synthesis and energy level characterization were outside the study’s scope and remain necessary to validate the predictions.

The May 24, 2001 collection of Enron-related news covers energy disputes, political developments and industry investment:

Forty-two states reported high flu activity, and 53 children have died this season. The dominant H3N2 strain typically causes more cases, hospitalizations and deaths. A Canadian report found the vaccine 17 percent effective against H3N2, but officials still recommend vaccination to reduce severity. Antivirals should be started promptly. Widespread flu activity continues nationwide except in Oregon and Hawaii.

After federal agents destroyed Diane Monson’s medical marijuana plants in 2002, she and Angel Raich challenged Congress’ authority to prohibit their local, noncommercial cannabis use, which was legal under California law. The government argued that regulating such activity was essential to enforcing its ban on the interstate marijuana market.

The Supreme Court ruled 6–3 for the government, accepting that locally grown medical cannabis could enter the interstate black market. Justice Antonin Scalia separately grounded federal authority in the necessary and proper clause.

Chief Justice William Rehnquist and Justices Sandra Day O’Connor and Clarence Thomas dissented. O’Connor warned that incorporating local activity into broader regulatory schemes removed meaningful limits on congressional commerce power. Thomas argued that the women’s activities were not commerce and that Congress had supplied no evidence establishing the necessity of regulating them.

The ruling disappointed advocates seeking stronger constitutional limits on federal power. A later challenge to the federal health insurance mandate established that Congress’ commerce power did not extend to inactivity, although the mandate survived as a tax. Raich’s subsequent constitutional challenge also failed. Thomas continued questioning expansive commerce authority and later criticized federal marijuana policy as contradictory and unstable.

The University of Minnesota Morris occupies a former Indian boarding school site, where Native American children were taught to abandon their languages and cultures. Bitcoin rose by more than a third to about $9,300, with buy orders accounting for over 92% of market activity. Motley Fool Money discloses advertiser compensation that may influence product placement and coverage, but states that it does not affect ratings.

Karnataka’s Students Achievement Survey found that over 10 lakh government and aided school students in Classes 4–9 need remedial classes, including about 4.5 lakh in Mathematics and Science. Over 36 lakh students from 50,000 schools participated. Teachers have received remedial guidance and will counsel students.

Auckland Airport resumed international screening after police and Aviation Security located a woman involved in a security breach. A knife had been detected during screening, but she continued into the terminal. The shutdown created long queues and a backlog, with at least four flights affected.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for improving occlusion between physical and virtual objects in head-mounted display passthrough visualizations. Passthrough uses external-camera images and a reconstructed 3D environment to render physical surroundings from the user’s eye positions, accounting for camera-eye misalignment and providing parallax.

Depth measurements may be generated from stereo images using GPU-based optical flow or, on resource-limited devices, video-encoder motion vectors. Encoder-derived correspondences may undergo geometric and temporal filtering before producing a point cloud. The system can use these points to deform a mesh approximating the environment’s contours. Rendering then combines the mesh with captured images to produce views for each eye.

Inaccurate depth measurements and smoothed mesh boundaries can cause physical objects to occlude too much or too little of nearby virtual objects. To address this, the system generates instance segmentation masks identifying pixels belonging to particular physical objects, such as people or pets. Each identified object receives a representative depth derived from corresponding portions of the 3D model, using an average depth or the depth of a computed centroid.

To reduce excessive occlusion around object edges, the system may create padded borders around segmentation masks and assign those borders substantially farther depth values. During rendering, it compares the representative depths of segmented objects or their borders with virtual-object depths to determine visibility. Where no segmentation applies, it uses the original model depths. These techniques aim to produce more consistent, visually improved occlusion effects.

The disclosure also describes supporting artificial-reality hardware, network environments, and computer systems, with implementations accommodating different computational capabilities and power budgets.

U.S. stocks rose Monday, with the S&P 500 recording its largest daily gain since April. Fed official William Dudley anticipated another 2017 rate increase. Eurozone industrial output declined, China’s economy slowed, and Japan posted 4% annualized growth. Canada sought environmental provisions in NAFTA while defending its dispute-settlement process. Oil reached a three-week low, and gold fell as U.S.–North Korea tensions eased.

NASA’s Suomi NPP satellite captured an infrared image of the northern lights across northern Canada on Dec. 22. Auroras occur when solar particles interact with Earth’s magnetic field, energizing atmospheric gases that release colored light. Solar storms producing the most magnificent displays peak roughly every 11 years; the 2013 peak was the weakest observed in a century.

The speaker argues that Ryan Smyth should remain an Oiler for his lasting contributions, passion and connection with fans. Edmonton believed its core could succeed in the playoffs and added players, including Peca and Pronger, with a stronger Canadian dollar helping further acquisitions during the season. Despite late-season struggles, the team retained confidence in its ability.

The speaker emphasizes skating and game awareness as strengths shared by Edmonton and Carolina, and anticipates compelling stories involving older players seeking their first championship. He also reflects on the Oilers’ influence on younger players, including Ray Whitney.

Edmonton acquired Dwayne Roloson for his experience, competitiveness, team-oriented attitude and strong save percentage. A study in a low-malaria-transmission area of southern Zambia examined antimalarial drug resistance markers in samples collected through health-center and community surveillance from 2018 to 2023. Of 570 samples tested, 540 were successfully sequenced at one or more loci.

The Pfk13 P441L mutation, a WHO candidate marker of artemisinin partial resistance, occurred in 30 of 501 samples (6%). Its prevalence increased from 0% in 2018 to 7.2% in 2023, peaking at 9.3% in 2022. It was detected at all four participating health centers. Both the overall prevalence and the 2023 prevalence exceeded the WHO’s 5% threshold warranting further investigation and monitoring. The Pfk13 A578S mutation, which is not associated with artemisinin resistance, appeared in three individuals in 2023.

MDR1 Y184F prevalence was 41% and remained stable over time. Wildtype MDR1 N86, associated with possible reduced lumefantrine susceptibility, occurred in all samples. Resistance markers for sulfadoxine-pyrimethamine were highly prevalent.

Limitations included incomplete sequencing across loci, incomplete Pfk13 coverage, and variable sample sizes. The extent of P441L’s association with artemisinin resistance remains uncertain. The authors recommend therapeutic efficacy and ex-vivo studies, whole-genome sequencing, and integration of molecular resistance monitoring into routine national and multinational surveillance.

Nintendo announced Mario Kart Tour, a smartphone app in development, scheduled for release between April 2018 and March 2019. No gameplay details were disclosed. Nintendo has previously released smartphone games including Super Mario Run and Animal Crossing: Pocket Camp.

The Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 describes SD Memory Card interfaces, communication protocols, operating modes, registers, electrical requirements, and performance features. Its contents also cover SPI operation, security-related commands, power management, and mechanical references.

- **Card types and capacity:** Cards may be read/write or read-only. SDSC supports up to 2 GB, SDHC supports more than 2 GB through 32 GB, and SDXC supports more than 32 GB through 2 TB. Capacity includes separate User and Protected Areas; access to the Protected Area requires authentication.
- **Security and compatibility:** Features include content protection, password locking, and write protection. SDIO cards, specified separately, provide I/O functionality with optional memory and retain mechanical, electrical, power, signaling, and software compatibility with SD Memory Cards.
- **Interfaces and speed:** The SD interface uses nine pins and supports single- or four-line data transfer. Default and High Speed modes reach 12.5 and 25 MB/s. UHS-I reaches 104 MB/s using 1.8 V signaling. Version 6.00 introduces FD624, with a maximum bus speed of 624 MB/s. UHS-II-capable hosts must also support the legacy SD interface.
- **Performance features:** Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 specify minimum performance of 2, 4, 6, and 10 MB/s; Class 0 specifies none. Application Performance Classes define minimum random and sequential performance. Cache, self-maintenance, and command queues support performance improvements. Unflushed cached data may be lost when power is removed.
- **Communication and initialization:** Hosts control communication through broadcast or addressed commands. Initialization validates operating conditions, identifies cards, and establishes relative addresses. CMD8 is mandatory before the first ACMD41 when initializing SDHC or SDXC cards. UHS-I voltage switching requires host-card agreement.
- **Data transfer:** Transfers use CRC-protected blocks and support single- and multiple-block operations. CMD7 selects a card, and CMD12 stops transfers. Read interruption or card removal does not destroy stored data, but interruption of programming or erase operations may damage contents.

Tyreek Hill underwent successful surgery to repair a dislocated left knee and multiple torn ligaments, including his ACL, according to agent Drew Rosenhaus. No additional surgery is needed, and Hill aims to return at the start of the 2026 season. He suffered the season-ending injury during Miami’s 27-21 victory Monday night. Coach Mike McDaniel reported encouraging information regarding potential nerve damage. The Dolphins, off to a 1-3 start, must replace Hill’s production, with other receivers, tight ends and running backs potentially taking larger roles.

This study examined factors that attract and retain special education teachers in remote rural districts through 93 completed surveys from three special education cooperatives in the Midwestern United States. Participants identified four main themes: financial incentives, support, job-related conditions, and rural recruitment initiatives.

Financial incentives were recommended by 96% of respondents for attracting teachers and 53% for retaining them. Suggestions included higher salaries, improved health insurance, college tuition assistance, loan forgiveness, housing benefits, and sign-on bonuses. Support from administrators, colleagues, and communities was identified by 70% as important for retention and 31% for recruitment.

Participants also recommended reducing paperwork and caseloads, providing relevant professional development and resources, and improving work-life balance. Rural initiatives included Grow Your Own programs and career fairs hosted by rural teachers.

Statistical analyses found that greater perceived support and job satisfaction were associated with plans to remain, while more experienced teachers reported less support. These associations do not establish causation.

The authors recommend combining financial incentives with supportive leadership, collaboration, improved working conditions, and locally focused recruitment. The MSPM0G3519, MSPM0G3518, MSPM0G1519, and MSPM0G1518 documentation describes peripheral capabilities, implementation requirements, development resources, and packaging information.

- **Analog functions:** The temperature sensor produces a voltage proportional to device temperature and connects internally to an ADC channel. Factory calibration supports temperature estimation. VREF provides selectable 1.4-V and 2.5-V internal references or an external reference and requires decoupling. Comparators support low-power wakeup and timer fault handling. The buffered DAC offers 8-bit or 12-bit resolution, offset self-calibration, FIFO, DMA, and hardware triggering. DAC_OUT uses PA15; external signals on that pin are not recommended while DAC_OUT is enabled.
- **Security and computation:** Features include AES-128/256 hardware acceleration, code and data firewalls, secure storage for up to four AES keys, and 16-bit and 32-bit CRC. The TRNG generates 32-bit random numbers for use as a source to a deterministic random number generator. MATHACL accelerates 32-bit mathematical operations to reduce CPU workload.
- **Communications:** UART supports configurable parity, baud rates, LIN, FIFOs, and loopback. I2C supports 7-bit and 10-bit addressing, rates up to 1 Mbit/s, DMA, SMBus 3.0, filtering, and address-match wakeup. SPI supports controller and peripheral operation at rates up to 32 Mbit/s, with rates above 16 Mbit/s requiring HSIO pins. CAN supports CAN2.0A, CAN2.0B, and CAN-FD at up to 5 Mbit/s.
- **Timing and supervision:** The low-frequency subsystem includes RTC_B and an independent watchdog. RTC functions include calendar tracking, alarms, periodic interrupts, and calibration. The independent watchdog generates a power-on reset if software fails to service it; the windowed watchdog can generate a reset or interrupt. General-purpose and advanced timers support synchronization and peripheral triggering; advanced timers also provide complementary PWM, dead-band insertion, and fault handling.
- **Configuration and programming:** IOMUX selects pin functions and controls input, output, and shutdown wakeup behavior. A two-wire SWD interface provides debugging. The UART/I2C bootstrap loader supports programming and configuration, uses a 256-bit user-defined password, and can be disabled. Read-only factory memory stores identification, capability, revision, and trim information.
- **Hardware implementation:** TI recommends nearby 10-µF and 0.1-µF supply-decoupling capacitors and a 47-kΩ pullup with a 10-nF pulldown capacitor on NRST. VCORE requires a nearby 0.47-µF capacitor and must not connect to other circuits. SYSOSC frequency correction requires a specified external 100-kΩ precision resistor. Open-drain outputs require pullups to drive high.
- **Support and qualification:** Resources include development boards, SDKs, configuration tools, training, IDEs, and support forums. MSP-prefixed devices are qualified production devices; X-prefixed devices are experimental and not recommended for production. The April 2025 revision updates specifications and peripheral descriptions. Packaging guidance addresses thermal-pad soldering and assembly considerations. TI emphasizes ESD precautions and assigns customers responsibility for component selection, application validation, testing, and compliance.

Thomas H. Fisher appealed a summary judgment favoring Homer P. Hargrave, a partner of Merrill Lynch, Pierce, Fenner & Beane. Fisher sought an accounting for $6,500 paid to Fuller, Rodney & Co. in commodity transactions, arguing that Merrill Lynch or its predecessors had succeeded to that firm’s business and assumed its liabilities.

Affidavits based on personal knowledge and the firms’ written agreement showed that Merrill Lynch’s predecessors accepted only selected customer accounts with customer consent and assumed no liability for accounts not transferred. Fisher’s account was not transferred. The affidavits also denied any merger, consolidation, or general assumption of Fuller, Rodney & Co.’s liabilities.

The appellate court found that Fisher’s opposing affidavit relied on information, belief, speculation, and conclusions rather than competent evidence, leaving no factual issue requiring trial. Although Fisher claimed the trial court denied discovery, the record showed neither that he presented a discovery motion for a ruling nor that the court denied one.

The court held that the accounting action fell within the Civil Practice Act’s summary-judgment provisions. It also rejected Fisher’s argument that assuming one office lease and admitting two former Fuller, Rodney & Co. partners imposed liability for the former firm’s obligations. The decree granting summary judgment to Hargrave was affirmed.

For a 95-square-meter home meeting the urban residential standard for a four-person household, commutes exceeding 52 minutes reached the insomnia cutoff. Researchers suggested that housing choices and supply accounting for location and size could improve commuters’ sleep health and reduce sleep-related economic losses.

A proper one-on-one soccer defensive stance helps defenders stay goal side, react quickly, slow or redirect opponents, and prepare to tackle. Defenders should place one foot forward and one back, balance on the balls of both feet, bend their knees slightly, and keep their arms somewhat out with elbows bent. On the right side of the field, the left foot generally leads; on the left, the right foot leads, encouraging attackers toward the sideline. In the center, the lead foot depends on play. Training should progress from slow movements without a ball to faster ball-carrying drills, emphasizing positioning and stance adjustments. Defenders must not use their arms to impede opponents.

Iso is a downhill running play common in I-formation and traditional pro-style offenses. It uses a fullback isolated against a linebacker, supported by base blocks and double teams, to move the ball vertically as quickly as possible.

Its strengths are quick downhill movement, simple instruction, and consistent yardage when supported by a powerful tailback and offensive linemen capable of sustaining one-on-one blocks. Its main weakness is personnel dependence: smaller, weaker linemen may struggle, and the fullback must handle a linebacker in the running lane.

Blocking assignments vary against 3-4 and 4-3 defenses, but the tailback follows the fullback and runs toward his blocking leverage. Variations include shotgun Iso, which gives spread offenses a downhill run without reading a defender and was often paired with an RPO at Baylor, and weakside Iso, which can offer more favorable double-team angles.

Its mobile-first, cloud-first strategy focused on three priorities: reinventing productivity and business processes, building an intelligent cloud platform, and creating more personal computing. Beginning in fiscal 2016, Microsoft reported results through three segments:
- **Productivity and Business Processes:** Office Commercial, Office Consumer, and Dynamics business solutions.
- **Intelligent Cloud:** Server products, Azure, and enterprise support and consulting services.
- **More Personal Computing:** Windows, devices, gaming, and search advertising.

Microsoft emphasized Office 365 subscriptions, Azure’s public and hybrid cloud capabilities, and Windows 10 as a platform spanning multiple device categories. It distributed products through equipment manufacturers, distributors, resellers, online channels, and Microsoft stores, offering licensing programs for organizations of different sizes. No individual customer accounted for more than 10% of revenue in fiscal 2016, 2015, or 2014.

Research and development spending totaled $12.0 billion in fiscal 2016, representing 14% of revenue. Microsoft held more than 61,000 issued U.S. and international patents, with over 35,000 pending.

As of June 30, 2016, Microsoft employed approximately 114,000 full-time workers, including 63,000 in the United States. Restructuring eliminated approximately 7,400 positions during fiscal 2016, primarily in phone hardware. Further plans included eliminating 1,850 positions announced in May 2016 and approximately 2,850 additional roles, with completion expected by the end of fiscal 2017. Microsoft also announced the sale of its entry-level feature phone business.

In June 2016, Microsoft announced an approximately $26.2 billion acquisition of LinkedIn. Its phone business incurred a $480 million intangible-asset impairment charge in fiscal 2016, following substantial goodwill and intangible-asset impairments in fiscal 2015.

The study reviews eight leadership models in education, examining their benefits, limitations and practical challenges:

- **Administrative/managerial leadership** provides clear structures, responsibilities and rules, but rigidity can restrict innovation, creativity and adaptability.
- **Instructional leadership** prioritizes teaching, learning, shared goals and supportive environments. Its limitations include top-down control, principals’ knowledge gaps and insufficient attention to student well-being and other school activities.
- **Transformational leadership** promotes shared vision, innovation, individualized support and professional development. However, efforts to change teachers’ attitudes can become authoritarian.
- **Distributed leadership** shares leadership responsibilities across the school community, strengthening collaboration, teacher engagement and learning outcomes. Challenges include conflicts, communication difficulties and uneven willingness or ability to assume leadership roles.
- **Transactional leadership** uses rewards and exchanges to secure cooperation and improve performance. It can undermine morale, teamwork, innovation and long-term development.
- **Ethical leadership** emphasizes fairness, honesty, accountability and trust. Differences between leaders’ values and those of the school community can cause conflict, while efforts to establish common ethics may overshadow professional development needs.
- **Contingent leadership** adapts leadership practices to particular circumstances, requiring continual assessment and flexible responses, especially during crises.
- **Participative leadership** involves school community members in decisions, supporting trust, satisfaction, creativity and shared responsibility. Potential drawbacks include slower decisions, conflict and disclosure of sensitive information.

The study concludes that no single model adequately addresses changing educational demands. It recommends combining complementary strengths: managerial structure, transformational innovation, distributed and participative collaboration, ethical integrity, situational adaptability and transactional tools for daily operations. This integrated approach aims to improve school effectiveness and responsiveness to community needs.

The study investigates whether exchange bias in incoherent RuO₂/Fe heterostructures reflects intrinsic antiferromagnetic or altermagnetic ordering in RuO₂. Researchers combined magnetometry, neutron diffraction and reflectometry, atom probe tomography, electron microscopy, and spectroscopy to examine magnetic behavior and interfacial chemistry.

Fe-based heterostructures exhibited exchange bias below approximately 50 K, with its direction dependent on field-cooling history. Polarized neutron diffraction detected no compensated magnetic ordering in sputtered RuO₂ films, establishing an upper detection limit of 0.01 μB per Ru atom. Neutron reflectometry instead identified canted, uncompensated interfacial moments whose orientations changed with magnetic-field history.

Chemical and structural measurements revealed an oxidized reaction layer containing magnetite (Fe₃O₄), reduced Ru, and an Fe concentration gradient extending into RuO₂. These findings support interfacial magnetic coupling and moment pinning as the origin of exchange bias. The precise coupling mechanism remains uncertain; possible contributions include a magnetite transition and spin-glass behavior.

Control heterostructures using Ni instead of Fe showed no exchange bias down to 5 K. Fe/Ru bilayers without RuO₂ exhibited weaker exchange bias, attributed to oxidation through the Ru cap. Time-dependent magnetization measurements also supported different oxidation behavior in Fe- and Ni-based structures.

The authors conclude that exchange bias in these RuO₂/Fe structures arises from chemically formed magnetic interfaces rather than intrinsic RuO₂ ordering. Exchange bias alone therefore does not establish antiferromagnetism or altermagnetism in RuO₂, although the findings do not exclude altermagnetism under other conditions.

The SD Physical Layer Simplified Specification Version 6.00 defines card capacities, interfaces, communication protocols, initialization, data operations, and protection features. “Shall” and “will” indicate mandatory requirements, “should” recommendations, and “may” optional features.

- **Card types and capacities:** Cards may be read/write or read-only, with standard, miniSD, and microSD form factors. SDSC supports up to 2 GB; SDHC supports more than 2 GB through 32 GB; SDXC supports more than 32 GB through 2 TB. Hosts supporting higher-capacity categories must also support lower-capacity cards. Total capacity includes the User Area and authenticated Protected Area.

- **Voltage and performance:** High-voltage cards operate at 2.7–3.6 V; UHS-II also uses a 1.70–1.95 V supply. Default and High Speed modes provide up to 12.5 and 25 MB/s. UHS-I supports up to 104 MB/s using 1.8 V signaling and a four-bit bus, applies to SDHC and SDXC, and is unavailable in SPI mode. Version 6.00 introduces FD624, with a maximum bus speed of 624 MB/s. Speed Classes 2, 4, 6, and 10 specify corresponding minimum MB/s performance; Class 0 specifies none.

- **Communication and initialization:** The host controls communication through broadcast or addressed commands. Commands and responses use the CMD line, while data transfers occur in CRC-protected blocks. Initialization includes resetting cards, checking operating voltage, determining capacity support, obtaining identification information, and assigning relative addresses. CMD8 must precede the first ACMD41 when initializing SDHC or SDXC. UHS-I voltage switching requires negotiation and CMD11; returning from 1.8 V to 3.3 V signaling requires a power cycle. UHS-II initialization includes physical-interface setup, device initialization, enumeration, configuration, and SD command transport initialization.

- **Data operations:** Cards support single- and multiple-block reads and writes. Multiple-block writing and pre-erased block settings can improve write performance. DAT0 indicates busy status during programming and erase operations. Read interruption or card removal during reading does not damage contents, but resetting during programming may destroy data. Erase operations use start-address, end-address, and execution commands. Optional DISCARD and Full User Area Logical Erase are available for SDHC and SDXC outside SPI mode.

- **Additional performance features:** Application Performance Classes specify minimum random and sequential performance. Cache may improve performance but risks data loss if not flushed before power removal. Self Maintenance supports background data management. Command Queue permits task submission during transfers, with either reordered or sequential execution.

- **Protection:** Protection methods include a host-enforced mechanical switch, internal write protection, and password locking through CMD42. Passwords persist across power cycles, and locked cards permit initialization and status operations but not data access. Optional Card Ownership Protection adds a Force Erase Password. Setting it disables ordinary Force Erase and password clearing, requires COP Unlock after power-on or reset, and permits password-controlled FEP Force Erase. Password or command errors are reported through card status.

The lecture connects orthonormal expansions in infinite-dimensional spaces with digital communication and pulse-amplitude modulation (PAM).

Orthonormal expansions approximate vectors through successive projections, with the residual orthogonal to the expansion functions. Completeness determines whether the expansion recovers the entire vector. For L2 functions, the Schwarz inequality ensures finite inner products. Normalized Fourier-series functions provide an example, while prolate spheroidal functions address energy concentration within specified time and frequency intervals. Vector notation simplifies these representations but can obscure convergence issues.

Communication systems are organized into layers: sources become binary data, discrete encoding produces symbols, and modulation converts symbols into transmitted waveforms. Separating source processing from channel transmission reduces the number of specialized devices required. The lecture distinguishes symbols, which are alphabet elements, from signals, which have numerical values and distances.

A simple modulation scheme maps binary digits to +1 and −1 and forms a waveform from weighted, shifted sinc pulses. Ideal sinc pulses are impractical because they extend indefinitely and decay slowly. Timing recovery allows propagation delay to be treated separately, while attenuation is handled through link budgets and signal-to-noise considerations.

PAM generalizes this example by using real-valued signal constellations and an alternative pulse shape. Standard PAM uses equally spaced signals centered around zero. For M equiprobable signals separated by distance d, the mean signal energy is d²(M²−1)/12. Encoding b bits per signal requires M = 2ᵇ, so increasing bits per signal rapidly increases energy requirements when spacing is maintained to limit noise-induced errors.

The transmitted waveform is a sum of shifted pulses weighted by signal values. A receiver filters this waveform and samples it. Ignoring noise, transmitter and receiver filters combine into a single response, g(t). Exact recovery without intersymbol interference requires g(0) = 1 and g(kT) = 0 for every nonzero integer k. This ideal Nyquist condition ensures each sample contains only its intended signal value.

The lecture derives a frequency-domain Nyquist criterion using aliasing. Sinc pulses satisfy the criterion at the minimum bandwidth, 1/(2T), but improved time decay requires additional bandwidth. Suitable band-edge symmetry permits smoother frequency responses while preserving zero intersymbol interference. Raised-cosine filters provide a practical example, trading excess bandwidth for faster pulse decay.

The passage describes methods and apparatus for improving binaural sound localization during electronic communication, gaming, and augmented or virtual reality experiences. It addresses difficulties in localizing sounds at near-field distances, generally less than one meter, where head-related transfer functions (HRTFs) can vary significantly, require intensive processing, and produce unreliable localization.

The proposed methods process sound to coordinates behind or near a sound source rather than precisely at its location. For a nearby image or device, far-field HRTFs can position sound behind the source along a line extending from the listener’s head through the source. Visual associations and directional cues can then cause the listener to perceive the sound as originating from the source. Sound may be delivered through headphones or other wearable devices even when the apparent source emits no sound.

Additional techniques include:
- Positioning sound before, behind, or adjacent to the source’s direction.
- Adjusting volume to correspond to the source’s apparent distance rather than the processing coordinates.
- Varying processing distances and gathering listener feedback to improve localization.
- Updating HRTFs as the listener’s head or the electronic device moves.
- Processing multiple voices separately so they appear to originate from their corresponding displayed images.

The passage also describes switching between externally localized binaural sound and internally localized mono or stereo sound in response to detected actions or device states. Triggers include device rotation, head orientation, gaze, facial detection, sensor obstruction, lighting changes, listener distance, headphone connection, and battery status. These controls allow listeners to change audio presentation quickly, maintain localization during movement, identify devices producing alerts, or conserve battery power by stopping binaural processing.

Localization accuracy varies with factors including sound type, source visibility, distance, surrounding noise, and listener sensitivity.

The paper develops a Bayesian model of implicature comprehension grounded in relevance theory and implements it in ProbLog. It focuses on how audiences infer speakers’ intended meanings from utterances, contextual knowledge, and expectations of relevance.

Explicatures are propositions derived by contextually developing an utterance’s logical form, including reference resolution and enrichment. Implicatures are implicitly communicated premises and conclusions not obtained through this development. In the central example, Mary responds to an offer of coffee by saying she does not want energizing drinks. Understanding her refusal requires the contextual premise that coffee is energizing.

Relevance theory describes cognition as seeking positive cognitive effects while limiting processing effort. Overt communication conveys a presumption of optimal relevance: it should warrant the audience’s attention and be as relevant as the communicator’s abilities and preferences permit. Audiences consider interpretations in order of accessibility and accept the first that satisfies their relevance expectations. Explicatures, contextual premises, and implicated conclusions develop through interconnected, parallel adjustments rather than a strictly sequential process.

The paper distinguishes strongly and weakly communicated implicatures by degrees of manifestness, which combines information’s accessibility and likelihood of acceptance as true. Specific relevance expectations can support strong implicatures, while less specific expectations may support numerous weak implicatures or interpretation through explicatures alone.

Unlike standard Rational Speech Act approaches involving literal speakers or listeners, the proposed model concentrates on relevance-guided comprehension. It represents encyclopaedic knowledge as probabilistic graphs, links expressions to concepts through probabilistic inference rules, and models dependencies between explicatures and implicatures using a Bayesian network. Relevance expectations are represented as queries about potential cognitive effects.

The authors propose measuring utterance utility through Kullback–Leibler divergence between an audience’s prior and posterior probabilities for communicated assumptions. Comparisons among five manually constructed interpretations illustrate how contextual knowledge and relevance expectations affect interpretation. Additional knowledge may support useful inferences, introduce unnecessary processing costs, or become useful when expectations change. When interpretations have equal divergence measures, the model uses the size of their Herbrand bases as an indicator of processing effort.

The resulting optimization procedure excludes interpretations that fail relevance expectations, prefers the smaller Herbrand base when divergence measures are equal, and then selects the remaining interpretation with the highest divergence measure. The authors present this as an “as-if” optimization model capable of generating quantitative predictions for investigating the relevance-theoretic comprehension heuristic.

The model evaluates manually supplied hypotheses rather than generating them and focuses on audiences rather than speakers. Proposed extensions include speakers’ assessments of others’ relevance expectations, higher-level explicatures, irony, quotation, and reported speech and thought.

Researchers combined 102 medical imaging datasets to train ResNet-18, ResNet-50 and VGG16 neural networks to classify CT, MRI, PET and X-ray images across body locations. The study describes a 4.5-million-image dataset, although image totals differ between sections. Entire datasets were assigned to training, validation or testing to prevent data leakage and assess generalisation. Three-dimensional scans were processed as individual two-dimensional slices, resized and normalised.

After 10 training epochs, ResNet-18 achieved the highest test accuracy, at 96.00%, with 86.17% balanced accuracy. ResNet-50 achieved 95.60% accuracy and VGG16 achieved 94.58%. Performance was strong for CT, MRI and PET, but weaker for some bone X-ray datasets: ResNet-18 achieved 28% accuracy on MURA and 62% on the Osteoarthritis Initiative dataset. The authors identify broader X-ray coverage as an area for improvement.

The study suggests potential applications in large imaging repositories and healthcare institutions, with future work extending classification to complete three-dimensional scans. The code is openly available. This preprint has not been peer reviewed and should not guide clinical practice.

Its one-year limited warranty applies to the original purchaser and excludes third-party software and specified forms of damage or misuse. Remedies may include repair, replacement, or refund. Software is supplied without warranties, with liability limitations, and is not intended for high-risk applications. The passage presents educational pacifism as a moral rejection of educational practices that harm students, even when those practices pursue beneficial outcomes. Harm is defined as negatively affecting a person’s important interests. The author argues that mass formal schooling causes significant, often normalized harm through hierarchical, authoritarian, and coercive practices.

The passage distinguishes personal harm, such as bullying and verbal abuse, from systemic harm, which it describes as more pervasive and less readily recognized. Systemic harm comprises three categories:
- **Structural harm:** authoritarian relationships, discriminatory practices, and coercion through rewards and punishments that undermine students’ motivation, engagement, and expression.
- **Objective harm:** schooling structures that reinforce economic inequality and prepare students for subordinate roles.
- **Symbolic harm:** curricula, testing, ranking, surveillance, and institutional communication that normalize domination, conformity, and dependence.

Drawing on Kant’s principle that people must not be treated merely as means, educational pacifism holds that harming innocent students is unjust. Most students are innocent in the relevant sense because they are not unjustly harming or threatening others. Their protection against harm does not depend on whether they qualify as persons. The author distinguishes harmful control from legitimate guidance and argues that peaceful alternatives mean mass formal schooling cannot be defended as a last resort. However, the argument does not claim that all schooling is inherently harmful or should be abolished.

The author identifies substantial alignment between educational pacifism and Montessori’s philosophy. Montessori criticized coercion, competition, forced obedience, and suppression of children’s natural activity. She understood lasting peace as more than the absence of violence and connected peaceful societies with children’s freedom, harmonious activity, and development. Her educational approach sought both individual liberation and social reform.

The passage argues that contemporary Montessori educators should reject educational harm, respect students’ agency, and maintain nonharmful guidance and structure. It also highlights concerns about weak implementation, testing, timetabling, coercion, and socioeconomic or racial segregation in Montessori schools. The author concludes that Montessori education can provide a peaceful alternative only when its practices consistently protect students from harm and make that alternative available as effectively, justly, and widely as possible.

Education researchers express cautious optimism about rebuilding federal research capacity after deep Trump administration cuts. Following lawsuits over canceled contracts, the Education Department said it planned to reinstate 20 research contracts, while 10 regional education labs can restart work for the remainder of their federal contract.

The department is seeking public input on modernizing the Institute of Education Sciences (IES), and researcher Amber Northern is advising on its reform. Hiring for at least eight assessment positions at the National Center for Education Statistics (NCES) and planned survey updates have also encouraged researchers. The administration says it supports a national education research entity providing useful, high-quality data.

Significant concerns remain. DOGE reduced NCES staffing from about 100 employees to three, and researchers warn that shortages threaten data quality and research progress. A new requirement to collect five years of college admissions data adds pressure. Cuts to National Assessment of Educational Progress reporting could make results less useful, while reductions in supporting data operations could compromise future tests.

Some researchers see opportunities to make federal research programs more effective, but uncertainty over funding, staffing and the administration’s plans continues to affect the field.

Russ Tedrake introduces MIT’s Underactuated Robotics course, which examines how robots can exploit their natural dynamics rather than override them with strong actuation and conservative control. Prerequisites include differential equations and linear algebra; MATLAB familiarity is helpful, but prior robotics coursework is not assumed.

The lecture contrasts Honda’s ASIMO, whose conservative walking uses substantial energy, with passive dynamic walkers that descend ramps using gravity alone. Examples involving bird flight, perching aircraft, and fish exploiting water vortices illustrate the importance of dynamics for efficiency and maneuverability.

For systems whose accelerations depend linearly on control inputs, full actuation means the input mapping has rank equal to the number of configuration coordinates. Underactuation means control inputs cannot produce acceleration in every direction. Fully actuated systems can use feedback linearization to cancel nonlinear dynamics and impose simpler behavior, subject to limitations such as available torque. Underactuated systems require reasoning about their nonlinear dynamics.

Using a two-link arm, Tedrake demonstrates how kinematics, kinetic and potential energy, and Lagrangian mechanics yield equations of motion. He introduces the manipulator equations, including inertia, Coriolis, gravity, and input-mapping terms. With motors at both joints, the arm is fully actuated. Removing the shoulder motor creates the Acrobot, which can still swing upward through appropriately controlled elbow torque but requires a more difficult control strategy.

Walking, jumping, flying, and some manipulation tasks involve underactuation. For example, internal joint motions cannot change a jumping robot’s center-of-mass trajectory while airborne when aerodynamic forces are ignored.

The course progresses from pendulums, cart-pole systems, and the Acrobot to walking robots, higher-dimensional systems, uncertainty, and unknown models. Its computational methods include optimal control, dynamic programming, policy search, numerical optimization, motion planning, and reinforcement learning, with new tools repeatedly tested on simpler systems.

Metagenomic binning groups DNA fragments by genome of origin. Existing methods typically generate deterministic embeddings from k-mer profiles or raw sequences. These representations face ambiguity when sequences occur in multiple genomes or when distinct sequences have similar k-mer profiles. Lightweight k-mer approaches can achieve performance comparable to genome foundation models with substantially lower computational costs.

The passage introduces UNCERTAINGEN, a probabilistic embedding framework that maps DNA fragments to distributions rather than fixed points. These distributions encode uncertainty associated with shared sequences and ambiguous k-mer representations. Its contrastive-learning formulation derives non-Euclidean comparisons from a probability distribution over embedding space and provides closed-form expected pairwise likelihoods for scalable optimization.

The authors provide theoretical results on embedding distinguishability, showing that variable covariance expands modeling capacity, and report improvements over deterministic k-mer and language-model embeddings on real metagenomic datasets.

The approach builds on lightweight, self-supervised methods that split sequences into halves to create positive pairs and sample segments from different sequences as negative pairs. A shared neural network embeds their k-mer profiles, learning representations intended to preserve genome-related cluster structure while modeling uncertainty.

Tor developer Nick Mathewson explains the network’s motivations, architecture, limitations, and research priorities. Tor uses volunteer-operated relays to support anonymous communication for individuals, researchers, companies, and law enforcement, while also being used for criminal activity. Mathewson argues that privacy enables freer communication and that restricting security because criminals use it would undermine effective protection.

Anonymity means preventing observers from linking participants to activities, rather than concealing all online activity. Tor prioritizes usability for web browsing and interactive protocols. Its low-latency design does not prevent attackers observing both ends of a connection from correlating traffic timing and volume. A large, diverse user population is therefore important, alongside efforts to reduce the likelihood that attackers observe both ends.

Tor routes TCP stream contents through circuits of relays, negotiating separate symmetric keys and applying layered encryption. This distributes trust rather than relying on a single intermediary. Multiple directory authorities vote on relay information and publish signed consensus documents, helping clients use a common network view while limiting manipulation.

Network anonymity alone does not prevent applications from revealing identity. Browsers can expose identifying information through fonts, window dimensions, cookies, and caches. Unencrypted application traffic can also be observed or modified by hostile exit relays, making end-to-end encryption important.

Abuse creates operational challenges, particularly when websites block Tor exit addresses to deter disruptive behavior. Restricting exit ports does not eliminate abuse. Potential alternatives to broad IP blocking include unlinkable account creation and anonymously usable credentials that can be revoked.

Hidden services aim to conceal a server’s location while enabling encrypted communication through Tor. Their design uses public keys, directory information, and relay paths. Proposed key-blinding changes would address enumeration attacks against service directories.

Other threats include traffic tagging, denial-of-service attacks, and cryptographic implementation errors. Censorship resistance relies on unlisted bridge relays and pluggable traffic transformations, which require ongoing adaptation.

Future priorities include stronger cryptography, redesigned hidden services, improved path selection and congestion control, greater scalability, and better-supported defenses against traffic analysis. Mathewson emphasizes that Tor remains a work in progress and should not be the sole protection when users’ lives or freedom are at stake.

Saving a penalty kick is a demanding goalkeeper task, with a save probability generally below 15%. Dedicated training should combine knowledge of the rules, psychological preparation, physical technique, observation, and research.

Under Law 14, penalty kicks are taken from a stationary ball on the penalty mark, 12 yards from goal. The goalkeeper must face the kicker between the posts and keep at least part of one foot touching, in line with, or behind the goal-line before the kick. Unfair distraction is prohibited. A goalkeeper violation that prevents a goal requires a retake; other outcomes determine whether a retake is necessary. Violations resulting in retakes bring a warning for the first offense and cautions thereafter.

Coaches should provide consistent encouragement, make clear that goalkeepers are not expected to save well-placed penalties, and prevent teammates from blaming them. Preparation should include regular and individual practice, suitable equipment, and training in reactions, jumping, diving, and footwork.

The passage favors “read and react” over guessing, particularly for younger players. Goalkeepers should study kickers’ tendencies and identify useful cues, including their gaze, approach, run-up, plant foot, hips, body lean, and dominant foot. Observation during practices, live matches, and videos can develop these skills. At advanced levels, coaches and goalkeepers should jointly decide whether reacting or guessing is appropriate.

Mental preparation includes visualization, positive self-talk, consistent pre-shot routines, controlled breathing, and attention to the present. Goalkeepers should remain composed, avoid reacting prematurely to feints or stutter runs, and commit to their response. They should attempt to catch the ball or direct it out of play or away from danger.

Preparation must also cover what happens after the kick. Goalkeepers should immediately respond to rebounds, organize defenders for subsequent restarts, or distribute the ball after securing possession. Teammates should cover opponents and provide outlets rather than celebrate while play remains live. At higher levels, updated records of opponents’ penalty-taking patterns can inform decisions, although kickers may change their techniques.

This study developed a world model-based reinforcement learning framework for autonomous navigation during mechanical thrombectomy (MT), aiming to support a single agent across multiple tasks and patient vasculatures. Limited access to MT and treatment delays motivate research into robotic assistance and autonomous navigation.

Researchers divided first-phase MT navigation into five tasks and compared the model-based TD-MPC2 algorithm with model-free Soft Actor-Critic (SAC). Training and testing used simulated guidewire and catheter navigation across ten patient-specific vascular anatomies. Agents received device-position and target coordinates without visual information about vessel geometry. Data from separately trained single-task SAC agents initialized replay buffers for multi-task training.

TD-MPC2 achieved a mean multi-task success rate of 65%, compared with 37% for SAC (p < 0.001). Its reported mean path ratio was 73%, versus 47% for SAC, while mean procedure time increased from 8.2 to 15.2 seconds. TD-MPC2 significantly improved success rates in three tasks, but left-sided navigation remained challenging. Single-task SAC agents achieved success rates of 82–100%, demonstrating stronger performance when specialized.

The findings support the feasibility of world models for multi-task autonomous MT navigation, but performance remains insufficient for clinical deployment. Limitations include incomplete task success, longer procedures, reliance on pre-existing training data, and scalability constraints associated with online planning. Proposed future work includes broader datasets, improved planning efficiency, more detailed simulations incorporating contact forces and vessel motion, evaluation on unseen vasculatures, and transition to in vitro testing.

The Household Sewing Machines—Global Market Status and Trend Report 2013–2023 covers global and regional market data for 2013–2017 and forecasts for 2018–2023. It examines production, demand, revenue, pricing, profitability, market trends, growth drivers and challenges.
