The London breakout strategy is a forex day trading approach that trades breaks above or below the Asian session’s trading range, usually within the first three hours of the London session. Traders take long positions on upward breakouts and short positions on downward breakouts, seeking to exploit London’s liquidity and volatility.

The range can be defined using the Asian session’s highest and lowest prices or its highest and lowest opening/closing prices, excluding candle wicks. Breakouts may also occur during the preceding Frankfurt opening hour.

Custom London breakout indicators provide entry, stop-loss, and take-profit levels. Some incorporate false breakouts, and their signals can be used to automate trading.

The passage’s EUR/USD backtests showed losses when buying breakouts above the range high. Buying breaks below the range low performed better, but average gains remained near zero. The authors conclude that additional parameters or risk management are needed and remain skeptical of the strategy’s performance.

A Nigerian bank support worker warned that scammers at ATMs ask people to receive transfers and withdraw cash, using stolen phones or hacked bank accounts. Recipients risk frozen accounts, flagged BVNs and arrest. The worker described two cases: an 18-year-old forced at gunpoint to withdraw 40,000 naira, and an adult who unknowingly helped withdraw 50,000 naira and subsequently faced an arrest notice. The banker urged people to refuse requests to receive transfers and withdraw money for others at ATMs.

This study evaluated the maturity of healthcare AI publications from 2019–2021 using a BERT-based classifier and manual annotation. Maturity was assessed by whether a proposed model’s output could directly and actionably affect patient care. Publications were examined across medical specialties, geographic locations, data types, and model types.

The authors reported that approximately 5% of publications described mature models. Reported annual maturity rates were 6.01% in 2019, 7.7% in 2020, and 1.81% in 2021. Radiology had the most mature models across all three years, while gastroenterology, oncology, and ophthalmology showed increasing numbers of mature publications.

Mature publications were geographically concentrated. The United States led in 2019 and 2020, followed by China; China led in 2021. South America, Eastern Europe, and Africa were underrepresented.

Image data appeared in approximately 88–89% of mature publications. Deep learning was the most common model type, used in 66% of mature publications in 2019, 71% in 2020, and 62% in 2021. Text and tabular data were substantially less represented.

The findings highlight gaps between growing publication volumes and clinically relevant, deployable AI. The authors identify opportunities to expand the use of diverse datasets and models across healthcare specialties and to support research in underrepresented regions. Limitations include reliance on PubMed and English-language publications, potentially excluding relevant research.

California’s Department of Fish and Wildlife re-approved Newhall Ranch after certifying additional environmental analysis addressing greenhouse gas emissions and protections for the endangered unarmored three spine stickleback, as ordered by the California Supreme Court in 2015. Developer Newhall Land proposed 13 measures targeting net-zero emissions and construction changes avoiding water contact, eliminating the need to collect and relocate the fish. The California Air Resources Board found adequate grounds to conclude the revised project would add no net greenhouse gas emissions. Los Angeles County supervisors are expected to consider final re-approval of the first two villages on July 19.

The study examines antiferromagnetic domain-wall dynamics driven by spin-orbit torque, reporting steady precession, constant-velocity propagation, and periodic motion between two positions when spin polarization has both in-plane and perpendicular components. Damping breaks Lorentz invariance, so propagating walls are not simple Lorentz transformations of static walls.

The model includes antiferromagnetic exchange, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, perpendicular anisotropy, damping, and spin torque, although most analysis assumes no Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction. A continuum description extends the nonlinear sigma model using tetramers appropriate to a two-dimensional square lattice. Numerical results come from discrete spin-lattice simulations.

The study also considers magnetic moments associated with domain-wall dynamics. For spin polarization along the anisotropy axis and no Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction, simulations reach steady spin precession. The theoretical treatment gives an asymptotic angular frequency equal to the negative ratio of the scaled spin-torque parameter to damping.

Young African entrepreneurs are developing technologies to strengthen agriculture, address climate change and create employment. Their projects were showcased at the MasterCard Foundation’s Young Africa Works Summit 2017 in Kigali.

In Rwanda, Jean Bosco Nzeyimana’s Habona employs 25 young people, turning organic waste into cooking briquettes and fertiliser. It produces 50 tonnes of fuel monthly and plans to expand nationwide.

In Malawi, Pilirani Khoza’s organisation supports disadvantaged female science students who, in return, train rural women in farming methods suited to harsh climatic conditions. The project has reached 360 farmers.

In Kenya, Brian Bosire’s UjuziKilimo uses handheld soil sensors and mobile-phone advice to help farmers choose crops and inputs. It aims to reach 200,000 farmers within two years.

U.N. Environment Programme official Richard Munang said agriculture offers significant potential to reduce poverty and generate jobs. He advocated improvements across supply chains, including technology connecting farmers to markets and clean energy for food processing.

Tesla entered into an underwriting agreement on February 13, 2020, with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley as representatives of the underwriters to sell 2,650,000 common shares. The underwriters fully exercised an option to purchase an additional 397,500 shares on February 18. The offering closed February 19, generating approximately $2.31 billion in net proceeds after underwriting discounts, commissions and estimated expenses.

Tesla and holders of the required minimum number of securities waived certain registration rights related to the offering. The Form 8-K includes the underwriting agreement, registration-rights waiver, legal opinion and press release announcing the offering.

The study investigates how melt flow and manganese availability govern the structure and magnetism of MnBi₂Te₄/(Bi₂Te₃)ₙ crystals grown by the Inverted Vertical Bridgman Method. Electron microscopy, elemental analysis, SQUID magnetometry, and magnetic resonance measurements revealed substantial variations along a single ingot.

Four growth stages were identified:
- Turbulent flow supports pure MnBi₂Te₄ formation by suppressing early MnTe precipitation.
- Rapid MnTe precipitation reduces manganese concentration from approximately 14 to 7 at.% and initiates mixed septuple-layer/quintuple-layer structures.
- Stationary flow promotes ordered layer assembly, with septuple-layer spacing increasing as MnTe supersaturation decreases.
- Cessation of flow produces diffusion-dominated transport, manganese depletion within septuple layers, and greater structural disorder.

Closely spaced, compositionally complete septuple layers exhibited antiferromagnetic transitions: Sample A showed transitions at 26 and 13.5 K, while Sample B showed a dominant transition at 13.5 K. More widely separated layers produced ferromagnetic behavior, with Curie temperatures of approximately 11 K in Sample C and 9 K in Sample D. Sample C had stronger magnetic anisotropy and higher saturation magnetization despite lower overall manganese content, consistent with its better-preserved septuple layers.

The proposed growth model attributes layer spacing to diffusion-limited competition for MnTe between growing septuple-layer edges. The findings emphasize control of melt composition and flow dynamics as essential for tuning stacking order, layer composition, and magnetic properties.

Bar Harbor Bankshares reported 2016 net income of $14.9 million, including $2.7 million in acquisition and system conversion charges. Assets increased to $1.8 billion, loans grew 14 percent, and non-interest income rose 38 percent.

Staff at Silverbluff Audubon Center in Aiken County, South Carolina, support the Philadelphia Eagles in the Super Bowl because of the center’s resident bald eagles. Director Paul Koehler says a nesting pair has been there since 1994.

The Supreme Court heard arguments over whether the U.S. Postal Service and federal government can be sued for intentionally failing to deliver mail. Texas landlady Lebene Konan alleges postal workers deliberately withheld mail as part of racial harassment, harming her rental business and causing emotional distress.

The government argues that intentional nondelivery falls within a statutory “postal exception” preserving immunity for claims arising from mail’s “loss, miscarriage, or negligent transmission.” A district court dismissed Konan’s case, but the 5th Circuit allowed claims against the USPS and United States to proceed.

Several justices questioned the government’s interpretation, while Justices Brett Kavanaugh and Samuel Alito expressed concerns about increased litigation. Konan’s lawyer disputed that prediction. Justices Sonia Sotomayor and Ketanji Brown Jackson emphasized the difficulty of proving intentional nondelivery and warned against shielding deliberate interference with ballots or Social Security checks.

A decision is expected by early July, possibly sooner.

Radford University selected Dr. Thomas C. Segar and Dr. Ann Marie Klotz as finalists for Vice President for Student Affairs, a position held temporarily by Susan Trageser following Dr. Irvin Clark’s departure announcement. The candidates participated in campus forums on September 11–12, 2017.

Segar, Vice President for Student Affairs at Shepherd University, has more than 26 years of professional experience. His priorities include student success, belonging, social justice, experiential learning, student services and institutional pride.

Klotz, a student affairs dean at the New York Institute of Technology, emphasized mentorship, support for first-generation students and adapting university programs to students’ changing needs. She also proposed using social media to share students’ experiences and strengthen Radford’s visibility. Both candidates emphasized building a supportive campus community.

All four analysts predict Dariush will beat Evan Dunham at UFC 216, citing his superior overall skills. Steven Rondina, Craig Amos and Scott Harris expect a unanimous decision; Nathan McCarter predicts a second-round submission, citing Dunham’s wear and tear.

Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia (MEN) comprises autosomal dominant cancer syndromes associated with endocrine tumors. MEN1, MEN2 and MEN4 are linked to mutations in MEN1, RET and CDKN1B, respectively. The study investigated MEN-associated genetic variants in India and developed resources for genetic testing and interpretation.

Researchers classified 1,324 unique variants from IndiGen, ClinVar and Mastermind using ACMG/AMP guidelines. Analysis of IndiGen, comprising 1,029 healthy individuals, identified two likely pathogenic RET variants and estimated that approximately 1 in 341 individuals in India carries MEN-linked pathogenic RET mutations. However, one variant’s classification relied solely on non-functional supporting evidence; the authors acknowledged that stricter criteria could exclude it from prevalence calculations.

Combining classified variants with ClinVar expert-panel entries produced MAPVar, a searchable database containing 3,280 variants: 1,094 pathogenic or likely pathogenic, 1,591 benign or likely benign, and 595 of uncertain significance. Comparison with 18 population datasets found one IndiGen RET variant absent elsewhere and the other at comparatively higher frequency in IndiGen.

Querying the GUaRDIAN endocrine cohort identified five unique pathogenic variants across seven patients. Researchers also developed a sequencing panel covering all coding regions of RET, MEN1 and CDKN1B. Applied to 72 patients with endocrine disorders, it resolved three cases with pathogenic MEN1 mutations.

The authors present MAPVar and the sequencing panel as resources supporting MEN diagnosis and variant interpretation, while calling for further studies of India-specific pathogenic variants, particularly in CDKN1B. MAPVar is available at https://clingen.igib.res.in/MAPVar/. The passage is a preprint not certified by peer review.

Enron’s November 19, 2001, quarterly filing disclosed worsening losses, debt pressures and risks to its proposed acquisition by Dynegy.

- Enron increased its third-quarter loss to $664 million, or 87 cents a share. It warned that credit concerns, reduced trading and declining asset values could hurt fourth-quarter results, including a possible $700 million pretax loss associated with its Whitewing partnership.
- A credit downgrade triggered a potential $690 million repayment obligation the following week unless Enron provided collateral or negotiated alternative arrangements. A further downgrade below investment grade could trigger $3.9 billion in additional repayments.
- Enron reported approximately $1.75 billion in available cash and credit against $9.15 billion in debt repayments and other obligations through the end of 2002. It sought additional financing, asset sales and debt restructuring, warning that adverse outcomes could threaten its ability to continue operating.
- Bankers questioned whether Dynegy might abandon the acquisition under material-adverse-change provisions. Shareholder litigation and possible undisclosed liabilities remained concerns. ChevronTexaco continued supporting the transaction while reviewing litigation risks.
- SEC and internal investigations focused on affiliated partnerships and accounting practices. Enron had reduced previously reported profits by $586 million, and Arthur Andersen had not completed its review of the latest statements. Representative John Dingell requested an investigation of Andersen’s audits of Enron and Waste Management.
- Enron’s water subsidiary, Azurix, warned it might need additional asset sales if it could not secure financing. Chairman Kenneth Lay relinquished a $60.6 million severance payment tied to the merger.

Nick Kyrgios defeated Jan-Lennard Struff 6-4, 6-4, 6-4 to level Australia’s 2018 Davis Cup tie against Germany at 1-1 in Brisbane. Earlier, Alexander Zverev beat Alex de Minaur in a five-set, four-hour match. The tie continues Saturday with doubles, followed by Sunday’s reverse singles featuring Kyrgios against Zverev and, if necessary, Struff against de Minaur.

R. Thomas Beach, testifying on behalf of Indicated Electric Generators, recommends that the California Public Utilities Commission adopt the Comprehensive Settlement Agreement rather than the Southern California Generation Coalition and The Utility Reform Network’s alternative, which would defer unbundling SoCalGas’ intrastate transmission services.

Beach argues that PG&E and SoCalGas face similar access and operational issues and that consistent statewide gas-market structures would benefit electric generators. He cites PG&E’s city-gate market as evidence that transmission unbundling can lower costs without requiring customers to hold capacity or pay demand charges. From May 1999 through April 2000, he reports that PG&E city-gate purchases cost $0.05–$0.11 per Dth less than border purchases plus full backbone transportation charges.

According to Beach, the Comprehensive Settlement would reduce electric generators’ transportation charges by $3 million annually in 2002, improve rate stability, shift backbone revenue-recovery risk to SoCalGas shareholders, and expand competitive purchasing, balancing, and storage options.

He disputes opponents’ estimates that demand charges could raise generators’ fixed costs by as much as 20%, arguing that their study assumes excessive capacity purchases and ignores mitigation options. These include interruptible service, capacity trading, alternative rate structures, and city-gate purchases. His recalculation using interruptible service produces a 0.6% increase in annual fixed costs.

Beach also identifies settlement provisions intended to prevent capacity concentration, including preferential initial access for end users, a 40% limit on any party’s holdings at individual receipt points after open seasons, and resale of unused firm capacity as interruptible service. He challenges claims that unbundling would cause plant closures or undermine electric reliability.
The jury ordered Richard Knight and Hannah, executrix of Hope Allen’s estate, to pay Jacob Allen his inheritance and court costs of 41 shillings five pence.

Parker Hogan, 19, pleaded not guilty to causing or aiding his roommate Michael Buskey’s suicide and falsifying physical evidence. Police allege Hogan helped plan the suicide and removed items afterward. Hogan posted bail and is scheduled to appear in court in July.

Hartman argues that Andropov’s foreign policy remains hard-line and largely unchanged from Brezhnev’s, although relations with the United States remain a Soviet priority. He recommends emphasizing arms control alongside defense to reduce nuclear-war risks and improve bilateral relations.

The Government is consulting on reforms to protect workers and suppliers affected by major insolvencies, following failures including Carillion and BHS. Proposals include reversing asset stripping to recover money for workers, disqualifying directors who sell struggling companies and strengthening Insolvency Service powers. Ministers aim to hold irresponsible directors accountable. Frank Field welcomed greater accountability, while Labour criticised the Government for not acting sooner.

Approximately one percent of U.S. higher education students participate in study abroad, despite institutions’ increasing emphasis on global competencies. Financial barriers and administrative complexity limit participation and program sustainability. The article provides a framework for developing education abroad business models that balance academic goals, operational requirements, financial viability, and accessibility.

Program planning centers on three interdependent drivers:

- **Curricular logistics:** Learning outcomes should guide program design rather than convenience or revenue. Considerations include elective versus required participation, academic credit, assessment and reflection, institutional alignment, competing programs, destination selection, activities, and duration. Shorter embedded programs may accommodate students whose commitments prevent semester-long participation.
- **Operational logistics:** Programs require clearly assigned responsibilities for design, travel coordination, and ongoing support. Planning encompasses leadership, risk management, transportation, accommodation, partnerships, communication, meals, emergency procedures, student preparation, and wellbeing. Faculty leadership supports academic integrity, while experienced staff, co-leaders, and partners can reduce workload and provide contingency support.
- **Financial logistics:** Expenditures should not exceed income. Budgets must account for faculty and staff time, travel, external services, projects, coordination, and emergencies. Income may include tuition allocations, student fees, institutional support, grants, corporate sponsorships, charitable donations, and partner cost-sharing. Funding restrictions and scholarship distribution affect affordability and access.

Drawing on a literature review and 14 informal interviews, the article presents adaptable business models grouped by leadership:

- **External-party-led programs** generally charge students fees covering program delivery. Outsourcing reduces faculty workload but can increase student costs and limit participation.
- **Faculty-led programs** may combine student payments, revenue-generating activities, corporate donations, and grants. Short-term programs are often more feasible than semester-long faculty-led travel, although their daily costs can be higher.
- **Student-led programs** are usually noncredit, club-based initiatives supported by fundraising, donations, sponsorships, and student activity fees. Student clubs may also complement faculty-led programs.

The article emphasizes tailoring and combining models to fit each program’s objectives, risks, resources, and constraints. Diversified funding, dedicated staff support, and appropriate delegation to students can reduce financial and logistical burdens while supporting sustainable global learning opportunities.

The Grand River Conservation Authority plans a $1.8-million, five-year LiDAR project to digitally map the Grand River’s entire floodplain and most floodplains along the Speed and Conestogo rivers. The detailed 3D maps will replace aging mapping and integrate with new forecasting software to provide near-real-time flood forecasts, identify threatened properties and support emergency notifications. John Bryant, a Sing Sing inmate proceeding pro se, brought a Section 1983 action against the New York State Department of Correctional Services (DOCS), Sing Sing, and Officer Hanser Hernandez. He alleged constitutional violations during an approximately twenty-day lockdown triggered by Hernandez’s false report of hidden ammunition. Bryant alleged intrusive cell searches, restrictions on religious activities and communication, deprivation of basic amenities, and limited medical care. He also challenged inmate compensation and restrictions on collective bargaining, seeking an injunction against future abusive conduct.

On June 14, 2001, the court adopted the magistrate judge’s recommendation and dismissed the claims against DOCS and Sing Sing under Eleventh Amendment immunity. New York had not consented to suit in federal court, and Section 1983 neither abrogated that immunity nor treated state agencies as “persons.”

The court stated that the action against Hernandez could proceed if service was properly completed or accepted. Bryant was directed to report the status of service by June 29, 2001.

The study examines how advanced technologies could transform the management and delivery of open and distance education. It focuses on artificial intelligence, blockchain, virtual and augmented reality, the metaverse, brain-computer interfaces, and brain chips.

Using a qualitative case-study approach, researchers conducted semi-structured interviews with four Anadolu University academics experienced in distance education and its management. Interview transcripts underwent content analysis, with researchers independently coding and comparing findings. Two main themes emerged: education and management.

Participants anticipated educational applications including personalized curricula, adaptive learning, AI-generated content, virtual teaching assistants, simulated internships, automated assessment, and blockchain-based recognition of prior learning. They also proposed potential uses of brain-computer interfaces and immersive virtual environments.

In management, participants expected AI to support decision-making, planning, supervision, evaluation, and service delivery. Some predicted reduced managerial hierarchies, more horizontal or networked organizations, and AI assuming managerial responsibilities. They emphasized careful implementation planning, accurate and updated information for AI systems, and continued human involvement.

Economic expectations included substantial initial infrastructure costs, potential long-term savings, increased productivity, and reduced demand for some employees. Participants also anticipated new technology-management jobs requiring technological literacy. They warned against adopting technologies merely because they are fashionable and recommended cost-benefit analysis and investment in human resources.

Potential sociocultural effects included changing lifestyles and communication patterns, increased technological dependence, virtual addiction, psychological problems, and emerging communities spanning physical and virtual environments. Participants highlighted the need for technology-literacy education and research into rights, ethics, and legal regulation.

The study recommends developing and testing AI assistants and managers, blockchain certification systems, adaptive synthetic content, and metaverse-based teaching environments. It also calls for further research on brain-computer interfaces and larger qualitative and quantitative studies involving different universities, disciplines, and geographical settings.

Engineers demonstrated an optical technique that screens structural properties of natural and synthetic proteins in milliseconds, including inside living bacteria, without killing cells. Using femtosecond and picosecond lasers with time-domain thermo-transmission, the method measures crystallinity before heating alters protein structure and allows selected proteins to be separated. Researchers are studying proteins adapted from squid ring teeth, which retain useful properties in water and may have marine applications. Penn State researcher Melik C. Demirel received funding to develop equipment for larger-scale screening.

A Senate committee criticized Supreme Court trial deadlines as unrealistic and issued 50 recommendations to speed up criminal proceedings. Sen. George Baker warned that “tens of thousands” of charges risked dismissal next year under the court’s 18- and 30-month limits.

A memorial football match for Aidan Sutherland, who died from diabetes complications shortly after turning 20, will take place at Stark’s Park on Sunday. Organised by his friend Ben Graham, it will raise diabetes awareness and support the Diabetes Research and Wellness Foundation. Friends, former teammates and professional players will participate, with family activities starting at noon and kick-off at 1pm. Cincinnati defeated 14th-ranked Iowa State 38-30 after building a 31-7 first-half lead, handing the Cyclones their first loss of the season and opening up the Big 12 championship race. The result follows an unpredictable season in which preseason outsiders BYU and Arizona State shared the regular-season title, while expected contenders Kansas State, Oklahoma State and Utah struggled.

The passage describes neural modulation systems and methods that use programmed electrode current distributions to create a linear electric field across targeted tissue, particularly for spinal cord pain therapy.

A system includes electrodes on one or more leads, a modulation generator, and a programming system. The programming system determines electrode fractionalizations from a target multipole containing at least three poles. Progressively distributing current among target anodes and cathodes shapes the field; some configurations assign higher current percentages to poles farther from the multipole’s center. Target poles may correspond to physical electrodes or be emulated through combinations of electrodes.

The field design aims to preferentially modulate dorsal horn or dorsal root tissue while reducing dorsal column activation, potentially providing pain relief without paresthesia. The passage associates dorsal horn activation with the first spatial derivative of voltage and dorsal column activation with the second derivative. A broad, approximately constant electric field is intended to support the former while limiting the latter. The design may also support therapies with perceived stimulation.

Field calculations may incorporate electrode positions, tissue-coupling calibration, perception thresholds, and mathematical models. Optimization methods determine electrode polarities and current percentages that approximate a desired field. Search heuristics may adjust pole spacing, amplitudes, number, orientation, focus, and spread.

Programming interfaces may let users adjust field angle, length, width, and intensity; identify anatomical regions or patient pain areas; and automatically determine or move target multipoles. Optional flanking electrodes provide edge guarding or current steering. Implementations include single or multiple leads, paddle leads, directional electrodes, implantable or external generators, clinician programmers, and patient remote controls.

Analysts are generally bullish on uranium, citing expanding nuclear capacity and demand exceeding current production. David Talbot forecasts 6% annual demand growth through 2020, while David Wang predicts prices near $65 a pound by 2019. The World Nuclear Association reports roughly 440 operating reactors, more than 160 planned and over 300 proposed.

The paper proposes a method for estimating the probability of failure before an e-commerce interaction in a digital business ecosystem. Risk combines the probability of failing to achieve desired outcomes with the consequences of that failure; the proposed method addresses the probability component.

The method uses “FailureLevel” to represent a prospective trusted agent’s inability to meet the initiating, or trusting, agent’s specific interaction criteria. Because risk changes over time, the assessment period is divided into non-overlapping time slots covering pre-interaction and post-interaction phases.

For pre-interaction slots, Previous FailureLevels (PFLs) are determined from relevant interaction history or recommendations. Recommendations are assessed for trustworthiness, timing, and relevance to the intended criteria. Untrustworthy recommendations are excluded, while trustworthy and recent recommendations receive greater weight. Criterion-specific FailureLevels are combined according to each criterion’s significance.

For future interaction slots, the method uses previous FailureLevels, their mean, and sample variance in a Gaussian distribution to estimate the probability of each failure level from 0 to 5, rather than assigning a single predicted value. When predicting additional future slots, the level with the highest probability in the preceding slot is incorporated into subsequent calculations.

An example compares two logistics providers for transporting goods worth $20,000, using three weeks of prior assessments to predict failure levels during a one-week interaction. Assessing the consequences of failure to complete the risk analysis is identified as future work.

The study examines the quality of inclusive distance education for students with disabilities in Kazakhstan during the COVID-19 pandemic, based on special education teachers’ opinions. It situates the research within Kazakhstan’s inclusive education reforms and principles of equal educational access, individualized learning support, teacher preparation and family participation.

Researchers conducted a qualitative case study involving 10 volunteer special education teachers working with students in grades 5–8 in special and general education schools. Participants taught students with hearing and speech impairments, visual impairments or mild intellectual disabilities. Online semi-structured interviews lasted approximately 30–35 minutes, were recorded and transcribed, and underwent thematic analysis.

Key findings included:
- Teachers used online lessons, video sharing, homework assignments and checking, online activities, and mobile applications.
- Seven teachers considered formal education more advantageous than distance education, two viewed them similarly, and one preferred distance education.
- Six teachers considered distance education insufficient for meeting students’ individual learning needs, three considered it partially sufficient, and one considered it sufficient.
- Barriers to family participation included high anxiety, reported by seven teachers; limited technological resources, by five; communication difficulties, by four; and inadequate online family education, by two.
- Six teachers reported weak teacher–student and peer interaction, while others identified insufficient time, poor-quality interaction and irregular interaction.

The study recommends diversifying technology-based teaching methods and improving infrastructure, developing learning content tailored to students’ individual needs, providing online seminars to support family participation, and organizing regular technology-supported social activities to strengthen teacher, student and peer relationships.

WIRED highlights Amazon Prime Day toy discounts for gifts or personal purchases. Deals include a 20-inch Diane Peach Bigfoot Squishmallow at more than half off, a 32-piece Magna-Tiles set reduced from $50 to $35, and several other Squishmallows priced from $5 to $24. Other featured toys include Lego’s retired Dried Flower Centerpiece, Play-Doh, and a skeleton-themed build. Listed discounts include Melissa & Doug’s wooden ice cream counter for $36, Crayola’s Color Wonder Magic Light Brush Station for $16, and a National Geographic rock tumbler kit for $52.

In his farewell address, the outgoing President thanks Congress for cooperation and wishes his successor peace and prosperity. He argues that America’s leadership depends on using its strength to advance peace, liberty, and human betterment while maintaining balance among national priorities.

He affirms the need for strong defenses but warns that the military-industrial complex could acquire unwarranted influence and endanger democratic processes. An informed citizenry must protect both security and liberty. He also cautions against federal funding dominating scholarship and against public policy becoming captive to a scientific-technological elite.

The President urges responsible stewardship of resources for future generations and advocates international cooperation, negotiation, and disarmament based on mutual trust and equality. Although war has been avoided and progress made, he expresses disappointment that lasting peace remains elusive. He closes by calling for humility in exercising power, devotion to principle, and worldwide efforts to promote freedom and opportunity and overcome poverty, disease, and ignorance.

Alzheimer’s disease (AD) and epilepsy have a bidirectional association involving neuronal hyperexcitability and overlapping molecular pathways. Seizures affect up to 15–20% of AD patients and are associated with earlier cognitive decline and faster disease progression, although the molecular mechanisms connecting the conditions remain poorly understood.

This study analyzed brain transcriptomic data from three cohorts—Knight ADRC, Mount Sinai Brain Bank, and ROSMAP—to investigate epilepsy-associated genes in an AD subtype characterized by synaptic plasticity dysfunction (SPD). This subtype is associated with more severe cognitive impairment, shorter survival after symptom onset, greater neurodegeneration, and astrogliosis. Analyses compared SPD cases with other sporadic AD cases, adjusting for sex, age at death, and estimated astrocyte and neuron proportions.

Of 105 selected epilepsy-associated genes, 45 were significantly dysregulated in Knight ADRC, 67 in Mount Sinai, and 41 in ROSMAP. Sixteen dysregulated genes were shared across all three cohorts: 15 were consistently downregulated, while CERS1 was upregulated. Many were highly expressed in neurons, and nine were synaptic genes, including GABRA1, GABRB3, GABRG2, GRIN2A, HCN1, SCN1A, and SCN8A.

Pathway analyses identified enrichment involving glutamatergic, GABAergic, and dopaminergic synapses, synaptic transmission, sodium transport, and ion-channel activity. In ROSMAP, 25 epilepsy-associated genes showed concordant expression changes in early and late AD compared with controls, with stronger effects in later disease stages.

The findings support shared molecular mechanisms between epilepsy and AD, particularly those involving synaptic function and neuronal excitability. These pathways may offer therapeutic targets, but whether epilepsy-related changes precede AD pathology, follow it, or vary between individuals remains uncertain. The study was posted as a preprint and had not been certified by peer review.

The Tax Court considered whether Elizabeth C. Dillingham’s noncharitable gifts by check were complete upon delivery in December 1980 or upon payment in January 1981. She delivered six $3,000 checks in December; the recipients cashed them approximately 35 days later, when she delivered another six $3,000 checks that were also paid.

The estate argued that payment related back to delivery. The court declined to apply the relation back doctrine because the estate failed to prove unconditional delivery. The unexplained delay and missing evidence concerning available funds contributed to that conclusion. The court expressly left open whether the doctrine could apply to other noncharitable gifts by check where unconditional delivery was established.

Applying Oklahoma law, the court concluded that delivery did not relinquish dominion and control because Dillingham retained the ability to stop payment. The gifts therefore became complete when the bank paid the checks in 1981.

Under the parties’ stipulations, the December checks consequently did not qualify for the annual gift-tax exclusion, $36,000 was omitted from the gross estate, and the six-year limitations period applied, leaving the estate-tax assessment timely.

Amazon received a patent for a delivery-drone system that would release components during malfunctions or adverse weather to control its descent. The drone would continually update a “fragmentation sequence” based on flight conditions, terrain and other factors, directing released parts toward preferred locations such as bodies of water, forests or open fields. Release order could account for component cost, weight, drag and purpose. Parts could be detached using mechanisms including latches, springs, compressed gas or small explosive charges. The patent does not guarantee the system will be deployed.

Methane bubbles generated by microbial decomposition in aquatic muds grow through elastic expansion and localized sediment fracturing. The passage presents a coupled mechanical–reaction–transport model that combines dissolved methane diffusion with Linear Elastic Fracture Mechanics (LEFM) to simulate individual bubbles in consolidated, water-saturated sediments.

The model treats bubbles as Mode I tensile cracks supplied by methane diffusing from surrounding pore water. It calculates methane accumulation, gas pressure, sediment deformation, and fracture propagation. Bubble growth occurs when the maximum stress intensity factor reaches sediment fracture toughness, with greater extension at the bubble head than at its tail. Simulations begin with a penny-shaped bubble of 4 mm radius, excluding nucleation and earlier growth, and continue until an inverted-teardrop configuration with a closed tail develops, marking the onset of ascent.

Implemented in COMSOL Multiphysics using finite elements, the model couples solute transport and solid mechanics with adaptive mesh deformation and occasional remeshing. Simulation inputs represent summer conditions at the NRL site in Eckernförde Bay, at 26 m water depth and 1 m sediment depth.

Numerical predictions of mature bubble shapes and sizes agree well with analytical solutions across varying fracture toughness. Lower toughness produces smaller, flatter bubbles, whereas higher toughness produces larger, more inflated bubbles.

The model applies only to individual bubbles. Upscaling their behavior to the effective properties of gas-bearing muds remains unresolved, limiting direct application to acoustic sensing, sediment stability assessment, and methane-flux prediction.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examines genetic variants and inflammatory markers as potential diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers of cerebral cavernous malformation (CCM). CCM affects 0.5%–1% of the population and may cause intracerebral hemorrhage or seizures, although many patients remain asymptomatic.

The single-site prospective observational study enrolled 103 patients, including 70 with symptomatic disease: 48 with hemorrhage and 22 with seizures without evidence of bleeding. Researchers analyzed five genetic variants in PTPN2, VDR and FCGR2A, along with plasma inflammatory markers. Forty-two patients were followed for four years.

Key findings included:
- PTPN2 rs72872125 CT and VDR rs7975232 CC genotypes were independently associated with an asymptomatic phenotype. PTPN2 CT was associated with higher IL-10 and lower IL-18 and IFN-γ levels; carrying a VDR rs7975232 C allele was associated with lower IL-27 and IL-23 levels.
- A biomarker combining PTPN2 rs72872125 CC genotype and plasma GM-CSF distinguished symptomatic from asymptomatic patients with an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.663, 41.3% sensitivity and 85.7% specificity. Performance was higher in familial disease and infratentorial lesions.
- Four patients experienced events during follow-up. FCGR2A rs1801274 GG was associated with these events, with an AUC of 0.796, increasing to 0.875 in a propensity-matched subgroup.
- Results linked VDR rs731236 AA to later symptom onset and VDR rs11568820 CC to earlier onset.

The authors propose these variants as potential biomarkers and hypothesize that immune-mediated inflammatory processes contribute to aggressive CCM behavior. The preprint states that its findings should not guide clinical practice.

Social media platforms are strengthening moderation policies and using artificial intelligence to identify inappropriate content. A.I. can recognize offensive language and images, but its accuracy varies, and it struggles with context and intent. Errors have included mislabeling dark-skinned people, incorrectly filtering LGBT search terms, and removing educational or anti-hate content.

A.I. can inherit human biases from its training data, and shared datasets can spread those biases across programs, making correction difficult. Human moderators remain necessary to determine whether flagged content violates community standards.

A.I. improves efficiency by screening posts and prioritizing human review. Facebook reported that its suicide-detection technology prompted 100 calls to emergency responders in one month in 2017. The company is also expanding its human review team. Experts cited in the passage emphasize continued human oversight and warn that ethical considerations risk falling behind technological development.

The passage examines a teacher education approach combining collaborative inquiry with panoramic cameras to strengthen teacher education students’ (TESs’) diagnosis of student learning problems and perceived instructional design capabilities. The literature emphasizes observing students’ responses to teaching activities, collecting concrete evidence, and using collaborative reflection to revise instruction. Panoramic recordings support this process through replay, adjustable viewing angles, and audio.

The study involved 22 TESs in five groups during a Taiwanese teacher education course from September 2022 to January 2023. After five weeks of preparation, participants completed four three-week cycles of collaborative lesson planning, junior high school teaching and observation, footage review, post-lesson discussion, and lesson-plan revision. Participants alternated teaching and observer roles.

Assessment used observation reports scored for evidence-based diagnosis and a 12-item questionnaire measuring perceived capabilities in lesson preparation, connecting student learning with teaching activities, and revising plans after discussion. Average diagnostic scores increased from approximately 0.47 out of 2 in the first cycle to 1.88 in the fourth. Researcher guidance encouraged participants to move from describing teacher behavior toward interpreting student performance across activities. Questionnaire results showed statistically significant improvements in all three areas of perceived capability.

The study concludes that the approach is feasible for teacher education and supports improved diagnostic abilities and perceived instructional design capabilities. However, determining whether participants’ proposed instructional adjustments effectively addressed learning problems remained difficult, potentially because of their limited teaching experience. Further opportunities to diagnose learning difficulties and evaluate instructional responses were recommended.

Connecticut municipal lobbyists asked Gov. Dannel P. Malloy for relief from costly state mandates and greater flexibility to control local expenses amid a budget stalemate. COST and CCM sought retirement-system changes, easier arbitration to support shared services, higher retained land-transfer fees and adjusted prevailing-wage thresholds. Malloy described the meeting as productive and supported easing regulations. CCM’s Joe DeLong said communities were not seeking protection from state-aid cuts, a claim Senate leader Martin Looney disputed. The state faced an estimated $3.5 billion deficit after union concessions and remained without a two-year budget nearly six weeks into the fiscal year.

NVIDIA’s GA10x Ampere architecture introduces improvements in graphics, AI processing, memory bandwidth, storage access, and video capabilities for gaming, workstations, and data centers.

- **Compute and ray tracing:** GA10x provides up to twice the performance in programmable shading, ray tracing, and AI. Second-generation RT Cores double ray/triangle intersection performance and accelerate ray-traced motion blur. Third-generation Tensor Cores support structured sparsity.
- **Structured sparsity and DLSS:** A 2:4 pruning pattern, followed by fine-tuning, halves weight storage and bandwidth requirements while doubling effective Tensor Core throughput, with virtually no inference accuracy loss in evaluated networks. Enhanced DLSS uses neural networks and details from multiple frames to reconstruct high-quality images, making 8K gaming at 60 fps feasible in ray-traced games.
- **GDDR6X memory:** Developed with Micron, GDDR6X uses four-level PAM4 signaling to transmit two bits per clock edge. GA10x supports data rates up to 19.5 Gbps and peak bandwidth of 936 GB/sec. Maximum Transition Avoidance encoding improves signal integrity. Error Detection and Replay retries failed memory transactions, allowing excessive overclocking to appear as plateauing performance, although crashes remain possible.
- **RTX IO:** Integrated with Microsoft DirectStorage, RTX IO enables GPU-based asset loading and lossless decompression, reducing CPU workload and storage bottlenecks. NVIDIA reports up to 100-fold I/O acceleration compared with hard drives and traditional storage APIs. Applications include game loading, texture streaming, rendering, and large professional datasets.
- **Professional GPUs:** The A40 targets data-center visual computing, simulation, AI, and virtual workstations. Compared with Quadro RTX 6000, it offers up to twice the FP32 and ray-tracing throughput and up to five times AI throughput, or ten times with sparsity. Both A40 and RTX A6000 provide 48 GB of memory per GPU, expandable to 96 GB by linking two GPUs through NVLink, and support virtualization.
- **Display and video:** Ampere supports DisplayPort 1.4a, HDMI 2.1, 4K at 120 Hz, and 8K at 60 Hz, with compression or pixel-format requirements for certain configurations. Fifth-generation NVDEC adds hardware AV1 decoding, including 8K60 HDR playback with low CPU usage. Seventh-generation NVENC offloads encoding and supports resolutions up to 4K with H.264 and 8K with HEVC.
- **GeForce models:** RTX 3090 includes 24 GB of GDDR6X and 10,496 CUDA cores. RTX 3070 uses GA104 and GDDR6, lacks NVLink, and is described as faster than RTX 2080 Ti.

NVIDIA provides the specifications without warranties, reserves the right to modify them, and assigns customers responsibility for verifying suitability for their applications.

SanDisk warranty service requires contacting 1-866-SanDisk or support@SanDisk.com, returning the product in tamper-resistant packaging with prepaid freight, and obtaining tracking confirmation. SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund the product; replacements retain the original warranty’s remaining term. SanDisk disclaims responsibility for lost data and limits liability to the purchase price, subject to jurisdictional exceptions. Products should not be used where failure could threaten injury or life.

Downloading, installing, or using the software constitutes acceptance of its license agreement. Users who disagree must not use it and must return the entire hardware/software package, if applicable, for a refund.

The license permits personal use of executable software with a SanDisk product on one device at a time. Restrictions prohibit modification, reverse engineering, rental, combining it with other software or devices, and disclosure of proprietary information. Permitted copies must retain notices and the agreement.

Software is provided “as is” without warranties to the extent permitted by law; users assume performance risks and correction costs. Liability for specified damages is excluded. Software is not intended for high-risk activities.

Transfer is permitted with the complete SanDisk product and agreement, ending the original user’s rights. Breach may result in immediate termination without notice. Government use carries restricted rights. California and controlling federal law govern the agreement, with exclusive jurisdiction in Santa Clara County courts. Export restrictions apply, and amendments or waivers require signed written agreement.

Diana Containerships reported a quarterly loss of $0.66 per share, beating estimates by $0.11. Revenue was $5.40 million versus an expected $7.50 million, down 63.8% year over year. Renaissance Technologies increased its stake by 94.4% to 231,485 shares, worth $644,000. Institutional investors owned 29.82% of the stock. Zacks Investment Research upgraded the company from “sell” to “hold.”

The passage documents silicon issues in the AMD Geode CS5535 Companion Device Revision A3, including DMA, interrupt, clock-gating, power-management, register-access, and interface failures.

Detailed issues include:
- PIT read-back commands do not cancel unfinished counter latch commands; software should complete latch commands first.
- The GLIU debug port hangs the system and should not be used.
- PIT count mode 3 loads new values immediately, disrupting ongoing counting.
- Delayed interrupt-request clearing causes duplicate CPU interrupts when automatic end-of-interrupt is enabled.
- DMA rotating priorities may produce incorrect transfer ordering, although transfers complete successfully.
- Thermal alarms trigger Faulted Standby, but the PMC cannot recover independently because the alarm resides in the Work power domain.
- Sleep Clock must be enabled in the PMC when related sleep options are used; it can instead be disabled at the GPIO if its output is unwanted.

Other listed problems include system hangs, data corruption, failed wake events, and unsuccessful device accesses.

The President reports that the United States is at peace with all nations and emphasizes neutrality, treaty obligations, constitutional limits, and preservation of the Union.

Foreign affairs include friendly relations with Great Britain, reciprocal shipping arrangements, and restored diplomatic intercourse with France. To uphold neutrality, the administration stopped naval assistance to a German warship and suppressed an expedition believed intended to invade Cuba. It supported recognition of Hungarian independence only if Hungary could sustain it, without intervening in the conflict. Unresolved American claims against Portugal remain a serious concern. The President also recommends legislation addressing forcible removal of people from American soil and strengthening suppression of American participation in the African slave trade.

Relations with Mexico remain friendly following the treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo. Additional funding is requested for the boundary survey, and government counsel is recommended for settling American claims. The President advocates stronger relations with other American states, protection of privately financed interoceanic transportation projects through Nicaragua, Mexico, and Panama, equal international access to those routes, and continued independence for the Sandwich Islands.

Projected Treasury deficits total approximately $16.4 million through July 1851, attributed to Mexican War and treaty expenses. Recommendations include borrowing authority, strict spending economy, tariff revision using specific duties to increase revenue and encourage domestic industry, reconsideration or modification of the subtreasury system, and creation of an agricultural bureau.

The President recommends favorable consideration of California’s anticipated statehood application if its constitution meets federal requirements and expects New Mexico eventually to seek admission. He urges Congress to await local action and avoid sectional controversies. Proposals for western territories include customs administration, coastal surveys and lighthouses, expanded Indian agencies, a California branch mint, adjudication of land titles, public-land surveys, and geological examination and disposal of mineral lands. A scientific survey should assess possible railroad routes connecting the Atlantic or Gulf with the Pacific before decisions on construction or federal assistance.

Other recommendations include river and harbor improvements, increased Army strength at western posts, provisions for disabled military personnel, naval reorganization, and improved postal service in California and Oregon. The President proposes uniform five-cent single-letter postage, with congressional mail costs paid from the Treasury or the franking privilege abolished. Congress is also urged to authorize the forthcoming census and attend to the District of Columbia.

The address concludes that each governmental branch must remain within its constitutional sphere. The President characterizes the veto as an exceptional safeguard rather than a means of directing legislation and pledges to defend the Union within his constitutional authority.

The passage describes computer-based methods and systems for generating multiple orthodontic treatment plans and manufacturing appliances for a selected plan. The process measures a patient’s tooth positions, receives tooth movement restrictions and treatment settings, evaluates malocclusions, and develops alternative plans with interim and final tooth arrangements.

Treatment plans branch according to whether specific conditions are maintained or corrected, including openbite, molar relationships, and posterior crossbite. Further evaluation addresses bi-protrusion, molar and canine class II or III malocclusions, and overjet. Alternatives may include bicuspid or lower incisor extraction, interproximal reduction, and changes to anterior spacing. Measurements of tooth positions, root apex displacement, and specified thresholds guide these decisions. Clinically unacceptable interim arrangements may be discarded.

A dental professional reviews proposed plans and selects one based on treatment characteristics, patient preferences, and factors such as extraction requirements, interproximal reduction, and the number of treatment stages. Movement paths and incremental stages are generated to reposition teeth from their initial arrangement toward the selected target while considering movement constraints and avoiding collisions.

The selected plan supports generation of appliance models and fabrication instructions. Appliances generally comprise tooth-receiving shells worn sequentially to produce incremental movement. Their geometry, thickness, stiffness, materials, and auxiliary components may be designed to deliver specified forces, optionally using computer simulations.

Manufacturing options include direct fabrication through additive or subtractive techniques, indirect fabrication such as thermoforming over dental models, or combinations of these methods. Appliances may contain multiple materials and undergo cleaning, post-curing, and support removal. The system may integrate scanners, processors, storage, user interfaces, and fabrication equipment at local or remote locations.

Roanoke’s Bittle tree, planted by its first president, Dr. David Bittle, was removed after more than 100 years because storm damage made it hazardous. Its wood became the Bittle Tree of Life Cross in Antrim Chapel for the College’s 175th anniversary. Reverend Chris Bowen and retired professor George Arthur designed the cross to symbolize the College’s roots and future.

This retrospective French study evaluated COVID-19 convalescent plasma (CCP) in 112 patients with hematological malignancies treated between May 2020 and April 2021. Patients received four CCP units; 87% had negative SARS-CoV-2 serology at transfusion, and none were vaccinated.

Overall 90-day survival was 64.9%, including 77.5% among patients with B-lymphoid neoplasms, 20% with myeloid neoplasms, and 36.8% with plasma-cell neoplasms. CCP transfusion was associated with decreased temperature and inflammatory markers and increased PCR cycle threshold values after seven days. Reported adverse events included three allergic reactions and two transient increases in oxygen requirements of uncertain attribution.

Older age, high blood pressure, and greater COVID-19 severity were associated with poorer survival. Previous anti-CD20 or anti-CD19 therapy was associated with better survival among CCP recipients.

A nested comparison examined 81 CCP-treated and 120 untreated patients with B-cell neoplasms. The main weighted analysis, restricted to 147 patients previously treated with anti-CD20 therapy and alive 16 days after hospitalization, associated CCP with a 63% reduction in mortality risk (95% confidence interval: 31%–80%). Sensitivity analyses also supported an association with reduced mortality.

The observational design could not establish causality despite statistical adjustments for treatment-selection and immortal-time biases. Viral strains were not assessed, and results could not be extended to the Delta variant. The authors identify CCP as a potentially useful treatment, particularly for B-cell-depleted patients, while emphasizing the need for prospective randomized confirmation and consideration of vaccination, variants, and anti-spike monoclonal antibodies.

May Baxter-Thornton from Newport and Emma Lewis from Swansea, both survivors of child sexual abuse, have joined the Independent Inquiry into Child Sexual Abuse’s victims and survivors panel. They will advise on reaching and listening to Welsh victims and survivors, ensuring their experiences inform the inquiry. Both have worked supporting vulnerable people.
The Louisiana Supreme Court granted review, ordered duplicate appellate records submitted, and directed that counsel be notified.

Tesla’s unaudited Form 10-Q for the quarter ended September 30, 2018 reports results for its automotive and energy generation and storage businesses.

- **Third-quarter results:** Revenue totaled $6.82 billion, compared with $2.98 billion a year earlier. Automotive revenue was $6.10 billion, energy generation and storage revenue was $399.3 million, and services and other revenue was $326.3 million. Operating income was $416.8 million, versus a $535.5 million loss. Net income attributable to common stockholders was $311.5 million, or $1.75 per diluted share, compared with a $619.4 million loss.
- **Nine-month results:** Revenue totaled $14.24 billion, compared with $8.47 billion in 2017. Net loss attributable to common stockholders was $1.12 billion, compared with $1.29 billion.
- **Cash flows:** Operating activities provided $863.2 million during the first nine months, versus using $570.5 million a year earlier. Investing activities used $1.97 billion, while financing activities provided $686.1 million. Cash, cash equivalents and restricted cash ended the period at $3.52 billion.
- **Financial position:** At September 30, total assets were $29.26 billion, liabilities were $23.41 billion, and stockholders’ equity was $4.51 billion. Cash and cash equivalents were $2.97 billion. Current assets totaled $7.92 billion and current liabilities totaled $9.78 billion. Inventory was $3.31 billion and customer deposits were $905.8 million.
- **Debt:** Unpaid debt principal totaled $10.90 billion, including $7.60 billion of recourse debt and $3.30 billion of non-recourse debt. Tesla reported compliance with all financial debt covenants.
- **Accounting changes:** Tesla adopted ASC 606 on January 1, 2018 without retrospectively adjusting prior periods. Certain vehicle sales with resale value guarantees changed from lease accounting to sales with a right of return. Adoption reduced opening accumulated deficit by $623.2 million and increased third-quarter net income attributable to common stockholders by $74.6 million.
- **Assets and obligations:** Net property, plant and equipment totaled $11.25 billion, and cumulative capitalized Gigafactory 1 costs reached $4.47 billion. The accrued warranty reserve was $644.5 million. Tesla identified dependence on predominantly single-source suppliers as a risk.
- **Executive compensation:** Stockholders approved a March 2018 award of 20,264,042 stock options to the CEO, divided into 12 tranches tied to operational milestones, market conditions and continued service.

Tesla cautioned that forward-looking statements involve risks and uncertainties and that interim results do not necessarily indicate full-year results.

Beth Utton challenges Rep. Ken Buck’s statement that health care is a commodity, arguing it is a right and advocating Medicare for all over profit-driven care. Bonnie New criticizes a Tribune headline about Denver’s nearly $1 million settlement with the family of a teen killed by police. She argues the headline should mention the teen was committing a crime, questions the settlement, and defends the officer’s right to self-defense.

The March 27–28, 2001 news compilation covers Enron’s finances, international projects and electricity-market developments:

- Enron awarded Chairman Kenneth Lay a $7 million bonus for 2000, up 79%, alongside a $1.3 million salary and $7.5 million in restricted stock. CEO Jeffrey Skilling projected 2001 revenue of $160–170 billion and reaffirmed earnings guidance of $1.70–$1.75 per share.
- Enron’s Japanese venture submitted plans for a 2,000-megawatt LNG-fired power plant in Aomori, targeting construction in 2004 and operation in 2007 or later. Environmental approval and transmission access remained hurdles.
- Enron and PowerGen withdrew from pursuing a stake in India’s Vijayanagar power project. Separately, Enron Wind sought approval for an Indian subsidiary with an initial $2 million investment.
- Dolphin Energy, in which Enron held 24.5%, planned to supply Qatari natural gas to the United Arab Emirates, where Dubai faced shortages.
- Skilling supported California’s electricity-rate increase as a way to reduce shortages but called for further deregulation. He expressed confidence in Texas’s approaching competitive electricity market, where companies were recruiting customers for a June pilot program.
- President Bush nominated Patrick Wood and Nora Brownell to the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission amid pressure for stronger intervention in California’s electricity crisis.
- Britain launched new electricity-trading arrangements expected to favor generators with flexible supply portfolios, while smaller and renewable producers voiced concerns.
- Enron and other companies urged the Export-Import Bank to permit private-lender export financing and opposed proposed budget cuts.
- Viacom abandoned plans to split off Blockbuster because of its improving business. Blockbuster’s video-on-demand partnership with Enron had recently ended.
- Other coverage addressed proposed restrictions on Indian states’ negotiations for multilateral loans and letters criticizing California electricity-rate increases.

Electric Resistance Welding (ERW) steel pipes transport petroleum, gas and other fluids under varying pressures. Their production offers high efficiency, low cost and material savings. Made from hot-rolled coils, they undergo burr removal and wall-thickness control. ERW pipes are used across industrial sectors and increasingly as main pipes in urban gas networks.

Steve Yzerman said Tampa Bay had no fixed timeline for building a successful team, emphasizing drafting, patient development and selective additions through trades and free agency. He credited scouts and development staff, noted the importance of inheriting Steven Stamkos and Victor Hedman, and acknowledged that some later-round picks exceeded expectations. He said sustained success requires home-grown talent, particularly under the salary cap.

Coach Cooper attributed the team’s Cup Final run to resilience, growing maturity and lessons from injuries and the previous year’s first-round sweep. He highlighted Ben Bishop’s responses to setbacks and the players’ confidence under playoff pressure. Cooper also credited his shared minor-league experience with young players for establishing trust and allowing them to develop through mistakes.

Both described Stamkos as an evolving leader who prioritized team success, accepted different responsibilities and encouraged teammates to contribute. Yzerman stressed that top players must contribute offensively and defensively.

Yzerman said attracting players depends primarily on running a competitive program and offering meaningful opportunities. Cooper praised the game-changing abilities of Kucherov, Johnson and Kane. Yzerman described his own playoff role as supporting coaches and players without interfering.

Deloitte’s survey found that 49% of respondents considered self-driving cars unsafe, down from 73% last year. Brand trust increased confidence, with 51% trusting traditional manufacturers to implement autonomous technology versus 21% trusting technology companies. Meanwhile, 73% preferred engine-powered vehicles and 2% preferred electric vehicles for their next purchase. Electric vehicle concerns included range, price and charging infrastructure, though 37% would consider them for lower ongoing costs. Customer service remained important to buyers. The UK government is launching an inquiry into autonomous vehicle safety.

New Jersey Governor Chris Christie signed legislation strengthening protections for people with developmental disabilities following Stephen Komninos’s 2007 group-home death. The law allows twice-yearly unannounced inspections, authorizes additional inspectors, requires injury notifications to parents or guardians within two-to-eight hours, and mandates family meetings at least twice annually.

The Browns have not ruled out selecting Baker Mayfield first overall in Thursday’s NFL draft, ESPN reported. General manager John Dorsey remains open to all options, while coach Hue Jackson said Mayfield, Sam Darnold, Josh Allen and Josh Rosen remain under consideration.

The Presidential Election Cycle theory, associated with Yale Hirsch and the Stock Trader’s Almanac, links U.S. stock market performance to four-year presidential terms. The passage gives conflicting accounts of whether the first or second half performs better, but cited Almanac findings identify the pre-election year as strongest and election year as second strongest.

Since 1952, average S&P 500 election-year returns cited were 12.5% when an incumbent sought reelection, 6.7% across all election years, and −1.5% without an incumbent running. Midterm years are described as generally weak until the fourth quarter, with increased volatility.

The theory does not consistently predict market outcomes, and major economic shocks can disrupt historical patterns. Election-related uncertainty and policy differences may particularly affect healthcare, energy, and trade. Congressional control also influences whether proposed policies become law.

The passage recommends monitoring policy effects, reassessing conditions after elections, staying invested, and maintaining a rebalanced portfolio rather than reacting primarily to election-related volatility.

Jefferies raised Ferguson Plc’s price target from GBX 5,170 to GBX 5,240, maintaining a hold rating. Across analysts, the stock had three hold ratings and four buy ratings, with an average target of GBX 5,265.71. Shares rose 0.68% to GBX 5,200 on Thursday, giving the company a market capitalization of GBX 13.17 billion. Ferguson, formerly Wolseley, is a Switzerland-based distributor of plumbing and heating products and building materials.

Intel’s Management Engine (ME) is an embedded system connected to storage, networking, and other peripherals that remains active when a computer is powered down. It runs Minix, and its closed-source implementation has limited security researchers’ ability to examine it.

Researchers Mark Ermolov and Maxim Goryachy presented an exploit at BlackHat Europe enabling arbitrary code execution on ME through physical access. The exploit affects ME versions above 11, excluding Macs according to the passage. A network-based exploit is discussed as a potential future threat, not an existing capability.

Mitigation depends on the computer manufacturer. System76 released firmware to disable ME, and Dell offers a laptop with ME disabled by default. Intel provides a detection tool, but no universal disabling method exists. Removing valid ME firmware causes shutdown after thirty minutes; the me_cleaner tool instead prevents ME operation while allowing the computer to function.

The passage emphasizes the security risks of unauditable code while acknowledging the current exploit’s physical-access limitation.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for identifying audio content through a playback device and retrieving associated metadata, particularly when incoming audio data lacks information.

A playback device receives digital audio data, sends a portion to an identification system, receives related information, and forwards that information to a control device. It also plays the audio through electrically connected speakers, which may be integrated or external. Using data already available to the playback device can avoid requiring the controller to capture sound through a microphone and convert it into digital information.

The identification system may operate over a local or wide-area network. Returned information may include track titles, performers, composers, album titles, release dates, network locations for retrieving metadata, or identifiers recognized by a metadata-curating device. In some embodiments, the identification system sends information directly to the controller.

Identification may be initiated by a controller command, detection of an audio discontinuity such as silence, or periodic transmission of audio samples. The playback device may decode audio, change its sample rate, extract data from different processing stages, or send selected frequency ranges to meet an identification system’s requirements. If one identification system cannot identify the content, another may be used.

The controller can display received information or retrieve additional metadata using supplied locations or identifiers. Users may request metadata refreshes or searches through its interface. The controller may also automatically request information when a metadata category is missing. Information can appear on the controller or a connected display.

The described operating environment includes networked playback devices, controllers, audio sources, and configurable playback zones. Devices may play different content independently or synchronize playback across zones, form stereo pairs, or divide frequency ranges among speakers. Controllers manage playback, volume, queues, sources, and zone configurations. Audio sources include local storage, network libraries, internet services, and line-in connections.

The disclosure includes device, method, and computer-readable-medium implementations. Its examples are illustrative rather than limiting, and components may be implemented through hardware, software, firmware, or combinations thereof.

The disclosure describes light-guiding and illumination systems for 2D, 3D, autostereoscopic, privacy, and multi-user displays. In a stepped-waveguide optical valve, light travels toward a reflective end substantially without loss, then returns and encounters tilted extraction features that direct it out toward the display. Reflective surfaces and extraction features may provide optical power to form viewing windows. Unlike conventional non-imaging backlights, these systems direct different sources toward different viewing positions.

The proposed privacy displays combine a backlight, transmissive spatial light modulator, input and output polarisers, an additional polariser, and one or more retarders. These components may reduce off-axis image visibility beyond that achieved by a directional backlight alone while substantially maintaining head-on luminance. Retarder options include crossed A-plates, C-plates, O-plates, and switchable liquid crystal retarders with passive correction. Different configurations may control angular attenuation, reduce colour variations, or limit component thickness and cost. Some embodiments use non-directional backlights.

A control system may coordinate light-source selection and retarder voltage to switch between narrow privacy and wider viewing modes. Additional options include independently addressable privacy regions, camouflage patterns, adjustment according to an observer’s location, and temporally multiplexed secondary images that obscure stray-light images outside the primary viewing window. Automotive embodiments may reduce visible reflections from windscreens and other transparent surfaces.

For autostereoscopic operation, synchronized illumination and sequential left- and right-eye images direct all display pixels toward different viewing windows in successive time slots. Observer tracking may adjust these windows as viewers move. Related arrangements support multiple viewers receiving different images. The disclosure presents these systems as approaches to thin, large-area directional displays with potential improvements in resolution, viewing freedom, privacy, and illumination efficiency.

This qualitative literature review examines Mortimer J. Adler’s perennialist philosophy in relation to Christian education, global educational management, and posthumanism. Drawing on Adler’s books and international journal research, it emphasizes enduring values, reasoning, and learners’ holistic development rather than instant achievement or preparation for employment alone.

The authors discuss posthumanism through questions about human dependence on ecosystems, technological developments, artificial intelligence, and challenges to human supremacy. They present posthumanist theory as unfinished and context-dependent, requiring criticism grounded in historical realities.

Adler’s perennialism emphasizes the continuity of educational ideas and intellectual self-development. His concept of docility involves temporarily postponing judgment to learn from a trusted teacher. The authors distinguish this from unquestioning submission: obedience should involve intellectual consideration, skepticism, and conscience rather than emotion. They maintain that docility can coexist with democracy and educational freedom.

The review extends educational management beyond administration to include spirituality, family relationships, cross-cultural participation, institutional transformation, business ethics, and community disaster resilience. It also identifies insufficient attention to women’s unequal educational opportunities in Adler’s account and calls for support from families and government.

The authors conclude that education should respect children’s capacities, curiosity, and enthusiasm rather than treat them as incomplete adults or future workers. Responsibility for educational failure should rest with teachers, parents, and the state rather than be displaced onto children. Educational management should prioritize enduring values and sustained intellectual development while attending to the vulnerabilities of learners and others involved in education.

Sepsis affects more than 30 million people worldwide annually, killing an estimated 6 million, including nearly 2 million children. It occurs when the body’s response to infection becomes uncontrolled, potentially causing vital organ failure. Among survivors, 40% experience lasting physical and mental symptoms.

Warning signs include pale, mottled skin, severe breathlessness, shivering or muscle pain, not urinating all day, nausea and vomiting. Immediate emergency help is advised.

There is no specific cure, although research into metformin and gene therapy offers potential treatments. Public awareness and recognition of symptoms remain limited, and healthcare professionals need greater education and clearer diagnostic guidance. While research may deliver new treatments, improving awareness is likely to have the greatest short-term impact on saving lives and reducing harm.

The invention describes an optical waveguide display designed to increase field of view and extend the usable wavelength range. Conventional waveguide displays are limited by the angles at which light can propagate through total internal reflection (TIR), with different wavelengths experiencing different field-of-view restrictions.

The proposed apparatus uses an input diffractive part to direct display light into a waveguide and an output diffractive part to release it for viewing. External surfaces responsible for internal reflection are coated with a material having a refractive index substantially equal to or below 1.0 at optical wavelengths. A lower-index coating reduces the critical angle for TIR, enabling retention of light that would otherwise escape. A coating with an index approximately equal to 1.0 can provide protection without degrading optical performance.

Suggested coatings include metamaterials comprising repeating magnetic resonators between conductive meshes, or arrays of parallel conductive nanowires. Their structural parameters can be adjusted to control refractive index and optical attenuation.

The display may use conjugated input and output gratings to reduce geometric distortion and chromatic dispersion. Multilayer versions contain separate waveguides tuned to different colours, joined by an intermediate low-index layer that also protects against contamination. Additional outer protective layers may strengthen the assembly.

Coatings may cover gratings for protection or leave input and output regions uncovered to avoid absorption losses when light passes through the metamaterial.
