The speaker respects the league’s decision regarding a recent incident and is focused on the next Stanley Cup Finals game. They acknowledge needing to avoid goalie contact and penalties, discuss teammates’ contributions, and describe balancing game preparation with family time and managing a fantasy baseball team.

AOL Instant Messenger (AIM), active since 1997, announced it would shut down on December 15, 2017. Once the leading U.S. instant messaging application, its usage declined as cell phone messaging and social media platforms grew.

Baker Mayfield’s statistical performance supports his case as the NFL draft’s top quarterback prospect, despite debate over his behavior, size and playing style. Pro Football Focus analysts unanimously ranked him highest in the class. He led college quarterbacks in passer rating under pressure for three consecutive seasons and graded as the class’s most accurate passer at every throwing distance.

Mayfield completed 38 of 67 passes traveling at least 20 air yards, compared with Josh Allen’s 13 of 42. Radar measurements also placed his throwing velocity just below Allen’s. Football Outsiders’ QBASE predictive model ranked Mayfield fourth among quarterback prospects since 1997, behind Philip Rivers, Donovan McNabb and Carson Palmer.

Concerns include his height, tendency to take unnecessary sacks and transition from Oklahoma’s Air Raid offense. NFL teams reportedly remain divided on him, but the passage anticipates that he will likely be selected in the top five.

Antonio Conte urged Chelsea to focus on beating Huddersfield rather than their February Champions League tie against Barcelona. Following a 1-0 defeat at West Ham, he said Chelsea could no longer defend their Premier League title and must fight for Champions League qualification. Chelsea sit third, while Huddersfield are 12th.

Theresa May will reportedly ask her Cabinet to support a soft Brexit plan at Friday’s Chequers summit. According to ITV’s Robert Peston, the UK would retain EU rules for goods and agricultural products, end freedom of movement while offering EU citizens preferential immigration access, and collect EU customs tariffs while pursuing independent trade deals.

Amid Conservative divisions, former minister Phillip Lee accused Brexiteers of planning a leadership coup following reports of fundraising by Jacob Rees-Mogg’s supporters. Former party leader William Hague urged ministers to compromise, warning that Parliament could impose a “watered-down” Brexit if they failed to agree and criticising potential resignations and leadership manoeuvring.

The paper presents NeuroAdapter, an end-to-end framework for reconstructing visual stimuli from fMRI activity. Unlike two-stage approaches that map brain signals into intermediate image or text embedding spaces, NeuroAdapter directly conditions a pretrained Stable Diffusion model on parcel-wise brain embeddings through cross-attention. Only the parcel-wise mapping and new cross-attention modules are trained; the remaining diffusion model parameters stay frozen. Training incorporates fMRI token dropout and min-SNR loss weighting. During evaluation, a brain encoder selects candidate reconstructions whose predicted neural responses correlate most strongly with measured activity.

Experiments on the Natural Scene Dataset show competitive reconstruction performance, particularly on high-level semantic metrics. Improvements on low-level image metrics are more modest than those of methods with dedicated low-level feature pathways. Additional evaluations on NSD-Imagery and Deeprecon demonstrate generalization to mental imagery and reconstruction of some visual properties from categories absent during training.

The paper also introduces the Image-Brain BI-directional interpretability framework, IBBI. It analyzes cross-attention across diffusion steps to quantify relative attention assigned to brain parcels and map where specific brain regions attend within reconstructed images. Perturbation experiments show that masking low-level regions preserves semantic content, whereas masking high-level regions substantially changes it.

The authors identify variability in generated image quality as a limitation, partly addressed by encoder-based selection. They argue that image-quality metrics alone may not establish faithful brain decoding and propose interpretability analysis as a complementary evaluation approach.

Earth experiences total solar eclipses because the moon is about 400 times smaller than the sun but also about 400 times closer, making them appear equally sized. The moon moves away from Earth about an inch and a half annually. In roughly 600 million years, it will appear too small to completely cover the sun, ending total solar eclipses on Earth.

In Bond v. District Court (1984), the Colorado Supreme Court reviewed an order requiring the Bond family to disclose mental health treatment records in their negligence lawsuit against YMCA of the Rockies. The lawsuit followed four-year-old Erin Bond’s severe injuries after falling from a YMCA truck and being run over.

The court held that the family waived physician-patient and psychologist-patient privileges by seeking damages for mental suffering and psychiatric care. However, waiver did not eliminate the possibility of a protective order under Colorado Rule of Civil Procedure 26(c).

The family had provided a psychological evaluation report detailing diagnoses, recommended treatment, and projected costs. An affidavit from the clinic’s director stated that disclosure of detailed therapy records could seriously harm family members and undermine their treatment. The Supreme Court concluded that this evidence demonstrated embarrassment and oppression warranting consideration alongside YMCA’s discovery interests.

The trial court abused its discretion by failing to balance the family’s interest in confidential treatment communications against YMCA’s need for evidence to contest the damages claims. The Supreme Court remanded for reconsideration under that balancing standard, without deciding whether the original disclosure ruling was necessarily incorrect. It noted that confidential document review, court-appointed experts, and tailored protective orders could help accommodate both parties’ interests.

During her acceptance speech for Choice Summer Movie Actress at the 2017 Teen Choice Awards, Zendaya urged young people to stay educated, pay attention to injustice, and use their voices against wrongdoing. She emphasized their power as future leaders to improve the world.

Coach Laviolette said his team was outskated, lost puck battles, struggled to generate effective shots and took costly undisciplined penalties. With one Stanley Cup game remaining at home, he emphasized returning to the team’s skating-based style and drawing on its veteran experience.

Doctors concluded that Erik’s healing had progressed as far as it would. Laviolette praised his return, describing him as physical and potentially the team’s best forward through two periods. Doug’s absence would be significant, but the coach rejected injury excuses and expected others to contribute. He also expected a strong performance from Joe despite his difficult recovery from knee surgery.

Laviolette acknowledged pregame anxiety and crowd influence but said execution, effort and special teams would determine the game. He described both teams as well-conditioned and emphasized the opportunity to compete for the Cup.

InfoWorld provides publicity and logo-use guidelines for Technology of the Year Award winners. Physical awards and reprints can be ordered through YGS Group, which sets production costs. Winners may purchase a license to use the award logo, which must remain unaltered, separate from other graphics, and at least one logo width or one inch from company and product names, whichever is greater.

Press communications must use approved naming conventions, identify winning subsidiaries rather than parent organizations, and attribute supplied quotes to Doug Dineley. Modified quotes require InfoWorld approval. The publication must first be identified as “IDG’s InfoWorld.”

The annual awards recognize innovative IT products tested during the preceding year, with final selections made by InfoWorld’s Reviews staff. Approved award descriptions and corporate boilerplate are available for publicity.

UN agencies and academic institutions support clean-water access through infrastructure, fundraising and innovation. Projects include a new water system in South Sudan, UNICEF’s restaurant-based fundraising in Vietnam, water-harvesting technology in Singapore, and UNHCR-supported standpipes serving about 800 people in Kyrgyzstan. The UN General Assembly called for dialogue to improve coordination on water-related sustainable development goals. General Assembly President Miroslav Lajčák urged preventing future wars and treating water appropriately.

Artificial intelligence offers higher education opportunities to personalize learning, improve administrative efficiency, support research, and inform institutional decisions. Potential applications include adaptive learning platforms, intelligent tutoring, automated grading, academic advising, predictive analytics, and immersive learning experiences. Accessibility tools, including transcription, translation, and alternative content formats, can support diverse student needs.

Effective implementation requires clear institutional objectives, reliable infrastructure, faculty and staff training, pilot projects, stakeholder participation, and continuous evaluation. The passage recommends governance committees, partnerships with technology providers, and policies addressing transparency, accountability, privacy, security, fairness, and inclusion. AI should support rather than replace educators, with human oversight maintained in critical decisions.

Challenges include implementation and maintenance costs, unequal access, faculty resistance, algorithmic bias, privacy breaches, technological dependence, cheating, potential teacher displacement, and reduced human interaction. Biased data can amplify discrimination, while excessive reliance on AI may weaken students’ critical-thinking and problem-solving skills.

The passage anticipates wider use of personalized learning, automated administration, predictive analytics, and assistive technologies, alongside changes in assessment, institutional roles, and AI ethics education. Its author recommends strategic institutional adoption but personally advises against AI use in school education and undergraduate and postgraduate learning and assignments. Research use is supported when researchers examine outputs for appropriateness, accuracy, and fairness. Referenced findings also present an alternative to outright bans: institutional guidelines, faculty training, revised assessments, and discussions with students about ethical AI use.

The Put-Call ratio measures put option volume or open interest relative to calls and is used to assess market sentiment. Calls provide the right to buy shares at a predetermined price within a specified period; puts provide the right to sell and can protect against falling prices.

High ratios generally indicate fear, while low ratios indicate complacency. Extreme readings are sometimes interpreted as contrarian signals. Ratios vary across indices and stocks, so there are no universal thresholds for favorable or unfavorable readings.

Volume measures contracts traded during a period, whereas open interest counts contracts still open at the end of the trading day. Ratio data are widely available on trading platforms and financial websites, though free downloadable data can be difficult to find.

The authors recommend backtesting rather than relying on indicator claims. Their reported backtest produced an average gain of 6.36% per trade after 115 days, excluding dividends. They consider the results unimpressive and favor other sentiment indicators, particularly the VIX.

The 2018 Chevrolet Equinox’s available 1.6L turbo-diesel engine offers highway fuel consumption of 6.0 L/100km in the FWD model, expected to lead its segment. It produces 240 lb-ft of torque, features stop/start technology and supports B20 biodiesel. The redesigned compact SUV offers increased cargo space, connectivity and available safety features. Pricing starts at $27,145, including destination charges; the turbo-diesel version starts at $35,645 and goes on sale in the fall.

The LakeSmart Team is delivering its summer Dock Talk program to promote healthy ecosystems on Lake of the Woods and neighbouring lakes. An initiative of the Lake of the Woods and District Property Owners Association, the program shares guidance on shoreline landscaping, septic systems, invasive species prevention and safe boating. The three-member student team will attend the Matiowki Farmer’s Market on Wednesdays in July and August, participate in scheduled presentations and tours, and offer presentations to lake groups on request.

The passage describes systems and methods for managing computing resources that host virtual desktop instances on a service provider network. These methods seek to reduce unused resource consumption while maintaining availability and limiting reconnection delays.

A computing resource instance manager monitors client connections, disconnections, and inactivity, then applies policies to determine whether and when to shut down underlying computing instances. Disconnections may be detected through session gateways, protocol-specific software agents, login and logoff events, or network traffic patterns indicating inactivity.

Shutdown policies may be defined by the service provider, customer administrators, or authorized end users. Policies can require immediate shutdown, a waiting period after disconnection, shutdown only during specified hours, or continued operation. Administrators may delegate policy selection to individual users.

Historical connection and disconnection data may support predictive models that proactively start or stop computing instances. Models may be refined through continued monitoring, with goals of keeping resources ready before users connect and minimizing operation without connected users. When usage patterns are too variable for reliable predictions, default policies may apply.

When a computing instance shuts down, associated storage volumes may be detached but retained. Upon reconnection, the provider may restart the original instance or launch another instance of the same or a different type, reattach the storage volumes, and relaunch applications.

The supporting infrastructure may provide virtualized computing and storage services, public and private IP addressing, virtual private networks, and overlay networking. Virtual desktops provide remote operating systems and applications, with user input transmitted from client devices and desktop output returned to them. Separate desktop stores preserve user data and preferences; replication and backups may support recovery from failures.

Connection records may also support billing that distinguishes periods when users are connected from periods when desktops remain active without a connection.

The Sansa c200 manual covers setup, media transfer, playback, recording, settings, troubleshooting, warranty terms, and software licensing.

- **Battery and controls:** The player uses a rechargeable lithium-ion battery installed in the rear compartment according to the battery icon and pins. The Hold switch disables all function keys when locked, indicated by visible orange coloring.
- **Computer connection:** Connecting by USB allows the computer to detect the player as “Sansa c200.” USB 2.0 is required for high-speed transfer. Files can be copied in MSC mode or transferred and synchronized in MTP mode. AutoDetect defaults to MTP, which supports Windows Media Player 10. Follow the computer’s safe-removal procedure before disconnecting.
- **Supported media:** Audio formats include MP3, WAV, WMA, and secure WMA. Unsupported formats must be converted. MP3 podcasts at 32–320 kbps are supported. Photo transfer requires Sansa Media Converter, which imports JPEG, TIFF, PNG, BMP, and GIF files.
- **Playback and photos:** Navigation controls support track selection, skipping, fast-forwarding, and rewinding. Music options include repeat, shuffle, preset and custom equalizers, and GoList management. Photos can be viewed individually or in slideshows with random order, looping, and adjustable slide duration.
- **Radio and recording:** Users can tune or scan FM stations, manage presets, and record broadcasts. Automatic station scanning erases existing presets. The built-in microphone supports voice recording. Voice and FM recordings are accessible through the Music menu.
- **Settings and troubleshooting:** Settings include backlight timing, contrast, automatic power-off or sleep, USB mode, and factory reset. Troubleshooting covers playback rights, file conversion, CD copying, missing ID3 information, and firmware updates.
- **Support and warranty:** Technical support is available at 1-866-726-3475 and through SanDisk’s website. The nontransferable one-year limited warranty applies to the original purchaser and excludes specified third-party issues, misuse, improper installation, unauthorized repair, modification, and accidental damage. SanDisk may repair, replace, or refund the product and does not cover lost data.
- **Software and rights:** The software license permits limited personal use and restricts modification, reverse engineering, rental, and other activities. Software is supplied without warranties, subject to liability limitations. Violating the agreement may terminate the license and require destruction of software copies. Windows Media DRM rights to acquire new protected-content licenses may be revoked if security is compromised; unprotected playback remains unaffected.
- **Disposal:** Do not discard the device with unsorted household waste. Consult local waste authorities for collection and return options.

Harvey Weinstein was indicted in New York on rape and criminal sex act charges involving two women, advancing the first criminal case arising from numerous sexual misconduct allegations against him. Weinstein denied nonconsensual sex and declined to testify before the grand jury, citing insufficient preparation time and political pressure. District Attorney Cyrus Vance Jr. defended the prosecution. Weinstein was free on $1 million bail with electronic monitoring. Gov. Andrew Cuomo ordered an investigation into Vance’s handling of a separate 2015 allegation that did not result in charges.

Touch Football Australia and the NRL announced an NRL Touch Premiership beginning May 18. Elite male and female players will represent teams aligned with six NRL clubs, playing nationally televised curtain-raisers across seven rounds. Ipswich Jillaroos player Ali Brigginshaw said the partnership could raise touch football’s profile and support transitions between the codes. She uses touch football to maintain fitness and skills but expects her rugby league schedule and Jillaroos contract to prevent her participation.

Apple Inc.’s Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended September 24, 2022 describes its business, operations and principal risks.

Apple designs, manufactures and markets smartphones, personal computers, tablets, wearables and accessories. Its products include iPhone, Mac, iPad, AirPods, Apple TV and Apple Watch. Services include advertising, AppleCare, cloud storage, digital content and subscriptions, and payment services.

The company serves consumer, business, education, enterprise and government customers. Direct distribution accounted for 38% of 2022 net sales, while indirect channels accounted for 62%. Sales outside the United States represented a majority of total net sales. Substantially all hardware manufacturing was performed by outsourcing partners primarily in Asia, and certain components came from single or limited sources.

Apple had approximately 164,000 full-time equivalent employees as of September 24, 2022. It emphasizes research and development, intellectual property protection, employee development, inclusion and workplace safety. Net sales historically have been highest in the first fiscal quarter, partly because of holiday demand.

Principal risks include:
- Economic weakness, inflation, currency fluctuations, trade restrictions, geopolitical conflicts, natural disasters and COVID-19 disruptions.
- Intense competition, rapid technological change and unsuccessful product introductions.
- Dependence on suppliers, manufacturing partners, distributors, third-party software developers and content providers.
- Component shortages, product defects, inventory write-downs and intellectual property licensing constraints.
- Cybersecurity incidents, confidential information losses and information technology disruptions.
- Employee recruitment and retention challenges, acquisition risks and substantial retail-store commitments.
- Litigation, antitrust scrutiny, privacy obligations and changing regulations, including potential changes to App Store practices.
- Fluctuating margins, investment and receivables credit risks, tax liabilities and stock-price volatility.

In Epic Games’ lawsuit, the district court ruled for Apple on nine of ten claims and on Apple’s breach-of-contract claims, but found certain App Store guidelines violated California’s unfair competition law. Both parties appealed, and Apple obtained a stay pending appeal.

Apple’s common stock trades on Nasdaq under AAPL. Non-affiliates’ stock holdings had an aggregate market value of approximately $2.83 trillion on March 25, 2022. As of October 14, 2022, approximately 15.91 billion common shares were outstanding, with 23,838 shareholders of record.

To replace an HDD with a SanDisk SSD, shut down the computer, disconnect power, and remove the notebook battery if applicable. For notebooks, transfer any brackets or adapters and firmly connect the SSD to the drive bay’s SATA connector. For desktops, remove the HDD, install the SSD using a 3.5-inch mounting adapter if needed, and reconnect SATA data and power cables. Close the drive bay or case, restore power, and start the computer. The old HDD may be retained as a backup.

Leapfrog’s latest Hospital Safety Grades show improvements in patient safety. Of approximately 2,500 hospitals graded, 30% earned an “A,” 28% a “B,” 35% a “C,” 6% a “D” and 1% an “F.” Forty-six hospitals received their first “A,” including five previously graded “F.” Maryland moved out of the bottom five state rankings, with three “A” hospitals, while Washington, D.C., received its first “A” hospital since 2013. Hawaii, Idaho, Rhode Island, Massachusetts and Virginia had the highest percentages of “A” hospitals. Forty-nine hospitals have earned an “A” in every update since spring 2012. Leapfrog updates grades twice yearly and invited public comments on proposed methodology changes for fall 2018.

The Boathouse at City Point opens June 17 on Hopewell’s riverfront, becoming Central Virginia’s fourth Boathouse location. It features indoor dining, a patio, event space and a reservable chef’s table. Part of Hopewell’s riverfront revitalization, the restaurant will offer coastal dishes with locally sourced ingredients, serving lunch and dinner daily and Sunday brunch.

The disclosure describes apparatuses and methods for AI-based image encoding and decoding intended to reduce bitrate. A down-scaling deep neural network (DNN) reduces an original image’s resolution before conventional encoding. After conventional decoding, an up-scaling DNN can increase the reconstructed image’s resolution. The down-scaling and up-scaling networks are jointly trained using shared loss information.

The encoder transmits compressed image data and AI data indicating whether AI down-scaling occurred and providing information for corresponding up-scaling. AI data may include resolution differences, target resolution, bitrate, codec information, network-setting identifiers, or DNN settings. Image data and AI data may be transmitted together or separately.

The decoder determines whether to perform AI up-scaling based on AI data and the availability of the required network and settings. If AI data is absent, down-scaling was not performed, or the up-scaling network is unavailable, it may output the conventionally decoded image. Alternatives include non-DNN up-scaling or requesting up-scaling by a display apparatus. Conventional decoders can decode the compressed image data without processing AI data.

Network settings or architectures may be selected according to resolution, bitrate, codec, decoding parameters, display capabilities, stored settings, or user preferences. Settings may apply to an entire video, groups of frames, or individual frames. Pixel-position information and encoding-parameter maps may provide additional inputs to the up-scaling network.

Described network architectures use convolution and activation layers and may combine a convolutional output with a bypass-scaled image. The encoder’s decision to down-scale may depend on image resolution, image or object type, and network availability. The apparatuses may use dedicated processors or software running on general-purpose processors.

GNU C Library 2.28 will build and run on GNU/Hurd without out-of-tree patches. GNU Guix can run on Android devices, though installation requires significant effort. Announced alongside Node.js v10, npm@6 introduces new security features for developers working with open-source code. Node.js 10.0 is expected to support it soon.

Madison Realty Capital provided JDS Development Group with a $137 million construction loan to fully capitalize Monad Terrace, a 59-residence waterfront development in South Beach designed by Jean Nouvel in collaboration with Kobi Karp Architecture and Interior Design. Sales were averaging nearly $2,000 per square foot, with a penthouse under contract at $2,700 per square foot. Residences range from two to five bedrooms and feature private elevators, custom interiors and outdoor terraces. Climate-resilience measures include elevating the building 11.5 feet. Construction was underway, with completion estimated for fall 2019.

TeraWulf is transitioning from bitcoin mining to digital infrastructure. An expanded Fluidstack agreement and $3.2 billion Google commitment position it for $760 million in annual revenue. The company plans to reach 1,150 MW of power capacity by 2030, potentially increasing annual revenue to $1.5 billion. The author considers its valuation attractive based on growth prospects, contracted revenues and Google’s support, while disclosing no positions in the companies mentioned and noting investment risks.

TI offers weekly product-update notifications through ti.com and engineering support through TI E2E forums. Revised documents include change details in their revision histories. Integrated circuits require ESD precautions to prevent performance degradation or failure.

Mechanical, packaging, and ordering information is subject to change without notice. Drawing notes address dimensions, tolerances, solder masks, and stencil design.

TI provides technical and design resources “AS IS,” without warranties. Developers are responsible for product selection, application design, validation, testing, and compliance with applicable requirements. Resource use is permitted only for developing applications using the described TI products; other reproduction and display are prohibited. TI disclaims responsibility for claims arising from resource use, and its products remain subject to applicable sales terms.

The disclosure describes methods, systems, and stored instructions for controlling light-source luminance in near-eye displays used for virtual, augmented, and mixed reality. The techniques aim to reduce power consumption while maintaining user experience by accounting for the eye’s lower sensitivity to light outside the foveal region.

A display controller selects a maximum-luminance location based on the user’s field of view. For the same input display value, a light source nearer this location emits at a higher luminance than one farther away. Display zones may use different relationships between input values and luminance, with larger luminance ranges near the maximum-luminance location. Some embodiments limit luminance differences to below a threshold noticeable to the user. Individually driven light sources may include OLEDs or micro-LEDs. Examples describe power reductions ranging from about 5% to 40%.

Eye tracking can dynamically update the higher-luminance region as the user’s gaze changes. The disclosed tracking techniques illuminate the eye, capture reflected light, identify pupil and corneal-reflection features, and estimate gaze direction. System and user calibration may improve accuracy. Alternative techniques use image comparisons, mapping functions, machine-learning models, or physical eye models.

The display implementations include headsets and glasses, with optional tracking sensors, external cameras, input devices, and consoles. Waveguide-based designs couple projected image light into a transparent substrate and direct it toward the eye while allowing environmental light to pass through. Images may be generated simultaneously by emitter arrays or assembled through synchronized scanning.

A controller architecture includes an application processor and display-driver integrated circuit. Eye-tracking data may be checked for accuracy and used to generate a map assigning luminance bands to display zones. A timing controller then instructs gate and source drivers to operate the light sources according to that map.

Archaeologists using airborne lidar technology discovered more than 60,000 previously unknown Mayan structures in Guatemala’s jungle, including house foundations, fortifications, elevated causeways and a seven-story pyramid. Lidar uses laser pulses to create detailed three-dimensional maps of terrain beneath vegetation. The findings suggest the Mayans controlled extensive territories with sophisticated trade networks and industrial-scale food production, rather than isolated city-states. Researchers believe the population may have reached 10–15 million, substantially exceeding earlier estimates. They also found evidence of landscape modifications to irrigate crops and protect buildings from flooding.

The PGA848’s linear input range extends within 3V of either power supply, maintaining common-mode rejection across temperatures. Its valid common-mode range depends on common-mode and differential input voltages, gain, and reference voltage.

A typical application drives the ADS8860 16-bit, 1MSPS SAR ADC using single-ended or differential signals. The PGA848 input stage uses ±15V supplies, while its output stage shares the ADC’s 5.3V supply to prevent ADC input overload during PGA overdrive. A REF6250 provides the 5V ADC reference; a precision divider and OPA192 buffer establish the PGA848’s 2.5V reference.

Three filters address input interference, feedback bandwidth, and ADC charge kickback. Nominal bandwidth is 318kHz, decreasing to 277kHz at the high end of feedback-resistor tolerance, with −0.1dB flatness maintained to 41kHz. The reference buffer uses dual feedback for stability; changes to bypass capacitance require recalculating stability components and verifying more than 60° phase margin.

Nominal PGA848 performance is specified with ±15V input- and output-stage supplies. Supply voltages above 40V (±20V) permanently damage the device. Recommended PCB practices include symmetrical input paths, closely placed 0.1µF supply bypass capacitors, separation of sensitive and noisy traces, minimized leakage and parasitic capacitance, and reduced thermal junctions. Appropriate ESD precautions are required.

TI provides PSpice and TINA-TI simulation tools, related documentation, update notifications, and support forums. Mechanical and ordering information may change without notice. Technical resources are supplied “as is”; developers remain responsible for product selection, application validation, testing, and compliance.

Hong Liu explains how large N gauge theories suggest a connection to string theory. Their expansions share a topological structure when the string coupling is identified with \(1/N\). Single-trace operators correspond to string states, the leading large N limit corresponds to classical string theory, and higher-genus contributions represent string-loop quantum corrections.

Feynman diagrams can be interpreted as discretizations of two-dimensional surfaces. Summing diagrams of a fixed genus resembles summing over worldsheet geometries. Establishing an actual equivalence requires identifying diagram weights with a string action, which is difficult because the appropriate target spacetime and worldsheet degrees of freedom are unknown. A continuum geometric description is expected at strong coupling, where complicated diagrams provide fine discretizations. Explicit connections are possible in simpler matrix integrals and matrix quantum mechanics.

Adding fields in fundamental representations introduces surfaces with boundaries, corresponding to open strings. Other symmetry groups can introduce non-orientable surfaces and strings.

A straightforward string description of four-dimensional QCD encounters obstacles. The simplest strings require particular spacetime dimensions for quantum consistency. Compactifying additional dimensions still produces a four-dimensional massless spin-2 particle, incompatible with QCD under the Weinberg–Witten theorem. These difficulties motivate considering an additional noncompact spatial dimension.

The holographic principle suggests that a gravitational theory could correspond to a nongravitational theory in one fewer dimension. Requiring a five-dimensional geometry to preserve four-dimensional Poincaré symmetry restricts its metric to a warped form. Additional scale invariance fixes the warp factor and yields anti-de Sitter spacetime. Thus, if a large N conformal field theory in \(d\) dimensions admits this string description, the corresponding strings should propagate in \(AdS_{d+1}\). This is presented as a necessary consistency condition, not a proof.

The lecture traces developments leading to this correspondence, including large N expansions, string theory’s gravitational interpretation, matrix models, holography, and D-branes. Maldacena supplied explicit examples in 1997, and Witten subsequently connected them to the holographic principle. Deriving the correspondence will require studying string spectra and D-brane physics.

Finally, Liu introduces strings as worldsheets embedded in a target spacetime. The Nambu–Goto action measures worldsheet area using the induced metric. Introducing an independent worldsheet metric gives the classically equivalent Polyakov action, avoiding the square-root form. Quantization integrates over both embeddings and worldsheet metrics, reformulating the problem as two-dimensional gravity coupled to scalar fields.

Companies planned to enlist about 100,000 smaller suppliers. The White House characterized the bank’s activities as corporate welfare; supporters argued its financing helped U.S. companies compete internationally. Enron received $135 million in Ex-Im financing in fiscal 2000.
- Dutch short-term gas trading was expanding, with Enron among active participants. Disputes over Gasunie’s balancing charges, transportation tariffs and storage access continued to impede competition.
- Southern California Edison’s tentative $2.7 billion transmission-line sale to California could take until 2002 to close. Suppliers, including a group involving Enron Wind, were suing Edison over unpaid bills.
- Many California power contracts announced by Governor Gray Davis remained unsigned or disputed. Enron said terms were agreed except for credit-related details. Nonpayment had also shut down small generators capable of producing 1,800 megawatts.

A five-metre bronze sculpture, “The Last Three,” in New York commemorates Africa’s last three Northern White Rhinos. Critic Jerry Saltz condemned it, while supporters praised its efforts to raise awareness of imperilled rhinos.

Ultralight backpacking is defined here as carrying a base weight of 10 pounds or less, excluding worn clothing and consumables. More broadly, it is an approach to staying comfortable, safe, and well-fed while carrying less.

The author recommends first removing unnecessary items rather than buying lighter equipment. Evaluate whether each item is needed for warmth, comfort, food, or safety. After eliminating extras, focus on the heaviest components: shelter, sleep system, and backpack. Choose shelter and sleeping equipment before determining the required pack size.

Experimenting with alternatives, such as quilts or tarp camping, can help identify what works for individual needs. Carrying less also simplifies packing, unpacking, and adjusting routines, including eating separately from camp.

Reaching a particular weight immediately is not essential. Continued experimentation and refinement can reduce unnecessary equipment and make the outdoor experience more enjoyable.

Researchers investigated whether a new RSV variant contributed to the unusually early, severe U.S. surge in autumn 2022 by sequencing samples from 105 symptomatic patients in the Greater Boston Area. They obtained 77 near-complete or partial genomes: 91% RSV-A and 9% RSV-B.

Analysis identified multiple pre-existing lineages, including at least 10 RSV-A lineages. Several lineages were shared with Washington State samples. Genetic divergence was consistent with estimated evolutionary rates, rather than accelerated evolution.

These findings are inconsistent with a single, highly transmissible RSV lineage causing the surge. The authors recommend investigating non-viral factors, including changes in immunity associated with altered RSV circulation during the COVID-19 pandemic. The study was a preprint not certified by peer review.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examined whether the BCHE-K genetic variant was associated with age at Alzheimer disease (AD) diagnosis in APOE4 carriers. Researchers conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline clinical, genetic, cerebrospinal fluid biomarker, and brain imaging data from 45 clinical trial participants aged 50–74 with biomarker-confirmed mild AD.

Among 33 APOE4 carriers, the 11 who also carried BCHE-K were diagnosed an average of 6.4 years earlier than noncarriers: 60.6 versus 67.0 years. This association remained significant after adjustment for sex and baseline cognitive score. No similar association appeared among the 12 APOE4 noncarriers. APOE4 carriers with BCHE-K had slightly greater amyloid and tau accumulation despite being more than six years younger at baseline.

APOE4 homozygotes, particularly those carrying BCHE-K, exhibited an amyloid-predominant, limbic-amnestic phenotype, with relatively lower tau pathology and glial activation markers. Regression analyses associated greater amyloid accumulation with APOE4 carriage, larger ventricular volume, less synaptic injury, and less tau pathology. Greater tau pathology was associated with neuroaxonal damage, synaptic injury, and glial activation.

The authors propose that interactions among cholinergic signaling, glial function, and amyloid clearance may help explain these genotype-associated differences and could inform prognosis and treatment research.

Limitations include the small, potentially unrepresentative sample, cross-sectional design, diagnostic assessment variability, and uncertainties in biomarker interpretation. Findings should not be extrapolated to patients older than 75 and require confirmation in larger prospective longitudinal studies.

Ben Affleck was photographed appearing upbeat at what was believed to be an outpatient treatment centre in Los Angeles, seven months after announcing treatment for alcohol addiction. In March, he described rehab as the first of many steps toward recovery, expressed his desire to be the best father possible, and thanked family, friends and estranged wife Jennifer Garner for their support.

The passage argues that Russia unlawfully seized the Cape Horn Pigeon while it was whaling on the high seas, violating treaty rights and international law. Russia’s inquiry claimed the vessel had entered Russian waters but found no grounds for confiscation; Russia attributed the arrest to a misunderstanding, returned the vessel, and offered indemnity. The owners, officers, and crew claimed $45,000 for lost vessel service, estimated from average catches on previous voyages minus the catch already taken. The passage characterizes this loss as direct damage and cites earlier arbitration decisions allowing compensation for lost profits.

The lecture examines finite impulse response (FIR) filter structures and practical factors affecting digital filter implementation.

FIR filters have finitely many nonzero impulse-response samples, and their difference equations correspond to finite convolution sums. They can use direct, transposed, or cascade structures.

For linear-phase FIR filters with symmetric impulse responses, paired delayed inputs can be added before multiplication by shared coefficients. This reduces the number of multiplications by approximately half without reducing the required delays. An eight-sample example uses seven delays and four coefficients.

Frequency-sampling structures represent filters using discrete Fourier transform coefficients, which are samples of the frequency response. They combine a common section with parallel recursive branches whose poles are canceled by zeros, leaving an overall FIR response. Although these cancellations present finite-register-length drawbacks, the structure offers two principal advantages:
- Zero-valued frequency samples allow corresponding branches to be omitted, potentially reducing computation and storage.
- Filters with the same impulse-response length can share much of the structure, making it useful for filter banks.

Mathematically equivalent filter structures differ in practical requirements, including delay registers, multiplication counts, modularity, and sensitivity to finite-register-length effects. Arithmetic rounding or truncation introduces output noise, while coefficient quantization changes system parameters and pole locations.

The lecture explains that clustered poles become more sensitive to coefficient errors when implemented through higher-order polynomials. Cascade and parallel implementations using low-order sections are therefore less sensitive than direct-form implementations.

The realization of individual second-order sections also matters. A direct-form pole-pair section quantizes parameters involving \(r^2\) and \(2r\cos\theta\), restricting realizable poles to intersections of circles and vertical lines. A coupled-form section quantizes \(r\cos\theta\) and \(r\sin\theta\), producing a rectangular grid of realizable pole locations. These examples illustrate why choosing a filter structure requires attention to both overall organization and individual section implementation.

Researchers analyzed US death certificates from 2014–2020 to assess cancer mortality during the first year of COVID-19, comparing underlying-cause records with records mentioning cancer anywhere on the certificate. They estimated excess deaths against modeled pre-pandemic trends and examined national patterns and those in New York, California, and Texas.

Underlying-cause cancer mortality showed no significant increase. However, records mentioning cancer showed approximately 12,000 excess deaths nationally in 2020, a statistically significant 2% increase over baseline. Hematological cancers had the largest relative increase, at 5%, while pancreatic and lung cancers showed no excess mortality. In comparison, multiple-cause mortality increased by 39% for diabetes and 31% for Alzheimer’s disease. State-level cancer increases were generally modest and statistically nonsignificant.

A demographic model suggested that differences in age, population size, and baseline mortality could explain much of the variation between conditions. High competing mortality from cancer, particularly pancreatic and lung cancers, could limit the relative increase attributable to COVID-19. The authors favored this explanation over the hypothesis that cancer-related immunosuppression provides protection. Changes in death-certificate coding also affected observed patterns, demonstrating the importance of examining multiple causes of death.

Limitations included uncertain model inputs, possible shielding among cancer patients, wide confidence intervals in state-level estimates, and restriction to mortality during 2020. The time-trend analysis does not establish causation. Longer-term effects of disrupted cancer care, vaccination, hospitalization, and Long COVID require further study.

Nabors sold Quail Tools for more than its purchase price and plans to use the proceeds to reduce debt by 25%. The author suggests Nabors’ key U.S. and Saudi Arabian markets are near cyclical troughs. Despite rising 70% from recent lows, the stock remains below historical valuations, with the author seeing further upside potential.

Foreigners entered a bivouac despite warnings and were eventually escorted out. K. Otori denied demanding the dismissal of Korea’s naval instructor, Mr. Collwell, and requested that C. T. Gardner retract telegrams reporting such a demand. Gardner directed Otori to seek information through usual channels.

Mr. Gresham informed Mr. Bayard that war between China and Japan appeared possible. Korea sought U.S. assistance because Chinese and Japanese troops threatened its independence. Mr. Sill reported that Korea’s rebellion had been suppressed, but foreign troops remained; China favored simultaneous withdrawal, while Japan refused. Korea reported that Japan conditioned withdrawal on political changes. The United States expressed sympathy and willingness to exert friendly influence but insisted on impartial neutrality and ruled out joint intervention with other powers.

This descriptive study examined the readiness, expertise, and educational multimedia learning needs of students in the Faculty of Industrial Education. An online survey of 124 students assessed access to production tools, multimedia design skills, and training needs across 11 topics.

Students demonstrated substantial access to devices, with notebooks used by 93.3%, smartphones by 88.9%, and tablets by 48.9%. Overall multimedia expertise averaged 3.51 out of five, classified as high, while learning needs averaged 4.62, classified as the highest level. The assessment table identified copyright and educational metaverse creation as the lowest-rated areas of expertise. Learning needs were high across all assessed topics.

The study emphasised targeted learning materials and training to help future teachers create and integrate educational multimedia. Its findings were intended to inform policymakers, course developers, and professional development providers. Limitations included the small sample and limited population diversity; further research was recommended with larger, more diverse groups and a focus on effective multimedia learning materials.

The passage examines interdisciplinary basic music education, integrating music with mathematics, language, science, psychology, technology, and other arts. Reviewed research links this approach to cognitive development, academic achievement, creativity, critical thinking, cultural awareness, and social-emotional skills. Applications range from preschool music-based games to university programs combining music with engineering or psychology.

The study combines a qualitative literature review and content analysis with a single-participant case study using a semi-structured interview. The participant, a social studies teacher studying music at a Fine Arts Faculty, described inadequate foundational music education and university instructors’ assumptions about students’ prior knowledge. The participant recommended preparatory instruction and differentiated classes reflecting students’ backgrounds and proficiency.

Other concerns included limited practical teacher preparation, insufficient workshop facilities, and weaknesses in broader academic engagement. Recommended courses included creative drama, media literacy, material design, music and movement, speech training, and practically taught learning and developmental psychology. The participant also supported learning-style assessments to encourage self-understanding.

Teaching recommendations emphasized practical application of approaches such as Kodály, Suzuki, Orff, and Dalcroze; micro-teaching with recorded lessons and classroom feedback; instructor demonstrations; and preparation for teaching where instruments are unavailable. Suggested instrumental training included song-accompaniment repertoires for bağlama and piano, alongside guitar and ukulele.

The passage concludes that interdisciplinary music education should extend beyond technical musical skills to support broader intellectual, emotional, and cultural development. It recommends revising curricula and education policies to encourage collaboration across disciplines, developing programs with teachers, strengthening music teachers’ interdisciplinary competencies, and expanding related research and practice.

Anton Shekhovtsov’s “Tango Noir: Russia and the Western Far Right” examines Moscow’s cultivation of Western far-right activists, tracing Soviet precedents and developments under Vladimir Putin. The book identifies Russia’s 2008 invasion of Georgia and the international condemnation it provoked as a turning point toward full-scale information warfare.

Russian state-controlled media, particularly RT, use fringe activists to portray the West as chaotic and Russia as an alternative global power. Shekhovtsov identifies three tactics: “nudge propaganda,” which promotes Russian interests through activists; “narrative laundering,” which obscures the origins of false stories; and selective sourcing. Far-right election observers have also helped legitimize Russia’s annexation of Crimea.

The book describes competing groups around Putin and interconnected networks of activists, think tanks, oligarchs, diplomats and political officials seeking influence abroad. Shekhovtsov concludes that these efforts have yielded limited results, although Germany may represent a recent success. The review notes omissions concerning Brexit and alleged interference in the US election, while highlighting concerns about Russian paramilitary assistance encouraging violence among Europe’s far right.

Florida International University reopened Monday in mourning, four days after a pedestrian bridge collapse killed six people, including student Alexa Duran. The university planned a moment of silence and a Wednesday vigil. Officials focused on supporting victims’ families and cooperating with investigators. Southwest Eighth Street remained closed indefinitely, raising concerns about traffic congestion.

Environmental education supports sustainable development by fostering awareness, knowledge, attitudes, skills, participation, and evaluation abilities needed to prevent and address environmental problems. International initiatives, including the 1972 Stockholm conference, the 1975 Belgrade workshop, and the 1992 Earth Summit, emphasized resource conservation, environmental learning, and global cooperation.

Environmental education is presented as a lifelong, interdisciplinary process addressing natural and human-made environments. Its principles include active participation, attention to regional differences within a global perspective, consideration of development impacts, and preparation for current and future environmental challenges. Effective school implementation requires integrating environmental topics across subjects and developing teachers’ knowledge and teaching practices. Formal and non-formal education, practical activities, and outdoor learning connect environmental understanding with real situations. Studies cited in the passage report benefits for students’ knowledge, attitudes, retention, and environmental skills, including among learners with disabilities.

Environmental knowledge encompasses natural resources, social environments, environmental technology, waste, and pollution. Understanding environmental interdependence, ecosystem relationships, chain reactions, resilience, and change over time supports responsible behavior and resource management.

Sustainable development meets present needs without compromising future generations’ ability to meet theirs. It combines environmental preservation with economic progress, equitable resource distribution, and quality of life. The passage identifies environmental sustainability as a foundation for the interconnected goals of social and economic development.

Recommended practices include reducing energy consumption, minimizing waste, conserving natural resources, and adopting clean technologies. Environmental management combines planning, conservation, scientific evidence, and technological, economic, social, and legal measures. Community cooperation and changes in everyday behavior are emphasized throughout.

Examples from Thailand include community learning initiatives, the Huai Sai development project, natural capital accounting, and ecosystem assessment. These illustrate approaches connecting environmental knowledge, participation, policy, conservation, and livelihoods. The passage concludes that environmental education and practical engagement can strengthen the awareness and skills necessary for sustained environmental improvement.

Teacher Caroline Hope, 37, died in Glasgow after contracting E.coli during colon cancer surgery in Turkey. Family and friends raised over £31,000 for her medical evacuation to Scotland. Her mother thanked donors and hospital staff who cared for her.

Two stackless assembler procedures use register-based interfaces to manage pre-memory stacks on all processor cores. Initialization configures processors, caches, stack regions, and MTRRs, adjusts stack addressing for protected or real mode, and creates UEFI_SEC_PEI_HAND_OFF. Status codes indicate successful allocation, stack reentry, or an unknown processor family. Removal preserves EBX and disables CAR mode once main memory is available, assuming stack relocation and MTRR synchronization are complete. AARCH64 APUs with PSP do not use the stack and very early macros; PSP initializes DRAM.

Alabama faces a challenge containing Texas A&M’s Christian Kirk, whom Nick Saban called probably the SEC’s best all-purpose player. In two games against Alabama, Kirk recorded 16 catches for 148 yards, a touchdown reception and a punt-return touchdown. This season, he is tied for the SEC lead with four touchdown catches and has returned a kickoff for a touchdown.

Initial coin offerings (ICOs) have increased sharply in Hong Kong and Singapore following bans in China and South Korea. Neither destination has specific ICO rules, and digital-token fundraising remains loosely regulated. Chinese companies have moved fundraising abroad to avoid legal risks, including Beijing-based Xender, which is seeking US$10 million through an ICO in Singapore. Bithumb reportedly plans to launch a “Bithumb Coin” ICO through a Singaporean corporation, while startup Zikto is reportedly preparing an ICO there. The passage lists 179 songs certified diamond by the Recording Industry Association of America (RIAA), in order of certification date. Diamond certification requires at least 10 million equivalent units from sales and streaming, plus an application from the artist or label.

Elton John’s “Something About the Way You Look Tonight / Candle in the Wind” was the first qualifying song, recognized in 1997, two years before the diamond award officially launched. It remains the only diamond-certified physical single. Shaboozey’s “A Bar Song (Tipsy)” is the latest recipient, certified September 15, 2025.

Drake holds the record with 10 diamond singles, including collaborations, followed by Post Malone with nine. Rihanna and The Weeknd each have seven; Rihanna leads female artists. Katy Perry and Bruno Mars each have six.

Perry’s “Teenage Dream” is the first and only album with four diamond-certified songs. Taylor Swift became the first female artist in US history with both a diamond-certified single and album when “Shake It Off” received certification in 2020.

The May 24, 2001 news compilation focuses on California’s energy crisis, proposed blackout measures, market investigations and political developments.

- Gov. Gray Davis’ administration was considering paying businesses to operate diesel backup generators during electricity emergencies. Officials described this as a last resort to prevent blackouts, while environmentalists and air-quality regulators warned of substantial pollution. The generators could supply about 550 megawatts.
- Davis was expected to require at least one hour’s notice before blackouts, with additional advance warnings under consideration for the public and law enforcement.
- California Public Utilities Commission President Loretta Lynch said investigators found evidence that generators varied plant output to increase prices. Generators cited legitimate operational, environmental and financial reasons for limiting production.
- El Paso Merchant Group President Ralph Eads denied manipulating California natural-gas prices. He testified that fixed-price hedges prevented the company from earning nearly $700 million in additional profits. California regulators and Southern California Edison alleged that the company withheld pipeline capacity.
- Reliant offered substantial electricity-price reductions if regulators relaxed operating-hour restrictions. Air-quality officials questioned the proposal, saying regulatory relief had already been granted or offered.
- President Bush agreed to meet Davis during his upcoming California visit. Davis sought wholesale electricity price caps, which Bush opposed.
- Sen. James Jeffords’ anticipated departure from the Republican Party could give Democrats Senate control and increase California’s influence over energy and environmental policy, lawmakers and lobbyists said.
- A Field Poll found widespread dissatisfaction with the crisis response. Davis’ favorable rating fell from 41% in January to 27%, though utilities, energy suppliers and Bush received worse negative ratings.
- A profile of Los Angeles mayoral candidate Antonio Villaraigosa described his rapid Assembly rise, bipartisan negotiating skills and legislative achievements, alongside criticism of his policy-detail weaknesses, disputed credit for legislation and strained relationships.
- A commentary by Jonathan Wilcox criticized California officials’ attacks on Texas energy companies and urged a stronger corporate response.

North Carolina’s GenX water health goal of 140 parts per trillion anticipates no adverse non-cancer effects. Toxicologist Susanne Brander cited perfluorinated compounds’ associations with thyroid disease and reproductive effects, while noting limited research on cancer associations.

Russian cosmonauts Alexander Misurkin and Anton Shkaplerov completed a record Russian spacewalk lasting 8 hours and 13 minutes while upgrading an International Space Station communications antenna. After replacing an electronics box, they struggled to reposition the antenna, which ended up 180 degrees beyond its intended position. NASA reported it was still working, while Russian officials assembled a team to assess whether further action was needed. If a SanDisk SSD is not recognized, disconnect other USB devices. Use cloning software to copy data from the existing HDD to the SSD, selecting source and destination drives and waiting for completion.

The old HDD may be retained as a backup.

Josh Allen called Cook an “all-time teammate” and suggested resolving his contract helped him play more freely. The 4-0 Bills face the Patriots in Week 5 with a chance to improve to 3-0 in their division.

Trump administration policies and funding uncertainty have disrupted services for more than 5 million English language learners in public schools. Educators report canceled professional development, closed or consolidated newcomer centers, suspended teacher hiring, and halted adult English classes and classroom purchases.

Rapid action during a stroke can help prevent lasting damage. The American Stroke Association’s FAST acronym identifies key warning signs: Face drooping, Arm weakness, and Speech difficulty; Time to call 911 means calling immediately if any symptom appears, even if it disappears. Note when symptoms began. Another mnemonic, STR, prompts asking the person to Smile, Talk, and Raise both arms; difficulty with any action warrants calling for help.

The Gold Overnight Trading Strategy involves buying gold futures or ETFs at the market close and selling at the next open to capture overnight price movements.

Backtests show GDX averaged a 0.12% overnight gain versus a 0.09% intraday loss. GLD’s overnight annual return was 8.4%, compared with 8.2% for buy-and-hold, while intraday gains were practically zero. However, the passage considers these average overnight gains too small to trade profitably.

Two conditional strategies under testing showed stronger results: a long overnight strategy averaged 0.17% across 741 trades, declining to 0.11% since 2012; a GDX short overnight strategy averaged 0.7% across 205 trades.

The passage emphasizes substantial risk and volatility from economic conditions, geopolitical events, and market sentiment. It describes commodity strategies as less robust than stock strategies and prone to deterioration. Trading requires defined entry and exit rules, risk management, discipline, patience, and emotional control.

Most occupational shifts predated widespread AI adoption, and measures of AI exposure, automation, and augmentation showed no relationship with employment or unemployment changes.

SOS low-post defense emphasizes strong individual defense, aggressive post fronting, and coordinated traps to disrupt post scoring. Its six options are:

- **Post Front:** The primary method limits entry passes, touches, and shots. On lob passes, the low Helpside I defender joins the post defender in a double team while teammates rotate.
- **Base Go:** The primary low-post trap directs the offensive post toward the baseline, where the low Helpside I defender supplies a hard double team.
- **Go Top:** The high Helpside I defender traps as the post defender directs the offensive player toward the middle. This option is effective against posts who turn inside and can address difficulties with fronting.
- **Go Wing:** The wing defender follows the entry pass to double-team the post. This secondary option can be used when the offensive wing is a poor outside shooter.
- **Hold:** The post defender plays one-on-one from a three-quarter denial position while teammates stay home and deny kick-out passes, limiting open three-point shots.
- **Yo-Yo:** Against a non-shooting wing, the wing defender drops in and out to help on the post, then closes out if the ball returns outside.

Trap rotations begin as the ball leaves the passer’s hands. After passes out of traps, defenders close out, deny return passes, restore post coverage, and reestablish helpside positions. The passage describes corresponding rotations for both sides of the court.

On World Wetlands Day, Beignet the Nutria did not see his shadow, symbolically predicting a mild hurricane season for South Louisiana. Raised by Jonathan Foret under a special permit, Beignet serves as a mascot educating students about invasive species.

The author criticizes cryopreservation, citing a British teenager whose body was stored in the US for £37,000. Children’s mobile phone ownership varies widely across countries. Sara Zaske’s daughter showed little interest in owning a phone in Berlin but requested one after moving to California, where she was the only fourth-grader in her class without a smartphone.

A European study surveying children ages 9 to 16 in seven countries found that 46% owned smartphones in 2013–2014. School restrictions and costs influenced their use. In the United States, a Nielsen report found that about 45% of children ages 10 to 12 had smartphones with service plans, while another report found that 42% of children 8 and younger owned tablets.

Studies reported smartphone ownership among 72% of South Korean children ages 11 to 12, while phone ownership was substantially lower among children in Ghana and Malawi. Turkish parents differed on the appropriate age for ownership. An Australian study found a median age of 8 for first owning or using a mobile phone.

The American Academy of Pediatrics identifies no single “right” age for a first phone. It recommends age-based media limits, monitoring content and apps, avoiding screens before bedtime, and keeping meals screen-free.

Enron faced growing scrutiny on November 5, 2001, over executive-linked partnerships, financial disclosures and liquidity pressures. The SEC had begun a formal investigation, while Enron maintained its transactions were legal and properly disclosed.

Reports identified a $35 million payment in March to Chewco Investments, managed by Enron officer Michael Kopper, as apparently completing transactions that kept hundreds of millions of dollars in debt off Enron’s balance sheet. Enron subsequently consolidated the JEDI partnership and repaid approximately $620 million of its third-party debt. Questions remained about the entities’ independence and any gains received by Kopper.

Short seller James Chanos had identified warning signs in Enron’s filings, including low returns on invested capital, complex related-party transactions and insider stock sales. Enron shares had fallen 86% during the year. Auditor Arthur Andersen faced potential scrutiny over whether the financial statements adequately explained partnership dealings, particularly following a $1.2 billion reduction in shareholder equity.

The AFL-CIO and Amalgamated Bank called for broader investigations and governance reforms, including reviews of insider transactions, executive compensation and director independence.

Despite securing $1 billion in new credit, Enron suffered another credit-rating downgrade, and bankers suggested asset sales might be necessary. Enron was discussing the sale of its 50% interest in a Korean gas venture.

In India, Enron sought to sell its 65% stake in Dabhol Power amid unpaid bills and a dispute with its sole customer, the Maharashtra State Electricity Board. Investigators are also examining possible tax evasion by Chairman Cho Yang-ho and relatives, including taxes on inherited overseas assets, and suspicious money flows. Australia’s performance reflected substantial dividend contributions: dividends accounted for 53% of total market gains, compared with 42% in the United States. The passage also identifies commodity exports, a strong banking sector, and a service-based economy as possible contributors.

Stock investing offers potential returns, inflation protection, dividend income, ownership, liquidity, diversification, and opportunities to begin with small amounts. Incorporated in January 2000 and launched that June with four vehicles, the company sought to use Internet reservations and wireless technology to create a scalable car-sharing business.

The disclosure describes systems and methods for changed-block tracking to support incremental and differential backups of virtual machines in network or cloud environments that lack native tracking capabilities or accessible APIs. It also addresses differences between data formats used by cloud architectures or hypervisors and those supported by an information management system. Images of a virtual machine disk generated at different times are compared to identify changed blocks and create a location map. A virtual server agent loads a disk copy, uses the map to extract changed blocks, and backs them up.

The information management system protects and manages production data, metadata, and secondary copies across physical, virtual, and cloud resources. Its principal components include:
- A storage manager that coordinates operations, maintains management information, applies policies, schedules jobs, and supports monitoring and recovery.
- Data agents that prepare and restore application data, potentially performing compression, deduplication, encryption, and metadata capture.
- Media agents that facilitate access to secondary storage and maintain indexes for locating, browsing, and restoring stored data.

Primary data is live production data generally stored in its source application’s native format. Secondary copies preserve data for recovery, retention, compliance, search, and other management purposes. They may use different formats, reside on lower-cost storage, and require restoration processing before applications can use them. Components can be distributed to reduce production workloads, support scaling, balance loads, and provide failover, or consolidated on shared computing devices.

Supported operations include backups, archiving, snapshots, replication, deduplication, and storage-tier migration. Full backups capture complete protected data; differential backups capture changes since the last full backup; incremental backups capture changes since the most recent backup. Synthetic full backups consolidate existing backups without transferring primary data again. Archiving copies and removes source data, while snapshots preserve point-in-time states and replication protects data as changes occur. Deduplication reduces redundancy by storing new data portions and referencing existing ones. Information lifecycle management and hierarchical storage management move data between storage tiers according to criteria such as age, size, or importance.

Stanford researchers developed biofilm lithography, using blue light and genetically engineered E. coli to grow intricate bacterial patterns overnight at 25-micrometer resolution. The bacteria secrete a sticky protein in response to light, attaching to illuminated areas. Researchers say the method offers speed, simplicity and compatibility with varied surfaces, including closed microfluidic devices. Unexpectedly sharp patterns provided evidence that many bacteria were already weakly attached to the surface. The technique could help investigate bacterial interactions and support novel biomaterials or biofilm-based circuits. Researchers are working toward growing multiple bacterial strains simultaneously, particularly to study how biofilms may share antibiotic resistance.

This non-peer-reviewed preprint examines SARS-CoV-2 genomic diversity in Rio Grande do Sul (RS), Brazil, and selection pressures on the structural proteins Envelope (E), Membrane (M), and Nucleocapsid (N).

Researchers sequenced 12 respiratory samples collected in Esteio between April and June 2021. All belonged to the Gamma variant: 10 to lineage P.1 and two to P.1.17. They identified 68 nucleotide substitutions, including 36 non-synonymous substitutions. Several mutations were reported for the first time in RS; NSP3:D1208A was newly reported in Brazil, and NSP12:I136V had not previously been described in GISAID.

Analysis of 4,706 RS genomes collected between March 2020 and May 2022 documented successive lineage predominance: B.1.1.33 in 2020, followed by Zeta, Gamma, Delta, and Omicron. Omicron accounted for more than 90% of sequenced genomes between January and April 2022. Sequenced genomes represented approximately 0.19% of reported state cases.

Phylogenomic analyses identified supported groups corresponding to major variants and several sublineages. Eight Esteio genomes had closely related sequences from Brazil or other countries, while four had no identifiable matches. Sequencing quality and sampling limitations prevented firm conclusions about possible migration events.

Tests using FUBAR, FEL, and SLAC identified:
- E protein: no positively selected sites and two negatively selected sites.
- M protein: two positively selected sites and 12 negatively selected sites.

This qualitative study examined preschool teachers’ views on sensory education, classroom practices, and related difficulties. Twenty teachers from varied institutions and settlements participated in approximately 30-minute, semi-structured interviews. Content analysis produced 81 codes, nine categories, and three themes: sensory education’s importance, its relationship with the preschool curriculum, and implementation challenges.

All participants considered sensory education important in early childhood and beneficial across developmental areas. They advocated integrating it into daily routines through age-appropriate activities, enriched environments, individual support, and family involvement. However, almost all described only five senses, and some confused “sense” with “emotion.”

Teachers reported incorporating sensory experiences through art, music, rhythm, games, experiments, drama, tactile materials, and balance activities. Evaluation generally relied on observation and children’s responses. Family involvement included communication, meetings, training, and activities at home or in classrooms.

Most participants considered sensory education insufficiently explicit in the preschool curriculum. The discussion noted that the curriculum contains sensory-related outcomes and permits flexible planning. Teachers also reported inadequate materials, unsuitable physical environments, and limited competence in addressing sensory integration problems; almost all wanted further training.

Recommendations included in-service training, greater undergraduate coverage of sensory education, improved classroom materials, occupational therapist support, and collaboratively developed sample activities.

This study protocol describes a three-arm randomized controlled trial evaluating Digital-MindCAN, a live, videoconference-based mindfulness psychoeducation programme tailored to cancer survivors in Singapore. Existing mindfulness interventions often lack cancer-specific content, and evidence remains limited regarding symptom prevention, psychological well-being, resilience, and objectively measured stress.

The trial will recruit 150 cancer survivors from a tertiary hospital and randomly assign 50 participants each to Digital-MindCAN plus standard care, Palouse Mindfulness plus standard care, or a wait-list control group. Eligible participants are adults aged 21–65 with stage 0–III cancer who completed treatment within the specified two-week-to-two-year period, except ongoing hormonal therapy.

Both intervention programmes comprise eight weekly, 90-minute sessions and encourage 10–30 minutes of daily home practice. Digital-MindCAN combines mindfulness education and practice with information about cancer-related stressors, symptoms, treatment effects, emotions, and relationships. Palouse Mindfulness provides general stress reduction without cancer-specific content. Wait-listed participants may attend either programme after study data collection.

Primary outcomes are objective and subjective stress. Secondary outcomes include psychological well-being, relaxation, mindfulness, resilience, depression, and anxiety. Researchers will collect questionnaires, physiological measurements—including skin temperature, heart rate, and oxygen saturation—and post-intervention focus group interviews. Quantitative analyses will use intention-to-treat methods, covariance analysis, and repeated-measures analysis of variance; qualitative data will undergo realist analysis.

The trial will test whether Digital-MindCAN is superior to wait-list control and non-inferior to Palouse Mindfulness, while exploring participants’ experiences. Ethics approval and trial registration have been obtained. Anticipated challenges include recruitment and attrition. Positive findings could support offering Digital-MindCAN as an additional service for cancer survivors; the passage reports no trial results.
